top_reviews.content:
I recently tried two drinks from this place – Plantea and Passion Fruit Tea – and honestly, both were so good!
The Plantea had such a smooth and refreshing taste. You can tell they use good quality ingredients. It wasn’t too heavy or overly sweet, just nicely balanced and super enjoyable.
The Passion Fruit Tea was my favorite though! The sugar level was just perfect – not too sweet, not too bland. It had that fresh, tangy kick that makes you want to keep sipping. They really got the sweetness level right.
What I appreciated even more is their effort to reduce plastic waste here in California. Instead of the usual plastic cups, they served the drinks in reusable glass bottles — and at the same price as a regular cup! That’s such a thoughtful move, and it feels good to support a business that actually cares about the environment.
Great taste, perfect sweetness, and eco-friendly too — definitely coming back again! 😊

Wonderful customer service. Delish drinks. Quick service. They provide their drinks in a glass container which you can save to redeem a new drink at 10% off. If you turn in 10 bottles, you get a free drink. I recommend going. Enough seats for 12 people.

We were craving boba tea late at night and found this spot open until 11 PM! My boyfriend tried a sample of the Thai tea first to make sure it wasn’t too sweet—and it blew our mind. It was perfectly balanced with just the right amount of sweetness, exactly what we always been looking for. Bubble tea can sometimes be way too sugary, but not here. They had run out of tapioca pearls, so my boyfriend went with grass jelly instead, and honestly, it was the most delicious Thai tea I’ve ever had! Definitely will come back here again when we in SF!
I got the Nutella Milk Tea with sea salt sprinkles and… my soul left my body for a few minutes of bliss. Super tasty and affordable!

One of my go to's whenever I'm in the area! Highly recommend their grape fruit tea with sea salt crema (blueberry is my second choice)! The tea flavors here are better than the other boba shops. I still opt for 0% sugar, but y'all may want to go a little bit higher.

Sustainability is one of their core values. They offer glass bottles at the same price. You can get 10% off your drink if you reuse it!

reviews_snippets.content: "Food: 4 Decor: 3 Service: 3 Came here to grab some cold oolong milk tea."
"They offer fresh fruit teas, super friendly staff."

top_reviews.content:
The matcha latte had a delicate, smooth flavor — creamy, gentle, and perfectly balanced.
The ichigo daifuku was simply delightful: soft, chewy mochi wrapped around a juicy fresh strawberry, with a subtle sweetness that complemented the fruit beautifully.
A lovely combination!

Stopped by to grab a drink and was pleasantly surprised. The milk tea was really good, and the drinks came out fairly quickly. I ordered a matcha milk tea with boba, and the flavors were nicely balanced. The matcha wasn’t too bitter, and the boba had a great chewy texture.
I also picked up a croissant, and it was surprisingly good. Light, flaky, and a nice little treat to go with the drink. It was an easy and enjoyable stop, and I’d definitely come back to try more items on the menu next time.

This tea house is supported by the sale of bubble tea and other tea-family sweet drinks served in plastic disposable cups and straws. The space is cool, but the vibe is ruined by poorly amp'd junk music that is more sound graffiti than music. They would be better off with ambient sounds or no music at all. But invest is speakers first.

I know a thing or two about tea, so I wanted to enjoy some properly brewed Chinese tea while in Downtown Berkeley.  I opted for Da Hong Pao (Great Red Robe), a generally wonderful tea from Fujian. I watched the staff brew it in a small pot; after steeping,  they served it to me in 8 oz ceramic cup. Serving chinese tea to westerners in a way that works in  can be hard. I prefer gongfu places where I can brew myself and get multiple steeps.  Or places devoted only to tea and not tea infused drinks. That said, it wasn't a bad brew. But one doesn't get to linger over the tea, or enjoy the other aspects associated with traditional tea culture here.

I won't come back unless it's empty, the music is off, or something else changes.

If you want a fruit, milk or bubble tea, I would recommend. Head to Blue Willow, Far Leaves, or Teance if you want to drink actual tea.  They could certainly do it here, but they can't do both starbucks-style tea and fine tea at the same time. It's a shame.

Great teas!
Yummy matcha soft serve!
Compostable cups and straws!
Oh my.
And the boba was perfectly cooked (not heavily sugared like most boba places).
We also got daifaiku which they sell from another vendor.
I love that the tea quality wasn’t secondary like many shops.
Staff were friendly too.

I highly recommend this place.

Nice tea house at Berkeley.  They have another location at SF. We stopped by after lunch. Looks like it is a good place to study or work as I see many customers working on the laptop.
I heard this tea house is pretty famous. it has nice interior and high ceiling. They also have one popup store inside when we visit.
There are plenty of teas  and match varieties. They also sell the match powder, tea leaf and Hojicha powder . They also have imperial Matcha powder.  We ordered just cold matcha and it was good.  it was not that strong.  We will stop by next time to try other tea.

Stumbled upon this with my friend, I got the regular iced matcha latte and she got the blood orange matcha latte. The iced matcha latte was perfect~ the blood orange matcha latte was interesting in a good way! You taste both the orange and the matcha, it was a perfect  balance of the two.

It’s a super cute matcha cafe. They sell matcha here and other teas. Service was fast and they were all very helpful.

We stopped here after a recommendation. I love a creamy, umami, nutty, and minimally bitter or astringent matcha. My friend and I both got the plain matcha latte, and we were floored. It was so delicious!! Both one of our favorite matchas ever! I live in Seattle but will come back on my next trip!

Used to be good, the quality is worse and more expensive now. I work nearby and so I have come here often over a long period of time. I used to feel it was worth it paying more than other shops to have quality. But then they started to upcharge everything, even for getting no ice 😂 and they put less matcha every time. This last time it was almost pure milk, so I asked for an extra shot. This is how the color is with a double shot of matcha. One of the baristas has yet to make my drink to my specifications, so it’s super inconsistent. This is a photo of when I asked for a double shot (after the double shot was poured in). Basically milk
One of the best matcha spots in the city! The matcha is always smooth and high quality, and the boba is delicious with the perfect texture. Definitely one of my favorite places to grab a drink.

I really thought this place was cute, and their menu was amazing with so many delicious options. But when I got my drink, the matcha wasn't very strong, there was a lot of ice (I got light ice), and the Asian pear I got in it was chunky and not very flavorful. The size was also pretty small, and this whole drink cost $8.15!! I also asked for it 'for here,' but it came in the same cup as the 'to-go' cups. Overall, it wasn't that good and I would likely not come again. Maybe their other drinks are better though!

top_reviews.content:
Hey Tea is my most favorite boba spot in Bay no doubt. I could not find a drink that I hate here 🥹 Today I tried their new seasonal drink - pistachio cloud jasmine coconut and I really like it. It tastes super fresh, light and not too sweet at all. Basically just coconut juice with a nutty creamy pistachio foam on top but it went really well together. You can even choose 0 cal sweetener to lower the calories intake, which I did, so I didn’t feel guilty at all drinking the whole thing!
It wasn’t busy when I went, maybe I got lucky, but I got my drink in like 5 mins after ordering. But if you want to save time, you can download the Hey Tea app and order ahead, really convenient if you don’t wanna wait. I don't have enough phone storage for it but I would do that if I can 😂

Our first time at a Heytea store was in New York. We liked it a lot. So we were happily surprised when we came across this place in San Francisco. The teas taste very good and the prices are fair. The store is clean and the workers are hygienic. There were a lot of customers which speaks for itself. We will be back.

It’s always so busy but the staff always had great attitude. Loved the two drinks I got here and downloaded the app and ordered in advance since the wait is about 20-40mins on average especially if they have conferences that day
Amazing fresh tea and signature cheese foam! Real fruit ingredients, customizable sweetness, clean shop and nice service. My go-to bubble tea shop, highly recommend!！

The lychee jelly is standard and good. I got the honey grapefruit boba, which was less sweet than I thought at 25%. The boba itself was watery and kinda not very strongly tea flavored. The grapefruit rind at the bottom was good and flavorful but did not translate to the rest of the drink

I tried the Hong Kong–style bubble tea here, and it was good. The tea is strong and bold, made with condensed milk, which gives it a rich flavor. Definitely a tasty and satisfying drink if you enjoy stronger tea.
One of the best I’ve tried. The signature tea, the mango latte were amazing. Quick service.

The level of customization with the ice, sugar, and dairy options are always a plus. T4 is always a great spot

T4 Oakland is a go-to spot for delicious popcorn chicken and tasty milk tea. The flavors are great, and the prices are reasonable. I really appreciate how customizable the drinks are—you can adjust sweetness, ice levels, and toppings to your liking. Highly recommended if you’re craving a solid boba and snack combo!

Elegant Rose Aloe was so good! It's a lovely caffeine free rose-flavored iced drink that has coconut and aloe jellies in it. The words used to describe it in the advertisement on the TV menu were "romantic, fancy, and floral" and I would say that description was accurate. The lowest sweetness option was still a little too sweet for me but I still enjoyed it very much. I felt very romantic, fancy and floral. : )

This place has some of the best prices for boba around. They have seats inside allowing you to spend some time with friends. The staff was friendly and quick with my order. I only wish that their payment system was a bit more updated to easily tip.

top_reviews.content: My absolute favorite for multiple reasons: 1) They really know how to brew tea perfectly. For me that's the most important criteria when it comes to boba places. If you are a tea lover like me I recommend getting the Alishan Jinxuan Oolong. For this tea, you usually have to wait 15 min but it is absolutely worth the wait. Smooth texture, zero bitterness, subtle floral notes - just perfect. 2) They also have a lot of those drinks that I consider more a dessert like their jelly series (teas with grass jelly, pudding, tofuhua etc), cream brûlée milk tea, fresh taro milk tea.. Those drinks are also absolutely amazing! 3) Consistent quality. I've been here many, many, many times and always left satisfied. 4) The location is good as well. Sure, it is not the cutest boba spot. But it doesn't need to be. All I want is a friendly face taking my order and then walking around Lake Merritt with an amazing drink in my hand.
Got the White Peach Blossom Tea. The service was very fast. The line can be long here but usually goes quick. Boba is soft and not frozen. Great choice for an afternoon drink!

I’ve been visiting this boba shop regularly to pick up drinks for my wife. It’s one of her favorites, and over time one of mine as well. The quality keep us coming back. I’ll be sure to capture better photos next time to do the presentation justice.

Since I started coming here, the menu has undergone a few changes. Some longtime favorites have been retired ( I still miss the banana milk tea) but they’ve introduced new specials that continue to impress.

On this visit, I tried the Cocoa Volcano Brown Sugar Boba, White Peach Oolong Tea Latte, and the Durian Coffee Latte. The Cocoa Volcano is one of our staples.  The White Peach Oolong, topped with fresh cream was a standout, but not in the right cup for my preference. The Durian Coffee Latte was unique. There were a good amount of durian chunks that I ended up blending, and added a bit more coffee to suit my taste, and the result was great.

Our usual picks also include the Matcha and Coffee Volcano, as well as the Lychee, Passion Fruit Tea, and Hazelnut Milk Tea. All consistently well-executed with fresh flavors and high-quality ingredients.

My absolute FAVORITE place to get boba! They make beautifully curated and high quality tea drinks that aren't going to cost you $8 a drink (including the classic add-ons!). You honestly can't go wrong with any flavor you choose.

In lieu of that sentiment, I tried the Puff Cream Milk Tea for the first time yesterday and it was SO GOOD. The cream is cake flavor so you get an earthy/sweet/dessert balance with the black tea and cream. I picked up a classic jasmine milk tea for my friend. I usually get a plant based milk and chose soy milk for both.

I'm hoping to try their soy milk tea special next time. It seems like their currently out?? 😭

top_reviews.content:
BW is the friendliest, loveliest place to sit and enjoy a tasty drink in Berkeley. Their tea is so consistently delicious and the staff is so knowledgeable and welcoming. Everyone who works here has been so warm and generous in creating a space that truly feels like a community hub that brings the best of all the colorful sides of life that the bay has to offer. I’ve spent hours talking with strangers at the bar about art and poetry and life, and I’ve spent hours reading and writing in peaceful solitude. Blue willow is truly an escape from the stress of daily life.

Their wide range of teas is a testament to the very intentional curation and selection of really special cakes and leaves from around the world. Their in house blends and herbal options are also a treat. But nothing beats their hojicha latte on a cloudy day.

The acupressure + tea tasting I did there in the fall was one of the sweetest little moments of last year. Pairing a grounding puerh with a lesson on acupressure points related to the lungs and grief, giving me a chance to tune into my body and mind in a safe, educating space.

I’m so grateful that such a beautiful place like this exists and is thriving so well, community spaces like this are what allow us to share our lives and selves, and spaces like this are what makes Berkeley and the east bay feel like home.

Thanks BW for offering a sense of place, and a beautiful space to inspire creativity and community.

Superb Japanese tea house experience in the heart of Berkeley with caring people and clean, artfully decorated premises. Just learned about this establishment today due to recommendation from Artis Coffee (top notch roastery) and hit the mother lode. Aly, the exceptionally kind and engaged owner took care of us personally while Niko served the beverages with authentic courtesy and care. The establishment is bright and airy, with several intimate spaces creatively designed for Zen like relaxation which encourages one to linger. I’ve never observed a broader selection of quality teas, however, Aly and Niko helped us efficiently navigate choices to match our taste profile. You can even order a flight to sample several teas and from there decide what to purchase for taking home (Blood Orange super tasty). In addition to tea, Blue Willow offers high quality pastries and Japanese cookies as well as tea preparation and serving ware. Happened to hit their 9 year anniversary which elevated the experience. This establishment which exudes pride of ownership throughout fit us to a ‘tea’ and we can’t wait to return. Bravo Aly!

This was such a fun find in Berkeley! We came after wanting to try something different that didn't involve alcohol and tea sounded perfect.

Good:
- The private room was really good! We got out own private spot for about an hour and thirty minutes
- The service was great - we had our own tea steeper and had enough tea for the entire time
- Loved the duck s*** tea and the dragon tea and puerh tea, super tasty and we even tried mixing it a lot
- The place is so cute! Very relaxing

Bad:
- Gets super busy, so make a reservation ahead of time!

Overall, really enjoyed having the time to sit and relax and be present with me and my boyfriend!

This is my new favorite teahouse. You know it's legit when there's a bookshelf, awesome music, friendly staff and great lighting. The Sakura mochi was amazing and we shared a pot of shou that tealuminated us in all the right ways. Great prices, great packaging, a one of a kind vibe. I'll most definitely be coming back to explore more varieties of tea. Black Phoenix on Ice this Summer sounds like just the thing!

The tea and atmosphere were great, and the place is beautiful. However, we didn’t feel welcomed. We were taking a few photos because we loved the decor, but one staff member kept following us and asking what we were photographing, which made us uncomfortable. Later, my brother accidentally closed the communal room door, and she immediately came in to tell us to keep it open. She also warned us not to touch the decorations, even though we hadn’t touched anything. Unfortunately, the experience was disappointing because we felt like we were being watched instead of welcomed.

9/24/25

A friend recommended this place, & I came to try many times.  I think these 4 are the ok drinks here: the supreme bobo milk tea (for 1st time, after that it becomes boring, too creamy & to sweet), the cold  jasmine milk tea (very strong), coconut mango boom ( which my son likes), & recently the pistachio cloud king jasmine (light/less sugar adjustment).

Downside: take really long time to get the drink, all their milk teas taste the same flavour as the supreme bobo milk tea. Nothing different when adding bobo into the drink.  I guess they using too much brown sugar, that’s why it becomes too sweet when adding bobo into the drink.
I don’t recommend to add bobo into the black milk tea with less sugar. It tastes sooo sweet.  I bought my drink at 13:25 & just drink 2 sips to taste, & the drink still full at 10:41pm.  This is the first time I’ve ever been able to drink a milk teas.
Second one is the triple supreme matcha latte, it tastes bitter & blind, we had to throw it away.

I have had Heytea before, trying the Triple Matcha and the Mulberry Boom.

🍵 Triple Matcha: I think my favorite was the triple matcha with the combination of Jasmine and matcha giving a very strong green tea flavor along with the matcha heavy cream.

☕ Yingde Mochi Milk Tea: This time I tried their Yingde mochi milktea which was very unique. I had tried mochi milk tea before but the last time I had it, it was a choking hazard. I just wished I could see the pretty layers of this drink in a clear cup. I hope I can order this again next time!

top_reviews.content:
Cute little boba shop tucked away in Berkeley, in the Telegraph district, close to several popular food joints. Parking is super convenient with several reasonably priced garages and plenty of cheap street parking. This place has a small seating area with a few tables and pickup options available. Ordering is efficient through a kiosk and fulfilled quickly.

We ordered a matcha yuzu tea, a strawberry pudding with boba, a taro tea and a signature black tea with boba. All were excellent. They allowed for customizing the ice and sugar levels for all drinks. My favorites were the matcha yuzu and the signature black tea. The matcha yuzu was light, extremely fresh and citrusy. The black tea was strong and very high quality. The strawberry one was on the sweeter side so opting for a lower sugar level is a good idea. The taro one had an overpowering taro flavor.

All in all, highly recommend this for a post meal dessert if you're in the area!

I’m a huge fan of this place because their drinks especially the milk tea are spot on. But beyond the flavors, the service here is truly top-notch. There’s a young guy (who looks Chinese) who is always smiling and even remembers my usual order. Also, the woman who can speak Thai is absolutely wonderful. Both of them go above and beyond, and whenever there’s a hiccup with an order, they handle it so helpfully and with a great attitude. Even the manager is amazing. I once had an issue with an order and called the store, and the manager handled it personally. He didn't let the problem slide and was super enthusiastic about making things right. The customer service here is truly next-level. The owner is honestly so lucky to have such an amazing team!!

This was one of the BEST Boba drinks I have ever had. I tried the lychee rose ice slushy with boba added and no extra sugar. The flavour was delicate, the blended ice made it refreshing and subtle sweetness from lychee fruit balanced it out! I am definitely coming back and sharing with friends.

Haven’t been to this TP Tea location in years! Used to come here weekly while I was in school. I’m glad to see that they are still doing well and in the same spot.

When you enter, there are 3-4 different self order stations which is great because there was no wait/line! If you prefer ordering from a real person, it’s a bit hard to get their attention but if you’re lucky and can waive someone over they’re happy to help.

I ordered the Boba Fresh Milk Tornado with 50% sweetness for $6.25. I was really craving a matcha tornado but they only had the fresh milk and Thai tea tornados.

Considering that it was only boba pearls, tornado (custard/cream), milk, and ice it was actually very good. Super refreshing, the custard went very well with the milk and perfectly cooked boba pearls. The pearls were bouncy and didn’t stick to your teeth, they were also not over saturated in sugar either.

I do have to say that the store itself was uncomfortably hot and humid. I’m not sure what was going on with the ventilation. They even had one of the front doors propped open and it felt like a completely different climate inside the store. Hopefully that gets fixed soon.

Ordered two boba milk teas from TPT and they were both great.

The tea had strong flavor, not overly sweet (0% and 30% sweet) and the boba was fresh with the right chew. Drinks were made quickly and the staff was friendly. Clean shop with a simple vibe—no frills, just solid milk tea.

Definitely a spot I’d come back to when I’m craving boba. No rest room here so that needs to change soon. Don’t
Worry about parking near the store as it’s impossible to find parking. You are better off parking at the nearby parking garage.

top_reviews.content:
The Imperial Tea Court restaurant in the Ferry Building has been holding the San Francisco Tea Festival each year. And I didn’t want to miss out this special Spring event - May 2nd & 3rd. As a tea fan, I attended the 1st day - 5/2/26. I enjoyed it so much!
The curated group of vendors from China/Japan/Taiwan/Nepal/India/Europe and USA at this event is always interesting and I usually find a new tea or two.
Asian American purveyors of tea, local pastry treats, tea infused chocolate and tea paraphernalia fill out the show. Attendees got to sample from all vendors. Then, for those teas I liked, I got to purchase the teas! The best: an outstanding Indonesian Ginger tea from a company called NUSA which was started by a young Asian American young man who shifted careers to start his own tea business! Amazing!
I also attended a lecture about Kore tea but there was a later lecture on how to cook with tea - the room was packed…note to myself: arrive early to the lecture room for the next tea lecture of interest!
As an early bird attendee, I received a white tote bag filled with a variety of tea samples and the porcelain sampling teacup cup! What a fun day!

we shared a Beijing Braise pork belly and Dragon Well Dumplings , and both were incredibly delicious 😋 pork belly is usually hit or miss for me but it melted in my mouth. I was so excited to see the large selection of tea they had with detailed descriptions and bought two types to try. The gaiwan teacups are a good price too, which is nice considering the area can be a bit pricey towards tourists. The Hong Kong milk tea was delicious and sweet how I like it! will be stopping by every time I take the ferry now!

p.s. I suggest putting some tea pets out to sell too ! I bet customers would love them!

We got a vegetarian dim sum sampler (5 tofu/purple rice dim sums, one spring roll and two steamed buns) for takeout. The staff at the front was super accommodating by making it all vegetarian and made it ready in some minutes. We were running short of time, otherwise we would have dined in. It seemed a good place for dining in or takeout. Good that they have vegetarian options in the menu since there are only a few restaurants in the ferry building serving dishes suitable for 100% vegetarian diet.
Had the pork hand pulled noodles, they were amazing! Lovely spot for lunch and tea.
I got the pork BBQ steam bun to go. They had to reheat the buns as they were closing. The steam buns and its fillings were dry.

top_reviews.content: Make your reservations TODAY! I absolutely LOVE LOVE LOVE Malaya Tea Room! I have been countless times and have recommended it to so many different people and everyone has LOVED it and raved about it once they go or once I’ve taken them! The whole experience is amazing, delicious variety of teas to choose from: black teas, green teas, Asian teas, no caffeine herbal teas. There is also a large variety of traditional European sandwiches to choose from as well as delicious Malaysian/asian flavored sandwiches! During December they have a special fixed holiday menu that’s also different than usual. They also change the desserts selections frequently so it’s always a different experience every time you go. The service is always impeccable and kind. Atmosphere and decor is beautiful and comfortable, like a favorite auntie’s warm and inviting home who loves to feed you! Visit this place to treat yourself (I’ve gone solo and they have tea for one!), or book for a special event or your besties birthday. They have 3 seatings a day on their open days which are Thursday - Sunday. The times are 11 am, 1 pm, and 3 pm. They very often get booked out and full, so plan ahead and make your reservations!

**credentials: Teahead with a good amount of tea experience in the US, BC, and UK; recently relocated to the Bay and on the hunt for the best tea service locally.**

Kicking off the series here with Malaya, a tribute to British Malayan culture; an unconventional but intriguing pick.

Ambiance: Tea for two on a rainy Saturday afternoon. 1:15 p.m. time slot; full house, too packed for an audible conversation. I’d recommend booking the proper 3 p.m. slot.

Our table was directly in front of the open entrance, so expect some wind and chills.

Tea: Refillable water, non-refillable tea. The Apple Cider lacked apple flavor. The Genmaicha with Coconut was pleasant but weak; I had to ask for a double bag.

Eats: The Southeast Asian–style sardine sandwich was well-seasoned and balanced with cucumbers, absolutely phenomenal!

The Chicken Apple came on brown bread with generous apple chunks.

The Turkey and Smoked Salmon sandwiches were mediocre.

The scone was on the dry side, but the clotted cream was proper. Unsure if the jam was homemade or commercial. Fruits were fresh and sweet. The pandan cake was a nice twist, subtle enough for those unfamiliar with the flavor.

Service: The servers were very polite and kind, with some training in tea knowledge. They kept interactions minimal to avoid disruption. Ring the bell for service.

Amenities: The room was clean and well kept, with a spacious restroom in the back. Non-formal china. Low coffee table. Chairs and tiered stands can be wobbly.

Accessibility: The entrance is ADA-compliant, though the packed seating can pose challenges for wheelchair access. I’d recommend noting your needs during booking to ensure the best seating.

Overall: A cozy neighborhood spot for those seeking a casual outing. A lot of thought and emphasis have been put into showcasing the owner’s Southeast Asian heritage, and I’d highly recommend exploring that when ordering.

google.description: Flowery dining room offering tea, cakes & finger sandwiches for ladies' lunches & birthday parties.

top_reviews.content:
What a fantastic experience! Dartealing’s High Tea was truly the best I’ve ever had. The seasonal menu was beautifully curated, with every item fresh, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. The house special Baja fish sandwich was outstanding and absolutely worth the additional $9.

The service was equally impressive. My server, Keith, was attentive, friendly, and helped make the afternoon even more enjoyable. I highly recommend Dartealing to anyone looking for an exceptional tea experience, and I’m already looking forward to my next visit!

Darteeling has absolutely ruined me--I don't think I'll be able to enjoy another tea lounge for a good while. I've been to Rundle Bar in Banff, Courtyard in Boston, Majorelle in NY, and a few other places in DC and as wonderful as those locations were, I always left feeling the savory sandwiches were underwhelming or not really savory/bland and sweets were too sweet with flavor profiles that seemed too unique for my taste.

Dartealing's savory bites this season were balanced, familiar but elevated, had great contrasting textures and genuinely delicious. The sweets were also not too sweet, which I appreciated because I finished my entire portion before my husband finished his (this never happens). I also felt the preset menu was very intentional in how it was composed and loved how there was no silverware (don't know if this was intentional) because that typically takes up so much space on the table.

It was also super cozy inside and felt homey which is my preference. I felt like I could just  sit and enjoy my tea time without worrying about anything else.

I don't live in SF, but would be willing to fly from the opposite coast to come here again!

I spotted Dartealing Lounge several times when riding by on a SF Muni bus going from Caltrain towards downtown. A lover of tea, I was happy to finally try it with a friend this past weekend.
The experience was good. 😊
Ambiance: the lounge is in an old (historic) building on 3rd Street in SOMA. The long room has a cozy feel with the cutest décor (decorative lamps, chintz curtains, a variety of seats and photos). It is spacious compared to another SF (Noe Valley) tea room I’d visited years ago - giving you some privacy.
Food: the Proper Tea service was what the two of us ordered. It is two pots of tea (separate flavors) in gorgeous heavy china teapots and a 3-tiered plated tower with a mix of savory and sweet creations. We happened to be at the lounge while the June menu was « Latin flavor ». My absolute favorite things were the tea sandwiches. The shop makes their own sauces and recipes for these. There were two corn (elote), two chicken salad and two cucumber sandwich triangles per person - basically we each ended up with 1.5 entire full-sized sandwiches on soft white and brown bread.
The acclaimed scone was just okay.
I found having my scone sliced already and a spot of clotted cream and a spot of lemon curd on it (rather than keeping it whole and the toppings in side cups) to be less pleasurable. The scones were small and slightly toasted - they ended up being dry :(
Cutting one small scone in half with a result of two pieces was dainty-looking but not substantial. The puréed black bean (with chunks of bean) empanada was yummy but underbaked and the chorizo roll in puff pastry was nice but there was very little chorizo.
Teas: I chose a black tea (Her Majesty’s Secret Service) and my friend chose a white, fruity tea (Cabana Boy). Both teas had light aromas and tastes. They went well with the food.
Service: Very pleasant. We were asked to wait in the entry lounge for 5 minutes until our official start time of 11:30am commenced. Then right on time, we were escorted to our table - a cute round set up in a corner. The wingback chair I sat in was plush and I sank in. The tea service was clearly explained to us and we placed our orders. We were asked how things were once and had the water in the teapot’s replenished.
Interesting fact: the lounge has been in business for 17 years. That’s some longevity!!!
Overall, Dartealing Lounge provides a nice tea service at a reasonable price. The other patrons (Moms with daughters, Grandmothers with grandkids or just groups of friends) were enjoying the experience. The 90 minutes for this reservation went by so quickly that we had to box some of the food to takeaway. I’m sure others were like me wishing we were given more time to relax.

OMG so much fun. The food was excellent, tea was delicious, and environment was beyond charming. I highly recommend trying this at least once. The flavors were an inventive, global version of high tea. DO make a reservation, they only offer the afternoon tea on weekends. Unless there is a game happening (though it explicitly says no game parking), the side street is good for parking.

P.s. If they have baja fish sandwich, say yes.

This place deserves five stars. We were lucky to dine on the last day of the Asian-inspired menu, and boy oh boy, did I feel pampered. The black sesame scone was the best scone I ever had in my life. All the sandwiches and little bites were unique and flavorful.

Our group had 1 pescatarian and they went above and beyond to accommodate. Sweet and knowledgeable staff.

top_reviews.content:
I first want to say that the shop itself is very lovely and everything looked to be high quality.

That being said there is a chance that if you go there they will flat out ignore you. I had some questions about some of the teaware and the Pu-erh but none of it got answered. I tried to make eye contact. Nothing. There was a younger person helping a couple and I was waiting till they were done but there was an older woman who walked through who went out of her way to avoid me. I eventually ended up leaving and bought some tea down the street.

I did go back into the store to get photos of the teaware I was interested because maybe I can find it somewhere else. The older woman gave me kind of a dirty look while she was helping other customers. So I know she worked there.

I have no idea what I did wrong but my guess it was probably my look. I have tattoos and piercings. I’ve never encountered this in the Bay Area so it was weird that it happened in a tea shop of all places. I’m not sensitive about not getting helped immediately, I milled around for 20ish minutes, but honestly it bummed me out a little that no one even wanted to talk to me or give me their tea opinions. I expect this kind of thing from a designer store not a tea shop.

All this to say is if you are alternative looking maybe don’t be surprised if they ignore you here. I’m pretty sure this is the same place that used to be on 4th street and they were REALLY nice and helpful before, but that’s also before I had piercings and tattoos. So who knows. Maybe that wasn’t it and maybe I just got unlucky, and I hope so. I’ll probably try again in a few months and maybe I’ll go earlier in the day and not an hour before closing.

I’ll change my rating if it turns out that was I just being a baby about the whole thing and update the whole review.

I really did want that travel set though. It’s so dang cute and I love the bag. 🫠

top_reviews.content:
Sweetheart Cafe, Oakland’s Chinatown

This Sweetheart Cafe location has been here for more than 30 years. It originally sells snacks and tons of candies in different aisles . Later on, they sold dried fruits also. Eventually they sold hot foods like popcorn chicken, curry fish balls and different boba drinks. They have seatings as well.

Their boba drinks had became so popular that they opened locations in Berkeley, San Francisco and Milpitas.

I love their bobas, it’s sweet, bouncy and great chewing texture. They used to have small tapioca options which I had loved, but it isn’t an option anymore. All their drinks are pretty good so you can’t be wrong what drinks you choose.

I highly recommend their drinks and their popcorn chicken. I will definitely come back and try other drinks as well.
One of the best Avacado smoothies in east bay. No chunks of ice but still a good density of smoothie and generous amount of boba balls 🤌🤌

This was the first boba shop in Oakland Chinatown. Been going here since I was a kid..

Got the açaí strawberry banana smoothie and my burger,  Best meal ever!

This place is SO SLEPT ON! This review is only for the popcorn chicken.

Ever since I moved from SoCal to the Bay Area, I’ve been trying to find a popcorn chicken spot that meets all my requirements: has to have basil, use chicken dark meat, super crispy, fresh, consistent, and reasonably price.

This is THE SPOT! And the pricing is so good especially in this economy. Half size is decent portion for $7.55 and Full size is $10.25.

The service is as good as it gets - people generally do takeout. You order on the monitor outside or can do mobile order, and they’ll text you when your order is ready, which really helps if you’re struggling to find a parking spot.

Parking is typical in Chinatown - it’s usually bustling and packed but no one is going to give you shit if you emergency park on the street haha.

The inside of the place has some snacks and candy. You CAN sit down and eat there but it’s not the best dining spot and there’s a lot of clutter.

In my opinion, drinks and boba are pretty mid. It does the job but nothing amazing.

My go-to spot for popcorn chicken though ❤️

Very honest and clean mom and pop shop. One of the best popcorn chickens that I've had in my life and I've had a lot of different ones in Taiwan. Love how they always include the fried basil as that's the soul of this street dish. Also love their Barley tea creama, so perfect for the hot weather. Generous amount and fairly priced. Will continue to support the business! (Regular sized rose/oolong/barley tea creama is on sale now for $3.45! Not sure how long the sale would last)

top_reviews.content: Not a big fan of fruit tea, but I love their mango green tea! I always go for 0 sugar with lychee jelly, they’re a perfect match! I appreciate that they are up to 1 or 2am, as I like to get boba or tea in the midnight lol

Their boba is consistently chewy and I find that they actually read the “less ice” detail I add to the my orders. Today I saw the lady sift out the ice before sealing my drink since I asked for 50% ice

I also like that they have an honest review policy and they respond genuinely to most reviews on Google maps and try to make things right.

Decor is simple, not necessarily a place I’d study at but I’m really only here to get boba quickly

My experience at Sharetea in Berkeley was nothing short of phenomenal, particularly due to their creative collaboration with ATEEZ fans for a cupsleeve event. As an ardent fan of the K-pop group, I was thrilled to attend a gathering that celebrated their music and brought fans together. Sharetea went the extra mile by infusing the cafe with K-pop-themed decorations, playing ATEEZ's hits, and offering exclusive merchandise. The ambiance was electric; you could feel the excitement and camaraderie among fans. The cupsleeve event was like a mini-festival, complete with photo opportunities and social interactions that made it a memorable day.

What impressed me the most was how seamlessly Sharetea managed to balance the bustling event with their usual level of quality service and professionalism. Despite the crowd, the staff remained attentive and patient, ensuring that everyone felt welcome and well-served. The drinks were consistently delicious, showcasing the quality that Sharetea is known for. Their bubbly enthusiasm and warm interactions added a personal touch, making each person feel like a valued guest, whether they were there for the event or just to grab a quick drink. It's this elevated level of service that distinguishes Sharetea from other establishments.

In addition, the logistical execution of the events was impeccable. Sharetea seamlessly integrated the ATEEZ-themed activities without disrupting the regular flow of business. This coordination not only kept the fans happy but also ensured that the other customers were not inconvenienced. They managed to create an inclusive environment where everyone could enjoy their time without feeling overwhelmed. Overall, Sharetea's ability to host such a specialized event while maintaining their high standards of service speaks volumes about their dedication and versatility. This experience solidified my admiration for Sharetea, making it my go-to spot in Berkeley.

top_reviews.content: Great atmosphere, very weak tea. I’m sure it’s a great spot if you happen to like very delicate brews, but they don’t appreciate requests to steep the tea longer and it is very very light. Their black tea was weak the two times I’ve been here - like are you sure this is tea it has no flavor at all kind of weak - and there won’t be a third time.

I don't know how to put this any other way, but this is one of the most special places I have ever been too.  This might seem a little extreme for a tea shop; however, Sophie's Cuppa Tea is a sanctuary of peace and serenity.  The owners, Bei and John, are two of the most incredible people I have ever met and they also serve the best tea I have ever had.  I can promise everyone that they will not be disappointed if they come to this shop.   In addition to the shop, if you are looking for your next vacation, ask them about their yearly China Tea Trip.  It is a once in a life time opportunity (although I plan on going every year!).  See photos below :). BTW: They have amazing snacks and salads (fresh and organic).

As I was walking and saw the sign that said "SOPHIE'S CUPPA TEA Not all caffeine is black" I had an immediate reaction.  I love tea and I love to support local mom's and pop's shops, and would have loved to try a cuppa where, according to the website, one doesn't need to put milk and sugar in it.

However, the undertext of the signage didn't sit quite well with me.  I was curious as to why I had such a visceral reaction, so much so that I researched the chemical composition of caffeine.  In my research caffeine is not one color at all, but is comprised of all colors as it comes in a white powdered form.  White is all the colors in the visible light spectrum.  Perhaps the owner had good intentions with this sign, but she totally missed the context clues of the surrounding environment, Oakland, CA.

The best tea I’ve ever had in my life. Everything about this place is made with a lot of love. The owners are very passionate about what they do and that is clearly reflected into their business. The shop is very cozy, peaceful and cute. Love it!

top_reviews.content: The best & most authentic matcha I've ever had! Deep, rich, nutty flavor with a delicious strawberry purée that complemented each flavor very well. Not overly sweet. Would definitely come back for more.

My husband and I really enjoyed our visit to the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art! We happened to visit on our wedding anniversary, and it turned out to be Community Day, so admission was completely free—a very nice surprise and a memorable way to celebrate our anniversary!

The museum itself is gorgeous, and we loved exploring the different floors and discovering how varied the exhibits were. There was a great mix of art and experiences, ranging from more classical works and photography to contemporary pieces and large-scale sculptures. The variety made the visit feel engaging and kept us excited to see what was around the next corner.

One of the highlights for us was getting to experience Yayoi Kusama’s exhibit. With her recent passing, we feel especially fortunate that we had the opportunity to see her work in person beforehand. Her installation was such a memorable experience and definitely something that stood out during our visit.

There was also an immersive sound exhibit that was a lot of fun and gave us a completely different way to experience art. I really appreciated that the museum wasn’t limited to simply looking at artwork on the walls—it incorporated installations and interactive experiences that made the visit more dynamic.

SFMOMA also has a small café with a spacious outdoor patio, which is a great place to take a break and relax. There seemed to be plenty of seating to accommodate even busier days.

Overall, we had a wonderful time at SFMOMA. Between the beautiful building, diverse exhibits, memorable installations, and the chance to experience Kusama’s work, it made for a fantastic anniversary outing. Definitely worth visiting if you enjoy modern and contemporary art!

The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art is one of the best museums in San Francisco, and a must-visit for anyone with even a passing interest in modern and contemporary art. We have visited twice, and both experiences exceeded our expectations.

The museum feels modern from the moment you step inside. The architecture and layout feel intentional and thoughtfully designed, creating a space that is both visually striking and easy to navigate. The collection is varied, and the galleries are arranged in a way that rarely feels overcrowded. This was particularly impressive given that we visited on a Saturday during the summer holiday season, while a special exhibition was also running. The works on display range from familiar names such as Warhol and Lichtenstein to pieces that are provocative, bizarre, and unapologetically avant-garde.

Most recently, we attended the *Matisse’s Femme au chapeau: A Modern Scandal* exhibition, and it was one of the strongest special exhibitions we have seen in San Francisco. My partner and I have visited a number of special exhibitions throughout the city, and while many have been excellent, few have demonstrated the same level of attention to detail. The curators meticulously recreated the original salon gallery where the works debuted, adding valuable historical context and helping visitors better appreciate the controversy and significance surrounding the painting.

The museum café offers a pleasant place to take a break between galleries. The outdoor courtyard is tastefully accented with sculptures and provides impressive views of the surrounding city. The food was surprisingly good, and while the prices were average for the area, they felt reasonable by museum standards. The tart was particularly memorable: fresh, light, and flavorful. It is more of a snack than a meal, but it makes for a nice accompaniment to a coffee and conversation. For budget-conscious visitors, the meal pictured below cost around $15, which felt quite reasonable for a museum café in San Francisco.

To make the most of your visit, purchase your tickets online in advance. They can be added directly to your phone’s wallet, allowing you to bypass the ticket line. If you plan to attend a special exhibition, arrive close to your scheduled entry time, as visitors are generally not admitted early. Afterward, consider spending some time in the Yerba Buena Gardens across the street. It is a peaceful place to relax, reflect on the exhibits, and bring a wonderful day to a close.

The Perfect Park Day in North Beach

​TL;DR: The ultimate park to grab world-class pizza, touch grass, and soak up the sun. Located right in the heart of North Beach (Little Italy), it’s a gorgeous, lively spot for picnics, dog-watching, and pure SF culture. Parking is tough, but the vibes are immaculate.

​🍕 The Ultimate "Grab & Go" Picnic Spot
​Washington Square is practically a front yard for some of the best food in San Francisco. Because it's nestled right in Little Italy, the move here is to grab takeout and have a feast on the lawn.

​The Food Scene: You are steps away from absolute legendary spots. Snag a legendary pie from Tony’s Pizza Napoletana, grab classic Italian comfort food from Original Joe’s, or pop into any of the nearby cafes for a pastry and espresso.

​The Setup: There is plenty of space on the lush green grass to spread out a blanket. It is the perfect spot to sit back with friends, crush some incredible food, and just enjoy the day.

​☀️ The Vibe & Culture

​This park is a beautiful melting pot of tourists, neighborhood locals, and different cultures. No matter what time of day you cruise by, there’s always something beautiful happening:

​Morning to Evening: In the morning, you’ll see neighbors practicing yoga or Tai Chi on the grass. By lunchtime, local workers are out soaking up the sun, and by the weekend, it transforms into a lively community hub with local festivals and pop-up markets.

​Dog & Kid Friendly: If you have a pup, bring them! It's a massive hub for local dog owners, and there’s plenty of room for kids to run around and play.

​The Backdrop: The views here are stunning, framed beautifully by the historic Saints Peter and Paul Church right across the street.

​🎒 Quick Insider Tips for Your Visit
​The Weather: Unlike the foggier sides of the city, North Beach usually gets pretty great, warm weather. It’s an awesome spot to actually catch some reliable rays.
​Getting There & Parking: Honestly, trying to park in North Beach can be a total headache and will definitely require some extra laps around the block. If you can, save yourself the stress and take Muni—tons of bus lines drop you off right by the square.

​Whether you're a local on a lunch break or a visitor wanting to feel the heartbeat of North Beach, this park is pure magic

Salesforce Park is one of the most unique and beautiful places to visit in downtown San Francisco. I was pleasantly surprised by how peaceful and green it feels despite being right in the middle of the city.

The park is built on top of the Salesforce Transit Center, and the design is really impressive. There are beautifully landscaped gardens, walking paths, trees, flowers, fountains, open spaces, and plenty of places to sit and relax. The combination of greenery and the surrounding skyscrapers makes for some great views and photo opportunities.

I particularly enjoyed just walking around and taking in the different sections of the park. It’s very well maintained and feels like a peaceful escape from the busy streets below. The architecture of the transit center itself is also impressive, and the park gives you a completely different perspective of downtown San Francisco.

It’s a great place to visit if you’re looking for somewhere to take a relaxing walk, enjoy some fresh air, have a coffee, or simply take a break while exploring the city. It’s also a great spot for visitors because it’s free and easy to access.

Definitely worth checking out if you’re in downtown San Francisco. A hidden gem in the middle of the city!

The variety of plant life and greenery makes it feel like a true urban oasis, and it’s a great place to walk, relax, or take in views of the city.

That said, the signage could definitely be improved. While the park itself is enjoyable to explore, there isn’t always enough clear information about directions, features, or points of interest. The adjoining transit center can also be confusing to navigate, especially for first-time visitors. Better information screens and clearer transit signage would make the overall experience much smoother and less disorienting.

Overall, it’s a fantastic public space with impressive design and upkeep — it just needs clearer wayfinding and transit information to fully match the quality of the park itself.

We used to go here every few months for family movie night. Went a few weeks ago for The Odyssey. We won't be going back until there's a return to how things used to be pre-Sony.

TL;DR for prospective movie-goers: Very sad to say that you should skip the Alamo. Either go to your true locals like the Balboa, or to the corporates like AMC and Regal that can actually deliver.

Issues for Management:

1. New seats are dramatically less comfortable, recline less, and feel cheap. Check minus.

2. The food feels lower quality, almost Cisco-like. Their "special menu" items also seem much more soulless.  2-3 years ago, you'd have some special app, a few unique cocktails, a tailored entree or pizza. Today, it's a lemonade with blue + red syrup for spiderman.

3. I'm sure as victims of circumstance, the morale of the -remaining staff after lay-offs seems epically low. I feel for them.

4. The irony of the new cell phone ordering policy is absurd. To quote Alamo's new policy: "Putting ordering control directly in our guests’ hands allows us to move faster and more efficiently, creating a smoother, more responsive experience without added distraction." What a red herring. You've made a deal with the devil, laying off hardworking people in exchange for a poorly designed app and a worse customer experience. Stop trying to hide behind "efficiency" and a "more responsive experience" when you're putting people out of work for the sake of profiteering.

5. Have I mentioned that the app itself is also pretty poorly designed and nearly impossible to navigate? Sidenote - there is no way to transition tabs or previous orders from the bar to your seats, which felt like a con. I wouldn't usually complain about this, but when the new price for a 16 oz Coca-Cola is $7.99 and you're told "there's no way to honor refills if it's not in the app", you can't help but feel salty.

Great exhibits on 1/2/26...we really enjoyed the Oakland Museum of California. It was much more expansive and engaging than we expected and very well organized overall. Some sections are fuller than others, but nothing felt confusing or disjointed.

🏛️ Layout & Exhibits
The museum is divided into three main sections on three different levels: (1) California & Oakland history, (2) Science, and (3) Art.

The history exhibits were a highlight—walking through the decades made California and Oakland’s story feel much clearer and more connected. What stood out most is that everyone was genuinely engaged: the kids explored on their own (not just tagging along), and the adults were just as absorbed. It worked well for all of us at the same time.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Ages
Good for all ages, but younger kids will enjoy the science section the most. The history and art sections felt best suited for older kids (8+), which matched our experience. Walking through the decades of California/Oakland history helped everything click in a clear, connected way—great for homeschoolers or families who value contextual learning.

🎒 Bags, Food & Lockers
- No purses allowed, but jackets with pockets were fine
- No food or water bottles allowed inside
- Lockers available for belongings

♿ Accessibility
There are many stairs, but also ramps and elevators connecting all levels of the three museum sections. Wheelchairs are available. Security is present at entrances and throughout.

🚗 Parking (Important Notes)
There is an on-site parking garage, and you can pay inside or outside. Once you pay, you have about 15 minutes to exit.
⚠️ When the museum starts closing, everyone is pushed out at once, which caused a line to exit the garage—plan extra time.

⏰ Closing Time — Plan Ahead
Although it says they close at 5:00 PM, they begin closing everything around 4:45 PM. Bathrooms close, doors lock, and visitors are directed out. We didn’t even make it to the gift shop because we didn’t realize how firm this was.
‼️If anyone in your group needs the bathroom, go earlier—otherwise expect a long wait or to miss it entirely.

Overall: A really engaging, well-designed museum that works for meaningful family learning: kids and adults at the same time. Just plan your timing carefully near closing. Absolutely worth the visit.

We traveled in through the Amtrak Gold Runner partnership from Merced, and the museum staff were welcoming and accommodating to our intergenerational group, from elementary age students to seasoned community leaders. As an A-List member who visits AMC multiple times a month, this is completely unacceptable. This theater is in such bad shape that it’s embarrassing for a chain as large as AMC Theatres. The management here either doesn’t care or has given up entirely — and unless something drastically changes, patrons will start cancelling memberships or driving much farther just to avoid this location. The nearest clean options aren’t even close; you basically have to cross the bridge to San Francisco or trek to Walnut Creek or Fremont.

After tonight, I’m cancelling my A-List membership. I refuse to keep paying premium prices to sit in dirty, stained seats inside a theater that smells like it hasn’t seen proper cleaning or maintenance in ages.

AMC needs to step in, replace management, retrain staff, or shut this location down for a deep clean — because right now, it’s an absolute health hazard.

As you can imagine, when I went to the Alameda Cineplex to see Sheep Detectives, I was very hopeful that it would be a light-hearted movie to raise my spirits, even though I was devastated to be going alone. Unfortunately, when I got to the box office, they looked me dead in the eye, assessed my face very visibly, scanning top to bottom, and told me that I was apparently visibly too soft to handle the intense subject matter of the movie Sheep Detectives. After some light verbal abuse from all six employees and the manager commenting on my soft eyes and weak spirit that apparently manifested itself through my posture, I conceded to watch The Backrooms instead for a lighter movie that they deemed I could handle.

However, around 30 minutes into The Backrooms, I decided that it was not my cup of tea. Not all was bad about The Back Rooms, but  it was too liminal, and the character The Onion had an incredibly grating voice. Despite me being a large fan of the character Gorp, his presence was simply not strong enough in the movie to override my hatred of The Onion, so I decided to leave the theater and try to theater-hop into Sheep Detectives.

When I came into Sheep Detectives, the sheep were all crowded around Hugh Jackman's character, kicking him and beating him in order to initiate him into their gang. I was immediately drawn into the story. The leading sheep, played by Danny DeVito, was by far my favorite character. His dark and demented backstory really resonated with me, and my recent experience losing my job and my girlfriend and 18 dogs. Unfortunately, 13 27ft tall security guards each accompanied one of my ex's dogs, trained now as, fear sniffing attack hounds, all rushed into the movie theater and airlifted me out of my seat, while the dogs clung on me with their massive genetically modified jaws. They attacked me for my movie hopping, beating me relentlessly and throwing me out onto the curb. I can't type due to my lack of fingers on my right hand and lack of a left arm, so i am writing this using my new nuro-link, which gives me debilitating migraines when every i do a think. I have also lost one eye and 1.83 ears. I am currently writing this from the hospital where they charge 2,000,000 per ibuprofen on top of my massive other medical debts and other credit card debts accrued by my sensory deprivation tank addiction.

Side note: the movie popcorn hit hard.
Three stars.

top_reviews.content: I've run through this area nearly every day for the past decade.   It's amazing how many things have changed and how much has stayed the same.  Great animal watching, plant watching, and people watching year round, and at every hour.

I found the scenery beautiful, and saw some good birds while I was there, and some water birds. It was a pleasant experience.

With as populated as the Bay Area is, it can be more challenging than some might think to get a taste of nature without leaving the city. This takes me the Emeryville/Berkeley area where I had the opportunity in visiting "McLaughlin Eastshore State Park". There is no actual street address here but it is where University Ave. & W. Frontage Rd. meet. It is also about 1/2 mile from I-80 so it is quite easy to get to when traveling my car.

I had come here during the evening of Saturday 6/23/2022 at around 7:45pm. The weather was a comfortable 64°F while being crystal clear with no clouds in sight as well as no Bay Area fog for that matter. What makes this state park convenient is that they offer a sizable parking lot (which is free of charge) as well as several trash bins and a few porta potties within a mere 50 yards from the bay water and trails.

The hours of operation are from 5am to 10pm seven days a week. Since this is a protected open space preserve area, the park actually extends 8.5 miles along the East Bay shoreline from the Bay Bridge to Richmond, This includes tidelands along the waterfronts of Oakland, Emeryville, Berkeley, Albany, and Richmond. Since I-80 is a very heavily traveled highway, you can witness joggers, cyclists, and walkers exercising from a distance if you look close enough.

Since I arrive right before dusk to check out the sunset, I luckily parked a stones throw from the water, rocks, and sandy beach area. Since this area stretches a very long distance, it never seems super crowded as opposed to a way more densely popular park or bike trail. And if you arrive during the time I did, you can witness some of the most awesome sunsets in all of the Bay Area.

With the good things about this park, you also need to consider the not-so good things as well. On any given day, you will spot quite a few homeless people (in tents, sitting in cars, and even just sleeping on the streets). It is the grim reality of many that hit hard times. But for the most part, many people here are courteous and keep to themselves. I felt safe during my visit and was able to soak in some of that fresh bay air while enjoying a perfect sunset. With that said and done, I am going to give "McLaughlin Eastshore State Park" an above average four-star rating.

The bartender pointed us toward three guys who had just walked in, and after chatting with them for a bit, one of them offered to see if he could add a little surprise to our reservation.
That surprise turned into one of our favorite memories from San Francisco.
Later that night, we arrived at Bourbon & Branch and were escorted into Wilson & Wilson Private Detective Agency—the hidden speakeasy inside the speakeasy. We were treated to an incredible experience, a surprise tour, and when we asked for the check, the bartender smiled and told us our drinks were on the house. That's when we learned the person we'd been talking to at Rickhouse earlier that day was actually one of the owners.
Rickhouse was already fantastic on its own. The cocktails were exceptional (we're still trying to recreate them at home), the bartenders were welcoming, and the atmosphere was exactly what we love. But it's the kindness and genuine hospitality that made this experience unforgettable.
We'll never forget the afternoon that one conversation at Rickhouse led us through a series of unexpected doors—and into one of our favorite travel memories.

top_reviews.content:
This park is one of my favorites in the city 💚 It’s a steep hike up, but you’re rewarded with incredible views of the bay, the Bay Bridge, the Transamerica Pyramid, Salesforce Tower, Coit Tower, and Chinatown 🌉🏙️.

The nature in this little park is so beautiful: trumpet trees, lots of hummingbirds 🐦, colorful flowers 🌸, and little benches where you can sit and just take in the city views. On the other side of the park, you can see Alcatraz and the bay!

Yes, the climb is steep, but it is so, so worth it. And if you want to keep going, you can cross the street (just be careful, there’s no real crosswalk and cars come up fast). Keep climbing for even more views all the way to the top of Russian Hill. Or walk down one block and walk the Macondray lane (another favorite!).

One of those places that really reminds you how special this city is ✨❤️

As a beautiful place and green space, I give it a nice 5-star review.  However there are a lot of stairs with a high elevation gain/descent.  I can’t imagine anybody with any kind of walking handicap being able to enjoy this greenspace.    It’s pretty but taxing in your body.  Please be comfortable climbing 130 steps. 👍🏼

Ina Coolbrith Park is a forgotten hidden jewel of The City attached with a touching story of legendary American pioneers🫡 and it also has awesome views from Coit Tower, Alcatraz to the Bay Bridge and landmark downtown skyscrapers. The park is situated on 1715 Taylor Street what was once a steep and impassable section of Vallejo Street running downhill towards Chinatown in Russian Hill neighborhood.[*A few houses north from Coolbrith’s original home located at 1604 Taylor street that was destroyed in the 1906 earthquake and fire. It is said that although Coolbrith who is also a “cat lady” 😉escaped alive with her two white Persian cats and a female companion her personal library of over 3000 volumes of valuable books, correspondence, and her nearly finished manuscript on the history of early California literature were lost.😔]
The park is named after Ina Donna Coolbrith (1841-1928)(born Josephine Donna Smith, who was the niece of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints founder Joseph Smith🫡to my friends “Elder Murray” et al. from Utah whom I befriended at Chinatown church on Washington Street), a prominent San Francisco poet who became California's first Poet Laureate in 1915 during the Panama–Pacific International Exposition in San Francisco, who left the Mormon community with her mother (Née Coolbrith) as a child in 1851 after death of both her father and legendary uncle in the midst of prejudice, violence and persecution on a wagon train to Los Angeles, California, where she began to learn and write poetry. Although her personal life is sadly entangled with tragedies and poverty, Coolbrith managed to have published hundreds of works over a span of 50 years. More importantly, in order to support her family (her mother and sister who were sick then died in late 1870s) Coolbrith who was known to (if not admired by) many “big shots” figures including Mark Twain, Bret Harte, Joaquin Miller and John Muir had to work as Oakland’s first public librarian (and female imagine that) who mentored Jack London and Isadora Duncan who also lived or otherwise had ties there when they were teens. [* Note: Ira became an honorary member of the Bohemian Club, a rare feat in the history of that exclusive all-male San Francisco secretive private club that is also located on Taylor Street @ Post Street. "Weaving spiders come not here…"]
The park was dedicated to Ira in 1911 and a memorial plaque was placed in 1947. It's terraces and wooden staircases were carved from the hillside, creating a hidden garden effect similar to Greenwich or Gilbert steps (aka “The mother and daughter steps.”) Suggestion for following walking/hiking routes:❶Muni T-Chinatown, 30 (Stockton), 45 (Union/Stockton), 12 (Folsom/Pacific), 8 (Bayshore), 39 (Coit) walk up on Vallejo Street passing Central police station reach Mason Street climb up stairs to top of the park about 15 floors. {*The OA house (season 2 on Netflix) another City’s historic landmark is situated across the park on 1001 Vallejo Street.} ❷ Muni 30 (Stockton), 28 (19th Avenue) walk/climb up on steep Taylor street alone from North Point cutting through Columbus or Jones and Leavenworth about 25-30 floors. ❸ Muni 19 (Polk/Lombard), 49 (Van Ness/Mission), 30 (Stockton), 28 (19th Avenue) walk/climb up on Lombard then turn on Taylor about 40-45 floors. {If you choose to continue on Lombard it will take you all the way up to Coit Tower through Pioneer Park which would add on an additional 17 to 20 floors. You can then go back to the top of the Coolbrith park southbound on Taylor or via Vallejo at Mason from the bottom.}
Enjoy views of The City while appreciating our history and doing a little workout! 😉
“To its great City of the Seven Hills
And lo! The city bore Saint Francis’ name!”

What a gem! Super cool area tucked into a residential area. We visited close to sunset on a Sunday and the top of the rock was speckled with small groups enjoying the view. And what a view! The view from the top is beautiful. You can see the bay and San Francisco city and also Golden Gate Bridge. However, I would like to call out a few things that might help folks make their decision as to whether to visit or not - especially if they’re driving from far.

1) This place is basically a large rock that one needs to climb. Once at the top, you get access to this beautiful view. The climb itself is barely 5-10 minutes. There are stairs to do so. If you truly want to “rock climb”, you can take the non-stairs route and climb from one of the other sides. But if you’re not a trained climber and you are going to take the stairs anyway, this is barely a 5-10 minute climb.

2) While the view is beautiful, getting to this place is basically driving for several miles on hilly roads with lots of stops/traffic lights through narrow streets. The distance from wherever you live might not be much but it’ll be a slow drive due to how much you’d have to stop just to get here.

3) There’s no designated parking here as such. This is a residential area and you will have to park on the street. Finding a parking spot itself took us 10-15 mins. It might take more if you come during busy hours. The lanes are VERY narrow and a pain to navigate in a car.

4) The view itself is nice but maybe something that you can sit and enjoy for no more than 15-20 mins perhaps.

Overall, if you live in the area and don’t have to drive a long way to visit this spot or deal with parking, I’d totally recommend this spot. However, if you’re driving from a distance and if you will need a parking spot, it may not be that productive a use of your time and energy.

Cafe Strada in Berkeley: Hot Chocolate That Didn't Live Up to the Hype

If you're searching for the cozy cafe to spend a weekend afternoon in Berkeley, Cafe Strada may come up on your radar — but don't get too excited about the hot chocolate. Despite all the hype, it didn’t quite deliver the rich, indulgent experience you might expect from a café with such a strong reputation. The chocolate was decent, but nothing extraordinary.

The café, though, is a bustling hub of activity, especially on weekends. Expect to find it packed with students and those just chilling with friends. The ambiance is laid-back yet vibrant, making it a spot to catch up or get some work done. A friend introduced me to this spot, and while the crowd may be overwhelming at times, the environment has a certain charm. It’s a lively place where you can soak in the energy of the city, but if you're looking for solitude, you might want to come during the quieter hours.

So, if you're in the mood for a bustling atmosphere and a place to hang out, Cafe Strada won’t disappoint. Just maybe skip the hot chocolate and try one of their other drinks instead.

A favorite coffee shop of ours that we've been going to for years. When we are in town we always make it a point to stop at Cafee Strada's to enjoy one of their hot beverages. Hey friends! This review is about sustainability only.

I so appreciate your attention to detail when it comes to how folks here can use reusable mugs, and also limit their impact on the environment via plastic pollution.

The real silverware, the real glassware, the real mugs, the real spoon for the bowl of sugar, and the recycled napkins are an excellent touch!

That said, I was a bit disheartened to see how many people were enjoying their coffee to stay, but in to go cups. I understand that these to go cups might be compostable. But a quick glance into the recycling and trash bins shows that there is no delineation between the two. I wonder if there are ways that the barista can work clearly articulate the for-here option, by asking if people are staying to work or meet a friend.

I was also a bit disheartened to see the sale of plastic bottled water here. By 2050, there will be more plastic in the ocean than fish. And over 95% of the plastic that we try to recycle does not actually get recycled. But rather ends up in landfills, oceans, or burned in incinerators.

By now, there are tons of options for at least better water. Maybe aluminum canned?

Thank you for considering my feedback. All in all, I was impressed by your Sustainable offerings. Just would love to see some better communication to folks dining in, who would be able to skip the trash made entirely. Thanks again! Lovely courtyard too.

A decent spot for HK-style cravings in the Bay, but lacks authenticity

Review Content:
Shooting Star Cafe offers a variety of Hong Kong-style dishes that are somewhat hard to find in the Bay Area, but the execution is a bit hit-or-miss.

• Clay Pot Rice: The flavor is good, but if you order takeout, don’t expect that signature crispy rice crust (guoba) at the bottom. It loses its texture in the container.

• Chicken: The meat was very tender and flavorful, though there were quite a lot of small bone fragments to navigate.

• Beef Brisket with Rice Rolls: The taste was acceptable, but the portion of beef was disappointing.

• Sweet and Sour Pork: A bit too sweet for my preference; it becomes a little overwhelming after a few bites.

• French Toast: Disappointing as it lacked the expected crispiness and fragrant buttery taste.

• Coconut Sago: Just average.

Summary:
It’s a convenient spot that captures the "idea" of Hong Kong cafe food, but it still has a way to go before it feels truly authentic or "grounded." Good for a quick fix, but keep your expectations in check.

You need to come here with something in mind or else you’ll get lost in the menu. They have everything and everything is on the menu. I arrived early, so there were plenty of seats to choose from. In addition to the required 2 drink , per person, minimum (And they stick by that), we ordered the nachos, which were very good. The comedians were also pretty funny and there was really no bad seat.

If I wasn’t required to give a star, this would be 0 stars.

I received an email from Punch Line SF offering two free tickets and confirmed our attendance for Red Richardson on September 19. We hadn’t been to Punch Line in about a month and were looking forward to seeing the show.

I have a disability that requires strict dietary restrictions, and because of medication I had just taken, I could only drink basic tap water. After we were seated, I explained this to a staff member, who said he would notify our server.

When our server, Kat, came to the table, I again explained my situation and asked for tap water. She said she would bring it but that I would still be charged $7 for the Liquid Death water they provide. I explained that I specifically needed basic tap water and was dehydrated. She then told me that I was still required to purchase two drinks for myself and that my boyfriend had to purchase two drinks as well.

I explained that paying was not the issue. My boyfriend was happy to meet the two-drink minimum, but I was not going to pay for tap water that I medically needed. Kat laughed, told me I had to comply, and then said, “Let me get my manager so he can talk with you. I’m sure he will make you leave.”

This entire exchange happened while the MC was on stage, and it was loud enough that people around us were looking over.

The manager, Kim, asked me to step outside the venue so we could discuss the situation. I explained what happened and asked for Kat’s name, which Kim provided. Kim explained the two-drink policy and offered a reasonable accommodation: my boyfriend could purchase two food items and two drinks to satisfy the minimum, while I would not be charged for tap water. I accepted that solution. She also asked whether I was comfortable having Kat continue as our server. I said no, so she arranged for another server.

Unfortunately, when Kim returned inside and told Kat that she had lost our table, I could hear Kat laughing loudly and making racist comments about me. My boyfriend heard them as well. At that point, we decided we could no longer stay.

The replacement server came to take our order. I thanked her and explained why we were leaving. I also told Kim on our way out that we were leaving because of Kat’s behavior. There was no apology or apparent concern. Security also watched my movements as we left, which added to an already uncomfortable experience.

The issue was never about paying. It was about how I was treated when I disclosed a legitimate disability-related need. I understand that businesses have policies, and Kim did ultimately offer a workable accommodation. But the way Kat handled the situation—including laughing at me, refusing to identify herself, threatening that I might be removed, and the racist comments we heard afterward—completely ruined our evening.

The two-drink minimum is also a recurring complaint in the reviews, and I understand why. The prices are extremely high for food and beverages at a comedy club. Whether tickets are complimentary or purchased, requiring customers to spend substantial additional money to satisfy a drink minimum can make an already expensive evening even more costly.

I am an event manager and promoter and operate my own event business. I work with a large professional network, and many of my clients rent entire venues for their events. Because of this experience, I will not recommend Punch Line SF to my clients, use it for my own events, or choose it for my own entertainment.

Punch Line SF: do better.

I brought my niece who was visiting for her Spring break and we had ample time to write our love notes to San Francisco; hers about her first visit to a big city that she wants to get to know and mine about how I came here 20 years ago with no intention to stay - both were read on stage by the performers, creating a special memory for us together.

These people are so talented! What a great show! Would recommend and absolutely go back! We sat on the stage and our seats were amazing. I would love to see it again from every angle.

What I enjoyed most about the show were the acrobatics. I also liked how it incorporates excerpts from poems by local writers, giving the audience a glimpse into San Francisco’s culture and the ideas of some of its most influential thinkers from the early to mid-20th century.

The show begins by referencing the great 1906 earthquake and then moves chronologically through the city’s history, touching on milestones such as the LGBTQ+ rights movement, even featuring trans acrobats as part of the cast. By the end, I felt the production was deeply rooted in San Francisco and created by and for its community. At first, that local focus might make it seem less accessible to visitors, but it actually adds authenticity and charm.

I really liked the concept of blending world-class acrobatics with the city’s history, poetry, and culture. It’s a very unique experience, and I definitely recommend it.
