I was walking by at night and just happened to see a line outside of the theater. I didn’t know about the theater before so I walked up to see what the buzz was about. I ended up seeing “The Lunchbox” as they had one rush ticket left 2 minutes before the doors closed.

Well, that was a great decision to go in. I’m so glad I now know about this awesome theater! I am definitely coming back.

I went to see the Lunchbox which is a set in Bombay India. The music was awesome and the acting was beautiful.  The talented voices rang out. I loved it. Not allowed to take pictures with my phone but I took one picture of the set which was also very creative with a moving stage. The underlying theme was about women and their role in the family.

Attended the All My Sons play at the Berkeley Rep. I'm so glad I did.
This was our first time the theater has great staff.
Took BART from the city a quick trip. Exited at Downtown Berkeley and walked to the Addison Street access.  It was a quick left and only steps to the Berkeley Rep.
Picked my tickets at will-call no problems.
The play was fantastic.

Berkeley Repertory Theater is a jewel in the East Bay and in America.   Berkeley Rep is recognized as one of the finest regional theaters in the country.  It puts on quality productions with the best creative teams and actors in the world.  You can see new productions of older and recent plays as well as brand new productions of plays that have never been presented before.  In some of these cases, the theater acts as an incubator for shows that will go on to Broadway and London and other venues.  It deserves your attendance and financial support.

Berkeley rep is an asset to the community. It’s such a wonderful experience. Both theaters are fairly small and yet they managed to get superb talent.

They have fostered new shows that end up going to Broadway.

They are minutes from the downtown Berkeley BART station.

They offer a wide variety of baked goods: bread, cookies, donuts, bagels, pies, cinnamon rolls, empanadas, sandwiches, cupcakes, cookies, cakes. They also offer frozen doughs and breads. My GO-TO bakery.
For like EVERYTHING.
For 7 years straight.

My faves: the fruit/cheese danish, the cheese scone, the buttermilk biscuits, the cheesecake, I mean, my bday cake was from here.

Kinda pricey, ngl. But very worth it. If you are gluten-free & want tasty baked goods.

They also now have a stuffed bacon, egg and cheese bagel that’s amazing.

Follow me on IG: @freshdotdaily

3.5⭐️ Selection: insane, prices kinda high even for gf but not atypical..but doesn’t match the taste, which was only ok.

There must be over 60 different gf items in this bakery! Some are other packeged brands, most are theirs.

We tried a few things and they were ok good but nothing I need to return for. I’m a decent cook/baker so I know how good gf bakes can taste. I will say the vibe and setting is GREAT. Lovely spot with some seating indoors and out and an airy design.

The white bread🍞was pretty good but again, a pretty straight forward gf bread. The best selling cinnamon bun🥮wasn’t as moist as I’d expected given moist is one thing gf CAN do well. It was a bit cakey and the icing was too sweet. I realized it was just a sugar icing vs the classic and expected, WAY tastier cream cheese style icing. That was a big miss for me which could’ve made this scrummy, as Mary Barry would say😉

Of course prices as elevated for the gf part and most seem pretty on par with the market. Bigger things like full cakes and cobbler trays were overpriced I thought.

Check it out once. And if you’re easy to please (like most here giving a 5⭐️review) or celiacs and don’t bake or have kids, you’ll love this place!
I love this place where everything is gluten free! I buy fresh, hot food & get a bag of goodies to go home with! This location is so much easier to find & get to than their ferry building location!

I’m happy that Mariposa Baking Company exists and has a great selection of dairy-free and gluten-free treats.

top_reviews.content:
Absolutely loved The Game Parlour — genuinely one of my favorite places we visited while in San Francisco.

As someone with celiac disease, finding places that are not only safe but also fun and genuinely exciting to eat at can be difficult, and this place absolutely delivered. Everything being gluten-free immediately made it feel more relaxing, but what really surprised me was just how many options they had. It was honestly hard to choose because so much of the menu sounded good.

There were two of us, and we ended up ordering three items to split because we wanted to try multiple things, but the portions were way more filling than we expected. The waffle sandwiches especially were substantial, and combined with fries and drinks, we were struggling to finish everything by the end — definitely not a complaint!

Beyond the food, the whole concept and atmosphere were just great. It’s part board game café, part restaurant, and it created such a fun, welcoming environment. They had board games, cards, games for purchase, and what appeared to be rentable/playable games as well. Even in the middle of the week around lunchtime, there was a nice mix of people there — some working remotely, some grabbing lunch, some hanging out and playing games. It really felt like a community space.

The owners/staff were also incredibly kind and patient while I asked a million questions trying to decide what to order because there were so many things I wanted to try. They were genuinely helpful and welcoming throughout the whole experience.

The space itself was comfortable too, with nice bathrooms and what appeared to be outdoor seating for warmer weather.

Overall, this is exactly the kind of business I love supporting: inclusive, social, community-oriented, and safe for people with dietary restrictions without making the experience feel limited or boring. I truly hope they continue to thrive because I would 1000% go back and already want to return next time I’m in San Francisco.

Spent a few hours here on our last day visiting San Fransisco. Was very busy and we felt lucky to get a table. Big selection of boardgames with welcoming staff keen to help with our decision making. Great coffee, chicken waffle sandwich was delicious, served quickly and came with the best fries we experienced in San Francisco. TGP was fairly noisy when we visited but that's to be expected as there were gaming events happinging at the same time. Great place that I dont hesitate to recommend.

Also, they have a great catalog of games to play with your friends if you want to make this into an outing. The food there is also delicious and to the best of my knowledge It’s all gluten-free, which is great for me and I’m always gonna shout that out in a review so other gluten-free people can find it. Definitely recommend checking this place out.

Food was SO good! All gluten free- waffle sandwiches and crispy chicken dishes. It’s also a place to go play board games, so we happen to visit when there was a competition. We had an hour to eat, I wish we had longer but it was nice to see all these people gather together.

Perfect hangout place to chill and enjoy the company of your favorite people.

And the atmosphere is the best part. I really like it, plus the many board & card games you can play. It’s better to go in groups but two people can also have fun.

Every role is filled with an undergrad who has no authority to make any decisions, so they “have to talk to their manager” about every single issue that comes up, and then 100% of the time they say they can’t do anything to help you. If you ask for the manager’s name to follow up, they tell you they “do not have the authority to disclose that information.” This is university bureaucracy at its finest - petty tyrants making terrible policies and then hiding from the public rather than actually making good decisions and being accountable. She was actually manning the bar with her regulars while we were there, keeping the energy high.

My siblings and I would go swimming and our great uncle would be near the men at the picnic tables taking a shot and giving us change for the snow cone truck. At 15 no more parks for me and my family lived on 37th and Webster across from Moss wood. I will always love this park . precious family memories. The baseball field is gone. Today so many White People at the Park. When I was growing up all Black hard working folks. Our visit today was for Patricia Lowe..Queen of Line dancing..

An area asset. Historical importance can't be understated. I met in the old house building just yesterday to action against unjust coal plans in Oakland. The legacy of protest is alive, but we should haveadw more progress. Don't forget the history or the struggle.

On Saturday, June 20, 2026, I ate at U :Dessert Story for my birthday.

We went there a little bit after 5 pm. The place wasn't busy at all. There were a few people eating there.

Here's what we ordered. The Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast, Chocolate Volcano Bingsu 🌋 and Mango Stick Rice Bingsu. The Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast was hands down one of the best desserts I've ever eaten. The orange Egg custard sauce was delicious and the Brick Toast was warm and soft. The vanilla bean ice cream on top was the perfect addition to this dessert. Hands down the best dessert out of the 3 we ordered and definitely a 5 out of a 5! The Chocolate Volcano Bingsu was good. It wasn't knock your socks off good like the Salted Egg Yolk Brick Toast but good overall. The chocolate flavor was lacking in my opinion. I wanted it to taste more like chocolate and have more of a chocolate pronounced flavor but it didn't. The chocolate flavor was mild at best. There were bananas, cocoa krispies, corn flakes and brownie chunks throughout the chocolate volvcano. I can see why a lot of people order this dessert because the presentation is cool. It's pretty big and it comes out with a dry ice cube on top that makes it look smoky and foggy to simulate a volcano that just erupted. Cool concept. The mango sticky rice Bingsu was my least favorite. The mango chunks weren't ripe and were hard. They didn't taste good or have good flavor. The sticky rice which was green tasted okay but not so great. The condensed milk on the side was super sweet and made the dessert taste somewhat better. But overall the mango sticky rice Bingsu was a failure. I don't recommend ordering this dessert.

Even though the mango sticky rice Bingsu wasn't good, I would still come back and try more desserts. I would try another Brick Toast and some other chocolate desserts that sounded good on the menu.

I came with friends for dessert one evening, but it was a bit disappointing overall.
When we arrived (a little late), all the toast items were already sold out. The staff didn’t inform us beforehand and just let us sit down, which felt quite unprofessional.

The regular cakes were average — nothing special. The shaved ice (bingsu)was less sweet than I expected, which was actually a good thing for me, but it was served in very basic, low-quality dishes that didn’t match the café’s supposed aesthetic or price level.

The biggest disappointment was the Thai Tea Mille Crepe. The sauce was not smooth at all — it had clumps and felt very sweet(looks like curry?). I still finished it, but the next day I suffered from severe diarrhea. I strongly suspect the sauce and cream in the Thai Tea mille crepe were not fresh.

Lesson learned: it’s probably best to avoid dairy-based desserts here in the evening.
Will think twice before returning.

Second time here & the quality of food + service were amazing both times :) I know everyone comes here for the bingsu but don’t sleep on their pastries! They make them all from scratch in-house. The chocolate matcha lava cake is SUPERB. Instead of chocolate oozing out, it’s matcha flavor filling. A bite of the cake, matcha filling, matcha ice cream and cookie crunch… heaven :)

Also, the wings were honest to god, some of the best I’ve had. The crunch is unreal & flavor was so good. The batter they coat the wings with was perfectly spiced. We got the wings with sauce on the side so the crispiness was at peak level.

Can’t wait to come back again!

Their packaging changed recently and it’s bad. No more sealed drinks. They packaged my drinks in a to-go bag. When I was already gone, I noticed the bag was dripping. They spilled. They don’t put any cup holders in the bag to hold your drinks… The worst part is…
The boba was UNDERCOOKED. It was HARD.

Disgusting.

I visit this spot every time I want to treat myself after completing a stressful semester. Every time I get the mango sticky rice toast and it’s absolute perfection! It comes with a side of pandan coconut sticky rice and mango sauce, but I always ask for the coconut sauce instead because the coconut sauce is better, and traditionally mango with sticky rice is served with the coconut sauce, not mango sauce. I tried deviating for my usual once, and I ordered the salted egg yolk toast and I wasn’t impressed. 4 stars because it is pricey, and the mango sticky rice toast should be served with coconut sauce.

Live Oak Park is a nice city park with a mix of amenities and spaces for meeting up with friends. There are several distinct areas for different activity types, and this park is especially popular with families.

Between Shattuck and Walnut Streets, there is a green space for groups and families to hang out. There are some nice trees and an idyllic stream where you can catch nature vibes.

Directly south of the lawn and separated by the stream, there is the Live Oak Community Center and Live Oak Theater for community events and performing arts. This side of the park contains playgrounds, basketball courts, and tennis courts. The playground amenities are much better for older children than toddlers. The varuous ball courts are in decent-but-not-amazing condition.

Across the street (between Walnut and Oxford), there is a smaller park "Area 2" with some picnic tables and a grill. There isn't much green space on this side, but you can visit the Berkeley Art Center while here. I recommend stopping by if you are visiting when the Art Center is open (12pm-5pm, Fri-Sun, free admission).

That’s not just shady, that’s credit card FRAUD. This bartender was unprofessional, dishonest, and clearly had no interest in doing his job. First time at this bar and definitely the last. If you go here, watch your drinks, your tab, and your receipt. He clearly thought he could get away with it and probably has. this place used to be THE spot for midweek karaoke, and now karaoke is every night, meaning it might be the spot for weekend karaoke too! i don't think it has thus transformed into A Karaoke Bar though, even if it is one per se. (note: this is legally correct use of "per se", whether you like it or not.) it's kind of an offbeat-but-earnest divey vibe, which hasn't changed over the years — i find this comforting. usually i just go to hang out with my own group of friends, but it is very common that i will end up chatting a bit with someone new, and everyone is always very kind and very cool. it's an eclectic crowd made up of nonetheless normal and genuine people. years ago, i thought the bartenders didn't really like me because they were making me weak drinks (i always tipped well, in case that's what you were thinking). i kept going anyway. now i feel like that problem has been fully corrected, although that might just be because my tolerance is dropping now that middle age is approaching on the horizon. i do see some reviews mentioning bartenders being rude, and for what it's worth, i've never personally had that experience. management also seems to be handling these situations appropriately. but the thing is: i kind of don't want to go to a bar where someone hasn't complained about a rude bartender? that's how i know a spot has character. a metaphor: this bar shares the name for a soldier in a core unit of the ancient roman army, but when you arrive, you will be greeted by a sign reading "cead míle fáilte", which feels like an ironic juxtaposition, especially for someone like me whose family came from ireland through scotland to the united states. rome never openly attempted to conquer hibernia (their name for ireland), but they did exert a proto-colonial type of influence over the region, primarily through christianity. however, catholicism came to be a defining aspect of irish identity, especially during the troubles. small aspects of gaelic paganism survived even into my own family's traditions by being fully wrapped in a christian coat. now these things are inextricable; culture is messy like that. and in that respect, the name kind of works. that's this bar — it's a lot of things, and they weirdly fit together into being a special little community. the reason i have to withhold a star, even though (in case you haven't figured it out by now) this is my favorite bar is that the drinks... are fine? this is mostly a review of the experience, but drinks are a part of that experience, and they're honestly whatever. they're good enough! it's the memories and fun times that keep me coming back. objectively, it's a four out of five. but subjectively... well, everybody knows it has a perfect score in my heart.

North Beach Playground History

I've lived in North Beach for over two decades. Back then, the playground's official name was "North Beach Playground," and it was a bit behind on maintenance. Then, when the great Joe DiMaggio passed away, the city decided to rename it. The story goes that the Hall of Famer's estate did not take kindly to the fact that his name was associated with a rundown playground. So in 2005, the city completed a $7.5 million renovation and significantly improved the facilities.

The park is a great place for all in the neighborhood. Families can bring their kids and take advantage of the kids' playground. There are tennis, basketball, and Bocce courts, a public pool, and a multi-use community building with table tennis tables available for all.

Many people might not know that Joe DiMaggio grew up in North Beach and played baseball in the very same area where the playground now stands. His legacy and connection to the community made the renaming and renovation even more meaningful. The park is a recreational space and a tribute to the iconic baseball legend who became a local hero.

The playground is also home to some interesting public art pieces, including murals depicting scenes from DiMaggio’s life and career. This adds a unique cultural and historical layer to the park, making it a place for physical activities and a spot for reflection and appreciation of local history.

Moreover, the playground is beautifully integrated into the North Beach community, surrounded by charming cafes, bakeries, and historic landmarks. It's a place where you can feel the vibrant spirit of the neighborhood, whether you're taking a stroll or engaging in a friendly game of Bocce.

The Joe DiMaggio Playground is truly a gem in the heart of North Beach, blending history, culture, and recreation in a way that enriches the lives of all who visit. Whether you're a local or just passing through, it's definitely worth a visit to experience its unique charm and significance.

There is a huge climbing dome with sideless bottomless slide, a climbing merry-go-round, a spinning cup, bucket swings, a swinging meets teeter-totter (so much fun!), and a mosaic fish sculpture that you can climb in and on.
The play structure is on a higher level of the play area and is accessible by a ramp or amphitheater-style steps has two slides (a spiral and a double), steps, ladders, a sliding pole, a bridge, activities, a small and climbing wall. The double slide is long and goes from the structure through the amphitheater-style steps to the lower level of the playground. Nearly all of the flooring at this park is astroturf.

I think this place has potential, but it could really benefit from better maintenance and a few layout improvements. The pinsetters feel a bit dated, and there were a couple times where pins weren’t set properly, which can be frustrating during a game.

The approach area is on the tighter side, and the seating layout isn’t the most practical. It would help to have a table in the middle so there’s somewhere to put personal items instead of everything feeling cramped.

The Qubica scoring system also felt a bit slow and laggy at times, which adds up over multiple games.

One thing I noticed as well is how the waitlist is handled. When it’s busy, allowing current bowlers to add more games can extend wait times for others. It might be worth tightening that up to keep things moving more efficiently.

For comparison, Earl Anthony's Dublin Bowl is only about 10 minutes away and is a far superior place to bowl. It has more lanes, updated equipment, and is noticeably better maintained even while still running original A2 pinsetters.

Overall, it’s still a decent place to bowl, but with some updates to maintenance and a few adjustments to the setup and management, it could be a much better experience.

A jewel in San Francisco.

Belmo Café – A Rare Bakery Gem Worth the Journey
At last—we’ve found a truly exceptional bakery. Belmo Café is an absolute treasure, offering baklava of every kind imaginable, each one crafted to perfection with delicate layers, balanced sweetness, and rich, authentic flavor.

The Cheese Board is a co-op that started as a cheese store, but now also has a beloved bakery and pizzeria (next door). If you are visiting Berkeley, you must stop by the Cheese Board.

The bakery is one of the best all-around bakeries in the area -- other places in the East Bay may specialize in a certain type of baked good, but the Cheese Board can make everything well (especially if it has cheese!)

If stopping by for the bakery, you must try the signature cheese roll. Otherwise, there is a rotating selection of breads and pastries, some of which were "invented" in house and have special names (wolverines, zampanos, chocolate things, etc.). The bakery items are continually made throughout the day.

While waiting in line for the bakery, you can also get a selection of cheese and prepared sauces. The $25 Adventure Bag contains a good choice of random cheeses, and the green hot sauce is also tasty as a condiment/dip.

You can buy par-baked pizzas to finish baking at home. The pizzas are always vegetarian and change every day. If you're just visiting, you can get a baked pizza at the pizzeria next door instead. The pizza is the best pizza in Berkeley.

Everything you can buy here is delicious. You can't go wrong with any of the food choices.

---

For first time visitors or a casual stop, I recommend buying a cheese roll, seeded baguette, and any pastry that tickles your fancy.

For a more substantial amount of food to bring home, I recommend a pizza, a 6-pack of English muffins, the green sauce, and a cheese Adventure Bag. The green sauce usually goes well on the pizza.

Staff here are very friendly, knowledgeable and helpful.

A great variety of cheeses are available here, with 3 flavors available to try each week. They offer plentiful amounts of sheep and goat cheeses as well more common cheeses as well.

Service is quick but doesn't feel rushed. Store is very clean and well presented.

Great stuff.

Peña Pachamama is definitely a unique experience in San Francisco, especially if you enjoy vegan food, live music, and South American culture. The entire menu is vegan or plant based, and they had a lot more options than I expected, which was great to see.

We ordered the Raw sampler and the Andean sampler. The food itself was good and flavorful, though I’ll admit I was a little surprised by the portion-to-price ratio. The plates were $30, and from the descriptions I initially thought they were more “shareable” style platters with multiple items for the table. In reality, they were more individual-sized entrees with a few different components on the plate. Still good, just a little expensive for what you get.

What really made the night memorable was the atmosphere. They had live music and traditional Peruvian dancing during dinner, which gave the whole place a really warm, cultural vibe. It felt more like an experience than just going out to eat.

Overall, I’m glad we went and I would absolutely come back again. If you’re vegan or plant bases or somply looking for a different kind of dinner spot in San Francisco with live entertainment and Andean-inspired food, Peña Pachamama is worth checking out .

I'll be returning soon to try the rest of the menu

I really, really wanted to love this place as I always support local vegan businesses whenever I am traveling and want them to thrive, but I left feeling so disappointed. I was expecting a much more reasonably priced menu considering the vibe/atmosphere, but was surprised to find that it is priced more like a fine dining establishment. And the quality did not live up to the price either. I was also surprised that there weren’t any appetizers on the menu for one person besides a single empanada and chips. I came alone for happy hour (which is supposed to include beverage and empanada discounts) only to find that I was charged full price for my wine and empanada. Again, if the quality was good I wouldn’t have minded being overcharged, but it just was not very good. Not to mention it smelled absolutely awful in there, like a very old and musty home. I had to eat really fast just so I could get out of there. I’ve been to hundreds of vegan establishments all over the world and this is the first one I’ve been to that was so far off on price vs quality/atmosphere. I’m from NYC and have never seen such high prices for a fast casual restaurant (even raw/vegan/organic ones). But maybe this is common in SF and I just don’t get it!

Cedar Rose Park is a popular park for families and groups. It is a large open green space along the Ohlone Greenway, best suited for laying in the sun or casually meeting up with friends.

On the Rose Street side, there are two tennis courts and four pickleball courts. On the other side of Cedar Street (in Crystol Red Park), there is also a basketball court and racquetball court.

Cedar Rose contains two small playgrounds for toddlers and young children. The park is popular with dog owners due to the large lawn.

There is one grill and picnic area on the main lawn that is usually occupied. There are also a couple of extra picnic tables near the Cedar Street playground. Most parkgoers tend to picnic and play in the main lawn.

There is one single-occupant bathroom structure located on the Cedar Street side.

a review from @amom2kidsandapark

This Berkeley park is one of the many parks and green areas along the Ohlone Greenway, a walking/biking,running path that starts all the way down near downtown Berkeley and connects with the Richmond Greenway Trail in Richmond.
This park offers two playgrounds, a grass area, picnic benches with bbq, basketball, tennis and volleyball court, a small amphitheater, and sidewalks for biking and walking. The grassy area is really sunny as most trees are on the outer rim.
The larger play area has a structure, standard swings, and a tire swing. The structure has two slides (a double and a spiral), steps, ladders, a bridge, and activities.
The smaller play area is completely enclosed and has a large bridge with tunnels underneath, a play structure, a teeter totter, a climbing turtles a swing set with two buckets swings and a standard swings and steps that lead to nothin (😅 seriously why are they there??). The structure is made of wood and has two slides (a tube and a double), steps and a very low inclined climbing wall.  This area is perfect for toddlers!
There are bathrooms here and street parking was easy. The different sports areas are separate from the grassy area and play areas. You’ll have to cross a street to get to them. This park had a lot of day “campers” but nothing felt that made us uncomfortable.

top_reviews.content:
Typical East Bay regional park, complete with classic EBRPD trail layout which go directly up the steepest parts of a hill. I don't know who or if anyone plans these trails, but it sure seems like their motto is "The shortest way from Point A to Point B". We started at the Stonewall-Panoramic trailhead off of Claremont Ave, which has almost no parking, you're fighting with residents and other hikers to find a spot. We got there around 8AM and still had trouble parking. Narrow winding road, parallel parking on steep inclines, cars park 2 inches from your bumper, fun stuff!

The trails we took were nice, again the start was extraordinarily steep, right off the jump you go from resting HR to max effort. The trail network is bracketed by Claremont Ave and Grizzly Peak Blvd. There are nice spots for panoramic vistas of the Bay, and some flatter trails as well. The views are the best reason to visit this park, it's just a bit of a headache to park and the steepness of the trails is annoying. Good wildflower displays in spring.
No parking? Two lane winding road.  Beautiful drive.  Overlooking the San Francisco Bay Area.  Court tower and the bay and Golden Gate Bridge’s can be seen.  No cell service in areas.   Hiking trails

I love watching the sunset from here, it's amazing. During the day it's excellent to hike for the views alone. I highly recommend visiting at least once and taking a good camera. Lots of incredible views and trails. The trails have numerous steep parts, so bring water and good trail shoes.

Great park with challenging hikes and fantastic views. There are trails here that ascend ~1,500 feet - all the way to the base of Tilden Regional Park. It’s a park I frequent when weather permits (which fairly often) for the hikes.

I’ve seen all manner of wildlife on trails in this park: Coyotes, deer, prairie dogs (or at least that is what I think they are), rabbits, rattle snakes, lizards, etc… but haven’t had any issues.

Gorgeous view of the city and the bay from the preserve! The best view points are close to different trail heads around  Berkeley, the Berkeley Overlook Vista Point and a place marked as Pano. However, those segments of the trail are also the steepest so definitely be prepared for some strenuous climb.
The trail east of Panoramic Way is significantly quieter with much less foot traffic but also you are getting away from the best views and getting into the woods.

top_reviews.content: Been here too many times to not leave a review. Perfect spot for date night, girls night or an outing with friends.  Creative cocktails, amazing service and the atmosphere is even better in person. Music always on point. From NYC to cali- let’s go!!

We enjoyed the DJ and the music selections were amazing! Food was very limited...I think the kitchen was close to closing time... so we ordered off of the not main menu but the happy hour. Beef Empanadas and the stuffed Plantain which was yummy. We had 3 Caribbean Pineapple Old fashions and I am not a newbie to Old Fashions and have an understanding of mixology...When I say strong I mean strong. The flavor wasn't bad but the entire drink was a bit over powering for the palate. We did have some trouble with our waitress...maybe it was just a long night for her...but she didn't seem like she wanted to be there in all honesty. The ambience is very nice and the live music will probably be the reason we return... I suppose we could get there earlier and try the regular menu next time. Bathroom was acceptable and overall it was a good experience. Prices a bit steep but everything is steep these days especially in the area.

Sobre Mesa is a refined and welcoming restaurant that offers a memorable dining experience built around great food, elegant ambiance, and warm hospitality. From the moment guests enter, they are greeted with a stylish and thoughtfully designed interior that creates a calm yet upscale atmosphere. The lighting, seating, and overall layout are carefully planned to make every visit comfortable, whether it’s a casual meal, a family gathering, or a special celebration.
The menu at Sobre Mesa is one of its strongest highlights, offering a diverse selection of dishes prepared with fresh ingredients and attention to detail. Each dish is presented beautifully and delivers well-balanced flavors that appeal to a wide range of tastes. From appetizers to main courses and signature items, the restaurant focuses on quality and consistency, ensuring that every plate meets high standards. The culinary team clearly emphasizes freshness, creativity, and taste in every preparation.
Customer service at Sobre Mesa is equally impressive. The staff is polite, attentive, and professional, always ready to assist guests with recommendations and ensure a smooth dining experience. Their warm behavior adds a personal touch that makes customers feel valued and comfortable throughout their visit.
Cleanliness and hygiene are maintained at a high level, contributing to a safe and pleasant environment. The calm music and relaxed vibe further enhance the overall dining experience, making it ideal for both intimate dinners and social outings.
Overall, Sobre Mesa stands out as a premium dining destination that successfully combines delicious food, excellent service, and a sophisticated ambiance. It is a place where guests can enjoy quality meals and create enjoyable, lasting memories with every visit.

The menu is so beautifully conceived, but the execution is mid. Basic items like the black beans were very under salted. We tried about 60% of the menu items, and there were some good flavors. But almost everything needed more salt. The cocktails are good, and the service was solid. The plantains were great. But for expensive small plates, I’m gonna need the flavors to pop a LOT more.

I watched Chef Nelson on Top Chef, so I was excited about my daughter, Rhonda taking us a party of 4 to Sobre Mesa in Oakland. We had reservations, the wait wasn't too bad for a Friday night. We were finally seated in the front left corner that seemed big for a party of 4. I did comment on that, but we were seated and we ordered drinks and looked at the menu. The food  and astmosphere were good. We were still eating our food and the waitress (hispanic) came and told us there was another reservation and we needed to hurry. That ruined it for all of us. Here's the problem, nobody advised us there was a time limit when we were seated. The waitress brought our food, but she didn't check with us to see if we needed anything. I paid our bill which was about $400.00. The other 3 left the tip. I was extremely disappointed that the food and atmosphere were ruined by the service. Chef Nelson needs to fix that as instead of having a good restaurant, he could have a great restaurant!! I used to be a waitress in my younger days and for me the service was more important than the food. I don't know if I'll go back as that really bothered and hurt me. I'm not trying to be a problem, but I hope Chef Nelson will remember what it took for him to get to where he is. A restaurant is only as good as the service that is provided to the customers that come in and come back to support your dream!!!!!!!

"Delicious french toast & hearty egg & sausage plate ✨ suburban rainforest vibes"

name: Apple Cinemas Van Ness IMAX
address: 1000 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States

google.name: Apple Cinemas Van Ness IMAX
google.address: 1000 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States

top_reviews.content:
Back after almost a year and I guess nothing has really changed.

- you are told to have your online code ready for your ticket only to have to go to a kiosk to print out a physical ticket. Like why not just have the person sitting down at the bottom of the escalator scan you in.

- hot offerings at concessions are depressing. Not even a soggy hot dog?  Also if you want good popcorn you’re gonna be sorely disappointed.

- also it’s just vacant as hell inside. Everyone’s caught on that this theatre is just not it.

- the guard rail in the front row is way too high lol

- also walked into the theatre to one of the worker’s just spraying the seats without even wiping them down. So there’s just a bunch of wet seats. Super cool.

Sad to see that this place isn’t looking very promising. Wouldn’t be surprised if this place closes down within the next couple of years and becomes a bunch of overpriced apartments.

—————————————————————————————

I’m giving this place five stars PURELY for its potential, not for the actual experience.

Number one: this place just opened so totally get the need to figure out everything.

Number two: with all things considered, kinda think some systems need to be put in place to make sure this place runs a little more smoothly.

Basically came right at opening. Barely anyone working here ( I’m sure staffing is challenging)

Couldn’t find anyone to check my ticket. Couldn’t find anyone to take an order for snacks. The theatre was dark when I entered it. It felt like a scene out of the twilight zone. Again. Not mad, just saying that to make peoples’ first impressions better, maybe open when you can at least meet some baseline requirements. I know it’s hard to start something new but people judge far too much on first impressions.

Anyways, best of luck. There’s a lot of potential to make this place great.

Great new theater that recently opened! Very clean and welcoming employees who care! Came for the Tuesday deals of $7.50 / movie.

Maria at the entrance was kind and gave us 50% off concessions and tickets up to 10/31!

Lucy was very helpful to us in helping us as we booked tickets online but didn't get the discount. She was kind and patient in helping us. Habeeb the manager was able to assist us as well and was very kind and they both definitely had customer service first attitudes!

There were a lot of theaters and I appreciated the maps outside of them guiding you onto the seats.

I appreciated the self serve popcorn and you could set your own butter. Everything was clean and new.

The seats themselves were new. Not reclining so not as comfy as they didn't go back as much. The aisles were also not too wide so not the most spacious leg room but doable for a movie.

Sound was great as well and screen was clear!

Overall a great experience, cheap, clean and great employees!

Okay, I’ll admit I was skeptical when Apple Cinemas took over the old AMC on Van Ness. We’ve all been burned by “new and improved” theaters that somehow manage to be worse than what came before. But damn, they actually pulled it off. First time walking in, I was genuinely surprised. The lobby doesn’t feel like the usual sticky-floor movie theater vibe. It’s got this cool industrial thing going with the brick walls, and the escalator setup is actually pretty slick. My friend made fun of me for taking a photo, but whatever - it looks good.
The IMAX theater is insane. Look, it’s spread across 7 floors which sounds like a pain, but the escalators work and there are signs everywhere. I’m directionally challenged and even I figured it out. The whole place just feels… maintained? Clean bathrooms, no weird smells, screens that aren’t covered in mysterious stains. Basic stuff that somehow a lot of theaters can’t manage.

Hidden gem theater.
Great location. Great seating. Great AV quality for standard screenings.
They ought to advertise, honestly.

I only heard about this place a couple weeks ago and finally made it to see Supergirl today.

Unlimited popcorn.
Great tuesday matinee discount prices.

Only complaints are they need hotdogs on their menu and that I wish I had heard of this place sooner.
And you can hardly tell it exists from the street.
Again, you gotta advertise a little. I wasn’t even sure I was at the right place until I went inside.

And, they have all this water saving equipment in their bathrooms for some reason, and you just end up using more water to rinse the soap off your hands and for the toilets to flush anything than if they just had normal sinks and normal toilets. I thought that we, as a society, had already learned our lesson on this failed “savings” gimmick. I guess not.

Everything else is good here.

I had a really wonderful experience. Everything was easy, smooth, and enjoyable from start to finish. I watched the movie and truly enjoyed it. Special thanks to the manager, Julia, for being so kind, friendly, and helpful throughout the whole process!

"Excellent service, great environment, loved the atmosphere."

Love this place, except the under-the-highway location. I wouldn't take my dog here-- yuck! But I do visit the playground as it's not completely under the freeway/train. top_reviews.content:
The best escape room I have ever been to!

Our group of 8 did “The Attraction” room and it was so immersive! The challenges were diverse, and not repetitive in any way so each piece of the puzzle suited different skills. You really have to work as a group to get out in the 2 hr limit.

Located quite literally in the Palace of Fine Arts building this is a must do group activity!

10/10 recommend!

This was hands down one of the most memorable experiences of our entire California trip.

We came as a family of five with three kids (ages 3, 7 and 10) to celebrate our oldest daughter’s 10th birthday, and choosing the Edison Room turned out to be the perfect birthday gift.

What impressed us most was that every single family member could participate. Even our 3-year-old had little “missions” and felt like an important part of the team. Our 7- and 10-year-olds solved plenty of puzzles, while the adults had enough challenging moments to stay fully engaged. I’d definitely recommend having at least one puzzle-loving adult in the group, but that’s exactly what makes it such a rewarding family experience.

The puzzles are incredibly creative, varied and satisfying. Nothing felt repetitive or cliché. Every new discovery made us smile and made us want to keep exploring.

What made this room truly special, though, was its educational value. It’s much more than an escape room—it’s an immersive journey into the world of Thomas Edison, inventions, electricity, innovation and the spirit of discovery. On our way home we spent another hour talking with our daughters about Edison, his laboratory, the history of electricity and how great inventions changed the world. That’s something we definitely didn’t expect from an escape room!

A huge thank you to the entire Palace Games team for creating such a thoughtful experience. Especially to Andrew for his thoughtful advice which room to choose, and AJ who was incredible hands-on game manager at the place. It was worth every penny and became a birthday our daughter—and all of us—will remember for many years.

We have done 3 rooms here, all of the rooms are the best of the best. "The Attraction," is truly amazing. I doubt I'll ever find an escape room that well designed and elaborate ever again. The staff is always great. Important note, drive through the pay parking lot to the parking right in front of the entrance. :)

The most fun escape room I’ve experienced! The right balance of challenging puzzles and teamwork for our group of 6! I think 6-8 people is the perfect number - a smaller group might find the teamwork portion hard to complete. Highly recommend!

Had an awesome experience with a group of friends (6 total) in the Houdini room. The production value was seriously impressive, and the puzzles were fun and challenging. They seem to dole out hints at the perfect rate to get you moving if you're seriously stuck, but let you work through things on your own when you want. Can't wait to come back and try the others, kudos to the designers and the very friendly staff.

top_reviews.content:
A grassy field, stage, and benches are present at this park, which seems to be designed for events or occasions.

This is a brief walk away from the Downtown Berkeley BART station and two parking lots. It's directly across from the Berkeley City Hall and near some other government buildings. There are events frequently in the park or near the park. There isn't a playground for kids or restrooms. There are a few works of public art which help to make it look nicer. Some restaurants are nearby and this could be a place to sit if you take your food to go. There is a farmers' market every Saturday on one of the streets that border this park.

The park itself seems to be a place where homeless people congregate during the week. On weekends there are other activities taking place and seems more family friendly. This Saturday we saw a farmers market and on Sunday attended a Lowrider car show on our way to get donuts nearby. An awesome find, we talked to the team from Vajitos Bikes and they were great!

Wide open space in  the central plaza of city government facilities. A bit rundown from near constant occupation since its opening decades ago. But still providing the desired effect of grandure for the municipal complex

Awesome first time experience! The Fried Lobster with Garlic Noodles was out of this world. Mac&Cheese with Lobster was to die for...I am looking forward to next year being bigger and better! Thanks for the memories...
Nice quiet park some lady yelled every 5 minutes but was harmless cool climbing trees nice place for a dog walk

top_reviews.content: Classy, elegant and relaxing atmosphere. A memorable experience for sure. The service was so good, and the drinks were perfect. I recommend trying a Vesper here because they absolutely nailed it. Will definitely be coming back next time I’m in town.

We came to The Red Room since we were staying at the hotel for the night. We really enjoyed the atmosphere at firs…the cocktails were great, the bottle of wine was excellent, the smash burgers were delicious, and the live music created a fun vibe.

Unfortunately, the experience took a turn when we noticed a cockroach crawling on the wall directly behind our table. We immediately pointed it out to our server, who simply said, “Okay, I’ll take care of it.” However, nothing was done. The roach continued crawling around behind our table for another 15–20 minutes.

We mentioned it a second time, and the server told us he would “handle it when they close.” That response was honestly shocking. A cockroach in a dining area should be addressed immediately, not left to continue crawling around near guests while they’re eating and drinking. We ended up moving tables but it was still crawling around.

The server did offer us a complimentary drink, which we appreciated, but it didn’t make up for the lack of urgency or concern regarding cleanliness. It’s disappointing because everything else about the evening had been enjoyable. I hope management takes this seriously and addresses both the pest issue and how situations like this are handled in the future.

Fantastic bar that emanates history and class.  High ceilings, rich redwood paneling, original Gustav Klimt paintings, and elegant seating all heighten the experience.  Drinks are excellent, and our waitress was friendly and attentive.  There was a terrific live jazz ensemble when we were there on a Thursday evening.  Definitely worth a visit!

This bar was lovely. The elegant entrance, leading to a high-ceilinged space accented with stunning Klimt-inspired artwork, immediately captivated me. The drinks were excellent, and the burgers and truffle fries were absolutely delicious.

While the service wasn’t the best—requiring effort to get the staff’s attention when needed—they were attentive and helpful once they noticed us. They could intentionally look around for customers' needs instead of chatting with each other. Additionally, the round tables we were seated at by the wall felt rather small for a group; larger tables would have been more comfortable.

Despite these minor issues, I still give it a 5 out of 5 because the overall experience was fantastic.

Hands-down, my favorite bar in San Francisco. Classy, classic, sophisticated, stylish and yet low-key. The bar is something to just simply marvelous. The etched glass, the under lighting just gives it such an cool speakeasy vibe. The drinks are great, the only place that makes a Chocolate Martini that I actually enjoy. The hosts and the bartenders are awesome, and the lobby is just a thrill to be in with incredible furniture.

top_reviews.content: This is the good stuff! We found them as Ippuku was partnering with them for dessert but unfortunately, that’s now concluded. They have unique in house made flavors which change weekly that you won’t find anywhere else!

The best gelato place I've ever been to. They are innovative with their seasonal flavors (which actually taste good and aren't just different), and their usual flavors are also phenomenal. We come almost every week. Our favorites are muscat grape, Arabic coffee, watermelon, and the best, walnut (it blew out minds).

By far my favorite gelato place in the universe! I have visited this place multiple times. The seasonal fruit flavors are always punchy and intensely flavored—for example, the pluot king and watermelon gelatos taste like the best, most condensed versions of the fruits themselves. I found out today that one of the founders graduated from a gelato university in Bologna, which explains a lot.

Tip: you can get two flavors in the regular cup. I always pair a fruity flavor with a darker or creamier one. Pictured here is the strawberry and black sesame; calamansi lime and fiordilatte (background).

Great ice cream, usually super friendly service. Advice to management: be sure to adequately train staff on adjusting speed to meet demand. There did not appear to be any sense of urgency as the line extended out the door and progress remained glacial (pun intended); staff actually appeared oblivious to the wait time. If the staff has limitations making them unable to serve customers that have been waiting patiently since well before closing time, those customers should be given sufficient warning in advance, not after having already waited 20 minutes.
Such good gelato, the best one we tried in Berkeley. They have unique seasonal flavors and they hand make their waffles. We will be coming back for this next time we visit.

top_reviews.content: What a gift to the city! You can tell the folks that own and operate Free Gold Watch value FUN! I love the line-up of pinball machines~ a vast array from the good old days to the most modern. It’s quirky and human-centric, and a fabulous way to spend a day!

As a pinhead, I wanted to share what a cool place this is. Machines were in great shape. Lots of unique pins for the connoisseur. They have all the latest, hard to find machines, with a great collection of EM's that I really enjoyed. Met the owner, who was great. And the staff were solid as well. Big fan overall.

This place is awesome!! I am not a pinball aficionado, but I can't help but feel like any pro would be happy here.

Plays seem to be about $1 across the board with one monthly $0.25 machine and some other non-pinball games.

They also have some snacks and a screen printing service?!

I don't know how to describe this place other than a warehouse of pure, concentrated fun.

Try the old school 2v2 pong. If you've never tried that CRT-analog dial control, it's a very cool sensation if you're only used to digital inputs.

The BEST — play for all ages, incredible selection of pinball and other games, from latest and coolest pinball machines that you never knew about — try the Godzilla! — to old school and retro games that are good clean fun in a retro and playful atmosphere.  No-brainer for any day of the week, or particularly when Carl is in town

Great selection of machines, most in excellent condition. I appreciate that events can be held in the back and silk screening is offered. However, the machines are a bit sensitive to bumping, especially in crowded areas. I chose to play in less congested spots after experiencing that. Overall, it's definitely worth supporting this hidden gem!

I have been wanting to come to this museum since last year. My dad was a pilot for Transocean Airlines. I found out about this museum and their collection of memorabilia from the museum folks at the SFO museum. I thought it was a pleasant experience and the kids that were visiting were obviously very excited about flying. Looks like Father's Day this year will be a terrific day to come visit since they will have a lot of events planned.

Highly recommend and a hidden gem!! Tucked away behind the Oakland airport, this museum should definitely a perfect stop for you and or family or destination. They have a variety of aircraft, great gift shop and courteous staff. Very reasonable priced and they also partner with cool events. Will definitely be back soon, thanks and had an Awesome time!!

Really cool opportunity to see aircraft across the years.  From some scale models to replicas to actual aircraft.  Very low key but enjoyable.  I would've loved to see the inside of the flying boat passenger plane, but that was a separate guided tour we didn't have time to do during our visit.  A couple videos, history of women in aviation, and pieces on Amelia Earhart were a few of the many interesting exhibits

Fun place for anyone who loves fighter jets, and appreciates the history of the older and retired craft.
The president of the Museum was able to give us a tour and was very informative with all the exhibits.
The outdoor portion is home to an F-14 Tomcat!!!
If you love fighter jets, this is a great place to start.

Great cocktail bar. It was themed with "The Shining" for Halloween when we visited.

top_reviews.content: Francisco Park is a beautiful and well-designed neighborhood park with amazing views of the Bay. The walking paths, open green spaces, and modern playground make it a great destination for visitors of all ages. Everything is clean, well maintained, and thoughtfully planned. Francisco Park in San Francisco is a wonderful place to spend time outdoors. From Reservoir to Recreation

Francisco Park is located on the corner of Bay and Hyde Streets in San Francisco. Its interesting history mirrors the city's development and community spirit. Initially, this was the site of the Francisco Reservoir, which was constructed in 1860 and decommissioned in 1940 after the Lombard Street reservoir was established.

The reservoir served as a critical water source for the growing city. However, by 1940, it had become obsolete due to advancements in the city's water infrastructure. Over the following decades, the site remained unused and largely forgotten, becoming an overgrown and fenced-off area entirely contrasting with its vibrant neighborhoods. In the late 1990s and early 2000s, when I worked at the Civic Center, I used to walk home through or along this location and wonder why such a precious piece of real estate was left forgotten and unattended, but that was not the case, of course!

In the early 2000s, residents and civic groups started pushing to turn the forgotten site into a community hangout. After years of planning, fundraising, and battling red tape, Francisco Park opened its doors in 2021. The park's all about lush greenery, walking paths, playgrounds, and killer views of the Bay, Golden Gate Bridge, and Alcatraz. It's a testament to the power of people and the city's willingness to save and reuse its historic spaces for everyone to enjoy.

One of Francisco Park's nice features is the dog playground, a dedicated space where dogs can exercise and socialize off-leash. Designed with both pets and their owners in mind, the playground features secure fencing and shaded seating areas. It provides plenty of room for dogs to run freely and play while promoting responsible pet ownership through well-maintained facilities and clear rules. This addition to the park enhances its appeal as a community hub, encouraging interactions among dog owners and contributing to the overall vibrancy and inclusiveness of Francisco Park.

A Hidden Gem Between Chinatown and the Financial District

St. Mary’s Square is one of those places you might pass by numerous times without realizing how interesting it truly is. I did just that for years! I walked by it from different sides many times and never took the opportunity to walk in, look around, and learn more about it.

At first glance, the park appears to be a standard city park, but it’s actually a rooftop plaza, redesigned in the 1950s by landscape architect Robert Royston and built atop an underground parking garage. The square has served as a community gathering place since the mid-1800s, although the atmosphere back then was vastly different from today’s calm lunchtime scene.

In the late 19th century, this area was part of a notoriously rowdy section of San Francisco, filled with saloons, brothels, and opium dens. It became so infamous that the leaders of Old St. Mary’s Cathedral, located directly across the street, carved the phrase “Son, Observe the Time and Fly from Evil” onto the cathedral’s clock tower—clearly intended as a warning to those lingering below. The 1906 earthquake and fires devastated much of the surrounding neighborhood, creating an opportunity to reimagine the space as a public square rather than a problem zone.

Today, the park is notable not only for its location but also for its artwork and historical significance. The most prominent feature is the 14-foot statue of Dr. Sun Yat-sen, the founder of the Republic of China, created by renowned San Francisco sculptor Beniamino Bufano. This tribute is significant; Sun Yat-sen spent considerable time in San Francisco raising funds and support for his revolutionary efforts, and this square was one of the places he frequented during his years in exile.

More recently, the square became home to the Comfort Women Memorial, installed in 2017 to honor the victims of wartime sexual slavery during World War II. This memorial adds another thoughtful and reflective layer to an already meaningful space.

With its layered history, public art, and peaceful setting above the bustling city streets, St. Mary’s Square is an excellent place to grab a coffee, sit for a while, and quietly take in one of San Francisco’s most fascinating corners.

One of my favorite parks to visit in San Francisco. It tends to be quieter and calmer than others, and it’s slightly hidden away from the main Chinatown area (I actually discovered it on accident). That makes it a great place to chill and relax amongst the hustle and bustle of the rest of the city. It is simultaneously on street level and on rooftop level thanks to being on a hill, and harbors views of 555 California Street, 333 Bush Street, the Hartford Building, and the Russ Building. The park is right next to the California St cable car line, which is very convenient. There is also a parking garage underneath the park. Overall, 5/5.

top_reviews.content:
A must-visit place for anyone living in the area (4/5 Green Stars)
Bring cash! That’s the first rule of Schmidt’s Pub. Maybe it’s the only rule! I’ve been coming here a bit more regularly, lately – more visits in the last year compared to the previous decade, in fact. Now I wonder what I was waiting for.

According to the East Bay Express, Schmidt’s Pub is “basically your living room, but better” – that does sum it up, except that very few of us have living rooms anything like this, with a cozy fireplace surrounded by comfy armchairs and rustic tables beside sunny windows. Not many of us have living rooms with Old Speckled Hen on tap, or populated with an entertaining parade of quirky folk and friendly dogs. If the people and dogs are not entertaining enough then pick up a copy of Calvin and Hobbes or A History of Clay Pipes (okay, I made that one up) and have a little retreat with a pint.

4/5 Green Stars for social and environmental impact, based on these factors:
•	Beer on tap (transported in reusable kegs) has a much lower footprint compared to bottles or cans.
•	Allows you to bring your own food, which is good for folk like vegans who are often more comfortable with BYO.
•	The snacks available at the counter could be a bit more Berkeley (or Albany)! They were mostly from big corps – Lays chips (PepsiCo) and chocolate bars from Mars. Would be nice to see a more imaginative/ethical selection.
•	A great community space with an inclusive atmosphere. Schmidt’s is home to many groups (e.g., knitting) and provides a second family for many, some who send postcards from their trips!
•	Finally, we shouldn’t underestimate the importance of having a place to slow down, reflect and connect with each other a little. In that respect, Schmidt’s Pub is worth its weight in gold.

Schmidt's is a rare anomaly. A cross between an English pub, a bed and breakfast and the living room of cultured intellectual. Where else in the East Bay can you enter a 100+ year old house, choose from a selection of ales, lagers and stouts on draft and in bottles and cans and an assortment of fine tobacco, cigars and smoking accessories, sit down in a chair with a wooden table and read something, including the books on the shelves? Truly a wonder. And if you do purchase a cigar, you can smoke it outside. I wouldn't be surprised if people discuss Proust here. Cheers!

Absolutely a cozy spot to smoke and enjoy a community vibe.  Cash only slowed me down…I didn’t want to leave this gem.

I ordered their iced pistachio latte, and genuinely my jaw dropped when I took the first sip, because I wasn’t expecting it to taste that good. They use a very high quality spread that tastes like the nut itself, and adds a sweetness to the drink that does not overpower the coffee at all. It’s perfect. I noticed a lot of coffee use pistachio syrup for a pistachio flavoured drink, which I personally despise. But Heyma use a spread that really enhances the coffee. Going here is an experience, transporting you to a different place and culture. As a Middle Eastern girl myself, it is officially one of my favourite coffee shops in the world.

Been going to Round 1 for years but never been so disrespected by the staff as I have here. I was visiting last weekend and went to the Stonestown Round 1 to see if they had any good prizes at the exchange since I had ~16,000 tickets saved up over the years and my local Round 1 doesn't have many good prizes.

I chose a locked up prize worth 10,000 tickets and had to fill out some paperwork for the exchange. They swiped my card and the screen showed the purchase. I filled out the paperwork, handed it to the staff and asked if there was anything else I needed to do. The woman behind the counter told me "No, my manager just needs to sign it" and walked away to help someone at a different counter. I stood around for around 30 seconds, not sure if I needed to be present any longer but couldn't get her attention while she was busy. I figured the transaction was complete so I took the prize and walked out to my car— I had an appointment to get to soon, a gift from the family member hosting me while visiting SF.

Just after I got back to my car and started navigating, I got a phone call. It was the manager at Round 1, demanding I return immediately. He said he needed me back to "verify my tickets are legitimate". I explained I was visiting and had an appointment to get to, etc, that they had my member card information if they needed to verify anything like that. That I could email them any more info if they needed something since I really didn't have time to spare. He said that his staff said I swiped the item and took off after she told me I needed to wait for the manager, and he told me that he'd report me for stealing the item if I didn't return.

I reluctantly hurried back and got the counter. I handed my card over to the staff (again) and she swiped it, looking to her screen and pressing something on there to pull up my transaction history. She swore up and down that they'd "tried refreshing it like 6 times" but that it didn't work before. She went to get her manager who did me the kindness of showing up after 4 minutes before proceeding to stare at the screen and scroll through year after year of every time I earned tickets at round 1. He did this for a few more minutes, saying nothing to me, not looking at me, before signing his part of the paperwork and saying "Thank you" to me before walking off.

After all the hassle he'd put me through, the stress of knowing I'd be late to my appointment, that I couldn't do my family the decency of showing up to an appointment on time, after threatening to report me as stealing his merchandise, he can't even look at me and give me a simple apology for the difficulty. For making me trudge back to fix his mistake since he clearly hasn't trained his staff to communicate clearly, all so he could swipe my card again since I guess there must have been something wrong with it on his end the first time. So he could idly look through my years upon years of visits to Round 1 after having insulted me and called me a thief.

I peeked at the screen while he was going through my history. Seems over the years I've spent more than $1200 at Round 1, but no more. Absolutely baffling that someone in his position could lack the most basic semblance of customer service skills, it's no wonder his staff are incompetent.

top_reviews.content:
**A Must-Visit Dive Bar with Character and Cocktails**

Specs is the kind of place that reminds you why dive bars are the heart and soul of a city. Nestled in the bustling streets of San Francisco, this local gem offers a vibrant, eclectic atmosphere that keeps guests coming back.

The cocktails? Simply excellent—crafted with care and never lacking in quality. The bar’s interior is a sight to behold, an unmissable stop for those who appreciate quirky, history-soaked decor. From the walls lined with artifacts to the dim lighting that creates the perfect laid-back vibe, every detail feels intentional.

One of Specs’ standout qualities is its incredibly mixed and diverse crowd, creating a welcoming space for all. And yes, even the bathroom deserves a mention—it’s truly unique in its own way, adding to the charm that makes this dive bar unforgettable.

My coworkers and I spent an afternoon hanging out here recently, and it was nothing short of a fantastic experience. Whether you’re a local or just visiting, Specs is a must for anyone looking to enjoy great drinks, good conversation, and an atmosphere that feels effortlessly cool.

Cheers to Specs! 🍸

---

We just ducked in here to get away from the cold. I had a great old fashioned here that was quick but perfectly done jack daniels mix.

It was just a quick drink but the atmosphere was so good and friendly. The patrons were all ages and did not make old me feel out of place. It was fun.

I have been coming here for over thirty years. And . . . it . . . hasn’t . . . changed. Well, they take cards these days. Otherwise, not much. The floor still flexes when you go back to the Hostel-style bathrooms (where privacy is a foolish notion and sanitation is an open question).

I continue to find some nook or cranny that holds yet another fascinating item I never saw before (or, perhaps, forgot about). Come for the reasonably-poured drinks, friendly conversation, great people watching, and stay for the Saltines and cheese?!?! Yep. It just works.

I get the connection to Vesuvio. But I find that place to often be overly packed and often annoying (not the place, but the tourists who flock in after doing the requisite alley pictures and bookstore noodling). When you can go there and it is not packed? The slightly more affected kissing cousin to Specs’. But, if forced, I will always choose Specs’, even if it, too, can become a humid mess of humanity at peak hours on warmer days. Thing is, it seems to save itself by being tucked away in that little half-alley. Almost like a force-field.

I still have a matchbook that says “Takes No Guff.” I still miss the regulars, now passed, who used to occupy the same seat every time I would infrequently visit, and who would regale you with tales of the old days. But the building feels like it still retains those things in trace form. So, while every visit is a new experience, there is still something that reminds me why I came here the first time, years ago. That’s reason enough for me to already be planning to come back again the next time I am in town.

A rare instance where an ‘institution’ deserves the moniker, likely in multiple senses.
A true Beat dive bar, they used to call it “crossing the river” from Vesuvio to the this place. Don’t come here if you’re looking to be coddled. That’s part of the charm.

Welcome to the “old San Francisco”, a place that  represents how San Francisco used to be. Unique, a little worn, with its own character, a bit corky AND !!! Where the bartender knows the regulars by name and where the bartender gives regulars preferred treatment. That means you might have to wait a bit longer to get served- as the bartender asks the regulars if they want a refill- without them having to ask. The crowd is eclectic to  eccentric. Young and old. Specs is ALWAYS good for a surprise- and also still a place people go to talk to strangers instead of making love to their cell phones. One of my favorites: the bar snack. A nice chunk of cheese cut from a wheel.

I’m grateful for this place.

The bartenders here are especially kind and personable. I always look forward to interacting with staff here.

They check IDs at the door, so be ready for that.

I prefer to resolve incidents like this offline as I hate to make negative feedback public, but I have contacted the restaurant directly several days ago and received no response about the incident below and I am sharing my experience here on Google so other customers may be aware and choose wisely.

Incident: My party of 7 came to Mad Oak around 5pm on Monday evening, 7/20. I did not have my ID on hand as I didn't realize I needed it for entry. I was not planning to consume alcohol. The staff member in charge of the outdoor entry let me in anyway after a little bit of friendly back and forth.
One of our friends arrived later and similarly did not have their ID. The same staff member turned them away very rudely and dismissively. I went over to the staff member to let him know that our friend was with us and I also did not have my ID. He responded very rudely despite all members of our party being very respectful. He replied me saying, "What did I tell her?! What did I tell her?!", without explanation.
Our friend who was turned away identifies as they/them and without explanation from the staff member, and inconsistent application of rules pertaining to ID, I suspect it might have been a situation where our friend was unfairly discriminated against for their appearance.

To sum it up, it was not clear that IDs were required for entry otherwise I would have prepared my party ahead of time; the staff member inconsistently applied an already unclear rule; he did not explain why one guest was allowed and not another, even in the same party; and lastly, he was unnecessarily rude.

Our whole party ended up leaving Mad Oak to go somewhere we could all be together.

In my outreach to the restaurant a couple days later, I asked for a response to let me know that they have addressed the issue and there has been no response to date.

Such a great place for casual trivia and a beer with friends. Went on a Tuesday night and was surprised with how busy it was — tons of good energy paired with an expansive outdoor patio (don’t forget your jacket though, it got cold!) made for a great evening.

Otherwise, things were great — especially the expansive beer and cider menu. We also ordered the nachos, and they were well received by everyone.

One last thing to know — the place cleared out immediately after trivia was over, so expect to pack up and head out by 9:30pm.

came here to watch game 7 spurs/thunder. for some reason the roof was $10/person, so it took us a while waiting on drinks but eventually the group i was with (5 ppl) got a spot to sit and enjoy the game. at halftime, I went and ordered food and a few more drinks - as the 3rd quarter started, we were told our table was being reserved for 6:30 (it was already 6:40) and would need to leave the table. 5 minutes later, the group comes and we get kicked off the table despite not even being able to finish the food or drinks we just ordered. out of curiosity, we asked the arriving party what it took to reserve the tables - $100/table, probably less than the 5 of us had spent on drinks+food, and there were at least 5 or so additional folks being displaced by this as well. the place was still crowded, so effectively this made us throw half our food out, finish our drinks standing, and leave to go find somewhere else to watch the game we showed up there for.

very strange experience. i've seen the warriors win a few championships here, used to really recommend it, but probably won't be back. i don't think i've ever written a review before, but if you are going to turn your picnic tables into a VIP section, I'd recommend maybe 1) letting folks know well before that the table is reserved, 2) directing "reservations" to the roof, which was already reserved for people who wanted to pay to enter or 3) maybe charging more than $100 and compensating the people being affected with a drink or something? it seems insane to effectively be able to kick a group out of a table in the middle of a game for less than what they had already paid for food + drinks

Around six months before we got married in Berkeley in August, we started reaching out to possible welcome party venues for the night before the big day. We wanted to find a place that would allow for outside food at a reasonable cost, provide quality drinks for a fair price, and has a nice access-controlled event space on premises. As someone who has run a number of large events previously, I know well that this task can be somewhere between tough and impossible. The minute one uses the term “wedding” to any vendor, costs can go way up. Or venues can charge exorbitant fees for space reservations, or have minimum spends that are crazy. And, honestly, it is really hard to simply find venues that allow for outside food.

So we started the search, and emailed venues throughout the East Bay area (Oakland, Berkeley, Emeryville, Albany, Alameda), At first, the only possible venues I could find were craft brewing establishments. The one with the best location for us charged a lot for space reservation, and for a space that was not access controlled, and without our own dedicated bar. So, in effect, we would be paying thousands for a craft beer spot to a few “reserved” signs on some random tables for us. Suffice to say, we were starting to get discouraged.

Then, after another internet search, I found a listing for Acme Bar in west Berkeley. Having never been there before (it has been a few years since I have lived in the East Bay), I asked around and realized that it’s a pretty cool bar with good service and great drinks. We checked in out in person, and was pretty impressed with the available event space. But our greatest surprise was when we actually emailed Acme, and got to know the owner of the bar. She must have had a previous life as an event planner or something, cause she was amazing. The prices she quoted were quite fair, and she helped identify possible outside food vendors that met our needs. She helped arrange special drinks for our event, which ended up being really tasty. The beer selection we ended up having was top notch as well, as was the wine selection. We arranged for our own dedicated space on a Friday evening, with our own bar. She helped identify our needs for us, and went out of her way – along with her great staff – to ensure we had a great event.

Some of my friends are quite experienced with events, and others are pretty hard to please, and everyone had a great time. The price quoted was on target, and there were absolutely no surprises, price-wise. I have never been more satisfied with a venue, or had a better event for the price. Working with Acme was, in two words, both fair and fun. We highly recommend working with them – you will not be disappointed.

We hosted a large milestone birthday at Acme Bar and Co and I can’t say enough about it. The team was so amazing and kind and easy to work with in the planning phase. Our guests loved the venue - the flow from the main bar to back patio to back building is great and creates 3 distinct and intimate feeling zones. The day of bar tender staff were great. Cocktails superb. We created a dance floor inside at the end and it was nothing short of perfect. 10/10 — highly recommend this place for any party or event rental

top_reviews.content:
I went to 924 Gilman Street last night for a hardcore show, and it was honestly one of the most beautiful, heartwarming experiences I’ve had in a long time. My partner used to go to Gilman 20 years ago and really wanted me to see it.
All of the bands were indígena, and the energy was just through-the-roof positive. Before the second band started, they played norteño and were like, “We’re proud of who we are and where we’re from. ICE can’t take that from us.” It was so powerful. One moment people were dancing bachata, and the next it turned into hardstyle two-step.
It made me so proud to be Chicano,and so proud of our young ones. You could really feel how important hardcore is. Arms flailing, incredible twirls, cartwheels, roundhouse kicks, playful punching. There’s a kind of radical freedom in hardcore that’s so rare to witness.
When the show ended and we were driving home, I looked at my partner and said, “Wow… that venue has probably saved so many lives.” An all-ages space, no drugs, no booze, shows happening constantly,it’s no wonder it’s such an institution. It creates room for people to safely be themselves.
Definitely my favorite place in the bay. So worth visiting.

- Multiple bars (one per floor)
- Friendly, helpful bartenders
- Great rooftop seating

The bad:

The location isn't the best but there's not much to be done about that except plan accordingly. There's nothing else around there and it's a 10-15min walk from West Oakland BART.

There's no coat check so plan for that as well.

Which brings us to the glaring flaw: the security team. I've been to two events here and both have staffed the same snobby, pushy and overreaching security guards who seem out to make your life more difficult.

We (four people) arrived at the venue via Uber. The second we stepped out of the vehicle, a security guard told us we needed to have our IDs ready (we were nowhere near the line and did not intend on going in until the rest of our party arrived). He saw me with a can of soda and told me that he couldn't let me in if he saw me drinking in front of the venue. On our way to leave the block and get as far away from him as possible while we waited, he shouted at another group that they couldn't stand on the ample sidewalk.

When our party arrived, we got in line to enter. One of my friends accidentally got out his French ID which prompted a different security guard to say he "was really hoping he was gonna get the chance to kick him out" before my friend retrieved his passport.

I organize and run bar events. I get that bar patrons are not always the easiest to work with. In this case 1) there was no crowd 2) we were sober, attentive, and listening 3) this is not the first time The Continental security team has seemed absolutely done with their job at the beginning of the night.
