google.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
google.address: 1570 Stockton St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States
google.description: Bustling Italian eatery with varied pizza options from coal-fired to Roman-style, plus beer on tap.

top_reviews.content:
Tony’s Pizza definitely lives up to its reputation for quality. The fresh ingredients really stand out, and the New Yorker pizza was outstanding. The crust was perfectly cooked with an incredible crispness that gave every bite great texture without being overdone. You can tell they take pride in using high-quality ingredients.

The service was very friendly, although it was a bit slower than expected. It almost felt like our table was just outside our waitress’s usual service area, so there were a few longer waits than we’d have liked.

The prices are what you’d expect for California, but the quality of the food makes it worthwhile. If you’re looking for exceptional pizza made with fresh ingredients and a perfectly crispy crust, Tony’s is absolutely worth a visit.

Tony’s Pizza Napoletana is absolutely worth the visit. The pizza was outstanding, with fresh ingredients, a perfectly crispy crust, and incredible flavor in every bite. The menu offers a great variety, and everything was served fresh and beautifully prepared. The staff were friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. One of the best pizza experiences I’ve ever had—I’ll definitely be back the next time I’m in San Francisco!

Decided to walk down to Tony's on a Sunday while visiting San Francisco. For whatever reason, I showed up early - and I was glad I did. There was a line 1/2 block long and I arrived 10 minutes early before the place even opened! Soon, the line was practically down the end of the block. I figured - wow 😲 this place must be amazing! I was seated at the bar which was fine. Bartender greeted me pretty quickly and provided me a menu. The menu was pretty extensive. I decided to try the gluten free deep dish Detroit style pizza with sausage. It took over 45 minutes to receive the order. The pizza was very average. I honestly don't think sausage was even on it unless it was so finely ground that it melted into the crust. The crust was dense and chewy and honestly felt overcooked. Overall, I felt it wasn't worth the $27 I spent. I did like the atmosphere; it was very busy with a lot of activity and conversation among patrons. Nonetheless, I would go back next time I'm in SF and try something else to see if my opinion improves.

It was a great pizza restaurant in San Francisco’s little Italy neighborhood. It is rare to find coal-fired wood style pizza these days and they have it.  We had garlic breads and the coal fired wood pepperoni thin crust pizza. It was delicious like New York pizza and the portion was generous. The server was attentive and friendly and the restaurant is warm and vibrant. Please make sure you join their waitlist on line beforehand and check-in with them when you get there.

Tony's Pizza is an icon in the pizza world. They are rated as one of the top pizza spots in the entire country, and for good reason. Instead of focusing on just one style, they feature a wide variety of pizzas to pick from including New York, Detroit, and coal fired options. I'm a sucker for a good New York pie, and I found theirs to be delicious and absolutely massive. The garlic cheese bread was also tasty, and came with a delicious agave dipping sauce that I've never seen before but became a big fan of. The food does take a while to come out, but it's worth the wait. Service was super friendly as well. Also, heads up that they get super busy regardless of the day and time that you visit. I highly recommend getting on the virtual wait-list way before you arrive in order to save yourself potentially well over an hour of waiting for a table.

reviews_snippets.content: "We got Caesar salad, bbq wings, lemon pesto sun-dried tomatoes chicken pizza."
"Ordered the Paulie Pizza, and the combo spicy regular calamari."
"Awesome service, awesome staff, awesome food and awesome atmosphere."

name: Jack London Square
address: 472 Water St, Oakland, CA 94607, United States

google.name: Jack London Square
google.address: 472 Water St, Oakland, CA 94607, United States
google.description: Restaurants & bars surrounding a lively 1800s waterfront, plus a bike trail & kayaking.

top_reviews.content: Great place to spend. Free boat for Alameda - a great facility and experience. Nice food, drinks, parking area..music, what not.

Jack London Square along the Oakland marina is one of those places that quietly grows on you over time. Years ago, this was part of my regular Capitol Corridor commute — a transfer point between sides of the Bay and just another stop in a busy schedule. Coming back now with a camera in hand, it feels completely different.

The marina has a calming rhythm: boats gently rocking, reflections on the water, and that open Bay light that changes by the minute. It’s a great spot for photography, especially around sunset when the sky and water start to mirror each other. The mix of modern waterfront and historic character gives it personality without trying too hard.

What really stands out for me is the nostalgia. Returning years later brought back memories of those commute days, but in a much more relaxed way. Now it’s a place to slow down, walk the promenade, and enjoy Oakland’s waterfront vibe.

If you’re in the East Bay, it’s worth spending some time here — whether for photos, a stroll, or just to sit by the water and take in the scene.

Went here on short trip to Oakland! The place was ok nothing much to do over there but we went before 5pm and didn't know nothing was open before 5pm. Was trying to eat and enjoy the views but restaurants were closed so go after 5pm. Beautiful area tho.
A hip and lively locale with seaside town type vibe. A nice little way to spend an afternoon.
Nice place to hangout out  and take a boat ride to sf from here.

reviews_snippets.content: "Pricy but good seafood, good service, friendly staff."
"I love this place, the weather, scenery, people, restaurants, etc."
"Beautiful area, great food, cocktails, shopping & vibe."

name: Super Duper Burgers
address: 721 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

google.name: Super Duper Burgers
google.address: 721 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States
google.description: Counter-service chain outpost using local ingredients in its burgers, fries & organic milkshakes.

top_reviews.content:
Super Duper Burgers is one of the best fast-casual burger spots in San Francisco.

The burger is simple but done right. The beef patty is juicy, well-seasoned, and has a nice char that gives it extra flavor. The bun is soft but holds everything together perfectly, and the fresh toppings make a big difference.

The garlic fries are a must. Crispy, garlicky, and honestly one of the highlights of the meal. Pair it with a milkshake and you’ve got a perfect combo.

The vibe is casual and busy, especially during lunch hours. It’s not a place to relax for long, but great for a quick, satisfying meal.

Prices are a bit higher than typical fast food, but still reasonable for San Francisco.

⚠️ It gets crowded, and seating can be limited during peak times.

Overall, a solid choice if you want a high-quality burger without going to a full restaurant.

👉 Check my profile for more food spots and travel tips.

Stopped by Super Duper Burgers for a casual lunch and ordered their organic egg sandwich along with the signature garlic fries. The sandwich was fresh, satisfying, and packed with flavor, while the garlic fries were definitely the highlight—crispy, cheesy, and incredibly appetizing. The ingredients tasted fresh, and the overall quality stood out from a typical fast-casual burger spot. Great option for a quick bite in San Francisco. Would gladly stop by again! 🍔🍟😋

Delicious fresh handmade burgers and crispy fries ❤️🍔, hypster and modern style spot👍🏼. Very clean! All crew where nice and had rapid service. I would just recommend to lower a lil bit the music. It seemed it was a disco  (glad they had bose sound system because at least it sounded good quality 😬) but i came to have a tranquile meal, not to be pushed to put noise cancelling headphones.

We visited Super Duper Burger with my kids and they loved it! The burgers were crispy, juicy, and full of flavor, with delicious homemade pickles on the side. They enjoyed every bite!

For me, it was a little too rich because I’m not usually a big burger fan, but I can see why this place is popular. Definitely a great spot for burger lovers.

Most amazing and juiciest burgers we’ve ever had! 12/10 experience. The staff are super friendly too. We’re from Canada and this is the first food place we visited over here; overall such a wonderful experience.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great food, service, ambience and selection music."
"This place has delicious garlic fries, tasty greasy burgers and good milkshakes."
"The fries with garlic & aged cheese tastes as good as it smells."

name: Brenda's French Soul Food
address: 652 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States

google.name: Brenda's French Soul Food
google.address: 652 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94102, United States
google.description: Cozy eatery serving French, Creole, and Southern cuisine, including beignets and po' boys.

top_reviews.content: Good food, but not quite great. It's a solid 4 out of 5, not bad. We love coming here. Wine and liquor selections are minimal but okay. The fried chicken is incredible. The greens are really good. The grits are 8 out of 10. Everything was good. I recommend Brenda's to all.

A different type of French cuisines. The place is unassuming, affordable and has local diners. Good service overall. The fried chicken is good, served hot. The bloody Mary with pickled okra is a bit bitter. The crawfish bignet is tasty, more cheesy than clawfish, worth a try. If you like sausage, you would enjoy andouille, a different kind of sausage like meat. If you like new orlean dish, you would enjoy the French soul food offered here. We like this variation from the most refined French dish.

This is a well-known brunch and breakfast spot in San Francisco. Their food tends to be on the salty side, but their coffee is excellent with a wide variety of options. The atmosphere is enjoyable. I love this place, especially if they used less salt.

Brenda’s French Soul Food delivered a solid dining experience with a few standout dishes and a few that didn’t quite hit the mark. Our party unanimously agreed that the fried chicken was the highlight—crispy, flavorful, and definitely worth the visit. The beignets were also a treat, light and tasty with just the right touch of sweetness.
Some dishes were more middle-of-the-road. The red beans and rice and the biscuits were decent but didn’t stand out in a memorable way. Unfortunately, the shrimp and grits fell short of expectations and didn’t quite come together in flavor.
Overall, it was a good experience with some hits and misses, and we’d rate it a 7 out of 10. Worth trying, especially for the fried chicken and beignets.

Not a bad place to get some fun French/Southern food. If you’re into grits, the shrimp and grits are a favorite. And we also like the chicken sandwich. The beignets are also really good if you’ve got enough room for dessert.

The service here isn’t bad, but it is an amazing. We arrived with a reservation a few minutes early and the restaurant was almost completely empty and they still didn’t see us. But they did see a bunch of walk-ins which was a little weird. And then even before we were done with our meal, they were consistently trying to rush us out of our table, even though there were more open tables, and nobody waiting to be seated.

That being said, that atmosphere is really fun and if you go on Sunday evenings, they have live music being played. Makes for a really fun atmosphere during dinner.

reviews_snippets.content: "My fave dishes were the hush puppies, fried chicken, and red beans and rice."
"BBQ Shrimp - Shrimp cooked in a tomato based sauce served over rice."

top_reviews.content: House of Nanking is an absolute must-visit! The food was fresh, full of flavor, and every dish we ordered was outstanding. The portions were generous, and the service was warm, attentive, and made us feel right at home. You can tell they take pride in both the quality of their food and the experience they provide. If you’re looking for delicious Chinese food with a welcoming atmosphere, this place is definitely worth a visit. I’ll be coming back!

If you're looking for great food with good prices this is the place.
Staff were very friendly and the service was very good. Very busy place with a good atmosphere and history.
Came back a 2nd time for dinner on Sunday
Ordered 3 dishes one chicken, one pork and noodles. Asked the waitress for the chefs choice and we were not disappointed.
Pork Ribs glazed with Zucchini,  Chicken with sweet potatoes and sauce, and last of all noodles with herbs.
The taste was amazing, l would highly recommend trying this.

Best Chinese food I have ever had. Each and every dish was soooo flavorful and delicious.

It’s a small restaurant but it’s very renowned and it’s been featured in several food channels and magazines.

It’s Keanu Reeves’s favorite restaurant as well.

We had such a wonderful experience at House of Nanking.

We arrived just before the dinner rush, and even though there was already a long line forming outside, the staff kept things moving efficiently and had everyone seated surprisingly quickly.

Our kids felt welcome and enjoyed the decor. The walls had articles and awards. Seated close to other tables but comfortable.

What made this visit especially memorable was meeting Chef Peter Fang himself. It was incredibly humbling to watch someone so renowned and successful personally greeting guests, taking orders, and checking on tables. Seeing a chef of his caliber so hands-on and genuinely invested in his customers says a lot about the restaurant and the person behind it. His humility and passion left just as much of an impression on us as the food.

We ordered the short ribs with bok choy, the pork confit, the duck buns, and the House Noodles. Every dish was packed with flavor and thoughtfully prepared. The standout for me was definitely the duck buns - they were absolutely incredible and something I'd order again in a heartbeat. The House Noodles were also delicious, and the short ribs were tender and full of rich, savory flavor.

If you're visiting San Francisco's Chinatown, House of Nanking is absolutely worth the wait. Great food, generous portions, and an unforgettable dining experience made even better by Chef Peter Fang's genuine hospitality.

After hearing from multiple sources this was the best Chinese food in San Francisco, my wife and I were alittle disappointed. Whilst the Sesame Chicken came out very fast and was delicious, the House Noodles took a while to come out. To the point where we had basically finished the chicken, when we had hoped to eat both dishes at the same time. The house noodles were underwhelming, not very flavoursome and tasted over cooked and slightly soggy. Perhaps the restaurant's massive popularity with tourists has resulted in their standards slipping recently.

It was a little pricier than a generic fast food burger place but it was worth it!

Ordered the double BBQ bacon burger with fries and it absolutely hit. The burger was juicy, stacked perfectly, and the BBQ sauce + bacon combo was on point without being overwhelming. Fries were hot, crispy, and fresh.

What really stood out was the customer service—super friendly when I asked questions about the menu, and they were happy to give extra sauce without any attitude. You can tell they actually care about the experience, not just the food.

Definitely a spot I’d come back to when I’m craving a solid burger.

Mushroom Swiss had tender mushrooms and the adding the melt sauce brought all the flavors together!

I had lettuce wrap melt cheeseburger and it was the perfect size!

We didn't see any seats downstairs, but had the balcony all to ourselves! Easy to hear conversations and chill vibes!

Def a great smash burger place to enjoy!

Went there as soon as they opened to get a breakfast sandwich and it did not disappoint!! I was able to customize it the way I wanted to and it turned out amazing. An egg melt with avocado, caramelized onions and mushrooms. Absolutely delicious

Good food and the atmosphere is very relaxed. The wait times can be pretty good but no one really says if your order is ready if you order online. It's difficult to get someone's attention. Other than that the whole place is good.

name: The Grove Restaurant & Bar
address: 690 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94105, United States

google.address: 690 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94105, United States
google.description: Popular spot for American home cooking in a mountain-lodge-like setting with communal seats.

top_reviews.content:
We stopped here for lunch while visiting SFMOMA. It was peak lunch hour and there was a line outside, but it moved quickly—it was more of an entry line than a wait. Once inside, you order at a kiosk, get a number, find a seat, and the food is brought to your table.

I had the New York-style pastrami sandwich, served with a pickle and a small side of lettuce (chips are also an option). The pastrami was meaty, rich, and quite filling—half the sandwich was enough for me to take the rest home. It was fresh and definitely not bad, although having had some excellent pastrami in New York, I wouldn’t call this exceptional.

My friend had a slice of apple pie and really enjoyed it. She found it fresh and pleasantly, mildly sweet without being overly sugary.

They have a good selection of all-day breakfast items and sandwiches. The restaurant was almost full and clearly popular. Overall, nothing extraordinary that you’ll remember for years, but a solid, reliable spot for a satisfying lunch in the area.

I really enjoyed the vibe here. Perfect for a lunch date. You order your food, pay at the register, and they give you a number, and you can go sit wherever you want. They servers will find you. My lady and I sat upstairs. I ordered the Crisp Oven Fried Chicken Sandwich and my lady ordered the Roadt Chicken Apple Salad. I also was being a fat ass and ordered a huge chocolate chip cookie and a (I think it was a coffee cake or a crumble, my bad.) But it was good. The cookie was alright, I give the cookie a C but everything else was on point. Sit up stairs for the best ambience. We went around 1130 am.

The chairs next to the fireplace are the spot on a rainy day - cozy and warm.

I ordered the avocado toast with poached eggs, which came with a side salad. It was very filling and well-balanced.

***No WiFi *** so plan accordingly. Bring a hotspot if you need to work, or take it as an opportunity to unplug and just enjoy the space.

Overall, a great place to slow down, especially when the weather calls for something warm and relaxed.

Wonderful environment, well situated in the city too. If you're here with a lot of people you're likely to have a good time, but even parties of two or one suffice. The food is scrumptious, and the whole place feels like a cabin you'd eat at before embarking upon a beautiful hike across some snowcapped peaks.

I was a regular at the Grove when living in San Francisco and specifically when there were several locations before the lockdown. My favorites were located on Hayes and in the designer's district. Only this one at Yerba Buena now remains. I still like the food (not cheap) and they offer a very tasty GF bread.

However, I asked for only one instead of two poached eggs with the avocado toast and was told: "it will be the same price"!
"Yes, ok I understand" . However I suggested to comp me the bread since I had to pay extra for the GF bread (which I never understood  why most restaurants charge extra for GF bread in the first place; it is not that much more expensive than regular bread).
The cashier: "Well, I can't; I would need to have a manager do it."

And is it that difficult to call a manager to ask? My thought, that I didn't bother to express because at that point, I was annoyed, especially after learning that the orange juice was more than $9.00. I declined to add the juice to my order!!
My tip was not as generous as usual!
The weather was beautiful so eating outside was nice.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great atmosphere and service with solid food, good portions, and lots of options"

name: Golden Boy Pizza
address: 542 Green St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States

google.address: 542 Green St, San Francisco, CA 94133, United States
google.description: Funky joint specializing in focaccia pizzas with a variety of meat & veggie toppings.

top_reviews.content:
Went here with my family and wow… what a scene. The line was LOOOONG. We waited about 1 hour and 15 minutes for our pizza. With hungry kids, that is basically a survival challenge.
But then we took the first bite… and suddenly nobody was complaining. The pizza was sooo soft, almost like a fluffy cloud, and it just melted in your mouth. The crust was thick but light, crispy on the outside and pillowy inside. Super simple, super good.
Only downside: very limited options if you are vegetarian and nothing for vegans. There was just choice between pesto veggie and cheese. Overall though, totally worth the wait. Next time I am 100% ordering ahead because now I know the pizza is worth it, but my feet cannot handle another hour-long line.

Golden Boy Pizza is a must-visit in San Francisco! The pizza was absolutely delicious, fresh and full of flavour. The crust was perfectly cooked, the toppings were generous, and every slice was outstanding.

The atmosphere was lively, the service was quick, and it is easy to see why this place is so popular with both locals and visitors. Even with a queue, the food was worth the wait.

Decent pizza for the price. Thick crust, generous toppings, efficient gruff service that reminds me of New York. Park nearby to consume your goods at! Take away only. Slices and whole pies available. They heat up your slices so it's a bit of a wait but they stay piping hot for a while. I'd be happy to return if I were in the area again.

The pizza here is amazing. I tried the pepperoni slice and it was genuinely delicious with a very authentic flavor. Even late at night the queue was surprisingly long, which says a lot about how popular the place is.

It’s just a small takeaway counter, so don’t expect a premium atmosphere, more of a classic, local vibe. During peak hours you’ll need to wait in line, and once you reach the front you place your order, pay, and give your name. After that there’s a short wait until they call you, and then you get your pizza.

Overall, great taste and totally worth the wait if you’re craving a quality slice.
How is it possible I didn't find Golden Boy Pizza back in the 80s when I spent a lot of time in this neighborhood? The pizza is fantastic and at an excellent price. The crust is delicious.

reviews_snippets.content: "Best place to grab a whole pie or a slice great food great people"
"It’s a walk-up counter, no inside service, so I can’t rate the “atmosphere.”"
"Their crust, sauce, cheese and ingredients makes their pizza the best in town."

top_reviews.content: This is one of the real jewels for eating well prepared seafood and a beautiful view. I went here recently for my birthday.  The whole experience was wonderful! We started with the market salad with grilled peaches and artichokes. The ceviche with house made chips. AmThe eggplant Katsu.  All were really great but the star of the show was the eggplant katsu! Surprisingly awesome! Our entrees were the grilled swordfish with green papaya and the grilled Dorado with chili braised cabbage. Both were very fresh and well prepared.  The service was excellent and professional! A magical birthday experience!

Best views, beautiful ambiance, and exceptional service from Brian and his colleagues. The food was delicious, and I couldn’t have asked for a better birthday lunch experience. I love that they offer a reservation system, and everyone here is genuinely warm and welcoming. The restaurant itself is a vibe…elegant, inviting, and beautifully designed. The two large fish tanks really elevate the entire dining room and create a unique atmosphere. The martini was also excellent. This is exactly why I keep coming back time and time again.

Lovely bar lounge upon entry with sweeping views of the Bay Bridge.

Top quality seafood, highest levels of freshness. Excellent option for raw bar, with Seafood Tower coming with half dozen oysters and clams, half lobster, shrimp and crab cocktails as well as ceviche served with tostones.

Menu flavors are clean and simple — though notably, not heavy on spice (i.e classically New American)

Perfect for celebrating a special occasion.

Had a great time at Waterbar with some friends a few days ago. The atmosphere was incredible and the view on the terrace was top-tier. Staff was friendly, and a special mention to Pete who was very welcoming and hospitable. All the food we tried, especially the fish and seafood, was phenomenal. It was all cooked to perfection and full of flavor. The dessert was decadent and completed our meal beautifully. No alcohol for me, but the mocktail I had was refreshing and delicious. Definitely a must if you’re visiting San Francisco!

First time in this restaurant. We went to celebrate our 12th Anniversary. The restaurant had an amazing detail leaving us a card with the signature of each employee congratulating us. The atmosphere is very welcome and cozy. The two fish tanks make the place unique. Also, the view to bay bridge make my night. Food exquisite.

name: Viks Chaat
address: 2390 Fourth St, Berkeley, CA 94710, United States

google.name: Viks Chaat
google.address: 2390 Fourth St, Berkeley, CA 94710, United States
google.description: Ample Indian grocery store with lots of traditional food items & spices, plus a quick-serve cafe.

top_reviews.content:
Had a solid experience at Viks Chaat. The food definitely leans very spicy, so be prepared if you’re sensitive to heat, but there’s still good flavor throughout the menu. The setup is more cafeteria-style than a traditional sit-down restaurant, which gives it a casual, bustling atmosphere that fits the place well.

The portions are generous and overall it’s good value for the money, especially considering Bay Area prices. The lamb biriyani stood out as a particularly good deal — hearty, flavorful, and filling. Pairing it with one of their draught lagers worked really well and balanced the spice nicely.

Not the place for a quiet upscale dining experience, but if you want satisfying Indian comfort food with solid portions and a lively atmosphere, it’s worth checking out.

Viks is a great one stop for groceries and Indian home style food.

The lunch thali is great at the price point with tandoori chicken or lamb, a daal, rice and a roti.

The chole bature is great. The chole has some tamarind chutney for that nice sour tangyness and some raw red onions and mango pickle. The bhatura is always piping hot and fried to order.

The tandoori chicken was nice and juicy but you don't get the smoky taste from a tandoor. Daal was nice and home style with not too much butter/ghee.

The dahi puri was cool and refreshing.

The lamb was nice but I prefer goat.

Not much ambience and service is self service.

I love to get mango lassi from the supermarket.

All in all will be back again and again.

Viks in Berkeley is a cool hybrid cafeteria and market. No tipping, super fast service, and the whole place—from the restrooms to the dining area—is spotless. The food leans mostly sweet and sour. The Mango Lassi is basically the Indian version of Mango Pomelo Sago—mind-blowingly good!
The only downside was the first cashier, who looked completely over life. Turns out they forgot my Mango Lassi, which you're supposed to get right after ordering. I only figured it out while waiting for my food when I saw the next cashier hand a drink to another customer immediately.
Overall verdict: Definitely worth coming back.

Overall okay kind of restaurant. Not bad but not good that one can miss. Self service mess type atmosphere, clean your own table, can be huge lines when peak time, food quality is bringing street side flavor but prices are mid scale restaurant.

An amazing place serving Indian chaat. Can get crowded on the weekends, but still the service is pretty quick. Plenty of seating options both indoors and outdoors. We ordered Chole Bhature, Dahi Batata Puri, Pav Bhaji, Kaathi roll and Samosas. The Samosad were top notch, followed by Dahi Batata Puri, Bhatura was amazing but Chole could have been little more flavorful. Pav Bhajj and Kathi roll were decent but not very amazing. They serve Campa Cola too.

reviews_snippets.content: "The place had a nice backyard where people can sit and eat their food."

top_reviews.content: Loved every moment at Honey Honey Cafe & Crepery. I had the Crab Cake Florentine and it was perfect. It comes with potatoes on the side and those were well seasoned. As some who has a sweet tooth, I also got a Honey Cake and it was delicious, the cake has a side of real whipped cream (not from a can) which I decided to use to top my cappuccino. I am very happy that I decided to have my breakfast here and I will definitely be coming back to try some of the other options. The staff were very friendly and welcoming.

Long line but this team hustles. The menu is large. Don’t try too hard to find the best thing… pick what sticks out to you, and it will be good.

The coconut cake is delightful.
OJ & Kiwi smoothie seemed like an unusual combo, but I highly recommend it.
Hot chocolate is made with milk, instead of water (as all hot chocolate should be)
Breakfast crepe has great balance for a savory option
Strawberry Nutella crepe perfect for a sweet tooth
Even the scrambled eggs are cooked to perfection

Popped in here for Breakfast as it was around the corner from our hotel. We ordered a few crepes. Nutella & Strawberry, Nutella & Banana and the North Beach. Plus a Chorizo scramble Omelette. Fresh OJ and A Chai Latte. Everything was outstanding and quick service too. Highly recommend

@honeyhoney. It was that good, we came back again today for breakfast again.

Great food overall and crepes are amazing, many vegetarian options available. came here twice out of the three days we stayed in SF and regretted not coming the third day as well. Very clean and organized atmosphere which was the best part.

Finally had a chance to stop in for breakfast. We split a breakfast crepe and a desert crepe. You order and then take a seat. They bring you the food. Not a huge fan of this but they do it quickly so our experience was good. The food is good.

top_reviews.content: Public Market Emeryville was just a hop and a skip from our hotel so we ended up there a couple times. One night we had Japanese tonkatsu to go, and one night we ate in, having Korean bento box! Tuesday is trivia night with teams competing against each other, and although we didn't stay, we could hear the laughter and fun going on over the speaker. Big screen TV was great for the sports enthusiasts watching the world soccer series. Public market was really convenient for us since we were without a car. Easy to walk to, good people, great food!
Second time being here. The first time, there was a live band playing. It's pretty loud for us so we sat farther away. There were folks real close, so some people are fine with it.

There are so many great food options that everyone can find something they like, which makes it perfect for meeting up with friends. I also love that it’s a comfortable place to get some work done if you want a change of scenery. During the World Cup, they had the matches playing on projectors throughout the market, which created such a fun atmosphere and made it feel like a community event.

I haven't been here for many years and I remember back than that there were more restaurants and little eateries, now I only see a few places and a majority of the places close up early.  Came here on a Saturday 6pm and most places were closing up at 8pm. Peet's coffee closed at 7pm... wth.. my group thought we could hang out here for a bit longer to catch up on times and ended leaving cuz there were not many places open. Good thing the pizzeria Mercato was still open until 10pm.
Great market to catch a meal whether you are going solo, with family or a larger group!

reviews_snippets.content: "From Asian fusion, noodles, burgers, pizza, subs, Indian, Latin flavors."
"I had teriyaki beef at We Sushi, very tough and flavorless beef over rice."

name: Jupiter

top_reviews.content: Great vibes all around. The place feels welcoming the moment you walk in, and the energy is just right lively but not loud. The pizza tasted clean and fresh, which made it super easy to enjoy without feeling heavy afterward. The beer selection was solid too and paired perfectly with the food. Overall, a really good spot. I’d definitely go again.

After recommendations from three locals to try this spot, I couldn't ignore it anymore.

I got the eutropia and the wings. The naming of the pizzas as celestial bodies is quite cute. The eutropia was very good and dare I say it tastes better after reheating as leftovers.

The wings tossed with honey Sriracha were good but the ranch was something special. I asked one of the staff what it was and they told me regular ranch. I felt like I was being gas lit in real time, it didn't look like regular ranch and it for sure tasted better than regular ranch. My waitress came over and I asked her the same question and she let me know it was special house made ranch with dill and other ingredients! Thank you! I would have had crashed out if this flavor came from thousand island or some bottled ranch and re-evaluated my life. Needless to say I took that shit home and dipped my leftover pizza. A+ ranch!

What a hidden gem in Berkeley!
I was in the mood for good, authentic pizza — and as someone from New York, I’m definitely spoiled — but this place really impressed me. The pizza was amazing, and the manager, Sami, went above and beyond to get us a great table and make sure our food and drinks were perfect. I really appreciated his friendliness, and even our server mentioned what a great manager he is. I’ll definitely be coming back — not just for the food, but for the hospitality and the wonderful atmosphere. 🥰

Came in for pizza and beer here because this used to be my husband's favorite place when he was in college at uc berkeley!
We were a large group and took some time to decide on the seating and the menu - and the server was so patient with us🙏
We got four pizzas and they were all so good! If I had to pick a favorite, it would probably be Circe. The outdoor space was heated and wonderful.

Decent pizza, lots of options and a nice restaurant and outdoor patio space. Extensive beer selection but unfortunately they were out of the first three I wanted so I settled for a fourth option. Note that they can't split checks which is not a big deal. Just plan accordingly.

reviews_snippets.content: "Awsome place, greate pizza, beer and super friendly service!"
"Food -creative pizzas and good prices, Beer - tasty and many options."

name: Cheese Board Collective Pizzeria
address: 1512 Shattuck Ave., Berkeley, CA 94709, United States

google.name: Cheese Board Collective Pizzeria
google.address: 1512 Shattuck Ave., Berkeley, CA 94709, United States
google.description: A pizzeria, bakery & cheese shop, this spot serves 1 style of veggie pizza per day & limited seats.

top_reviews.content: A well-oiled machine for distribution of delicious baked goods.  As a newbie to the bakery, I ended up going in the wrong door and found myself at the coffee station, but what I should have done is follow the line of people waiting for their go at the counter to order.  The morning is peak time for buying baked goodies, and the vibe of the bakery is that the crowd were either locals or (many time) repeat customers.  After the quick progression to the counter from entering, I was greeted by a wall of delicious looking bread of all varieties.  The Asiago olive loaf was my first sampling, and I toasted it to add a little crispiness once I got it home.  The mix of slightly baked onions and olives in the sinewy loaf was amazing, the cheese being a lovely accent.  It made me wish I had bought at least one more.  The scones were the real bread all-stars for me.  The corn-cherry scones were so damned hearty.  The corn meal added an even richer texture to the scone, so I loved it even more, but the crown jewel of the scones was the oat-cranberry scone.  The crust was this and crispy, and the inside was perfectly crumbly and soft.  Definitely buying that again on my next visit.   So many things still on the menu that I want to try.  The cost performance of this bakery is incredible.  The only hassle is parking in the area, which being in Berkeley means it’s going to be awful just about all of the time.  The staff was effective as hell and got me through quickly, but the staff seemed willing to step me through examining some of the offerings, but customer speed did seem to be valued as part of the bread buying experience.
Hands down, the best pizza I had in my life. Every day, they prepare only one kind of veggie pizza. There is always line, but moves fast. Don’t miss it, if you are around.

Finally made it to the Cheese Board Pizza Collective in Berkeley — a spot I’ve wanted to try for years.

They serve one style of pizza a day, and when it’s gone, it’s gone. Today’s slice with baby chard and kale, leek, mozzarella, ricotta salata, garlic olive oil, and citrus zest was fresh, unique, and seriously good.

I’m usually a simple pizza guy, but this one delivered. Absolutely worth the wait. A true Berkeley staple.

Popped in on April 30 and tried the mushroom pizza + salad. They do a different vegan pizza every day. As a huge meat lover, I was surprised by how much I liked the mushroom one. The staff were super sweet and even gave me an extra slice! Also, the salad was so fresh, and that green sauce is so good that I bought a small tub to take home.

Love that it’s a worker-owned co-op with a classic Berkeley feel. Their website is actually super helpful too. You can check the daily pizza/bakery menu and live music schedule before you go.
MUST Visit this place especially if you are a strict vegetarian. You CANNOT go wrong with their quality and hygiene. Be ready to wait for 15-20 mins in line to enjoy the pizza

reviews_snippets.content: "Great food, quality ingredients, fair prices, happy workers, happy customers..."

top_reviews.content:
Great spot for Mexican food! The menu offers a solid variety of options, and while nothing was over-the-top standout, everything we tried was still really enjoyable and done well.

Service was pretty standard. Friendly and efficient with no issues throughout the visit. The option for both indoor and outdoor seating is a nice touch, especially on days where the weather is favourable.

Overall, a great experience and definitely a place I’d recommend checking out!

Only in SF will I pay $25 for tacos and not get mad about it. The various meats were delicious, the tortillas fresh, and I’ve never had such flavorful black beans, like really good beans. The restaurant has great vibes and pleasant staff.

Always a fan of mexican cuisine.. but this place was even better.

Everything was exceptional, the birria tacos were melting in my mouth.. and the carne asada ones were almost as food.

but the chile relleno was the surprise of the evening, mildly spicy with so much flavour.

The classic margarita was 10/10, but the other ones were just so sweet, not a fan. Highly recommend the classic one!

One of the best restaurants I’ve ever been to. The atmosphere is on point, the food is a culinary delight, and the drinks are perfect. We are PICKY. Even the chips and salsa are better. Service was great, very attentive. We devoured the meal 🍽️

🍹 Came for One Drink, Stayed for the Vibe

I've been coming to Tropisueño for years, but last night was something special.

The food was amazing as always, and the cocktails were spot on, but the bartenders completely made the night. They were having fun, interacting with everyone at the bar, making killer drinks, and creating the kind of atmosphere that makes you want to stay for "just one more."

You know those rare places where the staff's energy elevates the entire experience? That was exactly what happened. These guys were talented, personable, and genuinely seemed to love what they do. Watching them work together behind the bar was almost as enjoyable as the drinks themselves.

I've had a lot of good experiences at Tropisueño over the years, but this was easily one of the most memorable. It's not often you leave a restaurant talking more about the people than the food, but that's exactly what happened.

Huge thanks to the bartenders for making a great night even better. I'll definitely be back soon.

🍹🌮❤️

top_reviews.content: Z & Y Restaurant was a great Chinatown dining experience. The Peking duck was excellent, with a beautiful smoky flavor and perfectly roasted skin. You can really taste the technique behind it. The shrimp fried rice was also very good, flavorful, well cooked, and satisfying. Overall, the food felt authentically Sichuan, bold, aromatic, and full of character. Definitely worth trying if you’re looking for real Chinese food in San Francisco Chinatown.

Absolutely fantastic food. They do not hold back the spice. Both the food and service were top notch. It does get crowded and the place is small. Make reservations beforehand. They will greet you with Kung fu tea which I found very cool. Overall I loved everything about the restraunt. I will definitely go there again.

The food was delicious and authentic. What was “medium” spicy burned through our throats but tasty nonetheless. The tea-smoked duck was great, but it should be bundled with greens, sauce and wrappers by default cause it makes no sense any other way - it could just be $10 more expensive and come as a package. Other than that the service was good and the overall experience well worth a Michelin Bib-Gourmand.

I was a bit surprised by the comments here, because the actual ratings don’t seem to match my experience, I’m usually hesitant to judge a restaurant, especially when it comes to food from not my background, but for a place associated with the Michelin Guide or positioned in this price range, I think it should at least start with good quality ingredients. I think most people just saying good because Chinese cuisine have a strong fry and good chili oil culture, but that doesn't mean we should just say tasty to every meal that taste like it (referencing the comments).

Unfortunately, many of the reviews here feel driven more by hype, after visiting, I noticed a “leave a comment and get a free dessert” sign, which might help explain the inflated ratings.

The food wasn’t bad, but in this area there are definitely better and more affordable options, I just want to say, I didn’t try every item on the menu, but I’m not willing to spend $100+ just to fully evaluate the place.

I wouldn’t normally be this critical, but the experience was frustrating, especially with waitress asking for the tip and being mad not receiving, added service charge with a table that didn’t even have basic items like salt or napkins.

Don't think that I'm mad, this is just a objective review in the end.

This restaurant in Chinatown is a perfect 10/10. The food is incredible with so many amazing choices. Service is great and although you may have to wait, it’s well worth it! Michelin star, served multiple international heads of state - the door has more prestigious awards than I thought possible… if you go to one place in China town, Z & Y won’t disappoint!

"This price you can eat better resturant which has more tasty and better service."

top_reviews.content: We found this small popular lively ramen shop when we arrived to San Francisco in the evening.  We tried their unique clam ramen and karage. The ramen was fresh and the clam broth was light and flavorful with a refreshing beer. It was a perfect meal after a long trip. Please use the machine in front of the door to join the waitlist. Waiting on line without joining it would not get you into the que.

A delightful little ramen restaurant featuring a beautiful Japanese-style wood interior. There is seating for about 15 pairs of diners, one slightly longer table, and a few outdoor tables as well. The food is fantastic. The menu offers around three or four dishes at a time—options include vegetarian, spicy, and meat-based varieties—which can be paired with Japanese beer or sake if desired. Prices range from $20 to $30 per dish. Anyone who loves Japanese udon soup will be more than satisfied here—a fact attested to by the many Asian patrons.

After several great meals in San Francisco, this was one of the surprises of the trip. The ramen was outstanding from the first bite to the last, with a rich, flavorful broth, fresh noodles, and quality toppings that all came together perfectly.

The star of the bowl was the poached egg. I’ve eaten a lot of eggs over the years, and this was hands down the best poached egg I’ve ever had. Perfectly cooked with an unbelievably creamy yolk that made every bite even better.

The atmosphere was upbeat and energetic without feeling rushed, and the service matched the food—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. If you’re staying near Union Square and craving ramen, this is an easy recommendation. We’ll definitely be back the next time we’re in San Francisco.

Paloma was a great server and provided excellent service. She checked on us so much, each time she came I had food in my mouth and couldn’t speak lol. The ramen was very good especially with this SF weather. I definitely recommend the gyoza and chicken karaage
The food was great but what stood out the most was the service. Paloma was the best server! She really made sure that we’re comfortable while we were dining. She’s very nice and very energetic!

reviews_snippets.content: "Staff is polite and food is served quick with good portion/price for the area."

name: Mensho Tokyo SF

google.description: American spin-off of Tokyo’s standout ramen brand brings a variety of combos to petite, modern digs.

top_reviews.content:
Let me get the only minor negative out of the way: they expect everyone to purchase a bowl of ramen. I understand that, but we had two kids with us who can share. We ordered two sides (wagyu sashimi and uni/wagyu) which were more than the ramen bowls themselves so they were okay with that.

With that out of the way, the ramen was the best I ever tasted (in the States). It does rival ramen I've had in Japan. That is saying a whole lot for those who haven't been to Japan, the ramen there is top notch obviously.

The ramen noodle itself was perfect texture of chewy, smooth and aldente at the same time. It was perfect. The broth was creamy but you didn't feel it was over bearing with cream, it didn't feel heavy. Meat was buttery soft and delicious.

The wagyu sashimi was almost too smooth, there I couldn't taste any flavor. I'd honestly rather eat thick wagyu seared slightly in each side.

Overall, I'm glad we waited on the long line. That line is consistently long for a reason. A must try in SF!

Hands down the best ramen we’ve ever had.
The signature bowl is rich and deeply flavorful, while the classic is a great option if you prefer something lighter. The GKO and lamb cumin ramen bring in Chinese-inspired flavors, which is a unique and creative twist. Everything we tried was delicious—highly recommend!

The signature ramen was delicious. The matcha duck ramen was creative, but the taste was only so so. The wagyu beef sushi was good. The fried enoki was crispy and nice. The wait for not too long for a Monday evening around 6-7pm. Overall, we had a good dinner.

Hands down the best ramen I’ve ever had. The broth is incredibly rich, creamy, and packed with flavor—every spoonful feels carefully crafted. The noodles have the perfect texture, and the toppings are high quality and unique.

This isn’t your typical ramen spot—it feels elevated, almost like a Michelin-level experience in terms of technique and flavor. You can really tell there’s a lot of thought behind every element of the bowl.

If you’re into bold, intense flavors and don’t mind something a bit heavier, this place is a must-try. I’d absolutely come back

Tried Mensho Tokyo in San Francisco and it absolutely lived up to the hype.

We ordered the Spicy Lamb and the Extra Spicy GKO both were incredible. The broth is rich, thick, and almost curry-like, packed with deep, bold flavors that really stand out from typical ramen.

They’ve got a great variety of veg and non-veg options, which makes it an easy pick for mixed groups too.

Definitely one of the best ramen spots I’ve been to, highly recommend checking it out!

top_reviews.content: Nice place to enjoy a delicious meal before an excellent show performed by Kieko Matsui.  Be sure to catch her the next she’s in Oakland. There was a good selection of food and everything was very tasty. The staff were friendly and pretty attentive given how busy they were before the show.

Japanese with Jazz!
Thanks to our friends who introduced Yoshi's to us. The meal and the concert following made for a truly memorable experience. We drove from San Jose to Oakland for it - totally worth the effort!
The package deal includes parking within the structure - unheard of! They validate - so remember to pass by the electronic validation machine on your way out.
Warm sake, sushi, and Jazz - life should be so good!

This is easily my favorite music venue in the Bay without a doubt.  My wife and I used to live in Oakland and could walk here.  And we would go once a month at least.  First of all, the food is phenomenal.  Most live music venues are not known for their food.  But the sushi, ambiance and service from this restaurant are top notch.  If you make a reservation for food before the concert, you often get priority seating too.  The music venue is in a separate room inside the restaurant.  Once you enter the music venue, it is small and close knit.  There are no bad seats in the house.  Bartenders will serve you drinks and food during concerts as well so you never have to leave your seat.  I was shocked at the list of artists that come into this place.  Artists that can probably fill up stadiums and arenas perform here.  Depending on the artists, it can turn into a party.  I’ve seen the audience get up and dance in their seats on plenty of occasions.  And the ticket prices are decent.  This place is a must try!  It’s easily what we miss the most from Oakland.

Yoshi's is a standout when it comes to authentic Japanese cuisine. From the moment you enter, you’re greeted with a warm, inviting atmosphere that sets the tone for an exceptional dining experience. The decor is sleek yet cozy, offering the perfect environment for both casual meals and special celebrations.

The menu at Yoshi’s is packed with options, but the sushi is what truly shines. The fish is always incredibly fresh, and each piece is prepared with attention to detail. Whether you're enjoying a classic California roll or a more adventurous specialty roll, you can taste the quality in every bite. For sashimi lovers, the selection is extensive and always perfectly sliced.

Aside from sushi, Yoshi's also offers a variety of other Japanese dishes, like ramen and teriyaki, that are equally impressive. The service is top-notch—attentive but never overbearing, and the staff is knowledgeable about the menu, always ready to offer recommendations.

If you're a fan of Japanese food, Yoshi's should definitely be on your radar. The combination of amazing food, great atmosphere, and excellent service makes it a must-visit spot. Whether you're a sushi aficionado or new to Japanese cuisine, you’ll leave Yoshi’s feeling satisfied and eager to return!

Fantastic place! We have beard great things about Yoshi's prior to visiting. One of our favorite jazz singers had a show there, so we went. We started the evening with some delicious and fresh sushi. The lychee drink was great! The atmosphere was lively and bright. The desert we ordered was delicious. Great food, great music, great vibes. Visiting again soon!

The chilly naan is a must for anyone who prefers spicy food!! Saag , naan, kheer & gulag jamun were all so good. Great Food! No matter what is your order you will enjoy it. Excellent Service, the staff is really cool. Attentive and friendly.

top_reviews.content: Everything was delicious,  just as our server warned.  I had the fried catfish,  which was served with potato salad on a bed of hush puppies.  The fish was delicate and flaky without being over cooked.  The breading was seasoned but not over-powering. Others in our group enjoyed the buttermilk fried chicken.  Impressed by our mains,  we decided dessert was in order,  so we had the chocolate cake,  which does have a satisfying amount of cayenne- just enough to feel the warmth,  not so much as to be spicy. The rum infused whipped cream was a decadent touch.  The bread pudding was also a hit. Only issue was our server was stretched a bit thin,(surprise post- lunch rush) but he was still friendly and helpful.

I just moved to California recently and I had my first dine in experience at Angeline’s Louisiana Kitchen. I had such a lovely time! Our server, Melody, was very kind and attentive! She checked on us from time to time and made sure we were okay. The food was just as amazing and I can’t wait to go back!! It was my first time trying southern food and I loved it!

Thank you Melody and Angeline’s Louisiana Kitchen! 🩷

I've been here a couple of times now. The first time I had high expectations from having enjoyed great food while in Louisiana.  Angeline's didn't quiet feel the same. It's definitely a great spot in the Bay when craving Louisiana food, but it still doesn't come close to the bold flavors I've had during my visit.

Apart from that, they have very good service and ambiance is cozy as well.

These are just my two cents so take it for what you will. Go check them and see what you think.

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I decided to come here for lunch. This is a very nice restaurant that offers indoor and outdoor seating.
We opted for indoor and we were seated with four other tables.
My husband ordered the half crab, which was disappointing because it was not cracked, it came in a sauce so if you dropped a piece, you were not given a bib or extra napkins. We constantly had to look around for someone who was working on the floor as they would serve someone and then disappear. I had the salmon which was okay.
Our server came around a couple of times to see if everything was okay, but after giving us the check, he disappeared. All the other tables were empty and there was no one to be found.
After ten minutes of waiting, we took the check and went downstairs to find someone so we could pay the check and leave.
I may go back someday if i'm in the area as it is a very nice and clean looking restaurant with very pretty views.

Came here for a work dinner recently and while we overall had an enjoyable time with a stellar atmosphere, the food itself was a bit disappointing.

The service itself was great. It’s never easy to handle a big group and our wait staff was patient and helpful. We were quickly seated outside and had a lovely view of the lake.

Atmosphere is definitely what you’re paying for when coming to this restaurant and with a lovely sunset it makes for incredible backdrop.

Now for the food. While the food itself generally looked good and the vast menu had options to support many preferences, what I actually ate left something to be desired. The rice in my dish was pretty bland overall and the slaw while flavorful didn’t have enough punch to save the dish.

Highlights were actually the drinks and dessert. The tamarind marg was delicious and the desserts, specifically the bread pudding, were a hit.

Overall we enjoyed a nice meal but I think the food in certain cases leaves room for improvement.

I ordered the SESAME SEARED AHI BOWL, and it was below average. The tuna was overcooked, everything in the salad was okay. I told my server about the tuna and he said "I'll let the kitchen know", and that was the last time I saw my server. Another server brought me the check. Beer was good, though, although they didn't have the one I would have wanted to try, even though they make their own beers per the waiter.
I'll be coming back to Oakland next month, but I will definitely not be going back to this bar and grill.

Wonderful place to celebrate my daughter’s 35 th birthday with family.  We sat outside so our 1 year old didn’t bother anyone. Weather helped make it wonderful but we loved our waiter, Ryan and the owner was super nice and even helped us celebrate!

Great service and great atmosphere. That's why I gave 4 stars.  Lovely seating everyone was nice . The food  was pretty average. I enjoyed the appetizer the best calamari was fresh and fried just right. I order a dish without fish and the cook decided to replace it with another fish. Can't hurt him for trying however the fish would have nearly killed me 😆. The manager was ultra nice about it. Kevin was his name, great way to make up for the mix up . We left smiling and happy
The hamburger that replaced the fish item was a good size and alot of toppings.
I'd come back because everyone was so kind.

Large restaurant with a nice ambiance, though it can get pretty noisy. Generous portions. We ordered three entrées and one dessert to share between two people and still had leftovers. Service was excellent, and the staff was friendly.

The only surprise was the automatic 20% gratuity plus a 5% surcharge added to our bill for a party of two, since that’s usually only standard for large parties. Extensive menu with options for everyone! The food good but not the best Chinese I’ve ever had, and certainly not authentic. Service was solid. The place was incredibly loud but you could still hold a conversation. It was fine but I probably wouldn’t return considering there are so many restaurants in the vicinity.

Fun spot to go with a group and sample all the fun food options on the menu. I loved the soup dumplings and the bao, oh and the green beans were great too! It can get a bit noisy, in case you’re looking for something quiet this is not your spot. Come here and get your hipster vibe on!

We came here on Sunday evening, and the restaurant was relatively full. The food was great. We enjoyed the roasted duck with the sesame bread, the pan fried baos and the thousand years eggs. Look forward to coming back and trying more dishes one day!

The food was delicious. We had a reservation so we didn't have to wait. Our waiter was great, our food came quickly. To be honest, we had trouble deciding. We chose 3 small bite plates, thinking we'd order an entree to share but we were full before we were finished. The entrees we saw leaving the kitchen all looked wonderful and the portions were large. The Bao buns and spring rolls were our favorite. I wish we had been able to try more. Definitely a yes!

Delicious pizza! My husband went 6 years ago and now that we are both visiting the area he brought me and I can confirm it's absolutely exquisite! We ordered a Zachary's special. Staff was super nice even on a Monday at 8.30. Will definitely come back soon

Must try the stuffed mushroom and spinach. The crust and sauce are too good to be true!

Came here for a hackathon event and had a great time. It’s a fun spot to hang out with a large group, with plenty of space to socialize, play games, and unwind between sessions. Very nice venue,  located in Jack London Square, across from Scott's.   We had lunch early afternoon and it wasn't busy. We ordered the fish and chips and chicken salad.  Both were delicious!!  I was told the place gets packed, during sports season, and they offer many outdoor tvs for viewing.

The first couple of times I went to Plank it was fun, but expensive, so now I only go for Taco Tuesday. Not anymore. Last couple of times I went, the tacos were so disappointing and took forever. Last time I went; my order was wrong, the tacos took forever and were too chewy, overly full of onions, and service was subpar. No one checked on us to make sure we got our food or if we needed anything, we had to get up multiple times to check on our stuff.

top_reviews.content: E/Z access from the freeway. Underground parking available near by. A refreshing walk to the restaurant. Seating right on the water. Service by Pearl was EXCELLENT! She made sure we had everything we needed! Food was Excellent. Great atmosphere with live piano music in the background. Very pleasant, I HIGHLY recommend.

Beautiful restaurant with a beautiful view. The food is decent, but it does not reach a top-tier or Michelin-level standard. The service is professional, but it does not go beyond a basic level of execution.
My biggest disappointment was the use of Dreyer’s commercial ice cream in the dessert presentation. For a serious steakhouse, this is not acceptable. In Oakland, with so many excellent artisanal ice cream makers nearby, the restaurant should either source a premium local product or make its own. A high-end dining experience requires attention to detail in every element, including the final course.

I had a wonderful experience at Scott’s Seafood in Oakland. I used to visit their Walnut Creek location often, so I was a bit sad when it closed—but this location definitely lived up to my expectations.

The restaurant is beautifully situated near the bay, which creates a relaxing and scenic atmosphere. The interior design is elegant and inviting, making it a great spot for both casual meals and special occasions.

The food quality was excellent—fresh, flavorful, and perfectly prepared. Everything we ordered was delicious, and you can really tell they take pride in their seafood.

What stood out the most was the service. Our server went above and beyond to make sure we were comfortable and had everything we needed. Their attention to detail and friendliness made the whole experience even better.

Overall, we had a fantastic time—honestly, a 5/5 experience. I highly recommend this location, especially if you’re looking for great seafood, a beautiful view, and outstanding service. I’ll definitely be coming back!

I've been to Scott's now for dinner and for their new Jazz Brunch and both have been nice! For dinner we had calamari, very delicious oyster Rockefeller (endorsed by my mother in law from New Orleans), seafood sautee and my husband had crab stuffed salmon with lobster sauce. Bananas foster bread pudding was also really good. We also sat by the window and had a beautiful sunset!

For brunch the selection was bigger than I expected. A nice chilled seafood section, mini bagels with lox and all the fixins, carving board, assorted composed dishes like crab cake Benedict and seafood en croute, and several sweet options including my favorite - blintzes! I took my mom there and she was thrilled. Jazz band played a lot of fun songs as well.

Overall this restaurant is perfect for a nice meal out. Tasty and scenic and well located in Jack London. Would definitely recommend!

Another excellent lunch at Scott's.  This is my family's go-to place in the Bay Area. Over the past few decades the food, service and atmosphere have remained excellent. The parking is convenient, views gorgeous and location perfect.

We look forward to many more years enjoying Scott's excellent food and service.

top_reviews.content: Il Casaro Pizzeria was an absolute throwback to Napoli. From our Italian waiter’s impeccable recommendations to the vibrant, energetic neighborhood vibe, this spot checked every single box: busy, fast, fresh, and authentic. The carbonara was easily the best we’ve had since visiting Rome—finally, a kitchen that knows how to execute it properly. The Neapolitan Calabrese tasted just like what we remember from Naples, and wrapping up the meal with a classic espresso and an exceptional panna cotta was the perfect finish. Hands down one of the best pizza spots we’ve eaten at since Italy!

Everything was so good! Our waitress was super welcoming and helped us navigate the menu since it was our first time. Just a heads-up: the portions are huge. We were totally stuffed and still couldn’t finish everything—wish we had more room!
We were so hungry at first that we forgot to snap a photo of the grilled calamari, but it was amazing. It’s done in the pizza oven, so it has that perfect char without being greasy like the fried stuff.
I added the imported Burrata to my pizza, and it’s so perfect! Much better than the same thing I got from supermarket, so creamy and rich. The pizza crust was perfectly charred too, with a LOT of mushrooms and prosciutto. My partner originally said she wasn't in the mood for pizza, but she literally couldn't stop eating it lol.
The Pesto pasta she ordered was also fresh and light, which balanced out the richness of the pizza.

We ordered Tiramisu for dessert- it’s moist and light, not overly sweet (which is important) but packed with flavor.

Also, I have to mention their Calabrian chilies!! Those little peppers are salty, fiery, and have that perfect fermented tang. They remind me so much of the pickled peppers from Hunan China.

Hands down the best pizza I’ve had since moving to the United States nearly a decade ago. We ordered the Quattro Formaggi and the Diavola, and both were downright mind-blowing. Truly authentic, delicious pizza. Highly, highly recommended!

Some of the best pizza in San Francisco! My dad works with Italians and they loved this place so I had to check it out. The dough is soft but not too thick. The pizza is cooked perfectly. Thryvhave a nice selection all day but if you want the classic marinara you can get that in the happy hour menu, which is 3 to 5. My girlfriend also liked their spritzer. For dessert we got the lemon sorbet and afagado which were both expertly made.

The pizzas were absolutely amazing! The crust was fresh, the toppings were high quality, and all the flavors came together perfectly. If you're looking for an authentic Italian pizza experience, this is definitely the place to go. We also ordered the tiramisu for dessert, and it was just as incredible as the pizza. Everything was delicious, and we'll definitely be back!

top_reviews.content:
Gott’s @Marketplace 1, Ferry Building, Ferry Plz Bldg #6, San Francisco, CA 94111

This newly opened branch at the San Francisco Ferry Terminal is a great addition to the area. We chose to eat here because dogs are welcome in the outdoor seating section, which is a big plus for pet owners.
The line can get long during busy hours, but ordering is simple since you can grab a menu while waiting. Prices are reasonable, and the food was excellent. We tried the burger, tacos, and French fries, and everything was fresh, flavorful, and satisfying.
The restaurant is clean and well organized. Condiments and a water refill station are conveniently located on the side. There’s also plenty of seating indoors, along with a large TV. Overall, it was a pleasant dining experience, and we’ll definitely be back to try more items on the menu. Highly recommended!

I ordered the double cheeseburger. They serve them with a little bit of pink in the middle. Most places default to well-done, but this was juicy and tasted like high-quality protein. The buns were solid and they didn’t skimp on the sauce, which I always appreciate.
We came in with a group of six, So I obviously had to wait a bit for my order. However, I think this place is usually pretty busy, so be prepared to wait for a bit. The staff was kind.
For the side, I tried the onion rings. To be fair, I’m not a huge 'onion guy' to begin with, but these tasted a bit underwhelming. If you’re like me, you might want to stick to the burger—which is clearly the star of the show anyway.
I'd be more inclined to give it a higher score if it didn't cost as much as it did. If I'm going to spend $17 for one burger ( not including fries) I need to be super impressed.
Overall, a very solid experience and a  7.8 out of 10. I’d recommend it if you’re in the area."

I honestly love the place and very satisfied with the service. I am vegetarian and I ordered Texas avocado burger with veggie Pattie and cheese fries !! I love it. I would recommend people who are vegetarian and looking for nice place to have a burger. (Although I guess they have egg bun- not sure. Just confirm your priorities before you order )

But over all, highly satisfied food quality! Even though it was busy, it was good !

I love the space, clean lines, simple, full of natural light. Classy but no frills. Bus your own table. Staff always polite and helpful. These are generous burgers, and based on how they come out I think they are cooked on what seems to be a traditional flat grill. I appreciate that you can get wine, beer, hotdogs, sweet potato fries and other things besides burgers. Great pitstop in ferry bldg before or after ferry trip.

Soft serve ice cream. Tried their Straus Vanilla and can definitely stand behind Strauss quality! Will have to come back and try some other flavors. For a little sweet treat, it is not a bad price as most places! Check it out!
Also note, they have a "Soft Serve" booth that is completely separate from the restaurant! I have not tried their burgers, but will give it a try at some point.

top_reviews.content:
the salads, entrees, and dessert were very well balanced. i love how their ingredients were.

i did prefer the egg for the salad to be a little more runny.

loved the sweet and savory balance of the fig toast and prosciutto

the pasta with veggies did not really do it for me. i felt it was an overabundance of corn and veggie accoutrements, which was distracting.

pork loin was nice and tender. the seasoning for the loin was nicely done.

the olive oil cake was something special. i could taste the olive oil from the cake. nice and fluffy as well

although not in the pictures, the apricot galette was not my favorites. i think the apricot filling was too tart and sweet. it is a tricky dessert to get right, as cooking the apricot will make it even more sweet. I would suggest adding a tad bit of salt to balance the tartness, and sweetness.

The last five years I came here, they used to scrape the bread crumbs off the table for me. this time they did not do it even after we finished the bread and going into the entree round. they finally did it before the desserts.

overall, i applaud the use of fresh ingredients.

Delicious food and great service.  Definitely price and a special occasion kind of place.  We were pleasantly surprised with the small appetizer, dessert tea, and small candies (orange peel and chocolate covered almonds) included with the prix fixe menu!

Had lunch at the cafe -- 3.5 stars, rounded down. It was frustratingly almost great. But IMO for an $80 lunch it needs to be solidly fantastic.

My waiter took long to take my order for main and for dessert. Food wait times were very long as well. Took many minutes for my dessert to come, and it was a slice of galette with a scoop of ice cream.

Apricot galette - Almost incredible. Overall it was just too tart, even with the ice cream trying to balance things out. The crust was great though.

Their cooking is a harmonious blend of simplicity and elegance, avoiding any over-the-top or flashy elements. Chez Panisse truly understands the intricacies of each ingredient and flavor, employing the most effective techniques to elevate them to their fullest potential.

If you need a delicious, top-tier bowl of ramen - even on a tight schedule - this is the place to go.

Hidden gem! This place has one of the best Ramen I’ve ever had! The flavors were on point with the perfect amount of spice! The atmosphere is perfect, open kitchen dim lights and nice decor. I would recommend it.

Ippudo is a great ramen spot  close to Union Square.

top_reviews.content: One of the best Italian spots I’ve been to! The portions are HUGE (come hungry), and the owners are incredibly warm and welcoming — they truly treat you like family. We ordered Pasta and their specialty Roman Pizza. The dough of the Pizza takes 72hrs to rise! What an incredible experience. Ended up our night with Tiramasu 🤩Definitely coming back when in San Francisco area!

As Authentic as It Gets – An Absolute Gem in SF! 🇮🇹
As someone who was born and raised in Italy, I have a pretty high bar when it comes to Italian food outside of home. Il Piccolo Forno doesn't just meet that standard: it completely exceeds it. This place is as authentic as it gets.
From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere is warm, welcoming, and wonderfully family-oriented. The customer service is stellar across the board, and the owner, Giuseppe, is a fantastic host who makes you feel like family the second you sit down.
Now, let’s talk about the food, because it’s nothing short of incredible:
The Pasta: You can immediately tell it’s genuine homemade pasta. The texture, rich flavors, and sauce pairings in all the pasta dishes are absolute perfection.
The Pinsa: The Roman pinsa pizza is hands-down amazing. The crust has that ideal light, airy crunch that is so hard to find outside of Italy.
If you’re looking for true Italian hospitality and mind-blowing, traditional food in San Francisco, do yourself a favor and visit Il Piccolo Forno. Buon appetito 😋

A cosy restaurant serving genuinely delicious Italian fare. The meal began with complimentary bread and olive oil. The burrata arrived like a cloud - creamy, soft, and beautifully balanced with briny olives and sweet cherry tomatoes. The lobster stuffing of ravioli di aragosta was perfectly minced, and luxurious. The spaghetti alla carbonara was silky, and lifted by generous chunks of guanciale. We ended with an affogato that delivered the perfect finale - bold, sweet and beautifully comforting. The pastas did take a while to reach our table, but knowing everything was freshly prepared made the wait feel entirely worth it. The staff were warm, cheerful, and genuinely welcoming throughout our meal. This is one spot I’ll happily return to, no hesitation.

This place is everything I like about a small neighborhood Italian spot - simple, casual, and completely unpretentious.

Food - We ordered the lobster ravioli and a pasta with truffle sauce, and both were absolutely delicious. I’m honestly drooling just thinking about them again. The flavors were rich and comforting without feeling overly heavy.

Service - The staff were also very friendly, which added to the relaxed vibe of the place. The restaurant itself is very small, so it’s a good idea to make reservations beforehand.

Nothing fancy here, just really good food and a laid-back atmosphere. If you’re in the area and craving good Italian food, this spot is definitely worth a visit.

From the moment I walked into Piccolo Forno, I was greeted so warmly by the Italian servers that I immediately felt like family, even dining solo. The hospitality alone set the tone for what became one of the nicest dining experiences I’ve had.

I started with a glass of crisp Pinot Grigio and the complimentary bread basket served with absolutely incredible olive oil and balsamic, simple, authentic, and impossible to stop eating. The ambiance was vibrant and lively, like sitting in a charming Italian countryside trattoria filled with energy, conversation, and warmth.

The Caesar salad with anchovies was perfectly balanced and fresh, and the special fussili with seafood was outstanding—rich, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. Every bite tasted authentic, comforting, and deeply satisfying. Their chili oil was an absolute delight with the pasta. I almost didn’t ask for it because I didn’t want to offend anyone, but the waiter jokingly said, “Maybe you like it spicy,” and I’m so glad he did. That chili oil elevated the dish to another level. I know I will be dreaming about it.

To finish, the tiramisu was heavenly: light, creamy, and the perfect ending to an exceptional meal.

Piccolo Forno didn’t just serve amazing food — it gave me a genuine piece of Italy. From the atmosphere to the service to every course, this place is truly special.

Truly truly delicious food and the best way to end a lonnggg day. Very quick speed and every single dish we tried was just heaven on earth, specifically on my tongue. GO HERE!!!!! Best comfort food ever, you will NOT REGRET IT. Flavours exploded in my mouth when I tried the Dahi Puri, and I was blown away by the Momos, the Dal Makhani and Saag Paneer were impeccable and I will be recommending this place to all my SF friends.

Fantastic food, all fresh made and authentic in a laid back environment. There was only one waiter working when we went in for lunch but he absolutely hustled around. The chow mein was the star of the show, the spices used and chicken were completely unique to anything I've ever eaten!

After craving Tandoori Chicken for about 6 months...no shit 6 months!

This place has decent prices, but it’s still slightly higher than you would pay at most Indian places, especially if you compared to other cities with large amounts of Indian restaurants.
