top_reviews.content: Fantastic authentic jewish and Israeli cuisine in Berkeley! Definitely recommend checking out Saul’s if you are missing your Bubbe in Brooklyn. Of course you are paying for the authenticity ($26 for a sandwich w/ side), but that feels like a given in Berkeley. It is what it is. Don’t let it stop you from coming to try Saul’s. I recommend the corned beef reuben. You can skip the deserts and the latkes (too oily for my taste).
For the real ones, this place is the closest thing to Au Coquelet (shut down years ago). Cozy seating, yummy food, immaculate vibes. A little pricey, though! Also try their flourless chocolate cake.

Large open space, clean, tidy and well-attended. Thursdays there may be a Farmer's Market out front at noon, or one (weather permitting). We happen to be here on one of those less amenable weather days.
One visit only, so no in-depth review here.
Great Bagels and Smoked Salmon.
Well worth visiting and getting to know this place.
Staff are friendly, helpful, and try to keep my modifications from costing too much. The pastry cases are hard to pass up. Rugelach and Hamentashen come in 4 flavors, maracoons 2.
I am not eating everything to report, but the one chocolate Rugelach was dreamy.

I have loved coming to Saul’s for lunch/brunch with friends and family for 10 years. And even with the ownership change, the experience and food remain top notch! The pastrami is the best I’ve had. Get the knish, French fries and pickles. Do not sleep on their Bloody Mary as it is one of the best in the East Bay. Honestly can’t wait to go back

I really wanted to love this place, but the food was sub-par, though I did have a nice and attentive waiter, and the atmosphere was fine.

At least 1/3 of my pastrami sandwich was inedible fat & gristle (see posted pic).  While I never love picking that much fat off a sandwich, I especially didn't love it when the sandwich costs $26.95.  While, I wouldn't call the meat portion skimpy, I also wouldn't call it generous and thickly stacked like, you often get in a traditional Jewish deli, so to have a third of it be inedible was really a waste of money. The flavor was fine, but I didn't pay for a "fat" sandwich.

Also I got a latke for my side (an extra $2.95), and it was very greasy + rubbery and burned (see posted pic of inedible burned portions). It also had a slight fish flavor.  Made me wonder when the last time was they changed their frying oil?

I won't be going back - too disappointing.

top_reviews.content: Please don’t listen to the reviews. Got dal makhni and pav bhaji. Pav bhaji wasn’t authentic (tasted sweet?) and dal makhni was alright. If one review can change your mind about going to this restaurant, let it be this one. All the bad reviews are there for a reason. Please don’t take a chance thinking you’ll have a better experience.

Let’s start with the customer service, which is pretty much nonexistent.

We’ve been here multiple times, and every single time, we’ve actively tried to avoid getting this particular server because he simply does not know how to take an order properly. This time was easily the worst.

We ordered 3 appetizers and 2 main dishes, and within ONE MINUTE of placing our order, they brought out one of the main dishes. That honestly made me question whether the food is even being freshly prepared. We asked them to take it back and bring the appetizers first, as we had originally requested.

Then came the appetizers. We specifically asked for only the yogurt to be served on the side. Instead, they brought every single sauce on the side. So the appetizers basically came dry, and we had to assemble our own food at the table.

And somehow, it got even worse. Despite us very clearly saying that we wanted to eat the appetizers first, they brought the rest of the main courses out at the same time as the appetizers.

The most frustrating part? There wasn’t even a genuine apology or acknowledgment that they had messed up.

As for the food the biryani was basically coated in oil and food coloring. It had almost no salt, while the shrimp itself was unbelievably salty. The chili chicken was essentially just oil and sauce. There was barely any balance or flavor to it.

And throughout all of this, our server never once asked how the food was.

To make things even more uncomfortable, my friend was watching a show on his phone while we were waiting, and the server randomly started questioning him about what he was watching, asking, “Why are you watching a cartoon?” Like… why is that any of your business? Read the room.

The entire interaction felt dismissive and disrespectful.

We came back because we genuinely liked some of the food here, but after this experience, we’re done. Bad food can happen. Mistakes can happen. But when the service is consistently careless, the staff doesn’t take responsibility for mistakes, and the food itself is this disappointing, there’s really no reason to come back.

Save yourself the money and the frustration. AVOID THIS RESTAURANT AT ANY COST.

Osha Thai down by the Embarcadero is a decent spot, but with so much amazing Thai food in SF, it just doesn’t really stand out from the pack. Wow, so delicious!! We got the best roti canai I've ever had, and the service was stellar. We were there on a weekday, so the cool patio wasn't open, but the inside is beautiful too. It seems like a great place to host a business lunch, we saw several companies with multiple tables.

top_reviews.content: Super Duper Burger@Lower FIDI is located on Mission between Spear and Steuart streets not too far from YMCA "Barcadero," according to my experience, should be regarded of one of the best out of its 10 locations in The City. Super Duper Burgers was founded in 2010 in San Francisco's Castro district by Adriano Paganini with co-founder Eddie Sarti who have a joint vision to improve both quality and service of fast-food burger in the Bay Area. The company focuses on qualitative, locally sourced, and fresh ingredients, well cooked with a mission to provide a fast-food experience with "slow food values" and the fast-food chain has since grown to numerous locations beyond The City limits across the entire Bay Area from Napa, Concord to San Ho. Lower FIDI is conveniently connected to all transit and just one block from the Ferry Building. The location is clean, spacious (indoor and outdoor seatings) and accommodated with quality food and more importantly, a super friendly service team who will greet you as soon as you walk in. 😲My favorite order off its menu is its Chicken Sandwich with Chipotle Aioli on a fresh Ciabatta Bun with a small addon of Jalapenos for just $11.50. I have (and I am confident that you would as well) have nothing to complaint except they should place a "cookie jar" at the cashier so customers could effective place their appreciation tokens as quite often orders are placed via self-ordering kiosks. PS Regrettably, Super Duper locations on Market Downtown and Metron where I used to go have declined in both food quality and service. Service is terrible to no service at all ppl constantly chatting or joking around among themselves.  Its burgers are not well cooked (pinkish and "smooshy"). The same chicken sandwich is terribly prepared and lacks proper and quality ingredients at Metron that would make Lower FIDI a five-star location. 👼

I recently visited Super Duper Burger at 98 Mission Street in San Francisco, and I have to say, the experience was fantastic! I ordered their fried chicken sandwich, a side of fries, and a strawberry milkshake, and everything exceeded my expectations. The chicken was perfectly crispy and flavorful, the fries were hot and golden, and the strawberry milkshake was rich, creamy, and bursting with real strawberry flavor. The combination made for an incredibly satisfying meal. The service was friendly and quick, making the whole experience even better. I highly recommend checking out Super Duper Burger if you're in the area!

Delicious burgers! They do t have a gluten free bun but they offer a lettuce wrap. The burger is pretty juicy though so I would recommend a fork and knife. The garlic fries were delicious but heavy on the garlic so be prepared! The home made pickles were very unique and tangy. Would recommend!

Tasty burgers and plenty of seating.

After ordering on the kiosk, I received my mini burger about five minutes later. It was warm, on a toasted bun, and cooked perfectly. If you're looking to eat without human interaction, this is a place to do it.

The interior has plenty of seating, as does the outside. You can find some art and the nice signs that are standard at every location. However, it's not the cleanest Super Duper Burgers location. I recommend sitting inside, because it's cold outside and there are pigeons. This is a good place for a good burger.

Burger was moist and flavorful. Garlic fries were good as well. I wish they could have melted the cheese on the fries, but that is just my opinion. top_reviews.content: I do feel this place is overrated. The portions are tiny and overpriced. It was good, but not as amazing as expected. Had been to Flour + Water recently and definitely preferred it there. The Raviolo is one large ravioli drenched in melted butter for over $30. We also ordered the Corn Triangoli Pasta and Fiore Di Zucca Pizza. The pasta was good, the pizza was just ok. Felt we could've gotten a better meal elsewhere, but worth a try. Enjoyed the vibes at our table outside with a heated lamp, yet service was pretty slow. Difficult to get a reservation. Had to wait a while once arrived even with the reservation. Probably won't return.

We had an incredible experience at Cotogna! We arrived right at opening on a Tuesday without a reservation and were pleasantly surprised to get seats at the bar immediately.

Everything we ordered was excellent, but the pastas completely stole the show—they were easily the best part of the meal. The lamb ragù pasta was absolutely outstanding and one of the best pasta dishes we’ve ever had. The steak was cooked perfectly, the margarita pizza was fresh and delicious with an amazing crust, and the cannoli was the perfect sweet ending.

The service was just as memorable as the food. Everyone was warm, attentive, and welcoming, making the entire experience feel relaxed and enjoyable.

If you’re visiting San Francisco, Cotogna is absolutely worth a visit. We can’t wait to come back!

Exceptional Pasta & Open-Fire Cooking
Our dinner at Cotogna was a fantastic experience, highlighted by incredible technique and standout pasta dishes that absolutely stole the show.
We started with the salmon appetizer, which was a work of art. Not only was it visually stunning, but the flavors were balanced perfectly—light, bright, and the ideal way to wake up the palate and open up our appetite.
For the mains, the pastas were the undisputed champions of the night. Both dishes we tried were a massive hit, but the egg raviolo was truly outstanding. It was executed with absolute perfection—delicate, rich, and flawlessly cooked. The waiter did mention upfront that they are primarily known for their pastas, and they certainly delivered.
We also tried the funghi pizza, which unfortunately was a bit of a miss for us compared to the high bar set by the rest of the meal. On the other hand, the lamb was beautifully done. Cooked over an open fire, it had a wonderful smoky depth, and the accompanying sauces really bonded the entire dish together. While the wood-fired meat was impressive, the pasta here is so legendary that I’ll likely just stick to an all-pasta lineup next time.
Overall, Cotogna offers a beautiful atmosphere, excellent service, and some decadent pasta you can find. A must-visit!

Such a wonderful dinner at Cotogna with our family of four. We shared two appetizers and ordered three pastas, and everything was absolutely delicious. As an unexpected surprise, they even brought us an amazing funghi pizza on the house! top_reviews.content:
Would definitely come back here. Must try.

The Pretty Hot Wings were flavorful and juicy — not your flour or breadcrumb crust, more of a skin-crusted wing, with a tangy tamarind-based sauce.

The Nam Tok Beans were a very nice surprise — something I'd never tried before. Lightly coated, deep-fried beans with great seasoning, served with lettuce leaves and cucumber so you can make little lettuce wraps. A little on the spicier side, but I loved it.

The Pad Kee Mao was the best dish of the night — perfectly seasoned flat noodles, great aroma, full of umami. Loved it.

The Masaman Curry had a huge chunk of beef with small potatoes and shallots in a rich, creamy, flavorful gravy, and the beef was perfectly cooked. Flavor was on point — though $60 for it is steep.

Sticky rice was basic and perfect.

The Black Rice Pudding dessert was something I wasn't sure about, but it was amazing — crispy puffed rice, strawberry jam, a peanuty flavor, and sesame. Very unique and great tasting.

Will definitely order the pad kee mao again.

Just had a really good bowl at Kin Khao in San Francisco while sitting outside. The presentation was beautiful rich broth, soft-boiled egg with a perfect golden yolk, tender chashu, bamboo shoots, fresh greens, nori, and sesame seeds. Everything tasted clean and well-balanced. The broth had depth without feeling heavy, and the toppings were clearly made with care.
Sitting outside made it even better, watching the city go by. Service was friendly and the whole experience felt special without trying too hard. If you’re looking for thoughtful, high-quality food in SF, this place delivers. Already thinking about coming back.

Cute, cozy, and flavorful place. The service is professional and warm. The menu has dishes that you will recognize but with a fun and exciting twist, and there are some other dishes that are their personal creations. Everything is well thought out and balanced with textures, temperatures, colors and flavors. The dishes spark your taste buds with umami, bitter, sweet, salty, and sour ingredients. Its a full experience. Their wine list is perfectly curated to dance with the menu and take it to another level.

Pretty hot wings were a pleasant surprise. Khao Yum presented an interesting combination of flavors and texture. Green curry rabbit is a venture for me, meat is tender easily separated from bones, meat balls in the curry more taste. Pork belly was very good. All dishes were well prepared. This restaurant is probably the most authentic Thai restaurant that we have been to in the States. Between the three of us, we got the mushroom hor mok (highly recommend!), charred eggplant salad, yaowaraj noodle‍, and massaman nuea. top_reviews.content:
La Note is *the* brunch spot in Berkeley for a reason. The patio is lovely, the service was great, and I’ll absolutely be back to try other menu items.

That said, I ordered the Lemon Gingerbread Pancakes with Poached Pears, and my expectations and reality had a brief disagreement.

When someone says “pancakes,” I imagine soft, tender, fluffy clouds that happily absorb maple syrup. These were more like:

* Dense
* Cakey
* Crumbly
* Heavy

The texture reminded me less of a pancake and more of a gingerbread muffin that accidentally got promoted to breakfast.

The flavors were nice, the poached pears were beautiful, but the interior texture wasn’t for me. If you love gingerbread cake, you may love these. If you’re expecting a classic fluffy pancake experience, you may be surprised.

Would I come back to La Note? Absolutely.

Would I order the Lemon Gingerbread Pancakes again?

Not unless they come with a warning label that says:

“Attention: This pancake identifies as cake.”

Really adorable French cafe. Very busy Sunday morning for breakfast, but getting a table inside worked out well for us. Definitely faster than waiting for the patio.

The service was excellent: fun, friendly and attentive.

The food was solid but not incredible. The baguette with goat cheese and honey was delicious, but the breakfast sausages (apple and spicy - I forget the actual names) were underwhelming. The Bloody Mary was spicy and good.

Pricy but good. We’d go back.

Five stars all the way. The breakfast potatoes were crispy and perfectly seasoned, finished with fragrant herbs and mellow roasted garlic that added a rich depth. The scrambled eggs had a light, creamy texture that felt comforting and well prepared. The pear and gingerbread pancakes were not my favorite choice, so next time I would try a different flavor combination with a stronger fruit presence. The atmosphere felt warm and inviting, and the service was attentive and friendly. A lovely spot to relax and enjoy a satisfying brunch experience.
It’s my first time to try French food and I like the taste. The pancake is soft and not so sweet (they provided me with syrup). The oat meal is like a bowl of light sweet porridge, which is ok.

I had eggs benedict and honestly, the highlight for me was the herb and garlic potatoes on the side—so flavorful and perfectly cooked. It’s amazing how something so simple can taste that good. The menu being in French added a nice touch, and the cozy ambiance made it even better, especially with the rainy weather outside. A really warm and satisfying experience overall.

top_reviews.content:
I checked out Tempest Bar & Box Kitchen on a Thursday around 10 p.m. with some friends after finding it on Google as one of the top-rated spots in the area. The photos looked great, and I was excited to try it out.

Unfortunately, our experience didn’t quite match the expectations — and to be fair, this is just based on the specific time we visited. When we arrived, there didn’t seem to be any floor staff managing the tables. Almost every open table was dirty, with leftover food, debris, and empty glasses. We genuinely couldn’t find a clean place to sit, which was a bit surprising given that the space itself looks really cool and has a great vibe.

We ended up heading to the bar where there were only two available seats for our group of four, so we made it work with two sitting and two standing. The bartender seemed friendly but was clearly very busy. Despite waiting for close to 10 minutes, we weren’t able to get service — even though the venue itself wasn’t particularly busy at the time, with only a couple of tables occupied (though the bar area was full).

At that point, we decided to leave.

That said, I do want to highlight that the aesthetic of the bar is really nice — it has a vibrant, laid-back energy that I can see being great on a different night. I’d be open to giving it another try in the future, but based on this visit, the lack of cleanliness and service made it a disappointing experience.

Solid food and a laid-back bar atmosphere. The burger and fries were the highlight—cooked just right, full of flavor, and served hot. The fries paired perfectly with the burger and made for a really satisfying meal.

One thing that really stands out is the drink selection. There are plenty of options to choose from, whether you’re into beer, cocktails, or something simple. It’s a great place to grab a drink and relax with friends or unwind after a long day.

The vibe is casual and welcoming, with a clean space and a fun, no-frills atmosphere that fits perfectly with the location. The staff were friendly and kept things moving smoothly, adding to the overall experience.

Between the great food, wide drink selection, and relaxed environment, Tempest Bar & Box Kitchen is definitely worth checking out. A solid go-to spot in San Francisco for a good burger and a drink. Highly recommend!

I also love that all locations have art pieces of Zachary’s in different media, it’s very fun and unique!

Supposedly this restaurant has been open since 1983, I’m not sure how they survived for that long if their pizzas were like what we had eaten. The place was still relatively crowded near closing, and was decorated with nostalgic memorabilia. Caesar salad was pretty good but standard and on the heavier side. The two pizzas we got were the thin style Rustic Italian and the Chicago style Zachary’s special. The Rustic Italian had pretty good flavor and I liked the whole garlic cloves, though it could be more roasted. The biggest problem was the crust; it was so granular it almost felt like it could break apart easily, and it did not have that pizza char that it could greatly benefit from. The Zachary’s special was very disappointing, it was filled with basically just canned tomato sauce with very sparse sausage (that was just steamed inside the pizza) and other toppings. The flavor was just sweet and lacked any depth. The crust was even worse on this one, and was just a chore to even finish. The prices for these were also more on the expensive side at around 25-35 dollars per 10 inch pizza. There are many other pizza places you can go to in Berkeley before even considering this one.
Even their smallest pizza good for 2-3 people. Great quality ingredients. They told us how long since some were deep dish. Six people. Everyone loved their choice.

top_reviews.content: Classic student friendly pricing, this is the spot for Italian food. Lunch special is the way to go , the portion sizing is on point, easily sharable. Godfather’s favorite is what I ordered and it was bomb. The side salad is a nice touches. I would def return here and try more of the menu. The calzone’s and pizza looks great as well. Paying with cash is the pro move to avoid surcharge.

Located in the student Asian ghetto.
Won’t go wrong with any of their late-night Italian cuisine. Fast processing queue with multiple cooks!
Good price for a generous portion, and it looks great and tastes fantastic.
The meat is fresh as well.

Food was good and satisfying at an acceptable price point. Service was super friendly, kind, and deserving of a generous tip. The restaurant was clean; seating was very tight (not their fault that they are popular). Each pasta was cooked to perfection, not mushy. Sauces were flavorful, and meats were fairly tender. Portions were the perfect ratios of carbs, protein, veggies. Love the roasted garlic cloves on the bread! Everyone who was with me said they would come back again.

Food isn't very high quality but it's close to the bars so its price for quantity is good value. Discount for cash and extremely packed on a Friday night so food takes a while.

I got their pesto calzone for $15. Huge, but not very good (I got sick of it after a few bites) and took over 20min for a takeout place.

The pesto was oily and a bit bland. Chicken and the thick dough tasted cold and very, very dry.  Ambiance is not nice to sit at, feels like an indoor taco truck.

This place probably isn't in my top 5 for the area because its not too good and it takes a long time, but if someone wanted to eat here I wouldn't argue against it.

Absolutely love this place! I can see why there are plenty of students here! The food here is very filling and comes with huge portions! I do have to say the salad needs a bit more dressing as there's not enough. Nonetheless it's still a 5/5.

top_reviews.content: True to it’s promise, Nations is there for you always! The food, the atmosphere, and the service transports you back into a classic American diner. I love the one egger(pictured) and the PIE!!! So much food for a great price. Our waitress, Raquel, was incredibly sweet and helpful as well. Love this place!!!!

I've heard their pies are really good, so we got one for the birthday cake. We ordered the Cheesecake with Blueberry Topping Pie, made with cream cheese in a hand-pressed graham cracker crust, topped with blueberry compote. It tasted really amazing, it's sweet, with a subtle lemon aroma that would slowly come through. I'd recommend enjoying it with a cup of tea or coffee. I can't wait to try their other pies!

My experience today at this particular nations was amazing!!! Overall the food was great. Socorro attended me very well and treated me and my family as if we were her family. Really did appreciate that!! Overall a great nations location

Such great breakfast! the place is clean, spacious and has lots of free parking. Everything on the menu is excellent. Soccoro and Christine are the nicest employees and are great cooks! One of the last affordable and still delicious spots on the Bay Area! They also have great pies, coffee and burgers- but we come for the all day breakfast!!! We love Nations Berkeley!

I had a great experience at Nations in Berkeley. The food was fresh, hot, and exactly what you expect every time — solid breakfast and great pies.

What really stood out was the service. Socorro and Araceli were both incredibly friendly, attentive, and welcoming from the moment we walked in. They made sure everything was correct with our order and checked in to see if we needed anything else. It’s always nice to see staff who genuinely care about customer service.

I’ll definitely be coming back. Thank you for the great experience!

name: HINODEYA Ramen & Bar Downtown
address: 680 Clay St, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States

google.name: HINODEYA Ramen & Bar Downtown
google.address: 680 Clay St, San Francisco, CA 94111, United States

top_reviews.content:
A small coincidence on my first day in San Francisco turned into my favourite spot. I needed to check in to the hostel but it was too early, so I searched for ramen on Google Maps and found HINODEYA nearby. Good reviews, so I gave it a try. The pork katsu ramen was one of the best I have had, the umami flavour was amazing.

On my last day in San Francisco I went back, exactly two weeks later. This time I ordered the Spicy Miso, equally good. What makes this place special is the staff. Genuine, warm, and you feel seen even if you are eating alone. The kitchen staff joke around and seem to enjoy themselves, and that energy spreads through the whole room.

A nice detail: when guests arrive, the staff beat a taiko, a traditional Japanese drum with roots in festivals and temple ceremonies. Historically it was used to create energy and mark important moments, and here it becomes a personal and memorable way to welcome guests.

Two visits, same high standard both times. Highly recommended, and it has also sparked an interest in exploring more Japanese food in Japan itself.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Such an amazing experience dining here! I was solo and sat at the bar. Had the house ramen…seriously some of the best ramen I’ve ever had, and definitely the best Chashu pork I’ve ever had in a ramen. They have little crispy’s you can add to your ramen on the table, DO IT! It elevates the dish so much. Also tried the Matcha Beer. Love matcha so had to give it a try! They whisked matcha in a ceremonial bowl and then added it to my Asahi beer. Paloma was the absolute sweetest server and was the cherry on top to an amazing lunch. She was so sweet and attentive, and made me feel like family! I can’t wait to come back here.

We came for dinner and ordered a variety of dishes. I had the Hinodeya Ramen, while we also shared chicken karaae, takoyaki, and gyoza. For drinks, we tried the Matcha Beer, Yuzu soda, and Ume soda.

The ramen was decent, but the broth wasn't particularly memorable.

The standout dish was definitely the chicken karaage. It was crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and incredibly tender.

As for the drinks, it was my first time trying Matcha Beer, and it had a unique and interesting flavor. The Yuzu Soda and Ume Soda were both refreshing and delicious, though they leaned toward the sweeter side.

The food came so fast and was so delicious. The perfect lunch place.

The chicken karaage as a starter was perfectly cooked. And the spicy miso soup was so flavourful. Absolutely loved every sip. The pork belly was slightly crunchy but so tasty.

This is an amazing Japanese restaurant with authentic Japanese flavors. I had the spicy miso ramen with corn and butter, along with the takoyaki, and everything was delicious!!
A special thank you to Paloma and Nobel for their excellent service. I truly had a wonderful lunch here and enjoyed every dish. Highly recommended!

reviews_snippets.content: "The tofu and crispy greens in the creamy vegan bowl was amazing."

name: Lapisara Eatery

google.name: Lapisara Eatery

google.description: Chic destination serving American classics for three meals a day, plus a few Thai dinner dishes.

top_reviews.content: Great brunch place if you want a fusion breakfast. Good cappuccino and iced caramel macchiato (with a sweet teddy bear floating). We had the ‘Holy Chili Bomb Basil Omelette (a fancy name for a omelette with Thai Basil ground Chicken filling), the Tom Yum Burrito (self explanatory), and the Chicken Waffle (too much of syrup). Everything was pretty good. We would’ve liked it a bit more spicy but it’s not a dealbreaker at all. Definitely a good place to go. Area is also free of homeless people (I guess being in Nob Hill 😇). Enjoy and let me know if you agree with my review if you do visit.

Great Saturday morning brunch spot! We didn’t have a reservation, but adding our name to the iPad waitlist at the door was seamless, and we were seated in just 5–10 minutes.
​The vibe was lively and nice, and the service was super quick and efficient. We tried the avocado toast, the Sweet Dream, and an ube latte—everything tasted amazing! The presentation was gorgeous with edible flowers on the plates, and the drinks came in the cutest bear cups.
​Highly recommend Lapisara for a fun and delicious brunch in SF! 🌸🐻

An overall better taste than other good brunch we tried. We ordered pacific scramble, steak and egg, and fried chicken waffle. The scramble is fresh and the shrimp is juicy and almost crunchy. Steak has a funny durian flavor, my girlfriend find it a little weird. Salad is slight marinated with lemon and honey? But it was great and has a more smooth texture. Waffle is flavored just spot on, I can’t stop eating it.

Came here on a Saturday for brunch.

I got the Holy Chili Bomb Basil Omelette. It had ground chicken and veggies inside, and the chicken and basil were the flavors that stood out. I wouldn’t call it spicy at all. The omelette felt small for the price and there wasn’t much filling inside.

It came with a side of potatoes that were really good. They had a nice crisp on the outside and were soft on the inside. I also got a regular coffee, and they do unlimited refills.

The place was busy for brunch, and I liked the bear theme. Some of the coffees came in bear-shaped glasses, and some of the lattes had a decorative bear made out of ice.

The food presentation and taste was out of this world! I loved it so so much and I would definitely recommend this restaurant to everyone I know. I ordered the Sweet Dream Belgium waffle and it was truly so delicious. I especially loved the Ube Latte not just because of the cute bear but also because it tasted like authentic Ube. The staff were really nice and accommodating as well!

reviews_snippets.content: "Cosy space Great and friendly local place Quick service Good tasting food"

name: La Mission
address: 1255 University Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702, United States

google.name: La Mission
google.address: 1255 University Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702, United States
google.description: Busy joint offering burritos & tacos in small, bright digs with painted walls plus outdoor seating.

top_reviews.content:
We stopped by this restaurant late at night, around 10 PM, for dinner. I wasn’t extremely hungry, so I ordered three tacos — though I could only finish two and ended up taking one home. My friend also ordered a few tacos along with a Baja fish taco and another item.

The place has a very casual, chic, student-friendly vibe and offers a wide variety of Mexican dishes on the menu. The food felt fresh and made from scratch, which I really appreciated.

Among everything I tried, the chorizo taco was definitely the standout. It was flavorful, juicy, and perfectly seasoned. I also tried carnitas and al pastor. Usually al pastor is my all-time favorite, but this version didn’t quite match the ones I’ve had in Mexico City. Still, it wasn’t bad by any means.

They had a salsa station where you could pick your own sauces, though I noticed they didn’t offer the usual grilled onions or spring onions that many more traditional Mexican spots serve. Overall, the restaurant felt more like a California-style Mexican place with its own twist rather than a fully authentic Mexican taqueria.

That said, the freshness and quality of the food really stood out. I’d definitely go back, especially for the chorizo tacos. Overall, a really nice late-night food spot.

This is a MEXICAN restaurant. The very  kindest and nicest service. The food is just way off the high end of the charts. The atmosphere... Fantastic. 6/5. Across the board. They have a chocolate horchata that is the best I have ever had.

This place is conveniently located right on University Avenue. The staff is extremely friendly and they offer many homemade items including homemade corn bread, etc. I ordered the steak nachos and they were perfect. Wait times were non existent and the service was very quick and professional. Will be back!

Quick service and sweet staff.
However I felt the legumbres vegetarian burrito could have had more flavor.
The chocolate cake was good but the icing was maybe a touch too sweet.
Husband liked his chicken burrito.
Lovely outdoor seating area.

Great burritos and other Mexican food. They’ve got beer and wine too.
Nice outdoor patio area. It’s screened off from University Ave with plants but you can hear some traffic.
Staff here are super nice and friendly.

name: Oren's Hummus
address: 71 3rd St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

google.name: Oren's Hummus

top_reviews.content: First time dining at Oren. I had the lamb skewers and the schnitzel with hummus and fluffy pitas. The hummus was amazingly rich and smooth, that is new to me. The lamb skewers were well seasoned and no gaminess! Love it 😍. The schnitzel is well made and crunchy. Overall I thought my meal was wonderfully cooked. Definitely recommend this place. This restaurant is centrally located in downtown SF and walking distance from union square.

Oren's Hummus is one of the best Mediterranean restaurants I've been to in San Francisco! The atmosphere is warm, modern, and inviting, and the service was outstanding from start to finish. We ordered the chicken rice bowl and the kebab rice bowl, and both were incredibly fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Every bite was delicious, and the portions were generous. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients. I'll definitely be coming back the next time I'm in San Francisco. Highly recommended!

Located in the heart of Union Square, this is such a cute and cozy spot with great food. We ordered the hummus chicken, and sweet potatoes, and everything was delicious. We were visiting from NYC, were a bit jet-lagged, and celebrated our anniversary here, which made the evening even more special.

One standout was the spicy dip served with the starter—I haven’t had anything quite like it before, and it was absolutely delicious.

The only downside was the service. It was a bit slow, and we often had to call someone over, even for something as simple as getting drinking water. Other than that, we had a lovely experience and would definitely recommend giving this place a try.

I lost track of how many times I said “mmm” while eating this meal!

My server was friendly and very knowledgeable about the menu. He had great suggestions. After taking my order, he returned with a complimentary snack that was pickled red pepper and I think cabbage.

I wanted to try 2 different types of hummus, so I got the smaller side portions of the Jaffa hummus with pine nuts, and the Muhammara hummus. OMG, the Jaffa version is the best hummus I’ve ever had outside of the Carmel Market in Tel Aviv! It’s delicious and airy, and next time I will get a huge portion of just that.

I had never tried Muhammara before and it did not disappoint. It’s very flavorful with a little bit of sweet, heat, tangy & savory flavors. It came with crunchy pita strips. I ordered extra white pita bread for my dips, and highly recommend it. It was soft and also identical to what I enjoyed in Israel.

Near the floor by many tables were outlets, which made charging phones or devices easy for tourists. The meal was pricy, but worth it for me as a treat.

The food was so flavourful and delicious, absolutely recommend it.

The chicken hummus was delicious, but the main attraction was the australian lamb. Marinated in harissa, this was so delicious we loved it. Too bad there was only two pieces of roasted vegetables, I would’ve eaten a side dish only with roasted veggies from this place!!

top_reviews.content:
I hadn't been to Picante since the remodel so I was looking forward to seeing what had changed. The remodel is fine, definitely more of a modern aesthetic. I remember the food being good but pricey and I'd say now they are closer to being average and pricey. I ordered two shrimp tacos which cost $6.95 each! I was expecting a hefty portion of shrimps for that price. Each taco came with two sad looking shrimps with the rest of the taco being filled with salsa and slaw. I also had an horchata which was fine but it's hard to mess up horchata. I gave it an extra star just for the helpful staff. Overall I was very disappointed with Picante and won't be coming back for future visits with so many amazing Mexican places in Richmond and Oakland.

Recommendation: If you want the most delicious shrimp tacos go to Tacos el Tucan in Richmond, top notch.

The food is great here. The server is fast/average, but the register was is SLOW. They could probably handle a slightly faster pace.

There is a hot sauce refrigerator where you can get three different levels of "hot". Be bold, try the habanero! It doesn't hurt going in or out!

They recently completed a remodel, but unfortunately the atmosphere changed. It seems a bit too "upscale", even if it looks REALLY nice inside and out.

i’ve been coming here for many years and i went again last night with family for a lovely meal.  at first i did not care for the new renovation, and strongly preferred the original picante with red vinyl booths, papeles hanging, viewable tortilla station, etc.  i am starting to better appreciate how nice it now is though in a different way.  we enjoyed our food a lot.  this is high quality food beautifully presented. staff are always friendly and efficient. food comes out so so quick. we have not had to wait in line at the front but even if u do, the food comes out very quickly once you order.  overall id say tho we do miss the old picante we will be returning soon! thanks to the staff for always serving us a beautiful meal. shout out to Alex for his warm hospitality!

It is consistently good. During covid they went thru some changes trying to make things work and come together... They're better now than they ever were! The food is really good! The atmosphere is clean, open, indoor and outdoor seating. The service is quick and efficient. The bathrooms are maintained well. (When that changes, there's a problem).

Picante is one of the best Mexican restaurants in Berkeley. Their food is good and tasty, but it’s a bit pricey, which is why I knocked their rating down a star. Street parking is difficult during most of the day, but there is a small parking lot across the street and to the south about half a block. That often fills up too though. They have a bar and a lot of alcohol to select from and I see people drinking margaritas, but I’ve never tried them. The chips are just so so, they’re thick and a little greasy. I suspect there are some people that like them as they are not the normal chips you’d get in a Mexican place, but they’re just too greasy. The salsas are in the fridge by the door and they are pretty good. Everything else I’ve had here has been good, my favorite are the mole enchiladas, which are probably some of the best mole that I’ve had. They make good guacamole, and good salads as well. If it’s not too cold out, there’s an outdoor seating place.

top_reviews.content: I’ve been coming here for years. I went two days in a row this week for them Lion’s Mane Sliders. 10/10 I recommend. The Crispy buns with cabbage, the swamp sauce and pickles. The lion’s mane is so tender and breading has the perfect crunch. Go get that.

Disclaimer: I am NOT a vegan but wowwwww! I’ve been turned onto it because the food here is better than any southern cooking I’ve ever had. Love the ambiance, old school hip hop playing, delicious cocktails and amazing service. Highly recommend the vegan Mac and the beignets!!! Chefs kiss

100% VEGAN awesomeness!!!
What more can be said?  All the food is concocted and made right there. No beyond or impossible meat. They have their own unique menu, with unique flavors, so simply stuff you can’t find anywhere else and DELICIOUS!!Go support these people!

Souley Vegan is a great spot for comforting vegan food right near Jack London Square. The fried steak was the standout, crispy on the outside with a satisfying texture, and the mashed potatoes were rich and flavorful without feeling too heavy. Portions were filling, and the large indoor dining space made it easy to settle in.
I went in the morning and there was about a 15 to 20 minute wait with just one group ahead, which suggested they were a bit light on staff. That said, the team was friendly and welcoming throughout.
The location is especially convenient if you are coming from the ferry, making it an easy stop for a casual meal. One practical note: the app did not work for takeout orders in the morning, but calling in works since they handle to go orders all day.
Overall, a reliable option for hearty vegan comfort food, and I would definitely go back. Might be THE best in Oakland!
I’ve been a fan of Souley Vegan for many years. Some of the best vegan soul food you’ll ever have. Highly recommended!

reviews_snippets.content: "I'm a happy guy after bbq tofu, mac & cheese, red beans & rice and a salad."

top_reviews.content:
Shan Dong is definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for delicious Chinese food in Oakland. The food is flavorful, fresh, and packed with taste across the dishes we ordered. Service was quick and efficient, and despite the restaurant being busy, we didn’t have to wait long to be seated as a party of two.

The portions are very generous, so it’s easy to have leftovers or share a few dishes. Considering the quality, quantity, and overall experience, it offers excellent value for the money. And whatever you order, make sure you request the handmade noodles—they’re absolutely worth it and really elevate the meal.

I’d happily come back the next time I’m craving great Chinese food.

Came on a Sunday around 5:30 and waited around 40 minutes to get seated.

Loved the string beans- great flavor with a mix of chili oil and garlic, couldn’t stop eating it cause it was so addicting! I ordered the pork chow mein with the hand pulled noodles - HUGE portion (I had leftover that lasted me 2 meals) and the noodles are super thick and chewy which I love, no other place do their noodles like this place!

Note to self: make sure to mix the noodles before eating since the sauce is accumulated in the bottom to actually get the flavor!

A very delicious place in Oakland’s Chinatown. I had their shandong chicken, dry fried green beans, salt and pepper pork and chicken and they were all excellent. The shandong chicken is your typical orange chicken, but they did something to the sauce that gives it this dark toasted caramel taste to it. The green beans I highly recommend, it’s lightly fried and then stir fried with their sauce that gives it a rich and umami flavor. Their salt and pepper options, my only complaint is that I wish they gave more protein. But other than that, a great place to stop by in Chinatown if you’re ever in the area.

I've been here a few times and don't really get the hype. The atmosphere is great due to the place always being packed, but honestly the food leaves something to be desired. Their famous hand pulled noodles are unevenly shaped to the point that some parts are cooked while others are inedibly hard. Wok dishes often lean super salty. There are better options in the area.
Absolutely delicious!! Onion pancake & dumplings were amazing. Chicken was 🔥 too. Noodles were a lil spicy but nothing we couldn’t handle. Ordered on Doosdash & it did not disappoint! 🥡🥢

top_reviews.content:
5 star experience for everything!
Excellent customer service
They missed 3 of my items and I had to wait which I didn't mind but the staff gave me a free shake for my patience which is so fun and nice
Atmosphere is great outdoor and indoor seating when I went there was a parade happening outside it was fun to look at while eating the food was so good greatly recommended the spicy chicken sandwich and ranch and bacon fries and of course the cookies and cream milkshake they gave me! Tried sweet potato fries for the first time here at the melt absolutely delicious!

After a lackluster meal at Mel's the night before, I decided to search for a top rated location this time. I came across The Melt which was heavily favored and rightfully so.

Although the location was busy, I was able to walk right up and use one of the self service kiosks to place my order. The interface was easy and helpful. I ordered a double BBQ Bacon Meltburger and a Cookies and Cream shake. Within a few minutes my order was ready and it looked great. This burger was huge, and since it cost 18 bucks, it better be! I could barely bite into this burger it was so massive. It was fantastic, so much flavor and quality meat. The shake was equally as great and helped wash down this tasty burger. The food was a little pricey, but you definitely get your money's worth. This is the perfect spot for a lunch or late night grub. Would definitely revisit if I had the chance because some of the other meals look just as good.

I have been a long time customer at this location for at least 7 years and have never felt more disrespected than when I went to pick up a burger and fries on the night of July 4th 2026. I ordered a double melt burger with fries add bacon to the Burger with the emphasis extra crispy bacon please. After my order was complete I looked at the counter and observed that the bacon was not extra crispy. I told the woman that said she was the supervisor and she completely ignored me. After about a minute I asked what's going on and so-called supervisor said "it's coming up, we dont need this. If you dont like it we can refund you and you can get out." Remind you all of this because I asked for extra crispy bacon that they could not produce. At that point I told her to refund me and I will be leaving a review. The gentleman that took my order initially told me they weren't taking cash orders as well as all bathrooms were closed which was not the case. Ultimately they refunded my order, kicked me out of the restaurant and I left there hungry and empty-handed all because I asked for extra crispy bacon. I implore supervisors and upper management to look at the cameras and review this you'll find that everything I'm saying is factual. What an embarrassing experien.
It’s still a $20 grilled cheese, but it wasn’t overly complicated or fancy but it was in fact, delicious! 🤤 yes… yes I would have another!

Randomly wandered in here, and was very pleased with the food options.
Its is burgers, fries, etc. so don't expect a lot of non-meat things on the menu. Prices are also higher than your chain places, and also because this is in SanFran.
Ordering was pretty fast and efficient, and the staff working there both times I stopped in were on point. (You can order via kiosk or at the counter).
Food tasted very fresh, the fountain drink options were local flavors of pop, which I really liked.
Seating was fairly plentiful, and the security & regular staff kept the location pretty clean & tidy.
Definetly a restaurant I'd dine at regularly, just to try all the various items on the menu.

top_reviews.content: Our first time here and it was amazing! Sunday  all you can eat Buffet was an amazing sampler of their delicious food! I really liked the juicey Carnitas and Birria! The Posole was filled with delicious ham hocks (watch out for the bones) and hominy and veggies.

Fun place with great environment.  The food is really good, I had the crispy taco (grilled beef) and it was amazing. The only knock would be, it is a litte too greasy. I also had the street corn, it was good.
Service is really good and fast.
Also I came in a Tuesday which is all you can eat from the taco bar, only $15 and kids under eat free.
You have to try. The Churo desert,  best I've ever had.

Came in on a sunday at 1pm, pretty crowded so i was on a waitlist and was able to get a seat by 2:30pm. No problems with the free parking garage nearby.

Regional Review: Farmhouse Kitchen Thai

A midday stop brought my tracking to Jack London Square for a busy lunch session. The front-of-house execution was seamless; the hostess politely greeted us and offered an immediate choice between the interior or the deck. We chose the outdoor patio and secured an excellent table with a direct, unobstructed view of the waterfront. The patio layout is exceptionally pleasant and well-shaded, and they stage the tables with beautiful plates that are perfect for sharing. While we opted for the fresh air, the interior design—featuring a polished counter and well-spaced table seating—also looked highly refined and inviting.

Service pacing was sharp. The staff handled multiple table check-ins, kept waters continuously replenished, and deployed our dishes remarkably fast. It is a fantastic, high-energy atmosphere all around.

Hat Yai Fried Chicken: A definitive winner on the table. The execution on the chicken was flawless, achieving an incredibly crisp crunch while retaining a perfectly juicy interior. It pairs beautifully with the striking blue rice. The curry was delicious and well-balanced, and the accompanying roti was honestly some of the best I have ever evaluated—immensely flaky and perfectly cooked.

Pork Pad Thai: This classic baseline dish was excellent. We swapped in pork as our primary protein, and the flavor balance was spot-on. It delivered great traditional depth without veering into the common pitfall of being overly sweet.

Cocktail Flight: The aesthetic presentation on this flight of four different drinks was visually striking and well-crafted. Overall, the drinks did the job, but the flavor profiles on the palate were a bit of a mixed bag; one of the specific variants had a heavy, medicinal finish that honestly reminded me of mouthwash. Next time around, a crisp beer would likely be the better pairing.

Sharp service, rapid execution, and a fantastic view. The kitchen proves it can back up its vibrant, high-end aesthetic with genuine technical proficiency. While the food, service, and atmosphere were all undeniable 5-star caliber, the mixed note on the cocktail flight slightly tempers the overall score. I would absolutely return to explore more of the menu, and for that exceptional chicken and roti alone.

top_reviews.content:
Dumpling Home definitely lived up to the hype. I came on a Tuesday evening with no reservation and was seated quickly. The outdoor seating was a nice bonus and made for a great dining experience in San Francisco's cool weather.

The highlight of the meal was the Numb & Spicy Pork Xiao Long Bao. The soup dumplings were fresh, juicy, packed with flavorful broth, and absolutely delicious. They also serve complimentary hot jasmine tea, which pairs really well with the meal, and the Thai iced tea was creamy and refreshing.

The Beef Brisket Noodle Soup was flavorful with tender beef and handmade noodles, although the broth was a little oilier than I personally prefer.

A tip for first-time visitors: don't skip the black vinegar and fresh ginger that come with the soup dumplings. Dip each dumpling lightly, bite a small hole first to sip the hot broth, then enjoy the rest. It really elevates the experience.

Overall, excellent food, friendly service, easy seating, and I'd definitely come back. Highly recommended if you're looking for authentic handmade dumplings in San Francisco.

overall a decent spot for Chinese dumplings. The soup dumplings were good, but if you’re used to really good Asian/Chinese food, I’d say most of the dishes were fairly average rather than exceptional.

The pan-fried dumplings, though, were amazing, easily the standout of the meal and something I’d absolutely come back for. Service was great as well. The restaurant itself is pretty casual and nothing particularly special atmosphere-wise, but you’re really here for the dumplings.

Overall, a solid meal and worth trying, especially for the pan-fried dumplings.

These are, without exaggeration, some of the best soup dumplings I've had in recent memory. Dumpling Home, tucked into a corner spot on Gough St in San Francisco's Hayes Valley, earns every bit of the hype  and the Michelin Bib Gourmand it's been awarded for good reason.

Every single thing I tried was packed with flavor. There's nothing phoned-in on this menu. The xiao long bao are the standout: thin, supple skins that hold together just long enough to deliver a spoonful of intensely flavorful broth the second you bite in. Chefs are wrapping and folding everything by hand all day, and you can taste the difference. These aren't your standard one-note pork dumplings either; they go beyond with chicken, beef, and a Sichuan-inspired numbing pork that's become a personal favorite.

This is a walk-in-only spot, so yes, there will likely be a wait, but don't let that stop you. It's worth every minute. Grab a table, order generously, and prepare to leave full and thoroughly impressed.

If you're anywhere near Hayes Valley and you haven't been, fix that immediately. Go here.

Had the Fresh cucumber with garlic sauce (just wanted to eat the whole plate, couldn’t stop eating them), pan fried dumplings (crispy on the bottom and steamed on top; different crunch profile with good flavor), soup dumplings were very good, had nice big red spoon to eat the dumplings, they a soy sauce, ginger, vinegar dipping sauce. Overall, it was amazingly good. We were able to come and had no wait for a party of 4.

Went for lunch on a weekend. Waited about 10 minutes for a table which wasn’t bad. We got to sit outdoors along the sidewalk. Service was prompt and efficient. Be sure to ask for the chili oil as it adds an extra zing. We ordered the numb and spicy pork xiao long bao, steamed chicken and mushroom dumplings, and the friend beef bao. The broth in the xiao long bao had the perfect tingle without being overwhelmingly spicy. The steamed dumplings we the most plain but paired well with the chili oil. The pan friend bao were piping hot and packed full of flavour. Everything was so fresh and flavourful. Worth waiting in the line

top_reviews.content: Boulevard is an iconic waterfront restaurant on Mission Street, San Francisco.  The main dining room is classy and warm.  Staff is friendly, professional and accommodating.  Food quality of the beautifully plated California cuisine is better than average.  The decent 3-course dinner is reasonably priced at USD 128/person.

I’ve visited Boulevard twice — once for dinner and once for cocktails with a friend — and both experiences were wonderful.

The dinner was absolutely excellent. Every dish was beautifully prepared, and the quality of the ingredients was outstanding. You can truly tell that great attention is paid to every detail.

I would make just one small suggestion: considering the elegance and high standard of the restaurant, upgrading the wine glasses to more refined ones would enhance the overall experience even further.

The bar was fantastic as well. The staff were incredibly warm and welcoming. My friend ordered a cocktail that she didn’t love, and the bartenders were happy to replace it without any hesitation.

And the pâté was simply outstanding — absolutely delicious.

Boulevard is a true San Francisco classic, and I look forward to coming back again 🌸💕

It’s always thrilling for my family to sit at the chef’s dining counter. Love seeing how things come together and the talented chefs make magic for the senses! Beauty created in organized chaos! It’s  like watching a real-life version of a Food Network show - the thrill of seeing your meals being prepared. I’m always excited about the plating part. The whole experience is very personal with the chefs chatting with you and answering questions.

This is our go to place for fine food!

We went there for dinner and had their prix fixed menu. The food was pretty good. Previous night we went to chez panisse - between the two restaurants- I prefer this one. This restaurant has been in business for a very long time.  They’ve kept up their food quality and service. There’s a beautiful view of the bridge from the back part of the dinning room. Definitely recommend for date night and special occasions.
The Softshell Crab, Crudo, Scallops, Halibut were all amazing! The Cheesecake Crème brûlée is a must!  Great service, ensured no use alcohol in any of the dishes we ordered.

reviews_snippets.content: "Great combo of highest quality staff, food and setting."

top_reviews.content:
Very good food with interesting variations on familiar dishes. The hot and sour soup was unique and enjoyable. It is not the thick wood ear mushroom and dark broth variation. It's more like a vegetable and egg drop soup. Definitely preferred over the more common version by my partner.
The steamed shrimp dumplings are visually stunning and delicious. The vegetable dumplings were incredibly rich and flavorful. Everyone in our party enjoyed the pan fried wantans. The steamed buns were fluffy and composed (surprisingly) taco style with moist and seasoned chicken breast, and pickled diakon and carrot.
The Fang's crispy chillie honey short ribs melt in your mouth, definitely recommend.
The steamed fish was served with ginger, spinach, and a very mild chili oil. They do make a  house blend samba oelic style chilli paste that is hot and steals the show on flavor.
The sesame chicken was crispy and served with sweet potatoes. Generally good flavor but it would have benefited from some sour to balance the sweetness.

I had an amazing dining experience at Fang. The restaurant has a super modern and trendy atmosphere that really stands out, while still serving incredible Chinese cuisine.

The food was absolutely delicious. Honestly, it was the best Chinese food I’ve had in San Francisco. Everything we tried was flavorful, fresh, and beautifully presented.

What really made the experience special was the service. The gentleman who took our order suggested that we trust him and allow him to choose dishes for us, and we trusted him. Every single dish he selected was outstanding and ended up being a perfect mix of flavors.

The service throughout the night was excellent and the staff were attentive and welcoming. The location is also great and makes for a really fun dinner spot if you’re in the area.

Highly recommend if you’re looking for amazing Chinese food in San Francisco.

I walked by Fang a couple times while they were closed, and finally caught them open — I’m seriously glad I stopped in.

The food was incredible. They have a really good selection of specialty dishes, and everything is served family style, which I loved. Definitely the kind of place where you want to come with a few people, order a bunch of different things, and share everything.

Also, I absolutely love all the pictures of the owners with Keanu Reeves 😂 There are so many of them, and honestly… who doesn’t like Keanu Reeves?

Great food, cool atmosphere, and just a really memorable spot. Definitely glad I finally stopped in and I’ll be back!

Went with a group of friends to Fang’s recently. It’s family style, so we ordered a ton of items and shared. The standouts were the beef steamed potstickers and the crispy short ribs. It’s a really great place to go for group dinners. Service could be a little better but overall worth checking out.

Is Taiwanese braised pork over rice supposed to be sweet like a sweet teriyaki? I’ve had good one here before but this one seems like a miss. Oh I’ve had the real traditional Taiwanese dish so I know.

top_reviews.content: We enjoyed a nice restaurant week meal here during spring 2026. The set menu for the week was steak and sea bass, both quite good. We also ordered a large plate of different sushi types which were tasty as well. The restaurant is very large inside with great views of the bay bridge out the back windows. It is not an affordable restaurant either, be prepared to spend a pretty penny on food and drinks here. Overall I enjoyed my meal here and would return for some sushi.

In terms of sushi- really a 3/5 if you’ve ever been spoiled by socal’s Sugarfish/Nozawa. The rice was a little undercooked and the fish wasn’t stellar.

In terms of robata- better luck with the small plates and grilled items at Ozumo. Hitokuchi was our favorite dish.

Our server was phenomenal despite being in charge of our entire section of 6 tables and a large party. She was accommodating, patient and so helpful with explaining menu items.

The atmosphere is chic and you can choose seating between the main dining area and lounge. The dining area has views to the bay.

Ozumo was equal parts delicious and magical. My boyfriend and I went out for a nice dinner on a recommendation from a friend. This restaurant had everything we were looking for, from the food and drink pairings, to the ambiance and hospitality of the establishment.

The food was fresh, flavorful and beautifully presented. The ambiance was was modern design, while still being very relaxing with a classy elegance. The lighting is a vit lower during the dinner and late night times, which sets the mood with an elegant formality, making it a good choice for a date night or a calm classy celebration for work or personal accolades if booking their private dining space. I do recommend making a reservation in advance if you want a table for dinner, we were flexible about seating and there were a couple of seats available at the bar when we arrived later in thr evening around 8:30/9:00pm.

We arrived later in the night and sat at the bar thinking we would just get some sushi and head home. We saw the menu and ordered a fouritems to share, a couple of sushi rolls, Nigiri and one of their appetizers. We met Mau who was working at the bar that night, he gave us some wine and beer pairing options per our discussions and preferences for drinks. As the meal went on, Mau continued to share pairing ideas and more information about the menu items, he is so knowledgeable and truly made us feel welcome. His genuine attention to detail and expansive knowledge of food and beverage pairings made it such a wonderful evening. Additionally Mario helped expand our palates and knowledge of Sake pairings (we stepped out of our comfort zone and had no regrets!). We had an unexpected and greatly appreciated culinary experience that night. Thank you Mau and Mario for your hospitality and expertise. We definitely will be back again for the food and great company in the future. Highly recommend!
In from out of town and a colleague brought me here. The nigiri plate was spectacular in its simplicity and the sake flight was a perfect complement for the meal.

Good food and service was ok. Place is usually packed. Food was done well and tasty, decent portions. Good for sharing. Took along time to get my green tea and never got the hot water refill despite several requests.

top_reviews.content:
Grand Lake Kitchen near Lake Merritt is easily one of my favorite spots in the area, and my latest visit reminded me why. The atmosphere is always lively and welcoming, making it the perfect place to sit back and enjoy a great meal.

​The food was absolutely stellar. I ordered:
​The Savory French Toast: If you haven’t tried this yet, you are missing out. It is the perfect, comforting twist on a classic—rich, beautifully seasoned, and incredibly satisfying.

​Chicken Burger (Customized): I wanted something a bit lighter, so I asked for the chicken burger as a lettuce wrap with no bun, paired with a side salad. The kitchen handled the modification flawlessly. The chicken was perfectly cooked, juicy, and flavorful, and the salad was crisp and fresh.
​It’s always a huge plus when a restaurant handles dietary preferences or custom modifications so seamlessly without sacrificing flavor or presentation. The service was attentive and friendly from start to finish. I’ll definitely be back soon!

Pork chop is cooked perfectly as was Ahi for the sandwich. Server was delightful!  sorry I didn’t get his name.  We had a great time.  My daughter also got Moroccan style roasted carrots. don’t have picture, but they were delicious!  Try something!

This is a lovely brunch spot before you take a walk near the lake. Especially on a sunny day! If you sit on the outside, the sun can get a bit warm. They also do have indoor seating.

Server was friendly and helpful. And the casual ambiance was relaxing. We did reserve a table for a weekend brunch since it was recommended.

The chilaquiles verdes were good but not as big of a portion as other places. Was asked by our server if wanted scrambled or poached eggs, and when I asked for her recs, she said scrambled eggs. So I went with half and half to try both. But Chilaquiles verdes with poached eggs were actually way better. Oh and they charged me + $4 for one scrambled egg (didn’t know that’s what she’d do). That’s a dozen in the fridge lol

Pastrami Benedict was good too.

Anyhow! Street parking is a bit difficult on weekends so just be prepared to walk around a little bit.

I wish we could give 4.5 stars. It was ALMOST perfect. Mom said her lamb chops were incredible. Grandma said the BBQ pulled pork sandwich was good but the sauce wasn't really her vibe. My Cali bowl was delicious. The donuts are incredible. The drinks are good. My matza ball soup was perfect. Our server was friendly, attentive, and incredibly patient with my indecisive family. The only things that threw me were: the house made pickled veggies were, well, kinda gross. And the bathrooms were not clean which always makes you second guess what other spaces behind closed doors look like. But anyway, great staff, fresh ingredients, great location, reasonable prices, overall very happy and will be back.

On weekends, you either need to have a reservation or come in right when it opens at 9. We got lucky! Weekdays you don't need a reservation. We came early so we could just walk in and there was still parking.

The mezze bowl is pretty good, the pita is almost like they made it fresh there (maybe they did!) and the dips are filling. I got full on just that with some bacon. Only thing with the bowl is that it was a little salty, maybe next time I'll ask for less salt.

Corned beef hash, coffee, the ranchero. Delicious with filling portion sizes, friendly and minimally intrusive service, great outdoor and indoor seating in quiet neighborhood.

top_reviews.content:
Authentic Italian pizzeria with a curated list of only Italian wines. Thoughtful upcycling design that gives a bit  of nostalgia into the past, like the sewing machine table we sat at.
It gets busy around 6:30 pm. We had reservations for 5:45 pm and our table was ready. Great staff as well with full knowledge of the menu and wines.

Back in 2018, my now-husband suggested Montesacro SoMa for our first date. The pinsas are absolutely divine and it has been a favorite restaurant of ours for years now. So much so, that we reached out and asked if they'd be willing to cater our cocktail hour for 160+ guests at our June 2025 wedding in Petaluma. To our luck and surprise, they agreed and even attended our venue walkthrough to ensure they'd be able to use the on-site, outdoor brick oven. The pinsas were the highlight of the night and our guests still rave about them to this day. We worked with Chefs Anna and Mattia - both of whom were so receptive to our requests. I mean, Chef Anna was individually casing the sausage at the venue on the day-of. Need I say more?!

Lovely small space for delicious pinsas. Excellent short wine list. Old world charm. Feels so local, so Roman, so authentic of itself. Cozy old chairs and tables burnished by extended service. Not for glam, but for the glory of crispy pinsa, killer salads. Close to theaters

Delicious pizza with a special recipe dough.  It's just a little bit different, but not blatantly obviously so.  Regardless it's delicious!  Great friendly knowledgeable service.  Wildly interesting eclectic decor, especially the washroom.  The neighbourhood is a little more gritty but not dangerous by my accounts, and there are neighbourhood ambassadors around as well.

The pinsa was sooooo good! We got the artichoke and pecorina crema pinsa and the dough was exquisite. We also tried the pinsa with prosciutto, really good too. Highly recommend! Just be aware that the neighborhood isn't great.

This is a fantastic healthy place to have a good breakfast and coffee in the thick of things in San Francisco. They can have a big line but it moves very fast and is well worth the wait. The ingredients are high quality and very fresh and both sweet and savory dishes are delicious. Highly recommend.

I've been here many times, it's a go to for me when I'm in SF. The staff have worked here a long time and are very pleasant. I saw them be quite kind with a difficult homeless person today, which made me want to patronize this cafe even more often and post this review.

Super nice café near Market Street, would for sure go there again!

The home fries especially stood out, they were absolutely delicious and exceeded my expectations. Great food, quick service, and a place I looked forward to coming back to every morning!

Food was pretty good. The syrup was the best. Drawn and kept warm so the drizzle on the toast and souffle was delightful. The place is super busy. I had to wait sometime for the syrup because I got my souffle (takes longer than other food to prepare they warned ahead of time) before the syrup came.

Oceanview Diner was a delightful dining experience from start to finish. I ordered the potato pancakes served with sour cream, house-made applesauce, and a sausage, and every bite was flavorful and satisfying. I also had the chance to sample my husband’s pancakes and my daughter’s potato salad, and everything across the table was consistently delicious.
The coffee was fresh, hot, and the perfect complement to the meal. Overall, a thoroughly enjoyable experience with comforting, well-prepared food. I would happily rate Oceanview Diner an 8 out of 10.

I found this pancake mix yesterday in a pantry of a condo in Florida. Was expecting it to be a couple years old and was shocked to see it's 30 yrs old so I had to look up the diner and read about it's history. The side had an order form for merch that you cut out and mail in with payment. And while I'm excited to eat her pancakes, I think I'll wait till I'm in the area for some fresh ones.

I mean . . . talk about amazing traditional diner. The question is always “would you go back to that restaurant again?!” 100% yes. Worth the wait for sure - latte was superb, omelette with avocado, salsa and sour cream - add bacon - crazy good. Fish tacos - gluten free- awesome! Thanks Oceanview Diner - Happy Memorial Day!

name: Great China

top_reviews.content:
We’ve eaten at a few Bib Gourmands in the past and we mean it when we say it: this place deserves a star. We had a reservation and the place was so packed it had a line around the block at the opening for dinner service. The wait was about 15-20 minutes from when they opened as they were working quickly to get everyone seated and setup. We were seated at their family sized tables in the back and the service was fantastic. We ordered quite a bit of food since we had a large party so here’s a list of what we got:

Pork dumplings 8/10 - devoured in minutes within our party, everyone loved it.
Salt & pepper spare ribs 10/10 - some of, if not, the best we’ve ever had. Perfect seasoning and chew to them.
Fried rice 9/10 - just delicious, nothing special about it and yet still amazing.
Ginger scallion crab 6/10 - seafood is not really our thing to be fair, but we still did enjoy the meat, the sauce was a bit of a miss though.
Duck bone soup 9/10 - unbelievably good, the cilantro and onion pack it with flavor and the consistency is great.
Broccoli, beef, and string beans 8/10 - a classic just done right, seasoned well and broccoli with a good chew; beef perfect texture and velvety.
Chicken chow mein 10/10 - perfect chew, perfect flavor. Would’ve ordered another if we weren’t so full.
Peking duck with steamed buns and flat bread 11/10 - on this scale an 11 denotes it’s the best we’ve ever had, just in case you thought we failed 1st grade math. Crispy skin and delicious, tender meat.

Great China is undoubtedly some of the best Chinese food we’ve ever had. Add onto the fact that it’s at a better value than other places and it becomes clear that this is a special place. The food itself deserves a star but sprinkle in the service and it begs the question as to why it doesn’t have one. More on the service actually, they were incredibly patient as we ordered many dishes with different requests and were on top of everything from refilling water and tea to removing plates. When the only issue with a place is the parking situation then you know it’s good. (Side note: parking is pretty hard to find and we saw a lot of cars getting tickets for invalid parking so keep an eye out). That shouldn’t deter anyone though as this place might just be worth that fine, half kidding. Do yourself the favor and come here at all costs.

If you come to this restaurant, and I highly recommend you do, keep in mind it is very popular and there will be a wait. The only question is how long. We were expecting to wait a long time, but we got there before it opened on a Sunday, and only waited about 10 minutes. We felt very lucky! We came here in a big group, which is definitely the way to do it because you can get a variety of dishes. Everything was absolutely delicious! The Peking duck was our favorite. But we also liked many other dishes. The only dish that I would say was not fantastic was a fried rice, but that could be just my taste, because someone else actually liked it. This is a really terrific place to come with a group for delicious Chinese food. Highly, highly recommend.

Food is pretty good, though don’t expect authentic Chinese cuisine; this is more Chinese-American food.

The double skin is an interesting dish and definitely worth trying. The walnut prawns are also good, though I’ve had better versions elsewhere. The guo ta fish is a little underwhelming, as it’s just very simple steamed fish with soy sauce, but not very good quality fish.

Portions are fairly decent, but I still found the pricing a little high.

Peking duck is great with pancakes. Pricy but worthy the money. We also ordered eggplant with tofu, sadly was greasy and not impressed. Will skip this dish is possible. Overall, very authentic Peking duck.

This place has the best American Chinese food I’ve ever had anywhere.  The prices are a bit higher than other places.  But well worth it.   Everything always tastes fresh and well made and each visit provides consistency from the last.  The spring rolls are some of the best I’ve had anywhere.   And the steak dishes are always tender which is not always the case as most Chinese food establishments.  Service is quick and efficient.   I’ve never found better Chinese anywhere.  The quality is definitely worth the price.

top_reviews.content: I absolutely love this restaurant. The food is delicious, the staff is friendly, and the prices are affordable. It is such a pleasure to sit at a table with a white tablecloth and see waiters dressed in white shirts:)

Delancey Street is at a great Location.   So it's a good spot to stop for breakfast before a Giants game or watch the boats along the waterfront or just people watch as they pass along the Embarcadero.  The service is outstanding.  And the food is good. We got lucky and we're able to enjoy our late breakfast on the patio. You can't beat that on a sunny day!

I went to Delancey Street Restaurant with my friend, and we’re both in ninth grade. The food was amazing and surprisingly affordable, which we really appreciated. However, the atmosphere made us feel uncomfortable from the moment we walked in. We were stared at in silence, and it immediately felt like we didn’t really belong there.

top_reviews.content: Came to SF from New York and really enjoyed this Beijing spot in Chinatown. We ordered quite a lot, but a few dishes really stood out to us. The Peking duck had super crispy skin without being too fatty, and both the beef and lamb spine were really flavorful. We also loved the tofu soup and the crab soup, especially on a chilly SF night. The kung fu tea performance was so fun to watch, and I even got to try it myself! Ling took great care of us and was super warm and helpful, especially with recommending dishes for the table.

We shared a half Peking Duck between two people, as well as the Beijing Pot Stickers. Both items were delicious, well-presented, and very tasty. In addition, the service was prompt, attentive, and professional.

The ambiance in the restaurant is very nice. It's not a large place and it did begin to fill up quickly for lunch, but the noise level was not a problem.

The staff was also attentive and accommodating to the gluten-free requirements of one diner, which was very much appreciated.

Overall, if you are searching for a high-quality dining experience, then head over to Z & Y Peking Duck in the Chinatown district of San Francisco. It is worth the trip!

The Peking Duck is absolutely delicious. Such a unique dish and tender duck with a crispy skin that is incredible. Don’t miss out on the green beans! Have not had lost of exposure to great Chinese cuisine and this place set an awesome bar. Would definitely recommend! FYI, the portions are HUGE for dishes that aren’t the Peking Duck so come hungry and be prepared to take some home if you order multiple things.

The food was excellent. Short wait to get in even though there was a line. Great vibe, modern decor. It looks like they have a downstairs. We were able to get their Peking Duck and we were able to get more pancakes. Overall, it was a good experience. We definitely would consider coming back. Just note they do charge an automatic 8% to your bill for a San Francisco service fee.

Amazing Peking Duck!  Reminiscent of the quality experienced in Beijing. Everything was delicious, the sous vide short rib was so tender and flavorful, miso sea bass was perfectly flavored, the honey dew shrimp was delicious and unique, the abalone was tender and full of umami, yummy eggplant in spicy garlic sauce. We loved our meal and service so much that we made a reservation for the rest of our family. We’re coming back😋!
