top_reviews.content: Dinner at Palette Tea House was fantastic from start to finish. The atmosphere is vibrant and stylish, paired with attentive, truly excellent service. The bar program sets a high bar right away—the Oolong Goddess was an incredibly inventive cocktail that started the evening off right. For the food, the stars were easily the xiao long bao sampler (an absolute must-order for the creative flavor combinations), the rich congee with uni, the savory Iberico with green garlic dumplings in kimchee sauce, and the bold Szechuan seafood dumplings. Every single dish was impeccably seasoned and artfully presented, making for a memorable dining experience.

great quality for a mix of chinese cuisine with a hint of modern fusion! our eyes are always bigger than our stomach and we ended up over ordering just to try everything, but i would come back just for the shu mai and the ha gow! not a big big fan of soup dumplings but they were good here. high recommend also their roasted duck congee with a side of chinese doughnut

A beautiful Michelin-recognized tea house experience with amazing service, flavorful food, and a really unique atmosphere.

Stopped by Palette Tea House with The Kid after FoodieLand thinking we were just coming for tea… and ended up having a full experience.

We sat at the communal high-top table in the center of the restaurant, which has a small pond built into it with little goldfish and even a tiny rubber duck sitting on the rock formation — such a cute detail and definitely adds to the ambiance.

Our server Ken was fantastic and incredibly knowledgeable about the menu. He recommended the Iron Goddess tea, which ended up being excellent. The Kid ordered the Milk Aroma Oolong, which surprisingly tasted almost like milk tea even though it’s just brewed tea.

Each tea comes with its own kettle, and Ken even came back to refill the hot water for us.

For food, we ordered the Wagyu Beef Fried Rice, which was a huge portion and easily shareable. Very flavorful and well prepared.

We also tried the Sichuan Seafood Dumplings and the Iberico Pork Dumplings, both of which were delicious. One order is definitely enough to share.

The dumplings come with several dipping sauces including soy sauce, vinegar, chili oil, hot mustard, and a cilantro-based sauce that had a slightly sweet, horseradish-like flavor that really stood out.

Service throughout the meal was amazing. Even without a reservation, we were seated immediately.

As a Michelin-recognized restaurant for 2025, it definitely felt like a special treat and lived up to the experience.

Delicious and delightful! The food was awesome and ambrosial. The service was great and good-natured. The atmosphere was casual but also classy. It was a bit too expensive and exorbitant. The dumplings were simple and SOOOO GOOD!!! If you're in the area, eat here!

We had a great dining experience here. The menu offers a wide variety of authentic Asian dishes, and the location is very convenient. Every dish we ordered was delicious and beautifully presented.
The milk tea was especially rich and flavorful—if you're a milk tea fan like me, it's a must-order! The Wok-Fried Gai Lan & Shiitake Mushroom was outstanding; the mushrooms had an incredibly meaty texture and were packed with flavor. The Wagyu Beef Chow Fun was another favorite at our table.

The service was attentive and friendly throughout our visit. One thing to note is that this restaurant is definitely on the pricey side. We were surprised to find that the rice was charged at $4 per bowl, and there were additional service fees automatically added to the bill.

That said, the food quality and service were excellent. If you're looking for authentic Asian cuisine and don't mind paying a premium, this place is worth a visit.

top_reviews.content:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An absolute San Francisco institution!
You can’t say you’ve truly experienced North Beach without a stop at Molinari Delicatessen. Stepping inside this legendary shop on Columbus Ave feels like being transported straight to a classic Italian deli in New York or Naples.

The Food:
The sandwiches are massive and use the highest quality meats and cheeses. The North Beach Special is a masterpiece, but you really can't go wrong with the Renzo Special or the Luciano Special.

The Bread: It’s all about the crunch! Grab your own bread from the bin at the back before heading to the counter—the Dutch Crunch and sourdough are iconic.

The Goods: Beyond sandwiches, it’s a foodie paradise stocked with imported olive oils, house-made pastas, and a deli case full of incredible cured meats.

The Vibe:
It’s bustling, chaotic in the best way, and smells like heaven (garlic and aged provolone). There's no indoor seating, so do what the locals do: grab your sub and walk a block over to Washington Square Park for the ultimate SF lunch.

Pro Tip: This place is popular for a reason. If you're visiting on a weekend, get there early to beat the rush, and remember to grab a number as soon as you walk in!

It's authentic Italian deli, market with lots of delicious stuff with variety of deli meats like prosciutto di parma aged for 18 months!

Wonderful service and excellent drinks. Perfect location if you are going to a show at The Masonic. I stopped by late in the evening and only ordered the churros for dessert.

The service was great—friendly, welcoming, and attentive. The staff made me feel comfortable even though I came in close to closing time, and I have nothing negative to say about the customer service.

For the churros, they were a bit disappointing. The texture suggested they may not have been freshly made. Instead of having a crisp outer layer, it was slightly soft and soggy, blending into the inside. Because of that, the texture was the biggest drawback of the dish.

However, the sugar coating was well-balanced and not overly sweet, and it paired nicely with the chocolate dipping sauce.

My wife and I used to eat here frequently when we lived here and always liked it. So on a recent visit, we made Matador our first meal. And I think it was even better than ever! We only had a small meal, but it was super tasty. The chips and salsa are fresh and the salsa was very authentic and spiced very well. The taco trio (we ordered caulifower, ground beef and chicken)  was tasty as well, the only reco would be to serve the ground beef gringo-style in a hard shell. But other than that, it's great. The people are very nice, the space is very comfortable and the tequila and wine selection is great. Go!

The atmosphere, food, & staff were amazing. I originally was going to ask to sit up front so I could watch outside passersbyers, but the hostess asked if I was interested in sitting in the back room. Curiously, I asked her to show me and decided to sit back there. It was small, quaint and beautifully decorated with Mexican art work. The female bartender / server was great.

I’ve lived in Chicago, Dallas, Austin, Irving, & Tucson, I really enjoyed the Mexican food and flavors. I loved the American authenticity of the Mexican food, it is 100 times better than TexMex, and reminded me of the Mexican food I’m used to in Chicago & Tucson.

Absolutely exceptional experience from start to finish. Every dish felt intentional, beautifully executed, and incredibly fresh.
The nigiri was a standout. Perfectly seasoned rice with delicate, high-quality fish, topped with thoughtful touches that elevated each bite without overpowering it. The salmon dish with chili and sesame had just the right balance of heat and brightness, and the crispy rice was addictive.
The grilled shishito peppers were simple but done right, blistered with a deep, smoky flavor and finished with bonito that added a subtle umami depth. The octopus was tender and flavorful, paired with acidity and texture that made it one of the most memorable dishes of the night.
Beyond the food, the presentation was stunning across the board. Every plate felt curated, not just assembled. The atmosphere was warm and stylish, and the service was attentive without being intrusive.
This is the kind of place you go when you want sushi that feels thoughtful and elevated.
The restaurant’s interior is just stunning. We really enjoyed the ambiance here and the service was amazing! Some of the best dishes we had were the fried chicken and steak sirloin with bone marrow.
Best Japanese Steakhouse we've ever been to. From the A5 wagyu that melts like butter in your mouth, to the sushi/sashimi/nagiri and desserts - amazing menu.  Top notch service.  Will come back

pleasant atmosphere, attentive servers that are easy to get the attention of, and good food. our reservation was for 8pm and the server kindly informed us that the kitchen closed at 9 so ordering any extra food before then was acceptable. we first ordered the sashimi platter, dry aged ribeye, wagyu tartare, fresh oysters, and bone marrow. around halfway through our meal we also ordered the corn, more oysters, and a bowl of rice. the staff were very accomodating when we asked for plain rice around 9pm, didnt expect them to accept that order but they managed to fulfill it.

one issue we had was how long it took for the corn, dry aged rib eye, and bone marrow to arrive to our table. the sashimi, tartare, and oysters were quick, but the other three took much longer and didnt arrive until the 44 minute mark of the hour. otherwise, amazing service.

the oysters and bone marrow were our favorites, everything else was okay. the wasabi was textured and different from every other place we have dined at on the east and qest coast! truly wonder how roka akor prepares the wasabi.

Wonderful staff and clearly care about their customers and the food. $24ish total for the fried chicken sandwich and potato balls. Definitely recommend coming by if you’re in Oakland.
Everything was so good!! Thoroughly enjoyed the meal and sitting outside. Wish they had slightly more seating and a bathroom so that's why only 3 stars for atmosphere. Potato balls were bomb!

The flavor is solid in *most* bites!

I had the fried buttermilk chicken filet with cole slaw on French roll (fancy way to say chicken sando 🤣). The bread was fluffy with every bite, and the flavor palette works really well between the classic well-seasoned chicken patty and cole slaw combo.

To be nit picky, the proportions are a little off:
1. There was too much bread for the amount of meat and coleslaw. The cole slaw could be kept better in the sandwich if it was more finely chopped. Going from rough to fine chops allows the slaw to be more flexible (like solid to liquid) and fill out the inside volume of the sandwich instead of constantly falling out of the sandwich.
2. While the chicken was perfectly salt-and-pepper seasoned, had a nice crispy crust, and looked appetizing, it's skinnier cuts relative to the wider roll left more savoriness to be desired. Butterfly-style cuts can help produce wider chicken slabs increasing surface area-to-volume ratio enabling the display of more of its flavor.

The real thing that'd discourage me is the price and not enough seating. My friend and I paid half a benji for 2 sandwiches and potato balls that we couldn't enjoy until we got home.

Again, the above are nit picks, and wouldn't discourage me from eating here again! In fact, I'm writing this review in hopes that my feedback is valued to make the chicken sando better than it already is. :) The potato puffs are 🔥!!! And the server peeps were super friendly!

top_reviews.content:
Trestle is one of those places that really gets everything right.

The prix fixe menu is excellent, well balanced, seasonal, and thoughtfully put together. Every dish feels intentional without being overly complicated.

The grilled salmon and the carbonara were both outstanding, and the carrot soup to start was also delicious. The presentation across the courses was clean and well executed.

What stood out to me the most is the atmosphere. It has a warm, local neighborhood vibe while still delivering a high level of quality. It doesn’t feel overly formal, which makes it very comfortable.

Service was also on point, attentive, friendly, and professional without being intrusive.

I am not from this neighborhood, but I would definitely come back with friends and would also consider using it for business occasions.

Overall, a very solid dining experience. Definitely a place I’d come back to

The ambience is romantic and cozy, with good acoustics that make conversation easy. My only gripes: the room felt a bit too cold for my taste, and the chocolate donut dessert was slightly disappointing compared to the rest of the meal.

All in all, great value for money and a restaurant I'd happily recommend. Will be back!

10/10! Had a great dinner here. We started with the Caesar salad and the soup. My Caesar was exactly what I was looking for, and my friend’s soup was a knockout. We both had the tagliatelle with clams and thoroughly enjoyed it.

For mains, the fish was excellent. It had a light, thin, crispy batter with a subtle coconut texture, not an overpowering coconut batter, and it was cooked perfectly. The stuffed chicken was also very good, especially paired with the asparagus.

We finished with dessert, and I was craving chocolate cake. It absolutely delivered. It was light and airy, with a melt-in-your-mouth texture that made it dangerously easy to keep eating. I honestly think I could have eaten an entire cake.

Our waiter also helped us choose a wine, and it was perfect for the meal. Overall, this was a great experience: lively atmosphere, excellent food, strong service, and a very good value for what was offered. I’ll definitely be back.
Easily one of the best stops in SF if you enjoy set menus. Exemplary service, and the food was fantastic. They wouldn't give me the recipe of the sauce for the schnitzel unfortunately.

We went here with another couple on a Friday night at 6pm. Cozy atmosphere, attentive service, great food.
One complaint is not the 36% in tax and fees (20% for service, 6% for SF health, and 10% for CA sales tax) but that the same fees apply to corkage. So the $35 corkage is actually $48. My initial thought was that the wine was diverse and reasonably priced,so bought a $109 bottle of champs off the list and brought an aged CA red from our cellar. I was surprised the alcohol tab for those 2 bottles was almost $200.
My other issue is that the space is LOUD. Maybe it was because  we were sitting next to the brick wall, or because the floors are bare and hard, or the ceiling 15-20’ high or all of the above. But I found it incredibly difficult to have a table conversation for 4. So, my recommendation is only go with one other person that you really like so you can lean in to talk to each other.

top_reviews.content: I’ve been eating here for the past at least the past 37 years now, dating back to when they had their amazing crab cake sandwich that I will never stop missing! If you want a great burger or a perfectly cooked steak, this is the spot! I also miss their pulled pork sandwich, hoping they bring it back. They have a lovely bar that makes incredible cocktails, and the decor changes with the seasons. They usually have great oysters on a 1/2 shell too (the Miyagi’s are my fave’s) and you gotta end with their crème brûlée!

House salad is not a standard fare in a good way with spicy peacans and strawberries. I added avocado which made it even better. The French onion soup is good and had House made cookies for dessert. Daughter had a steak which she enjoyed.

We came here around Christmas looking for a festive dinner and it was exactly what we hoped! Every inch was completely decked out in the best way, and I could tell even in non-Christmas times the decor was cool.

Food was great as well! We had the pate and onion soup for appetizer and for our mains a ribeye + baked potato and a caesar + added steak. Everything was well seasoned and the steak add portion on the salad is excellent! Our server was really nice and everything came out promptly. There's a lot of good looking things on the menu and I'd love to go back and try some more!

I recently had my engagement photos taken at The Fat Lady, and it couldn’t have been a more perfect setting. The restaurant has so much character and such an incredible atmosphere—it made every photo look amazing.

After the photos, we stayed for cocktails and dinner, and everything was outstanding. The fried zucchini is an absolute 10/10, and honestly, nothing compares to the dipping sauce that comes with it. I could eat that alone! The burger was also one of the best I’ve had—perfectly cooked and full of flavor.

On top of the great food, the service was exceptional. Everyone was friendly, attentive, and made us feel genuinely welcome from start to finish.

Whether you’re looking for a unique date night, a place to celebrate a special occasion, or just an amazing meal in Oakland, The Fat Lady is a must-visit. We’ll definitely be back!

This place is simply amazing and the atmosphere is so nice. Excellent vintage beer signs and awesome stained glass goes along with plenty of paintings on the walls just give a great place to enjoy a meal and lovely cocktails. The Greco Lamb was amazing! French Fried Zucchini was delicious and I cannot wait to come back for some more awesome cocktails and delicious food. What a great experience here. Staff was lovely and service was perfect. I cannot recommend this restaurant enough. Absolutely worth the trip to enjoy!!

top_reviews.content:
Loud Ventilation: The air vents are excessively loud, making it incredibly frustrating to try and talk over them

Mediocre / Average Food: The overall food is just decent, but missing basic things that all KBBQ should have such as refills on beverages, it's missing fried chicken and fries as appetizers which are usually in every KBBQ.

Mixed Service: While the staff's service itself was noted as generally good, their scissors were dull which made cutting meat a nightmare, this detracted from the overall experience.

Wasn’t sure what to expect because hadn’t had Korean BBQ in this area, but it turned out a great experience.

First thing I noticed is they’re very nice. Very welcoming. That sets the tone. Next thing I noticed is they have a fairly large rectangular grill which is better than the circles I usually see. And they are fast about changing the grill expeditiously as it gets gunked up with the sauces.

It’s spacious and yet urban nice inside. Perhaps a little dark but different strokes for different folks. We were in the side room which was darker.

About $40 for the all you can eat, which I would recommend. You get two appetizers and four meats at a time. Also can get a couple sides and/or veggies.

Good selection of meats. And the meats are GOOD portion size. And good thickness. Excellent soup and sides. Specifically the tofu soup. Softener kinds of rice. All goodness.

You will leave here full of you get the all you can eat.

Parking lot is a little odd. Slotted, angled spaces; so you need to back out to the street to exit. But at least they have a posting lot at all! Better than street parking.

Just as every review says, this place is awesome! I love Korean BBQ and it’s all you can eat, Need I say more! You do cook the food yourself which is just a fun experience with everyone. The short ribs and the kimchi pancakes were probably my favorite thing we got. We also got the garlic pork belly, shrimp, brisket, sirloin.. pretty much everything on the menu. Everything was fantastic. The service was amazing as well. We never felt like we were missing food or was waiting for more. They also come around change out your burner top so it’s always clean. If you really need convincing and your not just sure. Just walk in front of the building and you’ll be convinced by the amazing aroma of Korean BBQ food!

AVOID if you're looking for authentic korean BBQ! this place used to be good but it changed over the years. first off, Kimchi is totally wrong- it taste like sour,sugary.. weird thing that looks like kimchi? Rice was watery and slimy? their whole grain rice is not actually whole grain, just purple rice mixed in to change color. they don't give you enough banchan and meat so you have to constantly bother the server who also gives you attitude for it. I used to love this place but the owner changed to someone who doesn't actually understand korean food and its culture. also it's pricy on top of it. sadly I wont go back to it anymore.

All you can eat for $32. Short ribs are the best. Their banchan is also excellent. Staff are friendly and attentive, we never had to wait to order more meat.

The only areas of improvement would be brighter lighting (when it gets dark), providing wet wipes or more napkins from the start (grilling is a messy process), and cleaner restrooms. But the service and the food was great, so I'm still giving a 5 star review.

top_reviews.content:
The experience was genuinely disappointing. The service was very slow from the start, and more concerning, even when it was clear the grill was burning, the staff did nothing about it, as if they didn’t care.

At one point, I called a waiter and was completely ignored, which made the experience even worse. I understand that places can get busy, but that wasn’t the case here—there were only about seven tables occupied.

Overall, the service left a lot to be desired. I’ve been to many Korean restaurants, and considering the value for the price, this experience was not good enough to make me want to come back.
We were seated pretty fast considering we went during dinner time (7pm) so that’s a plus. The menu selections were on the smaller but had the basic meats. Service was alright.

My partner and I are big Korean BBQ fans and go often back home in NYC, so we were excited to try YakiniQ for the first time. Unfortunately, it didn’t live up to expectations. The food was just okay and lacked flavor, even on the premium plate. The beef bulgogi didn’t really taste like beef, and overall, nothing stood out.

Service was also disappointing. After waiting an hour to be seated, it took another 10 minutes before anyone checked in to take our order, and the couple next to us (who arrived after) were served first. Even water took about 20 minutes to arrive….

I also didn’t realize it was self-cook, which might be fine for some, but the experience felt very “here’s your meat, good luck.” The ventilation could use improvement too; the smoke builds up quickly and makes your eyes sting.

Overall, not the experience we were hoping for.

YakiniQ has some strong points, but overall, my experience fell short. As a first timer in a Korean BBQ costumer, I’ll start with the positives: the service is truly outstanding. The waitstaff is attentive, patient with explaining the process and how it works, friendly and quick, making you feel well taken care of throughout the meal.

Now, the downsides: the food, unfortunately, lacked flavor. For a BBQ spot, I was expecting bold and exciting tastes, but it just wasn’t there. The restaurant also felt overcrowded, and with poor ventilation, the smoke from the grills clings to your clothes—definitely not ideal.

At $45 per person, there are plenty of options for prime cuts. A big issue was the automatic 18% service fee for parties of 5 or more. While this isn’t unusual, the waiters should clearly explain this policy upfront, especially before asking for an additional tip. For those like me who don’t pay close attention to the bill, this feels misleading and can leave a bad taste after an otherwise polite dining experience.

Would I go again? Probably. The service is excellent, but transparency around the service charge is a must.

Love this place. Met the manager from here, Aaron Tan, who was very welcoming and made our first experience here unforgettable. Amazing service, food, and all around great vibes! If anyone is looking for a place for some sensational Korean BBQ, this is it.

top_reviews.content:
Since moving to Hayes Valley, I've been here at Papito Hayes about six or seven times for lunch, so I think I'm ready to share some thoughts about this place.

Walking in, you're greeted with a friendly atmosphere and a beautiful mural. The service is polite and chill, and they usually invite me to sit wherever I'd like at the small open tables inside. There's also a small outdoor area if you'd rather sit outside.

The staff always have a friendly buzz about them and seem to all be friends, which I like to see. It gives the place a welcoming feeling.

Compared to some of the other places nearby, this spot has slightly cheaper options, but expect to spend close to $30 per person.

By far my favorite things to order are the chicken soup and the asada enchiladas.

The way the enchiladas are served is unique and adds to the flavor of the dish. The rice and beans are placed beneath the enchiladas in a small skillet, so all the juices and sauce drip into them, which makes it a pleasure to tuck into. The asada enchiladas also come with a tasty red sauce, and the smoky bites of steak inside each enchilada make me devour them every time.

I've also tried the pork enchiladas, which are pretty good for similar reasons. The chicken enchiladas weren't for me—but that might just be because I don't really like the taste of mole.

For $9, you're served a surprisingly filling bowl of chicken soup with rice. The rice is never mushy, and the broth is really savory and moreish, probably because it's made with bone broth. It also comes with plenty of chicken and vegetables, plus a big pile of cilantro, which I really like.

I've also tried a bunch of their tacos. I wouldn't recommend the duck confit tacos, as they're a little too sweet in my opinion. However, the Baja-style fish tacos are really nice, as are the fried chicken tacos. They're not super traditional, but they're tasty and balanced with a little cilantro and salad in each.

If you ask, they'll also give you a small bottle of what seems to be homemade habanero sauce. I consider myself pretty good with spicy food, but this stuff is actually pretty hot, so be careful with it.

There was one time when they didn't really hit the mark. I ordered the chicken soup, as I always do, and it came out tasting much blander than usual, with much drier chicken. I let the staff know, and they gave me a discount, which was nice.

Overall, I really like the vibe of this place and the bright flavors they offer. Compared to Souvla nearby which I'd put in a similar bracket, I prefer to come here. I'll definitely be coming back for lunch again.

Papito Hayes is a good Mexican spot in Hayes Valley for lunch or brunch with great vibes. The food quality is solid, but honestly it lacked flavor overall. Even the habanero salsa wasn’t spicy, which was surprising. Didn’t get a chance to try their drinks, but would come back for the ambiance and give it another shot.
Solid take on Mexican favorites (don’t expect Abuelita’s cooking) and it’s a great spot for a happy hour with friends! I recommend you get a couple of apps to share, especially the guacamole!

top_reviews.content: Our family (10 people) came for brunch on July 4. The food was exceptional and the service was stupendous. Every dish was delicious, perfectly seasoned and cooked. The potatoes (bravas & aioli) were cooked to perfection. They were crispy on the outside and creamy in the inside. We highly recommend La Marcha and will be back when we are in the area again.

On Saturday, February 14, 2026 (Valentine's Day), I dined at La Marcha for brunch.

The atmosphere and vibe was nice and cool. The tables and seating are pretty close together. You could literally hear what other guests were talking about and reach out and touch them. That's how close the seating/tables were.

We ordered the Panqueques which were pancakes topped with chocolate cream, fruit and granola. They were really good. The pancakes were fluffy and the texture was on point. The only thing wrong with the pancakes was the young girl who served this dish to us said the chocolate cream on top was melting and sliding off and part of the chocolate cream was on part of her hand! I wouldn't have served this to a guest if the foods was literally sliding off and touching my hand but she still did. We didn't say anything to the manager or complain because the pancakes actually tasted delicious. I still want to bring this up though because hygiene should be at the highest standard and quality at any restaurant.

We ordered the Torrijas Trea Leches French toast. It was delicious and full of flavor. The syrup served for both the pancakes and French toast were on point!

We also ordered the Paella Mananera 🥘. It was good. The chicken, serrano ham, chorizo and the runny egg eaten with the rice all tasted good together. It was some of the paella I've ever had.

I would highly recommend La Marcha to everyone who wants good quality food with high-end ingredients. Every dish delivered and was on point!

Make a reservation if you are coming on a weekend.

No one refilled our water even once, and no one checked in to see if we needed anything. We saw servers refilling water at other tables, but they never came to ours. Servers were basically nowhere to be found, to the point where when I finally saw one closing out another table, I handed her my card before she could run away because I was worried she'd disappear again and we wouldn't be able to pay for another business day.

We added a bottle of sparkling water to our bill before closing it out but it wasn't brought out until we were waiting at the door ready to leave, that was also after when we had to ask again for it.

At no point were we acknowledged for being ignored. Nothing like "It's busy tonight" or "We're short staffed". We would've understood if there were special circumstances, but we received nothing aside from what felt like attitude and impatience from the waitresses. (God bless them, hope they had a better night than I did)

The experience left us speechless. For a place where per-person spending is $100+, the service was shockingly bad (although is it really "bad" if it were nonexistent?) The menu deserved better service. Just stick to DoorDashing or takeout.

Hopefully others won't have the same experience we did.

Yarsa Napalese Cuisine in San Francisco offers an authentic and delightful journey for the taste buds, making it a must-visit for anyone craving high-quality South Asian flavors. Based on my recent order, everything was executed beautifully, from the rich curries to the fresh sides.
​The Stars of the Show
​Chicken Tikka Masala: This classic dish was a creamy revelation. The chicken was incredibly tender, and the sauce struck a perfect balance--rich and flavorful without being overly heavy or sweet. It's easily one of the best versions I've had in the city.
​Saag Curry Lamb: A true highlight! The lamb was cooked to perfection, falling apart with gentle pressure. The Saag (spinach) curry itself was deeply savory and earthy, seasoned masterfully to complement the meat. It had a wonderful, comforting depth of flavor.
​Sides & Bread Perfection
​Yellow Rice with Vegetables: This was a vibrant and flavorful accompaniment. The rice was perfectly cooked--fluffy and separate--and the inclusion of fresh, tender vegetables (carrots, peas, etc.) made it a substantive and refreshing side dish.
​Garlic Cheese Naan: Absolutely essential! The naan was warm, pillowy, and generously stuffed with melted cheese and fresh garlic. It wasn't greasy, and the balance of savory garlic and gooey cheese made it irresistible for dipping into the curry sauces.
​Overall Verdict
​Yarsa Napalese Cuisine delivers an exceptional dining experience. The ingredients taste fresh, the spices are complex and aromatic, and the preparation shows genuine care and expertise. If you're looking for fantastic Nepalese and Indian classics in San Francisco, look no further. This place is a gem! The service was great ! The waiter was very friendly and it was a nice vibe in. The restaurant.
​Highly Recommended Dishes: Chicken Tikka Masala and Saag Curry Lamb.

Jong Ga House is the real deal if you’re looking for an authentic Korean meal. The food was excellent, the staff was wonderful, and the entire experience felt genuine and welcoming.

We tried quite a few dishes, and there were some definite standouts. The bulgogi was amazing, tender and packed with flavor. We also really liked the spicy pork, which had a great balance of heat and flavor. The hot pot bibimbap was another hit, arriving sizzling hot with that wonderful crispy rice developing along the bottom.

The kalbi had excellent flavor, although the meat was a little chewier than I would have liked. I’m also a fan of Korean BBQ cooked over charcoal, so I would have preferred charcoal grills to the gas grills they use here. There’s just something about that smoky charcoal flavor that takes Korean BBQ to another level.

Those are relatively minor complaints, though. Overall, we had a great meal with plenty of dishes we’d happily order again. Great food, wonderful service, and an authentic experience. Definitely a place I’d return to.

Located in a convenient location with plenty of street parking. So much variety on the menu as well! I want to come back to try the other dishes for sure.

I'd give it 5 stars, except for the staff was not very welcoming. The boss was nice, but that was it.

The prices were reasonable considering the amount and quality of the food.

If you like hot pot (shabu-shabu), or you want a culinary adventure, then I definetely recommend you give it a try.

Extremely disappointing birthday experience

I came here to celebrate my birthday with my birthday cake and was expecting a fun Korean BBQ dinner. Instead, the way I was treated—especially by our server, Eddie—completely ruined the celebration.

I celebrate my birthday according to the Chinese lunar calendar. When I asked about the birthday discount, Eddie refused to honor it because my Chinese birthday apparently did not count as a valid birthday. I understand that restaurants can have rules for promotions, but the issue was not just the discount. It was the dismissive and indifferent attitude that came with it.

I found the whole interaction disrespectful. I had my birthday cake sitting right there, and I was clearly there to celebrate my birthday. Rather than explaining the policy with basic courtesy, Eddie made me feel like my birthday and the cultural tradition behind it were not legitimate.

As a Chinese customer, I found that especially upsetting. A Chinese lunar-calendar birthday is still a birthday. If the restaurant has a strict policy requiring a government ID or only recognizes the Gregorian calendar for its promotion, then state that clearly. There is absolutely no reason to make a customer feel belittled over a cultural difference.

The service throughout the meal also felt cold, unfriendly, and indifferent. There was no effort to make the situation better or even acknowledge how poorly it was handled. What should have been a happy birthday dinner ended with me feeling unwelcome and disrespected.

I’m not upset over a discount. I’m upset over how I was treated. There is a big difference between politely saying, “Unfortunately, our promotion only applies to the birthday listed on your ID,” and treating someone’s cultural tradition like it is not real.

Management should seriously address how Eddie and the staff handle situations like this. Customers from different cultural backgrounds deserve the same basic respect as everyone else. I would not choose this restaurant again after this experience.

I stumbled upon Little Delhi purely out of necessity—my phone battery had completely died, and I was desperately looking for a place nearby to charge it. This spot came up just a short walk from Market Street, not too far away from Powell station near Carl.

From the very first moment, the customer service stood out. Without even asking much, the staff immediately helped me find a place to charge my phone and even lent me a charger. Brownie points right there.

Since my mum and I were already there (and feeling a little tingle in the stomach, though not starving), we decided to sit down for a light bite while the phone charged. We ordered samosa chaat and two cups of chai ($7.99 & $3.99 e.c) The prices were very reasonable, especially considering it’s right in the heart of downtown. The street itself may look a bit edgy or rough, but if you give this place a chance, you’ll be pleasantly surprised.

After tasting the samosa chaat, we couldn’t resist ordering their aloo paratha as well. It was nicely cooked, soft, and comforting. The only small thing I wished for was a side of pickle or chutney, which would have made it even better.

We also picked up rasmalai as a takeaway, and it was a perfect sweet ending to the experience.

It’s an Indo-Nepali restaurant, which I only realized after looking at the menu—and that was a nice surprise. The flavors were really good, the chaat was tasty, and the wait time wasn’t long at all. The space itself is beautifully decorated—minimalistic yet classy. It’s the kind of place where you could easily spend 2–3 hours sipping tea, reading a book, or having a good, relaxed conversation with friends.

Another thing worth mentioning: the restrooms were super clean, and even the seating area was being regularly cleaned, which really adds to the overall comfort and hygiene of the place.

The customer service remained fabulous from start to finish. Gopal, who helped us, was exceptional—attentive, kind, and genuinely welcoming. There was also another gentleman with spectacles who assisted us; special mention to him as well for being very prompt and helpful.

As a small suggestion: I’d love to see more chaat options like golgappe, or classic North Indian dishes such as chole-bhature. Maybe even a vegetarian burger with an Indian twist. With flavors this good and a name like Little Delhi, this place truly has the potential to go a long way.

Overall, a comforting spot with great service, good food, and a welcoming vibe. Definitely worth stopping by.

top_reviews.content:
BLAND FLAVORLESS NOTHING
Can't recommend this place.

Let me make this clear before I continue. The staff is great, they were totally cool with me, friendly and helpful. This has nothing to do with the staff or how they prepare the sandwiches.
The ingredients IB's is using are substandard. I've worked in the restaurant business for 35 years and I know, when substandard ingredients are being used.
The sweet peppers have no flavor at all, the cheese has no sharpness, the buns are bland and the meat is either under seasoned or just doesn't have a lot of flavor. These are the hallmarks of restaurants that source all of the ingredients from one company and the company kind of just throws them together to make a profit.
I drove 50 mi, because I had heard it was a great cheesesteak, and I am a fanatic for great cheesesteaks, and got a large one to share with my buddies, and what I got was a bland, bland, bland. No flavor, no sharpness, no cut.
You know that when a cheesesteak is properly constructed and still has no flavor, it has nothing to do with the staff, it has to do with where the owner is sourcing the ingredients from, and the ingredients suck. Okay I feel bad for the staff there, having to work with those ingredients. It's probably going to cost them in the long run, because cutting corners like that, will lessen your business in an area where people want strong flavors.
Anyway the staff was totally cool, I didn't mind the price for the gigantic sandwich, but the experience was just boring, and bland, and no flavor.
Anyway, I wish I could send a better report, I hope they do better maybe I'll give it another chance at another time, but probably not if it's going to be like this.
I'm sure the management is going to respond to this with some cookie cutter response, not taking responsibility, because people that take responsibility for their food, don't work with food like this. It looks like they've gotten in trouble with dozens of people before, and apparently the sale from the old owner has resulted in not only poor quality ingredients, but also poor quality responses.
Stitch incoming 3.2.1

We had an incredible experience here! Finding a place that pairs top-tier food with a genuinely welcoming environment for families can be a challenge, but this spot nailed it.

We recently had the pleasure of dining at Chutney Restaurant in San Francisco, and overall, it was a pleasant experience with room for growth. The ambiance was cozy and welcoming, though a bit more attention to lighting and decor could enhance the atmosphere.
To start, we ordered the garlic naan, which was perfectly fluffy and fragrant, with just the right amount of garlic and butter. It paired beautifully with the chicken tikka masala, which featured tender chunks of chicken bathed in a creamy, spiced tomato sauce. The flavors were robust and well-balanced, making it a highlight of the meal.
The chicken breast dish was also well-cooked, juicy, and paired with a mild sauce that complemented its natural flavors. The lamb chops were another standout: they were succulent and had a nice char, with a marinade that brought out deep, savory notes.
The biryani was aromatic, with fluffy rice and well-spiced seasoning. Each bite had a nice blend of herbs and tender meat. The beef dish was flavorful, though it could have used a bit more seasoning to elevate it further.
A lovely touch was the complimentary milk tea, which was soothing and well-prepared, offering a nice, sweet finish to the meal.
In summary, while the food at Chutney Restaurant was enjoyable and showcased some really tasty dishes, there’s definitely potential for refinement and improvement. I’m excited to see how they evolve and enhance their offerings in the future.

I went to Chutney with a friend recently and was absolutely delighted. I ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and branded biryani — the meat is perfectly marinated, the spices are bright and balanced, the portions are large, you can safely share. Excellent price/quality ratio for San Francisco, I will definitely be back.

A single slice ranges around $6.40, depending on the variety, but the quality doesn’t justify the price. Vitello Tonnato ($19): Slow-roasted veal with capers and arugula. This was my favorite starter—beautifully presented, delicious, and a generous portion.
Heirloom Tomato Salad ($19): Mozzarella, pressed watermelon, and cucumbers with mint, basil, tarragon, and champagne-lemon vinaigrette. Fresh and flavorful.

Pasta:
Pappardelle ($31): Wide pasta ribbons with slow-cooked short rib ragu and scallion horseradish crema. This is one of their signature dishes, and it's always outstanding—never disappoints.

Secondi:
Liberty Farm Duck Breast ($40): Generous portion of perfectly cooked duck breast. Absolutely delicious.

Dessert:
Panna Cotta - they make the most delicious Panna Cotta in the world ! They often changed the fruit/sauce that accompany the Panna cotta.

top_reviews.content:
Some restaurants simply serve food. Others create an experience. This place belongs firmly in the second category.

We arrived around 6:00 p.m. and were pleasantly surprised by the efficiency. Despite a growing crowd, the wait was only about 10 minutes before we were seated. From the moment we walked in, it was clear this restaurant runs like a well-rehearsed orchestra. Every member of the staff seemed to know exactly where they needed to be, creating a smooth, welcoming atmosphere that immediately sets the tone for the evening.

The restaurant itself is spotless, modern, and full of energy without ever feeling chaotic.

The menu is extensive—but in the best possible way. Instead of feeling overwhelming, it feels like an invitation to come back again and again because there’s simply so much worth exploring.

Every dish that arrived at our table was memorable. The pork belly was outstanding, cooked with that perfect balance of crispy edges and tender, juicy meat that almost springs back with every bite. The cheesy noodles arrived still bubbling with heat, rich, comforting, and packed with layers of flavor. What impressed me most wasn’t just how good each dish tasted, but how every ingredient held its own while contributing to the bigger picture. Nothing disappeared into the background. Every bite told its own story before coming together in perfect harmony.

A few Korean soju shots, a couple of cold beers, great company, and incredible food turned dinner into one of those evenings you don’t really want to end.

As the night went on, the restaurant filled to capacity, and after eating there, it wasn’t difficult to understand why. Great food, attentive service, fair prices, and an atmosphere that makes you want to linger a little longer.

Some restaurants leave you full. The best ones leave you planning your next visit before you’ve even paid the bill.

This is absolutely one of those places, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it.

We were seated immediately for a late Monday dinner. We ordered the spicy rose rice cakes and bulgogi. The banchan was served right away after we ordered which was great. Service was good all around from start to finish. Highly recommend when you’re in the area!

We also tried the Spicy Stir-fried Octopus & Noodle, which tasted really delicious. it came with lots of small octopus and shrimps, and the flaor was enhanced by Bonito flakes and sesame oil, giving it a really unique taste. I would highly recommend this dish!

top_reviews.content:
Belotti Ristorante e Bottega in Oakland is a must-visit destination for anyone looking for authentic Northern Italian cuisine in the East Bay. The kitchen operates with a level of precision that is rare to find, and the consistency from start to finish is excellent.

The handmade pasta is the clear highlight of the menu. Their Casoncelli, prepared Bergamo-style with beef, prosciutto, pork shoulder, and Grana Padano, is a masterclass in balance. The dough is rolled perfectly—thin and delicate, but with enough bite to stand up to the savory butter and sage sauce. The addition of chewy smoked pancetta adds just the right amount of texture to the dish.

For starters, the Uovo Asparagi e Tartufo is a standout and a great example of layering textures. The egg has a perfectly crisp exterior that yields to a rich, molten yolk, and they aren't shy with the fresh truffle shavings. It’s an earthy, savory dish that works incredibly well with the fresh asparagus and creamy, savory fonduta underneath. The Vitello Tonnato—slow-roasted, grass-fed Piedmontese beef with a delicate yellowfin tuna sauce—is equally precise, with the caper essence and lemon zest providing a bright, clean finish.

Even while dining in the outdoor parklet, the experience was great. It’s well-designed and comfortable, making the most of the natural light while keeping the atmosphere quiet and enjoyable. I also appreciated that they serve imported Italian MoleCola rather than standard sodas; it has a crisp, refreshing bite that cleanses the palate effectively between heavier courses.

Dessert service was exceptional. The Affogato al Caffe is excellent on its own, but adding a splash of Grand Marnier gives it a sophisticated, citrusy complexity that pairs perfectly with the espresso and vanilla gelato. The Bunet Piemontese was also a highlight—a rich, velvety pudding of cocoa and crushed amaretti cookies, encased in a 60% dark chocolate shell and topped with soft, unsweetened whipped cream. It is intense but not too heavy, which is exactly how a dessert like this should be.

There isn't a weak link in the experience at Belotti. It is officially one of the best spots in the East Bay for anyone seeking high-quality, authentic Italian food.

Fell in love with this place. Everything was so delicious. I rarely eat Northern Italian food. The flavors were such a treat. The weather was perfect for the parklet outdoors. Everything combined for a perfect meal. Can't wait to come back!

I'm so impressed with the dishes that they pump out of that tiny kitchen for the amount of tables they support inside and outside. Big claps to the chef and staff!!

We had an incredible lunch at Belotti Ristorante in Rockridge, Oakland. We tried the Pappardelle Al Funghi, Spaghetti Pomodoro with Burrata, Bruschetta, and Panna Cotta for dessert. Everything was outstanding, but the Pappardelle Al Funghi was truly unforgettable – rich, earthy, and perfectly balanced. The panna cotta was divine!
Staff is welcoming and service is great.

I ordered a burrito and soft drink, which came to $30 before tip $35 total after adding gratuity. While the food was acceptable, I don’t believe it justified the $30 price point. The service was mediocre at best, with no complimentary refills offered on soft drinks, and the burrito itself was noticeably smaller than what I’d expect for that price.
For the same money, I can get a more generous portion at Chipotle just down the street, with free refills included. top_reviews.content: I’ve had my eye on this little restaurant for quite a while now, as I’m a big fan of soups. The waiter did an excellent job—he actually advised me *not* to order a main course, warning me that the soup portion would be huge, and he was genuinely concerned I wouldn't be able to finish it all! I’m truly grateful to him for that; I definitely wouldn't have been able to handle a second dish as well. That is exactly how real waiters should operate—offering genuine recommendations on menu choices, rather than just trying to upsell you! Major kudos! And the soup was superb!

The Old Siam is conveniently located on the corner of Ellis and Mason streets in downtown area (two walking blocks away from Powell Street Subway Station) that is surrounded by hotels imhv should be regarded one of the few best authentic affordable Thai restaurants left in The City.
According to legendary “Chef Pam” from Bangkok authentic Thai food is indeed a marriage of Thai Chinese which is consisted of “five elements: salt, acid, spices, texture and the Maillard reaction, the chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that occur when heated.” However, there is a saying "green comes from blue, but intends to be better than blue." Signature Thai cuisine is unique which has many flavors:{ 1. sweet, 2. salty, 3. sour, 4. spicy, and 5.bitter} not overpowering one another yet robust with aromatic lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, coconut milk, palm sugar, and red chilies 😮 😳.
My favorites at the Old Siam are ❶Lunch Specials: Combination of Catfish Prik Khing @Goong Hom Par {Fried Shrimp Rolls(2)} ❷Chef Specials: Combination Seafood or Siam Seafood ❸ Thai Noodle Soup: Thai Traditional Noodle Soup or Seafood Noodle Soup. “Gin hâi à-ròi ná!”😉Kop Jai!🙏 Nick!🫡
PS: "Siam" is the former name of Thailand,  derived from foreign terms (possibly Sanskrit for "dark/brown" also in ancient Chinese referred to based on its pronunciation as Xian [暹] or, more commonly, Xianluo [暹羅]. Thai Chinese are the largest minority group in the country and possibly the largest overseas Chinese community in the world, estimated at 10 million people accounting for 11-14% of the total population of Thailand. The Chinese traders started migrating to neighboring Siam in mid 1300s and primarily are Cantonese, Hokkien, Teochew, Hainanese, and Hakka.  Under King Rama in early 20th century law required the adoption of Thai surnames by migrants, a move which was ostensibly aimed at the Thai Chinese community. Common Chinese Surnames according to AI are in two categories:
1. "Sae": Saelee/Saeli (李), Saetang/Saetung (陳), Sae-ung (黃), Sae-ngow (吳), Sae-lim (林), Sae-wong (王).
2. Long Surnames (Teochew/Thai mix):
Limcharoen / Tancharoen (Lim/Tan - 林).
Wongsuwan / Wongsawad (Wong - 黃/王).
Jiarawanon (Chia/Ha/Xia - 謝). Tongthaworn (Tong 唐 or 湯).{Is that right, Hannah 😂}

Stopped in to grab some slices to take to our hotel room.  For take home slice pizza it was pretty good.  Would loved to have sat down and tried their specialty there.  Kind of a pizza geek after spending lots of time in NYC touring pizza and taking classes to learn the art of pizza making at home.  Hope that their restaurant version is better than the slice take out.  Saw a lot of Tony's boxes around town so clearly it's a popular spot.

Ordered Sicilian Combo.  For my first experience I ordered just a slice.  It looks great in the display case.  I received bread with a super spicy sauce as if tomatoes and oregano didn’t exist.  You would think there would be cheese and all the toppings listed even if it was just a little bit.  It had nothing.

top_reviews.content: I used to frequent this place when I lived in the Bay Area, so when I have the chance to go back, I took my friends here. We waited over 40 min for 3 people on a Friday night. Unfortunately, most of our dishes fell flat - it was on the bland side and nothing spectacular. Even the sampler dish was just ok - nam kaow rice was not crispy enough nor was it well seasoned. The only dish we enjoyed was the wonton soup , which is the most flavorful. For comparison, Night and Song market in LA, or Sticky Rice Lao street food in Orlando, FL, blows this place out of the water. It definitely does not deserve the recognition it deserves. Or perhaps its quality has changed since I visited over 10 years ago. However, we did randomly run into an old friend we haven’t seen in 25 years here, so that was super cool.

Been going to CG for years. I'm stuffed and sleepy so short review.  All the food at CG is good you can't go wrong.  Get the sampler  plate that sausage will change your life the crispy rice that's a meal and a deal. I need a nap.

5 stars for food, but giving 4 because historically their phone almost never rings properly, and their hostess told me last call was 9:45pm when I called earlier today but they actually close at 9 🤦🏻‍♀️ Their website also doesn’t work properly… so yeah amazing food but management could really use some work.

Favorites:
- Larp
- Pumpkin curry
- Pad ped pla cook (catfish)
- Rice ball salad

Everything, especially the vegetables, is literally cooked to perfection.
Great food, menu has many options, Laotian and Thai selection, the food I got was just a bit sweet for me. Lovely service and food came quick!

Pad Thai was pretty good, and big portion. Green curry was excellent. Thai iced tea also good, and they even put less ice when asked. Mango sticky rice just okay. Rice was a little dense, but coconut sauce is flavorful, and mangoes were rice. Friendly service

top_reviews.content: Absolutely amazing experience from start to finish! The food was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned. Every dish tasted authentic and homemade, especially the grilled meats, hummus, and warm pita bread. The portions were generous, the service was friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy and welcoming. You can really tell they use high-quality ingredients and put care into every meal. Easily one of the best Mediterranean restaurants I’ve been to — highly recommend and will definitely be back!

We went for a family dinner with friends and kids and surprisingly we and one more table, were the only ones with kids. The other table sat outside.

There was no wait for a Sunday dinner.

The place has more of a formal but cozy ambience. You can dress up or be casual and both would go.

The food itself was a mix of good and okay.

They start out with some chips for the table. We had 4 vegetarians and 2 non vegetarians in the group and everyone had a good set of items to choose from.

We shared the brussel sprouts which were great, the grape leaf rice with herbs (warak inab) which was okay. The non vegetarians shared the Musakhan chicken rolls from appetizers which were great.

For main course we had the beet arugula salad (great), makhaluba with lamb (great) and mujjadara vegetarian (which was okay). We shared the baklava with ice cream dessert which was good!

Overall-
Food had some great items and others were just okay.  The overall menu is on pricier side. There is no kids menu but we never order from kids menu; and all dishes were kid friendly . So it wasn't an issue for us. But something to note as many families do look for a kids section and this place doesn't have one.

Ambience is nice and chattery but not noisy. People seemed to be having a good time

Good clean restrooms
There is outdoor seating and parking is on the street

I would definitely go again to try more dishes.

Food was very good.  5 of us were seated along with our 2 yr old. We were automatically charged the 6 or more person gratuity and taxed for the gratuity. If you will be automatically be assessed the gratuity, please provide good service. Please do not forget about us because you know you will automatically get your tip. It doesn't feel good.
The food was amazing. The ambience was lively. We had a great time. Looking forward to my next visit.

Really enjoyed a Friday night out with partner for first time dining at this lovely Mediterranean place.  Serverd by Erika, we had a great evening with her service. Explained many options on the menu, made perfect drink recommendations,  and all was with a smiling attitude.  Thats been hard to find lately.  Thank you for a great night Erika! Thank you Zaytoon. We'll be back

top_reviews.content:
Juan's Place has been proudly serving the Berkeley community since 1972, and being a customer for about 30 years makes the connection to this iconic spot even more meaningful. The restaurant’s remarkable history is rooted in a commitment to authentic Mexican cuisine and a welcoming, family-run atmosphere that has drawn generations of locals, Cal students, and visitors for over five decades.

Having been a loyal patron for around 30 years, it’s clear how special Juan’s Place is—a true staple where the flavors and traditions of Mexico are celebrated with every meal, continuing a legacy that began more than 50 years ago.

Pro's:

- Quiet place, at least for weekday lunch, no music playing, relaxing atmosphere

-Friendly staff who give you free soda refills and pretty much as much tortilla chips and salsa that you want. I believe they make their own tortilla chips and they are quite good. They will even give you a bag and little containers to take home some of the chips and salsa if you want to.

Con's:

Way too expensive for what you get! I can't say the food is bad or anything, but certainly nothing to write home about. It's simply over-priced!

Such an amazing spot to enjoy! Their super burrito is HUGE and the tacos are a very healthy serving.

The lime wine margarita was a solid drink choice. The waiters here are so kind and happy to strike up a conversation and share a laugh with you.

The prices are great, the food is great, and the parking was easy!

What an amazing, family restaurant! My wife and friends try to order from here once a week. They're always generous with their chips, salsa, and extras. Food is always fresh and you can tell by the dairy they use! The place is huge too with an under rated bar where we ate and watched the Warriors. Such an under rated restaurant in the bay!

This is a classic place that I hadn’t been to since I was in college. It hasn’t changed a bit. The decor is really cool and the food is very good. Prices are a little bit high, considering what you get. Service was good, but not great. I was surprised at how long it took for the food to get there. The servers and staff were very nice. The place is a bit off the beaten path, but if you’re in the area, it’s definitely worth checking out.

name: Kuma Sushi + Sake
address: 1040 Polk St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States

google.name: Kuma Sushi + Sake

google.description: Minimalist neighborhood locale for nigiri, sashimi & Japanese small bites.

top_reviews.content: So it was my birthday, and I really wanted sushi.  There is no dearth of quality sushi restaurants in San Francisco, however almost all of them are omakase – and to be honest, I am not a huge omakase fan (and I speak Japanese, have lived in Japan, and have consumed sushi all over the world – omakase does not necessarily mean better). Kuma’s execution and fish quality is some of the best I have had in the US in a long time. I dined with my mother, who is a Hamachi kama fan, and she said it was one of the best she has ever had. The atmosphere is no frills, and there were only two staff working the floor, one was I believe the manager – but service was attentive. Overall, this is probably my favorite new place to have non-omakase sushi in the city. Definitely recommend, and you definitely need a reservation.

In San Francisco for one night and wanted some great sushi and we lucked out finding this gem of a place. We grabbed a reservation which I highly recommend since it was packed. We sat at the sushi bar with a great view to watch them work their magic. I got the jackalope which was recommended by our sever and it was so good and I also ordered the Fresco which was also really yummy. My husband got sashimi of all kinds and loved it all. We also got a seaweed salad which was great too.
Appetizers were good, sushi is ok. We got the hamachi crudo and tofu apps + 3 rolls. One of our friends had bones in her raw fish (see photo below). Quite pricey as well. Would not recommend.

Fantastic experience. I love salmon so my waiter helped me pick the best sashimi and sushi roll. I sat at the bar and it was so nice watching the kitchen prepping everyone's orders. At the end the almighty ice cream which I chose the pistachio flavor. The best ice cream in the city I have tried lately. Highly recommend this restaurant to all sushi lovers.

Cute atmosphere, amazing, attentive service and great food! Def some of the best sushi my fiancé and I have had yet. We aren’t from the area but came from our engagement shoot over at city hall and we loveeee sushi- we decided what better place to get fresh sushi than sf- we couldn’t be more pleased with our pick! the cinch roll and the hey girl rolls were my personal fav, but everything was so tasty. And the sake🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟we even got the sweetest little surprise at the end as a congratulations to us on our upcoming wedding🥹🫶🏻 100000/10 food + experience and can’t wait to be back!

top_reviews.content:
Nice looking Italian bistro style restaurant, they ah e small bar by the entrance where you can order drinks.
We ordered 2 bottles of the Montepulciano and it was a good vino, but with the pasta it put me in a good coma for hours 🥱

The food can be hit or miss, for appetizers we got the mussels and clams in a red sauce and the beef tartare and arugula salad with pistachios and golden beets. The tartare was pretty unremarkable and didn’t have a zing in the dressing, it was quite plain and ordinary. The arugula salad was also quite ordinary but the clams and mussels were quite flavorful but a tad too salty

For mains I tried the classic spaghetti and meatballs, but the sauce and the meatballs were quite flavorless, and I sent it back. My friends enjoyed their Calabrian pasta which was the most flavorful dish in the place and the pasta was al dente to the max which added to the flavor of the dish.

For dessert we share a tiramisu and it was quite good, but not made in house.

Very cozy Italian spot - feels like old school family vibe. Food was decent, I liked the Pavarotti pasta with chicken, Illini and dried tomatoes - very tender fusilli and creamy sauce. Was not a fan of gnocchi- on a chewy side, lacking softness. But the pesto sauce was great. The service was very nice and good came fast. We definitely enjoyed the neighborhood vibes seating next to the window and watching couples and families entering the restaurant for a weekend dinner.

I always complain about how hard it is (impossible even, when it comes to sandwiches) to find comparable Italian fare in the SF bay area, coming from NY/NJ. I visited here for dinner based on others' recommendations. It's no doubt a proud joint with long history (which serves as a proof of quality itself), so obviously there's some lower bound on the food/service quality to expect.

TLDR; the food was ok. I had gnocchi and as everyone mentions this place really wants everything al dente so it was a bit too firm for my taste. I personally found the sauce (I got the creamy tomato) had two problems: (1) it was too little (barely any left to soak up with bread), and (2) it was a bit too mild in flavor. All in all I had had better gnocchi at a random Italian restaurant I dropped by on the street in NY. I also had tiramisu for dessert, but this was unfortunately absolutely mediocre. I think it was the quality of store-bought.

I did enjoy the glass of cab which was a good pick and poured generously! And the staff was exceptionally hospitable, so no problem there. I think it's still a solid option in the area, hence 4 stars. But for me the food wasn't quite hitting the level I'd have liked, especially for the very high price they charge.

Honestly so delicious! Lovely neighborhood trattoria on street corner. Host and my server, Jesus Al., were so nice, thoughtful and attentive.  I had the Polpettine (spaghetti and meatballs).  The beef and pork meatballs were so flavorful and tender, pasta perfectly cooked, and tomato sauce was so flavorful.  A side of broccoli with lemon and Parmesan was perfect accompaniment.  Nicely crafted martini.  Highly recommend !!  Oh and value was great too!

I had a great experience at this cozy Italian restaurant. The atmosphere is warm and inviting, with a charmingly rustic feel, complete with a well-stocked bar and string lights that give it a homey, comfortable vibe. The service was friendly and attentive without being overbearing, and our waiter was helpful with the menu.

The real standout of the meal, and something you can tell from the photos, is the sheer size of the portions. They don't mess around! I ordered a pasta dish topped with a generous amount of fresh basil and what looked like burrata or a similar creamy cheese. My friend's spaghetti with a huge, impressive-looking meatball was also massive, and the clams in white wine sauce were abundant and delicious. You definitely get your money's worth here, and you'll likely have leftovers.

For dessert, we had a simple but delicious bowl of vanilla ice cream with chocolate syrup. It was the perfect way to cap off a very filling meal. I highly recommend giving this place a try.

Surprisingly the asada tacos did not impress. The meat was overcooked and had that pasty texture I don’t like.
Chicken burrito fell apart. Flavor was basic.

The place is fine, ambience is fine - maybe a little too in-your-face to appeal to a more generic demographic but I don't mind. But that doesn't mean anything if I'm taking a bite of my somewhat mediocre quesadilla (can we flavor the chicken just a *little* more please) and a black hair falls out of the chicken. Their mole amarillo was at least authentic enough. But still. I clearly bit into someone's hair. And that's an automatic one-star review.

Wow! The torta I got was delicious! I would gladly drill a few more holes in my belt to make room for more of those.
I wish I worked close by.

Highly recommend the corn and zucchini taco, I actually thought it was more flavorful than the fish taco. You pay at the front before sitting down.

Plenty of seating and the food comes out fast. There’s two bathrooms in the back.

I’ve been eating here since I was a kid and it never disappoints. The tacos are delicious and the churros are super super fresh. I love the limonata and it’s the perfect lunch spot if you’re shopping on 4th street.

top_reviews.content: My wife and I stopped in on a Friday night after an event at Ft. Mason. We were seated right away in a heated outdoor booth. Service was quick, the food was excellent, and the atmosphere was perfect.

Absolutely fantastic experience at Sodini’s. The food was outstanding—easily some of the best Italian I’ve had, and that’s coming from someone who’s spent plenty of time in New York. The pasta was perfectly cooked, the sauce rich and flavorful, and everything tasted fresh and authentic.

What really made the experience stand out was the hospitality. Mark, the owner, was incredibly welcoming and made me feel genuinely special. I was traveling alone, and he went out of his way to make the experience enjoyable.

The atmosphere has that classic old-school Italian charm that’s hard to find. This is the kind of place you come back to every time you’re in San Francisco. Highly recommend.

We had amazing Service here.  My spaghetti and meatballs was good. As as the salad.  People at my table, had the Jeannine and clamps that they said was excellent.    Our server went out of her way to make us feel comfortable, even though we had a two-year-old at the table.   They have a lovely red wine in carafe’s for a good price.  Not a bad place to check out. They have been around for years.

Server got irritated after only giving us two seconds to give her our order. Instead of ordering more food, we were rushed to order only two entrees. Not only that, it took her almost half an hour to serve us bread.

The service was absolutely garbage. It didn't even matter what the food tasted like.

By the way, we sat at the bar and Mark was not funny. He was "switching drinks" around as a joke, and managed to contaminate my drink with his hands.

If you want to eat at a circus, feel free.

It was ok overall. The atmosphere was nice as we went their early too so no loud dinner rush and nice staff. However the food was average at best unfortunately. The Bruschetta wasn't very good as the tomatoes wernt very good quality/fresh. The Fritto Misto was ok. The artichoke harts were cooked well but the calamari was slightly stringy. The dips were good but the batter maybe could have had more seasoning. The main dishes we had was the Ravoli with white sauce and Canaloni. The Ravioli unfortunately seemed to have been some sort of frozen thing, the cheese was dry on the inside and the pasta itself seemed gummy/overcooked. Somehow the sauce was also very overly rich and not a present meal overall. The Canaloni was just average. It wasn't bad but it wasn't great. Unfortunately we likely wouldn't go back especially due to the pricing.

top_reviews.content:
I ordered 3 chicken tenders and coleslaw and the cashier immediately assumed I wanted it to go which made me feel unwelcome.

The service was very fast but the food was extremely bad. The coleslaw tasted like it was several days expired and the lemonaide was extremely tart and the chicken was tough with almost no seasoning. The house dipping sauce was the only good thing about the meal – and the waitress was very nice to look at.

The breakfast menu looks much more appealing than the dinner menu. I would give this restaurant another try for breakfast but sadly I am only in town today and fly back to San Diego tomorrow.

This was my first time here and I will be back. The menu was huge, the food was delicious (!!) and the service was excellent. The biscuits need a special mention. I love a good biscuit and these did not disappoint.

Still a classic after re-opening!! the menu is slightly different from before closing in 2024 but it is largely the same place. yummy options aplenty. Note that gratuity is additionally charged automatically to support employees so menu prices don’t reflect the whole price - it’s worth it though! picture is the maple orange glazed chicken sandwich, my personal go to.

They make everything from scratch and these kind of diners are an anomaly nowadays. Four kinds of house made hot sauces, jam and seasonal specialties, gluten free toast, easy parking in the neighborhood, the most awesome staff, family-run, community-minded. What’s not to love?

A 20% tip was pre-added to the bill without disclosure and couldn’t be adjusted. You serve yourself water, get your own coffee, and walk to the counter to pay, so there isn’t really any service that warrants a 20% tip (you’re essentially paying the worker’s wage, as their receipt even says). The servers never checked in after dropping off the food, and the table wasn’t clean; there was still food stuck on it after staff wiped it down. They also seemed understaffed, as the bathroom was nasty 😭. At this point, I’d rather just pick up the food myself. About half an hour after eating (my first and only meal of the day) my stomach didn’t feel great. I’m in agony hours after 🙃

top_reviews.content:
Miss Saigon is one of those hidden gems that reminds you why family-owned restaurants are so special.

The atmosphere feels warm and authentic, with Christmas lights, religious décor, and patriotic American touches that make it feel like you're dining in someone's home rather than a commercial chain. It's a true mom-and-pop restaurant with plenty of character.

I ordered the filet mignon pho and the filet mignon bánh xèo, and both were outstanding. The pho broth was clear, rich, and full of flavor without being overly salty. The filet mignon was tender, and the fresh herbs, bean sprouts, jalapeños, onions, and lime let you customize every bowl. The bánh xèo was huge, perfectly crispy, generously filled, and served with fresh vegetables and a delicious dipping sauce.

The portions were generous, the ingredients were fresh, and the service was friendly and welcoming.

If you're looking for authentic Vietnamese comfort food in San Francisco instead of a trendy, overpriced restaurant, Miss Saigon is absolutely worth the visit. I'll definitely be back. Highly recommended! 🍜🇻🇳

Came in mid afternoon on a Sunday, naturally it wasn’t very busy at this time, but wow i’m so happy at how good this place was in terms of food and service. Exactly what you would expect from a mom and pop viet restaurant. Get the fried crab spring rolls, I kid you not these might be in my top 5 all time spring rolls and I’ve had a crap ton of viet in my time. Also the Pho Ga is free range chicken so delicious and heals the soul.
The best freaking Banh mi sandwich you’ll ever have in the city. It’s fresh and soft. There spring rolls are also the best. It’s beautiful inside it’s just the best !

Service was good it was just two girls making their rounds to everyone.

Atmosphere was unique and fun and made me feel like I was in Asia.

Food was honestly amazing. Seriously everything was so fresh and all the veggies to put on my pho were too and I loved that part. It’s the little details.

I had the chicken pho and a side of fried egg rolls.

I’ve ordered takeout twice — the smiley face the first time and the little heart this time were both so heartwarming! The food was also very satisfying. And thanks for the complimentary Sprite today, it was such a nice surprise!

reviews_snippets.content: "Their food is well above standard quality and the staff are very kind."

top_reviews.content:
I am so appreciate to the work for all of the foods here. I don’t try all of the meal here so I don’t know everything about this restaurant. This is my first time and I ordered 3 meals. My favorite is “cơm tấm” with 100% whole food and house made, that what I love and I really respect it, the taste is just perfect for me.
I like the test of Papaya salad with soy protein but I wish the soy is house made
And the last meal is salty for me.
People here are nice and the restaurant is clean, huge there are tables for 1, 2 or even group of 6-8 people I think 🤔

Maybe I will comeback again to try other meals. But the “cơm tấm” is so good 😊. I am so happy with this meal

Golden Era, hands down best Asian inspired vegan restaurant in S.F. The food is always delicious here. The seitan is the best I have had! I don't know the magic they do, but it's exceptional. Spring rolls, drumsticks, rainbow salad all 5 stars the beef stew was good.

Golden Era is a rare find in the plant-based dining scene. While too many vegan establishments focus on ethical and environmental benefits but serve what is essentially non-meat junk food, this restaurant takes a different approach. The food here is not only good for the planet and the animals but is also good for your health.

The extensive menu encompasses Vietnamese and Chinese specialties that can be customized to meet specific dietary needs. The service was caring and family-like, filled with helpful advice. When we requested adjustments to our dishes, they were executed perfectly. Furthermore, when we mentioned that one of our party is a fan of spicy food, the staff responded not with a single option, but with three different sources of heat—a gesture that was highly appreciated and added significant enjoyment to the meal.

The cuisine is excellent and the service is commendable, but we must point out one significant weakness: the restroom. Unfortunately, we found the entire mirror covered with rude inscriptions. For a family-friendly establishment, this is out of place, and the management would do well to clean it up promptly.

As ordinary consumers, we are not paid or compensated in any way for this review. We appreciate the healthy, high-quality food and hope the facility maintenance matches the kitchen's standards in the future.

Golden Era is a 100% vegan Vietnamese spot with delicious noodle soups. I ordered the vegan crab noodle soup (bun rieu chay) and it tasted so close to the traditional non-vegan version. The tomato-based broth was the best part of the whole bowl, a bit sour, light, comforting and full of flavor. It came with tofu, soy protein, green herbs and all the toppings went well together, super addicting!

I came around 5:30pm, so it was pretty quiet and easy to get seated. Their menu is also hugeeeeee, with everything from banh mi, noodle soups, entrees and rice plates to desserts and drinks. You’ll want to come with a group so everyone can order different dishes to share.

Highly recommend if you’re in SF and looking for a great vegan restaurant, or even if you’re not vegan and just want to explore unique twists of Vietnamese dishes!

This place is a vegetarian’s heaven. It’s truly a relief to have such well salted, well marinated vegetarian food in SF. Lemongrass deluxe, Thai fried rice are some of our favorites. Chow fun was decent. But overall this place is a win for vegans. I will definitely keep going back.
