top_reviews.content: I know this is a historical location that is thriving with plenty of diversity. I saw peeps from all walks of life happy and ready to be served. Really good customer service and awesome variety. Everything is made to order, so you may wait a few minutes. I’ll make this a staple for Chinese food. I got carry out so haven’t had the food just yet but when I get home it’s on! Shrimp egg fo young extra green onion, vegetable fried rice with extra onions about $47, but servings are huge enough for 2-3 meals from what I can see.

Nice Peking duck served on platter with some sauce underneath the duck and that’s it. Our server recommended The Gold Medal Chop Suey as a starch to accompany the duck and it was delicious with slices of beef, chicken, pork and pieces of scallops and other tasty sea critters which I couldn’t recognize. Service is fast, maybe even curt, but that’s what it takes for them to be so fast at such a busy small place. The 9pm crowd was very diverse with a large table of loud post-clubbing guests which added to the “ambiance.”  Not for everyone but I really enjoyed this place.

We saw this restaurant was recommended by people for their hours and decent offerings. We came pretty late in the night, so there was no wait and parking was a breeze.

Food itself was OK. Their menu is pretty big with reasonable prices. We got a few things, like the BBQ pork rice platter, roast duck, congee, and wonton noodle soup. The standout was definitely the duck, while everything else was pretty average or so-so.

If you've never been to an authentic CANTONESE restaurant, the service may put you off at first. But Cantonese people and restaurants tend to be very straight forward and can seem unfriendly. I wouldn't say service was unfriendly at all, but it was more for efficiency. They do charge a service charge, but it is not unreasonable.

Overall, if you want some Cantonese comfort food this is a good place to have it, especially if it is super late at night. Maybe we just came at a time where food was more mediocre but we were happy this restaurant was open. When we left it was bordering towards midnight and the restaurant started to fill up, so looks like many people appreciate for this restaurant for their hours.

This is a locals go-to for decades. From seafood to meat dishes all your traditional Chinese dishes can be found here. Nothing is amaricanized like the panda food. You can’t go wrong with bbq duck, wontons, salt n pepper fried pork chops, chow meins, and even vegetarian options are good here. Lobster and crabs are also delicious.
Bring your friends or family here and eat an authentic Chinese meal here. It’s almost a whole in the wall so no need to dressed up.

Don’t forget to follow me on IG for more great foodie spots to try!
@Only1Christinelu

My friend and I were looking for Chinese cuisine after 10:30pm on a Friday and night and Google led us to New Gold Medal Restaurant in Oakland, at 389kk 8th St.  It clean and friendly with a large menu to choose from.  Walnut shrimp is my JAM and I was not disappointed.  The serving was hearty, the walnuts nice and sweet and the shrimp....FRESH!, as was the shrimp in the fried rice I ordered. My picky friend ordered egg-foo-young and beef and vegetable chow-mein and there were no complaints.  We had enough food for the next day; lunch and dinner. I am excited to visit this wonderful eatery again.
Great service from start to finish.
No craziness either. This restaurant is quiet and pleasing.
Open till 3am but check before you go.

Capo’s is a true gem for anyone who loves classic Chicago style deep dish pizza. The pizza was outstanding, with a rich, flavorful sauce, generous toppings, and a perfectly baked crust that brought everything together. Every bite was delicious.

The portions are good for two persons. We ordered a César Salad with anchovies, a baked reguetoni Genovese, a vanilla ice cream and a tiramisu and everything resulted 70 USD. top_reviews.content: Went here late afternoon. Very fun, chill hangout spot. Great beer and cocktail selection. I had the root beer old fashioned, which came with a root beer dumdum!  Service was very friendly and alert. Food was delicious. My partner and I both had burgers (patty melt and 5150). We shared the porcetta fries (por que no!). My only minor nitpick is that my medium rare burger wasn't.  It was cooked just like my partner's medium, and even that want exactly medium. Luckily both were still juicy and delicious! The fries were bomb. Definitely coming back here and bringing friends.

Quite possibly one of the best cheeseburgers I've had in a long long time. If they ask you how you'd like that meat done -- don't bother.  It's all medium.   I don't know why they ask. Still juicy though.  4 on food just because of that.  A little pink would have made that a 5

Beeryland is absolutely fantastic. I've been coming here for the star trek trivia for almost two years. The adult slushies are yummy, and so is most of the food. I don't know if the kimchi grilled cheese is still on the menu, but it's a divisive item. My friends like it but I despise it. Use caution. As you can see by the state of my AmInal Fries (yes the spelling is correct), I am one happy customer. Four stars on the atmosphere because the bathroom could use a facelift, but it is a bar. Cheers!

The burger & garlic fries here were amazing. Good beer list, lots of outdoor tables and warmers in the evening. Cool that it has a room of pinball machines. Definitely want to come back to try other items on the menu!

Hi, I went into Berryland today as it is Fourth of July and wanted some burger as well as beers from my favorite burger place. I ordered a 5150 w a side of mac and cheese, no veggies with a cider. And my partner ordered the impossible burger w lettuce only, and a dirty Shirley. We paid, and I tipped the man (who turns out to be the owner 15%). My partner sits down, and I wait for the drinks. I watch him make the Shirley and there is no alcohol placed in at all. It’s okay, I won’t make a fuss I go and sit down. Partner and I disappointed, but whatever. And then my order comes out completely wrong. It comes out as a Mac and cheese burger. My partners burger has no lettuce at all. I clarify all these issues to the waitress. She apologizes and goes back to the kitchen to correct this. She speaks to the man who took our order and he marches over. First starting by telling us that it does have vodka in it, I inform I watched him make it and there was no vodka. He takes a taste and agrees to make us a new drink. He argues and says that there is vodka in it and he can taste it and that he does not make mistakes. I then go “‘my Order was completely wrong and so was my partners” and he begins yelling at me. I walk over to the waitress to ask to speak to a manager or owner, to which I am informed it is this man. He is the owner. The owner yelled at me over him being wrong. I asked for a refund and got yelled at more. We left and will not be returning. A shame to see my favorite burger joint of the last few months ruined by the owner being a terrible person.

Cafe Colucci has been on our list for months so glad we had the opportunity to visit on MLK Jr. Day ❤️

Everything from the vibe, food, and service were better than we could’ve imagined. What a fun time and thanks to Damian for the hospitality🔥

Some favorites were the sambusas, fish, lentils, tibs, and tiramisu. We will absolutely be back ✨

Overall, a satisfying experience and a solid choice for burger lovers in Berkeley.

top_reviews.content:
Ippudo is the closest you'll get to authentic Japanese ramen in the states.  The price is average to high, but its definitely worth it.
If youre eating ramen, save enough broth to do kaedama (its free)!

Parking in Berkeley is a bit tough, so I would recommend parking a little ways away and walking 5 mins or so.

We reserved a table for 7 a day before but when we got there in time, we still have to wait a whopping 20 minutes. On top of that, the portion size was not generous (little soup which is extremely salty because there was no liquid, basically no meat, and no toppings). I feel like I am basically spending 20 dollars for just a bunch of plain noodles. I would not recommend this place at all.

Ippudi's hakata ramen is the best I have found outside of Japan. Always consistently good and made with quality ingredients. Our table was not cleaned well and the condiments on the table looked old and the containers looked like they needed to be cleaned, hence the reason for my 3 and 4 stars on the service and the atmosphere.
Pictures says it all: Ramen egg was served with a gigantic hole. I understand that eggs have variations but even at home if I open an egg that looks like that, I would never serve it to my guests.

Food: OK, solid for US ramen. Nice to be able to get Hakata style. Broth was solid, presentation was lacking but not terrible. As lunch, this bowl of ramen did not leave me feeling disgusted at the amount of food and oil consumed, which I think is a failing in the world of ramen. It lacks the carefully put-together excess that should be present.

Price: too high. Without adding the $4 egg, my $17 bowl of ramen was fairly simplistic and the portion size didn't feel like a serious indulgence the way ramen really should. I think this is one of the better options for ramen I've had in the bay, but as with most US ramen, the value is just not there and this value is worse than some other very solid I've had in the area.

Atmosphere and Service: Nice, clean restaurant with attentive staff. The disposable chopsticks are cheap and do fray - not the end of the world. A few hand-trucks of ingredients came through the front at about 1pm - also not a big deal, but did have to interact with that on my way out. Overall very pleased with the atmosphere and service, no strong complains or issues. The Japanese menu wall art is a nice touch.

Overall: For me personally, I probably won't come back, but if you're into the local ramen scene you'll probably enjoy this spot.

top_reviews.content:
An ok 3.5 / 5 experience.  Rounding up to 4 🫥

I understand that carrots and zucchinis in your taco burrito can throw people off. On the other hand if you want more veggies in your Mexican food, this place would be a blessing. I think they should do bell pepper and onion fajitas, instead of carrots and zucchini.

I got the chicken soup burrito, which came out to $15 before tip

The chicken was a little under flavored, and the beans did not have that signature Mexican umami depth to it.

Overall, under spiced and missed the mark flavored, but freshly made, which is always nice.

I did wish they grilled their burritos like many other Mexican places. Or just generally made it less soggy and wet.

Perhaps this place is more suited for people who don’t want as many spices in their food and don’t have a pepper tolerance

They do have a little kids plate for $6.50 which is nice. Seating space is very limited so take out is advised.

We’ll probably give this place another shot for their tacos, but not for their burritos

Great crispy taco, carnita with everything. Well cooked meat, plenty of food. Gets a bit messy if the counter person is sloppy with the sauces but still always good. Friendly check out, fair pricing fast service.

A classic, awesome burrito place, I’ve been going to Gordo’s for 20+ years. Simple, delicious ingredients, fast service and friendly staff. Love it!
A little tight space and light on the seating but still a cool vibe.

Just like another reviewer, I had started with Gordo’s on Clement St. when I moved to East Bay, the college Ave location was the tops.

It had been 20 years since I was in the Bay Area, and was so happy to nothing changed.  Just delicious burritos.

I think Gordo’s secret is steaming the tortilla with the cheese.  Get it all melt.

I hope it won’t be another 20 years; but if it is Gordo’s: please don’t change. 👍👍

In response to some of the other reviews:

The pollo asado is the best I’ve ever had—perfectly cooked. If someone is afraid of, or confused by, blackness on their chicken, may I recommend Chipotle.

The moisture in the burritos is part of the excellent cooking. The beans are perfect, every time, and this means that they are perfectly moist; as is the salsa, the meat, and the rice. All perfect, every time. So, yes: you won’t get a super-dry burrito, and yes, this means that if you insist on taking it home, it may degrade slightly in structure (it will be perfect if eaten in-taqueria). My friends and I have been eating these burritos for over twenty years and have enjoyed many a one at home, just a little wetter. It’s worth it to have perfectly cooked ingredients.

Atmosphere. Let’s talk about atmosphere. This is one of the last  not Starbucked, not third-wave-coffee-housed joints left in the Bay. If you’re uncomfortable with the small space or old-school tables and chairs, then, again, allow me to recommend Chipotle. Or Taco Bell. How about Taco Bell? They keep their revolving-door A.I. market image updated every few months. You shouldn’t be bothered by any authenticity or lasting tradition there.

Bottom line: Gordo Taqueria is a Bay original. So many old authentic Bay Area eateries have been bought out, disappeared, or made unrecognizable. Please let Bay Area natives enjoy this one in peace before we flip every last space into a Tesla showroom.

I am sorry to hear about poor customer service, if it’s true; and to hear that long-timers have experienced bad food service. I hope that everything is going Ok for the owners and staff during a weird, tough time in the Bay and the world. Customers do have a right to demand civil treatment and continued quality.

An outdoor to-go stand only. Might need luck finding parking but the order came out pretty quick.

Strawberry Shortcake ($8.00): Basically a deconstructed shortcake, if you like that kind of stuff. A biscuit in one corner, cream in another, then topped with strawberries. It's pretty good but not mind-blowing.

Do not underestimate the power of the local pie store in the Temescal neighborhood! If you're looking for a local business that makes the best pies, whether it be apple, blueberry, or more -- look no further than Bakesale Bettty!

They are located right off of Telegraph and 51st Street, right across from the Children's Hospital of Oakland. Though they do most of their sales outside (rain or shine), they know just how to impress the right people -- and one of those people would have to include me because their pies really took me to a different level of pie appreciation.

We went on a Friday morning (keep in mind they are closed Monday through Wednesday, so plan accordingly when you want to go buy these pies), and while the lines were a bit long, the line wasn't too bad, and they went rather quick.

Me and my friend got the banana cream pie, and the key lime pie. I love how tart the pies were -- the banana cream was so layered, made with actual banana and it was topped with another layer of cream and chocolate covering. All in all, $7 a slice for a piece of pie is not bad at all, especially if they were made by food artisans who knew their craft.

Ambiance is rather good, and not underwhelming at all. This place IS worth the hype forsure xD

I'm definitely recommending Bakesale Betty to any and all friends who want to try this :)) till we meet again!!

I don't get the hype. I've bought the chicken sandwich twice now and it's nothing special other than it's kind of big. Also why is the counter always out on the sidewalk? Everyone should take a breath and walk down to OK's Deli for their delicious sandwiches aha... Sorry guys I tried to enjoy yours - you can do better!

Bake sale Betty…… Mmmm Mmmmm DELICIOUS!  this place gets packed and busy and the operation time is limited, so if you go there, it may have a long line, but they will get the orders in and out real quick. top_reviews.content:
This restaurant has a different interpretation on Vietnamese food. Some people raves about it and others complain.

There’s different menus for lunch and dinner. Lunch has Pho, chicken wings, spring rolls etc.  Dinner menu omits all that’s offered at lunch, and offers more sophisticated dishes.

Tried the special of the day and it was not great. Angel hair pasta fried with seafood and topped with crab meat. It was too dry to eat!!

Service was ok. Atmosphere is ok… nothing outstanding. Food was lukewarm.

Bodega SF had been on our list for a while, especially after seeing it ranked in The Infatuation’s top 20 restaurants in San Francisco, so we were excited to finally try it. We made a reservation for a Wednesday night and were seated quickly upon arrival, while there was a noticeable line for walk ins.
The space has a trendy, lively atmosphere that sets the tone for a fun dining experience. We ordered a variety of dishes: steamed rice rolls, tiger prawns, stir fried pho noodles, mushrooms with quail eggs, and crab fat fried rice.

There were definitely some highlights. The tiger prawns and mushrooms with quail eggs were standouts, and I especially loved the stir fried pho noodles since they felt unique and creative compared to typical noodle dishes. However, not everything landed. My sister and mom found the filling in the steamed rice rolls to be a bit dry, and the crab fat fried rice did not quite work for us as a combination of flavors.

Service was the main downside of the evening. Although the restaurant was busy, our waiter passed by our table multiple times without stopping to take our order, and our food took over 20 minutes to arrive.
Overall, Bodega SF offers a stylish setting and some memorable dishes, but the experience was mixed due to inconsistent execution and service.

I haven't been able to find any Vietnamese food that i like in the city and have had my eye on this spot for a while so i booked a reservation on a weeknight for dinner to treat my sister! It really scratched the itch for the homesickness of my mom or grandma's homecooked viet food but make it a little upscale but still approachable and comforting.  I really appreciated the family style menu. Jeremy was our server and was very knowledgeable, kind, and attentive. They really hit all the marks. I could eat like forty of the banh khots. The Bo luc lac was the star of the show for my sister and is definitely a must try but the off-menu razor clams were my personal favorite! We also loved the crab fat fried rice, matcha crepe cake and hochija pannacotta! We will definitely be back.

Came on a weekday and tried out the chef's tasting menu. It was surprisingly filling. I hardly could finish the last of the entree, completely stuffed. We enjoyed the varieties of Vietnamese cuisine within the selection. A tad too similar in taste with the overuse of fish sauce in all their dressing and sauces. Vietnamese cuisine has other sauces, but they might be too pungent for the western palate.

I’m so glad we tried this spot. It is a unique and I would say elevated take on classic Vietnamese food. We had the Shaking Beef and Chimichurri Banh Mi. The spices and flavors of the Shaking Beef was really good however it did leans slightly salty. The Banh Mi came with a beef pho broth dipping sauce. This was a delicious combo and the beef broth itself was super flavorful.

top_reviews.content: Arrived about 3:10pm, after lunch before dinner service, not a full menu available. I tried their pastrami sandwich which was really tasty and fries. Everything was good. Nothing blew my socks off though. Will be back to try dinner. Make your reservations ahead of time, the place is small, I thought it would be bigger. Some paid parking available along the street.

Food is 5 stars for flavors and presentation and the cocktails are quite tasty too. We had the potato fennel soup and Brussel sprouts to start. The soup had a surprising  kick and the sprouts had bite from the apple and acv that made them totally pop.

One of our entrees was the pork chop with seasonal veggies, a grilled peach and sausage bites. Each component on its own was a burst of flavor but when you put them all together it was a true flavor explosion. This sausage bits we amazing!

Our other entree was the half chicken with roasted potatoes, which also had great flavor and again when the components were eaten in one bite, the combination was fantastic. The sauces on both dishes did their job and brought the dishes together too.

For desert, we chose the profiteroles with seasonal fruit and ice cream and that was a great way to end the meal.

We may have caught them on an off night, but service was a bit slower than we prefer - was just over an hour from being seated to main course, but the food was worth the wait.

It was a clean restaurant too, but could use some sound baffling to make conversation a bit easier. We were seated in the center of the room and found it a bit noisy.

We will definitely be back again!

We got to the Oakland restaurant right before they opened for lunch and were greeted warmly by the staff. They gave us our choice of a table right by the window or a spot further inside the dining room. We picked the window, which turned out to be an awesome people-watching node while we looked over the lunch menu.

Our waiter was incredibly friendly and helpful. We ordered the pastrami sandwich and the hot pork sandwich, telling him we planned on splitting them. When we asked if they came with fries, he mentioned they usually come with coleslaw, but he kindly let us swap out one of the slaws so we could try the french fries too. A short time later, the kitchen went completely above and beyond—they brought our food out pre-split on four separate plates. Getting a perfect half-sandwich, fries, and slaw delivered right to each of us without us having to messily cut them at the table was a really kind, thoughtful touch of hospitality.

Starting with the sides, the fries came out piping hot, perfectly crisp, and well-seasoned. They tasted great with just standard ketchup.

As for the best pastrami sandwich in the East Bay contender? It completely delivered. The meat itself was deeply savory, perfectly cured, and piled high on a phenomenal, crusty baguette from La Farine bakery. The Dijon-horseradish dressing gave it a great, sharp kick that cut through the richness. It’s an absolute triumph and entirely worth the trip.

The hot pork sandwich, however, hit a weird bump (3/5 stars for this one). As I picked up my half, the first thing I noticed wasn't the sharp, bitter scent of broccoli rabe, but a strong smell of cooked spinach. When I took a bite, an overpowering spinach flavor totally took over the palate, completely masking the taste of the pork. My partner noticed the exact same thing. I opened up the baguette to check it out, and while there were a few actual pieces of broccoli rabe, the main culprit was a dark green, long, stringy mass. I ended up scraping most of it off. When I isolated the pulled pork by itself, it was actually delicious, tender, and beautifully seasoned, and the bread was excellent. But with that heavy cooked spinach smell and taste, I just can’t recommend the pork sandwich in its current state. It completely ruined the sandwich for me.

Overall, between the flawless service, and the great tavern atmosphere, Wood Tavern is easily one of the top places for a pastrami sandwich in Oakland.

Probably the best New American restaurant in the East Bay. Their steak never misses—perfectly cooked, delicious, and big portions. Rotating dinner menu (except steak and pork chops) and even the veggies included differ depending on what they have available. The scallops and risotto are always so good when it’s on the menu. Bonus: complimentary bread and butter.

It’s always packed and busy, even on weekdays. It’s been a local staple in the piedmont area. And it’s really the only new American restaurant that I find myself revisiting!

Wow, I didn't know this place was scheduled to close on December 31, 2026. I can remember eating here when they had a soft opening  years ago. Today I had a terrific lunch with a friend. Do try the charcuterie, so many yummy choices of cheese. Definitely add the duck, It was fantastic. Any of the sandage choices are great. The  seafood stew was superb. For dessert, we had the two scoops of ice cream/ gelato. I'm definitely going to try to squeeze in two more visits before they close. Definitely worth adding to your list if you've not been here.

top_reviews.content:
July 15, 2026

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

There are pizza nights, and then there are nights where the pizza gods themselves look down from the heavens, nod approvingly, and whisper, “Yeah… that’s the order.”

Today was one of those days.

I rolled in and ordered a 16-inch pepperoni pizza, two sides of ranch, and a pint of whatever magical liquid everyone else seems to order when they know more than I do. Sometimes the best strategy in life is trusting the professionals, and this establishment did not disappoint.

From the moment I walked in, the service was phenomenal.

The staff was friendly, welcoming, and genuinely happy to help. No attitude. No rushing. No feeling like you’re just another transaction. Just good people providing great service with the kind of effortless professionalism that makes everything feel easy.

And then the food arrived.

Let’s talk about that pizza.

Absolute top-tier.

The kind of pizza that makes you take a bite, pause for a second, and immediately start calculating how many slices you’re willing to share versus how many you’re secretly planning to protect with your life.

The pepperoni was on point.

The crust was exactly where it needed to be.

The cheese delivered that perfect combination of flavor, texture, and happiness that only great pizza can provide.

And the ranch?

Let’s just say there are dipping sauces, and then there are lifestyle choices. Those two sides of ranch were not merely condiments. They were valued members of the team.

Every bite felt like the kitchen genuinely cared about what they were sending out. There is a difference between food being made and food being crafted, and you can taste that difference immediately.

What impressed me most was how seamlessly everything came together.

Great food.

Great service.

Great atmosphere.

No drama.

No problems.

No complaints.

Just an experience that reminded me why people keep coming back.

In a world where excellence often gets overlooked, it’s worth recognizing places that consistently get it right. The team here clearly takes pride in what they do, and it shows in every interaction and every bite.

I arrived hungry.

I left happy.

And somewhere between slice number one and “I’ll save the rest for later” (a promise I absolutely did not keep), this place earned a loyal customer.

If you’re debating whether to stop by, stop debating.

Order the pizza.

Get the ranch.

Trust the process.

Your future self will thank you.

Five stars all day long. 🍕🏆

Love Philomena! The mushroom pizza and Miss piggy are delicious! But if you love pesto… there are some yum options, too.
I always keep a bottle of Phil ranch in the fridge and use it at home for all sorts of things.
Okay… and then there is the meat lasagna. I swear a little old grandma made that sauce. With cheese, garlicky toasty bread.
I usually want to eat the whole thing but try and put half in a box right away so I can savor it for lunch the next day.
They have great ice creams and gelatos with rotating flavors.
Tricia night every other Tuesday is a hit and so fun. I work as a teacher and we enjoy getting a group together every so often. It’s a great hang!

Philomena's is an absolute gem that delivers on every front!
The pizza, top tier, hands down! I ordered the Mushroom Pizza. It has persillade sauce and green onions. I added the Italian sausage, so good. Some of the best pizza ever!

Special shoutout to Rico and Kyle—these two are best in show! Their energy, kindness, and attention completely elevated the experience. It’s rare to encounter such genuine hospitality, and they made sure everything was spot-on from start to finish.

Whether you're there for the pizza, craft beer or just the atmosphere, you'll leave with a full belly and an even fuller spirit. Perfect therapeutic escape after a taxing day. Highly recommend!

Whether you just want easy takeout or a good hang with friendly locals, this is the spot. A super diverse menu for a pizza place, with seasonal veg dishes and some great desserts too. The pizza is SO good, and the wings are a go-to. Super neighborhoody vibe with exceptionally friendly staff, a superb beer selection that is constantly rotating and fresh, and excellent salads.

Plus sports! Catch a random weeknight Dubs game or spend the better part of a Sunday watching NFL and noshing on pizza and beer.

This isn't your chain pizza joint; it's a legit original, and you can tell the moment you walk in.

I normally don't leave bad reviews. So the fact that I'm bothering with this should go to stress how awful this pizza was.

A simple margherita. Shouldn't be hard to get it right, no? No char on the underside. No gluten development, crust is completely deflated. Mozzarella is overcooked and rubbery. Tomato sauce was flavorless. My partner had their mushroom pizza and it was just as bad. Both pizzas went into the trash before the third slice.

If this pizza wasn't cooked from frozen, I would be genuinely shocked. I guess that's why you're not allowed to modify the "house pizzas".

As some other reviewers pointed out, this seems to be a consistent problem with their delivery as opposed to their dine in. Which wouldn't be anywhere near as offensive if it wasn't for how overpriced the Pizza is for the quality. Imagine paying $42 for what might as well be a $10 Digiorno.

top_reviews.content: Food was quick in a busy night. Everything was delicious and the wait staff was on point. I had the spicy pork bbq and it’s totally worth it! The projector above was playing very funny k pop videos. If you are in the area late night, you should swing by.

Great spot if looking for dinner late, everything was fresh, quickly served and reasonably priced. Good intimate vibe for groups and good service. Everything had a good taste but my favorite was definitely spicy chicken with cheese, bibimbap and the corn cheese

If you’re a Korean restaurant that cannot tell the difference between gyeranjjim and gyeranmari, between galbitang and ttarogukbap, then chances are you are catering to clueless K-Pop fans.
Food taste: The guk in the yukkejang and the ttarogukbap tasted the same and worse, suspiciously like it was made with ramen soup bases. Btw, the manager sent the waiter who had made a mistake (they brought galbitang instead of the ttarogukba we ordered) to suggest to us that they would spice up the galbitang to make it ttarogukbap...!!! That seems consistent with stuff tasting the same.
How do you like your eggs: We asked if they had steamed egg because this is a standard item (and because it was not listed in the menu). The waiter said they did and pointed to an item listed as “a big omelette”. I  wondered and they insisted . And then they plunked a dish of gyeran mari on the table. Oookay. But if I want my gyeran jjim that has been converted to a gyeran mari smothered in ketchup and cheese, then I will find my way to a proper Japanese joint. Leftovers - no thanks.
Banchan: Please check the banchan before you hit up a Korean restaurant. If you see measly excuses for banchan, the food cannot be far behind. We lowered our expectations after the banchan came out. That is not kimchi. It’s not about the kimchi being old or sour (although Korean restaurants worth their salt, especially in big cities will get you fresh kimchi) - this was watery and looked like it has been washed. If you are not getting a basic like kimchi right, then…But seriously, this is just an insult to Korean cuisine.The quantities are also consistent with how the managers are cuttings corners to cut cost - three kinds with a tablespoon each.
Ambience: The worst thing in the place is the noise level. You will sit cheek to jowl with what, after about 3 minutes, will feel like a bunch of howler monkeys on market day!  It felt great to conclude the meal in more ways than one.
Conclusion: We made a valiant effort with the food. A successful meal is when the rice and guk disappear.  Clearly not in this case. No worries Zzan, you do you and the K-Pop teeny boppers will go home feeling like they have scored authentic Korean food. But if you care and want to call yourself Korean, at least get your kimchi right. How hard would that be?

We have visited numerous Korean restaurants along the West Coast, including those in Hawaii. However, this was the first time we were disappointed by the food at a Korean restaurant. We ordered the SF special, cold noodles in kimchi broth, SF seafood soup in tang, and a deep fried noodle in seaweed. The cold noodles has the cube ice not shaved, the soup was bland and seemed like it was just water, and the seafood soup had little flavor. giving 2 rating  since the fried noodle was good!

The food was good, which is why we decided to come back a second night.

Last night, the service wasn’t great, but we decided to give the restaurant another chance because we really enjoyed the food. Unfortunately, tonight’s experience was even worse.

Halfway through eating my ramen, I found a strand of hair tangled in my noodles. I showed it to one of the staff members, he showed it to the lady. And the lady came and  took my bowl away. Naturally, I assumed they were making me a new one, so I waited.

After quite a while, I had to ask what was happening. That’s when I was told they had simply removed the ramen from my bill because the kitchen had already closed and couldn’t make another bowl.

I completely understand that the kitchen was closed. I wasn’t expecting the impossible. What disappointed me was that no one communicated this to me when they took my bowl away, and the lady did not even apologised. I was left sitting there hungry, waiting for food that was never coming.

I’m not someone who usually leaves negative reviews. I work in the food service industry myself, so I understand that mistakes happen. Finding a hair in food can happen anywhere. What matters is how the situation is handled, and unfortunately, this was handled very poorly.

The male staff member was polite, but the female staff member/ boss came across as dismissive and unfriendly throughout our visit, which made the experience even more unpleasant.

The food is 7/10 , but good food alone doesn’t make up for poor customer service. I hope the restaurant takes customer communication more seriously in the future. Please. 🙏🏻

top_reviews.content:
Good to know: No condiments on the tables (no chili, no ketchup) — first time I've experienced that at a place like this. They do give you a complimentary platter of shrimp chips though.

Came on a Friday night shortly after they opened — practically empty the whole meal. Staff was very friendly.

What we got:
- Large Tom Yum soup — excellent, a bit sour but I loved it
- Charcoal-grilled Hanger steak — great
- Coconut red curry braised short ribs — decent
- Khao Soi — too coconut-heavy for me, though my husband loved it
- Thai Fries with panang curry short ribs (HH menu) — disappointing, just regular fries with no ketchup available

The Tom Yum and hanger steak were the standouts. The short rib dishes and fries didn't do much for me. Might return for the soup alone.

Food was great. Highly recommend the crispy rice salad. We also got the basil chicken which I didn’t take a picture for, but it was amazing. The chicken was ground, which made the dish much better than it typically is in my opinion. They also poured generous wine pours at the bar.

Honestly, such a solid spot. The chicken spring rolls were the highlight—they have this super interesting, extra-crispy outer layer that’s way better than your average spring roll. Plus, the dipping sauce is literally to die for (perfectly sweet, hot, and sour). The tom kha was also super yummy.
We asked to sub pork for ground chicken in the spicy fried rice, but there was a little mix-up and it came out with pork at first. Honestly, they were so nice about it—super apologetic, swapped it out for the chicken right away, and even gave us free Thai teas for the trouble.
Great food and even better service. Definitely worth checking out!

Such a great vibe with good music and even better service! We had the pad kee mao, but the real standouts were the grilled pork skewers and the charcoal-grilled hanger steak. If you love meat, do not skip these. Already planning my next trip back!

I dream of this place. Best Thai food. Best drinks. Best bang for your buck. I typically come for lunch, and order drinks (happy hour lunch 11:30-2:30) and get the Ginger Drop or the Lychee cocktail. The soups are super flavorful I like they have a slightly smaller portion for one person reasonably priced! They can accommodate large groups or party of 1 like myself. Staff super friendly. My favorite place in SF right now.

top_reviews.content: Five stars. My son and I had the Omakase experience at Akiko's in San Francisco, and it was hands down the best sushi we've ever had. Every course was beautifully presented, incredibly fresh, and packed with flavors that exceeded our expectations. The chefs' attention to detail and craftsmanship were evident in every bite. The service was equally outstanding, warm, attentive, and perfectly paced from start to finish. The entire evening felt like a true culinary experience rather than just dinner. If you're looking for an unforgettable Omakase in San Francisco, Akiko's is absolutely worth it. Five stars. We can't wait to come back.

One of the most overpriced omakase places we’ve tried. The starting courses were okay but the nigiri lacked creativity and flavor(over sauced, sushi rice was plain, and when we asked for a little more wasabi the chef put too much to the point where we teared up). Also the chef never tried to make conversation with us, just told us the piece of fish which we could’ve just read off the menu, and she had an annoyed face the whole meal. The only dishes that stood out was the tuna and caviar over milk bread and the scallop dish. At $270 per person and we ordered 4 cocktails between my wife and I we spent over $800 total and we left hungry.

Akiko’s Restaurant is a solid omakase spot that I’ve visited twice—once at the bar and once seated at a table—and the experience does vary depending on where you sit.

The bar seating clearly stands out. Portions felt more generous, and the personal interaction with the chef made a noticeable difference. Watching each nigiri being prepared and served directly to you adds warmth and intention that elevates the meal. The table seating is more comfortable, especially for a longer dinner, but the experience feels slightly less engaging.

Some of the nigiri were truly outstanding. The coffee-cured bluefin and the chocolate-cured ocean trout were both memorable and creative without being gimmicky. The toro tuna belly was also excellent—rich, clean, and perfectly balanced.

Same-day reservations were possible on both visits, which is a big plus for an omakase of this caliber in San Francisco. Overall, Akiko’s offers high-quality sushi and a reliable experience, with the bar seating being the way to go if you want the best version of the omakase.

We had such a great experience, from the moment we walked in to when we left. We were greeted warmly when we entered, and the hostess acknowledged the special occasion we were celebrating, which was such a nice touch. We were seated exactly where we had requested, had our coats checked, and sat down at the bar where our menus were already waiting. The menu even included a note recognizing our celebration, which really made us feel welcomed.

The set omakase was excellent. We loved it all but particularly enjoyed their signature dish,and the coffee cured nigiri as well as the chocolate one. Every course was beautifully presented and tasted amazing. Our meal was well paced. The staff were friendly, knowledgeable, and easy to talk to. We also added a few pieces from the regular menu and those were just as good. The ice cream dessert was the perfect end to the meal.

What stood out as well was the service. The staff were attentive without hovering and clearly very experienced. It felt relaxed, polished, and genuinely welcoming.

Highly recommend Akiko’s if you are looking for incredible sushi and thoughtful service.

We did the Valentine’s Day set menu. The first half was a mix of different fish dishes and two of the 6 items were great. The others I could have done without. Then we had 6 different nigiris and all were amazing.

top_reviews.content:

We ordered quite a few dishes and started with Omakase gushi, which came with chicken breast, thigh with leek, heart, cartilage, and minced chicken.  We also ordered the oden set, sasami, tori tataki, gyu-tan, enoki bacon, and buta bara.

It was my first time trying raw chicken, and it tasted really good. The chicken breast was really tender, with a tuna-like texture, and without any slimy or odd flavors. Ever since then, I've been telling my friends to try it. The Tori Tataki was seared chicken breast sashimi with ponzu, which tasted a bit plain compared to the sasami. So  I would highly recommended to get theeir sasami!
Wow!!! i loved this place - great food, great atmosphere- about as japanese as you can get outside of japan - wish i lived closer so i could eat here all the time!! seriously worth going to.

Ippuku (一服), which means to take a short break for a cigarette or tea during a busy day (literally meaning “one dose”), had a very nice vibe walking in. The entrance was unassuming, but the interior transported me back to Japan. They had seating areas which simulated traditional seating on zabutons and tatami maps, and also more western style sitting areas. You can immediately tell they take pride in Japanese tradition without becoming pretentious or trying too hard to be "unique".

They gave a complimentary chunk of cabbage with kewpie mayo topped with togarashi. While pretty difficult to eat since it is just a large chunk of cabbage, it was a very nice palate cleanser throughout the whole meal. We ordered four skewers: Gyutan (beef tongue), Kurobutabara (pork belly), Negima (thigh with leek), and Kawa (skin). Additionally, we got the Ikasumi chahan (squid ink fried rice) and Kani korokke (dungeness crab creme croquettes).

The squid ink fried rice, while pretty good, was the biggest disappointment. It tasted like a standard rice that can be made at home, but colored with squid ink. The squid ink felt more like a gimmick that made my tongue and lips black after eating a few bites. The crab croquettes were very solid, a nice structural integrity and creaminess one bitten in. The crab slivers were noticeable and added a nice sweetness and crabby flavor overall. The sliced cabbage under them was a good palate cleanser too.

The skewers, specifically the yakitori, was their advertised specialty. Starting with the beef tongue, it was slightly thick, but cooked perfectly. It had a nice bite whilst not being too chewy, and the charred jalapeños provided a good spice that broke up the pieces of meat. It was also seasoned nicely, without need for a sauce. The chicken skin was my least favorite of the skewers. While the outside had a good crunch, which I love in chicken skin, the inside became very soggy and chewy. I would have preferred them to not be in skewer form, and to just be fried as whole skin pieces. The chicken thigh was very impressive. With a thin coating of sauce, the chicken was succulent and juicy, very flavorful, and the leeks provided a nice textural contrast as well as a freshness. This was a very impressive skewer that I would definitely get again. The pork belly was my favorite bite of the night. It was both juicy and had nicely rendered fat. It was a very meaty taste, accentuated by the simple seasoning of just salt and letting the charcoal flavor come through. The sauce they served with it was also really unique, a mix of miso paste and doubanjiang, giving a slightly fruity note and a perfect accompaniment to the pork belly.  The server also gave complimentary matcha ice cream, which was really good too. The matcha flavor was deep and was a creamy ice cream.

Overall, it was an obvious upgrade to the last izakaya, and no dish was bad. While only a few items truly wowed me, I enjoyed how they stuck to tradition to provide an unpretentious experience that reminded me of Japan. While pricey, this is a place I could recommend to others who want to try a very solid izakaya.

Appreciated the small dishes for variety, but quality differed between dishes and I also found many of them lacked flavor.

My favorite dishes were the negima (thigh with leek), the shisho making, and the goma yogoshi (spinach in sesame paste) for their more unique tastes. I wouldn't recommend the Nama-Yuba nor the mochi wrapped in bacon or nori.

Service is good with the plates coming out in intervals to accentuate the dining experience.

Would recommend making reservations since the restaurant gets packed quite easily.

top_reviews.content: Super busy izakaya but they somehow make each dish super flavorful and well balanced. The prices are on the high end for the amount you get but the quality is unmatched. Hidden gem with soul - this is where Japanese food feels right.
Every dish at Kiraku is crafted with care, precision, and that rare sense of warmth that’s hard to find outside Japan. But what truly sets this place apart isn’t just the taste - it’s the consistency. Year after year, the quality doesn’t fade. It actually improves.

The staff? Always kind. Always attentive. The atmosphere? Casual but cozy, like your favorite local spot back home.

If you’re new to the Bay Area or just hunting for a place that gets Japanese food right, start here. Kiraku isn’t just a restaurant. It’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back before you’ve even left.

This is honestly my favorite spot in the entire SF/Bay Area — no competition, no close second. I mean it. Nothing else compares.

I first came here around 2022 and was absolutely blown away. I live far, but this is still a place I’ll happily drive an hour for, wait 40+ minutes for, and revisit 10+ times without hesitation. Zero complaints. Always worth it.

The space isn’t big, but the sticker-covered walls and posters give it so much personality. It feels like a place that’s been loved and thoughtfully run for years — a true neighborhood gem with soul.

✨ My forever must-orders (these NEVER miss):

• Ankimo mousse + sweet potato chips — this combo is unreal
• Roasted beef tongue with truffle oil — insanely tender and bouncy; WAY better than the tongue skewers (not even the same level)
• Wagyu tataki — rich, buttery, milky wagyu flavor… I sometimes order two
• A5 ribeye nigiri — just WOW. If you love wagyu, you CANNOT skip this

These feel like permanent-menu-level safe choices. I’ve ordered them countless times and the quality is always consistent.

⸻

🌿 Other favorites from past visits

Corn tempura, miso black cod, and tuna 3 ways are also great picks.

⸻

🆕 New dishes we tried this time

• Hamachi carpaccio salad — light and refreshing, great palate reset
• Yuzu chicken udon — comforting, and the hint of yuzu is genius. So satisfying.

Grilled rice ball was just okay for me, but my boyfriend loved it.
Sweet potato brûlée for dessert was creamy and not overly sweet — so good.

⸻

💛 Service

Always lovely. Angelina especially is such a sweetheart. Every time we come, she always has the warmest smile and is so attentive, just adorable energy.

⚠️ Reality check

This place is VERY popular. Expect a 30–60 min wait, even on weekdays.

💡 Best tip: come right at 5:30pm opening or join the Yelp waitlist in advance.

Writing this review makes me sad thinking about the day I leave the Bay Area and can’t come back here anymore.

Kiraku is absolutely a must-try in the Bay Area. Come experience it yourself — you won’t regret it!

Absolute meet cute with a cozy vibe. Came here for a late night snack at 10pm.

They have a little table out front to check in, but as I was a walking they came to get me and seated promptly.

Whole place sits maybe thirty people tops thirty five

They have a tapas style menu of small plates which is nice if you want to mix and match.

I got the toasted green tea, clam miso soup, garlic edamame, and a skewer each of the eel and lamb.

The green tea wasn’t piping hot but warm. Tasted… toasty. Didn’t think I’d like it but three cups in it grew on me. Give it a chance.

Garlic edamame was excellent. Had a coating of anchovy bits that made it unique and had me snacking my lips. Will order this everytime.

They said that the miso soup usually comes at the end, after the other courses. When asked for a preference, I deferred to them. They thought it right away.

The soup had about five clams which imparted a salty brine depth that eclipsed the expected umami of the miso. I’m not mad. Tastes great. But I do like my miso on the lighter side. Worth trying to see if it’s for you.

Lamb skewer was well seasoned and light. It’s rare to find lamb in Japanese restaurants so I make it a point to order it. Had bits of scallions grilled with it, came with a dollop of mustard. Delicious.

The eel skewer was my absolute favorite. Soft and buttery, partitions on its own and melts in your mouth. Seasoning was strong but adequate. Cane with some wasabi. Avoid the wasabi for this one. You don’t need it, as it distracts from the unagi’s natural qualities.

They had a dessert menu, but I passed on it

The restaurant’s dark wood walls are sprinkled with vintage Japanese beer ads.

The staff are attentive and very sweet. When I came in, they asked if it was my first time here and walked me through the menu. Then they proceeded to give me a warm towel as I was coming in from the rain. An absolute vibe.

As I understand, the name Daimo stems from the Cantonese term "day mouw ( floor squat)" which is short for "day mouw goohn"...an impromptu,likely illegal,  food stand without chairs or tables where you practically have to squat to eat your food. Remembered fondly by some, these places were known for good food at cheap prices.

Daimo in Richmond is a far departure from those "day mouws" in China but is nonetheless a solid choice for those looking for traditional Chinese fare.

Their go-to dishes include their beef chow fuhn, beef stew over rice, and other assorted rice plates. Prices are moderate, but for certain items, portions are quite large.
In fact, they're well known for their large portions. People seem to come from far away to take advantage of this.

Service is good, and the waitresses are friendly and  helpful. The restaurant has a lot of windows and they give the place a bright airy feel.

If you're in the area and looking for Chinese food, give Daimo a try. The food is good, traditional and you certainly won't leave hungry.

Its a little retro 90s inside, but its spacious, my table was clean, they offered a complimentary hot tea & hot oil on the table for the food.

I ordered a lunch special for $15.95, I asked for her reccomendation - she suggested the beef Xo. This came with a beverage (I chose a can of coke) & a small soup (sweet & sour). The beef xo also had a side of white rice on the plate as well - which turned out great, because although the Xo is yummy, it is quite rich and salty, the white rice cuts that richness very well. The portion was also ample for a lunch serving. I say it is for sure worth it! The beef was super tender and flavorful as well. I really didnt care for the Celery in this dish though. Next time I'd ask them to leave it out, its really nothing but a filler & not a good one at that. The snow peas were a nice addition though.

I also ordered Beef & Chive chow fun i believe it was $17.95. This is a HUGE portion, so while $17.95 sounds high to me, this can easily fill 3 people with just the chow fun alone! This price is super reasonable. As far as taste of the chow fun - the beef was great and tender, I just wish the noodles were thicker and fatter. These arent typically the kind of noodles I envision when I think chow fun... this is probably closer to a thai pad see ewe noodle, still good! But i was really wanting a fatter wider noodle. The sauce was perfect - maybe id have liked it to be a little wetter even, but the flavor was good.

For appetizers i ordered a
- BBQ pork rice roll $7 8pc (my favorite thing out of everything!)
- Shrimp & Chive Dumplings 3pc (my least favorite of everything)
- Turnip cake $6 3pc (this was interesting - texturally like a mix between fake mashed potatoes & gelatin.. I didnt hate it. The seared parts were super yummy)

The shrimp & Chive Dumplings was a bit dry. Bland & a little over burnt on the seared outside. It also didnt come with any sauce. Id never order it again

The BBQ rice roll was texturally pleasant to me - with the super soft rice roll & the addition of the BBQ pork added texture + it was laying in a sort of ponzu or soju sauce which was also yummy.

Overall I'd rate everything a 4 out of 5. The service was great. The ladies were super friendly and wiling to make suggestions. They even packed my to go leftovers them selves, & didnt charge me for my extra coke... which may or may not have been intentional - either way I added what that cost would have been to their tip so it works out.

Id definitely be back!

I’ll be back!

top_reviews.content:
This place is super easy to miss in the daytime since it's set back from the street, but it's worth finding. You walk into a long bar with restaurant seating for maybe 20-30 people--very chill, laid-back vibe.

There was one guy running the whole show--bartender, server, runner, everything--and he held it down. You order and pay (a little pricey, gratuity included also) from a QR code at the table, then he brings your food out.

I got the tonkotsu with pork belly and it hit the spot. The broth was silky and full of flavor, hearty, and satisfying.

After we finished, they surprised us with some homemade strawberry ice cream, which was such a nice little touch.

Overall, just a really comfortable, no-frills neighborhood spot. I'll definitely be back.

Torraku was a comfortable, casual ramen spot with hearty options as well as vegetarian choices. We started with the chicken karaage, which was fried perfectly, along with a shareable bottle of sake.

I was excited to find a shoyu-based ramen in SF, as it’s not something I’ve come across as often. We also tried the miso-based vegetarian ramen and the classic tonkotsu ramen. The toppings were classic and well-executed, including nori, bamboo shoots, and pork belly. We were also given complimentary pecan ice cream at the end, which was a nice way to finish the meal.

Overall, the ramen was good and the service was quick and kind, though I’m not sure I’d go out of my way to eat here. If you’re in the area and craving a good bowl of ramen, I’d recommend giving Torraku a try, especially for the variety and friendly service.

The chicken karaage was perfectly crispy and juicy, but adding the lime and spicy sauce really took it to a whole new level! 🍗🔥
As for the ramen, the Super Paitan was incredibly well-balanced and just amazing—exactly what you need for a comforting, soul-warming meal. While the miso was also great, it just couldn't top the Paitan for me. Highly recommend!"
------------------------------
Quick Flavor Breakdown:

* Paitan Ramen: Known for its rich, creamy, and opaque broth (often chicken-based), offering a deeply savory "umami" profile that stays smooth and balanced.
* Miso Ramen: Typically features a bolder, heartier taste due to the fermented soybean paste, which can sometimes be more assertive than the silky Paitan.

The food is 4.5 , I would make it 5 after trying few more times for consistency across food n flavors

Chicken karaage was good, chrispy on the outside and tender on the inside.

Food is awesome! Great ramen and very tasty! We are just thankful so much to the Indonesian Server who was very patient with us from dropping our chopsticks to spilling glass of water. That man deserves a raise. Kudos. Recommended for Ramen

top_reviews.content:
There's a good Korean food restaurant in the area?! I was incredibly excited to try this place and happy to do so! Was shocked that this place so busy and many diners seemed to be new to Korean food.

Banchan side dishes were a good set of classic dishes.

The place was very busy with a lot of takeout orders. There were only 2 waitstaff in front and they were quite overwhelmed.

No patron bathroom inside this space; you'll have to borrow a key to go around the building. I decided to go home instead of waiting for the key.

Absolutely amazing. ❤️
This place was first recommended by a Korean friend, and it’s now easily the restaurant we’ve visited the most in the entire Bay Area. When we lived in Berkeley, we came at least every other weekend—and even now, we still happily drive for it. We’ve been here 20+ times.

I’ve brought many friends here, and every single one wants to come back. It always comes up whenever we talk about fried chicken.

The food:
•	Fried chicken — heavenly
•	Tofu soup — rich, comforting, and deeply delicious
•	Kimchi pancake & seafood pancake — both excellent
•	Banchan (Korean appetizers) — so good we often pack them to go

The food is comforting, addictive, and consistently outstanding. We clean our plates, scrape every last bite, and take leftovers whenever possible.

The service:
Warm and attentive, even when the place is packed and everyone is clearly working hard. It genuinely feels like eating at an auntie’s place—welcoming, caring, and full of heart.

We will absolutely be back again and again and again.

(Attached: photos over the years, the quality never changes)

Delicious food and incredibly friendly staff! I lived in Los Angeles for the past two years, just outside Koreatown, so I wasn’t sure I’d find Korean food in the Bay that could compare. I was pleasantly surprised—everything was authentic and absolutely delicious. I’m so happy I found this place, and it’s definitely going to be my go-to spot for Korean food from now on.

One of the best Korean restaurants this side of town.  Place can get packed so there will definitely be waiting time. Food is always consistent and delicious.  Prices can be expensive for what you pay for but if you want an excellent tofu or rice cake soup, this place is it.

The server is really friendly and helpful.  Food ordered and served hot and quickly.  We love their side dishes.  The beef and seafood combo was great.  The seafood pancake was really good.  We also had corn cheese.  It was a lot for just 2 of us.  We love their food and services.  We will return again.

I recently made the trip to Maya Halal Taqueria, and I can honestly say it was well worth it.
This is not a fancy restaurant with a prime location, a large dining area, or abundant parking. In fact, seating appears to be limited, and parking can require a little patience. But sometimes the best food is found in the most unexpected places, and Maya is a perfect example of that.
The food is exceptional. Everything tastes fresh, flavorful, and prepared with care. Finding high-quality Mexican food that is also halal is not always easy, but Maya has managed to create a menu that delivers both authenticity and quality. Every bite reflects attention to ingredients and consistency.
What impressed me just as much as the food was the warmth of the service. The staff are welcoming, friendly, and genuinely appreciative of their customers. That kind of hospitality makes a lasting impression.
Living in Fremont, I would not normally drive 25 to 35 minutes for a meal unless it was truly special. Maya Halal Taqueria is one of those rare places that makes the drive worthwhile.
If you're looking for excellent halal Mexican food, generous portions, and friendly service, I highly recommend giving this hidden gem a try. It may not have all the conveniences of a large restaurant, but what it does have is something far more important: outstanding food and people who care about what they serve.

top_reviews.content:
This is a tiny but fun little pizza spot with a cozy, laid back vibe. The entrance is surprisingly easy to miss even when following the map, which almost makes the name feel fitting because it really is "out of sight" in the most literal way.

They offer a good variety of pizza slices and have a few small tables if you're lucky enough to grab one. Otherwise, it's a great place to pick up a slice and enjoy it elsewhere.

We tried the chicken pesto pizza, and it was excellent. The crust was thin and had that classic New York style texture that I really enjoy. It was also very reasonably priced, making it an easy recommendation if you're looking for a quick and satisfying slice in San Francisco.

Good pizza but could be better.

I have been searching for a slice in SF that is both normally priced and can be held up from the crust. I found that here on my second visit. The cheese slice ($4.50) had cheese and sauce all the way to the crust and was pretty good except for the burnt parts. I understand charring but they went a little too far with my slice. Little carcinogenic charcoal bits were chipping off. But I peeled off the parts that were too burnt and the resulting slice was pretty good. The flavorful cheese balanced well with the sauce. There wasn't too much of one thing. I'd return again if I'm in the area and in the mood for pizza, but I'd ask to not go too far heating the slice up.

The interior is beautifully decorated with cartoony art on one wall and an assortment of items on another wall. Each table has paper towels, red pepper, and parmesan.

There are no words to describe the epic highs and lows of eating a pizza from here, i got myself the hot burrata and when i say the inside of my jeans will never be the same i mean it. The grief you experience coming to the last bites of each slice is akin to that of losing a loved one, the price of each slice is well worth the explosion of love and ingredients on your tongue, hospitality is great. Do yourself a favor and get yourself a slice. Water this plant, cause it should never ever wilt holy great freaking pizza!!

Got a very NY style pizza vibe! Love all the pizza slices we took from here for a picnic in the park. We had the ruby, buffalo chicken and Alfredo chicken and plain cheese for kiddo. The crust was good and sauces toppings everything was good. It is perfect for a quick to go meal. Stayed well and tasty even after travelling for 20-30 mins.

Definitely the best pizza I’ve had in SF so far, and rivals the NY ones. Love the Hot Burrata and Ruby flavors, and although on the pricier side, buying a whole pie is worth it. Amazing texture and love the grated parmesan.

This is not your ordinary ramen bar!

top_reviews.content: We ate as a party of 13 friends at the China Village located at Solano Ave, Albany near Berkely yesterday night on 5/21/26. The restaurant is located conveniently by itself across the sidewalk from parking. All you need to do to get there is cross a short sidewalk. The area felt clean and safe. When we arrived and walked in, we were greeted by many nice, beautiful and hospitable ladies who were to be our waiters and led to a private "Dragon" party room near the back. In the front were standard tables and a lot of pretty Chinese decor from Gold to Dragons. There were bathrooms separated by gender and area located near the front. There was also a fish tank full of sea-life such as Crabs and Fishes and Lobsters that were on the Chinese Cuisine's Menu. It was a very laid back vibe and very quiet and peaceful and relaxing. In the back, were we were seated, the tables had comfortable chairs and a round spinning table like something you would find at Chinese Dim Sum. The atmosphere felt very relaxed and easy-going and brought us back to feeling like we were in China or Shanghai's Nightlife. The waiter's service was great, they constantly came to check in on us and were very personable and formidable and made nice small talk with us and chatted and it felt like they were close friends which each waiter should strive to be. Our table was filled with neat napkins to wipe, put on your lap and to double as a handkerchief with, silverware, a glass of fresh water not tap as well as herbal fresh tea that was simmered just right with a hint of bitterness you would expect from fresh tea with leaves. We ordered and the food was promptly brought out almost immediately with little wait time. This restaurant is known for their fresh Chinese spark of Sichuan(Spicy) and Mala(Spicy) as well as Seafood(Seafood), once again it felt like we were transported back into the luxurious city of China. This was very authentic and fresh Chinese food, not like the fake food that is AmeriChinese like Panda Express. We ordered delicious food such as clams and oysters which were paired with a lot of extra garnish to truly bring out their wonderful shelly flavor, beautiful and delicious small crustacean prawns and shrimp that tasted fresh from the sea, Spicy Mala/Sichuan Beef as well as Fish which were pretty spicy yet savory, Yangzhou Fried Rice with the perfect amount of veggies and beef, Honeybee Lobster that was golden crisp, Orange Chicken that was not as sweet as many fake Chinese places make them so these were the authentic real deal, Pork and Shrimp Dumplings which were nicely coated and didnt fall apart, Shellfish which were deliciously chewy, Scallops which were very tasty and more. The food was very clean and fresh, they had a rich savory seafood taste and aroma and tasted like the deep blue ocean, and most of the food came with a side of unique sauce that was to be best paired individually with each unique dish. The service was great, the waiters were very attentive and attentful with their service, constantly refilling our glasses and helping us make way and navigate around our big party of guests and limited spaces to make way for new dishes to glaze our table. Everyone was full, we were not rushed and came out feeling very refreshed and sleepy as the food was so so delicious. Fair price! I attached some pictures below of what I had, if anyone is in the nearby area, I encourage you to come try the food at this delicious and authentic Chinese restaurant. Even if you are not in the immediate area, this place is worth a drive as we did coming from the Solano Area all the way here just to sample this delicious food from a mutual friend's wonderful recommendations. We are sure to come back in the near future to try their delicious other menus offerings and we are confident that we will be equally if not more impressed with their offerings the second time around as well. Thank you so much to China Village for hosting our large party and be very pleasant to be around for both service and coordination of the big dinner that took place yesterday.

top_reviews.content:
Square Pie Guys sits right in the heart of Old Oakland, an area that’s perfect for wandering and grazing across different shops and food spots. Inside, the vibe is casual but energetic with an open kitchen lets you watch the pizzas come to life, while a blazing blue neon sign highlights their signature square slices. There’s a steady flow of locals grabbing their boxes to go, mixed with small parties dining in. The space inside feels compact, the outside seating helps, but this location is not built for big groups. Parties larger than five or six will probably feel squeezed. It works perfectly, though, for grabbing a couple of slices with a few friends or a relaxed date night.

The staff clearly care about what they are doing. They are friendly, attentive, and genuinely knowledgeable about the menu. Even during busy stretches, while constantly pulling pies from the oven and managing orders, they stay patient and helpful. It feels like a team that enjoys the craft, not just the job.

The salads are reliably excellent: fresh ingredients, made to order, bright and satisfying. Don’t come expecting standard sodas from a fountain or domestics on tap. I like how they focus on local beers and craft soda options, so go there open to trying something new to drink.

Their Detroit-style crust hits that ideal balance of crispy edges while remaining airy inside. The “Mush-o-Roni” is a classic go to, layering classic pepperoni with mushrooms for a rich, umami-heavy bite. Whereas the “How Mush-Room” offers a creamy alternative with its white sauce that pairs well with the cheese blend to satisfy the fungi fanatics.

The lemon pepper wings deserve special mention. They are crispy on the outside, tender inside, and clearly made fresh. They are well-executed, though the seasoning could use a bit more of a punch. Pairing them with their signature lemon pepper pizza (featuring lemon ricotta cream, more of that lemon pepper chicken, and green onion) was a smart move. The sauce alone elevates the whole pie and made me glad I tried it.

The spicy pepperoni also deserves special mention. Those crispy cups of pepperoni, spicy vodka sauce both under and drizzled over the cheese for extra depth is something special. The Detroit-style crust and edges are consistently on point across all of their pies and keeps me coming back.

Square Pie Guys never lets me down. Fresh ingredients and respectful execution of Detroit style make it a strong alternative to the usual round pies. Go if you love thick, crispy-edged Detroit pizza, especially pepperoni-forward or creative combos, or if you’re a lemon pepper lover. The wings and pizza together satisfy that craving well. Ideal for small groups or casual outings. I am absolutely planning a return, probably soon. Solid 4.75/5.

Didn’t get to try the pizza but snacks and beer I had were great. Didn’t interest with staff too much but overall a good impression on service. Love all the natural lighting and color. Seems welcoming and fun.

I had been wanting to try Square Pie Guys for years. My wife and I had the day off together and we ended up in Emeryville for some errands. I decided that we should come and try Detroit style pizza. Street parking was easy to find right out front. We opted to sit outside because it was a nice day in Oakland, but it was like 1pm on a Monday so the streets and shop were pretty dead. The inside of the shop was also a little warm and stuffy from the pizza oven.

After looking over the menu I decided to order the spicy pepperoni and my wife got the ultimate plant with dairy free cheese - see photos. I also got an order of the Szechuan chicken wings - not pictured - and my wife got the chilled bowled salad - also not pictured.

First off the wings were dried fried style and has the crispiest exterior. The seasoning was a mix of salt, white pepper, and sugar; very reminiscent of Wingstop's fries with the sweet and salty combo. The cilantro lime crema dip that comes with the wings is also fantastic. Although I feel the crema is better with veggie sticks as it overpowers the wings when eaten together. By far the best wings I've ever had at a pizza place. Highly recommend.

The salad was delicious as far as salad goes but my only criticism is that it had too much dressing. I feel like they could have dialed it back a little bit. But I did love the gigante beans in the salad; very rare you come across those.

Lastly our pizzas. My spicy pepperoni was fantastic although I wished the bottom crust was a little more crispy and crunchy. The dough was nice and pillowly on top. The pepperoni was super crispy with a little bit of char. My wife loved her ultimate plant and they gave her a good mix of veggies. We both agreed that the pizza could have used a bit more sauce. For those of you who know, vegan cheese is very high in sodium. I felt like her pizza was way saltier than mine, and mine was pretty salty already. Just be aware that after two slices, you're gonna feel very bloated and dehydrated.

Overall we both loved Square Pie Guys, and are excited to go to the Walnut Creek location later this year - it's closer to us. It may not be the best Detroit pizza, but it's definitely good Detroit pizza.

top_reviews.content: We enjoyed our spaghetti pomodoro which had great flavor. The pizza was decent and the bread for the table was excellent. The restaurant is a bit tight and got quite loud as it filled up. We could see where that would be a great vibe with high energy but that night was not necessarily what we were going for.

The service was excellent. It’s got a very family like vibe with a friendly host. She was funny and talkative. She was the soul of the place.

But the food didn’t impress. The pizza had way too much sauce, and was under-seasoned. The pastas were better but they lacked depth of flavor. The tiramisu was good, though.

The atmosphere was fine, but the place is small and they don’t have any setup to prevent winds from blowing in towards the tables every time someone opens the door. It was a cold night, so with people coming in and out, it got chilly, and our food didn’t stay warm for long.

Overall, this place was charming but the food could be better.

The staff are genuine & welcoming!

We went here after looking for places to eat that were hard to find for my friend because she’s a vegetarian. It was really cold outside, so the hostess asked if we wanted to sit outside and I did not have my jacket so we said no. We had to wait about five minutes for an inside table, but that was totally fine! I did not mind waiting. As soon as we sat down the waiter asked if we wanted any drinks or anything to get started. We ordered two dirty martinis and the Burratta as an appetizer.  The Burrata was just OK by the way. Like 2 to 5 minutes later, he comes back and asked if we’re ready to order the main meals. We say we need just a couple more minutes. When he comes back again it seems like they are in a rush. Basically the waiter said yes it’s a busy night so if you guys can go ahead and order. I have never been rushed like that before at the beginning of dinner. I thought that was a really strange and rude. I ordered the Ragu pasta, which was really good and my friend ordered some spinach cheese ball things which was called a pasta, but she basically said it was just cheese balls with spinach.  The martinis came with olives that were not seedless. Normally in a martini they are.  Anyway, we wanted another cocktail before we left, but we decided to leave and go to spend our money at a different bar next-door that did not rush us one bit.  Even when they brought the food I wanted a before and after picture of before Parmesan versus after Parmesan on my pasta, and the guy with the Parmesan looked at me like he was annoyed. Rude.  You would think he would know what I was doing and what I would do with the pictures, reviews, hello !The inside of this restaurant is just OK looking as well. I rated this restaurant so low basically because of the customer service… while the hostess was really nice to get us a table, The rest of the dinner, customer service was just really bad. They kept hovering every 10 minutes to see how quickly we were eating.  Never in my life.

This place has a 30+ history for us :D. One of the waiters could still remember the group! First time for me though. We went there for a quick dinner during a friday night in the city.
Conveniently located in SoMa, easy to get to by car and on foot. Use paid street parking or a nearby garage. We had a reservation,  which was good how busy the place was. Very welcoming staff, friendly and helpful. We were seated almost immediately.
Nice selection of Italian staple food and wine list. Settled in with a cocktail and a glass of wine before placing our orders. Had a pasta dish and lasagna as mains. Served fairly quickly. Delicious comfort food, nice flavors and very tasty. We took an equally yummy Tiramisu to go (for a late night sweet with a drink in our hotel).
A minor mistake on the bill was proactively addressed without any fuss. Chapeau! Reasonable pricing for the city and good home-made food, what else are you looking for?! Recommended without any restrictions, will come back for sure.
