top_reviews.content:
Stopped in after a salon appointment in Albany and found this to be a slightly more polished version of your typical Bay Area pho spot.

Food:
The fresh spring rolls (gỏi cuốn) were fresh and well-prepared. Peanut sauce was good, nothing standout, but definitely enjoyable.

I ordered the bún bò Huế, which included traditional congealed pork blood (huyết), always a plus for authenticity. The broth had good depth of flavor, but it lacked the expected spice. This dish should have a bit of heat, and that was missing.

The side veggies leaned heavily on bean sprouts (very typical here), but I would’ve preferred more shredded cabbage for balance.

Drinks:
Vietnamese iced coffee came out almost immediately, so it’s clearly pre-made. Efficient, but you do miss the traditional drip experience.

Service & Atmosphere:
Service is very fast, everything came out within minutes. After that, it’s pretty hands-off, so you’ll need to flag someone down if you need anything.

The space itself is nicer than most pho spots, and the uniformed staff gives it a slightly more put-together feel.

Overall:
Good food, very quick service, and a clean, comfortable space. Not exceptional, but a solid, reliable option if you’re in the area. Pricing is in line with current Bay Area averages, though it feels slightly high given the quick-service, pho-house style experience.

Pricing (my order):
•	Fresh spring rolls: $10.95
•	Bún bò Huế: $17.25
•	Vietnamese iced coffee: $6.95

3.75⭐️

Overall great spot for Vietnamese food. Fresh and delicious. I like how they have a small bowl of broth on the side for their rice plates. It's a perfect pairing. The spring rolls are on point as well.

Outstanding Vietnamese Pho Experience!
This is hands down one of the best bowls of pho I've had in a long time. The broth is the true star—rich, deep, and full of flavor, yet incredibly clean and not greasy at all. You can tell it has been simmered for hours with great care. Every sip is comforting and satisfying.
I also love that the pho is served in a double-wall stainless steel bowl, which keeps the soup piping hot from the first bite to the last. It's such a thoughtful touch that makes the dining experience even better.
The fresh herbs, bean sprouts, and onions were crisp and vibrant, and the beef was tender and delicious. But what really impressed me was their house-made chili sauce—it's packed with flavor, perfectly spicy, and takes the pho to another level.
If you're looking for authentic Vietnamese pho with exceptional broth, excellent presentation, and attention to detail, this place is a must-visit. I'll definitely be coming back again and again. Highly recommended! 🍜🔥⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Pho family favorite!

Every time we are in town we come straight to this place. Staff are so family friendly. Food has been amazing for the past 6 years; never disappoints!

My go to is their Pho Chin, Nam, Ve Don which is Well-done brisket, well-done flank, and crunchy flank with extra lime squeezed. Everything is so fresh and homemade is at their best!

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Great Pho place in Albany with reasonable price. The food is delicious with great serving, you typically only need to wait < 10 mins before your order is ready. There is parking next to the restaurant. Also, the atmosphere is great and the staff are really nice.

top_reviews.content: I’m rating Gioia five stars on the pizza. I love it. Love it. And I love the style which is the New York style way. You order your slices which are pre made pies. Then they heat them in the oven which makes them hot and crispy. Several topping choices to choose. No indoor seating. Other than a bench there’s really no outdoor seating either. But the pizza is so good. And it’s nice, shady outside. Decent amount of street parking.

YUM. I’m so happy to have found this spot. This is some of the best pizza I’ve ever had, and I’m a former New Yorker.

The crust is perfectly chewy and the toppings are absolutely delicious. Our favorite is the Julian, which I’m pretty sure is perfect. The cheese and sausage are so yummy and they are generous with the garlic and lacinato kale. So delicious and dare I say healthy too?

The fact that you can get most of their specialty pizzas by the slice is the cherry on top and reminds me of my days in nyc, but pizza this good was even hard to come by there.

Tucked into the side of your average street in Berkeley is the best pizza we’ve had in the Bay Area. GIOIA is serving up some VERY good pizza out of what feels like a hole in the wall. Beware that parking may be hard to find as it’s right off the street although there is a lot just down the road. The inside is very bare bones, which in this case is a good sign. The smell of the oven and dough just hits you once you step in and it’s fantastic. Ordering was quick and easy and the slices are priced a bit high but for the quality of pizza we’d say it was worth it. We got some classic slices and also their fungi slice. From ordering to eating it took about 5-10 minutes despite a few people ahead of us so it was relatively quick.

And now time to try it… man was it good. It’s clearly a good representation of NY style. The crust is firm and crunchy but the pizza has a nice flop to it. The cheese is tasty with a good sauce under it too. The fungi also popped with flavor from the mushrooms, parsley, and olive oil; just a great series of slices. The best place to eat it is probably the bench seating they have outside but it may be full as a heads up. As far as we see it, GIOIA is a must stop in Berkeley. It came very highly recommended and was devoured in less than 5 minutes. We almost wish we didn’t have plans to eat later that day because we could’ve eaten 2 more slices each then and there. This is as close to true NYC style pizza as you can get outside of NYC.

There is the original location in Berkeley and then another location in Hayes Valley in San Francisco. We passed it all the time so we thought we would come in and try it. They are crust is incredible! Nine out of 10 in that category. They have a very interesting sauce, it’s almost on the edge of a pasta sauce, but not quite. I think honestly if they slightly changed up their sauce, the pizza would be better. If you like cheese on your pizza, this is the place to go because they’re pretty heavy handed on the cheese. Overall, we liked it and we would try different slices, but it is not our absolute favorite pizza in the bay area. We tried the margarita, so we haven’t tried all of the different slices and flavors that they offer. So we’ll have to go back and see how the others compare. Thus far, we would give it a solid 7/10.

This spot has been saved on my bookmarks for a while. Luckily I had a training nearby and had a chance to try it.

The space is small with some seating right in front of this business. The lines can rack up during lunch so far ready. They're fairly quick with the order. A co-worker in front of me recommended their avacado salad and Julian pizza. Both were delicious! The total came out to -$23 plus tip, which seems to be an average for lunch these days.

The pizza had a perfectly cooked thin crust. The dough was so sparkly doughy and stretchy with the right amount of firmness on the bottom of the crust. The toppings (kale, sausage, mozerlla cheese, garlic..)Jwent well together too with a fair amount dispersed on the slice.

The salad was filling. I probably didn't need to get the pizza. It was well balanced with farro, avacado, golden raisins, and almond. The vinaigrette was also a nice balance (you don't need much).

Go check them out!

top_reviews.content:
Tonight, we dined at Firenze By Night, a cozy Italian gem in San Francisco's North Beach neighborhood, and it was nothing short of spectacular during our Dec 2024 visit.
* Caesar Salad: Absolutely perfect! The greens were crisp, the croutons were perfectly crunchy, and the dressing was balanced with just the right tang and creaminess.
* Alfredo Pasta with Jumbo Prawns: Creamy, rich, and indulgent. The jumbo prawns were cooked to perfection, adding a fresh and luxurious touch to the dish.
* Fettuccine Pesto with Chicken: This was, without a doubt, the best pesto I've ever tasted. The vibrant basil flavor, paired with tender chicken and perfectly cooked fettuccine, made it unforgettable.
* Gnocchi: Light, pillowy, and coated in a delicious sauce--this award-winning dish lived up to its reputation.
* Bread with Olive Oil and Olive Paste: The olive oil itself was great, but the olive paste served with it was out of this world! It added an intense, savory richness that elevated the bread to another level.

The ambiance was warm and inviting, with a classic Italian charm, and the service was friendly and attentive throughout the evening. However, the place can get loud if there are too many large parties, which might affect the overall experience for some diners.

Overall, Firenze By Night delivered an exceptional dining experience. From the unforgettable pesto to the incredible olive paste, this is a must-visit spot for authentic Italian cuisine in San Francisco. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content: I am reviewing as I am finishing my meal, just in case I forget to review later. This place has phenomenal pastas, and I can’t believe the one I am eating is gluten-free, besides being completely vegan. The ambiance is nice and I would recommend this place to anyone looking for not just healthy, but tasty options. Ordered the Arnold Palmer mocktail which is good too.

**UPDATE**

The vegan pasta is fantastic: rich, comforting, with just a touch of heat. It’s exactly the kind of dish that reminds you vegan food can be every bit as satisfying as traditional comfort food.

Unfortunately, brunch was a very different experience. The vegan eggs came with potatoes, very sweet squash mixed into the scramble (squash and potatoes was a mushy texture overload) ketchup with a hint of curry, and a side salad with dressing so light I could barely tell it was there. I love eggs, and this had all the ingredients to become a favorite brunch dish, but it just didn’t come together and wasn’t a satisfying meal.

I also tried the Chimichurri Burger. The combination of grilled onions, peppers, greens, crunchy potato sticks, and chimichurri is genuinely creative and delicious. The bun, however, tasted several days old: dry, dense, and stale. Instead of absorbing the sauces and bringing everything together, it did the exact opposite.

I was going to order the French toast but decided to make it at home instead: fresh challah or brioche, vanilla bean, cinnamon, a pinch of salt, a splash of cream, maple syrup, and fresh berries. It may take more effort, but after this brunch experience I wasn’t willing to take the risk.

—————————————————————
Orecchiette with spicy sausage arrabbiata (Beyond Italian sausage, coconut parmesan, basil) was excellent - perfect level of heat. I couldn’t even tell it was chickpea pasta, and the vegan sausage didn’t cause any heaviness or heartburn.

The avocado chocolate ganache was also great. The whipped cream was light and delicious, and the berries with toasted almonds balanced the richness nicely. I probably wouldn’t order it again only because I prefer milk chocolate.

Good vegan place with lot of options and good ambience. Burgers are really good. Fries can have more salt and mapo tofu could have more flavor. It’s also order and sit down which is not great. Pasta was great tho.

This restaurant is excellent for lunch. I would not go to this Location for dinner time. Everything on the menu is plant based in Vegan. Extremely clean bathrooms. This Location accepts credit cards. This Location typically has a lot of mask delivery drivers hanging out in congregating around the restaurant during dinner hours and usually all hours of the day that the restaurant is open. I would consider this casual dining. This is a restaurant that I would only eat at takeout only.

Great place for healthy vegan food. prompt service. Plenty of seating. Neatball Masala was fantastic, most popular dish title is well earned.

However, lots of flies, and cauliflower appetizer could not hold the seasoning. Burger patty is delicious, but not enough sauce. We had to use the dressing from the cauliflower appetizer to bring it up to par.

Portions are modest, set expectations accordingly.

top_reviews.content:
This was a cute restaurant! The prices were reasonable (for the bay).
While I'm not a coffee drinker, my partner rather enjoyed it and described it as strong. I am a tea drinker however, and while the tea was good, I rather wished there was a better way of serving it, as the hot water in the clay tea cup made for rapidly cooling tea before it could steep :/

The service wasn't BAD persay, but could have been a bit more streamlined, as the outside tables were small. It seemed that there wasn't one food runner over seeing specific sections, so our order was initially placed on another customers table.

The bulgogi bowl was good but a bit on the sweet side. I had the Tater Tot Poutine and I feel they fell a bit short. When I think poutine, I'm thinking cheese curds. In fact, one of the reasons I chose this place was because I was very excited to see what an Asian influence on poutine looked like. Seeing my food arrive with no curds, I sent it back because I was sure something was missing. Alas, no, the cotija cheese was the cheese for this dish. I would have rather they used queso fresco instead. It doesn't have a strong flavor and would have satisfied my cheese curd craving </3 That being said, it still slapped.

The star of the show was the Millionaire's Bacon. The cuts were thick, flavorful, creamy (?) and almost melted in my mouth. I won't lie, it's heavily influencing my review.

I wish the outside tables were a bit more spaced, as I felt cramped.

I came here during a weekday for brunch. That is probably the best time to come due to street parking filling up fast.
To drink, I had the raspberry lemonade. This is easily 5/5. Perfect blend of sweetness & tartness.
For an appetizer we got the popcorn chicken & Korean FC. My favorite was the popcorn chicken it was 5/5 and I loved that they added actual popcorn. The Korean FC was okay 3/5.
The Mac N Cheese sounded very interesting, however, it fell flat. It was dry and not cheesy. I would rate it 2/5. We got the Chicken & Story Burger. The Chicken Burger 4/5 was definitely better than the Story Burger 2/5. The Story Burger was lacking in flavor. The potatoes wedges were really good though. Not pictured was the millionaire bacon 5/5. It was so good and I would love to try the BLT with millionaire bacon.
Lastly, we got the Lemon Ricotta Pancake 1/5 it was bitter and the second pancake under the first was burnt. We also got the Mascarpone Stuffed Deep Fried French Toast which was 100/5. Every bite was amazing. Would definitely come back again for that dish alone. Other than that, a lot of the dishes fell flat for me but the presentation of the food was beautiful and service was good as well.

This has easily become one of my favorite brunch spots in Oakland. I usually come with my dog, and one thing I really appreciate is how consistently warm and welcoming the manager and servers are :)

The menu has a Korean-inspired take on brunch, and I almost always order the Blackstone Benedict and the Lemon Ricotta Pancakes.

The Blackstone Benedict is probably my favorite savory dish here. The combination of bacon, asparagus, bread, and hollandaise just works, the richness from the sauce, the saltiness of the bacon, and the freshness of the asparagus are really well balanced. I will say that on a few visits, the sauce had a slightly eggy aroma that I wasn’t crazy about. It’s pretty subtle and hasn’t stopped me from ordering it :-)

As for the pancakes, I’ve tried a few of the options, and the Lemon Ricotta is easily the standout for me. The pancakes are incredibly soft and fluffy, with just enough lemon to brighten everything up without tasting overly citrusy. The ricotta adds this subtle creaminess and richness that makes them feel a little more special than your standard brunch pancakes.

Great food, genuinely kind service, and very dog-friendly, which, for me, is always a plus :-)

Phenomenal brunch flavors are worth the wait (and sore bum)!

Kitchen Story is an epic brunch spot. If you're planning a weekend visit, I definitely recommend making a reservation, or be prepared for a bit of a wait.

I met a friend here for Sunday brunch, and we ordered an assortment of plates and beverages to share. Everything was delicious and repeatable, but here's my order of personal preference for the food:

Korean FC Wings: Crispy, flavorful, and absolutely standout.

Lemon Ricotta Pancakes: Perfectly fluffy, and bright flavors on perfectly prepared pancakes.

Goji Bowl: A solid, satisfying savory option.

For beverages, the Ube Latte and the Millionaire's Bloody Mary were the stars of the show. Their house coffee and unsweetened passion fruit iced tea were good, but fairly standard.

My only suggestion for management would be to invest in more comfortable seating, but honestly, it was worth the sore bum to enjoy all those delicious flavors! I will definitely be returning and recommending to friends.

Wanted to try something different for Sunday brunch. The noodles with the egg, bacon and pork had just enough savory flavor to knock your socks off. The service was ok. The waiter forgot to process my order so I had to ask about my food after watching other people around me get seated and served before myself. He was apologetic and did comp my meal so he did make it right. Just disappointed because the food was soooo good.

top_reviews.content: Hmm, it was alright. I don't think I would come back, but it's important to try new things once in a while. If I remember correctly pasta base is between 11-13 dollars, and picking a sauce/topping adds an extra 4-6 dollars, so at the very least you'll be paying 15 dollars for one bowl of pasta. Kinda pricey. The bowls aren't even that big, only enough to feed one person with a big appetite, 2 people at most. It was enough to fill me up but the flavor was just not there. But it wasn't the worst pasta in the world, just one of those things where you know you could've made something better at home for a fraction of the price. Service and atmosphere are also lacking. Overall, 3/5.

Absolutely loved this place! The pasta was fresh and delicious — especially the tagliatelle with Bolognese and a generous amount of cheese on top. The flatbread on the side was a great surprise and paired perfectly with the meal. Cozy and welcoming interior with a rustic touch, and everything was clean and well organized. You can tell they put care into both their food and the space. Definitely a hidden gem — I’ll be coming back!

It was $50 for on lasagna and one tortellini order (I got no drinks) . You had to get up and order like in a fast food place. At the end you had to put your plates in this tray full of dirty soaking dishes. The lasagna was good but the tortellini was way too chewy and had this tangy flavor that did not go with marinera. The plates look nothing like the website photos. I came because the reviews said it’s great, but that sadly was not the case.

Great, authentic food. Homemade pasta. LARGE portions--prepare to share or take some home. Only suggestion is change pop music out for Italian tracks: Perche' no? Good service. It's an order and take to table situation, self serve. Can order ahead, pick up, and eat in, if desired.

Just like the one in San Francisco, this delicious pasta shop offers a mix & match option to choose a sauce and then a type of pasta. They are fast and delicious.

They also offer salads that are quite hearty and accompany the meal quite well or treat yourself to one of their gelato flavors.

My favorite part is that they have a pasta guide, and I highly recommend their gnocchi!

reviews_snippets.content: "Delicious, fresh food, super friendly service and a cosy interior."
"They also have a great selection of gelato, dry pasta, and cured meats."
"Ingredients are top quality, portions are generous and staff are friendly."

name: MAMA Oakland
address: 388 Grand Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States

google.name: MAMA Oakland
google.address: 388 Grand Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States
google.description: A modern, welcoming nook serving seasonally minded, three-course Italian dinners & thoughtful wines.

top_reviews.content:
Wow, exceptional taste for such a good value.

We loved all the tomato dishes.

We were seated outside and still quite warm (granted, during a "Bay Area summer").

Minus one star for lots of mix ups with our dietary restrictions and who ordered which dish, but that was easily fixed.

Looking forward to coming back!

Excellent food, great vibes, fair prices!

We did the latest Prix Fixe menu, which changes roughly monthly for seasonality.

The waiters were fun, service was fast, we got a seat for just us two on Friday night, and the food was just AWESOME.

Focaccia with olive tapenade slapped super hard, and both salad / soup we had for starters were awesome.
The braized pork in fresh pasta was unctuous and filling.
The panna cotta was my favorite dessert.

We spent $100 each for two full courses, plus scallops to share, without alcohol (but got one NA drink).

Had a fantastic anniversary dinner at MAMA Oakland. The food is fresh, flavorful and clearly made with care. While it’s Italian, it has a modern spin and beautiful presentation. We had the entire Restaurant week menu and has only led us to come back again. Its atmosphere is warm and a perfect spot for dinner with friends or a relaxed date. Staff is welcoming and attentive (big shout out to Chris - restaurant manager, terrific guy who makes you feel at home) and the whole place has that comfortable neighborhood restaurant feel. You will want to come back for more. Give it a go… and thanks for an amazing experience MAMA staff!

Setting: Outdoor Patio / Parklet Dining

The Damage: ~$43 per person (Base 3-Course Prix Fixe Menu)

The Vibe: High-energy neighborhood Italian gem with genuinely warm service.

The Starters: Comfort on a plate
House-Baked Focaccia & Accompaniments: ($6 add-on). This is an absolute must-order for a proper Bay Area restaurant review. The bread features a beautifully airy, high-hydration crumb with massive interior pockets that practically beg to sponge up olive oil. The crust delivers a loud, satisfying crunch. It's served with a velvety whipped tallow butter and a sharp, acidic caper-and-herb relish that cuts through the richness instantly.

Pork & Beef Meatballs: A total standout on the Oakland food scene. They feature an excellent outer sear that locks in an incredibly soft, moist, and loose interior grind. Pillowed under a generous snowcap of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, they sit in a vibrant, slow-simmered tomato marinara that achieves absolute balance. Frankly, I could pull up a chair, order just the meatballs and the focaccia, and walk away completely satisfied.

Sweet Corn Soup: Delivered with a tableside pour directly onto a layered mosaic of whole sweet corn kernels, smoky bacon lardons, and a clean swirl of crème fraîche. It’s a flawless emulsion—perfectly highlighting the natural sugars of summer corn while utilizing a sharp undercurrent of chive oil to balance the creaminess.

Summer Squash Carpaccio: Spring on a plate. Shaved mandolin-thin, the green and yellow squash discs remain ultra-fresh and crisp, showing zero signs of raw moisture weeping. Beautifully plated with fragile squash blossoms and a shower of salty ricotta salata, the entire dish is tied together by the distinct, buttery crunch of toasted pine nuts.

The Pastas: Why This Node Dominates the East Bay
Rigatoni with Mama's Sugo
Nothing in the local grid touches this long-braised meat base; it justifies a trip to Grand Avenue on its own merit for anyone hunting for the best pasta in Oakland. The house-extruded rigatoni features excellent, distinct ridges that act as a mechanical lock for the rich beef and pork sugo. The ragu is deeply comforting, rich, and consistent—the kind of pasta that forces a head-shake of absolute validation with every single bite.

Saffron Cavatelli with Calabrian Sausage
A truly spectacular plate. The hand-rolled cavatelli delivers a dense, perfectly calibrated al dente chew that frames the savory, milder pork sausage crumbles seamlessly. The addition of tender, charred broccolini on top introduces a fresh, vibrant crunch, while the residual spiced pork oil finishes the dish with spectacular depth.

The Sweet Finish
Plum Crostata with Ricotta Orange Gelato: One of the finest desserts I've encountered here. The presentation is pristine, featuring concentric layers of vibrant, tart plum slices resting on a flaky pastry base boasting a rich, buttery flavor profile. The gelato arrives at a dense, sub-zero temperature, creating a smooth, slow-melting sauce layer as it bleeds into the accompanying thyme honey.

Chocolate Devil's Food Cake: A chocolate lover's absolute dream. Slicing the sponge exposes an incredibly tender, open cell structure that retains its moisture perfectly along the lower base. The rich cocoa depth is front and center, balanced beautifully by dense chocolate buttercream and a sharp, pooling Amarena cherry glaze.

The Verdict: 5/5 Stars
At just under $43 per person for the core three courses, the price-to-value ratio at Mama Oakland is practically unmatched for East Bay fine dining. The outdoor patio layout provides plenty of space, a relaxed evening breeze, and a highly attentive, friendly service staff. It completely solidifies its status as an elite local institution for a casual date night, and being only a 10-minute drive away, I'm already looking forward to my next visit.

This may be the greatest restaurant in the entire world! You wouldn’t know it just by walking or driving by, but this Michelin star establishment has some of the best food in the entire world! And, it’s a three course meal, but it is extremely accessible in terms of price. The staff are incredible, and the environment is very welcoming and cozy. We literally go here to celebrate every major event in our lives (anniversaries, birthdays, you name it). Don’t sleep on MAMA!

"I can not wait to come back (this time i'll double check my table selection lol)"

name: Hai Ky Mi Gia Chinese Cuisine
address: 707 Ellis St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States

google.name: Hai Ky Mi Gia Chinese Cuisine
google.address: 707 Ellis St, San Francisco, CA 94109, United States
google.description: Chinese soups filled with ingredients like egg noodles, wontons, satay beef & duck.

top_reviews.content:
This noodle place is the real deal! The couple running the restaurant are the absolute sweetest. They were so patient with us, taking their time to explain the menu items and give great recommendations.

I ordered the #2 (wonton noodle soup) and it was absolutely delicious plus the portion size was great. I also had the Thai iced tea, which was perfection because it wasn’t overly sweet, just the way I like it. Exceptional food and even better hospitality. We will definitely be back!

Was craving some Teochew/Cambodian-style dry noodle and this place hit the spot. The owners were incredibly nice and there was a sweet elderly couple helping out around the restaurant.

Make the trip out here; it’s worth it.
My go-to noodle place in the city. Their 海记什锦 is the one. I really like their rice noodle (河粉）。It’s wide and looks homemade to me. The owner and staff are all very friendly.

I've been here several times and they are extremely consistent in taste and portion size. Prices are reasonable for the portions you get and the service is always very efficient and friendly. Sure it's messy in the TL, but the restaurant is a homey spot with lots of customers and comfortable on the inside.

Things I've ordered:
House special ho fun (soup and dry) - this is the must order here in my opinion, it is full of toppings over the noodles (shrimp, char siew, pork slices, ground pork, chicken strips, fish cakes, beef balls, bean sprouts, pork liver if you want it). I've only gotten the rice noodle version and like it dry with soup on the side. It is well seasoned on its own but you can jazz it up with pickled jalapenos and other sauces that they provide on the table. The fried garlic oil they put in it is delicious and I've never regretted ordering this.
Golden fried fish cakes - about 3 whole fishcakes in each order, cut into half and fried to golden perfection. They are a little greasy but tasty with a nice bounce, they taste great dipped in the hoisin sauce. Served with pickled vegetables on the side (cucumber and carrot) which cuts through the grease perfectly.
Wonton soup - the wontons are just ok, there's no shrimp in it that I could discern and is mostly just wrapper and ground pork. It's seasoned well and comes in the same soup that they serve with the house special noodles.
Beef stew ho fun - this was more soupy than stewy in my opinion, with a strong tomato flavor. The beef was alright and pretty chewy and tough, it would have been nice if they had stewed the meat a little longer to get it nice and soft. The rice noodles don't come with anything else except beef and bean sprouts. It's an ok option but I would opt for the house noodles over this anytime.

The crowds here seem inconsistent, I had to wait once for over 20 mins for a table and it was packed to the gills, and other times I got a table right away and there were a decent number of customers but no wait. The tables turn over quickly though since people are here to eat, not sit around for hours.
Braised Duck Leg Egg Noodle Soup(Dry) was delicious. Fast service. Homemade Soybean drink was good too.

name: Hunan House
address: 826 Washington St, San Francisco, CA 94108, United States

google.name: Hunan House
google.address: 826 Washington St, San Francisco, CA 94108, United States
google.description: Dumplings, noodle dishes, spicy entrees & veggie options served in casual digs with classic decor.

top_reviews.content:
Hunan House is one of those small Chinatown restaurants that proves you don’t need a huge dining room to deliver huge flavors.

The atmosphere has that cozy, neighborhood feel, but the food packs some serious punch. Every dish we ordered was delicious.

🔥 Spicy Chongqing Chicken – Crispy, flavorful, and loaded with the classic dried chilies that bring the heat without overpowering the chicken.

🥩 Spicy Numbing Beef Tendon – Tender, rich, and coated in that signature Sichuan mala flavor that leaves your lips tingling in the best way.

🍜 House Fried Noodles – A generous portion with great texture and plenty of flavor. The perfect dish to balance out the spicy entrées.

This is the kind of place that doesn’t need flashy decorations or a huge dining room. It lets the food do the talking, and it speaks loudly. If you’re exploring Chinatown and want authentic Hunan and Sichuan-inspired flavors, Hunan House deserves a spot on your list.

I can definitely see myself coming back to work my way through more of the menu.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Follow, like, and share for more local food reviews and hidden gems! 🍜🥢🌶️ #HunanHouse #ChinatownEats #SichuanCuisine #Foodie #HiddenGem #SupportLocal #SpicyFood #NoodleLover

Fantastic food! It is a little place where the locals eat, and was recommended to us by a local in Chinatown. The food was delicious, they had a menu in English so we could understand it, and they even gave us a fork along with the chopsticks. The only complaint is that they don't bring the food out all together, and we didn't get it appetizer until after we received our entree. We ordered one entree for two of us to share and one plate of vegetables (yummy), plus an appetizer. First we got the entree, then a few minutes later the side of rice that goes with it. Then about 5 minutes later the appetizer, and they didn't bring our vegetables. I finally signaled a server and apparently they forgot to make it, do they did it quickly and it was all good food but I would have liked the appetizer first, and then the entree, rice, and vegetables all together. But we stuffed ourselves and had plenty of food leftover, so the portions are big, and the price was incredibly reasonable, even cheap. The bathroom is a little scary, but they had nice hot water and soap to wash your hands, so that made up for it. But if you are squeemish about a clean bathroom, you may not want to try it.

A whole cockroach was found in my takeaway food after I had already eaten half the meal.外賣的農家小炒肉裡面有蟑螂！！
The restaurant refunded my order, but that does not change the fact that I had already consumed part of the food. They even didn't say sorry to me.This was one of the most disgusting dining experiences I have ever had.

One of the best Chinese food in Chinatown. We stayed at the Hilton in financial district and was looking for a place to have dinner, and was attracted by all the different Chinese dishes (both Cantonese and Sichuan) shown in their menu. The restaurant wasn’t fancy looking, just like an average restaurant with red antique decor, but their food was excellent. I had the best tasting Cantonese roasted duck that flavorful but not overly salty and crispy delicious skin. They weee sold out of their spicy lamb chops, but the server suggested their toothpick lamb which was excellent. The restaurant doesn’t offer live seafood in tanks, but will cook them for you if you bring them in. They do offer seafood dishes, just not live off the tanks. Their wine corkage fee is also the lowest I’ve paid (under $10).

Visited January 2nd, 2026

After an amazing visit at Mark’s Hair Salon, I asked the gentleman at the salon for a Chinese restaurant recommendation, specifically one that served dumplings. He not only recommended Hunan House, but he actually walked us there. That small act of kindness set the tone for what turned out to be a wonderful dining experience.

My daughters, who are six and seven, had been craving dumplings all day, especially after patiently waiting for over two hours while I got my hair done. When we arrived, we saw that the menu offered two types of dumplings, the Shanghai dumplings and the pan fried dumplings. We ordered both for the girls, and they absolutely devoured every single one. My husband and I did not even get a taste, which honestly says everything about how much they loved them.

We also ordered chow mein noodles with just chicken and noodles for the kids, which they enjoyed very much. The portions were generous and the flavors were comforting and satisfying, exactly what they wanted.

For my husband and I, we ordered the black pepper shredded pork and the crispy fried fish with explosive chilies. Both dishes were exceptional. The flavors were bold, well balanced, and incredibly enjoyable. Every bite was delicious, and we truly appreciated the care and skill that went into preparing the food.

The service was quick, efficient, and courteous, and the food arrived hot and fresh. From the kindness of the initial recommendation to the quality of the meal itself, this experience made our day even more special. We are so grateful for this recommendation and could not be happier with our visit.

top_reviews.content: Been to this place before with friends. Can be busy at times up to a 20-30 mins wait to get a table, indoor and outdoor seating, street parking as well. Food is pretty decent. I can personally say it’s a hit or miss. I’ve gone before where it’s a 10/10 knocked out of the ballpark and then others when it’s a 6/10 where the meat is overcooked and I’m still chewing on my steak for 5 mins. Place is pretty nice as well, it can be busy as I’ve mentioned before. If it’s busy, you can expect longer delays which tends to happen. Good for all ages.

It is always lovely to see friendly and welcoming Crystal.  She is there most times we visit and is knowledgeable and so enthusiastic telling us about new things to try, the things she loves and what's coming up next!  Many restaurants will offer vegan choices which just means it is minus something.  5 Tacos and Beers however gives us innovative and exciting new dishes full of flavor and actual vegan sour cream which adds a huge factor of deliciousness! This weekend I tried enchiladas with a tangy Verde sauce, cheese and lots of deep red beets and a side of black beans with vegan sour cream which were wonderful! The restaurant itself is a fun place with plenty of seating both indoors and out yet maintains charm.  I love that on good weather days they open up the doors to let in fresh air and a view of the passersby and outdoor diners.
If you love tacos and beers, this is a must-go. Absolutely delicious food and tasty beers. Just great. I come back every time I visit.

The ribeye taco is Hella good. I also tried the Octopus taco and that was pretty good too. Beans and rice could be a little better, but good. I tried the ceviche with Octopus,  scallops and Tuna and I thought it was good, but I wish there was more lime and flavor. But it was good. The service was good and we didn't wait long at all to be seated and to get all the items we ordered. I'm looking forward to visiting again, soon.

I came here right before happy hour, 3 pm to ?, and I liked it! The food was good, but the chips and guacamole are top notch! 👌🏻I ordered some drinks and had some tacos. Good tacos and good drinks! Happy hour pricing is 20% off regular prices. Would recommend and return!

top_reviews.content: We loved the seasonal peach pizza, very unique. We ordered foccacia to take home. We usually get the vegan mushroom & spinach but wanted to try something new today. We haven't been in for awhile, being parents of an energetic kid, we really appreciated the addition of games. They have rackets, corn hole, books, hula hoops and bubbles for kids. They have a dog leash station and water bowls for your pups. The cashier was warm and welcoming.
I’ve been here a few times - won’t be going back. If you’re charging $40 for a pizza - put some toppings on it. Barely anything on it, and the last inch and a half of the crust is completely bare.

I coworker turned me in to this place. Staff are very friendly and engaging. They keep the space clean and welcoming. The pizza is AMAZING! Seriously the best thin crust pizza I’ve ever had. While this location is out of my way for the most part, I’ll make it a point to stop by when I’m around. Thank you!

They have great thin crust sourdough pizza. It takes a lot of time and effort to master a great pizza dough not to mention a sourdough one. The staff were nice, very friendly, and welcoming. The soft chewy sourdough pizza crust will be memorable to us and we'll definitely return. The toppings and sauce were very good too.

Nick's pizza is the best pizza I've ever had. They also have really good baked goods and their homemade ranch is amazing. Their crust is so chewy and flavorful due to it being sourdough. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content: Walked in for dinner for 2 on a Thursday afternoon. There is some street parking around the area, we parked kind of far and just walked over. They have both indoor and outdoor seating and a nice little bar, it’s a cozy restaurant and it got busy. Service was also really friendly. We got the arancini to start, I think it was still a little cold and we also go bread with oil which was really good. I got the lasagna which was really big and I devoured it because I was starting. My friend got the involtini and he finished it as well. The food took some time but overall it’s a nice vibe and a cozy restaurant. They said the lasagna and ravioli porcini trifolati were popular dishes to get.

Really disappointing experience. We ordered four dishes and not a single one was done well.

The tomato burrata came with completely flavorless tomatoes. The tuna carpaccio was overly salty, drowning in dressing, with wet, salty tuna and even mayo on top—which felt completely out of place. The pasta ragu had noticeable chunks of pure pork fat, which made it hard to enjoy. The campagnola pasta was swimming in sauce and, instead of pappardelle, had random pieces of spaghetti mixed in.

Across the board, the pasta was overcooked, with strands stuck together. When we pointed it out, we were told this is “expected over time,” even though it arrived like that, and that the mixed pasta shapes were just an accident due to batch cooking.

Service was practically nonexistent. No one checked in to ask how anything tasted. Our half-eaten burrata and tuna were taken away without a single question. We interacted with at least four different people bringing plates, and even the wine was served by a busser, which made the whole experience feel disjointed and inattentive.

Overall, poor execution, questionable explanations, and not worth the price.

Inviting ambiance, absolutely delicious authentic food, and charming fantastic staff! Five stars easily, they transported me back to Italy! Let them order family style for your group so that you can enjoy all of their best dishes and drinks. Shout out Angelo, he was the best!

My friends, new to Berkeley, were telling me that they loved Italian food, so I told them that we must try Agrodolce Trattoria on Shattuck. I know that Agrodolce has roots going back to Caffe Sport in North Beach which I would go to in the 70's, and more recently Trattoria Siciliana on College which was my buddy David's favorite restaurant.
We loved it! The atmosphere was great, including projecting the classic film La Dolce Vita on the wall. The food was fantastic, my Swordfish was cooked, as the menu said" perfectly! The cocktail bar was  right out of an old movie. And the bread and dipping sauce was a signature classic.
My friends and I were able to catch up on recent trips to India, Normandy France and Budapest. It could hardly have been a better choice.
Needless to say we'll be back!

The food was variable...some dishes were very good, others were pretty mediocre.  The service was some of the worst I have experienced at a restaurant of this level for quite a long time.  Things started out fine. We ordered a second bottle of wine that took 15 minutes to arrive, by which time some of us were nearly finished with our main course.  I could see our bottle was sitting on the server's table where our server stood, joking with the other staff, for a good 5-10 minutes before I stood up, walked over, and requested that she bring the bottle to our table.  At dessert, we were handed two dessert menus for a table of six.  When we asked for a menu per person, we got quite the strange/annoyed look from the busboy.  A good 15 minutes had passed after we finished the desserts and no server came by to deliver the bill.  Not wanting to hang around longer, I went to the bar to request the bill.  It took them another 10 minutes to furnish the bill (the restaurant was not busy by then), upon which they added a mandatory 20% tip on the POST-TAX total, which I disputed but they refused to change.  We will not be returning, and given the long list of better and more professional options out there, I would caution anyone else from going.

top_reviews.content: We stopped in before a show at The Paramount with no expectations other than a simple ramen fix. We ordered a few appetizers to start, followed by ramen, and everything was… fine. Not bad, just pretty average. With so many stronger options in Oakland, I’m not sure I’d return—not because of a bad experience, but because the competition is simply better.

The words that kept popping into my head when describing the food at Itani is "clean eating". The broth for the Oxtail Ramen was not fatty as anticipated and was soothing even. The Spicy Shrimp Ramen packed more of a flavor punch and was well balanced in spice. The Fried Chicken Sandwich was very juicy and flavorful. The slaw is proper spicy, so be warned. Will definitely be back to try more.

This review is based on my delivery order.

I had the Recovery Meal; includes your choice of a ramen bowl, 3 pieces veggie or pork gyoza, negi chashu mini donburi or small salad, and a non-alcoholic drink. I opted for the Veggie Ramen, veggie gyoza, salad, and Yuzu lemonade.

The veggie ramen was flavorful. The veggie gyoza with the dipping sauce, yummy! The dressing on the salad made it so delicious. I’m a huge fan of yuzu and the yuzu lemonade really hit the spot!

I appreciate restaurants that have okay-based and vegan options. I hope they expand on these options.

Crazy good food! This little place was so cozy and our waiter took the time to tell us about the art and the story behind it. The food was incredible and rich. Would definitely come back.

top_reviews.content:
Very yummy food! Im a huge fan of mexican food, and this fusion food brings it to another level. Truthfully ive only ever gotten their bowl with chicken, but getting it with golden rice and all of that is so worth it. Its got a kind of richness and creaminess to it that i love. While ive only tried that one thing, i will say that their ingredients seem very good quality, and ive never gotten a piece of gristle, or wilted lettuce, or anything like that. Their salsas are also very yummy, although i wish they were a bit spicier. But they're very suitable for people with average to low spoce tolerance!!
The outside seating is very cute, and the "inside" seating next to the main building is pretty nice too. My friend and i normally just get take out, but eating there would be nice, and the place is pretty cute with its decorations.
I highly recommend you give the Afghan way a try!

I tried the Afghan burrito today, and it was absolutely delicious! Everything was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned — every bite was full of amazing taste. I loved it so much that I’ll definitely come back to enjoy it again and again.

The customer service was also excellent — very friendly, welcoming, and attentive, which made the experience even better.

It’s a great option for family meals and events too. Highly recommended!

Came to this spot last night to break our fast since we were in the area and had heard great things about it. The birria tacos were so delicious, the meat was high quality and very well priced. I also tried the burrito bowl, which came half golden rice, half lettuce, with chicken and topped with guacamole. The bowl was a bit on the blander side, although when I tasted some of the sauce (maybe the golden/sweet sauce?), it was good. I think next time I’d try something different.

Otherwise, the service was great. My only small complaints are that the sauce containers are tiny and the side of chips is more of a sprinkle than an actual side, lol. That said, I really appreciated that they offer dates to break your fast and have tons of Palestinian art and messages throughout the restaurant, it was amazing and very supportive to see. They also use halal meat, and the quality is excellent.

The bathrooms were impeccably clean, customer service was solid, and I loved that they carry Palestinian soda instead of Coke or Pepsi. Overall, a great experience and I’d definitely come back.

What a unique taco experience! It would be a great place with a larger group and there is total privacy which is fun.  We went back and forth on which tacos to order and settled on these but for both of us it was totally about the Birria tacos.   We didn’t finish the 5th one so they are filling.

I got the vegan Golden burrito here, it was very tasty and a huge portion! I wasn't blown away by the taste, but it was interesting to try since it was like a normal burrito (beans, rice, fajitas etc) but with their Golden sauce inside. The burrito comes with a few chips and sweet chili sauce on the side. The burrito leaked quite a bit near the end, so it's better to eat it over a plate with a fork ready.

The menu has clearly labeled vegan options, which I really appreciate! The restaurant is part of a planned outdoor space (Cal Food Garden), so there is plenty of high-quality outdoor seating as well as bike parking.

top_reviews.content: This was a great experience for us. The restaurant is in a rough looking neighborhood and parking was quite difficult as there is only street parking available. The restaurant has a few booths inside for small parties and a large garden patio with benches for larger parties. We had dinner on a Sunday evening and had a relatively short wait. We ordered both the cold and hot soba as well as the smoked duck breast. The duck was superbly done served chilled, the soba was out of this world. You can tell there was a lot of Care that went into the making of the noodles. Each bite breaks cleanly through the bouncy soba. If you have the opportunity to share in this experience I strongly suggest you make your way there.

I’ve never been wowed by soba and this place hasn’t changed that lol. Even though they make the noodles in house, the noodles taste about the same. The broth was a very plain dashing broth. I did really like the duck though! But it also took very long for the food to arrive (waited over 30 minutes for the noodles). I wouldn’t go out of my way to drive here unless you’re a big soba fan.

I got the duck last time and was seriously disappointed. Got the tenpura one this time and completely different story. Flavor is incredible especially with the chili flakes they give you. The wasabi salt is a great dipper for the tempura! Now we are hooked!

I really liked their cold soba with dipping sauce and garnishes, along with shrimp and kabocha tempura. The noodles had a nice chewiness and leaned toward a firmer side, which I enjoyed. The tempura was light, crispy, and not greasy. Highly recommended!

Loved everything! First time experiencing this hidden gem spot! HOWEVER, I couldn’t give it 4 stars because the veggies really need an extra wash — unfortunately, the fresh salad and the vegetables in the veggie soba still have a sandy taste. Other than that, I give 2 stars to the restaurant staff who’s very friendly and helpful!

We recently visited Pyeongchang Tofu House and it really hit the spot. My daughter was craving spicy pork, and I was in the mood for tofu stew, and this place delivered on both. The flavors were on point and exactly what we were hoping for.

The service was also great. The staff was attentive, friendly, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal.

One small note, they served us the crispy rice from the bottom of the clay pot. I remember having this growing up, but with sugar, and since I haven’t seen it in a long time, I wasn’t quite sure how it was meant to be enjoyed here. It would have been nice to have a little guidance, as I think we might have appreciated it more with some context.

Overall, a really solid experience. We’ll definitely be back when we’re craving comforting Korean food.

One of the best Korean places in the Bay Area. Started with great banchan. Eggplant was our favorite. A wide selection of bibimbap. We tried the wakame and seaweed one, and it didn’t disappoint. Tofu soup warmed us up on a chilly evening.

As someone who appreciates Korean food, I was disappointed with the quality and flavors of the dishes. Overall, the food did not live up to expectations. It felt underseasoned, lacked flavor, and was simply not very good. I wouldn’t recommend this place if you’re craving good Korean food.

Been coming here for 15 yrs straight, since undergrad! Amazing every time. Highly recommend the kimchi tofu soup, galbi tang, bi bim bop, bossam, gal bi, soba cold noodles. They have probably the best banchan. Thank you to all the staff and kitchen, this place is a true Oakland gem.

If it weren’t such a drive, I’d be back every week just for that. I also love that they serve crispy rice with the soft tofu soup, it adds the perfect crunch and soaks up the broth beautifully.

All in all, great food and pretty good value. Great atmosphere.

The service was kind, the atmosphere delectable.

I ordered this mushroom risotto off the specials at the recommendayion of the waiter.

When I tell you it was awesome, I do it with the full weight of my thesis advisors censure on the usage of the word for anything that was less than a sign from God. For in this case it was close to a religious experience. The greens were fresh, well blanched, and tender. They perfectly offset the richness of the risotto and mediated texture via the pumpkin. Around the edges dollops of parsley-garlic muddles provided bursts of flavor that provided the dish a well-modulated method of enhancing the senses. The mushrooms, well, they are freshly foraged and treated with care by the chef.

Taken together I will say I was blown away. It reminded me of a Slovenian risotto made by a grandmother who has cooked it for decades, but with a presentation and sophistication suitable for a diplomats table.

If you are so lucky as to have this offered on the menu, do not miss the chance.

If it is not already clear, compliments to the chef. I eagerly look forward to whatever they whip up next.

If we lived in San Francisco this would be a weekly stop. We ate fancy, touristy, and casual; and out of everything we ate on this trip, this was 100% our favorite, and it wasn’t even close.

I was running hungry downtown, the rain was starting to come down hard when I eyed this restaurant. It caught my attention for its interesting name including "Latin Asian", a name that was neither inaccurate nor disappointing as their menu items reflect what they advertise.

I was cold, tired, and slightly hungry- needing to leave room for a later dinner- and so wanted to pick at several appetizers with a friend, which this restaurant was perfect for. The first good sign was the steam rising, heat emanating from each dish served hot to the touch. I ordered the pork belly skewers, juicy with just enough toughness to be fun to chew, spring rolls, perfectly thin and crisp on the outside and extremely soft and flavourful on the inside, becoming a surprise highlight of my meal, and empanada, which was the size of both of my fists together and sopping in enough oil to warrant invasion by everyone's favourite stripes and stars- so much oil that it was literally drenching and dripping down my hands, delicious but maybe a little dangerous.

While pricing felt slightly expensive for some items, they were generally fair, as were portions. Staff was friendly and service was good, though initially slow to take orders and taking a bit more time than expected to serve the dishes, which maybe is a good sign that everything is cooked fresh.

Something I could crave every once in a while, and a restaurant I'm glad I know exists. 5.2/10.

The food is really flavorful. We ordered the pabellon with rice, beans and plantains, it was a big plate. The rotisserie chicken is amazing! Crispy, juicy, tender, and just perfect. The mini arepas are a must as a side dish. So glad we ended up in this place. Friendly staff and Latin music in the background was the cherry on top.

Not sure what happened or maybe went on a bad day.  Ordered grilled beef over rice and XL pho tai chin togo.  5 thin grilled beef slices over rice and 5 raw thin slices of beef for XL pho.  My dine in experience here 3 months ago was good but this is extremely discouraging me to come back for my Vietnamese food fix :/

Pretty good overall. I appreciated that it was easy to pull up and park here, even on a weekend. Portion sizes were solid; really loved the vermicelli bowl. The pho was solid, but might have had a bit too star anise in the seasoning for me, since it tasted a tad more licorice-y than I usually see. A sweeter broth, less complex in flavor. Still pretty good though- I loved the texture and bounciness of the banh pho, had a great chew to them.

*2/14/2024
The portion size was generous, but unfortunately, the soup base was overwhelmingly salty. We ended up guzzling water just to quench our thirst after eating it

7/7/2023
During my visit to Pho King in Oakland, I ordered the Bun Bo Hue, Spring Rolls, and Egg Rolls. The Bun Bo Hue consisted of Hot & Spicy Soup with Beef, Pork Blood, Pork Cake, and Vermicelli. Overall, the food tasted okay.

The Bun Bo Hue had a decent flavor, although it didn't particularly stand out. The soup had a good level of spiciness, and the inclusion of beef, pork blood, and pork cake added some variety to the dish. However, I found the taste to be average, without any exceptional elements.

Regarding the Spring Rolls and Egg Rolls, they were satisfactory, but they didn't leave a lasting impression. The flavors were acceptable, but I felt that they could have been more flavorful and distinctive.

In summary, the food at Pho King was decent and tasted okay. While nothing was particularly outstanding, it wasn't disappointing either. It would be great if they could focus on enhancing the flavors to make the dishes more memorable.

We had: CELERY ROOT TIRADÍTO (pure perfection, is was so good that after eat all I keep drinking the sauce) PATACONES (amazing, for sure gonna order again) BRUSELAS EL PRADO (really good but my least favorite). When I made the reservation I ltk I was going to Rosalia concert, and was a unexpected lovely that they played some of their songs ❤️
Me and my friend are for sure coming back, I will also bring my partner as well cause I love the experience!

I’m vegan, loved the menu very clear about what was vegan, vegetarian, gluten free… is so important when menus are clear for food restrictions and even more when this food is so so flavorful. Thank u!!

Such a great spot in Oakland! Everything we tried was delicious, and the menu felt really unique and different from the usual. It’s family style, which made it fun to order a bunch of dishes and share everything at the table. Every plate had so much flavor and felt really thoughtfully put together. Definitely a place I’d come back to!

5 stars across the board. The staff was very friendly and attentive. The food was amazing. They have a good variety of meat and vegetarian options, including some vegan, and the whole kitchen is gluten free, although you wouldn’t necessarily notice. The design of the space is also beautiful and joyful. Delicious cocktails and mocktails too!

We took Mom here for brunch and oh what a wonderful outing she had. Sharing items on the menu is allowed, so we ordered several dishes to get a good feel for their servings.  From the Bruselas El Prado to Arepa De Chocolo with chicken, then through Empanada De Ajiaco, and finally we had Flan De Coco dessert, it was a walk through a taste experience like I have not had before.  Their chef and the team are culinary magicians. The restaurant is decorated in what feels like an authentic Colombian restaurant, and the waiter kindly helped us figure out our meal.  I especially enjoyed the teamwork that made sure all our needs were met.  They had wonderful music playing in the background that made the vibe right.  The location is downtown so parking in the public lot next door is probably best.

🌟 Really fun, memorable dinner at Parch!

We came here around 6:45 on a Friday night for a double date and had a great experience. Parking was surprisingly easy to find, and an added bonus is that the meters stop at 6pm.

🎨 Atmosphere: The space is vibrant, lively, colorful, and really creatively decorated. I loved the tile, wallpaper, and all the little design details. It has a great energy and was perfect for a double date. The pacing of the meal was also just right—not rushed, but never dragging. I wouldn't necessarily come here for a quick bite, but it's a great place to settle in for an evening.

🍸 Cocktails: We tried several and they were excellent. The Mi Encanto and Tropiquita were both very good, but the standout for me was the El Hombre Caimán with green Chartreuse, a beautiful ice cube, and thick foam on top. It was unlike any cocktail I've had before. Highly recommend trying it if you're in the mood for something different.

🍽️ Food: We ordered a lot to share, which I think is the way to go here. The Tumaco ceviche had a delicious sauce and was a nice size for four people considering how many other dishes we ordered. The empanadas were also very good—the cornmeal exterior almost reminded me of corn dog batter in the best way, and the accompanying sauce was great.

The biggest surprise was the Arepa de las Monas with yellow corn and yuca masa and Oaxacan cheese. It was nothing like I pictured from the description—almost like a beautiful, cheesy puff pastry. Really, really delicious and probably my favorite of the smaller plates. The Chicharrón Crispitas were good as well, though pork belly can be a little rich for me.

For the larger plates, I loved the fried whole branzino. The fish itself was excellent with wonderfully crispy skin and surprisingly few bones. The accompanying rice was a little too sweet/coconut-forward for my taste, so I mostly skipped it.

The Corte Andino bone-in ribeye was probably the one dish I enjoyed less. It had a sweeter glaze, and I personally tend to prefer savory flavors. We ordered it medium rare, but I found the meat a little tough and chewy and actually wished it had been cooked a bit more.

Overall, though, the food was excellent and several dishes genuinely surprised us with how creative and delicious they were. Parch feels like the kind of restaurant where trying a bunch of different things is part of the fun. The staff was friendly, helpful and attentive. My glass was always full of water and they helped us select dishes to order. Great cocktails, beautiful atmosphere, and some really memorable food. Definitely worth checking out! 🍸✨

I recently had the extreme pleasure of dining at Sobo Ramen. I ate my meal in a mostly empty restaurant, which now seems odd to me. I'd describe the experience as a meal curated to my tastes specifically. There was a cover track of a compilation of Getz/Gilberto playing in the background which i found surprising at first but fit the vibe pretty well.

The squid ink ramen had just enough spice to it to not overwhelm the the other flavors. I ordered karage to go and the container was packed to the brim, but the quantity did not seem to forsake the quality.

I drank a Sapporo and the Suntory and as far as beer goes, the Suntory Premium Malt is great for a salty meal. The Sapporo is fine, I just drank a lot of it in Japan and it just tastes regular now lol.

All in all, I want to live next to this place. Food is delicious, staff is friendly, prices are modest. If you're looking to decompress after a long day or a good spot for a date, you can find it here.

The ramen we ordered was nice, it's not salty and you can definitely enjoy the hot soup.
Karaage was good. We ordered hot house sake too.
The servers was very nice.

The food here was damn good! We wanted ramen for our last night on our business trip. We decided to try this place despite the 3.5 rating on Yelp. The place was pretty empty at 530pm. Servers were prompt and polite, answering questions and giving recommendations when asked. We ordered steamed gyoza and three ramen dishes.  I ordered the country ramen, amazing flavor and mild spice.  My coworkers ordered the Tonkotsu with Tonkatsu and Sobo ramen with chicken and spicy - way too spicy for my liking but my coworker loved it. I'd love to come again on my next trip!

My family and I love this place.  We eat here at least once a month, perhaps more during  cold season.

The broth is very good particularly the spicy black tonkotsu.  Meat is just right and the whole bowl is simple, just how ramen should be.  A simple comfort food.

My wife and I have been in many ramen places around the Bay Area that are ranked or rated high on several sites and even from TV food shows and I can honestly say that Sobo Ramen is among the best we have tasted.

I just wish there are more options for appetizers but we love it here!  We are regulars here by now and we are welcomed here like family each time we eat at Sobo Ramen.  It is SOBOlicious!!!

if you're craving legit ramen that doesn't break the bank but still feels special, Sabi--er, Sobo Ramen--is one of the best in the East Bay. Easily top-tier. 10/10 would smash again, no cap. Go get that bowl, you won't regret it!

Ambience is cozy as hell. It's got that intimate, low-key Japanese ramen shop feel--nothing fancy, but warm lighting, clean setup, and it doesn't feel cramped even when busy. Perfect for solo slurping, a quick date, or grabbing with friends. In the heart of Oakland's Chinatown/Pacific Renaissance spot, it's easy to get to and feels authentic without being stuffy.

top_reviews.content:
Magnin Street Cafe is an absolute hidden gem and one of those places you almost want to keep to yourself. From the moment we walked in, we were welcomed with warm, genuine hospitality, and our server, Consuelo, made the entire experience exceptional. She was attentive, friendly, and truly went above and beyond to make us feel taken care of.
The food was fresh, beautifully prepared, and every plate that came out looked as good as it tasted. The omelet was perfectly fluffy, the Eggs Benedict was rich and delicious, and everything was paired with crisp, fresh greens and perfectly cooked sides. Even the coffee deserves a special mention because it was absolutely excellent, rich, smooth, and the perfect way to start the day.
Great food, outstanding service, wonderful coffee, and a cozy atmosphere make Magnin Street Cafe a true neighborhood treasure. We'll definitely be back, and we'll be asking for Consuelo again. Highly recommend!

What a delightful brunch experience! The café is beautifully decorated and spotlessly clean, creating a comfortable and welcoming atmosphere. The service was excellent, every staff member we met was kind, polite, and attentive. Our host was especially friendly and hospitable, making us feel valued and right at home from the moment we arrived.

As for the food, absolutely delicious. The pancakes and French toast were exceptionally soft and well-prepared. In fact, the French toast was one of the best I’ve ever had. I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a top-notch brunch in a lovely setting.

Me and my partner came to Magnin Street Cafe & Bistro for the first time on Thursday, May 21st for breakfast, and from the moment we walked in we knew this place was special. I had the steak and eggs while my partner had the French Toast Delight. Our waitress was beyond kind, we shared so many laughs with her and she made the whole experience feel warm and welcoming. Then the food touched our taste buds and we were in love. My steak was packed with flavor and perfectly juicy, and my scrambled eggs were cooked to perfection.

From that day on, we tried to come back every single day, but unfortunately there was always a huge line just to get in, which honestly told me everyone else saw what I saw too.

We finally made it back for dinner on Sunday, May 24th, and I technically sprinted up the hill in heels just to make it in time for dinner opening at 5 PM 😂. I had the steak frites and my partner had the chicken Alfredo, and once again the food DID NOT disappoint. That was genuinely one of the best chicken Alfredos I’ve ever had. Yes, I ended up eating both our meals because it was THAT good. No to-go boxes needed lol.

We also had cheesecake for dessert, and although I’m not usually a sweets person, this cheesecake was astounding.

As I’m writing this review on Monday morning, May 25th, I’m currently sitting back in the cafe ordering the same breakfast that made me fall in love with this place, and it still does not disappoint. During dinner we met the couple who owns the cafe, and when we came back for breakfast they remembered us immediately. They welcomed us back and even joked about how I didn’t have to run up the hill this time 😂. I absolutely loved how personable and genuine they were.

10/10 place to eat and visit if you’re new to or touring San Francisco. Amazing food, amazing people, amazing atmosphere. This place will never disappoint

Place was awesome and definitely one to check out if you have the time. Cindy my server seemed to really enjoy her job and it showed. The coffee had great flavor. My veggie omelet had lots of flavor and was stuffed full of fresh veggies other than the mushroom which I believe were from a can.

Stopped by for a solo breakfast and had a great experience. The staff were friendly and welcoming, making it an easy and comfortable spot to dine alone.

I ordered the steak and eggs, and it was absolutely delicious. The steak was tender and flavorful, the eggs were cooked perfectly, and the entire dish was satisfying and well prepared. I also had a coffee, which was excellent and paired perfectly with the meal.

Everything I ordered was great, and the quality of both the food and service really stood out. I’d happily return the next time I’m in the area.

went there for lunch and honestly I could not why anyone would go back like EVER. the food was bland and the naan was hard as a rock I had to soak it in water just to chew. we waited over 20 minutes for someone to even take our order and nobody was even that busy. then they brought out someone elses food to our table and just stood there while we tried to explain they had the WRONG order. server just shrugged and walked away without saying sorry. worst meal Ive had in a long time definately not going back again.

Loved this restaurant pre-covid. Always Went for the lunch buffet. Back then it was just $15 per person, all you can eat (now $21.99 each/ “thanks a lot” CA inflation). Pre-covid You could even get a take out container to fill if you wanted to buy the buffet food to-go. Went this week 1/7/26 and I brought my dad, who has never tried Indian cuisine before. I thought it would be a good way for him to try different dishes to see what he likes. Well it was disappointing. A majority of the dishes offered were so spicy-hot that our mouths were on fire! It made it hard to enjoy the flavors of each dish. We could barely get through the 1st plate because only a couple choices were mild enough to enjoy. Our 2nd plate was carefully selected mild choices like fruit and the 2-3 lightly fried veggy options. In all my previous years of enjoying the India Palace buffet I have never had this experience with food so spicy! We both left very disappointed. I don’t think it gave my dad a good impression or encourage him to try Indian food again. Sad because in the past I have “highly recommended” India Palace to many friends and business colleagues.

The live band was truly the cherry on top. And might I add… they poured complimentary glasses of celebratory champagne for the whole restaurant. I felt spoiled! Can’t wait to come back.

Went in with zero expectations and left planning my next visit.

Stopped by Tacos Mi Rancho near Lake Merritt and honestly didn’t know what to expect. From the outside, it looks like a straightforward taco truck, but wow was I surprised.

I ordered the Carnitas Super Taco, which came loaded with lettuce, cheese, cilantro, onions, sour cream, and guacamole. Everything was fresh, well seasoned, and packed with flavor. My only complaint? You only get one taco per order because I definitely could’ve eaten another.

The Kid ordered the Carne Asada Super Taco and before we even pulled away, she was asking for a second one. That’s usually a pretty good sign.

We also tried the horchata and jamaica, and both were delicious. The horchata was creamy and flavorful, while the jamaica was refreshing and not overly sweet.

What surprised me most was how quickly they got the food out, especially considering how popular this spot seems to be.

A few things to know:

* Cash or Venmo only
* Parking can be a challenge, but it’s worth it
* Keep an eye out for the new speed cameras in the area

Their hours are another plus:
Monday–Sunday: 9:30 am- midnight

Overall, this was one of those pleasant surprises that reminds you not to judge a place by appearances. Definitely looking forward to coming back.
Was excited to try this place. Tacos were very average. It just doesn't compare to some of the other great taco spots in Oakland.
Hard to find carne Asada fries around Oakland decided to try this place and they did not upset. Presentation and flavor was amazing. First timer and they gained me as a regular customer.

This place is very, very popular and is a town Hit. Now with that being said. Make sure the lady on the right side makes your order correctly? A good vegetarian or vegan meal is hard to find outside of this community. I had an offer to do business with this restaurant and I agreed. The restaurant goers mostly ordered take out. When they give you the second bill after scanning your card, there is no details on the charges and it still suggests tip amounts and has a section for it as if you haven't already paid for gratuity. Luckily, I noticed something off and asked what their "service charge" is before deciding on a tip.
Their system is deceptive and most likely people are double tipping all the time. My photos attached for reference to this.

top_reviews.content:
Really impressed with Pho 2000. I ordered the large Phở Đặc Biệt, a Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk, and a Thai iced tea, and everything was very good.

The pho was the highlight. The broth was flavorful and comforting, the portion was generous, and the combination of different beef cuts made it a great choice if you want to try a little bit of everything. It was also a breezy, overcast, foggy San Francisco evening in the low 60s, which made a hot bowl of pho feel absolutely perfect.

The Vietnamese coffee was strong, rich, and sweet, and the Thai iced tea was creamy and refreshing.

Overall, great food, generous portions, and a very satisfying meal. I would definitely come back to Pho 2000.

My daughter and I stopped by Pho 2000 after a show at the Orpheum Theater, and we're glad we did! The restaurant was packed when we arrived, which is always a good sign, but we were seated quickly. The staff was incredibly friendly, and the complimentary hot tea was the perfect start to the meal. The pho was absolutely delicious, and the prices were surprisingly affordable. Great food, great service, and great value. We'll definitely be back!

Pho 2000 is a no-nonsense hole-in-the-wall Vietnamese spot that is not especially fancy or polished, but it is serving up piping hot, flavorful bowls of pho that absolutely hit the spot. The staff were all super friendly and very prompt with things like water, tea, and bussing dirty plates and bowls, which I really appreciated.

I ordered the #3, the beef pho with rare steak, well-done flank, tendon, and tripe. I tried the broth on its own first and it had a nice depth of flavor before I added my usual dashes of hoisin and sriracha. I also ordered the rare steak on the side since I hate when it gets overcooked, and it was a good test of how hot the soup was when the slices started to turn that perfect light pink gradually as it continued to simmer in the broth.

I liked the pieces of tendon and tripe that were in the bowl, but honestly there could have been a lot more of both since those are some of my favorite bites of pho. The goi cuon, or shrimp and pork spring rolls, were pretty standard and decently fresh, though I'm not sure I'd order them again given the price as they were effectively 2 long rolls cut into 6 pieces for over $10.

Overall, this is a great spot if you're just looking to scratch a quick pho fix and happen to be in the neighborhood.

Whoever said this place has good bánh xèo: apologize to me, and I will take you to a better place. It was the worst bánh xèo I’ve had in my entire life. It was thick, wet, undercooked and unseasoned dough. Slimy and completely flavorless. I was genuinely confused. I’ve never had bad bánh xèo before, and I order it at every Vietnamese restaurant that serves it. How do you mess up a fried pancake?

As for the bún riêu, everything else was fine, but they used tofu that had clearly gone bad (2 out of the 4 pieces were distinctly sour, disgusting, and slimy inside). The bún bò Huế had good broth, but the amount of meat was disappointing, with very little variety in protein. I had been looking forward to coming here. I won’t be back.

I went here for the first time and it was an amazing experience. The food was incredible , especially the pho. The broth was so rich and flavorful, it really stood out.

What impressed me just as much as the food was the service. Our server carried the hot bowl of pho like it was nothing , I touched it for a second and it was really hot, so I was honestly amazed!

The staff made us feel so welcome and taken care of. Our server was very attentive, and even the manager came by to check on us, helped fix our plates, and made sure everything was perfect. That level of care made us feel really special.

If you’re looking for a solid, no-fuss pizza spot in San Francisco, Happy King’s Pizza absolutely delivers. 🍕

The pizza itself is the real star—crispy crust, flavorful sauce, and generous toppings without being over-the-top. Every bite hits that perfect balance of cheesy, savory, and satisfying. Whether you’re grabbing a slice on the go or ordering a whole pie to share, it’s consistently good.

What I really appreciate is the value—you get great quality without breaking the bank, which is rare in the city. It’s the kind of place you find yourself coming back to again and again.

Highly recommend if you’re in the area and craving a classic, delicious slice. 🍕🔥

Trash! Never been so disappointed by a pizza spot in SF. It's not made clear by the sign but the only style of pizza by the slice is pepperoni. The pepperoni were cupped full of grease as you might be able to see in my video. The vibe inside just felt sad as nobody looked like they enjoyed life! I wasn't given or told where to get napkins but I literally looked at everyone's table which had a roll of paper towels. The only reason why I didn't give them 1 star was because it beats paying $20 for a slice of pizza inside the ballpark! The portion was good and the price was right but please tell me this was just a fluke accident.

You can feel the love coming from a family type of restaurant. Great, friendly friends who were willing to go above and beyond to cook up a fresh slice when they had run out! They were so kind, knowing that were wasn’t much food around late, so they offered to cook one on the spot. Delicious and great portion size! Gotta try the paneer tikka pizza!

terrible pizzas and the person in counter was extremely rude. plus dirty washrooms. I wonder if the other reviews are paid folks because this is the second time i found the pizzas terrible. shouldn’t have come again. Avoid this place at all costs

We really enjoyed our meal at Wojia Hunan! The fresh boiled spicy fish was definitely the highlight — the fish was so tender and literally melted in your mouth. The pork ribs were crispy on the outside and tender and flavorful inside.

We ordered
1.Yang Chow Fried Rice  $25.95
2.Eggplant with String Beans  $25.95
3. Braised Pig Feet & Chicken Feet  $26.95
4. Glutinous Rice Balls (peanut filling)  $18.95
