The only downside was that they seemed pretty understaffed. We had to wait a while before anyone came to take our order. But honestly, all the food was really good. My favorite was definitely the eggplant with string beans, so flavorful and really well cooked. I also liked that you can ask for lower sodium dishes if you want. I would want to come back again to try other things on the menu.

This Hunan Restaurant offers a delicious and satisfying dining experience. The sticky rice pork ribs are tender and flavorful, while the green beans and eggplant are perfectly seasoned and rich in taste. The spicy lamb skewers are also a standout, bursting with bold flavor. Don’t miss the brown sugar ziba — it’s soft, sweet, and aromatic. The restaurant has a clean, traditional atmosphere that adds to the charm. I’ll definitely be coming back again!

Wojia is my favorite hunanese restaurant in the Bay area. Will definitely be back again and again.

The food is spicy and has good wok hei.

Farmers bowl is my favorite with mushroom, jalapenos, pork and egg.

The dan dan noodles are nice but skimp a little on the pork. The sauce is delicious tho.

The Kung Pao chicken was a tad sweet but still yummy. No cornstarch coating. No deep frying.

The water chestnut, broccoli and lilly was nice to cut the spice.

The human lamb was soft. The meat is velveted but not coated with starch which I prefer. Same with the Kung Pao chicken.

They don't have a parking lot.

This past weekend, I tried this place for the first time and ordered a vegan margherita pizza and fries for pickup. When I got home, I realized it was missing basil, which is a pretty key part of that style of pizza.

I called right away, and the staff was polite and offered to remake it, either that night or if I brought the pizza back within the next couple of days. I appreciated that they were willing to fix it, but having to hold onto the pizza and bring it back later felt a bit inconvenient—especially with a busy schedule. In my experience, many places are a bit more flexible and will honor a remake or refund with just a receipt or even a photo.

I did try a slice hoping it would still be decent, but unfortunately it just wasn’t good. The flavor really missed the mark, especially for a vegan option.

On a positive note, the staff was friendly and professional, which I do appreciate. I just think there’s some room for improvement in both quality (at least for the vegan margherita pizza) and how issues like this are handled for customers who can't easily return.

Not the best first experience especially after spending $45 for pizza and fries.  Customer service is very important in any restaurant business, therefore, if they can't make this right, I'm sure that was our last time ordering from there.
The shop is very clean and modern, very nice interior design and atmosphere. The pizza is amazing, owner is very friendly. I would highly recommend this pizza place, will definitely come back again

Ordered this twice on our trip. It is so good. I highly recommend. Some of the best pizza we've had. We had it delivered to our hotel. We stuck with cheese and sausage both times. Amazing. We got the 20 inch and it fed 9, 2 girls and 7 adults.

Our group thoroughly enjoyed the wide variety of pizzas offered at this restaurant. The menu features options for every preference, from classic cheese pizzas to vegetarian selections, hearty meat-lovers’ pies, and even creatively crafted Indian-inspired pizzas. Each pizza was thoughtfully prepared, with fresh ingredients and well-balanced flavors that kept everyone coming back for more. The diversity of options allowed each member of our party to find something they loved, making it an ideal choice for gatherings. The combination of quality ingredients, inventive flavor profiles, and consistently delicious execution makes this spot a standout for pizza enthusiasts. Whether you’re dining with friends, family, or colleagues, the variety and flavor ensure a satisfying and memorable experience. This restaurant is highly recommended for anyone seeking both traditional and innovative pizza options that deliver on taste and creativity.

I’m so impressed with this vegan selection pizza restaurant — everything tastes unbelievably fresh, and you can truly tell they take pride in what they do. The moment you take your first bite, you notice how thoughtfully crafted every part of the pizza is.

The standout for me is definitely the dough. The texture is perfectly chewy, soft, and so flavorful that you could honestly enjoy the bread by itself. It has that satisfying bite that you only get from dough made fresh in-house. It’s light yet still hearty, and it holds all the toppings beautifully without ever becoming soggy.

The flavors are bold, vibrant, and so unique. The Indian spices blend seamlessly with classic pizza elements, creating something comforting but exciting at the same time. Every topping tastes fresh — the vegetables are crisp, the sauces are well-balanced, and the cheese melts into everything so harmoniously. You can tell they don’t cut corners on ingredients.

Even though the shop isn’t huge, everything feels welcoming, warm, and made with care. The staff is friendly, the service is quick, and the quality is consistently excellent every time I visit. It’s the kind of place you immediately want to introduce to your friends.

If you’re looking for delicious vegan-style pizza with exceptional freshness and a crust that’s chewy, soft, and full of flavor, this spot is absolutely worth checking out. One bite and you’ll understand why so many people love it!

You can order your pizza at the counter, and the staff brings it to you in a laid-back and friendly manner.

June’s Pizza has been serving delicious pizzas for two years now. They have their own small parking lot and are open every evening until midnight. I can’t wait to return and explore their other pizzas and slices.

⭐⭐⭐⭐☆

June’s Pizza is a welcome addition to the neighborhood, and it’s easy to see why it’s so popular. The restaurant was very busy during our visit, with pizzas constantly moving through the assembly line and coming out of the oven at a steady pace. The staff was friendly, and it’s great to have another local pizza option nearby.

We ordered a Margherita pizza to go. The pizza itself was solid, but it wasn’t my favorite, especially considering the price. It felt a bit expensive for what you get.

One thing to be aware of if you’re ordering takeout: they call your name once when your pizza is ready and then set it on the pickup counter. There’s no warmer, and they don’t call your name again, so you’ll want to pay close attention to avoid your pizza sitting out longer than necessary.

Overall, it’s a good neighborhood spot with friendly service and a lively atmosphere. While the pizza didn’t quite justify the price for me, I’d still be open to trying some of their other offerings in the future.

Popular pizza place in West Oakland. Two-item menu. Usually a busy place with long line but efficient and quick.
Pizza is OK. For me, too much tomato sauce made it acidic taste with eggplant aftertaste.
Sourdough crust with kinda wood-burning oven is great though.
Indoor searing with very limited odor tables.
Limited parking spots shared with next door bar. Free street parking available.
Good for small groups, couples and not easy with kids.

I read the reviews and finally gave this place a try.
Casual spot with table and bar counter seating by the kitchen.
Cool decor.
Friendly staff.
Service was fairly quick at about a 10-15 min wait with 6 orders ahead of me.
XL pizza only (8 large slices) and each one is a meal.
Marg and Pepp were the only options besides a 1/2 & 1/2 combo.
Pizza tastes great, good mix of sauce, cheese and basil plus pepp, if you choose.
This is a definite spot worthy of a visit!

We had such a great time at June's! I love how simple the menu is, only offering three pizzas: margherita, pepperoni, and a rotating seasonal option. The staff were friendly and efficient. They answered my questions about allergens in the dipping sauces. Hooray for tree nut-free pesto! 🎉🍻

The ambiance was pretty rad too. The space has such tall ceilings that, although the tables are pretty crammed together, it didn't feel very cramped at all. The yellow tile on the pizza oven and the overall aesthetic of the place are really lovely.

The pizza was absolutely delicious. We particularly enjoyed the seasonal option, which had zucchini, green onion, and some other tasty toppings. The star of the show, though, was the pesto dipping sauce we got on the side.

We also had the steak which was also perfect, and the fresh arugula and Parmesan side made it delightful. Excellent wine list, classy service and elegant atmosphere. Perfect place for a special dinner.

We really enjoyed every bites of their food and the moment we interacted with the attentive staffs. It became our favorite in the area. During our 4 nights visit to Berkeley, we came here for dinner twice. The wooden patio in the nice North Berkeley made our dinning experience even more special!

Every dish that I ordered was outstanding.
The steak (bistecca) is phenomenal—much better than many Michelin-starred steakhouses I have been to in San Francisco.
The only downside for me was that, as a European, I prefer to take my time and enjoy my meal, but the service felt rushed. Our dishes arrived almost immediately after we ordered.

The food was incredible, crostini and the pasta were my favorites. The potatoes and eggplant were a pass for me personally. It was very loud and crowded inside the restaurant, we had reservations and were seated late. Also had to wait a long time for waters so I would recommend a reservation for sure on a weekend. $200 for everything pictured including tax + tip.

top_reviews.content:
I absolutely adore this place! I’ve been coming here for roughly 5 years and the food is absolutely scrumptious! I’m a creature of habit, so my go-to bowl of noodles here is the Chongqing Street Noodles. It’s so hearty and flavorful with the most deliciously chewy hand pulled noodles! I also love the peanuts and they make it perfectly spicy when I request for it. Also, the prices are super reasonable and the portions are ample.

It’s never super busy and they have searing both inside and outside. The lady who takes orders is super sweet and efficient. I love the robot that brings the food to the table! It’s always a hoot to watch. All in all, this is some of the best and most unique noodle soup that you’ll find in Oakland! I love it to pieces!

Unfortunately, this was our first and last visit to this noodle bar.

Vibe/Atmosphere: It was a sunny mid-day, and the indoor seating is so dark that makes you doubt if there's a power outage or if the restaurant is open. We took the outdoor seating, and there's dirty water at the bottom of both the bench and the table...

Service: We ordered noodles only, but the waitress kept asking if we want snacks, appetizers, drinks... To a point it started making us uncomfortable. And then we waited for 20+ min for two bowls of noodle soup, which would have taken 5 min in most noodle places. The robotic server also didn't make sense: the restaurant itself is small enough, and it was quiet enough for a real human to serve. What it did was adding another minutes for you to start eating, and you have to stand up and press on the touch screen after unloading the hot bowls yourself.

Food: Mediocre seems to be an overrate here. The noodle itself is ok, and that's probably the most positive thing I can say. Chongqing noodle being their signature dish was not Chongqing at all. The broths taste like MSG and the water-down instant noodle soup. While they were pretty generous with the noodle, the amount of meat is minimal. At $20 out-the-door price range, this is 0% authenticity and 100% disappointment. There are much better options if you go two more blocks into Chinatown. Or even just buy yourself a good pack of instant noodle - both faster and better.

Chewy hand shaven noodles, perfectly bouncy in every bite.  The spicy soup is delicious as well.  Recommend the chongqing street noodles.  Also the green bean is overpriced but comes with generous serving and it's flavored with some kind of may dried shrimp or dried scallops not sure but it's bomb.  Best greenbeen I have ever eaten. (Sorry no pictures)

Small but mighty shop serving up delicious noodle dishes within Swan’s Market! Highly recommend the Chongqing Street noodles (as soup but can also be dry) and the pig ears with garlic were surprisingly good, even though that part of a pig is not one you think of as a meal - they did it right!

Good place for a quick bite. The atmosphere and service are no frills, but the food is quite tasty.

We ordered the Chongqing Street Noodle (D11) and the Noodle with twice-cooked pork (D10). The portion sizes were good, but there was very little protein in either bowl. Aside from that, the noodles had a nice bounce to them and the broth was flavorful. Just beware that both were a bit spicy if you are sensitive to heat.

top_reviews.content: This is the first time I've captured photos of all food items for a review. Normally, I don't hold out on the grub down. I was staying at Hotel Julian next door and fell in love with this place! The girls were so sweet and made the best sandwiches and wraps. The Cuban should be permanently on the menu! Highly recommend!
The food at Bite is absolutely delicious! ❤️ Fresh, flavorful, beautifully prepared, and every bite feels so satisfying. A wonderful place for a truly tasty meal.

Ordered a recommendation from the employee behind the counter, it was a good sandwich with plenty of fillings, slightly over sauced hence the 4 stars. They also have a nice little beer selection as well as sodas and agua frescas.

This is one place I eat almost once a week. google.description: Thai standby provides a standard lineup of favorites in a functional setting. Open late.

top_reviews.content:
The Noodle is a fantastic Thai restaurant that brings authentic Thai food to Berkeley. It's small and casual, making it a really great place to bring your friends. It's also delicious and affordable, making the food addictive. My family and I have eaten here many times for all those reasons.

The menu at the Noodle is extensive, so much so that it is hard to pick a favorite. I've been here enough to summarize the following menu highlights. The fried spring rolls, fried calamari, and larb are the best appetizers I've had in this town. The Pad Thai and Pad Se Ew here are fresh-tasting, delicious noodles you've got to try. If you can handle a little spice, then try the Pad Kee Mao as well. If you like fried chicken, the fried rice with fried chicken and the crispy mango chicken are incredible! And I would also recommend a tase of the Massaman Gai curry before you top everything off with the fried ice cream or the sticky sweet rice with mango.

Some lesser known but still enticing menu items include the Khao Soi (which is great with their gluten free fried chicken) and the Lord of Noodles. Both of these are solid main courses you may or may not have tried elsewhere, made with the Noodle's signature Thai style. As for lesser known appetizers, try the Tom Kha soup, the Thai fish cakes, the chicken satay (which are totally addictive), and the papaya salad. These are not so famous but are very interesting choices.

This summer, they are adding Ka Na Moo Korb (pork belly with Chinese broccoli and egg) and cheesecake with Mitchell ice cream. I'm a real fan of these new options!

If you haven't tried the Noodle yet, I would definitely try it. Everything on the menu is so good. I know I'll be back for more!
A very clean place to grab lunch or dinner with 3-5 friends. Plan ahead for larger groups. Food was average but high quality dinnerware they serve in. Cleanliness top notch. Large portion size.

A wonderful find, light fresh food like Thai should be.
I looked in on the other Thai restaurants in the area but mostly looked hyped. This was the real deal which you could tell from the clientele and the footfall picking up for take out.
I always go for the Laab, as it’s a good test of authenticity and freshness, this did not disappoint. The people were lovely and the service was efficient, a superb light and very tasty meal!

No complaints about the service; they were quick and very friendly.

Unfortunately, I was not the biggest fan of the food. The green curry noodles came with vermicelli, and I wanted to try it since it’s what they recommend, but it just was not the right texture for the curry I felt. The flavor of the curry itself was not super flavorful. I felt like more coconut milk could have been added to coat the noodles more. The spring rolls were good. I enjoyed the peanut sauce. We also sat at the front by the door, and it was rather cold in that seat.

Food was great and the service was quick, efficient, and very friendly. The staff made the experience even better with their welcoming attitude. The place was clean and well-maintained, creating a comfortable environment to enjoy a meal. It’s a perfect spot whether you’re looking for a quick bite on the go or want to sit down and dine in. Overall, a solid choice for a casual and satisfying meal.

reviews_snippets.content: "Nice place with a great service and very well cooked plates."
"Great food, large potion size, friendly staff and good environment."
"Nice little eatery, ordered a rice dish."

name: Ming's Tasty
address: 940 Webster St, Oakland, CA 94607, United States

google.name: Ming's Tasty
google.address: 940 Webster St, Oakland, CA 94607, United States
google.description: Traditional Chinese dishes are available to eat in or take out at this no-nonsense venue.

top_reviews.content:
A friend of ours told us to try this place, and since we were passing by, why not.
We had to wait outside for about 10 minutes since the place was already packed. Service was quick and the food came out piping hot. The menu was quite extensive. We settled for 10 dishes.
Our absolute favorites were the Snowy Baked BBQ Pork Buns, Beef Tripe, and the fresh Roll Noodle with Shrimp. Honestly, everything was delicious, but our least favorite was the Salted Fish Clay Pot Rice. The salted fish was a bit bland and the portion was rather small. It was also overpriced.
We tried the Crispy Durian Puff. If you like Durian, you'll appreciate this dish. If you don't like durian, don't sit next to the person who's eating it because you can really smell it! 🫢

We ordered a lot! Everything here is really great and I would come here all the time if I could. Ming’s Tasty dim sum is one of the best in the Bay Area. You can taste the freshness of the dishes and it really shows. Their service and turnaround is relatively quick and efficient. We ordered the black bean pork spare ribs, chicken feet, siu mai, shrimp dumplings, meat-stuffed snow bun, shrimp rice rolls, fried turnip cake, and fried stuffed meat dumplings. All of their food is pretty good, but some of the must-try dishes here are the shrimp rice rolls and the fried stuffed meat dumplings. Best to come with a larger party, so you can try it all!

Good & cheap eats for Dim Sum in the heart of downtown Oakland.
Dim Sum here always cook fresh & hot when you ordered.
The claypot rice is good but too expensive.  Only has 4 pieces of chicken & 1 piece of black mushroom, lol, for almost $16.
Downside: The menu is smaller compared to other restaurants.  The wait is very long here since it’s a small restaurant.  The restaurant is always packed, especially at lunch time, weekends, & holidays.
It’s small, packed, & very noisy. So, not recommended for relaxing or big family gatherings. The waitresses here are crazily noisy. They always screaming & yelling around, adding the extra noises to the noisy restaurant, & making the environment very intense.
Recommend: 1st time here, ✍️ your name on the wait list, while waiting for your table, get the menu & filled what you want to order right away, once you get your table, just hand the filled menu to the waitress so you can get your food ready soon.

I went last week as a recommendation after having my blood drawn just a few blocks away. I had the shrimp dumplings, wonton noodle soup and the pork bun. I thoroughly enjoyed myself. I went early (around 11am) and it was packed. I was accommodated a seat at a shared table. The service is friendly and efficient. The food was all hot tasty and affordable.  I spent less than 30 for everything.  I didn't have any trouble with parking - parked at a meter.

Favorites were the custard bun, pea sprout dumpling (not pictured), rice noodle roll with fried shrimp, and snowy baked bbq pork bun! Pork & shrimp dumpling siu mai were nice and big, a bit on the salty side!
Friendly service!

reviews_snippets.content: "Fantastic and well-priced food accompanied by great service."
"The salted fish was a bit bland and the portion was rather small."

google.name: Mujiri

top_reviews.content: Very small sushi spot, with a few tiny tables inside, one outside on the sidewalk, and a few seats at the counter. Mostly sashimi and nigiri (a few salads too). Mochi and cheesecakes for desserts. Everything was great, ingredients (some terrific fat fishes) and cooking. And the sake menu is one of the best I've seen in the area, including a sake flight. Not the best option for a cheap feast, but with that in mind, absolutely recommended.

Extremely authentic sushi place that doesn’t skimp. Sushi were already seasoned perfectly when they hit the table. Nigiri combo allows you do choose 7 different nigiri from their list which is amazing value, which also comes with a set of maki rolls which were great. $28. Last lunch seating is 2:00 which is strictly enforced.
Excellent value for the quality. The sashimi is very fresh and the sushi rice was perfectly seasoned. The space could be nicer, but the food makes it worth visiting. 10/10.

My partner and I had just finished playing Dave the Diver one night and got a massive sushi craving, so we looked up nearby spots and found this place. We enjoyed it so much that we came back the very next day，this time for takeout. The packaging was really nice, the prices are a great deal, and the flavors are legit. Pretty sure this is going to be our go-to sushi takeout spot from now on.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
The fish here is beyond delicious.  It’s the kind of meal you have and then wake up craving again.  Spectacularly simple but impressively memorable.

reviews_snippets.content: "This place is a hole in the wall with excellent food and excellent service."
"Small sushi spot with a friendly staff and good sushi!"
"Ordered the trio and the first bit was probably the best thing I ate all week."

name: LIMEWOOD BAR & RESTAURANT
address: 41 Tunnel Rd, Berkeley, CA 94705, United States

google.name: LIMEWOOD BAR & RESTAURANT
google.address: 41 Tunnel Rd, Berkeley, CA 94705, United States
google.description: Refined Californian–New American stop with wine & cocktails offered in stylish, comfy environs.

top_reviews.content:
We arrived at 7:45 AM. Parking is accessible immediately adjacent to the entrance, eliminating long pedestrian transit from the vehicle. Note on the parking procedure: upon parking, you must scan the barcode on the sign in the parking lot and fill out your information; later, when you receive your dining receipt at the end of the meal, scanning the barcode provided on that receipt zeros out the parking fee before you exit the property. However, as we walked from the parking lot toward the hotel entrance, the outdoor fire pit and lounge areas were left in a messy state from the previous night or shift, featuring unbusied glassware, empty bottles, stray beverage containers, and rumpled throws left completely unmanaged well before opening. Inside, the Claremont maintains a classic, historic aesthetic. The restaurant entrance is located just inside the hotel on the left, and service doors opened promptly at 8:00 AM.

We were seated at a window table with a clear, elevated view of San Francisco in the distance. Water was provided immediately, and order intake followed shortly after. The latte was functional but lacked depth; an additional shot would have improved flavor balance, though it remained enjoyable.

I ordered the Signature Breakfast with scrambled eggs, country potatoes, and chicken apple sausage, alongside a side of grilled sourdough. Execution across the plates was solid: the scrambled eggs were properly cooked, the potatoes were well-prepared, and the chicken apple sausage was flavorful with a balanced, mild sweetness. The side of grilled sourdough outperformed expectations, as the char added strong structural flavor. My dining companion's order, consisting of fried eggs, potatoes, and thick, chewy bacon, was reported as excellent across all metrics.

Service ran smoothly during the initial phase, with the waitress performing a midpoint check-in, and secondary staff efficiently clearing plates. However, post-clearance follow-through lapsed toward the end of the meal, as no staff returned to the table, requiring an approximate 12-minute wait before attention could be actively flagged to request the check.

Overall, food quality sits above average, and the combination of historic room architecture and unobstructed valley views adequately justifies the pricing structure.

I visited for the first time to attend my friend’s birthday dinner, and this stunning restaurant truly impressed me! Located inside the beautiful Clairmont hotel, it offers a spectacular sunset view over the bay. The staff is friendly and attentive, and the food quality is good. The atmosphere is elegant and upscale, but there is no dress code, so guests can dress casually or more formally. We came on a Saturday evening and there were still a few parking spaces available. There's a charge for parking based on hours parked.
Fancy little restaurant in the hotel with exceptional view to the tennis courts and SF bay. Service was excellent, the food was just ok.

Took my best friend here for a belated birthday celebration and definitely treated ourselves! Drinks were yummy, and portions were pretty fair. Food was decadent, though you definitely are paying a bit more for the ambiance. Go during golden hour and sunset for great photo ops and lighting, just don’t forget your sunnies 🌞

Beautiful views, very attentive service. The drinks were great, we shared a couple of small plates: corn and octopus. Spilt the pork entree so that we had room for the chocolate cake and strawberry torte for dessert

reviews_snippets.content: "Good prices, relative to the area and services provided, for food and drinks."

top_reviews.content:
Chef Yosuke and his culinary team made our night very special.

Simple and delicious food, beautiful restaurant, great selection of Italian wines, and delicious cocktails.

Dolce Whisper or Dolce Whisperer? I can't rememberbthe name 😁, but that cocktail was so good.

100% recommended!

I ate here yesterday with my husband for the first time and it was very tasty.

We marked close by in the neighborhood. It was easy for us to find. I’m not sure what people are referring to when talking about windows getting smashed in a parking lot? But I did see broken glass in the library’s parking lot next door? FYI.

The food though was excellent. We got the fried olives, beet salad, pork chop, pasta dish (with crab and shrimp), tiramisu, and vanilla gelato.

My favorite was the beet salad (so refreshing!),
any of their house made pasta looks amazing, and the tiramisu was excellent.

Definitely would come again. Maybe next time I will consider doing their Oakland Restaurant deal which looked amazing but I couldn’t resist trying their pasta with the seafood :)

Fried olives were so good I almost choked to death, pizzas are good, just go ahead and order everything. Salmon was my fave! Finished with strong coffee and tiramisu. Drinks are all tasty as well. Staffs all super cool and the art they have up is dope!

A16 is Southern Italian food meets California. In a good way! The pizzas are excellent, with the true Neapolitan oven, especially recommended is the Montanara pizza which is briefly fried before being put in the pizza oven. Excellent also the appetizers, especially the squid with fried beans. And outstanding choice of Sicilian wines.

Almost every time we're in Berkeley, we come here as a family to eat. We had two college undergraduates, and typically end up celebrating most occasions here. Lots of options including vegetarian, vegan, friendly dishes. The salmon is perfectly crispy, moist, flavorful on a bed of vegetables. The pizzas, and specifically the pizza dough, are perfectly light, chewy, and flavorful. This place is such a vibe, and highly recommended if you're ever near the area.

reviews_snippets.content: "Excellent service and food of dining out of having a good time of eating pizza."
"The salmon is perfectly crispy, moist, flavorful on a bed of vegetables."

top_reviews.content:
Zevi Café was my first meal in San Francisco, and I couldn’t have picked a better place to start the trip. The food was delicious — a mix of Turkish dishes and American favorites.

It’s a family-owned business, and our waiter kindly shared the story behind the restaurant and even gave us a few recommendations for our stay in San Francisco, which made the experience feel very personal.

The portions are quite large — neither my best friend nor I could finish our plates — so sharing might be a good idea.

PS: The prices are also very reasonable.

Avocado toast was not tasty. Looked like the avocado spread was from a package. Shakshuka was not ok either. The cheese in it smelled bad and tomatoes were not fresh. They were from a can. Shakshuka did not have cilantro. Bread was like sponge. Coffee was bad too.

Poached were good though.

Amazing spot!The dishes were bursting with authentic flavor and everything tasted incredibly fresh. The mantı had the perfect balance of spices and sauce, the cheese pide was crisp on the outside and soft inside, and the kibbeh over yogurt and tomato was honestly one of the best I’ve tried. The hummus and warm bread were also outstanding and made the whole meal even better.
Huge appreciation to Chef Saim — his craftsmanship shows in every detail, from presentation to taste. You can tell he truly cares about the quality of the food he serves. A place I’ll definitely come back to💕
Pretty good place for breakfast. The cappuccino was very strong. I enjoyed the hollandaise sauce a lot. It was a little loud but not that you couldnt hear the people you were with.
Staff is extremely friendly and played with the kids while cheerfully serving food the whole time. The food was flavorful and tasty. The restaurant is light and bright and spacious.

reviews_snippets.content: "Choice of many dishes, quality food and excellent service."
"The place is spotlessly clean, credit to the owner and management."
"Finished everything on my plate cuz it was sooo tasty."

top_reviews.content:
Tasty Five Spice Chicken Pho, perfectly boiled rice noodles served with flavorful chicken broth and crispy skin Five Spice Chicken thigh.

A good Marina option that hits the spot when seeking flavors Vietnamese. Interior neither striking nor the most light-filled.

Restaurant was an absolute blast. The food was so good. It was a little bit noisy but I think we can get past that. Busy means good right and Food I would recommend the Beef and The potstickers. The service was amazing and we just left with four stomachs so yeah bye.

Considering the area, the menu makes sense for their customers. The food was okay, average. But it’s not the place for authentic Vietnamese cuisine.
The pho broth was okay, but the lack of herbs for topping were unfortunate. I had to ask for bean sprouts and received cilantro with it. I was hoping for Thai Basil’s and ngo gai (culantro), but they did not have it.
The garlic noodles with filet mignon were quite tasty, a little too salty. The filet mignon was a bit overcooked. Broccoli was an unusual addition to the dish but worked well. The nuoc mam (fish sauce) did not go well with the beef.  Typically, lime juice with salt and pepper is served with shaken beef.
Service was great, although some staff don’t speak Vietnamese. They all speak English though. You may even see the owner’s children helping around the restaurant!

Vermicelli noodles lacked bean sprouts and standard herbs (mint, cilantro, basil): lettuce seems to be the only greenery and pineapple (?) was involved. Fresh shrimp rolls also lacked herbs, peanut sauce was watery and flavorless. Added tons of sri racha and hoisin to no avail. Imperial rolls were okay.
Fantastic Vietnamese food, the pho and vermicelli were both top notch. Friendly service, and a laid back vibe. 5/5

reviews_snippets.content: "Good beef satay pho and garlic noodles with five spice chicken"
"Good service good drinks good pho good spring rolls Wish there was more meat"

top_reviews.content:
Nice restaurant and bar in the Four Seasons. I’ve been coming here for years when I’m in town because of the quality food and staff.

The bartenders are very friendly and efficient.  I had the salmon crudo that had both citrus and savory accents along with the perfectly seasoned crab cakes.

I love the fact that they serve little bar snacks with your cocktail.  Very classic and appreciated.

We all know when visiting / staying at a Four Seasons property, the expectations are set. Just like any other property I’ve experienced, San Francisco did not disappoint. I came for breakfast for this particular visit. Did not disappoint. Farm fresh food, white glove service, and a relaxing yet welcoming atmosphere. Great experience from being greeted by valet until paying the bill. See you guys soon.

Walked in 10 mins prior to start of dinner was booked for a table right away and sat at the bar until it was time. From the moment we walked in until we left experienced great service from all members of the staff. Food recommendations were spot on. Will definitely return.

All of the food was amazing- Dinner was delicious. Desserts were yummy- carrot cake with crème brûlée on top was really good. The prices were a bit over the top high- perhaps it’s b/c it’s inside of a hotel.

Absolutely the best bar in all of San Francisco financial District for dinner and happy hour and lunch for the business crowd.  All the locals love this not only the residents in the neighborhood not only The Four Seasons residents!  The service here is something else absolutely hundred percent impeccable so friendly. The people here are absolutely amazing.

reviews_snippets.content: "Quiet atmosphere, excellent service, and high-quality food."

top_reviews.content:
Pintoh Thai completely exceeded my expectations! I ordered the Khao Pad Pu (Crab Fried Rice), and it was absolutely incredible. The dish was packed with flavor, but what truly took it to another level was the fresh blue crab. You can really taste the quality and freshness in every bite it elevated the entire dish and made it one of the best Thai meals I've had in a long time.

Beyond the amazing food, the restaurant itself is super cute, warm, and welcoming. It has that special charm you only find in a family-owned restaurant where you can feel the love and care that goes into everything they do. It's the kind of place that makes you feel at home from the moment you walk in.

If you're looking for an authentic Thai spot that's a little hidden treasure in the city, Pintoh Thai is a must-visit. Great food, wonderful atmosphere, and a family-run feel that keeps you coming back. I can't wait to return and try more from the menu!

Got the vegan pineapple fried rice and server asked if I'm ok with tofu and vegetables to which I said yes, however they didn't put any tofu in there. Pineapple fried rice was ok, nothing special. Thai iced tea was really good! Overall the price does not justify the taste at all.
My favorite Thai restaurant in Oakland. Depends on how busy they are, the service could be a miss and take forever. But the food is really yummy, authentic and flavorful.

This is the best Thai food I have had in the Bay Area in 10 years. We were in Oakland for a volleyball tournament and dropped in here for a quick dinner. We had the Krapao Gai (Basil Chicken) and Tom Ko Gai. Everything was amazing and flavorful. The chicken was super clean and the vegetables very fresh. I loved that the restaurant was so clean and the staff was very friendly and helpful. I can’t wait to come back again.

Pintoh did the catering for my backyard wedding and I couldn’t be happier with the food and service.  Mary was so easy to work with and responded quickly to all my many questions.  We went into Pintoh to do a tasting and then came up with a menu that all my guests ended up loving. They were right on time and helped set everything up.  We had multiple guests say it was the best Thai food they have ever had and my Thai sister in law approved as well.  Highly recommend Pintoh for catering!

top_reviews.content: Shrimp fried rice tasted word, maybe because seaweed was on top, didn’t like this rendition. Chicken wings could have been fried a little longer but did have a good taste. The chicken soup with udon middles had me in the toilet for the past two days. Spent $67.68 and I’m not happy about it. Food costs too much to not be good to me!

Came here with some friends and overall had a good time. The chicken was on the dry side, but the seasoning powder had great flavor and definitely helped. Tried the seafood pot too — contents were fine, pretty standard taste, nothing that stood out but it hit the spot.

The real highlight here is the vibe. Fun atmosphere, good energy, and a nice place to just hang out for a while. Service was friendly and the space felt lively without being too overwhelming. Not perfect on the food, but I’d still come back for the overall experience.

We arrived later in the evening and experienced a brief wait due to the restaurant’s busy pace, but the overall experience was well worth it. The staff handled the crowd efficiently, and once seated, the service was attentive and welcoming. The food was excellent, offering a wide variety of flavors that were both vibrant and well-balanced. Each dish was thoughtfully prepared and satisfying. The soju selection was another highlight—smooth and enjoyable, though deceptively easy to drink. The lively atmosphere, combined with flavorful cuisine and a well-managed service team, made for a memorable dining experience. We would gladly return and recommend this spot to others looking for great food and a fun, energetic environment.

Ordered our food at 12:10 didn’t get our food until 1:38am. We ordered a simple dish (tteokbokki). Checked in with the server three times and gave us false time all times. Tables who entered after us basically finished and paid before our food arrived. Waited about 30-40mins to get in as well.

Love the vibe here and food is fantastic. Kimchi fried rice with spam was our favorite! The chicken wings were also crispy and delicious! I personally would prefer to order some with sauce so I’ll try that next time. Price was affordable too. The booths were a great way to enjoy our meal and I think I’ll bring my toddler back because it will be nice to have the booth to kind of isolate us haha. Am planning on coming back.

Waiters were nice and helpful too.

google.description: Unassuming eatery dishing up a variety of traditional Korean dishes in a casual setting.

top_reviews.content:
+ Extremely authentic and low profile. Feels like a family style restaurant and we saw lots of native Korean families there.
+ The soup is one of the best in the Bay Area. Rich and organic flavor. We ordered beef soup with tendon and tendons are so tender and soft that it almost melt in the mouth.
+ Large portions.
+ Owners are super friendly

The soups in this eatery are the bomb - we had seolleongtang (oxtail soup) and kalbitang (rib soup with mung bean noodles), both of which were nourishingly delicious. I had them with rice and it was just the perfect meal for a chilly day.

I liked it so much that I returned the next week - we had extra yukkejang, which was spicy and tasty and also the crispy and flavourful seafood pajeon.

This place has super fresh kim chee. Food comes out quickly. Their Kim Chee and chives pancake is perfect. I don't eat meat but my husband does and he was never disappointed with his order. He really likes their soup. The only thing to flag is that their soft tofu soup comes with pork even though it isn't listed on the menu. They were very nice to switch it out once I got it. Just wanted to flag for anyone who wanted the soft tofu soup but don't eat pork. The soft tofu soup with Kim Chee (no pork) is also totally yummy
Galbijim (braised beef soup) and sundaegug (rice blood sausage soup) were great. Expensive though — I’ve had same food at highly rated restaurants in other expensive cities for ~80% the price…

My family had an amazing Father’s Day meal at Seoul GomTang! We had many of their appetizers, soups, and noodle dishes. The food was amazing as usual - we were really happy with all of it. The portions were plentiful and the service was impeccable as well.

If you’re not sure what to order, I would look on the walls or ask the very nice server for advice. The owners know their food very well and try their best to help you out!

Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone curious about Korean food. Must try!

top_reviews.content: I always get breakfast, and their scrambled eggs are the best from any restaurant I’ve been to. You can tell that they use fresh, whole eggs, not liquid!!! The vegetables and fruit always test fresh and flavorful. I’ve never been dissatisfied. I looooooovveeee

It was just before 2PM and we wanted breakfast. That's why we decided to grab a bite to eat here.
Seems they are open until 3PM and they serve breakfast every day.
The inside dining area has many tables available and I can see them being busy during a brunch weekend in that neighborhood.
We ordered cinnamon French toast with banana, a side of bacon and eggs. We also ordered a bacon croissant egg sandwich. For beverages we ordered a chai latte with an espresso shot and a regular latte.
The food came out hot and quickly.  I do love a breakfast croissant sandwich. The bacon was cooked just the way I like and the yolk was perfectly runny. I didn't try the French toast but my friend ate it up. This place isn't a fancy brunch spot but it's a hangout and they have really good food options for breakfast every day.
I'm definitely going to try to go to brunch here one weekend.

Eclectic Space and Vibe! Pet friendly always makes me smile.  Cappuccino was perfect! Butterscotch Oat bar scrumptious. Service was exceptional. Perfect place for coffee and pastry Food menu was sparse.
Great breakfast spot! Had lots of classic options and asian fusion dishes as well. The homestyle sausages was delicious, order extra when you're there.

My first time eating here. We came here on Sunday after spotting the place a month ago when we stopped by the Donut Farm.
I had to try the Jambalaya and it was pretty good and a generous portion too!

reviews_snippets.content: "Affordable yummy breakfast and lunch lots of variety good atmosphere and service"

name: Super Super Pho
address: 1428 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702, United States

google.name: Super Super Pho
google.address: 1428 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley, CA 94702, United States

top_reviews.content:
Super super pho is my go-to Vietnamese spot in Berkeley/Emeryville. And so reasonably priced.

I always get the original banh no with the pate. Soo good with the freshnwss of the herbs and acidity and sweetness of the pickled carrots and diakon.

The beef pho with 3 kinds of beef is warm and hearty. Their broth is clear and so flavorful.

Will be back again and again.

This was my husband’s and my first time trying this restaurant. When you arrive, you place your order and pay at the counter first, then take a seat in the dining area to enjoy your meal.

The prices are quite reasonable, and the food was pretty good overall. For me, the broth wasn’t as rich or flavorful as I had hoped, though they do give you a generous amount of it. The staff provided decent service — not outstanding, but not bad either.

There are several pho restaurants along this street, and this was the first one we decided to try. Overall, it wasn’t bad at all and definitely worth a visit, but it’s not quite my top favorite just yet.

Self-service, order food at the front and pay after ordering. Get your own drinks. Server will bring your food out. I got the combo pho, it was very delicious. So far the best soup/pho I had. The portion is great. Totally worth the price. Hot tea is strong and tasted great too!

Ideally, I'd give this place 2.5/5.

Usually, the Yelp reviews for a restaurant are always on point, and they've never let me down in the past, but this time, it was a different story.

Super Super Pho has a great setup for a casual dining experience. The covered patio with string lights and heaters looked inviting, and the counter service with "find your own seat" was convenient. We arrived right after opening, so there was no wait and service was very fast. Perhaps a little too fast...

Our food came out within minutes of ordering, which was concerning. Especially considering we had fried chicken wings, a dish that typically takes longer to prepare. Unfortunately, the wings were the biggest letdown. They were bland and undercooked, not crispy and flavorful like you'd expect.

The pho (super pho combination) itself was a mixed bag. The portion was generous, with plenty of meat (rare steak, well-done brisket, and beef balls). However, the broth was a major disappointment. It lacked depth of flavor and really needed a lot of doctoring with the provided condiments like lemon and Sriracha. The meat itself was also unevenly cooked - some parts were dry, others undercooked.

The Thai tea was decent. It was milky (not watered down, thankfully), but it had some chalky aftertaste.

On the plus side, the staff was friendly when we did manage to flag them down. However, with only one other table occupied during our entire visit, the inattentiveness was surprising. We had to track someone down for water and takeout boxes.

Given today's rainy weather, I was really looking forward to some comforting pho, but unfortunately, this place did not deliver.

This was my first visit, and since it was a rainy day, I decided to try their pho. There’s something comforting about a warm bowl of soup on a cold, wet day. The soup had a rich, deep flavor that was enjoyable, but not remarkable. For comparison, my favorite pho spot is still Pho Vi Hoa in Palo Alto, which I feel has more balanced and complex flavors.

Ordering here was straightforward. You place your order at the counter, and the staff delivers your food to the table. The service was efficient and friendly, which added to the overall experience.

For starters, I ordered A2: Fresh Shrimp Spring Rolls. They were fresh, light, and paired well with the accompanying peanut dipping sauce. As for the main dish, I went with the Rare Steak Pho, adding extra noodles for $2. While the broth and rare steak were satisfying, I realized the portion of noodles was already quite generous without the extra. If you’re someone with a hearty appetite, you’ll likely find the regular portion sufficient.

Next time, I’ll skip the extra noodles and focus on the base dish. It’s a solid spot for a comforting bowl of pho, but I’d still rank it below my go-to pho spot in Palo Alto.

top_reviews.content: Great food great staff and lots of screens for World Cup games. Glad to have come here to enjoy the cheers and friendly atmosphere. Oakland finally has its sports bar back and it came back better.
The Oakland Athletic Club reopened just in time for the World Cup, and it did not miss. Walking into a packed house cheering the soccer match on any of 40 TVs with 20 independent sound zones felt like exactly what this neighborhood has been missing.
The space is cleaner and sharper than before with fresh energy. Seating covers every vibe: bar stools, booths, high tables, and a mezzanine VIP area ideal for larger groups. There isn't a bad view in the house.
The upgraded menu earns serious praise. The half chicken is a standout — juicy, well-seasoned, the kind of dish that's both satisfying and comforting in the best way. The bean and rice bowl is equally impressive: fresh, hearty, and far above what you'd expect from a sports bar. Real food.
What ties it all together is the staff and management. Genuinely welcoming from the moment you walk in, and attentive throughout, even on a packed game day. You never felt like just another table.
Whether you're coming solo, on a date, or rolling in with a big group, OAC handles it all with ease. This is Oakland's living room. It's back where it belongs. Will be back there again.

So glad this place is open again! I love that all the food is locally sourced- so I know I’m supporting local businesses and eating fresh options compared to other bars. Great sports bar with great vibes. Nice place to watch college football games, soccer, etc. Family friendly with games in the back!

- I also liked the cornbread.
- Mostly it was the vibes and the huge TV screens. It was a great place to watch the game. They had like nine TVs showing the different games and everyone on the staff was super nice.

Bad:
- The portion sizes are really small on most things.
- The black beans and rice is tiny.
- Cornbread was half a portion, which I thought it was.
- It also took us over an hour for our food to get there so it takes a while. You have to be pretty patient especially if it's a busy day.

I'm just glad we found this spot that was great for the vibes of World Cup.

My only complaint would be that the crust was a little chewy/tougher than I prefer, but that was only a minor distraction from an overall awesome pizza. The left slice pairs savory, robust meat toppings with a vibrant sauce and perfectly melted cheese, while the right slice elevates simplicity with fresh, creamy dollops of burrata, fragrant basil leaves, and a touch of chili flakes. The sambar, my usual first dipstick of how good a south Indian place is, was on point. The idlis were chopped up and dusted in Kandi podi. The portions were large enough where I was full right after the idly! The egg dosa came out next and had the same appeal. The chutneys and sambar were the same for all dishes, but they were well made.

My only complaint was the use of plastic for everything and as usual the filter coffee arrived without sugar. And adding it on the table never turns out as good as the original.

They have a buy 7 dosas and get one free offer. I am considering it!

Tasty Dosas in generous portions. Great place for a healthy meal in downtown Oakland. A speakeasy style cafe in the basement of the Ramada. Atmosphere is lack luster, but the food is worth it. Will return.

Good, authentic South Indian food is hard to find. Id Cafe isn’t exactly easy to find either. It’s located at the basement level of the Ramada Inn.

However, the food is fantastic. Truly South Indian sambar, great chutneys and excellent dishes. Syed, the man behind the counter had great suggestions, was sensitive to food allergies and had great energy.

I got idly sambar (large portions) and Hyderabad bandi dosa to go. Kudos to the chef.

For a place that’s only been open for 12 days, it is racking up reviews and business.

Worth multiple visits.

top_reviews.content: Our first time and we were not disappointed with all the beautiful dishes. Our 2 servers were wonderful. Recommended some dishes to us. The banh cuon was gorgeous. Cha ca la vong was sumptuous. Wife ordered spicy pho sate togo. We will be back to explore more of the menu.

Most recently we tried some dishes outside of what we might usually order and had the fried catfish dish, the shrimp ban xeo and the vegan bo bun hue. Everything was so tasty and fresh. I couldn't believe how much flavor was in the vegan bo bun hue (I've also had the non vegan and it's very delicious as well). The beef carpaccio dish and glutinous dumplings are some other favorites. The first time we came was Tet which made it extra special! The staff is so wonderful. They can get busy but it's definitely worth the wait.

I can confidently say Tay Ho is my favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Oakland! As a Vietnamese girlie who used to live in Orange County and had homemade meals from my mom, Tay Ho has all the right flavors and you can tell it’s high quality with good ingredients.

I absolutely love clean, modern dining, so you can tell why Tay Ho is my fave spot.

Service is great, vibes are great, and now to the food.

1. Banh Cuon Dac Biet - 5/5 - so good and lots of different styles of banh cuon and sides! Super solid and always fresh. Only available before 3pm.

2. Banh Xeo - 5/5 - super crispy and lots of fillings!

3. Banh Khot - 4/5 - this was my first time actually eating Banh Khot haha it was really good! It’s a bit too much coconut cream for me but still a solid pick if you like Banh Khot.

4. Bun Cha Ha Noi - 5/5 - this is so good AND they give you more than one meatball (cause a lot of viet restaurants it’s one meatball and the rest are the other thin cut meats). Very good but also on the expensive side.

5. Bo Tai Chanh - 4/5 - this was super good but I wish the Bo Tai was separated more - just felt like it was all stuck together but flavor is AMAZING!

6. Pho Dac Biet - 5/5 - so good and you can tell the broth is super clean. Flavorful as well! Love that they have satay cause most pho places around here don’t have that…

7. Green Thai Tea - 5/5 - so good and not too sweet… perfect for me! Cause too much sugar leaves a weird feeling in my mouth.

I cannot wait to try the rest of the menu - love this place and 10/10 recommend to go for food and vibes!

This is one of my favorite Vietnamese places in Oakland- food is delicious, service is excellent, and interior is nice. Would be good for a cute little date night.
My favorite appetizer to get is the Banh Khot. Absolutely yummy! It’s crispy and has just the right amount of coconut and flavor. I’ve been here multiple times and it’s something I always order. I don’t think i’ve had anything bad from this place. Their drinks are really good as well. It’s a bit on the pricey side for Viet food, but it’s well worth for the taste and quality. Cool vibes and great food at this downtown Vietnamese establishment. There is a bar with counter seating. My favorite were the banh Khot. Recommend!

The price point is definitely a bit out of touch as well. $72 for two appetizers and one wine flight seems  bit pricey. It was good though, so I won’t complain too much on that end. top_reviews.content:
This is genuinely the BEST restaurant in all of Berkeley, and I do not say that lightly. I’ve eaten at a lot of places around here, and nothing compares to this spot. Every single time I walk in, I’m greeted by the sweetest and kindest workers I’ve ever met in Berkeley. They are always so welcoming, warm, and genuinely happy to see you, which already makes the experience feel special before you even start eating.

Now the food is absolutely incredible. The chicken tikka masala is honestly one of the best dishes I’ve had anywhere. The sauce is rich, creamy, and packed with flavor, and the chicken is always perfectly cooked and tender. It’s the kind of dish where you keep saying “just one more bite” and suddenly the whole bowl is gone. The garlic naan is also amazing, soft, warm, buttery, and perfectly garlicky. It’s literally the perfect thing to scoop up the tikka masala with. I could honestly eat the naan alone and still be happy.

And you cannot leave without getting the mango lassi. It’s so refreshing and smooth, and it balances the spices from the food perfectly. It’s sweet, creamy, and honestly one of the best mango lassis I’ve ever had.

Another thing that makes this place stand out is the price and generosity. Berkeley can be pretty expensive when it comes to food, but this restaurant somehow manages to serve amazing quality food at a really good price. On top of that, they are incredibly generous, they almost always give us extra food or something for free, which is honestly so kind and makes the experience feel even more special. It feels like they truly care about their customers and want everyone to leave happy.

What I love most is that this place feels genuine and welcoming, not just another restaurant trying to rush people in and out. The workers are so friendly and kind, and the atmosphere is always warm. You can tell they take pride in their food and care about the people who come in.

If you’re anywhere near Berkeley and want amazing Nepalese food, this is the place you have to go. The chicken tikka masala, garlic naan, and mango lassi combination is absolutely unbeatable. Great food, incredible people, generous portions, and such a great experience every time. You can NOT beat the price or quality anywhere.

I honestly recommend this place to everyone I know. 10/10 — the best restaurant in Berkeley.
Excellent!!! The BEST Indian Food in Berkeley! Must try! Chicken Tikka Masala my favvvv! Lunch specials great deal too! Mango Lassi, lemonades, chai OMG SOOO GOOD!

The food is always 10/10!! This is the best Indian food in Berkeley & I guarantee you will LOVE whatever you get. Everything is so fresh & tastes amazing. The staff here is AMAZING. They are all so kind & make the experience amazing. My favorite is the butter chicken I highly recommend!!! You need to try this place for lunch they have an amazing $11 lunch special. One of my favorite spots in berkeley!
The service was amazing! It felt so homey and the food came out so fast. The kadai chicken and momos are to die for!!!

A gem hidden in plain sight !! This place has been around since I was in high
school (over a decade) and although it seems it may be receiving less foot traffic during the summer months, this is not a restaurant to miss!
I got the lunch set with lamb curry. The meat is tender, the spice perfect, the curry flavorful and delicious. It also came with a generous portion of naan and rice, plus chana on the side and a nice salad.
The rose lassi is also a refreshing choice, not too sweet :)

Service was so wonderful, warm and helpful staff. 100/10!
For under $20 it’s a great deal for lunch and a great place to visit.
Come check it out!

top_reviews.content:
DragonEats is a no-frills shop with no seating that serves up a tight, focused menu of Vietnamese offerings, with a clear emphasis on banh mis and bún. I know they have salads, rolls and even pho on the menu, but I came specifically for the banh mi and went with the classic roast pork.

The banh mis here are on the pricier side at $11 to $13 depending on which one you order, especially given the location near the Tenderloin and all the other delicious, cheaper options nearby. That said, I did find the flavors to be very good. The roast pork was seasoned and cooked really well, and the sandwich was absolutely bursting with pickled vegetables, jalapeño, cilantro, and pate. Big shoutout to the team for offering extra of literally anything in the sandwich besides the protein for free, which definitely helps justify the higher price. The portion is huge as a result, and you could easily split a half sandwich and a small soup for lunch and be set.

The bread is sturdy, with a nice crust on the outside that does not cut into the roof of your mouth, while the inside is super fluffy and soaks up all the pate and sauce beautifully. I added a small side of broth, which I was expecting to be a simple clear consommé, but I was pleasantly surprised to find it loaded with kale in addition to the shallots, cilantro, and lime, which you can also get extra of at no charge.

Ultimately, it is not the best banh mi I have had, as the bread could be a bit crustier and the pate could use a bit more punch, but overall it was a very satisfying meal at a fair price point for the city.

I stopped at DragonEats for the first time after a couple of colleagues recommended it when I asked for a new lunch spot near our office. I wanted something I could take back to work, so I ordered the Chicken Breast Fresh Bowl.

The bowl came with rice noodles, celery, carrots, cilantro, and several other ingredients. It was fresh, flavorful, and filling without being too heavy—a good choice for a quick workday lunch.

My takeout order was ready in about five or six minutes, making the entire experience fast and hassle-free. Based on this first visit, DragonEats is a convenient option for a fresh, satisfying lunch in Hayes Valley.

We ordered roasted pork and roasted duck sandwiches. They both are very tasty and have signature pastes. The buns are well toasted and just have enough crunchiness. The rolls are also good,  very fresh. Highly recommended.

Very quick and delicious! Got a teriyaki tofu bowl which was YUM. If you are vegetarian make sure to ask for soy sauce as a replacement instead of fish sauce. Highly recommend!  Note: has peanuts in it in case anyone is allergic. But looked like it was just a topping so could ask for it without

Wonderful take out restaurant with a tiny space that has a few high chairs to eat on the premises. Two basic foods done extremely well; ban mi and salad bowls!! We had a 5 spiced chicken salad bowl and the spicy pork ban mi and both were exceptional and tasty. Total cost was $22! So if you want a quick and cheap bite, look no further as this is the place!

Located right in the heart of Oakland Chinatown a beloved institution with authentic dining inside the Pacific Renaissance Plaza.
It is a classic, loud, no-frills hole-in-the-wall. The environment is cramped, lively, and unpretentious, with a steady hum of Cantonese spoken between staff and guests. It feels entirely frozen in time, capturing the nostalgic rhythm of an old-school Hong Kong diner where service here follows the traditional "Chinatown speed" model: fast, direct, and hyper-efficient.

In today's economy still affordable with generous, group-calibrated portion sizes. Most individual plates, bowls of porridge, or noodle soups run in the $10–$20 range

The easiest option is the paid underground parking garage directly beneath the Pacific Renaissance Plaza, which charges reasonable hourly rates instead of driving around in circles for over ten minutes and finding nothing.

Locals widely consider it to serve the best congee (rice porridge) in the East Bay, featuring a perfectly smooth texture. Combined with their house-roasted meats (like the crisp roast duck and char siu) and fresh, silky rice noodle rolls, it is widely considered an unmissable culinary landmark for authentic Cantonese soul food.

I didnt take a photo of my own food🤦🏻‍♂️ becuase I was too focused on my HK friend ordering ABC combo and getting the side eye

We also tried their BBQ Combo Dish, which included BBQ pork and roast duck bursting with flavor, thanks to the perfectly balanced marinade.

The Beef and Egg Over Rice was alright but not memorable.

To cleanse our palates, we enjoyed refreshing Lemon Tea, its citrusy zing complementing the savory dishes beautifully.

I also ordered their Beef Chow Fen for takeout, featuring wide rice noodles stir-fried with succulent beef, creating a harmonious blend of flavors and textures.

To conclude our meal, we ordered  the Thai coconut milk dessert, Ka-nom-tuay, served in a little porcelain cup. It was equally delightful. My husband and I were so impressed with the food that we’re already planning our next visit. Highly recommended!

I was a little nervous when I walked in at 1:30 and there was no one else there, but this place was fantastic. I got the hot and sour noodle soup and it was the perfect balance of flavor and spice and crunch. My Thai tea was also exactly the right level of sweetness. It got a lot busier as my meal went on, fortunately for them. It was hard to pick a restaurant in this very busy area of choices but this was a good one.

Too bad the food was just okay for the heavily decorated oldie Thai street theme. The dish I think is a waste of $37 is seafood crispy pancake. The rest were just not authentic enough. Pad Thai is off, there was no balance of fish sauce, palm sugar and tamarind tastes, but only tastes sour. I wouldn't touch any Pad Krapow that has long green bean in it. It's considered a cheap taste of the cooks who put them in Thailand. And this place isn't cheap. Somtum was a bit disappointing, bearable. Overall a disappointment.
Came for lunch. Crab fried rice and steamed veggies were awesome. Super fresh and flavorful! Thankful they didn’t hold back on the spice for the fried rice. True gem!

They offered a very good thai food. The serving is large and the price is reasonable. The staff in the restaurant are friendly and accommodating. The vibes of the restaurant is good with many ornaments showing thai traditional pop culture.

top_reviews.content: If you're looking for an authentic Italian restaurant in San Fran, look no further. We are from the East coast and have the best Italian restaurants here  and Bocconcino would fit right in here in Boston's North End. The GNOCCHI AL GORGONZOLA was phenomenal (Homade gnocchi). We also had the POLLO ALLA PARMIGIANO, MELANZANE ALLA PARMIGIANA and the SPAGHETTI CIPOLLA E SALSICCIA which were all outstanding.  We did have a reservation and were sat right away, but did see people get turned away if they didn't as the restaurant is small inside.

The restaurant had a nice atmosphere for dinner although it could get a bit loud at times. I had the Ravioli de Pesce which was very good and had a nice flavor, and I could actually taste the fish. The Ravioli de Pesto and the Tortelini were good but nothing special. The tiramisu was good but a little bland, however the chocolate cake was executed to perfection!

I have no idea how many restaurants you can pack into such a short stretch of roadway but this part of Green Street sure has plenty of options, and today's top choice is..Bocconcini.
I had big Mable Hatley with me because she's in town from her compound up in Monte Rio with her crew, The Monte Rio Muffin Mashers, and they plan on hitting every LBG joint in the city, so be forewarned because they don't take prisoners!
I had ordered a few things, but the pasta dish was deliciously amazing!
5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s and that by itself is worthy of a trip across the bridge!

Unfortunately, we didn’t have a great experience here. The restaurant looks charming from the outside, but inside it was extremely loud—we could barely hear each other and had to raise our voices throughout dinner. Even though we had a reservation, we were asked to wait outside, and the service felt inattentive. We had to ask for everything ourselves, including the menu.

We also ordered a salad to share, but it was served first and our pasta didn’t arrive until we had finished it. We would have preferred to enjoy the salad together with our main course rather than as a separate course.

The food was just okay. Having been to Italy, we expected more from a restaurant promoting itself as authentic Italian. The pasta was quite basic, and the tiramisu tasted more like cake than a traditional tiramisu. The house wine was excellent, and one waiter kindly offered me a complimentary glass after noticing we weren’t fully satisfied, which we appreciated. Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough to make up for the overall experience.

I cannot rate this place highly enough. I was craving cacio e pepe and feeling a bit homesick, and even though it wasn’t on the menu tonight, the owner offered to make it for me himself. The best I’ve had since Europe. Truly an authentic Italian experience — come here if you want to know what it means to feel the love of food. Will come back anytime I’m in town. Gratzie

top_reviews.content: Excellent beed tartare! Tortelli were okay, a bit underdone on edges and somewhat bland flavor profile. Pork very good. Expensive!

I recently tried this for lunch and overall thought it was just okay. The appetizers and ricotta were decent, but the cacio e pepe was a real disappointment. I almost never send food back, but in this case I couldn’t eat it — the pasta tasted like it had just been microwaved, lacking the freshness and flavor you’d expect from such a classic dish.

While the atmosphere was nice and some items were enjoyable, I probably wouldn’t try it again.

An amazing throwback to the era of sophisticated delicious food, an extensive menu, affordable nice wines, friendly attentive service, and comfortable quiet tables all at fair (not crazy) prices, in a neighborhood restaurant that is easy to book!  The seafood and vegetable-based appetizers and main dishes, breads, and desserts we ordered were wonderful.  (Did not try any meats.) We lingered over a Sunday night dinner for a couple of hours.

I really wanted to like this more. First time going, maybe one more try?
Went on a Thursday at about 6:30, plenty of tables available, no reservation, seated immediately. Got a brand new server - truly, it was his second day. Very sweet, polite guy, but didn't know anything yet. Took a long time for him to come take our drink orders (fatal mistake in the profit margin game of restaurants) and then didn't know what we ordered, but fair to him he probably wasn't or just barely 21 himself, so...

Menu selection is classically Italian, with a good mix of northern and southern cuisines. We ordered the risotto; good, not something we'd order again, but fair enough, and the squid ink pasta. Again, good, but depth of flavor was tragically missing. It needed a deep tomato/umami base that just wasn't there. With that, I think it would've been great - an inventive dish. I ordered it because you don't see it in a lot of places and I would not likely make it at home. So close, but no cigar. Everything else on theenu of course contained pork and milk, neither of which is edible to us, so that left us with few choices.

I will give the atmosphere and the senior wait staff (who took over for the kid, he might have been in the back trying to pronounce Fortaleza) a 4 star rating - both lovely, but not quite enough to make up for the early missteps and lackluster meals. Do get the focaccia/bread basket sampler! That was delicious 😋

We then added the truffle ravioli; downed everything with wine and left happy. Service was excellent also- no BS and quick, thanks for a nice time!

top_reviews.content:
We tried two dishes during my visit.

#21 - The broth was light and clean, and the ingredients tasted fresh. If you prefer a mild, simple flavor, this is a good choice.

#10 Seafood Ho Fun was disappointing. It came with only a few small pieces of squid and two shrimp, but a huge amount of noodles. The broth was extremely bland, and for the price it didn’t feel worth it.

The restaurant is cash only, and although the menu says prices include tax, the overall pricing still felt misleading. I probably wouldn’t return.

At this location, the fried garlic is served separately—a detail I truly appreciate. I also really enjoy their thin egg noodles, which strike a perfect balance between chewy and tender without becoming overly soft. However, the dish tends to be quite oily, so if you prefer lighter meals, this might not be ideal for you.

My usual order is the Number 1 without kidney, with the soup served on the side. I also always add fish cake as an appetizer. The total cost for two regular dishes plus one appetizer comes to $53.75.

What I love about this restaurant is how it evokes the authentic flavors of Thailand’s street food, especially the dry yellow egg noodles. While it doesn’t include traditional Thai-style char siu or wontons, the taste remains quite close to home.

This well-established Chinese restaurant impresses me with its surprisingly clean restrooms, likely due to my morning visits. Parking can be difficult, as only metered street parking is available. The branch tends to be busy, so clear communication with staff is important. Although there may be a short wait, the service is attentive and friendly.

Wow does this place get packed! I got the seafood ho fun, and it was aight. Like not mind blowing but it was good. I thought the lettuce was extremely weird. The place is cash only though so be prepared. Maybe I need to try this place again…
Waited about 15 minutes for lunch on Saturday. I thought the noodle was average, not sure what the hype is about. Also I think the noodle used to be cheaper but its much more expensive now.

*2/25/2024
I ordered the mixed noodles with both ho fun and rice noodles. The broth is light and clear, and it comes with lots of toppings like chili, sriracha, hoisin, vinegar, and Vien Huong's special chili sauce. There's a mix of meats in the dish—shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork pieces, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork—all served with your favorite type of rice noodles. The homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños give it a spicy kick, making the flavors really pop.

1/25/2024
No. 21 Chow Jew Ho Fun is a dish featuring shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork, all harmoniously paired with your preferred rice noodles.

The addition of homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños provides a spicy burst, delivering that extra kick! The flavorful combination keeps me coming back for more.

Venturing into something new this time, I got the fried fish cake. It proved to be incredibly tasty, although the only drawback is its slightly higher price for relatively smaller portions. But, it's definitely worth a try!

*Tip: Cash only.

12/27/2023
Vien Huong's No. 21 Chow Jew Ho Fun is a monthly ritual with my friend! Their exceptional chicken broth, light and clear, is unmatched. After trying other places, I keep coming back for its distinct flavor.

What makes Vien Huong special is the thoughtful addition of kidney, setting them apart. The dish includes shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork—all perfectly paired with your preferred rice noodles.

Vien Huong adds a spicy burst with homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños, providing that extra kick! A flavorful experience that keeps me hooked!

*Tip: Cash only.

11/27/2023
No. 21 Chow Jew Ho Fun takes center stage on their menu. This time, I tried their mixed noodles with ho fun and rice noodle. The chicken broth is a light and clear base for their impressive array of condiments such as chili, sriracha, hoisin, vinegar, and Vien Huong's house-made chili sauce. The dish features a generous medley of meats—shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork—all served with your preferred type of rice noodles. The homemade chili oil and pickled jalapeños add a spicy burst and extra kick, creating a delightful flavor combination.

We also tried their Sauteed Kidney with Ginger Onion, which I really enjoyed and highly recommend if you are not apprehensive about eating pork kidney. The kidney is well-seasoned and flavorful, with a crunchy but not mushy texture. The onions complement the kidney really well, even when paired with the Chow Jew Ho Fun.

*Tip: Cash only.

10/23/2023
Vien Huong Restaurant is a hidden treasure. I revisited this place, and it's just as amazing as ever.

Their No.21 Chow Jew Ho Fun takes center stage on their menu. The chicken broth is light and clear, giving you the perfect canvas to season to your liking with an impressive array of condiments. They offer chili, sriracha, hoisin, vinegar, and, of course, Vien Huong's house-made chili sauce. This dish is a generous medley of meats, including shrimp, fish balls, pork balls, pork bits, kidney, and your choice of sliced chicken or pork, all served with your preferred type of rice noodles.

Their homemade chili oil adds a spicy burst of flavor, and the pickled jalapeños give your meal an extra kick, creating a delightful flavor combination.

*Tip: This restaurant is cash-only, so be sure to come prepared. The prices are incredibly reasonable. You'll be pleasantly surprised at how affordable it is. Not to mention, the service is lightning fast; I can finish my meal in about 15 minutes and be on my way. Parking can be a bit challenging, but it's a minor inconvenience for the fantastic food.

This Korean-style Chinese restaurant located in Oakland, California, offers a variety of delightful dishes such as Tangsu-yuk (sweet and sour pork), fried dumplings, Jjajang-myon (black bean paste noodles), and Jjampong (spicy seafood noodles). The fried dumplings were exceptional, boasting a crispy exterior and a succulent, well-seasoned filling of pork and vegetables. The sweet and sour pork was equally impressive, with a delightful blend of sweetness in the sauce complementing the perfectly fried pork strips. While the noodle dishes were enjoyable, the texture of the noodles did not quite meet expectations, lacking the desired hand-stretched quality. The green chili sweet potato noodles provided a tasty kick with hot chili. The service was excellent, though there is room for improvement in the restaurant's overall ambiance to elevate the dining experience.

It’s truly a gem of the bay. This is probably the best Chinese/korean food in the bay. The jjajangmyeon, jjajang and tangsuyuk is all we come for.
