Visited here for lunch, ordered chicken kebab with fries and falafel plate. It also comes with side salad. You order at counter and food will be served at the table. Service was very good. Food was very tasty. Highly recommend this place.

Great discovery!!
Went on a Thursday night after a show at the Orpheum (two blocks away) around 9:45pm. Would be a great option after the Opera, Ballet and Symphony shows nearby.

We had two smoothies: strawberry mango and strawberry banana, both delicious. We also got the Blue Cheese burger to share that comes with fig jam and a decent side of fries. The burger was so tasty and flavorful. Food was so good that we devoured it without taking any pictures but now we have the perfect excuse to go back.

The place is clean, spacious and well kept. In addition, Jay was at the counter and he was very nice and kind to explain the multiple food options. Really looking forward to be back soon!

After finishing a meeting near Market and Van Ness, we were kind of hungry. My friend suggested we try some Hayes Valley restaurants, but they were all packed and noisy, not to mention too expensive. I suggested Jay's Grill because I walk past it every so often, and the menu looked good. There is a variety of Mediterranean dishes, including vegetarian and low-carb ones. Although busy, we got a nice table by the window. My friend ordered the beef kabob plate with rice, and I got a Caesar Salad with chicken. Our order was taken quickly and with courtesy. The plates were brought to our table within just a few minutes; faster than we'd expected. My salad was amazing! The dressing was on the side, and they gave me plenty of it. The chicken was tender and flavorful. This is one of the better Caesar salads I've had in San Francisco, even though it wasn't very expensive. I should also mention that it was BIG! Despite being hungry, I wasn't able to finish it. Our server brought us to-go boxes with a smile. I look forward to coming back here and trying something else from their menu. My only minor complaint is with some of the other patrons rather than the restaurant itself. One table was being especially loud. Luckily they left shortly after we got served.

I was really excited to try this spot since I love a good chicken shawarma wrap, but it ended up being a letdown. The $15 wrap was surprisingly tiny, overly greasy, and barely had any chicken. And what little chicken there was… just wasn’t good.

First time trying this type of cuisine, was not disappointed. Service was great, nice atmosphere. I ordered the creamy chicken tikka masala, garlic naan. Great portions, had to save some for later. Recommend giving it a try.

This is a beautiful restaurant. From the interior to the staff, everything is excellent. I asked about their bar menu, and they told me it was crafted with the help of one of the oldest bars in town. That showed me they truly want the best for their customers. We arrived early for dinner around 5:00 p.m., and it was just beginning to fill up. By the time we left around 6:30 p.m., there were people waiting for tables. It was a great experience. I rarely leave reviews, but this restaurant is truly one of a kind.

Tasted better the next day, but flavor combo didn't work for me. Noodles were bland (lacked salt), they tasted much better with soy sauce. Chicken was OK, but not really worth it compared to other similar food options in the area.

Everest Kitchen, my go-to spot for craft cocktails, has undergone a remarkable transformation within a year of its full bar opening. It has transformed into a haven that offers authentic food and the best cocktails.

Among the exquisite creations, the Amaretto Sour and Jameson Mule stood out as my favorites. They were expertly crafted to perfection.

Great casual Mexican spot! The tacos, burgers, chicken sandwich and fries are delicious, and the space is clean and bright. It's a fantastic location for a big group looking for a relaxed meal. Don't skip the fries!"

I got the California Burrito with Carnitas and everything in it. It was a very well-packed burrito. Nicely sealed tortilla and wrapped in aluminum foil. I didn’t have to rip apart layers and layers of aluminum foil since there was only one. The fries in the burrito are crinkle cut so there’s an extra nice texture to it when you bite into it. love the hasami age, mikuri age, bao bun, pumpkin soup, inari, vege-tofu curry!

google.name: Rose Pizzeria

top_reviews.content: If you’re just looking for a reliably good pizza place, this spot definitely delivers. They’ve got a really nice dough, tasty cheese, and a sauce that pulls everything together into a pretty satisfying personal pizza. They also have some nice drink options and a good range of wines if that’s your thing. Overall, it’s just a really nice place to grab a good pizza.

*For context, this review is largely for vegans (3.5/5 stars).

Had a reservation on a Friday evening on the back patio. Beautiful weather for the back patio. I had emailed the restaurant in advance to check on vegan menu items, and they assured me that most of the menu items can be made vegan. There seems to be some confusion between the staff and management though since when I came to the restaurant it wasn't as vegan friendly as advertised (e.g., it turns out the gigante beans could not be made vegan). That being said, they were still able to make vegan the two pizzas I was interested in the She Wolf and the Old Faithful. They use Daiya cheese which looks great, but doesn't have the strongest taste profile and texture isn't amazing when it cools down. We asked for salt to increase the taste on the pizza, but think they could do a lot more to increase the flavor profile on both pizzas, since we've had similar pizza toppings elsewhere that were more flavorful. (Honestly, the toppings combination for both pizzas were excellent, but a little undersalted with the current vegan cheese choice.) Both pizzas were still solid though. I am bummed I missed my opportunity to try the pizza back when they used Butcher's Son cheese. There's tons of better tasting vegan supermarket cheeses out there over Daiya too (Parmela, Good Planet, Miyokos, etc.), but perhaps they use Daiya because it melts nicely/better or they haven't tried the others. Food was good but could still do better, especially knowing the strong competition for pizza, vegan and non-vegan.

Highlight:
Delicious vegan-friendly pizza in a spotless space with a patio you’ll want to linger on.

Restaurant:
This cozy Berkeley pizza spot takes pride in crafting high-quality pies with fresh ingredients and thoughtful flavor combinations. The atmosphere is relaxed yet well-kept, and the charming patio is the kind of space that makes you want to extend your meal just to soak it all in.

Service:
Service here is warm, welcoming, and attentive without feeling rushed. Staff members know their menu well and seem genuinely happy to guide you toward great choices. The care they put into the dining experience is evident from start to finish.

Food:
We enjoyed a vegan pizza topped with sausage and peppers, and it was packed with flavor—savory, well-balanced, and cooked to perfection. The vegan Caesar salad was another standout, with a creamy, flavorful dressing that didn’t feel like a compromise. Every bite spoke to the attention paid to quality and freshness.

Recommendations:
Whether you’re vegan, vegetarian, or just a pizza lover, this is a must-visit. Grab a spot on the patio if the weather’s nice, and don’t skip the vegan Caesar—it’s a pleasant surprise. The spotless dining area and even cleaner bathroom say a lot about how much the team cares. Highly recommend for anyone seeking top-notch pizza in Berkeley.

This place is so special! I am not sure if it is the size of the establishment or the taste of the exquisite pizza, but Rose is a great place to bring friends or go on a date. The ambience is loud but warm and friendly. The service and staff were extremely timely and professional. I had a great dinner here with friends, and will be back for more. Parking is a sore, but what is new in Berkeley!? 10/10!

Our pizza aficionado friend had told us about this place. It delivers!
Ambiance: The outdoor seating in the back is chill and a great place to hang out and enjoy.
Food: We ordered a red sauce pizza and a white sauce pizza. Honestly I normally prefer white sauce but the red sauce at Rose is next level tasty. The crust was superb and the pizza was great with their house red wine.
Service: friendly and attentive
Price: Bay Area fair price for the best pizza around
I’d be happy to go back

top_reviews.content: We came here before they made changes but I wanted to leave a review about our experience.  I got a cold brew coffee with tahini and caramel and it was really good. We them ordered the toum caesar salad with halloumi, and the labneh and they were both fantastic. So much flavor in all the dishes. The knafeh pancake was my absolute favorite but we had to take most of it to go because it was too much food for 2 people. I will add the service was pretty slow on that Sunday morning because it took a long time to get our orders in, I had to remind them about the coffee a few times and then getting the check too a while too.

The food here is phenomenal. I’ve never had such creative fusion flavors that are both new and familiar. They have Mediterranean / Palestinian standards but with a twist; the flavor combos are so clever and they always taste amazing. They have slightly different menu items for dinner vs brunch so I’d really recommend trying both for the full experience. My favorites are too many to name but honestly you can’t go wrong—but the pancake is definitely top notch. Other favorites include the toum fries, the lentil soup, rotti wrap…actually you know what everything is good. I really don’t think you can go wrong. They also have vegetarian and vegan options, as well as other dietary restrictions options. Parking can be found on the street, though might be crowded during peak hours. I wish they were open more days of the week, it’s only Thursday - Sunday for now, but maybe in the future that will change…?

Was really sad to see my favorite unique + quality brunch spot in the bay change format to being fast casual. It was such an easy brunch pick to take out of towners or friends to.

Now instead, they've become easily one of the best fast-casual food in the bay. So I really can't complain.  I guess their format changed worked because I've eaten here more often than when they were full service. The value for the money you get here is pretty nuts. Still just as good ingredients & just as good preparation, all at a more approachable price point & form factor. What really gets me is I'm truly getting restaurant quality cooking for a unique cuisine I don't see very often, just a version that works better to-go. When you compare to some of the other casual lunch/dinner places in the area that have a similar format, it's really no competition. You'd be hard pressed to find a better way to spend $20-30/pp. I also love that they kept some of my favorite guilty pleasures from when they were a full service restaurant, like the knafe pancake.

Their in-house online ordering system is pretty slick and a good deal too. Works just as well as doordash without any of the bloated prices. Wouldn't mind seeing this spread around to more restaurants.

Pleasantly surprised to find that everything we had tasted just as good as it looked. Expected there to be too much focus on aesthetics and making everything pretty for photos, but all dishes were quite good.

Service was good and friendly, the atmosphere was bustling, and the new digs are cute. It's heavily brunch centric, but there are some more lunch dinner items.

Wish they had a beer and wine license, some natty skin contact would go great.

Review to be updated if experience changes.

Such a great brunch spot. The menu is full of super interesting and unique dishes. The Japanese sweet potatoes were addictive. They have super fun coffee options. I would definitely come back here and recommend it to anyone looking for a beautiful, unique brunch spot. It’s located in a cute part of town too!

name: Thai Basil

top_reviews.content: Hard to find but worth the search Thai food in downtown Berkeley.  Found this delicious food paradise close to UCB campus.  Tried the pineapple fried rice, but there was so much volume to it, I had to split it.  It had an undertone of curry flavor in it, a good amount of pineapple but not quite enough cashews for my taste.  The rice had just the right amount of oil to make everything more flavorful but not overly greasy.  The Thai iced tea was smooth and easy to drink without being over sweet.  The dining room was simple and easy to navigate, and the staff was helpful.  There’s an option for touch panel ordering for cashless orders or cash only options if you want to talk to an actual person while placing your order.  The menu is long, but not so much so that it’s overwhelming.
The food was pretty mediocre for its price, but my vegetarian coworker said his dish of rice was pretty good.

The veggie fried rice was fresh, flavorful, and perfectly seasoned with a great balance of textures. The portion size was very good and the spice level was well balanced. The veggie pad see ew was equally satisfying, with soft noodles, crisp vegetables, and a rich savory sauce. Overall, both dishes were comforting and delicious and definitely worth trying again.

Rats!

Eating there and I saw a rat run from under the fridge back into the kitchen, then later walking up in the ceiling decor.

Food is great for the price and area, downside is there are rats all over the neighborhood, I just wished they kept them out of the restaurant. It's too bad, I've been going here for years, hope they clean it up.

Thai Basil in Berkeley offers a convenient option for a quick Thai food fix. I tried their Basil Chili Chicken with fried egg, which was a decent portion size. The chicken itself was cooked well, but the overall flavor lacked the punch I was hoping for.

The ambiance of the restaurant is pretty basic, with simple décor and generic Asian-style furniture. It's clean and comfortable enough for a casual meal, but the inside space may feel very crowded when you have a few occupied tables. There is open seating outside the restaurant, which is shared by all the other restaurants in that section, so it's available on a first come, first served basis.

The service was fast but the staff could have been friendlier. When my friends and I asked for to-go boxes and utensils/napkins, we got an angry look from the staff. Please also note that the restaurant doesn't have a bathroom for its customers, so you'll have to find some place else if you really need to go.

Overall, Thai Basil is an average option. The food is decent, but a little pricey for what you get. If you're in the area and looking for a quick bite, it's not a bad choice, but there are probably better Thai restaurants in Berkeley worth exploring.

top_reviews.content: Amazing, amazing hospitality. Not to mention, one of the best chicken and pasta dishes I’ve had. Shoutout to our server Fabio: he was super attentive and kind to us despite how busy the place was. Highly recommend!

Really enjoyed this spot overall. The food was excellent and the service attentive. The chicken was cooked to perfection, with beautifully crisped skin and great flavor. The risotto was rich and creamy while still having just the right bite, and the wine pairings worked very well.

That said, the burrata appetizer was a real letdown. At $16 for just two pieces (with stale bread, no less), it felt underwhelming and overpriced, especially if you’re sharing. For a group of three or four, it just doesn’t make sense to serve it that way.

Overall, a great experience thanks to the main dishes and service.

The service was okay, but the prices were way too high for what we received. We spent over $150 plus tip, and by the time I got home, I still felt like making food because I was hungry. The salmon I ordered was extremely small, especially considering it cost $40.

For the price, I expected much better portions and overall value. Safe to say, we won’t be back.

Picked this resturant because of t he reviews and it didnot disappoint. The food was delicious. We had the brussels sprouts, fresh fettuccine and almond coffee pana cotta. The service was outstanding. The owners came by and spoke. It was just a great dinner.

There’s something undeniably special about Frascati, the kind of place that feels perfectly at home in its surroundings. Located on an idyllic tree-lined stretch of Hyde Street, with cable cars rolling by, it captures the charm of San Francisco in a way that feels effortless and authentic.

From the moment you walk in, the warmth is immediate. Rebecca, the owner, greets guests from the host stand with genuine kindness, making everyone feel less like a customer and more like a neighbor. She even waves to the passing cable cars, adding a personal touch that makes the experience feel fun and memorable.

My husband and I celebrated our anniversary here, and it could not have been a more perfect setting. The atmosphere strikes a beautiful balance, elegant but never pretentious, cozy but special enough for an occasion. It is the kind of place where you can come for a nice neighborhood dinner or celebrate something meaningful and feel equally at home.

The food is delicious, thoughtful and well executed without trying too hard to impress. And do not skip dessert. The array of house made ice cream, also made by Rebecca, is absolutely worth it.

Frascati is the definition of a neighborhood gem, welcoming, charming, and consistently great. It is a place you will want to return to again.

He reported it to the same waitress who simply said " Oh sorry, do you want me to get you a new plate of food". Lack of full apology, no managerial apology nor followup, no automatically insisting to clear it from the bill without being asked by the customer and the fact that they do expected the customer to pay any bill after going through possibly eating glass. The noise level was pretty high, mainly because of the birthday party I think, but the atmosphere is festive and fun. And it’s a great neighborhood location that clearly brings in a lot of regulars (no tourists that we could spot.) Reservations highly recommended, the place is intimate and every table was completely full by 6pm on a Saturday night. Walk-in’s weren’t turned away but had a lengthy wait out on the sidewalk. Serafina is officially at the top of our favorite restaurant list in SF. We will be back soon!

Kicking off the New Year with a meal at Serafina, perched atop Russian Hill, feels like coming home. This beloved neighborhood gem is where familiar faces gather and every dish is crafted with care. Known for its exceptional homemade pasta and decadent, house-made desserts, Serafina radiates a warmth you want to share with friends visiting from out of town. The journey up to Russian Hill—300 feet of San Francisco’s classic charm—only adds to the only in San Francisco experience. PS: One of the best gnocchi I've had outside NYC.

What a lovely locally owned gem. It’s small/quaint and the two servers are Italian men in their 50s. It’s not fussy but really focused on the food-homemade pasta and everything you need to feel like you’re like you’re in Italy.

The Tonnarelli al Nero di Seppia con Polpo was simply exceptional—easily one of the best pasta dishes I've had in San Francisco. The squid ink tonnarelli was perfectly cooked, with a wonderful texture and depth of flavor, while the octopus was tender, fresh, and expertly prepared.

Every bite reflected authentic Italian craftsmanship and a commitment to high-quality ingredients. The balance of flavors was outstanding, allowing the seafood to shine while complementing the richness of the pasta.

Beyond the incredible food, the service was warm, attentive, and professional. From start to finish, the entire dining experience was memorable.

If you're looking for outstanding Italian cuisine in San Francisco, the Tonnarelli al Nero di Seppia con Polpo is an absolute must-order. I'll definitely be back.

top_reviews.content:
We were craving poke on a hot day and decided to try this place because of its high ratings.

I ordered a regular poke bowl with tuna, bay scallops, salmon roe, crab salad, mixed greens, wakame salad, onions, seaweed, edamame, and cucumber.

Everything tasted fresh and flavorful, and the fish quality was great. My only complaint is the portion size. The fish scoops were pretty small, and the bowl cost around $20, making it feel a bit overpriced for what you get.

For those unfamiliar with this style of cuisine, this type of fast casual restaurant primarily prepares a traditional Hawaiian seasoned raw fish salad served with a bed of rice as the base, your choice of cut raw seafood on top, and some veggies mixed in.

It’s good, clean, and healthy eating.
But the menu is meager when it comes to hot and cooked food.
I mention this because I was looking for a basic cooked chicken over a bed of rice dish when I went, not knowing what their menu consisted of.

Although they don’t offer any cooked chicken, their poki bowls are tasty.

I particularly liked the seaweed and crab salad as my sides.

Customer service was good. The team was patient, helpful and did well to explain the process of how to build a bowl.

Do think the mini bowl portion size was plenty of food.
Price was fair.
Tip, only street side parking.

Great poke place with a Hawaiian flare (macaroni salad for example). I would say the portion size is okay for the price but they have great options for mix-in’s and thoughtful arrangement of the sides, rice, and greens. Would recommend the crab salad as a side!

Fish was fresh, I thought the seasonings on the rice and fish were great.
I had brown rice, salmon, albacore, shrimp. Seaweed salad and edamame. Photo of my takeout, the nice presentation got a bit scrambled when dropped it.

What a great start to begin the year with a new spot unlocked. Hashtag poki is quick and professional at their job. Order what you want, here’s your bowl. Seating inside very minimal but you would need to go during slow hours. I went here Sunday lunch, and enjoyed my meal. I was lucky enough to grab a seat and enjoy all the flavors bursting in my mouth. The wonton chips is definitely a must have in your poke bowl. Quite creative, I like the idea! Street parking is provided, not hard to miss. A corner restaurant to serve you. I am most likely coming back to this joint to enjoy more of their menu.

name: Pizzeria da Laura
address: 2049 Shattuck Ave., Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

google.name: Pizzeria da Laura
google.address: 2049 Shattuck Ave., Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

top_reviews.content:
On Saturday, June 20, 2026, I ate at Pizzeria Da Laura for my birthday.

Let me start off by saying if you don't know about Pizzeria Da Laura, you're sleeping big time on great pizza and Italian good in general.

The owner Laura, trained and worked under renowned Pizza Master Tony Gemignani. If you're from the Bay Area and don't know who Tony is, you've been asleep your entire life! Lol 😆 🤣 😂

I had high expectations for Laura's restaurant since she trained with and under Tony for years. Here's what we ordered. The Arancini which came with a red marina sauce, the Ray J New York Style Pizza 18 inch, the Grandma Style Pazzo Pizza, and the Rigatoni in Vodka cream sauce with sausage added to it. The Arancini was different compared to what I was used to. There were artichokes and a touch of lemon inside of the Arancini. It was very earthy tasting. The texture was spot on and the flavors were unique. The Ray J New York Style Pizza is some of the best pizza I've ever had. Two different types of pepperoni, fresh burrata cheese and drizzled with honey! It was such a unique and great tasting pizza. It's unlike anything I've ever had. I would highly recommend this pizza to everyone. The Pazzo Grandma style pizza was good. If you like combination pizza toppings, you'll definitely enjoy this pizza. This was my first time trying a grandma style pizza. I've tried Detroit and Sicilian style pizzas which are way thicker compared to a grandma style pizza. The grandma style pizza dough and crust was thin and very crunchy. It was served cut into an L/triangle shape. Pretty cool. I honestly was kinda upset because we wanted to try their lasagna but they ran out the night before and it wasn't available on Saturday when we are there around 4 pm. We opted for the Rigatoni pasta with Vodka cream sauce and sausage. It was beyond good! It really hit the spot! It was definitely one of the best pasta dishes I've ever eaten. The Vodka cream sauce wasn't spicy and the sausage was super flavorful. The pasta was cooked perfectly. A great dish overall!

I went with 8 people. Everyone loved the food. The atmosphere and decor/vibe of the restaurant is nice. There's a bar area and plasma screen TV's to watch a game. The restaurant is also connected a market/business right next door that sells slices of pizza from Pizzeria Da Laura, Gelato and cookies along with other Italian infused foods. Pretty cool.

Out waiter Justice was excellent! He was very attentive to details and had a great personality. Great service overall.

I took one star off because the Lasagna wasn't available. But its okay because this gives me a reason to go back and try the Lasagna.

Pizzeria Da Laura is definitely a 5 out of 5 star rating restaurant.

BTW, the owner Laura is very nice and down to earth. This was my first time meeting her. I enjoyed talking to her about Tony, various pizza/Italian infused restaurants throughout the Bay Area and just about food/pizza in general. Laura is a class act and I wish nothing but success for her restaurant and future business adventures.

Thanks again Laura and the staff at Pizzeria Da Laura for great food, great service/hospitality and a great birthday dinner!

Our first time so we ordered a crazy amount of pizza just so we could try three different styles: Sicilian, Detroit and NY. All were delicious with excellent crust and texture. The good news is that the pizza also reheats really well. We will certainly be coming back. 😋

Pizzeria da Laura in Berkeley is a fantastic spot for Italian food right in the heart of downtown, just steps from the university. The location gives it a lively downtown vibe with lots of energy from the surrounding area and nearby students.

The reservation and check-in process was very smooth. The staff were incredibly courteous, welcoming, and helpful throughout the visit. I actually arrived about 30 minutes earlier than my reservation time, and they were kind enough to seat us early, which was a really nice touch.

One thing I really like about this place is that they update their dishes a few times a year, so every visit can feel a little different and exciting. The menu has great variety, especially when it comes to pizza styles as you can choose from New York, Sicilian, Detroit, and Grandma-style pizzas, and the pricing is very straightforward for all the sizes they serve.

The pizza was perfectly cooked and tasted great. They also allow you to customize your pizza by adding or removing ingredients, which makes it very convenient for everyone to choose based on their liking. And they add toppings with open-heart.

The pasta was also excellent. We ordered the Peperoncino pasta, and it tasted amazing. The garlic flavor and breadcrumbs were really the highlight and brought out the authentic character of the spaghetti.

Another big plus is that they have plenty of vegetarian options, making it easy for different dietary preferences. The portions are generous and the prices are very reasonable for what they serve.

Food arrived quickly, and the service from the servers and staff was great throughout the visit. The restaurant also has plenty of space and handles reservations well.

The atmosphere is lively with lots of people around and students from the nearby university, which adds to the downtown Berkeley energy. A little more upbeat music could add even more charm to the place.

Overall, this is a place I would definitely recommend to anyone visiting Berkeley. It’s the kind of restaurant I’d happily come back to again and again.

Me and the lady went here, cause of Bay Area Check Please! You know? Cause that’s what we do. The evening we went it was busy, but we had little wait for our table. The homie Fernando was cool and on top of things. It Did however take a min to get the pies. But it wasn’t a crazy long wait. About the pies we got: I got the Detroit style of what’s called The Ray J which is named after Laura’s brother. I saw her make that on an episode Localish. My lady got a New York style of a “make your own”. Both were fire. The dough on the New York style was nice and slightly chewy. And on the Detroit style, the way the cheese cooked around the edges were tasty than a mug! If you know you know. The ambiance was cool. I mean, it’s a pizza place. Music was on point. Nah’mean?!?! Check it out.

Definitely one of the Top 3 Pizza restaurants I have ever been to. The food was INCREDIBLE! The service was top notch. The historic building was beautifully transformed into the perfect space of luxury. What a great experience, and I cannot wait to return to try some more of her Pizza. My wife bought her book in hopes of miraculously recreating our perfect meal! Thank you! ❤️❤️

top_reviews.content:
They pack generous portions for all options, and their grilled edamame is fantastic, given for free with plates and 3 triangle orders.

I started ordering from them during their opening week, and I have never been let down. Not once. I have tried every type of meat, plates, small plates, and triangles. Everything is superb.

There is no real seating, a couple of tables outside, but their whole menu is to go.

Unexpectedly ordered 3 triangles here for a late lunch and it didn’t disappoint. I ordered on the kiosk, and there was a little bit of a wait. It is a small space with only 4 seats inside. A lot of other people also in line to order and waiting for their food. I would definitely come back and try other triangles, I got the chicken teriyaki, grilled salmon and short rib. All very yummy. I would have been good with two triangles.

While I was waiting for my food, I couldn't help but overhear the employees' unpleasant way of speaking and the way they shouted at each other, with no regard for the space around them. The food is delicious; it was just the way the employees spoke that made me feel uncomfortable.

Heads up!  This is Americanized Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls).  You are not getting Japanese style “rice triangles” that you would find in Japan and Hawaii in terms of quality (type of rice and seaweed) and style (fillings).  Initially the price seemed expensive because in Hawaii you can get onigiri for $2-$4, but here they are generous with the fillings and it’s a little bigger in size so the price seems fair.  It was pretty good here, but I prefer the traditional Japanese style.

It’s in a school zone so it can get busy.  I found free street parking easily so that was nice.  You order and pay with card on the device to your left when you enter.  You can follow the directions on the screen to pay cash at the register.  It was a full house, but orders were distributed efficiently and quickly.  If the cashier is busy, the chefs help pass out the food so I thought that was great teamwork.

If you want something fast and filling, head to Oori Rice Triangles!
I had spicy pork,  short ribs, and salmon. It's was very delicious. I  also have had their triangles, which are excellent.

The lunch buffet is also an amazing deal with a wide variety of options that are consistently fresh and delicious.
Service is top-notch — the staff is friendly, attentive, and makes sure you feel taken care of throughout your meal.
Whether you're dining in, grabbing a quick lunch, or ordering catering, Copper Chimney delivers quality every single time. Highly recommended for anyone craving real Indian flavors!

Ordered delivery chicken tikka masala
Was expecting thigh meat, got overcooked/dry cubes of breast or at least tasted like breast oh well. The flavor of the chicken was under salted and bland, almost as if the cubes of chicken and the gravy were not cooked together for any length of time. Chicken meat was also beyond overcooked, dry and felt like cardboard. Unless the in chouse dining experience is better, this is 0/10 food.

We placed an order for pick up. The coconut chicken curry was absolutely amazing and had shredded coconut on top. Pickup was easy. The chicken tikka masala was decent, but not the best I’ve had in the city. The flavors were simple and the texture was more liquidy than creamy. Pippal delivers one of those dining experiences where everything clicks.

From the moment we walked in, the service stood out. The atmosphere matched that energy. Clean, thoughtfully designed, and comfortable in a way that lets you settle in and enjoy the meal.

The food absolutely held its own. The beetroot kebab was the highlight. Perfectly crusted on the outside, giving way to a creamy, cheesy center, all brought together with a rich beet sauce.

The chaat was vibrant and well-balanced, hitting all the textures and flavors you hope for. And the litti chokha was a great surprise.

This is the kind of place that feels dialed in across the board. Great service, great atmosphere, and food that lives up to both. Definitely worth a visit.

We didn't realize this place is both Indian and Mediterranean food, not fusion. The menu is split with different options from each cuisine.

Overall our experience was decent, but we wouldn't return due to the high cost vs portion size. For example, the butter chicken was $26 then to add rice or naan was an additional $6 or $8. The butter chicken was good but not worth it. The naan was too thin and crunchy.
The falafel wrap was good with 5 waffle fries, not a bad price at $18. Our friend got the plate of falafel which wasn't as great and had no sauce. They did provide a tiny cup of hummus to use on one falafel. The flavors were good so it's a shame how costly it is compared to other restaurants in the same area.

Another concern was the service was very slow, and there were only a few other tables taken. When we arrived they gave us a choice of only 2 tables so I thought it would be packed. We will try another place next time!

Omg!!  I have never really been into Indian food, but this place changed that for me. The food was soooooo delicious. The have Mediterranean food as well, but we didn’t try it this time. My hubby and I ordered their lamb chops, butter chicken, mono chicken and their version of potstickers!! All I can say is that I’d fly to Cali with this place on my mind every time!!!  🤤🤤🤤🤤🤤🤤🤤

Descent food, a little on the spicy side. Everything overpriced. $6.00 for a can of Coke!

-beef soup, just so good.
-pompono fish in the picture, bone licking good. flavor was so fresh.

Service was excellent as well.

If you’re looking for a great homemade thai meal this is the spot.

Tasty food ate within a beautiful ambiance as my wife and I celebrated our 10 yr relationship anniversary. That was our waitress that is pictured below. I had Pad See Ew and I can't remember what my wife had. However, she had an entree that had alot of seafood. We mouth enjoyed our meals.

Oh..we had wings, but I was not a fan.

This place is so amazing! My family suffers from celiac disease and so it's always great to find somewhere that can accommodate our diet. Nearly everything on their menu can be made gluten free and they were very knowledgeable about cross contamination prevention practices. Staff was amazing, food was amazing.  Highly recommend this place!

Was in the North Berkeley area and was looking up places to eat for dinner. It was a Saturday night and some places close fairly early and others have wait lists, on Yelp there was availability so we walked over from where we were at and they were able to seat our party of 2 and we didn’t have to sign up. It was very festive with party/club like music and busy! There was indoor and outdoor seating but it was cold outside and more of a waiting area. There’s street parking in a pretty busy main area.

We started with the Sai Aou- Pork Sausage, Thai Papaya Salad (less spicy than Lao), then ordered Panang Curry with Beef (slow cooked) I saw lots of people review this one. It honestly reminded me of Filipino Kare Kare. And we ordered a side of roti (so good to dip) and Pad See Ew with Chicken. My friend ordered a Thai tea and it was very tea/floral. Everything was really good and delicious! Definitely hit the Thai food craving! Lively, colorful, and bright inside! We were able to easily split the bill and they had a handheld machine to pay.

We came on Saturday evening for dinner. I’ve never been here. We came to do a little food tasting possibly use them for catering for an event. So the moment you get there you join a waitlist to be seated. The restaurant was busy but we didn’t have to wait for too long. We waited maybe 8-10 minutes and we were seated.

The restaurant is not that big but maybe they have an area for big parties? I’m not sure. However, the ambiance is cute, cozy, and inviting. I love the accent wall, it’s picture worthy.

Now, let’s talk about the food. We didn’t just order one or two appetizers we ordered four and I highly recommend them: crispy shrimp roll, spicy chicken wings, crispy tofu over peanut sauce, and Roti bread (which I can eat all day). Everything tasted so fresh and like off the stove.

We also order a few dishes: Nam Khao lettuce wrap, crab fried rice, pumpkin curry with chicken and Pad Thai of course. I don’t know if I was hungry or what but everything was delicious. I never had Nam Khao which is a crispy rice with Chinese sausage and crispy pork. I loved it! It is like an explosion ingredients in my mouth so tasty.

The price: I was surprised we ordered so much food and we spent less than $200. We even had cocktail drinks and dessert. Mango Sticky on point! I don’t know about you but I felt like I was eating some really good food but also sort of healthy. I recommend this place  100 percent.

top_reviews.content: Came here for lunch on a Saturday. Laos is one of the few Asian countries I haven’t been to so I can’t say whether it’s authentic but, damn was it good. Had the nom khao rice and the sai qua Laotian sausage . Family style and portions are huge!

I have high expectation of what the food would taste like based on an ad my Mother saw on Facebook.   We ordered four dishes, two were great and two were barely average IMO.

The crispy spring roll and a short ribs weee excellent. Our favorite was crispy spring roll and is a must-have. My son could have eaten it all by himself, he said.

Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for Rad Na and crab fried.  The Rad na was sweet and the restaurant does not have vinegar (น้ำพริกน้ำส้ม) even though they’re selling Thai food. That was a big disappointment because that is my mom’s favorite and we came here specifically to eat that.

The crab fried rice could be better with the wok being hotter. There is no “wok burn” smell, for all those that know how fried rice should be made. Uncle Roger would have given it a two out of five.

The waitresses were very nice and quick. The restaurant was clean and well decorated.

Overall, it’s an ok experience. I wish I could love it more. If the restaurant owner reads this, I suggest the rice rice you also have a green pickle, jalapeño in vinegar sauce available to serve. And make sure the wok is hot before smashing rice. That’s how a Thai person would eat Thai food.

This place now becomes my favorite place to go for a special Thai dish called Yum Nam Khao Tod (crispy rice ball salad with fermented pork). It takes the top spot in every way: the generous portion, the authentic flavor, and the freshness of the ingredients. Other dishes like papaya salad and spring rolls are also fresh and refreshing. I am so happy that my friend found this place and I would love to visit there again and again.

Everything was absolutely delicious. Highly recommend the Khao Soy soup- so comforting, fresh, and full of amazing ingredients. Service was very friendly, quick, and attentive. Will be stopping here anytime we’re back in Alameda.

We came here for an afterwork dinner gathering with a group of 12, and made a reservation ahead of time.

When we arrived, we were seated quickly. We ordered a bunch of dishes, so I'll review the ones that I remember.

I had the Pad Se Ew, Pad Thai, Angel Wings, Spicy Wings, Tom Kha, and the BMV Ultimate Papaya Platter.

Pad Se Ew, the fried flat wide rice noodles with black soy sauce, broccoli, and eggs. I really liked the flavor, and the noodle texture was to my liking.

Pad Thai, the fried thin rice noodles with tamarind sauce, tofu, eggs, and bean sprouts. Unlike Pad Se Ew, this dish felt a bit mediocre, the flavor was pretty bland.

Both Angel Wings and Spicy Wings tasted great; the crunch and seasoning were spot on.

Tom Kha, a coconut soup with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and fresh mushrooms, chicken or shrimp. Really creamy and delicious.

The BMV Ultimate Papaya Platter came with papaya salad, pork rinds, noodles, cabbage, and sticky rice. You can choose up to 3 proteins and a type of papaya salad, like Thai or Lao. We had the Thai Papaya salad with 2 crispy pork and angel wings. The papaya salad was really fragrant and paired well with the crispy pork, which helped cleanse the palate.  The crispy pork had a strong umami flavor, with the rich fattiness of the meat itself. You could smell the roasted meat and rendered fat. aroma.

Also, their Thai Iced Green Tea and Beerlao are worth a try!

google.description: Pho, spring rolls & other Vietnamese specialties in an unpretentious counter-service eatery.

top_reviews.content:
On the better end of pho restaurants around Oakland.

Prices are very fair with the portions you get. They’ve have an extra large option we tried and it’s huge !

Broth is very good and rich. It’s deeply flavored but still clear and not murky so you can bet it’s authentic.

The noodles can be improved tho, the noodles were cold and clumped together, makes me feel noodles pre prepped and they let it sit out precooked for some time and when a customer orders, they dump it in a bowl with the broth, hence the coldness and clumping

As with any authentic Asian restaurant, service is nonexistent, so you can bet the food is on the better side.

Very delicious, loved the pho it came with a perfect amount of garnishes, the place had these really nice sweet pickles and extra spicy sambal and Sriracha. The tea was not served in a tea cup which I thought was a bit funky lol. The pho flavor had just the right amount of complexity, not overly distinct on any particular spice, just the right blend. There was a nice amount of meat served with the regular size. The restaurant gets a lot of natural light and has friendly and quick service. I liked the overall dining experience and was pretty happy with the food.

The main reason for the 3-star rating is because it's not very sanitary. Our server was a young man with a silver earring on his left side who came to work obviously sick with a cold. He kept rubbing his nose with his bare hands while serving people. I kept a close eye and he never handled our food. He was restocking utensils with his bare hands touching the mouth side of all of them. Thankfully an older gentleman brought our food. Only once I saw the young man go to the restroom and it's not clear if he washed his hands. Take a soup and go home and rest dude.

The menu is very basic. They didn't have my favorites, beef stew or ox tail. I tried the brisket, rare steak, and tendon. The broth was good, though it could have used a bit more protein. The pickled chilies at the table were a good addition for flavor and heat.

Would have given 4 stars but seeing this server with a cold touching everything made me almost lose my appetite.

Good stuff. Small little parking lot. Staff super friendly and chill and nice. Drinks and smoothies tasted good. Pork a bit dry but that's a vibe kinda. Overall food came out fast and experience was pretty standard. Thanks.

“Phở Hương Quê” basically means pho of the homeland. I’m pretty picky about Vietnamese food in the Bay, but this spot hits.

It’s a low key hole in the wall. They have a special vegetarian section of the menu with tons of options, which is nice because many Vietnamese spots are usually not vegetarian friendly.

The grilled shrimp and vegetarian vermicelli bowls are *sublime*. Vermicelli can be hit or miss since a lot of places don’t season the protein enough, but here everything is nicely marinated and perfectly charred. The fish sauce ties it all together and they give you extra if you ask for it.

Spring rolls are bomb too.

They’re on DoorDash and other delivery apps, but you’ll save a few bucks just going in, and even more if you pay cash.

top_reviews.content: First time trying this place and everything was amazing. Me and my husband shared lasagna and linguine with arrabbiata sauce, then finished with the best tiramisu I’ve had and a perfect cappuccino.

Okay listen… if you go to Luna Cocina and don’t get Deena, Zahir, and David taking care of you, I’m telling you right now you are missing OUT 😭👏🏽

Let’s start with my girl Deena, my AMAZING server!!! When I say she set the tone for the entire experience, I mean that. She was so attentive, so warm, and just locked in the whole time. We never had to look around or wait on anything. She was already there. Drinks refreshed, orders handled smoothly, everything flowing exactly how it should. And the way she carries herself? You can tell she takes real pride in what she does. That kind of service is what makes people come back and ask for you by name.

Now Zahir… he was ON IT. Supporting the table, making sure nothing was missed, keeping everything moving seamlessly. The teamwork between him and Deena was flawless. You could feel that they genuinely care about the guest experience!

And David?? Let me tell you, it’s the attention to detail for me. So kind, so quick to help, and so intentional. He brought my soft serve margarita with a huge smile on his face so I have to give him props too. He added to my amazing experience!

Now let’s get into this FOOD and DRINKS because wow 😭🔥

The queso with steak? Rich, flavorful, and done RIGHT. The corn ribs? So good, perfectly seasoned, and something you just keep going back to. And baby… even the chips and salsa deserve their own moment. The salsa tastes homemade like you can tell it was made fresh with care. That alone had me impressed.

And the margaritas??? Yeah they are not playing over here. You can choose from so many flavors like mango, peach, strawberry, coconut and more, and every single one is actually GOOD. Not watered down, not basic… flavorful and balanced.

And of course we had to try the viral soft serve margarita 🙌🏽 I got the strawberry and pineapple and it was EVERYTHING. Fun, refreshing, and honestly just a whole experience on its own.

Overall, the food was amazing, the drinks were hitting, but the SERVICE??? Next level. Deena, Zahir, and David didn’t just do their jobs, they created an experience that makes you want to come back again and again.

I took my time to write this because I want to give them ALL the recognition because they truly deserve it 👏🏽

Great little Italian restaurant with an open kitchen. Everything was fresh and homemade. Caprese salad. Sauteed greens was a big plate of kale perfectly sauteed, with whole garlic cloves. And homemade meatballs. A perfect meal!!

Went to this restaurant with my boyfriend. Ordered a salad with chicken, they charged $8.50 for 3 pieces of chicken that was tasteless. (btw just the salad was $10, so the chicken was almost as expansive as just a single salad. 3 pieces of chicken, nonsense) then we ordered lasagna and linguine with alfredo and chicken. again $8.50 for 3 pieces of chicken which we didn’t know about. lasagna seemed reheated and there was a part that was completely frozen, hard to eat. linguine was completely tasteless, not a single flavor, horrible. Service was whatever, only saw the server twice. Ended up paying more than $70 for horrible flavored meals. Never coming back.

Luca Cucina Italiana is one of those hidden West Berkeley gems that feels like a slice of Italy—at least as far as I can tell, having never been to the motherland myself. I’ve eaten at plenty of places where people swear the food is authentically Italian, and this spot has that same unmistakable flavor. The homemade pasta is the real deal, and their tortellini is absolutely bomb. If you're looking for a vegetarian option, though, be sure to ask in advance.

The lasagna and chicken marsala come up a lot in other reviews, and I get why—classic comfort food, done right. The garlic bread? Personally, not my favorite. They season it a little heavier than I’d like, leaning on the saltier side. But that’s a minor quibble when the rest of the meal delivers.

I’ll admit, I’ve had an off night or two here in th
e past, but lately, they’ve been on a streak. The last three times I’ve been, it’s really been hitting. Add in the cozy, homey vibe and friendly service, and you’ve got a spot that’s worth revisiting. It’s small, so plan ahead, but if you’re craving fresh pasta with a solid Italian pedigree, Luca Cucina Italiana is worth your time.

top_reviews.content:
I recently attended a lunch celebration at Co Nam for my niece’s high school graduation, and it was a wonderful experience from beginning to end.

The food was outstanding. Every dish I tried was beautifully presented, fresh, and full of flavor. The shrimp rolls were light and refreshing, the grilled prawn citrus salad was vibrant and delicious, the garlic noodles were packed with flavor, and the roti with curry dipping sauce was impossible to stop eating. Everything that came to the table was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented.

What impressed me just as much as the food was the service. Our group spent hours at the restaurant enjoying the celebration, taking photos, and catching up with family. Throughout the afternoon, the staff remained warm, attentive, and accommodating. Even as we lingered well after lunch, they never made us feel rushed and continued to provide excellent service.

The atmosphere was perfect for the occasion. The restaurant felt inviting and the attention to detail throughout the space complemented the celebration beautifully.

It's easy to find a restaurant with good food. It's much harder to find one that pairs excellent food with genuine hospitality. Co Nam delivered both. I left impressed not only by the quality of the meal but by how welcome they made our entire group feel.

Thank you to the Co Nam team for helping make such a special day even more memorable.

Just paused a moment from this wondrous meal to write this. This is the second time I’ve come here. I refrained from a second order of Oysters. They were great, but the flavor from the “Filet Cheese “Phorench” Dip, Beef Pho Broth Banh Mi will send you to a familiar place you’ve never been to before. You will remember what content is once you’ve finished.

I really enjoyed this place. I bit outside the downtown area but in a nice street with several other places. The interior is relatively small but well decorated. This place is best for 2-4 people. The food was cooked by a seasoned cook from the motherland. They only had one server when we went there for lunch, but things moved relatively well. I really enjoyed the mocktails. The food was all around solid with a lot of flavor and plenty full. They also have an extensive selection of cocktails. Overall, I would give this place a visit and enjoy some really good Vietnamese food.

We went here on a Saturday around 3pm and were able to get seated right away. The inside is small and large selection at the bar. It is nicely decorated and could be a good evening spot to hang and drink. We got the ibiza, which is their sweetest drink, and the saigon french quarters, which was strong. Both were good and I look forward to trying other drinks here. They have quite the menu for drinks- alcoholic, non alcoholic, wine, juice, tiki drinks, etc. As for the food, I really enjoyed the roti and the fried wicked buns. The buns remind me of vietnamese donuts and are on the sweet side. They weren't dry at all or hard. They are not that dense either. The ribs and pork belly were fine, but I would be interested in trying more of their other food menu items as well. Parking is on the street and may be hard to fine. Staff was nice and attentive.
Good service! We liked most of the dishes (one in our party didn’t think this deserves a 5 star).  They have outdoor sitting which helped because we went with our dog.

top_reviews.content:
We had a great experience at GangNam Jjajang!

We ordered the jajangmyeon, jjambbong, jjambbong-jajang combo, shrimp fried rice, and sweet and sour pork (small), and everything was satisfying.

The jajangmyeon had a rich and savory black bean sauce that was perfectly balanced, and the noodles were chewy and well-cooked. The jjambbong was full of flavor with a deep, spicy broth and generous seafood, making it very comforting.

The shrimp fried rice was light yet flavorful, with nicely cooked rice and plenty of shrimp. The sweet and sour pork was crispy on the outside and tender inside, with a sauce that wasn’t overly sweet, which we really appreciated.

Overall, the portions were generous, the food came out quickly, and everything tasted fresh and well-prepared. We would definitely come back again!

This is the perfect place to hit up if you’re like me and experience intense, borderline violent jajangmyeon cravings. Sometimes you just need a big, comforting bowl of chewy noodles covered in rich black bean sauce, and this spot absolutely delivers.

Their jajangmyeon is done just right. The sauce is savory, hearty, and satisfying without feeling too heavy, and the noodles have that perfect chewy texture that makes the whole dish so comforting. The portion size is also massive, so you could definitely share one order between two people—although I completely understand wanting one all to yourself.

I also tried their fried chicken, which was decent, but it wasn’t the standout for me. It was fine as a side, but compared to the noodles, it didn’t feel like something I’d go out of my way to order again. Next time, I’d probably skip the chicken and focus on what they’re clearly known for: their noodle dishes.

Overall, this is a great spot when you’re craving classic, satisfying Korean comfort food. I’d definitely come back for the jajangmyeon and would recommend it to anyone looking for a generous, flavorful bowl of noodles.

Gangnam Jajang is the real deal!!! I am used to Korean-Chinese as a Korean who used to eat jajngmyeon (black bean noodles) and tang soo yook as a kid.

I started with the iced tea with mango cubes - refreshing, not too sweet, and the large mango cubes at the top were a nice touch. They even had a frozen bear on the top.

The wool-myeon and the chili oil black bean noodles stood out. The wool myeoj noodles have a silky texture with super generous portions with fresh seafood. The chili oil black bean noodles had a savoy jajang base with a kick of heat. The chili oil adds fragrance and makes the noodles super addictive.

The tang soo yook was crispy but chewy on the inside. Definitely recommend this as an appetizer.

The portions are generous based on the price point and the servers were very attentive too!

If you’re anywhere near Oakland and craving Korean-Chinese, do yourself a favor and check it out.

I’ve been coming to Gangnam Jajang since they first opened in January 2022, and it’s been great to see how much the restaurant has evolved over the years. The food has continued to improve little by little, and I can see why it has become a spot that appeals to both Korean and non-Korean diners.

One of their newer dishes, the Spicy Chili Pork Gan-Ja-Jang, is definitely worth trying if you enjoy a little hot. It can sometimes feel quite rich, but the kick from the peppers cuts through that richness surprisingly well. The combination is savory, spicy, and nicely balanced without losing the deep flavor you want from a good fresh Jajang sauce.

I also really like that they’ve added more size options for their Tang-Soo-Yuk (sweet and sour pork). It makes it much easier to order when dining alone without committing to a huge portion. The one pictured here is a medium, which I’d say is plenty for 2-3 people to share. The coating is crisp without being overly heavy, while the pork stays tender and juicy inside. Paired with the sweet and sour sauce on the side, it has that satisfying contrast in texture that makes good tangsuyuk so addictive :-)

After coming here for years, it’s nice to see a restaurant that keeps refining its food rather than simply staying the same. Definitely a place I’ll continue coming back tho whenever I’m craving Korean-Chinese food !

Wonderful Korean food at low prices, cooked fresh to order in a friendly casual venue. Had the jajang noodles with fried chili sauce, and was immediately impressed by the chewy home made noodles and aromatic sauce. Portion was enormous. The fried pork is fluffy and comes with a unique dipping sauce, bright and acidic, keeps you eating! I highly recommend.

top_reviews.content:
If you are looking for a late night cheesesteak, I would recommend IB’s (but if Cheesesteak Shop or Mills Cheesesteak are open I might reconsider). However, there were a few flaws with my experience.
I ordered the Truffle cheesesteak but instead got the surf n’ turf (small $16). It was fulfilling, I added hot peppers and mushrooms too for $1 each along with Garlic Onion Rings (except when I got my order it did not come with garlic which was an extra $2). The cheesesteak itself was great quality of meat and decent portion. Bread on the cheesesteak was fluffy, cheese was spread reasonably, and the toppings hit just right. The onion rings looked big and plump (there were about 7 or 8) but there was only filling for about 2 of them while the rest were shells. Ranch was good, spicy sauce (not ghost pepper, next time I will try) was like Raising Cain’s but with a hit of spicy similar to siracha level.
Overall, for the $30 I spent, I would say this place is alright. I understand I went at the end of night so things were forgotten and the customer service was great (the cashier was friendly). I would try one more time to see how good the Lamb meat is. I am glad they use halal and ingredients seem to be fresh. Hopefully, I will rate this place higher when I return.
Ordered chop cheese and garlic fries the sandwich came out really greasy when I asked for it to be remade I batley got  meat and lots of lettuce
First time here, did not disappoint. Highly recommend anyone that is hungry and can devour a big steak hoagie!  Flavor was on point and worth every penny!  Will definitely be back!

The food is good enough, but when I sat down to eat, one of the workers cleaned a big mirror near me with Windex. So I went outside and sat at table there. Then I noticed someone else sitting down to eat on the opposite side of the window and the same worker got the windex out and started cleaning a window not two feet away from the guy eating. He got up and left too. Do they realize what the smell of Windex does to the flavor of their food?
At first sight I was highly disappointed. The sandwich was fairly small compared to a normal full sized cheese steak.

The flavor is incredibly comforting—it might not be "Michelin star" complex, but it tastes like a warm, home-cooked meal made by family. Plus, the service is consistently fast and very welcoming to solo diners. I'll definitely be back!

We tried the house Pho (with everything in it) so while the broth was “clean” and okay, it didn’t really stand out and wasn’t hot enough to my liking when served, but it was still good.  We also ordered three other dishes and really enjoyed them too, and we would like to try other dishes next time. I recommend this place.

Definitely recommend! I got the turmeric chicken Bahn Mi and it was fantastic. The chicken itself was so flavorful and wasn’t dry at all. The servers were all very nice and the restaurant itself is very clean and has a great vibe. Looking forward to coming back next time I’m in the Bay Area :)

Started with Pani Puri, the crisp puffs with tangy spiced water were wonderfully refreshing. The Butter chicke and Malai Chicken were full of rich flavor, made with top-quality ingredients. The garlic cheese naan was exceptional, pairing perfectly with the curries and delicious on its own. A truly memorable meal.

Food was incredible.  Service was a bit slow...not enough staff.  Place was jam packed, however the tables very tightly arranged IMHO.  But, again, food was sooooo good.  I have eaten a LOT of Indian food in my time, this food was terrific.

Came for a late dinner on a Wednesday evening and this place was packed! We were seated within 5 minutes of arriving at 8pm.

To start, we ordered the watermelon salad to share. The presntation was gorgeous and colorful, was a refreshing appetizer to get us started.

For beverages, I had a pour of the fieldworks Belgian and my friend had a mango lassi. Both beverages were served in bespoke glassware and were delicious.

For mains, we ordered the butter chicken and lamb curry (both medium spicy) to share, with a side of naan and two sides of rice. The butter chicken was rich and creamy, while the curry lamb had a nice balance of flavor and heat. Both were enhanced by the side of garlic naan.

top_reviews.content: Not the most glamorous looking place inside but I'll tell you what, the food and prices definitely compensate for it. Great tasting Chinese food with nice-sized portions with unbeatable prices. The Mongolian beef and salt and pepper rock cod are definitely my go-to dishes here. Living here in San Francisco almost all my life I learned the places that are not the most prettiest crank out the best foods.

I recently dined at a Golden Kim star Chinese restaurant in San Francisco, and I must say, it exceeded my expectations. The Mongolian beef was tender, flavorful, and perfectly spiced. The vegetable fried rice was equally impressive, with a great mix of fresh vegetables and well-seasoned rice that complemented the beef beautifully. The steamed dumplings were a delightful surprise, with a soft, delicate exterior and a delicious, savory filling.

What really stood out, though, were the portions. They were simply incredible—the best I've ever had at a Chinese restaurant, hands down. I left feeling more than satisfied, with enough leftovers to enjoy another meal at home. If you're looking for great Chinese food with generous servings, this place is definitely worth a visit!
We ordered take out for a quick meal. As an Asian I have to say the food is authentic! Fast, affordable and quality to its price. Will order again.

As a vegan visiting from Australia this was a great find for us this evening! Plenty of options to choose from, very generous portions, accommodating of my husband’s not-too-spicy request, and produced lovely flavoursome dishes - we had the sizzling basil tofu, Mandarin spicy eggplant with tofu and veggie fried rice (egg free). Best value in San Fran!

Food was delicious and service was friendly. First time eating here and I will definitely eat here again. Reasonable price, great taste, and abundant portions. We ordered the beef chow fun and some other dishes I forgot.

Excellent, late-night Sichuan option in San Francisco — perfect for a pre-game or post-night sustenance when bar crawling along Polk. Dishes are elegantly mala, not too full-on, not too mild.

Highlights include Szechuan Noodle Soup, Salt and Pepper Prawns, and Garlic Sautéed Fish Filet.

Impressive flavor balance in a city where it’s not so easy finding good Chinese beyond Cantonese. Will certainly be back!

One of the reasons I gave 3 stars is because this place doesn't know if it's a regular restaurant or a casual fast food restaurant.  The servers don't take traditional orders, you scan a qr code and then you choose, order and pay for food through the website. Server delivers you the food you ordered. The sizzling rice soup lacked some of the seasoning and vegetables. Sesame chicken was tasty. Fried rice was good.
S e r v i c e was okay s

Don’t Come Here.

The lady at the front desk on Saturday night had one of the worst attitudes I’ve ever experienced. We came in around 12:10, asked if they were still taking customers, and she let us sit down. Since it was our first time, we ordered two entrées first to try the food before deciding whether to order more.

When I politely asked for extra bowls, she looked straight at me, snapped, “More bowls?”, and walked away with an attitude.

If she’s the owner, I honestly don’t see this restaurant lasting very long. You can’t take people’s money while treating them like they’re bothering you. Absolutely terrible customer service.

google.description: Rustic pick for artisanal Neapolitan pies, starters, pastas & soft-serve ice cream plus beer & wine.

top_reviews.content:
The Benchmark Pizza was very good. Sauce, crust, all of it. Delicious.  We also ordered the chopped salad and spicy carrots and a pasta dish that I can't recall the name of.

Overall the experience was great. If you have more than two people, order a second pizza.

Benchmark continues to be one of my favorite spots when a serious pizza craving hits. Last night, I stopped in specifically hoping to try the eggplant pizza, but unfortunately they were sold out. Since the only other pie I’d previously had there was the brown butter sage — delicious, though I’ve learned lemon on pizza simply isn’t my thing — I decided to go with their classic Benchmark margherita instead. It absolutely delivered.

This is Neo-Neapolitan pizza done right: bright, fresh tomato sauce, creamy mozzarella, torn basil, and a beautifully balanced crust with a perfectly thin base, nicely charred underside, and those airy, leopard-spotted edges that make wood-fired pizza so satisfying. Simple, restrained, and incredibly well executed.

It was an unusually warm evening, so I opted to sit outside. My only real complaint is that the tables closest to the street sit noticeably on a slant, making it a bit of a challenge to keep plates and glasses from slowly sliding downhill throughout the meal. A small detail, but worth noting.

That said, the staff were genuinely lovely and welcoming, and the overall experience was exactly what I was hoping for. One final recommendation: do yourself a favor and ask for a side of olive oil for dipping the crusts. It’s the perfect finishing touch.

I’ll absolutely be back the next time the craving strikes.

This place serves the best vegan pizza I’ve ever had—worth a visit for that alone. Highly recommend! I also loved their sparkling red wine; we thoroughly enjoyed it. The lemon pizza and the sage pizza were excellent as well.

A few small suggestions as feedback: it would be great to see some vegetarian pasta options added. All the appetizers leaned on sweetness, which wasn’t quite our preference—having a few truly savory starters would be nice. Some chocolate-based dessert options would also be a welcome addition.

Overall, this is easily one of the best pizza spots around! 🍕

The crust here is hands down the best! perfectly chewy with just the right amount of crisp and char. You can really taste the quality in every bite. Their pasta is also solid, always cooked just right and full of flavor. And no visit is complete without ordering the sundae ice cream! it’s a must-have! Creamy, rich, and the perfect way to end the meal. Highly recommend this place if you’re craving great pizza and a cozy, satisfying meal.

One of best pizza spots in the east bay!  Salami and Calabrian Chili pizza was superb. The meat was out of this world. The Caesar salad was excellent. All ingredients very fresh and well cooked. Flavors well balanced for both dishes. Wish I left room for dessert!

top_reviews.content: Jimmy made my first but not last experience at The Station a wonderful dining experience! I’m from Manhattan and my daughter was looking for a great restaurant for lunch and suggested coming to The Station! We actually arrived at 10:55 and Jimmy explained that they’d be opening at 11 . He was so friendly and sweet thst we happily sat and relaxed for a few minutes before ordering their most delicious kale salads. My daughter had hers with a beef patty and fries! Everything was delicious!

I got a double smash burger with a side of fries and the fries were probably the most perfect fries I’ve had. The smash burger was also great and definitely up there as well. When i did order it probably took five minutes before i got my food. Didn’t feel too greasy, tasted fresh, and have no complaints whatsoever. The spot is also very cozy and a homey feel. If i were to sum up the vibe, think a group of patagonia-puffer-with-chinos-with-a-toque-on corporate group Sunday brunch or somewhere i wish i went with my parents when i was maybe 7-8 years old (in a good way). I paid maybe 20 for my order+tip but i wouldn’t say the price was too crazy considering the quality of the food. I would come back again.

Food: 8.8/10 (phenomenal)
Atmosphere: 7/10 (cozy)
Service: 7/10 (nothing crazy but was quick)
Price: 5/10 (neither cheap nor too expensive)
Overall (8/10)

I've been here twice, once I purchased the Station burger, on a separate occasion the Saigon Smash chicken sandwich. Both selections were PHENOMENAL! The atmosphere is super nice, it feels like a comforting third space. The man at the register, Favi really brought the energy and made my group feel comfortable with whatever we needed, he felt like a ray of sunshine and an essential contribution to the vibe of the restaurant.

Tried this spot for dinner and the smash burgers were seriously so bomb. Easily the highlight of the meal. Super flavorful, and definitely the kind of burger that makes you want to come back. I’ll absolutely be back for another and already have my eye on the Saigon burger for next time.

The shakes, though, were a letdown. They looked good but were pretty lacking in flavor and too watery. The fries were just okay..Nothing bad, but nothing memorable.

My biggest issue was watching the employee pack the fries into the boats with his bare hands. It felt pretty unsettling and honestly unsanitary, especially handling hot, greasy fries that way. Just throw on some gloves or use tongs.

Overall, the burgers alone are worth coming back for, which is why I’m giving 4 stars. I just hope they tighten up the food handling practices a bit.

Very yummy smash burger, fries, and a chocolate shake. Trekked over here from SF to try out their burger and it’s worth the Bart/walk from rockridge. A lovely corner spot in a fancy neighborhood with outdoor seating. The line for ordering can get very very long so be patient.

reviews_snippets.content: "The location and vibes are perfect…def check this place out!"

The mocktails were also really nice! All in all recommend.

Cozy vibe. Nigiri is currently my go-to bc I love to enjoy the purity of each vegetable/fruit.
Eggplant is my ultimate fav. Avocado nigiri is good too but this time there was no truffle salt so that’s what makes this Nigiri. Pickled mango is my new fav in addition to eggplant. Enrygii is saucy!

Currently offering happy hour menu (food & drink) between 5-6pm.

Wow! You will love this place!! It’s rare to find vegan sushi and even more rare when it’s so exceptional. The Pacifica was the perfect amount of crunch, texture, flavor, and layers! The Monterey had a smoky undertone. I wish I could have ordered the whole menu!

As a vegetarian, the sushi’s are a must have! Unbelievable that it’s all vegan. I feel like I’m cheating and eating real sushi. Omg 🤤 so good! Servers were friendly and accommodating. This will be a repeat for sure! Only minor caveat is the place is quite small not enough seating during peak hours, so reserve ahead of time.

Excellent vegan sushi place. A bit on the pricey but kind of worth the experience and ambience.

Chill and cosy ambience. Appointment recommended as it gets pretty busy.

top_reviews.content: Very good prices for a Berkeley dive bar. Knowledgeable bartenders. Able to mix to order and very pleased with their abilities.  Atmosphere changes from empty to packed depending on game days and other events nearby.

Went to Kip's to watch G.S. WARRIORS game. Ordered Pineapple Fish bowl to share, Western burger and 5 tacos on Tuesday night. The burger came out first, 45 minutes after we ordered it. Having inquired about our drink, she admitted to forgetting to place drink order. 5 minutes later, we finally get our libation. She charges $35 for the drink, when they were on special for $25. Apparently the "special " had ended at 8pm. It was now 830. I explained that we ordered the drink well before 8 and were forced to suffer from dry mouth for way too long. Too bad, so sad. Shortly thereafter, my tacos arrived. Lots of screens, upbeat vibe, good food, and billiards are enough to return. Service and reconciliation difficult to attain.
easily the best bar in berkeley when a lot of people go. great dancing and great drink deals on Tuesdays too

The one person who seemed to be in charge up and left when there were some difficulties saying “I don’t know” and storming away, leaving me to scramble through their audio equipment and cables (all of which was extremely dirty and sticky) to figure out how to make THEIR sound system work. It was very chaotic. The inside was hot, sweaty with 0 ventilation and 1 fan. The cherry on top was the staff member who came backstage to flirt with a couple of guests I brought with me, making sexual jokes, physical advances, and being completely inappropriate towards all of us. He made us very uncomfortable and we had to ask him multiple times to leave us alone. It shocks me that college aged students attend a place where staff behave like this, I can only pray this was a one time incident.

The same unhelpful staff from earlier proceeded to shut the event down early, harshly cutting all power and corrupting my USB drive by doing so. This was by far one of the worst experiences I’ve ever had as a DJ and I hope to never set foot in a place like this again.

Theo and Bruna are the best bartenders ever.

They have a great food menu which I've tried most of but my ultimate favorite is the angus hamburger and the chicken strips and the BLT with chips and salsa on the side I'll always come visit cause the bartenders make me feel at home but in a better enviroment. Is a must if u visit Berkeley.
The photo represent Bruna after serving the greatest bloody Mary's I've ever had.

This is now one of our favorites in the area. I would definitely recommend to anyone who’s wanting to try Nepali/Indian Food for the first time.

incredible experience having nepalese thali here. This place is true to its taste Nd serves high quality food.very clean and hygienic place.Amazing vegetarian and pahadi food selection. I also got bir

Pricing is also very good, especially for the flavorful and well made food. If you like your food spicy, ask for it. Default spice local is somewhat mild.

Will definitely visit again when I'm in the area.

I’m usually a salad hater, but the salad was light, flavorful, and just enough.

Delicious dishes! It’s been a while since we’ve been here, but it’s by far, my favorite for Italian. It’s as close as we can get to Italy, but locally. It’s got a nice, chill and relaxed atmosphere. Great place for a small group since it’s a smaller space.

Some vegan options. Had the impossible platter in the past and it was enjoyable.

Usually there because of non vegan companion eater, so limited choices.

Finally ate here and the food is really quite good.  Mezze platter was delicious and I was able to get gluten free pita!  They also have a lot of vegetarian options, many featuring impossible meat. I love this place since being introduced to it by a friend years ago. The croissants taste like those in Europe, their olive bread is delicious, their food is top.  I have always had a great experience both to go and dining in.

The noodles had the perfect texture and bite. The fish was well seasoned however not very plentiful. The portion size was good but I would've liked more fish in the soup. The wontons were good too. Wait times vary depending on what time you get there. Also, customers are very close by, standing in line staring at their phones or at you wating their turn to finally sit down. You order and pay on a tablet once seated.  After trying almost everything on the menu, my go to is just the Beef noodle soup, spicy broth and thick noodles. It does not lack flavor and is never overly salty. The beef is always tender and noodles have the right amount of chew and taste fresh. On the side, the house wontons in chili sauce. A little salty and not really spicy in my opinion but flavorful with a good chew from the dough. Can be a little loud but once your food arrives I have noticed people stop talking to their companions and just eat. Good sign. This place is has always consistently good.

Wow wow wow this place was so good!!!! They have one clearly labeled vegetarian noodle dish and it tasted so good. Full of vegetables and the noodles were perfect. I’m definitely going to come back multiple times here.
