top_reviews.content:
I was waiting for the hype to die down a bit before trying Sforno, and I'm glad I finally did because it absolutely did not disappoint. I placed my pizza order online for pickup right when they opened, and when I arrived there was no line, though that could definitely be day and time dependent since I went on a weeknight. They had blocked the Pizza Portafoglio from online ordering, but it was easy enough to add on in person, which was well worth it.

This is very much a grab-and-go spot, with only a handful of 2-tops available, but there are a ton of outdoor seating options nearby, including the various bars that are all outside food friendly as well as Patricia Green just across Hayes, which makes it easy to enjoy your meal with a drink and/or soak in the weather.

In a city full of fantastic pizza options, I genuinely thought the pizza here was outstanding. The crust is airy and chewy with charred spots throughout, and while the undercarriage is not super sturdy, I think that is a feature, not a bug for Neapolitan-style pizza as it tends to have that signature "flop". That especially works for the Pizza Portafoglio, which is folded over twice and makes for the perfect compact bite on the go. It is surprisingly packed with flavor from such a simple lineup of ingredients, with the tart San Marzano red sauce, creamy cheeses, fresh basil, and the spicy, salty spianata piccante all working beautifully together. For just $11.50, or even less without the salami, it is one of the best deals in the city for a satisfying meal.

I also tried the Mortadella Speciali and loved that just as much. It had all the qualities I loved in the Pizza Portafoglio, but with the added richness of thin sliced mortadella, salty shaved parmesan, crunch from pistachios, and generous dollops of burrata throughout. I did not have room for dessert, but everything on the menu looked and sounded delicious, and I'm already planning to go back for those and to try the panozzis, especially the porchetta.
GREAT pizza! Nice sauce, just the right amount of cheese, lovely crust, fresh basil… and at a price so low it seems like a mistake. We will absolutely be back!

Probably the most authentic Italian style pizza you can find in the city. The lady in the kitchen helped me find the bathroom and she had a thick Italian accent so I’m assuming she’s the “Nonna” of the place. The highlight was the dough, textbook Neapolitan. The wallet pizza for $9.50 was our favorite, and the popular Spicy Trouble was also solid. Probably a 5 star spot for those that prefer Neapolitan style + mild toppings and sauce (I prefer NY style so giving it a 4 star). Highly recommend nonetheless. Parking is really tough as it’s in the center of Hayes Valley FYI.
The best pizza around! Small store and long line of people out on Octavia Street. Staff work nonstop and seamlessly together to make those soft and chewy pizzas.

One of the best pizzas I’ve had. I got the folded pizza and it was so good! Unfortunately it takes about 30 minutes to get your pizza. I understand that there’s only one person making the pizza which is fine but a suggestion I have is adding a self service station for water and utensils!

These both failed miserably by comparison.

I would much rather pay more for a sandwich that arrives with the fillings as expected.

Sadly, I won’t be back.

To my surprise it is not your typical Vietnamese vermicelli. I would consider it fusion Vietnamese. Instead of a bowl the meal is served on a plate. It looks like they are trying to accommodate the Western taste in every way. I was most impressed with the egg rolls. I normally don't like the standard Vietnamese egg rolls which are stuffed with some unknown mushy meat. However, the ones here are stuffed with ingredients that you can see and know what they are. Overall the food experience was good. I can't wait to find out how they serve their Pho and rice plate on my next visit.
A couple of things to watch: parking is awful around the area. It's better to come at night. During the day it's all metered parking so that will add cost to your meal. Secondly, prices at this restaurant are about 50% higher than your standard Vietnamese restaurant. I normally pay $10 somewhere else but here I paid $16 plus tips. Still a good experience.

The korean corn dogs are really good. Do not get the potato tornado it is 90 percent fried and 0 percent potato. Also do not get Hotteok they are also like 100 percent fried and 0 filling. I would only recommend for their Korean corn dogs. I was really disappointed with the other things.

One of the worst Indian restaurant, reason: this is totally not run by Indians nor someone who really have any idea about India food. The best small example for you: Biryani is basically kichidi and bisibeli bath and Rogan Josh lamb or chicken are basically marinara sauce base.

We had the mixed grill, chicken biriyani, lamb biriyani, chicken tikka masala, karahi lamb, plain naan, raita, a vegetable curry, papadum, chicken pakora and veggie pakora. The pakoras were pleasant but the chicken tikka masala and lamb dishes were standouts.  The lamb was both flavorful and tender.  The sauces were cleaned up with naan to get the last bit.  We will happily order again.  It's not cheap but it's very, very good.
Generous dinners, vegetables grilled to perfection, waiter very attentive. Owner so friendly. We were visiting from out of town but when we are in town, this will be our favorite spot!

We decided to be adventurous and try a new breakfast spot and ended up at Solano Junction on Solano Ave. The breakfast was flavorful, the portions were good, and the staff was friendly.
Parking can be a little challenging in this area, but that’s pretty typical for Solano Ave but worth the stop.
If you are looking for a local breakfast restaurant with good food and a comfortable atmosphere, Solano Junction is definitely a place to check out.
Ordered a omelette/scramble and fresh squeezed orange juice. The taste and quality was great for my Sunday brunch craving. Made it in time before it was a wait or really busy.

My cousin loves this spot and brought me along — now I see why! She swears by the eggs Benedict and says it never fails her. I had a bite and for my first time trying eggs Benedict, I genuinely enjoyed it too!

Her kids ordered the “mini pancakes,” which were definitely not mini 😅 but still super delicious. I got the breakfast sandwich, which was also really good — hearty and flavorful. The only thing I wasn’t crazy about were the potatoes; they could’ve used a bit more seasoning, but overall still a solid dish. The fruit on the side tasted super fresh, which I appreciated.

I also ordered the strawberry mimosa (my first mimosa ever!) and it definitely tasted “strong” to me — but that could just be because I’m not a mimosa drinker. Still glad I gave it a try!

The vibe of the place is great, the owner was friendly, service was quick, and the whole experience was really enjoyable. Definitely would come back again!

This was my second time at Solano Junction, and once again, it was absolutely amazing! The breakfast was absolutely delicious—from the perfectly seasoned crispy potatoes to the fluffy pancakes, fresh eggs, juicy sausage, and a refreshing fruit bowl.
Topped it off with a smooth mimosa and warm, friendly service. Cozy atmosphere, great food, and consistent quality. Definitely a favorite spot—highly recommended!
Delicious Breakfast. Awesome customer Service. We were seated immediately. Street Parking.

Great very authentic Thai food. Everything is very fresh and the restroom lives up to the "funky" name!

We really enjoyed the Pad Thai, and the fried chicken + roti special was also fantastic. Allow a bit of extra time for parking!
SO GOOD! Everything we ordered was great, standout was the beef and papaya salad.

top_reviews.content: I am an occasional burger eater and this place is one of my favorites. Our last visit was for my son's birthday and he picked it himself. All three of us ordered the same thing, the OG as a double with sauce on the side, plus an order of chili cheese fries. And of course a beer from Two Pitchers to round it out. The place is always busy and outside seating fills up fast, but you can usually find a spot at a shared table.

I was really glad I finally got a chance to eat here after knowing about it for a while.

I got the OG Burger (no ketchup & lettuce bun) and Chicago Dawg.  I really loved how they cooked the burger. The flavors were great and the patties was really juicy.

I thought the Chicago Dawg was OK, I would had maybe wished it was a little bigger so it would match the other Chicago Dogs I've had in thr past, but i'd say it's nice.

Heads up, this place is very popular. Even on a Wednesday around 6:30pm the place was pretty packed. Me and the 2 people I was with had to grab seating in the bar connected to the Resturant, which was also pretty packed. Even thoguh the place can be loud, it has a friendly chill vibe.

Loved the outdoor seating and also the eclectic set up in the pub. We went for fish and chips, but they were sold out so we had burgers. I wouldn't say they were the best. We didn't know they were smash burgers they are okay. 🙄🤷🏽‍♀️

WHEN: Thur @4pm

I wanted to come here at opening time for a few reasons:

- PARKING: It’s downtown so not sure how parking would be.  But lucky for us, we found free parking just around the corner!  When we left around 5pm, more opened up!  I’m guessing it’s because the auto repair shop was closing.

- THE CROWD:  This place is popular and there is usually a line.  Though they have a great amount of seatings available (outdoors), but I prefer a space I don’t feel like I have to menu ear so much around.

- THE FISHWICH THAT SELLS OUT:  I was told about this special fried fish sandwich that sells out.  So in order to guarantee there will be one for me to order, gotta get there early!

It’s my first time, and here’s what I had:

THE FISHWICH - $14.50
Panko crusted rockfish, American cheese, Pickle, Shredded Cabbage, Tartar, Potato Bun.
This is a limited supply item that is only available Wed-Sat until sellout.  A friend shared it was amazing, but sadly I couldn’t agree from one reason:  This was bland.  I love the softness of the potato bun, the crispy and hot pink-crusted textures, and the generous amount of tartar sauce.  But I tasted nothing—just all sorts of texture.  I owned up top it though and finished the entire thing.  Was I satisfied?  No, but my belly is full!

THE DRIVE THRU - $10.50
American cheese, Schmalz onion, Pickle, Lettuce, tomato, Special Sauce, Sesame Bun.
Overall decent burger, and I enjoyed it.  Really can’t say more without comparing it to SCOLARI’S but it’s a solid burger.

HAND CUT FRENCH FRIES - $5.35
Blanched and Fried chipperbec potatoes.
I think I enjoyed these fries because they remind me of SCOLARI’S friends, heh.

I was surprised I did not see o any of their merch for sale because I’m digging that carton character icon!  The brewery it shared a space with has a decent amount of merch though!

Got the Westerner burger and fries for this trip.
The wait is pretty standard for your food, but it's WORTH IT. Crispy edges on the patty and perfectly toasted bun. It has texture without it being dried out. Highly recommend stopping by, maybe ask for light salt on your fries, they have a heavy hand for it here.

The Izumi Judan sake was a hit, dry and yummy

The 5 piece salmon sampler was beautiful and tasty.

We'll be coming back for sure!

Walked with no reservations last night, with an hour to spare before a performance at Davies Hall and the staff were so kind, quick, and thoughtful. The omakase sashimi was fresh, seasonal and delicious, not the usual suspects. Subtle sauces that highlighted the flavor and texture of the fish. Finished with a scallop roll that was sublime. Next time I’m going to try the Lobster tempura or whatever season fare is on offer. Will come back again.

We had such a wonderful experience at Nakama Sushi in San Francisco! The food was fresh and delicious, and the wooden, calm vibe made it even better. But the highlight of our evening was our waiter, who introduced himself as “Uncle Ben.” He was warm, funny, and made us feel completely at home. His energy added so much joy to the night—truly unforgettable service. Can’t wait to go back!
Excellent sashimi. Perfect temperature and quality . Service rapid and always friendly. Will be back after their well-earned new years week off.

top_reviews.content:
My favorite restaurant in Berkeley!
I have been several times over the past 2 years. Food is excellent. Pastas and caprese are top drawer paired with an interesting selection of wines. The service is attentive, friendly but not invasive.
Just a great spot for great food.

I'm a native New Yorker who's been living in CA for over 20 years.  I know good pizza.  The Bay Area has some great pizza places and I like to try them all.  This place was a big let down.  If you like Domino's pizza, you might like it.  I won't be back.

This place is SUCH a perfect neighborhood gem and awesome for everything from family dinners to date nights. We have never felt so welcomed to a decent restaurant with our three very young kids in tow. And the food is always superb.

The food here was soo delicious!! We ordered the Ancient Grain Cheese Cannelloni and the Pennoni alla Norma (with Pennoni subbed for a very nice, soft Tagliatelle). The crepes in the Cannelloni were just the right amount of crispy, the Sheep milk ricotta had a very nice unique flavor, and the tomatoes were so well cooked and flavorful. Everything worked together so well! And the eggplant in the Pennoni alla Norma literally melted in your mouth leaving just the flavor of pure eggplant goodness. Paired with a very nice tomato garlicky sauce, and the very soft pasta noodles, it was also a very comforting dish. My girlfriend and I were both very impressed with both dishes! The serving sizes were also enough to leave us very filled after both dishes, and the prices were appropriate for the quality and amount of food.

Being vegetarian, I was very happy to see the wide variety of vegetarian options as main entrees on the menu. At many places, I've found that the vegetarian options are basically the non-vegetarian options with meat removed, but the vegetarian options here all felt like very complete and intentional meals designed to be had as is.

The service was also phenomenal. Our waitress was very nice and was patient in giving us recommendations. And at the end, one of the other ladies gave us a very passionate and interesting lesson on the history of Sicilian cuisine and how it is influenced by so many different cultures!

Cozy Italian restaurant in North Berkeley with great service! There was a good selection of pizzas, salads, and pastas. The interior is on the smaller side with a cozy feel. My friend and I ordered a combo pizza and the norma pasta to share and we both had enough left over to take home. Didn’t feel like it was especially unique or a “wow” factor, however.

Had a great experience having breakfast. The vegetarian options were really good and so were the drinks.

Group of 4. Ordered several dishes and everything was delicious. The customer service was great, especially considering how busy it was during Super Bowl weekend but the staff handled the crowd like pros! Would definitely recommend this place. Make reservations, especially on popular weekends!
Easily the best egg bennys I've had so far in SF! The coconut cream matcha was also really good, although I would order it with less ice next time. I got takeaway and the order was ready pretty fast.

top_reviews.content:
We ordered two large bowls of pho, but the portions were noticeably inconsistent. One bowl had significantly more noodles and ingredients than the other. The amount of meat in both bowls was also very limited.

We also ordered the fried chicken wings, and they were by far the worst part of the meal. The wings were extremely dry, greasy, and lacked any of the texture or flavor you would expect from freshly fried chicken. They tasted as if they had been cooked long before being served and simply reheated. To make matters worse, one of the wings still had feathers attached, which was honestly unacceptable and raised serious concerns about food preparation standards.

The meatballs were low quality and had a texture more like processed filler than actual meat.

Communication was also difficult. We clearly asked for two large bowls of pho. When the staff didn’t understand “large,” we tried saying “big bowl,” but it was somehow interpreted as adding extra meatballs instead.

I also ordered a Thai tea, but it took an unusually long time to arrive. I had already finished my bowl of pho before the drink was brought to the table. When it finally arrived, it was overly sweet and not particularly enjoyable.

We only came here because it was one of the few places open in the morning. Unfortunately, the food quality, service, and overall experience did not meet expectations. If you have other options nearby, I would recommend trying somewhere else.

The staff working there were nice but the service was lacking.  We waited a while for our food to come (about 35 minutes) and when it did,it was a bit lackluster.  The portions for the Bahn Xeo ordered just had small pieces of meat and shrimp.  The beef pho is just average,nothing to write home about.  They have nice tables and seating outside if you like. Also ,you can play the lottery at this place.  Once is enough for us at this restaurant.

Stopped into this place to have Pho for breakfast. I got the Brisket, Meatball and Steak Pho. The Steak was kinda tough but the broth had depth, it was beefy and flavorful. The basil and bean sprouts were fresh, which I appreciated.

I also tried the coconut juice. It was fresh off the the tree. I felt instantly hydrated after drinking it. What a treat it was to be able to scrape the inside of the coconut out and eat it fresh. 😋

top_reviews.content:
Union Square Pizza truly delivers an exceptional slice of Italy right to your table. From the very first bite, it’s clear that authenticity and quality are at the heart of everything they serve. The pizzas are simply outstanding—especially the pesto pizza, which strikes a perfect balance of fresh, herby flavors and a beautifully crisp crust. Pair that with their cheesy garlic bread, and you have a combination that’s both indulgent and unforgettable.
What really elevates the experience is the freshly prepared spaghetti sauce served alongside the garlic bread—warm, rich, and bursting with flavor. It’s the kind of thoughtful touch that transforms a great meal into a memorable one.
Beyond the food, the hospitality here is second to none. The owner goes above and beyond to make every guest feel welcome, adding a personal charm that’s rare to find. Their warmth and attention to detail truly enhance the entire dining experience.
If you’re looking for authentic Italian comfort food served with genuine care, Union Square Pizza is an absolute must-visit.
Great spot and it's open till midnight! Great to pick up some slices. NY style pizza with some Mexican style. It's a bit costly, but worths it.

Best pizza in San Francisco!
Union Square Pizza & Kitchen was fantastic from start to finish. Ramy provided great service—friendly, fast, and made the experience even better.

The New Englander pizza with hot honey was outstanding, with the perfect balance of crispy crust, savory flavor, and a touch of heat. The Chicken Bacon Ranch (CBR) was rich and satisfying, and our custom garlic pesto pizza did not disappoint. They had baklava which we had to give it a try and it was excellent and the perfect sweet finish.

If you’re looking for the best pizza in San Francisco, especially near Union Square, this place is a must-try. We’ll definitely be back! 🍕🔥

Late night, finishing up work. It was 10pm and I was looking for somewhere to grab a pizza. While wandering the Union Square area, I stumbled across this place and was not disappointed. When I first arrived, there was no one else there - just the staff. I first had to check if it was open. The staff promptly told me yes and welcomed me in. I ordered a pepperoni pizza and a beer. The staff were polite and the service was quick. The pizza was fantastic. I wouldn't say I'm a pizza connoisseur, but I know what I like, and I loved this one. Over the hour i was there, it filled up with other and also some takeaway orders were placed and collected. Only reason for making down atmosphere to 4 stars was that it was a little quiet. But maybe that is normal for a Wednesday night and I know some people like quiet.

On my first visit, Ramy and crew were quite accommodating to my special request for cheese on only one side of the Backyard BBQ pie.
Fun dining area with a couple of tall counters and bar stools as well as standard height tables and chairs.  Everything we ordered was yummy.
I will be back soon!

reviews_snippets.content: "Delicious homemade pizzas, salads, salad dressing, calzones and tiramisu."
"Found the place Friday for a late dinner, ordered the combo pizza and baklava."

name: Almond and Oak
address: 3311 Grand Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States

google.name: Almond and Oak
google.address: 3311 Grand Ave, Oakland, CA 94610, United States
google.description: Market-fresh California cuisine & cocktails offered in a warm eatery with a cool warehouse vibe .

top_reviews.content:
Have walked by this spot several times and finally got a chance to try it. I’m so glad I did!  Everything was excellent; the giant wood fired oven adds a wonderful touch to several of the menu items. My favorite was the prosciutto and melon salad, it was salty, sweet, crunchy, and fresh.

The space itself is really nice too with high ceilings, beautiful natural light, and an open kitchen.  Definitely make a reservation so you don’t get stuck waiting.

Came here for lunch with a friend at 1 PM on a Saturday. We came 15 minutes late after our reservation because of parking and they were understanding of it. As soon as you walk in, you're hit with the smell of a campfire from the oven. The restaurant is absolutely gorgeous with an Art Deco design. The ambiance is cozy but elevated.

Benedict (buttermilk biscuit, dungeness crab cakes, marinated swiss chard & beet greens, herbed hollandaise, poached eggs & mixed greens): I'm not a huge benedict person because they can feel heavy, but this one was fantastic. I loved the textures and flavors of the crab cakes pairing with the greens and vegetables. It felt balanced and not too creamy or exhausting to eat. It definitely stands out from the run-of-the-mill brunch benedict.

Vegetable Hash (roasted sweet potatoes, garnet yams, sunchokes, cauliflower, cremini mushrooms, celery root & onion, savoy spinach & poached eggs): This was also delicious and also set itself apart from the standard brunch hash. I loved the different vegetables in it besides being just potatoes and onions. The mushrooms and root vegetables worked really well together.

Everything was well-seasoned. I'm glad we ended up choosing these dishes even though neither were my original top choices (I decided on the menu with my friend). It made me feel like you can choose anything and it'd be a banger.

We were quite full from these dishes, and we forget we also ordered beignets to come out last. They were fluffy and mostly air (but not in a bad way).

The service throughout the meal was good. We were checked on from time-to-time and our waters were refilled, although I wish the water glasses were a little bigger. One small thing to note was that we were given the check while we were still eating, even though the restaurant was still seating people despite it being close to closing time. Unsure if/why we were rushed like this.

Overall, this was a memorable brunch spots I've been to in the Bay (dare I say one of the best?). We left smelling like a campfire. I would recommend it.

I was looking for a fancy place for a girls brunch on a Saturday and chose Almond and Oak because I figured we could go kill time at the farmers market across the street if the wait was too long.

We arrive around 11:30am and luckily a table for 2 was only a 20 minute wait. So we put our name down and walked around the neighboring shops before deciding to go to the flower shop right next door.

We had just finished purchasing a potted plant and some scented shower steamers when I got the text that our table was ready. The hostess sat us at a hightop communal table in the main dining room, which has a rustic warehouse feel and lots of natural light. We started with an Arnold Palmer and a fancy mocktail.

Drooling over all the delicious menu options, we decided to share a few dishes between the two of us. We ordered the skillet cornbread, the baked French toast, and a scrumptious quiche.

The food came out quickly and everything was so good that my date decided to order a second quiche to take home to her man.

The service was attentive, the noise level was mid range, and the overall vibe was hip but not pretentious. We would definitely eat here again, and based on the dishes we saw at neighboring tables, we plan to try the eggs benedict and their sandwiches next time.

I was genuinely confused and kept trying to clarify, even switching into Spanish, before eventually realizing it was meant as a joke. He then walked away without ever directly answering my question and just waited for me to figure it out. top_reviews.content:
When I think of a sandwich that has the ability to make my mouth water just thinking of it, few come to mind, but what the sandwiches they make at Southie is definitely one of them. I’ve had their Spicy Hog, steak with mushroom, a few Cubans, but the one that I always come back to is “The Balls” sandwich.

First off, this sandwich is massive, so be sure that you come here on an empty stomach. These beef meatballs are seasoned to perfection and bursting with flavor. The balls are covered in their red sauce with provolone and Grana Padano, which gives it that nutty and salty flavor that pairs extremely well with the meatballs and baguette. All the juices and cheese just get soaked up to perfection. The baguette bread they use is supplied by La Farine, which is just a few meters away from each other. Just putting out there that La Farine is hands down one of the best bakeries in Oakland, so it makes sense that this sandwich would be so dang good. I’ll be honest that I’m not a big fan of the chips or those chips in general and could be fine with just the sandwich. If you are going to have any sandwich to eat here first, I would highly recommend you try “The Balls” because I promise you will be not disappointed.

I will always say that the dozen or so times I’ve been here, the staff are always so friendly, and the atmosphere is very down to earth. The price of their sandwiches is in the $20 range, but the quality and portion make it totally worth it.

The service was stellar.  Haven't had such friendly and attentive service in quite awhile. The food was very good. We ordered Duck liver pate crostini and Roasted beet and goat cheese crostini.  Seared ahi tuna salad, fried chicken cutlet, beef & pork meatballs, grana polenta and warm ginger cake with roasted pears, vanella-pear brandy anglaise to end a great meal.

Southie has the coziest local vibe—walking in feels like stepping up to your own kitchen counter. Super casual, we seated ourselves and soaked in the relaxed atmosphere.

The menu is minimal, but don’t let that fool you. Everything on it is absolutely stellar. I ordered the poached eggs with bacon over a salad, and my husband went for the breakfast burrito. We consider ourselves breakfast burrito connoisseurs, and this one ranks among the best we’ve had. It skips the potatoes, which some will appreciate (though I do love a good California burrito loaded with fries). We shared bites of each other’s dishes and both were delicious.

The vibe here is totally unpretentious, but the food tells a different story—it’s crafted with real care. And just like being at home, they had wine on tap, so I strolled over to the counter and treated myself to a glass. Highly recommend.

Whether it’s a casual workday stop or a lazy weekend morning, I’d happily come back.

Had the Italian style sandwich here..... Really solid sandwich. What really got me though is the cook gave me this fantastic in-house made habanero sauce then I just ended up dunking over every bite I was absolutely in love with it. Really cool to sit at the counter and watch them cook, chef was such a friendly dude and the server as well! Really enjoyed the vibe of just hanging out and eating my meal

The fried chicken was exceptional, with an interesting take on mashed potatoes underneath — very hearty and filling. The coconut curry chicken was also excellent, though the naan was unusually thick and dry.

We also had the beet salad, which was delicious except for the avocados — they were so unripe that I couldn’t cut them with my fork and knife. Let me start by saying that my son and I found this spot by accident, and he looked it up on Google review and said it looked good! Now, living in California we tend to take Mexican food for granted but in reality it's hard to find a place that has exceptional Mexican cuisine. The menu is relatively small but what's on there really packs a punch!
The inside is light and airy giving you the feeling you could be on the coast and not in a... Well to be honest, kind of a hetchy-sketchy part of Berkeley. But I digress, the inside is very simple but upscale feeling and I love the tall ceilings and skylights. Our server Luis was extremely friendly and the service was fast but we never felt rushed. My son had the spicy pork tacos which he said were great, and I had the chicken verde enchiladas which also were phenomenal! We skipped dessert because we had started with an appetizer that was delicious but really way too much for two. What a delightful accident finding this place, I think it's safe to say we have a new favorite!
The Superb-intendent 🍀

Tasty, flavorful but not heavy Oaxaqueño food in a high ceiling elevated environment.

The drinks were lively but harmonious. The Tuna Tostado was sooo light and good. You could easily just order appetizers. But come as four people if you can so you can share. For two people it would be a romantic outing.

Service was excellent but unobtrusive.

We loved this place! So much seating and good vibes. Food was delicious! We ordered the chicken tacos, chicken enchiladas, a drink. Everything tasted fresh and was brought out very quick. For dessert we had the flan which was rich and hit the spot. We will definitely be back soon!

Had an amazing experience at Mercado 925 while visiting Berkeley. The food was excellent — incredibly authentic Mexican flavors with a modern approach that made every dish feel thoughtful and elevated. The drinks were outstanding, the music and overall vibe were perfect!

Nicole and Jose took such great care of us all night. Super sweet, attentive, and genuinely welcoming.

If you’re in Berkeley, this hidden gem is a must. We’ll absolutely be back!

Wow, just wow.  We lucked into this place...Just looking for a place to eat and found this on Google Maps.  Great venue.  Beautiful interior.  Great wait staff.  And then the food!!!  Try the tuna tostadas (ask for extra tostados).  My Al Pastor tacos were terrific!  Corn tortillas, lots of meat, Great salsa on the side.

top_reviews.content: This is a delicious Thai family owned spot in the Temescal. The food is Issan from Northwestern Thailand. Their specialty is larb - a delicious sort of ground meat (or mushroom & tofu) dish eaten with lettuce wraps and dipping sauce. We’ve also enjoyed the drunken noodles with ground chicken. They have a cool box set for $23 which is enough for two for lunch! It includes larb, choice of protein and green beans. And they have lots of curries!

I ran into this place during Covid and got hooked since. The food is exceptional, I don’t think I have tried anything I didn’t like here. The service also always friendly and attentive. My go-tos are Gai Gra Pao and Drunken Noodles. If you feel adventurous, the chicken heart skewers are delicious. If you can’t tolerate spicy, make sure to make it very clear.
I ate the best chicken wing of my life here. So crisp on the outside, so moist on the inside. Even if you go only to try the chicken wing, it'd be worth a trip.

A small Thai restaurant with a Thai street style.
The food was surprisingly delicious, even the simple papaya salad was great! Their Roti is very different, they put the topping on top instead of dipping it in sauce!

The tables are close together , maybe when it’s full house will not easy to talk with each others !

Overall the food is delicious but nothing that was phenomenal that would warrant me to go out of the way for unless I’m in the area EXCEPT that the fried chicken spring roll and Kao Ka Moo was tasty.

Chicken spring roll has outer layer that was not the usual spring roll and so it gives a nice texture to the meaty spring roll.

The Kao Ka Moo, stewed pork belly, was so tender that it just shreds and the flavor was yummy. This was the entree that we pretty much finished since it was yummy.

Pad see ew was so so. A little on the soggy side which I’m not used to and I prefer pad see ew from another location about 1 mile away that is hands down the best I’ve had.

Nam Kao was ok too.  Texture was lacking since everything was mostly soggy when I’ve like the crispy rice texture together with all the meat and vegetables.

Kao soi had good coconut milk soup but it didn’t have that spices depth to it. If it did, it would have been perfect, just as how I would remember it when I had it in Thailand.

top_reviews.content: As others have mentioned, it’s still a good spot, but there’s definitely room for improvement. We ordered two cheeseburgers and Brussels sprouts. The food arrived quickly, and the server was really friendly and attentive. The food was "good" but not exceptional. We didn’t mind since we were looking for a quick bite and really enjoyed the service and ambiance, but we probably wouldn’t return specifically for the food.

Impressive building with high ceilings and comfortable seating, both inside and out. I went alone but this would definitely be a good place for group gatherings. Vegetarian options available. I had the veggie burger, which itself was great, and it came with a liberal portion of fries. Will certainly be back.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but this experience was too uncomfortable to ignore.
My friend and I (two young women) were at a table with a pitcher of beer and I went to the bar to ask for a glass. The bartender, Joey, stared at me like I was crazy before asking for my ID — which is completely fine — but his demeanor was immediately hostile. Because of how rude the interaction was, my friend calmly asked if we had done something to upset the staff. His became more aggressive and told my friend “I won’t serve you!” For the rest of the night, he made faces at us, smiling and waving sarcastically from behind the bar.

At the end of the night, when we tried to speak to another bartender about what happened, Joey aggressively yelled across the bar, “Do you have something to say to me?” It was intimidating and completely inappropriate. As we were leaving, he continued glaring and making hostile faces. The other bartenders were kind and professional, and encouraged us to leave a review. Unfortunately, the manager was dismissive.
This was openly aggressive behavior that bordered on harassment. We did nothing to warrant it, and it made us uncomfortable for the rest of the night. Completely unacceptable.
Great range of beers and cocktails, good food, the staff are really friendly and helpful, there's plenty of outdoor seating in the quad behind the main bar. But it is LOUD.

This place was solid. It's just really far out there to get to for me so I had never visited before. The wings were good but a little overpriced. The alcohol selection was good and the food had a lot of variety. The bar set up seemed awkward and a nuisance for the 1 bartender that had to go from one spot to the other to get different kinds of beer from the tap.

top_reviews.content: I randomly stumbled into this shop during an adventure last year, and I've already been back three times. It's the kind of place where you could close your eyes and blindly point at anything on the menu, and it'd still be amazing. You say the neighborhood's sketchy? Well, there are plenty of elderly Asian residents around, and the staff at the pastry shop and supermarket are all around 65. The fresh lemonade here is absolutely incredible—perfectly balanced between sweet and sour. It's so good that even the jackfruit smoothie and rice plates, delicious as they are, can't replicate the pinnacle of flavor this lemonade achieves in that moment. The owner and employees, unsurprisingly, are all elderly. Aside from the owner, who's cheerful and loves cracking jokes, the others may not be the talkative type, but they're all incredibly efficient. Their service is better than 90% of restaurants out there—fast, polite, and not a single one of them pulls the "respect your elders" card. You can tell the owner is a kind-hearted person with a tough exterior who genuinely works hard to run a good restaurant. As long as her younger brother is still studying at Laney, I'll keep coming back to eat.

They serve one of the best Vietnamese beef balls and all the intestines noodle soups in Oakland. However, it's a little on the pricy side. Parking is easy—many Seatings. Staffs are friendly too.
Updated on 9/18/23
The business is returning—many customers sit inside and outside during lunchtime. But the prices are also getting prohibitive high. Customers, be warned!

I was here yesterday with my wife, when I went to pay; I paid in cash. The owner of the restaurant took my order and when it was time to pay the bill came out to be $31.45. I gave her $100 bill and she gave me change only $8.55, $60 was missing and when I realized the mistake I went back to the payment counter and the owner refused to pay me back the missing amount. I asked her to check the cameras for evidence and she said she can’t. Even without checking the cameras that she should have access to she still said no. And then I asked, doesn’t she do check and balances at the end of the day to see if the tabs and the money in the register matches, she said no. I was thinking it’s only $60, why would the owner of the restaurant be so greedy against me. I have dined at this establishment ever since I was a child and to have this type of disrespect and dishonesty when given out the wrong change and not pay it back is heart wrenching. I will never return to Pho Hoa Lao.

The foods good. The spring roles are kind of hard and the sauce isn’t that good compared to other places. The regular sized noodles are pretty small, and it’s little bit on the pricy side. BUT, unfortunately it’s cash only for payment which doesn’t make sense in this day of age. Had to go to the local 7 eleven to get cash just to pay. Really disappointed. If you’re looking for good vietnamese food, recommend Ao Sen in Albany. Also FYI there is NO signs saying Only Cash. Just says “For cash- Thank you” really small on top of the cashier.

I tried the Number 1 Special combo at Phở Hòa Lão Vietnamese Restaurant, which includes a mix of ingredients like rare steak, well-done brisket, flank, tendon, tripe, and spring rolls. The pho was satisfying but not exceptional. It's a good spot to curb your pho craving. The standout was their fresh and generously portioned spring rolls, accompanied by tasty peanut sauce.

*Keep in mind, this place is cash only.

Great place for counter service. Very friendly couple (I assume), delicious, no frills, affordable. Twelve dollar chicken curry plate with a marinated egg, potato, carrot and rice. Six piece sushi was surprisingly fresh for three dollars. Out the door total 15.25, cash or Venmo.

top_reviews.content: Tastes Steam Kitchen is a good place to share a meal with a group. The shabu shabu has many options for the base broth and also the items you can cook.

Highly Recommended Hot Pot Spot – Fresh, Flavorful, and Fantastic Value!
I recently visited this hot pot restaurant and it quickly became one of my new favorites in the area. From the moment we walked in, the experience was outstanding.
The ingredients are incredibly fresh — the thinly sliced meats, vibrant vegetables, and seafood all looked and tasted top-quality, with no signs of staleness. You can really tell they source high-quality items and prepare everything daily.
The broths and flavors are delicious! Whether you prefer a rich, spicy Sichuan-style pot or a milder, savory one, the soups are perfectly balanced and packed with depth. The dipping sauces are customizable and addictive — we couldn’t stop dipping and refilling our bowls. Everything was so tasty that we kept ordering more rounds.
Hygiene is clearly a priority here. The tables, utensils, and hot pot stations were spotlessly clean, and the staff maintained excellent cleanliness throughout our meal. It felt safe and comfortable, especially for sharing a hot pot experience.
The service was excellent — attentive, friendly, and efficient. Our server was knowledgeable about the menu, helped with recommendations, and made sure our broth stayed at the right temperature and our plates were cleared promptly. The whole team made us feel welcome and well taken care of.
Best of all, the prices are very reasonable for the quality and portion sizes you get. It’s genuinely good value — you leave satisfied without breaking the bank, making it perfect for casual dinners, family gatherings, or group outings.
Overall, if you’re craving authentic and satisfying hot pot, this place delivers on every level: freshness, taste, cleanliness, service, and affordability. We’ll definitely be back soon!

I pass by this place a lot during my lunch walks and finally decided to give it a try. They offer lunch special mini hotpots, and each pot comes with a free drink, a choice of green tea or black tea.

I was seated quickly, and the server took my order right away. The service was friendly and welcoming. Since I knew what I wanted and only had an hour for lunch, I placed my order immediately, knowing it might take some time to prepare.

I had the Szechuan Spicy Pot, which came with beef, fish filet, enoki, tofu, clam, shrimp, cabbage, glass noodles, fish ball, corn, pork blood, and squid balls, and a choice of rice or noodles. The portion-wise was good, and had lots of different ingredients. But the flavor was lacking; Szechuan flavor should have the bold, numbing, and tingling sensation, but I didn't find any from this pot.

My sister got the Satay Beef Pot; the flavor was spot on. So if you are craving spicy, I would not recommend getting their Szechuan Spicy Pot.
A fun and delicious experience to share with friends.  Strongly recommended if you want to chill and hangout with good food.

It's a new find for me. Evidently, this form of steam kitchen format is very popular new form of restaurants in China. The menu is huge. We did not go for the all-you-can-eat hot pot. Instead we went for the steamed pot. The staff did all the cooking in front of our table, making sure all the lovely fresh seafood is cooked to perfection.  While some dishes come with special tasty sauces, most vegetables are steamed plainly and we go to the buffet of sauces to make our own concoction of sauce dips.

All the seafood we tried, dungeness crab, razor clams, giant clams, scallops and fish were all super fresh and wonderful.

Service was good. Only complaint was when we made reservations, we were allowed only choice of either 5:00 or 7:30.

I did a side-by-side comparison of L&G vs.
Saigon. I tested an iced Vietnamese coffee and pork banh mi. I compares the price, flavor and service. L&G won in my opinion. L&G Vietnamese Sandwich was a great find. The bánh mì was fresh, packed with flavor, and the bread had the perfect crunch. Fast service, reasonable prices, and I’d definitely stop by again

Great service, atmosphere, and freshest kimchi and side dishes. The best for me was the Soy  garlic chicken wings and tofu soup. Will definitely be my go to spot when I'm craving Korean food.

top_reviews.content: This is a lovely restaurant with a great ambiance and great service. I have a gluten allergy and I emailed ahead of time and they assured me they take measures to prevent cross-contamination and my server was knowledgeable about all the gluten-free options. I ended up playing it extra safe and just going with a beet salad with chicken (although they did have gluten-free pizza dough available) which was delicious! Our waitress was extremely detail oriented and attentive to our large party. We had a mix of adults and kids and everybody had something that they liked. I will say that two of the people in our party did not like the Cesar salad, although I didn't try it.

My wife Ellie and I stumbled upon Creekwood while visiting Berkeley this evening, and it turned out to be the perfect find — the kind of dinner that reminds you why you love going out. From the moment we walked in, the atmosphere struck us: warm wood and metal, thoughtful lighting, casual yet genuinely refined. Someone with real design sensibility had a hand in this place.
The bar is great for drop-ins, the staff was wonderful throughout, and the ingredients in everything we ordered were fresh and inventive. We started with the winter salad — kale, pear, endive, lightly dressed — and it was exactly right. The mushroom pizza was delicious. Ellie had a glass of California Chardonnay and I had a Tuscan red blend; both were excellent choices for the evening.
We had the pleasure of meeting the owner, Greg, who has connections to Sonoma wine country — and it was genuinely fun to swap memories and talk shop. That kind of warmth from ownership shows up in every corner of the restaurant.
We'll absolutely be back. Highly recommend Creekwood to anyone looking for a neighborhood gem that punches well above its weight.

We were a group of 10 people, and owner Greg and the team took great care of us. Greg even went to the store to buy an extra umbrella!

Food was all really tasty

Amaaaaazing! Such a special neighborhood gem. We got and love the PEI mussels. Perfect amount of kick and couldn't get enough of that white wine butter sauce. The Margherita pizza and roasted beet salad also are must-gets. The salad has this yummy pistachio praline topping. I could eat that alone as a snack.

Service was warm and helpful, especially with the recommendations. I can't wait to be back and definitely want to try their brunch offerings as well!

top_reviews.content:
Excellent, high-quality food. I loved the fried chicken. It had a very thin layer of crust, which was perfectly crispy without feeling heavy. It was delicious.

I also had the short rib soup, and it was very yummy. The portion was a little big, so it would be great for sharing. I used some of the meat from the soup with the complimentary rice and banchan to make a little bibimbap, enjoyed it so much :)

We also loved the japchae and the barley tea. Everything was excellent.

The server was really nice and friendly, and I appreciated the service. Unfortunately, I was disappointed with the food. I ordered the spicy pork, and it didn’t taste fresh to me. It honestly tasted like it had been sitting for a while or was reheated from earlier.

I also ordered an iced tea, but it had almost no flavor at all. It basically tasted like water with food coloring. The service was great, but the quality of the food and drink was disappointing. I probably wouldn’t come back.

Excellent food quality. Friendly service. I just came back from South Korea a week before and this restaurant food tasted authentic. The bachans (side dishes) were tasty. Fried chickens, oyster pancakes, bibimbap and ginseng chicken soup were all delicious with complex flavors. Best of all they were not salty and I didn’t need to reach for water for the entire meal. While the prices were higher than other places I think you get what you pay for with high quality of food.

Had a fantastic dining experience with my fiancé here. The service was awesome, our waitress was incredibly friendly and very attentive. The food was absolutely delicious, and amazing as leftovers too! The sides (all of the little white dishes) were only  $2.50 which is incredibly rare, and they were very good. We got the fried chicken with soy & garlic sauce on the side (super yummy) and the sweet & spicy fried chicken (the perfect amount of spicy). Super crispy on the outside and perfectly cooked inside and tasted very fresh. 11/10 would recommend. After we were done with our meal we were brought a very yummy complimentary matcha ice cream. We will be back! :)

Came here for am early dinner and the restaurant was empty. Like noone there but me and my girlfriend.

We ordered 2 bbq items and opted to not grill our food and just have it come out. The food was delicious and their banchan was also yummy. We had the brisket and galbi and it came out sizzling, plentiful but most importantly yummy.

We also had the fried chicken which is crunchy and the sauce wasn't overly sweet. It was a nice contrast from the beef. The chicken. Was juicy but there were some bone marrow fragments from cutting through the bone. Still it was tasty and I would have it again just be mindful.

The service was the best part. The guy was so friendly and charismatic. He was very attentive and made our dining experience fun because of how animated he was everytime he came to deliver food.

I enjoyed eating here and the fact we were alone until the end it was a nice vibe given how busy and small most reataurants are. Definitely a gem here in Japantown and worth a try even with all the other kbbq spots in close proximity.

top_reviews.content: This was my first time trying Haitian food and T’chaka was the right spot. It was a little busy when I entered and I chose to sit outside. Chris was the only person on the floor at that moment and he was busy running around to various tables who were paying the bill and asking for service. I was patient and Chris eventually got to my table. He was very hospitable and sat down with me to help me order. I ordered the tradition Griot plate with Passion fruit juice in the side. Chris was literally running from table to table handling different orders, a real hard-worker and tried to give everyone his best attention. Most appreciated. The dish was vibrant in color and beautiful in presentation. They definitely pay attention to detail. The pork was tender on the inside and crispy on the outside, a flavor I’ve never tried before. I really liked the spice in the dish, even the salad had a nice flavor. The portion size was great, well balanced. This was worth the wait, and I look forward to trying a new dish next time. Haitian hospitality is one of a kind and they treat everyone like family.

Food: five stars
Service: five stars
Ambiance: five stars
I ordered the oxtail and my vegetarian friend ordered the legume. The oxtail was so tender and fell right off the bone. Perfectly cooked and deliciously flavored. My friends’ legume tasted like a comfort dish you get at someone’s home. The rice and beans were perfect. I also got the ginger sorrel which is jamaica and ginger and it was so refreshing and *not too sweet*! The servers and workers were so wonderful and kind. Even everyone inside was sweet and asking one another what they got, was it good, etc… vibes were immaculate. The interior decor is cozy and cultural. I’m already looking forward to coming back and trying what everyone else around me got! Doesn’t seem like you can go wrong with the menu. This was my friend’s first time trying Caribbean/Haitian food and this was the perfect place to take him to. Thank you T’chaka for your hospitality and yummy food!

As a Haitian American who hasn’t had the opportunity to visit Haiti, coming here felt like home and incredibly special. From the moment I walked in, I felt welcomed. The beautiful artwork, atmosphere, and overall design of the restaurant made the space feel warm and familiar, and the food genuinely reminded me of home.

Everything tasted fresh and prepared with care. The owners were also incredibly kind and welcoming. I also loved the music! They were playing old-school R&B and soul when I visited, and it complemented the atmosphere perfectly.

The restaurant is in a beautiful area as well, so the entire experience was memorable from beginning to end. You can tell how much work and love goes into this place. If you’re in the area, I definitely recommend stopping by T’Chaka and supporting them. I’m so glad I got to experience it while visiting California. ❤️🇭🇹

We ordered the Legume with an extra side of rice & beans and plantains, not a crumb was left behind. The sorrel and sangria were delicious as well. Love the ambiance here, and enjoyed watching the match here with my kids.

Everything slapped. I’m Haitian and this is just as good if not better than the food I had growing up. Griot was perfect and I had no complaints about anything else. Also had the Empanadas (Haitian patty) and the jerk chicken. Pineapple juice was addicting only regret was not having a third cup.

Is this "OMG the best in the world"? No. But it's not a ripoff and we didn't receive any tourist apathy.

I was super hungry at work and craving a burger, and saw this place was a short walk away. I feel bad for pre-judging the burger’s potential for excellence by its price of $8 (comparably low for SF) - it was absolutely amazing and perfectly cooked throughout. It felt like being at a barbecue where your buddy has been cooking burgers since he could reach the grill. This place is amazing and I’ll definitely be back many more times.

top_reviews.content: I went at 8:10PM (20 minutes before closing), and they treated me so kindly and let me stay and eat past the closing time. It is a cute little place with a good number of crowd even during their closing time. We ordered chicken jhol momo, veg jhol momo, paneer chilli and chicken chowmein. Everything was very tasty. Jhol was very authentic in taste. Loved the chowmein too!

I also want to share a very sweet gesture of the owner. We had a very good conversation while in the restaurant. And after knowing that it’s one of our friend’s birthday, she also gave us complimentary mango lassi. I will definitely love to go to this place again next time I am in Berkeley.

This place became more than just a restaurant for me. I’ve been eating here at least once a week for the past 3 years and the food never disappoints. You can tell that menu item has been perfected and is always made with love. The owners are incredible people, and I know that coming here for lunch or dinner will always make my day. Thank you Khendu and Gopal for being a second family away from home and making incredible food all these years

Modern Indian food. AMAZING. The food is out of this world. A hidden unassuming gem of the bay area. Rich flavors. Tucked away deep by the University of California Berkeley. Somebody said they can never eat butter chicken any where else again- I completely AGREE.

top_reviews.content: Wow, the food here is REALLY good! I tried the Double-Cooked Pork Belly soup with ramen noodles and it's awesome. It's in a rich, super-flavorful broth with a complex blend of herbs and spices that make a perfect blend of savory, a little spicy, and a bit sweet from the scallions, ginger, and other stuff. There's a lot more going on here than a typical soup broth. Plenty of thick-sliced pork like super soft thick bacon strips that fall apart in the bowl.  Note - this type of pork does have a lot of fat (it's supposed to!) so if that's not your thing maybe try their wonton soup. Friendly staff and quick service. I highly recommend this place.

Really enjoyed our visit!
Maybe family run? They seem to speak Cantonese and Mandarin.

The herbal soups were good! We tried #8 and #11 chicken with ginseng. Both tasted healthy but I think I preferred #8 a little more. The soups are in the little cylindrical ceramic containers and make a good appetizer/side dish. Fun to get as a part of one of their special combos.

The special dim sum of garlic clams was tasty and pretty fresh. Excellent value for $6.50!

Enjoyed the sticky rice too - well balanced flavors and not overly salty.

The beef tendon with noodles was tender and had a good texture. A smidge salty for my taste but flavorful and a good size.

Fast & friendly service - there was a bit of confusion about how many soups we ordered but got it sorted out.

The bathroom seems to be upstairs so might be a challenge if there are mobility limitations.

Look forward to trying other dishes next time!

Food as medicine is central to Chinese culture and the food here is tasty and healthy Cantonese fare. Steamed dishes and classic herbal soups. Muted and subtle Cantonese flavors. Exactly the kind of nutritious food you would encounter
in any self respecting Cantonese household.

This place slaps my taste buds, I got lamb noodle soup (flavor), beef shank over rice noodles (succulent), shrimp dumplings (delicate), the chicken buns (the best). Get a rice or noodle dish and the all day dim sum

The variety of the double-boiled soup (燉湯) was amazing. The steam rice with eel wrapped in lotus leaves was great. They also serve dim sum all day. The shrimp dumplings 蝦餃 is delicious. The osmanthus white sugar steam cake (桂花白糖糕) is a delightful surprise!

This was such a delightful find. The atmosphere is inviting with many options both inside and outside. The staff were very welcoming, knowledgeable about the menu and very attentive. The food was so good, fresh ingredients, tasty and seasoned to perfection. The optional red, green and yogurt sauces were fun and added a nice kick if you want it. The spinach was amazing. The Greek salad was yummy. The lentil soup was very good. The Kabob was a home run (husband’s reference). We are already planning our next visit!

Tasty and delicious food. Perfect for a good afternoon. Portions are plenty.

Great service, attentive, kind and always smiling. Timing was perfect, there were no big gaps.

Location was a walking distance from our hotel. Lovely walk to the city centre. And they have indoor and outdoor sitting.

Amazing grilled kabobs! We got the qourma and kabob sampler platters and were satisfied. The sabzi tastes just like my mom makes it. The lamb chops were my favorite. I would recommend if you’re looking for some traditional Afghani cooking!

My friends and I had an amazing lunch this past week. We were so happy one of us who works nearby noticed Saffron. We were all blown away with the delicious food. We were a large group and although he was the only server on the floor, he was the hostess with the most, busser  he was still so attentive to all our needs with a great smile.

top_reviews.content:
I was craving noodle soup and came across this spot. Plus, I hadn't had Lanzhou beef noodles in a while, so it was great to find one in Berkeley!

I ordered the Signature Lanzhou Beef Noodles, which came with tender beef slices, hand-pulled noodles, broth, chili oil, and fresh cilantro. You can also choose your preferred noodle thickness. The broth was rich and fragrant, the noodles were perfectly chewy, and the beef was tender.

I also tried the Scallion Pancake with Sliced Beef. The pancake was crispy and filled with beef and fresh herbs, but it arrived cold, and the flavor was a bit too sweet for my taste. I'd skip this dish next time.

That being said, the Lanzhou beef noodles alone are worth the visit!

Had a wonderful dining experience here! We ordered the Big Plate Chicken with Hand-Pulled Noodles, Lamb Chops, and Lamb Pilaf, and every dish was delicious.

The Big Plate Chicken was full of flavor, with tender chicken, soft potatoes, and fresh peppers in a rich, savory sauce. The hand-pulled noodles paired perfectly with the sauce and were chewy and satisfying.

The lamb chops were incredibly tender, juicy, and had no strong gamey taste. They were easy to pull apart and tasted even better with the dipping sauce and cumin chili seasoning.

The lamb pilaf was also excellent. The rice was fluffy and fragrant, the lamb was tender, and the carrots and raisins added a nice balance of sweetness. The pickled cucumbers were fresh and refreshing.

The portions were generous, the ingredients tasted fresh, and the service was friendly and efficient. Great value for the quality and quantity of food. If you’re looking for authentic Xinjiang cuisine, this place is definitely worth visiting. We’ll definitely be back!

Highly recommend: Big Plate Chicken with Hand-Pulled Noodles, Lamb Chops, and Lamb Pilaf.
Here again! Everything tasted very delicious as always! We got beef broth and lamb broth noodle soup. Both are delicious and have distinct flavors.
We ordered the hand pulled beef noodle soup and DH lamb rib fried rice. They were all delicious. Would come back to try other dishes.
Very good vibes, friendly service, and truly authentic Northwest China food (speaking as someone born there).

top_reviews.content: Outstanding staff, great drinks, loved the oysters plate! Delicious!!! Met the owner, really nice and down to earth. Came out with friends and family and made us feel like home. If you're visiting Oakland, this is a spot you shouldn't miss.

I've only gone to Low Bar a couple times, but I've enjoyed my experiences and find it to be a nice, chill place for folks to enjoy their delicacies like oysters and more.

I've had their blue corn hush puppies each time and they are precious! The cook is consistent and the sauce is delicious.

As a former restaurant service person (now a service person in a different field), I admire seeing the unity in this team. It ripples!

I had their oysters my 2nd visit and loved their unique mignonette they make. Has a nice little kick, yummy acidity, and great addition to the oysters. Didn't need to add any salt, etc. before enjoying.

The staff were so polite and professional when my card had some issues. We cleared it up, all was well, and I left feeling calmed down from my day. Looking forward to next time.

Thank you Low Bar team!

Came here after work for an early dinner. I shared the Low bar nachos with my friend and both of us liked it well enough. We liked the topping to chip ratio but lots of the toppings were very wet so the chips got soggy quickly. I got the pink flag cocktail and was happy that they put what glass it would be served in on the menu. The salt and pepper wings were crisp but a little too salty. My friend got the breaded fish tacos and she liked them but they came with a sauce that was very spicy

I hate that I am leaving this review, but a sad downfall has taken place. LowBar used to be possibly the best burger in the entire bay area, but it has fell off the cliff to barely average. This legit was an amazing burger that you would talk about for days, but now it is not even worth ordering. Sadly, on my last and final visit I ordered two extra patties but the server only ringed in 1. When asked where the other patty was he said well I have to charge you $3 per patty so I only gave you one. Who is this person to make that decision for me? Is he my financial adviser? I was also the only one in his section he asked for a credit card from before putting in an order. Just plain rude. But the missing patty was not the problem!!! The burger just is not good anymore! But hey for $22 you can have the smallest oysters on the planet. I used to love Low bar but I will never eat here ever again.

This place was fine. It’s a pretty basic bar/restaurant. The location is cool, the interior is small but chill. The staff was chill and laid back. The tequila selection is pretty mid. I had a great time because of the company I was with, but the food and drinks were just ok. There was nothing wrong with this place but there also wasn’t any reason I’d be dying to go back. If you’re just looking for a spot to drink and meet with people I think this spot is great. But for a fun and interesting meal? Probably not. It’s downtown Oakland so parking isn’t easy.

Will definitely return to try vegetarian bahn mi.

First time here. Ordered the grilled pork Vietnamese sandwich. It was ok. The pork was good but not much of it compared to the amount of veggies.

They have many drink selections from Costco. They also have cut fruits and flan cup desserts in the fridge.

They use the Louisiana hickory coffee for their Vietnamese style coffee.

Super great experience here! Their spicy grilled sandwich was super yummy and very sizeable especially for $10! The ingredients tasted fresh and the baguette was perfectly toasted. man i love fresh n best :D the banh mis huge and very fresh. I've tried juices, coffees, and smoothies and they never disappoint. i plan to come back again to try the rice bowls.

top_reviews.content: Every time I come to the Bay I visit to get the tacos - they’re delicious every time!! Absolutely packed with flavor and one of the few vegan places that arrest TRULY good tacos. I love the Al pastor and definitely get any of the mushroom flavors.
the carnitas nachos were the best nachos i've had in a long time. the watermelon agua fresca was so delicious and flavorful. i wish i lived closer so i could eat here all the time.
Long day. Ordered the ‘carne asada’ burrito with guacamole. Very tasty devoured in less than 5 minutes in my parked car. Would highly recommend.

I’ve been wanting to try this place for awhile and really love the idea of vegan Mexican food. I opted for the nachos for my first visit with asada. One thing I found weird is that the physical menu lists nachos+ meat as $15 pre tax, but the item was rung up as $15.25 pre tax. That’s not a huge deal, but why wouldn’t the physical menu reflect the real price?

The nachos themself were pretty good and the portion size was super generous. The chips were great and crunchy and didn’t get too soggy. Their salsas and queso taste great, especially for vegan queso. Beans were fine. I maybe wanted a little more guacamole, but I’m glad it’s included in the base item without additional charge.

However, I was disappointed by the asada. I’ve never had great luck with vegan beef, but I’m always willing to try it once. It was pretty dry and had what I can only describe as that old school vegan beef flavor, when morning star used to be the only option. I ended up pushing most of it to the side.

Overall, I enjoyed the food, but I wouldn’t get the asada again. Next time, I’ll go for something else and hopefully will enjoy that more. But, I’ll definitely go back!

We catered Venganza for a birthday party, and the food was phenomenal! We got the taco bar, so we had a sampling of all the different “meats”, and each one was delicious! Full of flavor and great texture. Plus, the handmade tortillas, pickled veggies and salsas were all so tasty! All our guests were raving about it, and were blown away that it was all vegan. The owners were great to work with - super professional and responsive! Plus, the dessert menu is incredible. We got cupcakes and they were a masterpiece - beautifully decorated (based on our party theme!) and absolutely delicious! Thank you so much!

We had the galbi tang and spicy cold noodles with beef at Daol Tofu in Oakland.

The galbi tang was rich and comforting — the broth had deep flavor, and the short ribs were tender and satisfying.

The spicy cold noodles were refreshing with just the right kick, perfectly balanced with the sliced beef.

Service was friendly and attentive, and the food came out quickly. The vibe felt cozy and casual, a great spot for comforting Korean food in the neighborhood.

Daol has been in the neighborhood a long time. It’s often quiet, and that translates to attentive service and made to order food. We went for lunch and had the chicken bento, the mackerel, and the tofu vegetable stew. Everything deliciously spicy, plenty of rice and banchan, tea, and miso soup. All for $13.99! Highly recommend.

Very authentic and Delicious thank you so much.
Bebimbap, seafood tofu soup, bulgogi, and fish. Will come back again next time.

We had an absolutely delicious dinner at Doal Tofu & Korean BBQ on Telegraph Avenue in Oakland. I must confess that this was my first experience eating Korean but it certainly will not be my last. Our waiter was enthusiastic and very helpful explaining the different kinds of dishes and why he was putting an uncooked egg on our table.we ordered the Galbi, which is a grilled beef that was very tasty and we also ordered Yachae Sundubu, which is a tofu stew that is served so sizzling and hot that we cracked the uncooked egg and added to the stew! It cooked instantly and added a wonderful unique texture to our dish. We also ordered a veggie pancake, that was the largest scallion- type pancake i’d ever seen. It tasted wonderful. We wisely had a bottle of Cass beer that’s a delicious Korean beer. The prices were very reasonable snd I can guarantee you that once you eat here, you’ll want to return often.

We randomly found this place on Google map, and we're super happy that we found it!

With 2 adults and two young kids (6 and 3,) we ordered 7 different dishes because we were excited with the variety of dishes they have to offer. And everything tastes so good!! Fish and pancake were also delicious. Bibimbub was also good.

Went here for a quick dinner. Shared nachos and a burrito. The nachos are interesting. Has a curry-ish sauce on top and shredded cheese with other toppings. Feels healthier than other nachos but the chips get real soggy since the sauce is watery. Comes with a great green sauce to put on top.

The owner is friendly and the food comes fast. Would definitely come back!

I’ve been coming to Hot Shop Gourmet Burrito in Albany since 2011, and it’s easily one of my go-to spots. The owner is truly amazing—always friendly, charismatic, and welcoming, with top-tier customer service that keeps you coming back.

If you’re in the area and want a reliable, delicious burrito spot with a personal touch, this place is definitely worth checking out.

top_reviews.content: Great food at a great value! The saag paneer is hearty and healthy! It’s very fresh and not oily. We’ve been ordering on door dash and love it. We get cheese naan and chicken tikka masala for the kids.

this place was great for a couple decades but tonight was pretty disappointing to return. no light in the bathroom. food was doubly not as ordered. waiter who previously was pretty solid was not hearing well or doesnt care anymore. i was the only customer but maybe thats why.

If you are looking for a take-out/old school joint sort of place that always hits the spot come to Mehak. I started eating here 20 years ago, and it's only gotten better. TGTG folks- the deal rocks, generous portions and it's actually a complete meal.

The dishes are consistent, hearty, rich and the naan is so delicious. The tikka masala is perfectly nostalgic, the saag lamb and saag paneer are fantastic, the malai kofta is one of my favorites of all time and the roasted eggplant curry (bahgain bartah?) lives in my dreams.

The people who run this place are fantastic, and it's always clean and relaxed inside.

I have been enjoying Mehak for over a year now. Since moving to the east bay I hadn't found an Indian restaurant in my area that makes butter chicken/chicken Mehkani the way I learned to love it until Mehak. This is my favorite dish and theirs is fantastic. We also enjoy the saag paneer and chana masala. The naan is delicious and such a good value that the curry comes with the rice.

Also have tried the mango lassi and kheer and enjoyed both! Best kheer I'd had in ages.

top_reviews.content: What an experience! I loved everything about this place. The tasting menu almost had a story, and each dish was dedicated to her own mother and someone close to her I believe. The presentation was out of the ball park and such an eye candy. It’s about enjoying the marriage of different ingredients creating intricate flavors. The servers were humorous and friendly. Two servers came to our table often and we had a great conversation with them. It was like a royal treatment. It was my husband’s bday dinner and they gave him a card signed by the staff and a small bday desert. We both don’t drink alcohol, but they offered good selections of NA wine. I strongly recommend it.

We have visited Nightbird 13 times in the past two years; the last time being December 31st 2025. Hands-down, it is our very favorite restaurant in San Francisco for dinner (we love Foreign Cinema for lunch / brunch). The tasting menu is out-of-this-world, Chef Kim does an incredible job of crafting delicious dishes in a way that some Michelin starred restaurants cannot. There's a couple of staple dishes that always appear on the menus, despite the seasonal rotations, there's clearly a reason for that - they are expertly constructed and very tasty.

Being attached to the Linden Room Bar allows you to select from a wide-range of beverages from the with a cocktail menu as you settle into the night. Both venues have their own distinct vibe, the restaurant is the perfect place if you like a low-to-medium level of noise from other diners and background music, this allows you to have very civilized conversations over dinner without raising your voice to be heard.

The servers are on-point and so kind and friendly. We always receive the warmest of welcomes (Thank you Jordan, Mark and William. They will also suggest wines as you move through the menu to complement each dish.

Do go and try Nightbird, it's a real gem in Hayes Valley and so easy to get to from Muni and Bart. It's also super-handy if you're seeing a show at the Orpheum, which is a stones throw away.

What a night! Absolutely beautiful food, service, and location. Literally everything was rock solid.

Came with a friend for a girl's night.  Service started swiftly and the pacing was just right, unrushed, but never lingering too long.

Every dish was really unique and we had so many favorites.  The crudo was fresh and clean, the scallop was perfect and tender, the squab was just perfect, the mouse donut was bizarrely wonderful.  Dessert was clean and cool and just completely light after it all.

The staff was amazing and my friend said the wine pairing and discussion with each team (most of them being sommeliers) was great.

10/10 would gladly come again.  Best food and experience of our girls trip so far.

Absolutely stunning, inventive, and beautifully crafted dishes. It was truly a journey through spring and impeccable culinary artistry. The service and wine recommendations were outstanding as well. This place is a must visit in San Francisco, and stands apart from many other fine dining restaurants in this region.

The food was poorly executed and simply did not taste good (to any of the people in my party). The beef with charred leeks tasted like it was rolled around in an ashtray. There are well executed smoky dishes and then there is this. The menu was a list of dead chefs' names and told us nothing about the dishes at all, so you had no understanding of how many savory vs sweet courses were next.

But the key reason for the one star is the imbalanced, poor service. One member of the wait staff showered all of the attention and adoration onto one of us, while completely ignoring the rest of us in my party. Only one of us was asked whether we wanted tea or coffee. Only one of us was asked how the food was. Only one of us was asked if they wanted another drink. Peculiar that those who were ignored were people of color 🤔.

The waitress told us we were vegetarians... And then apologized when she got the wrong table. She then congratulated us for our job promotion.... And then apologized she got the wrong table.

Fine dining establishments should teach their wait staff better. This is worse than Burger King.

address: 2122 Shattuck Ave., Berkeley, CA 94704, United States

google.name: Crave Subs
