top_reviews.content:
You’ve got to try the sandwiches and loaded fries at Crave Subs! This fun, comic-book-themed sub shop serves incredible, complex subs that are fascinating and delightful. They make sub sandwiches like you may have never seen before—thick, complex, beautiful, gooey, and oh so tasty. The many yummy layers of each sandwich stack together to become works of art in their own right.

The contrast between different textures and flavors comes in perfect harmony, creating sandwiches that are overpoweringly delicious. These are not just your typical sandwiches; instead, they are culinary masterpieces, carefully crafted for maximum deliciousness.

The sandwiches come on quality bread and are smothered in this delectable Crave Sauce and filled with fresh lettuce and tomato. You can choose from different types of bread, including gluten-free, Dutch Crunch, and more. The gluten-free bread tastes great (the lack of gluten does not translate to a lack of taste); in fact, it tastes delicious.

There’s also a nice variety of fillings available. They have vegan, vegetarian, and meat subs. It seems every sandwich is stuffed to the maximum with fillings and flavor. You cannot go wrong here, but I recommend you try: The Patrick Star, a next-level fried chicken sandwich with Korean barbecue sauce and pepperjack cheese, the Pikachu, a mouth-watering grilled chicken sub with just a bit of kick, and the Buzzlightyear, which is the ulitmate turkey-pesto combination!

Not to be overlooked are the scrumptious loaded fries. Delicious, salty curly fries come smothered in cheese, meat, and sauce to create a beautiful symphony of flavor and texture. The Wolverine and Goku Black fries are particularly satisfying, and I highly recommend them!
Been there multiple times. The food is good. The boom boom sauce, and the fries tastes great. Chicken, not so much imo. Try it.

First time trying Crave Subs in downtown Berkeley and it was an amazing experience! The sandwiches are top-tier—super fresh, flavorful, and the portions are great. I also love that they have an ice cream place right there; it's the perfect way to end the meal.
​The staff was incredibly welcoming and made me feel right at home. If you're in Berkeley, you definitely need to check this place out. 10/10!"

TLDR:
Overall: My top place to eat at Berkeley
My Order: Usually Tom & Jerry, Chicken Little, or Patrick Star - all are very good. Dutch Crunch is my go-to
Price Breakdown: Usually $16-$17 per sub. A bit pricey, but they do not skimp on the meat and the portions are huge!
Portions: One normal sized sub is so incredibly filling, I'm either stuffed or I end up with left overs.
Halal/Vegetarian Friendly: Meat is halal and they have vegetarian/vegan options.
Would get again: 100% absolutely, I have to physically restrain myself from coming here every day.

This place is absolutely phenomenal, I would eat here all the time if I could. I've already been here more timrd than I can count. Halal with so many options, and the subs are so juicy and addicting! Anytime a friend visits Berkeley, I take them here by default and each of them have begged to come back. Definitely a messy eat and a bit on the pricier side, but with the portion size and how flavorful each sub is, it is absolutely worth it. The balance of the tang, sweet, and savory is perfect every time yet varied enough that it feels like a fresh experience every visit. Will note that the wait time is usually a bit long, I either order first and then hang out at Half Price or order on snackpack abt 15 minutes before I get there. The shop itself is very vibey and uniquely comic book themed, making this such a fun spot to visit.

Delicious, mouth-watering halal subs.  Lots of variety.  It is located near Berkeley campus.  We ordered a Grogu, an Ed, Edd, and Eddy, and a Crave Reuben.  We also ordered the curly fries. It was about $75 total for the meal for three.  It's a bit on the pricier side, but everything was amazing.  PLUS: There's a yummy ice cream shop that shares the same location.

top_reviews.content:
I recently picked up a lunch order from Joodooboo in North Oakland, and the entire experience was fantastic from start to finish. I placed my order online a few days in advance, which was incredibly easy and stress-free. When I arrived, the pickup took literally seconds, and finding free, easy street parking right around the corner made the quick stop completely hassle-free. The clerk at the counter was also incredibly friendly and efficient.

There was a lovely neighborhood energy outside, with plenty of people enjoying their meals at the outdoor sidewalk tables, and it was bustling inside as well. Everything was carefully packaged for the ride home, keeping all the hot and cold components perfectly fresh and separated.

The meal itself is beautifully put together and highlights just how fresh and high-quality their ingredients are. The creamy tofu is exceptional—it has a delicate, crispy exterior with absolutely no oiliness, breaking away to a perfectly soft, velvety center. The seasonal banchan sides offer wonderful, clean flavors that bring a perfect balance of color and taste to the plate. It is an incredibly satisfying, complete meal that comes with the main tofu, a beautifully textured multi-grain rice, a comforting side soup, and fresh sides like the sweet corn and green salad.

Everything from the packaging to the cooking was executed beautifully. I highly recommend checking them out if you're looking for a top-tier, vegetable-forward meal in the East Bay.

It has been on my want to go list for a while, and I finally had the chance to check it out. The restaurant has a casual atmosphere, but the food presentation feels very thoughtful and artful.

I ordered the Nori Acorn Noodle Bowl and also tried the Fried Dooboo Set. I liked the acorn noodle bowl more; the chilled noodles, nori vinaigrette, kimchi, and pickled mushrooms made it super refreshing and flavorful. Their house tofu was silky, delicate, and packed with fresh soy flavor. It's a must-try. Portions are on the lighter side for the price.

The only downside was the ordering system. We came on a busy Saturday evening, and having everyone order before being seated made the front area crowded and a little chaotic. Seating was limited.

super healthy and quick casual restaurant after a long day in the winery estates. the fried tofu set was delicious, and the banchan went very well. loved the umami seaweed seasoning on the acorn noodles, they were bouncy in texture. red makgeolli paired well too!

Came for a pop-up menu they had with Bazaar Sonoma, and all the food was great. Regarding the Joodooboo items, the tofu quality is superb, really loved their dessert, super silky tofu with a brown butter syrup and granola, perfect level of sweetness and playful textures. Variety of food and drinks are great and everything is on theme and authentic. Definetely will stop by again if Im in the area and if you want to buy tofu, this is the place to buy it for sure.
Amazing food and a very warm welcome every time I visit. Everything is delicious, and the staff is always kind and friendly. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content:
Gusto is a locally owned small business that proudly brings authentic Algerian cuisine to downtown Berkeley for prices that the average person can afford. The owner is a kind man who loves his restaurant and really cares about brightening his customers' days. I am proud to support this new local business in its effort to allow Berkeley to try some fantastic Algerian food!

I think the best part is the slightly charred, carefully spiced, succulent Algerian meats. I liked the chicken and beef shawara bowls, but this was my first time trying Marguez, and I was completely blown away by the deliciousness. The chicken and beef shawarma bowls came with delightfully fresh vegetables, but the Marguez sandwich (which you've got to try) had this amazing balance between sauce, flavorful meat, fresh veggies, and the wrap it came in, plus it came with a nice portion of fries that had a bit of sauce of their own. The beef tongue sandwich was also amazing in a similar way. The Tajine plate lamb and the Joojeh Sultani are also great options, especially if you want something very substantial.

The Algerian sodas from the cooler are so enticing here. I really liked the one that tasted like carbonated lemonade, but there was also a really good one that tasted kind of like licorice. Definitely give them a try; they are so worth it!

And don't forget dessert. At the counter you pay at, you will see some amazing desserts on display. The Makrut (this pillowy doughnut-like pastry) and the baklava are delicious and a perfect way to end the meal!

The eating experience is super casual, and the ambiance is friendly and informal. It's pretty fun trying to catch a glimpse of the magic happening in the kitchen while you sit in the eating area, which is a little sparse and kind of simple but very fitting for a nice, laid-back place to eat alone or dine with family and friends. I love this place!

Its my first time trying Algerian cuisine here, and honestly it was a great experience!

We tried here the kebab plate which has lamb and chicken, both were tender, juicy,full of flavor and must important prepared fresh right infront.

also had their signature couscous pot, which was such a highlight for me. It’s a hearty, warm, and comforting dish with lamb, beef sausages, and chicken, all halal as confirmed by the owner.
It was rich, satisfying, and I can see why so many people around us were ordering the same dish.

The chicken shawarma wrap was also very good juicy, well-seasoned, and honestly stood out compared to other local shawarma spots

And I’ telling you their traditional sweets are not to be missed its absolutely delicious!
My favorite was the white one coated with a light lemon-dusted powder (I think). It was so well-balanced, fresh not overly sweet.

Overall, it’s a great addition to Berkeley. I would definitely recommend it and would revisit again

Absolutely phenomenal addition to the neighborhood serving authentic Algerian food and Persian kabobs. The owner is delightful and very passionate. The food is cooked perfectly and represents both cultures well.

Extremely fair prices, portion sizes and clean Ingredients. You don’t feel heavy at all after the meal. It’s also located super close to the Bart, I’d highly recommend going out of your way to come here.

The mixed couscous and joojeh soltani were both out of the park.

A new Algerian restaurant in Berkeley and such a great discovery!

Everything was fresh and full of flavor, you can really taste the quality. The welcome was also amazing! very warm and genuine.

Wishing them lots of success, they truly deserve it. I’ll definitely be back!🇩🇿🇩🇿

We tried the chicken kebab and the beef, and both were incredibly juicy, tender, and just perfect. The first time, we ordered it to go—but it was so good that we decided to come back again and dine in. It seems like there might be a new owner, and whatever changed, they’re doing an amazing job. Definitely worth a visit!

My wife was craving bulgogi after an appointment, but without all the fuss and cost of AYCE. This spot was nearby and had a perfect menu. Although near the tenderloin things were perfectly nice and we parked nearby at the Civic center. The restaurant was empty during an early weekday dinner, but they did send out a few pickup orders. The staff was lovely and invited us warmly to sit down.

She got an order of the beef bulgogi and I ordered the Army base stew, something I've been wanting to try but never see on menus in our areas. I got a Korean orange soda and she got a milk tea from the extensive drink options. The bulgogi was just was she was craving and in a very fair portion. It was salty, a little sweet and very tender, plus it all came with purple rice and kimchi which is lovely. Great meal at a fair price in a very comfortable little restaurant. You should go here.

Nice quiet  lunch several very nice and busy with to go orders yes I would come back again food was great I had the short rib soup and rice on the side with Thai ice tea very for my sweet tooth my order came to 26.61 before tip

Quiet Korean restaurant within the tenderloin area, really good and home style Korean food, no music played but perfect for eating after a part at the Phoenix hotel. Our group of 7 came here after a day party on new years and they have all types of Korean food and soju and beer. They were accommodating and we had the whole place to ourselves, one family came in and lots of door dash pick ups. We got their tofu soup with rice so good, seafood pancake, soy garlic chicken wings, chicken and fries, soju, makgeoili, and beer. top_reviews.content: The chicken is amazing! Usually I don't like fried wings because they are dry and mostly greasy, but these are so good, not greasy at all just chock full of flavor! The galbi recipe is so flavorful,and the coke slaw is hella good too! You can sit outside and enjoy the view of the Oakland hills and people watch. Enthusiastic two thumbs up!

Fantastic! Actually I suggested that they develop cheese balls at early July when ordering Uber Eats and they replied to me and they really developed it now!!! I feel deeply touched and I dined in today with my boyfriend (ordering cheese balls for sure) That’s amazing! Staff are friendly, too!

This place actually catered an event at my apartment building in Jack London, and the food was so good that my friends and I decided we had to visit the restaurant for lunch. I’m so glad we did!

We ordered the Original, Spicy Original, Honey Garlic, Gangnam Style, potstickers, and the Rose Ddeok-bokki. The Honey Garlic wings were hands down my favorite—they were perfectly crispy, flavorful, and had just the right balance of sweet and savory. The Original and Spicy Original were also really good, and the Gangnam Style didn’t disappoint either. The only thing I wouldn’t order again is the Rose Ddeok-bokki. It just wasn’t for me.

The only downside is the price. An 8-piece order of wings is about $18, which is definitely on the expensive side. That said, the quality of the food makes it worth treating yourself every now and then.

The restaurant itself is really cute, with a few outdoor tables and a small bar ledge inside if you want to dine in. The customer service has always been friendly whenever I’ve visited. Just keep in mind that the food is made fresh, so it usually takes about 20–30 minutes. Don’t go in super hungry unless you’re okay with waiting, or better yet, place your order ahead of time and take it to go.

Overall, this is a great spot if you’re craving delicious Korean fried chicken. I’ll definitely be back, especially for those Honey Garlic wings!

It's SO GOOD. We got 3 orders of wings, two bone-in and one boneless. The flavors we got were galbi, soy garlic, and gangnam style, plus regular fries and sweet potato fries.

I love Korean fried chicken and this was excellent. Light, mega crispy, flavorful sauces. Yes. When asked which was my favorite flavor, at the end of the meal, It was simply impossible to choose. I love soy sauce flavor and I love garlic and their sauc is delicious. I had expected the galbi to be insipid and oversweet, since that is not uncommon, but it was really delicious and had a very nice, unexpected smokiness to it. Would I like it to be a little bit less sweet? Yes. But would I order it next time? Also yes. The one I got was the Gangnam style, with a peppery sauce and some chilies on it. I loved the black pepper in there.

I want to particularly note that their boneless wings were surprising and wonderful. Normally when you get boneless wings, you get a nugget sized chunk of meat with bearing and sauce. There's not a strong sense of chicken to the whole thing. But these "wings" were large and a bit flat, slathered with sticky, smoky galbi sauce. First you get this burst of flavor followed quickly by layers of shatter-crisp batter and then your teeth sink into a satisfaction of tender meaty goodness. This is such a far cry from the usual boneless wing they don't even deserve to be called the same thing.

We also got an order of regular fries and an order of sweet potato fries. They were both delicious but for me the sweet potato fries were, hands down, the winner. I have a tendency to prefer sweet potato fries to regular fries anyway, though, so I'm biased, but my dinner companions very much enjoyed the regular fries and were surprised to find that they liked the sweet potato ones since they normally don't. I feel like there was a bit of cinnamon or something in them, that made them extra tasty.

I would also like to particularly note that they were unstintingly generous with their pickled radish. One of my friends is a pickled radish fiend and bemoans the limited amount she normally receives at other places. Here she was told that she could have as much as she wished, and her wishes were granted, with warm smiles and fast service.

I'm definitely going back. Lovely food, lovely service. Highly recommend.

I had a fantastic experience at bbq Chicken
in Oakland! The chicken was incredibly crispy, juicy, and packed with flavor. Every bite tasted fresh, and the sauces were absolutely delicious. The staff was friendly, welcoming, and made sure our order was prepared perfectly. The restaurant was clean, and the food was definitely worth the wait. If you’re looking for some of the best Korean fried chicken in the Bay Area, this is the place to go. I’ll definitely be coming back to try more flavors. Highly recommend!

top_reviews.content:
We stopped by this Nepali restaurant for a late weekend lunch. The place was mostly empty, but it has a large dining area and dedicated parking in the back, which is convenient.

We started with the tornado potato fries, which were crispy, flavorful, and probably my favorite item. The Indian-style chai was okay, while my friend wasn’t impressed with her latte.

Unfortunately, the main food was quite disappointing. The steamed chicken momos were extremely oily, with a strong stale-oil smell, and the chutney wasn’t particularly impressive. We also tried pork sekuwa, which had a nice smoky, char-grilled flavor, but again, everything was excessively oily and seemed to have been cooked in old oil. My vegetarian friend had the chow mein and had the same complaint—it was very oily with that unpleasant stale-oil taste.

Overall, we were disappointed, especially after seeing so many positive reviews. The food might have potential, but the quality of the oil completely overshadowed everything we tried and left a lingering unpleasant taste and smell. Definitely not the experience we were expecting.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We absolutely loved Tipsy Yeti Restaurant & Bar! We’re visiting San Francisco and decided to stop in, and I’m so glad we did. Everything we ordered was delicious! We had the pasta, burger and fries, pepperoni pizza, and drinks, and everything came out fresh and tasted amazing.

The atmosphere is really cute and welcoming, and the service was wonderful. Everyone was so friendly and attentive and made us feel right at home. It was one of those places where the whole experience..from the food to the drinks to the service…was just great.

Definitely recommend stopping by if you’re in San Francisco. We would absolutely come back! ❤️🍕🍝🍔🍹

Wow. This place. It was our first time trying this place out and it was incredible from start to finish! We were greeting by a very friendly, all smiles host. He really gave the initial feel of a friendly restaurant! We were seated and our waitress, a blonde young woman who was also very friendly and recommended I get lamb on my Himalayan Pizza and SHE WAS RIGHT BECAUSE IT WAS SO FREAKIN GOOD! The pizza had so much flavor, the spices, the taste!! It was FRESH and it was absolutely delicious! We also the got Tornado Fries and Chicken Chow Mein and both busting with flavor. I want to add that we also got the fried calamari- IVE NEVER HAD SUCH CRUNCHY CALAMARI IN MY LIFE it was so satisfying! I got a delicious mock tail and the mezcal drink that just knocked your socks off. If you want to try a place with fantastic and flavorful Nepal flavors, you have found your new favorite place! Thank to the friendly staff, really, your genuine smiles and constant attentiveness to your customers and delicious food has won our hearts!

What a lovely experience for a chill date night with my hubby. There was a live band lighting up the atmosphere with beautiful notes and jazzy vibes. The food was all delicious and perfectly prepared. The chicken momos were juicy, almost like soup dumplings. The tornado fries were flavorful, especially the sauces. The lamb was juicy and tender. The cocktail and mocktail were balanced in sweet, tart, savory and spirit (for the alcoholic drink). Our server was warm and friendly, providing us with on point food recommendations and even a nice movie recommendation. I can't wait to visit again on another date night or even with my kid (since they have such a broad menu).

What a gem! We stumbled upon this place by accident, and I’m so glad we did. Everything was absolutely delicious. It was so good that I’m already planning to come back before flying home. We tried a few mocktails: the pineapple coconut one was especially yummy and their famous steamed dumplings. We also ordered the goat curry and the pear and brie salad. Every dish came out looking beautiful and tasted just as amazing. Can’t wait to return!

We hit Om Sabor for happy hour and walked away seriously impressed.

The flautas were a standout right out of the gate: crispy, flavorful, and authentically done.

The barbacoa tacos were a big win for my husband. For me, the texture leaned a bit mushy, but the flavor still delivered.

Same story with the ceviche tostadas: he loved them, while I’m just not as into cold entrées, but they were undeniably fresh and authentic.

Then came dessert and wow, they absolutely knocked it out of the park with the Black Forest cheesecake. Easily the highlight. Rich, balanced, and just indulgent enough. The blueberries and strawberries paired beautifully with the cheesecake and elevated the whole dish. One small note: the microgreens on top added color, but the texture and flavor felt out of place. A different garnish could take it from great to perfect.

Friendly, attentive service tied everything together, rounding this up to a five-star experience.

top_reviews.content:
Beautiful restaurant and amazing food. Each dish was very delicious.

Our favorites were the beef salad and the pumpkin slices. Surprisingly the pumpkin was the star. Very crispy and the sauce that comes with it is a nice tough. Great appetizer you should get.

Beef salad hits all the notes a Thai dish should hit. Would recommend this as well.

Vibes were great here. Great music and they have a fully stacked bar. Perfect for a weekend night

I've been wanting to try this restaurant for a while, and I finally got the chance to check it out!

I started with the Tom Yum cocktail, made with rum, apple juice, lime, chili, and lemongrass. It was refreshing, flavorful, and delicious.

For the entrées, we ordered the Avocado Green Curry and the Pad Kee Mao. We asked for spicy, and they delivered! The Pad Kee Mao was packed with flavor, and the portion was decent.

It was my first time having avocado in Thai curry, and it worked really well. The curry was rich and flavorful, and the chunks of avocado were tasty.

Overall, a fantastic meal, and I will definitely be back!

The food was AMAZING! The riceberry rice is such a unique experience. Pad sew is 1000/10, Thai Thea good but very sweet.
Pad Thai 6/10, sticky rice is perfect.

Overall decent Thai food at Yimm. Both their flat noodle to pad kee mao/drunken noodle and the side thin noodle were well cooked to give the al dente chewy texture. Another highlight was the seasoning of the pad kee mao - tasteful and right-on-spot spicy.

That being said, there's plenty of room left to be desired. Both the chicken and beef we ordered were well overcooked, dry, rubbery, and plain. While the Tom Yum soup was spicy and sour, it lacked the authentic flavor from lemongrass and other herbs. The acidity was also too pungent to be enjoyable. Also wish their staff can be more friendly than the minimum service.

Not bad, really appreciated how it was not as oily like many other Thai restaurants. Would say the curries are spicier than the usual Thai places here, which I liked.

However, the portions (especially the soups) are on the smaller side for the price. Also I saw people recommended Lord’s noodles but it was honestly kind of average, the pork belly was dry and flavorless. But the avocado green curry is really good, spicy and creamy.

The mac and cheese was also insanely good, a ton of flavor and I loved that they used farfalle pasta.

Definitely will be back here soon. Thanks Eli’s!

you may or may not have heard that this bar, a long-standing oakland countercultural hub, has been through a lot of trouble in the last year or two because the legitimacy of one of its past construction projects was thrown into question. well, i believe the drama regarding the dubious "patio" space at eli's exemplifies not only a problem with the bar itself (on a level worthy of impacting any review of the establishment) but one with the punk movement in general, which we should all be old enough at this point to talk about (i do know there are gen z punks, but this particular conversation is for millennials and gen x for now). here's the thing: you can't "DIY attitude" your way out of complying with local regulations that exist for the preservation of health and safety. yeah, there's a lot of bureaucratic obstacles needlessly slowing down projects, and you can fight for reform on that, but you do unfortunately need to do it through slow, boring, above-board avenues. you can't just put up potentially unsafe or improperly ventilated structures and call them "good enough" when we live in a society where a basic level of trust is assumed by anyone walking through your doors. the stubborn aloofness underlying the way this bar operates is not cool, actually, and insistence to the contrary is related to elements of what it means to be punk that people don't seem to want to talk about. it's very true and important that specific music subcultures have been at the forefront of social change across the country and particularly in oakland. but let's be real: both the aesthetic trappings and the social ideals of these movements reduce with dangerous ease into layers of self-pastiche, and over time, the parts that had value can become buried under cartoonish antisociality. at their worst, music subcultures represent a selection of maladjusted weirdos brought together by a love for particular drugs. in the case of punks, the drug in question is unquestionably nicotine. now, i will confess that i actually still have a cigarette from time to time, though i don't really know why, so it is with swiftly decreasing regularity. it's not just the potential hypocrisy that stops me from wanting to tell other people what to do with their bodies, though; i genuinely think that people should have a high degree of personal freedom and that this is what makes our country a special place. however, if you are going to build a patio to smoke on, you have to do it properly, because you do in fact need to give a damn about other human beings you are sharing this city with. what you also do need to do is have an ACTUAL patio. i'm not sure what the status is now, but last time i was here, the former patio was still mostly closed off, and instead the bar was operating an almost-entirely-enclosed space with some limited opening of the ceiling, where i basically felt like i had stepped back into the nineties when indoor smoking was still legal. i went home with stale cigarette odor permeating my jacket and gloves despite personally never touching one, and i felt disgusting. secondhand smoke is a very real health risk, and it needs to be taken seriously. people should be able to go to a bar and have a drink without being exposed to that, and anyone who thinks otherwise is clinging on to the absolute worst that counterculture has on offer. listen, i still love punks. i have had nice times at eli's. the bartenders are kind. they make ok drinks, and this is the sort of place where if they made a drink that was more than ok, that might count as a point against it. but the overall attitude of the owners needs to change significantly if this bar doesn't want to develop a reputation as an embarrassment to the scene.

top_reviews.content:
Friendly staff and tasty pizza!
Visited per a friends recommendation, she's a big fan of their vegan pizzas seeing as she has specific dietery needs. The staff was very friendly and were quick in getting us drinks and food as we sat outside at their single table.

I had the TNT pizza which was all around good, the thai peppers were certainly spicy. The peppers came whole so it was easy to remove them if I wanted if the kick was too much. The size of each pizza is perfect to split between two or to have a leftover portion.

Given we sat outdoors in downtown, expect to hear frequent commotion. The nearby intersection had a lot of drama seeing as there's a lot of bad drivers in the area. I'm told they have indoor seating so there's alternative options.

Terrific vegan options that are creative, tasty, and not just an afterthought. They use Butcher’ Son mozzarella which is awesome. The TNT was fun and packed a punch (especially if you nibbled on the whole Thai chilis). The Nelly was saucy and full of umami.

One of the best Neopolitan style pizzas you can get in the Bay. Excellent dough, great tomatoes, and just good vibes. The crust is perfectly cooked, chewy, a little tangy. Pecorino Romano is so underappreciated as a finishing cheese, but Bare Knuckle showers pizzas in them. So good!
Great service, delicious wood fired pizzas, super cool staff!

Who pulls this out of an oven & thinks it’s ok to serve? The pizza is usually pretty good for bay area standards, but, coming from Trenton, this is terrible. The elements are there to make this a true tomato pie, but the tomato paste sauce was too sweet & the crust was indistinguishable from the remnants of the oven. The other two pizzas we ordered were pretty good, but what got me was the dough in the TKO was thick & raw in the middle while this thing was sent to hell.

The dumplings were delicious, and the cold appetizers were authentic and had a wonderful homemade flavor. This is definitely a must-try spot in the East Bay!

This is highly disturbing and concerning from any food establishment. Food containing fruits/vegetables should be thoroughly and carefully prepared to prevent insects, which may carry harmful diseases to humans, crawling about in the food. While mistakes do happen, I’m even more disappointed with Lunchbox’s response to the incident. They asked if I wanted my money back and showed an overall lack of concern, stating ‘that sometimes happens when we don’t wash our vegetables good enough’. I’m deeply concerned if you are routinely serving customers food with insects crawling inside of it. Hopefully this message will push Lunchbox to be more attentive when preparing food - nobody wants pay money to find nasty surprises in their cuisine.

top_reviews.content: Such an authentic and really good Korean food restaurant in El Cerrito. Recommend making a reservation for large parties and of any size. It gets busy here even on weeknights. We made a reservation for 4 at 6pm on a Thursday and when we were leaving so many people were waiting. They have their own private parking lot and there is also street parking. Not too far of a walk from El Cerrito bart too. You order through the kiosk and that’s how you ask for more items and refills for banchan. Their banchan is so fresh and good! They have Galbijim (braised shortribs) and we like to add cheese and watch it get torched. We also got their galbitang, bossam, seafood pancake, and I wanted to try their fried chicken (regular and soy garlic). The dishes come with either regular or purple rice, we got one set of each. Service was great! They serve hot tea and water, sodas, beer, and soju too. I can’t wait to come back and try their cold buckwheat noodles and other items on the menu we didn’t get a chance to order!

Wanted to celebrate my birthday especially after coming back from Korea. It’s a new restaurant that was recommended to me by my sister in law especially since they had their own parking lot which was a plus. We ordered: Galbijin (Short Rib) one with cheese, and no cheese, Jeon (pan cake) one with onion and other with seafood, 16 piece fried chicken,Japchae, and Rose spicy Rice cake. My favorite: Galbijiin and fried chicken. Love the rice cake but not the spicy part. For drinks: Soyu peach and kloud beer to create a beer bomb just like the dramas.:).. It was awesome tasting for me. I would definitely come back.

One of the best Korean Restaurant in town. I ate with my 2 friends, and we ordered the Rose Galbi Jim. I really liked the spices and the soup of the galbi, blended really well with the mozzarella cheese. Moreover, the texture of the tteokbokki was so soft and tasty. At the same time, the portion of the Galbi was so big, we couldn’t finish it so we took some back home.
the other best part was that you could refill the banchan. Would recommend you to ask more for the tofu and kimchi, really mouthwatering. the waiter and waitress were kind and friendly, they served you fast.
we visited the restaurant quite late in the afternoon, so we didn’t need to queue since there were plenty tables. the parking area was big too.

Came to try dinner before but it was during soft opening time. Very busy at night so not as enjoyable. This time I came for lunch and much has changed. Service was quick and we are ordering from a ordering system right at the table. Would recommend trying the combo as you can have the best of both worlds (Korean BBQ and one other famous Korean dish like cold noodle). Definitely will return to try more good food next time!

Seafood pancake was also great! Fresh ingredients. Servers were also all super nice and accommodating. Overall a great experience!

top_reviews.content: We were in the city for one night and had time for breakfast before our flight. We found Pistachio Kitchen and glad we did.  We started with the Pistachio Latte and it was creamy, nutty and everything we hoped for. I had the the avocado toast with a scrambled egg and the avocado was plentiful with a light and bright dressing. My partner had the croissant breakfast sandwich with crispy potatoes that looked so good I had a bite and it was as good as it looked. We look forward to our next visit to Pistachio Kitchen!

I really wanted to try the shrimp and grits without bacon. I know bacon creates that classic “Southern comfort” flavor, but I prefer letting shrimp shine.

The chef was a little skeptical, but accommodated my request. I added a touch of Cholula for smoky heat, and what I ended up with was unexpectedly Mediterranean-forward - bright chopped tomatoes, silky polenta, and shrimp that stood out instead of bacon hijacking the dish. It was amazing.

The polenta itself was incredibly creamy. I cook it at home occasionally, and it’s never this smooth. I may have to ask for their secret.

As a first-time guest, I even received a complimentary bag of Turkish pistachios, which made my day! I love pistachios.

I’ll definitely be back for more shrimp and grits - and next time I’m trying the pistachio pancakes.

top_reviews.content: One of the best Chinese spots in the East Bay, imo. Food here is excellent for lunch and dinner. Huge portions. Mouth watering tasty…. One of the best Chinese restaurants in the East Bay. This legendary restaurant in Elmwood serves delicious duck, pork, chicken, and vegetarian dishes. Large and reasonably priced dishes. Friendly and attentive staff. Indoor dining or take away.

Polished Setting, Uneven Fare

King Yen enjoys an ideal location on College Avenue with a bright, well-kept dining room and attentive service. The space is clean, welcoming, and clearly well-managed.

But while the atmosphere suggests elevated dining, the food rarely rises to the occasion. The Szechuan beef, though generously portioned and paired with a flavorful sauce, suffered from tough, low-quality meat—more leathery than tender. A prawn and vegetable stir-fry was better balanced and fresher, but still overpriced at $25.

Service is generally efficient, though there’s a noticeable shift in tone during the final half-hour before closing, with staff clearly eager to wrap up—a gesture at odds with Bay Area norms.

For diners seeking standout Chinese food in the area, Dumpling Express farther down College near Safeway and Philz is a stronger bet. Their handmade dumplings are excellent, the pricing is far more reasonable, and the surrounding options for drinks or coffee complete the experience.

King Yen has its strengths, but food quality and pricing leave it trailing better neighborhood alternatives.

top_reviews.content:
One of the best ramen spots I’ve tried!! everything was honestly sooo good. From the moment we walked in, the staff made us feel welcome. They were attentive, kind, and really added to the overall experience.

The ramen itself was the perfect bowl! the noodles had the ideal texture, and the broth was rich, flavorful, and comforting without being too heavy. You can tell a lot of care goes into every bowl.

Highly recommend

WHEN: Sat @6pm

PARKING: There is metered parking around, and is free after 6pm.  It may be a bit tricky especially around meal time, but keep circling and you’ll find a spot near by enough.

This cute little ramen shop has such perfect lighting coming through thanks to thier skylight.  We weren’t actually hungry so we shared the following:

TONKOTSU - $16.50 (Regular)
Pork Belly Chashu, Bamboo Shoots, Red Onion, Wood Ear Mushrooms, Green Onion, Ajitama Egg.

You get a choice of noodles to pick:
1.) Hakata - Thin Straight
2.) Sapporo - Medium Thick Wavy

Figured since it’s my first time here, I choose the most basic version of their bowl of ramen.  I chose Sapparo and for some reason expected it to be thicker/wider, but regardless it was still good!  The presentation of this bowl is just gorgeous, served on a small wooden platter.  The red onion is chopped, and the pork Belly is quite tender.  Regarding the egg, you get just half.  Overall this bowl of ramen is creamy, rich, and the right amount of flavor and salt.  But still make sure to drink at least a glass of water!

CREAMY CHASHU PORK CROQUETTES - $8.50
I have never seen anything like this so I must give it a try!  It actually didn’t come out piping hot, so I was able to drive in right away!  It was definitely creamy (like ramen) and had pieces of the Chasu pork, encased in a crispy and warm batter that was deep fried.  It also comes with a katsu sauce and I really enjoyed it.

The staff was friendly and didn’t make us feel bad for ordering enough of just one, but man I was so full.  Had to walk around downtown Berkeley for awhile.

By far the best Ramen I had in the Berkeley area. The two soup bases were both very rich in flavor. The toppings were very fresh. Pork and chicken cha soup both go well with the soup. Second, please use a QR code for customers to order food at the table. It’s fastest and it would not make any mistakes by the servers.
Third, hire more servers as they’re already busy enough.
If you claim you’re authentic Japanese Ramen, then do it more efficiently. You can turn your tables quicker that way.

One last thing, ask to take out the red onion in your ramen. It doesn’t belong in tradition noodle soup.

I think I just discovered my favorite restaraunt of all time in Berkeley. Though the exterior of the restaraunt is unassuming, and the building itself is quite small with limited seating, the interior is still very clean and neat, and the workers are very nice.

I placed an online order for the C Chicken Momos and the Garlic Cheese Naan, which were both phenomenal. The naan was some of the best I've ever had. It was so fluffy, thick, and pillowy soft, and was not overly charred/thin or too crispy like other naan. Just pure doughy goodness. There was also a perfect amount of cheese filling--enough that you got the subtle kick of milky acidity, but not too overpowering. The naan itself was also not too greasy, and the garlic flavor was very aromatic. You could also taste a hint of the slight tartness from (I'm assuming) the yogurt used to make the naan.

The "C" Chicken Momos came with eight large pieces, which is definitely enough to fill you up. The sauce tasted like a classic sweet-and-sour sauce with a very mild and pleasant spice. Also, because the dumplings were fried, they were crispy despite being covered in sauce, but still had a bit of the nice chew you would get from a steamed momo skin. The fillings themselves were also super flavorful. Because of the ginger, they tasted very herby and fresh, which balanced the tanginess of the sauce so the meal did not feel too heavy. The dumplings also had some warm broth in them, which is perfect for a cold day.

The prices are fair too. You can often find small discounts on Snackpass or delivery apps like GrubHub. Needless to say, I will definitely be coming back. Totally recommend!

Sichuan Fusion is a neighbourhood staple! I’ve been coming here regularly for dine-in and takeout since 2017 and will continue to eat here so long as I live in the Bay Area. It’s one of my favourite restaurants in the East Bay.

Every dish I’ve had here has been amazing. My must-trys are the baby lotus root with beef, Sichuan fish filet with pickled mustard soup, Chongqing chili chicken (need to get it with bone!), garlic eggplant, and Uyghur style sautéed lamb. But seriously, everything is fantastic.

Alright, It's been a year. This is one of the best  sichuan places in the bay. I have never had a bad meal here and unlike Spices 3, I am treated very nicely, no weird racial aggression.  It has a comfortable dining room  that's unpretentious and soothing. My favorite dishes are the chongqing chicken bone in, shrimp fried rice, stone pot cabbage, among many others. There are no bad dishes. I will admit dining in the quality is a bit higher, but it is still good. I am praying it stays in business and doesn't change.

I didn't expect to like this as much since I'm a little sensitive when it comes to spicy food, but I liked it!

Good:
- Really solid garlic glass noodles with shrimp - not spicy, but great flavoring and tasty noodles with just enough sauce!
- The soy milk they give out here is really good if you need something to cool the spiciness away
- The spicy noodles are tasty - chewy noodles
- The sour and spicy fish soup was really good as well - so soft and tender
- The boiled spinach was good in comparison to all of the spicy dishes
- Lotus root and beef was tasty but spicy - the beef was so tender

Bad:
- Takes some time for the food to come out
- The place is super casual ambiance wise, you have to be used to Chinese restaurants and speaking Chinese to have the best experience

Overall would come again, good authentic Chinese food.

Located inside the complex, past the 99 Ranch market in the back. We love this restaurant and often order delivery or eat in. I realized I didn't review it for years so now is a good time. They have great value for the size and quality of dishes.

We usually order Kung Pao chicken, schezuan fish soup (spicy), boiled beef (spicy), and garlic eggplant. These are our favorites however the Dan Dan noodles were good and huge - a much better price than the new soup restaurant next door. The fried rice and xiao long bao are decent. The pork dishes and fried chicken are also good. Free tea if you eat inside. We haven't had a dish we didn't like and overall enjoy every dish.

Service is quick and fine. Most dishes are around $15-20 and do not include rice. The portions are very large. I recommend going with a group to try many things.

Our beef fried rice never came out too. So I had to cancel it. Same with the noodle. It took nearly an additional 15 minutes after I paid my bill.

top_reviews.content:
We had a wonderful time, we have a group of people and we're seated quickly. They have a full bar which made ordering cocktails so easy. We got mojitos, amaretto sour and cadillac margarita.
We shared shrimp and beef empanadas which were so juicy.
Do not forget to order yourself those poblano cornbread because I had to share mine and I regret it.
I was so excited to get the crispy fried whole branzino because I have been wanting a fried fish like this for so long and I was so juicy and flavorful. Will order again.
But the seafood cioppino dish was so flavorful it made the whole table wished they had ordered this.
We did try raw oyster for the first time which made the weekend oyster deal worth it.
Of course we ended with the dessert menu we got the sweet potato beignet omg I wish I order a whole plate to myself. The tres leches which was perfectly soaked and flavored. Guava cheesecake with mango sauce, this is a steam cheesecake so this just melts in your mouth.

This review is long overdue. My husband and I live within walking distance of Bocanova, and we’ve already dined here several times. I’ve also attended events here through my ceramic studio Kollektiv Clay, so I can say firsthand that both the staff and the owner are incredibly warm and welcoming.

A couple of my all-time favorite dishes—the fried mushrooms and fried polenta—weren’t on the menu during our most recent visit. I’m hoping they’re just rotating dishes seasonally, because they’re absolutely delicious and definitely worth ordering if you ever see them available.

On this visit, we came for happy hour and stayed for dinner. My husband had a michelada and a beer, and I ordered a mocktail that was excellent (though I’ve also had their cocktails before, and they’re fantastic). We started with the crab deviled eggs, which are always a must-order for me. Any of their ceviches are amazing. We also tried the fried fish sliders, which were very good, and the scallops, which were cooked perfectly. My husband ordered a dinner special—a hearty oxtail stew—and finished every bite. Other standout dishes we’ve enjoyed in the past include the fried cauliflower and their tacos.

Everything we’ve had here has been consistently delicious. I was too full for dessert this time, but I’ve had the bread pudding before and would easily call it their best dessert.

I highly recommend Bocanova. The food and drinks are excellent, the service is consistently top-notch, and the staff is genuinely friendly. It’s a place we love supporting and returning to again and again.

Stopped by for happy hour. Good times.

Drinks- got wine and mocktail. My guest said the Jamaica was super refreshing.

Food- we got shrimp sliders, fish sliders, Brussels sprouts, and guac + chips. The Brussels were my favorite, great flavor and cook. Love the cornmeal crust in the shrimp and chips were hearty and well seasoned.

Service- we interacted with the bartender, server, and manager. All were friendly, attentive, and professional. helpful to each other as well.

Space- love to high ceilings, great natural light and spacious. The place is huge. Two outdoor patios, main dining room, large bar, and casual seating area.

Really beautifully decorated space, it’s elevated yet not stuffy. I came for their happy hour and ordered the 2 Buck Shuck Oysters and Pork Tacos. Both very delicious, highly recommend. I think I’ll try the Duck Tostada and Beef empanada next time I come. The service was great, very dry attentive and they have a good sense of humor.

This is a cute spot for those wanting a bit more class during happy hour in Oakland.

The bathroom is clean as well (super important for me).

Every visit to Bocanova reminds us why it is one of Oakland’s most reliable dinner spots. The atmosphere strikes that perfect balance of lively and relaxed, where somehow everyone looks like they are having a better night than they planned.

We went on a weekday evening and the place was packed, which immediately felt like a very good sign. Started with cocktails at the bar and could have happily stayed there all night. Bonus points for having genuinely good non alcoholic options too, because sometimes you want the fun without waking up wondering why you ordered “just one more.”

The food was fantastic from start to finish. The ceviche was incredibly fresh, the Caesar salad disappeared embarrassingly fast, and the steak was so good there was a brief moment of silence at the table which rarely happens with our group. Every dish felt thoughtful, flavorful, and beautifully prepared.

What really makes Bocanova stand out is the hospitality. The staff makes you feel taken care of without ever feeling formal or stuffy. It has that rare combination of polished service and a genuinely fun energy.

At this point, Bocanova is one of those restaurants we keep coming back to “just for a quick dinner” that somehow turns into a three hour night with dessert. Every single time.

Bombay Brasserie is a great upscale Indian spot. The ambiance and atmosphere is very chic Indian and it has a very friendly and attentive service staff.   The dishes on the menu are very unique and there are several fusion dishes too. The desserts are absolutely stunning and a treat to your taste buds. They also brought out a small birthday plate with chocolate cake pieces to celebrate a birthday in the party. They also provide a complimentary bread and papadum basket. I recommend making a reservation with them before visiting.

Disclaimer : don't believe in 4-5 star reviews. I got fooled too.

I was super excited to try this new restaurant in SF. However the food turned out to be mediocre at the least. Duck samosa was the better one out of all the 3 dishes we ordered. Rogan josh was cooked in a very basic tomato  gravy, no flavor nor it captures what that dish even meant to carry. We barely ate this dish and the 2 stars goes to the restaurant manager where she was considerate  to take our feedback and remove charge for this dish without asking.
Then we had fish which is forgettable . No flavor of coconut gravy.
The ambience is dark, closed , unpleasant for an upscale restaurant.

I really wish and hope the chef take a note of this and engage more Indian origin chefs who understands what actually Indian flavors taste like when you are charging $25 and more on an average for below average food.

If you don't change the ambience, train your staff well and important enough update food , this restaurant is soon to remain a forgettable and no go zone for upscale Indian.

PS: this actually ruined dinner we came to celebrate an important milestone in our life.

Honestly, not worth the hype. Way too expensive for the quality. Avocado bhel was the only thing we liked. Paneer makhni was below average. Drinks were good. Expect to spend around $65–70 per person, plus you handle your own parking.

Bombay Brasserie was near our friend's dress shopping location so we decided to have a special lunch here. We called in advance to make a reservation and fortunately, it wasn't busy at all when we arrived.

We ordered a mix of items for the table including their biryani, dosa, salad, and other appetizers. The food took a while to come out but after it did, everything tasted great. It was all well-seasoned and it was clear they took their craft seriously.

While the food was quite good and enough for the table, it was the confusing ordering system with the staff that made it a bit difficult.

We were first told prior to coming that there were a la carte and vegan options to choose from their menu. Upon arrival, it looked like they only had a weekend brunch prix fare menu. We spoke to them and they allowed us to order a la carte from that specific menu.

In regards to vegan friendly items, we ordered ones that were marked and even one that we asked to make vegan. When the dish came out, it was the wrong order so we had to ask for a new plate to be made.

I think if they were clearer on the menu on their vegan items, that would make ordering a little easier and quicker.

top_reviews.content: This an awesome space in the city with great food options and a chic space for working (superior option over a lot of coffee shops in the area), gathering with friends, or events. They do a drag bingo event the first Sunday of every month and June’s was so fun!

This a nice size food hall. You can move between places and get what you need. Friendly independent folks across the board. Great example of San Francisco. Food is off the charts. The bar is chill and friendly. Popcorn machine anyone? Peace.

Love this food hall!! They have a great selection of vendors, great vibes, and friendly staff. I’ve visited Saluhall several times for lunch / brunch, and I’ve been impressed every time by the variety — there’s an option for everyone, and, if you need a post-meal walk, you can always wander around the IKEA showroom. I love how spacious the space is, and I appreciate that they give each vendor a lot of space to work. I was initially a bit surprised by how few vendors / slots they had open for such a giant two-story space, but I think the extra kitchen space allows the vendors to operate a bit more like they would in a normal restaurant and serve more complex things (vs. say, Union Market in DC, where it feels like everyone is on top of each other).

My favorite vendors (so far — I haven’t tried them all) are:
- Momo — wonderful Sichuan-style noodle shop! The noodles are spicy and numbing, have a wonderful al dente texture, and come topped with super flavorful braised tofu (or meat). I think they could make the noodles even more spicy and numbing, but I may be a bit of an edge case.

- Curry Up Now — super tasty Indian street food spot! The tikka masala paneer is absolutely delicious, and the springy, but rich cheese goes wonderfully with the curry. The curry typically comes with a healthy serving of rice — about as much as the curry — and you can add naan for an extra fee. They also give out free chai that is quite tasty; it’s a bit sweet but not overly so, and super warm and comforting.

They also have a lovely cafe that I can’t remember the name of for the life of me, but the coffee is phenomenal. It’s super rich and nutty, and you can absolutely taste the flavor of the espresso, even through the milk of, say, a latte. And, of course, you can never go wrong with the IKEA food hall.

Overall, lovely food hall with tons of amazing goodies. I can’t wait to come back and try more of their stalls!
Such a great environment for having lunch regardless of group size. It’s very clean, very open, and there’s plenty of good food options. I’d definitely recommend this place, especially Smish Smash.

I love this place for all the vegan options it has to offer. Sadly the vegan burger place on the first floor is no longer there, but there are still a lot of options on the second floor! Vegan baklava and vegan lions mane steak at Kayma (also serves non-vegan options); Vegan skewers and desserts at Casa Borinqueña (100% vegan); Tacos and burritos at La Venganza (100% vegan). Saluhall is vegans' mecca and for them to invite none vegans to try some of the best vegan creations!

I visited this place around Christmas time in 2023. So, it's a long-overdue review. I went there with my family to have a special, year-end dinner out. I had a high expectation as this was my first visit to a Michelin star restaurant. The staff was attentive and courteous; the service was excellent; and the presentation was impressive. The food, however, although quite good, lacked the ingenuity/creativity one would expect from Michelin star restaurants. I doubt I'd give it another chance.

The ambiance was lovely. Calm decor with earth tones with good lighting and a low noise level. The service was great; friendly and playful.

The food was mostly good. I’d say all the small bites in the early courses were excellent. I especially loved the “pancake” ball and the eel wrap. Both packed a punch of flavor and creativity.

I didn’t love the cod dish served with rice, not just because it was served with milt, which I personally don’t care for, but also because the sauce seemed incomplete, almost like the authentic version but not quite there and didn’t enhance it in any meaningful way. I didn’t like the quail. It was very well executed but I didn’t think it went with the meal. Quail is not used much in Korean cuisine except for the eggs, but the course didn’t utilize the eggs at all.

Overall, it was a lovely meal and I would return for a new menu.

Fantastic service. Probably one of the best in town. It was warm, delicate, yet also casual and welcoming. We never felt pressured nor anything. It was just right.
The food is great. I particularly liked the bird. So tasty and wonderfully cooked.
The place is calm, roomy, the music might be just a tad too loud, but overall, it was ok, we can hear each other talking.
We had a wonderful time and I’ll definitely come back again. The service was truly top tier.

What a life changing meal. These photos are actually from over 2 years ago but I still think about this place regularly. I’ve had my fair share of renowned modern, refined korean food / Korean fine dining in NY and LA, and nothing quite elevates Korean food as authentically as SSAL.

This meal quite literally changed my life and showed me that fine dining can both be deeply comforting and beautifully refined at the same time.

Will probably travel to the bay just to dine here again at some point.

top_reviews.content: I stopped by this place on my way home from work and was greeted by the sweetest ladies. I got the vegan combo and while the flavors were slightly milder than I’m accustomed to, but still very flavorful and  they were unique in a way. I can’t tell you which way but so many Ethiopian spots taste exactly the same and this one doesn’t. Their injera is 100% teff which makes it gluten free, something you can’t find at every Ethiopian restaurant.

I am beyond grateful for the nourishing plates served at Cafe Dareye, which I recently visited!

I appreciate the simplicity of ordering a full or half plate of a delicious variety of vegan dishes on GF injera. The atmosphere is welcoming, whether you prefer to dine-in or take out.

We laughed, joked around, and the whole experience made the food taste 100x better. I can’t wait to go back to San Francisco and visit again. If you’re ever in SF, do yourself a favor and stop by Gambino’s!

On work vacay looking for some lunch, this place came up in google and I’ll forever be thankful. My sandwich is amazing and what seemed to be the owner took my order he was amazing as well . Super nice and informative with a great attitude. Will recommend to others !!

Best sandwiches in SF, no contest. Ordered the veggie steak and it genuinely blew me away. Perfectly seasoned, insanely satisfying, and nothing like the sad “veg option” you usually get. This is a real sandwich, built with care. I’d go back just for this.

A spot I’d go back to when I want something simple, fresh, and satisfying. Here is the banh uot w/ ham and nuoc mam. The xiu mai here is the best. The sticky rice black bean dessert yum. Cash only.

wow what a wonderful spot this is! we came for soup and had the hu tieu mi. so good! really excellent quality broth and ingredients. the inside is so cute, pristine, and food was ready quickly. can’t wait to try something else next time!

The do a great job on their phos! I absolutely love their chicken pho, the chicken is nice and tender. I LOVE their veggie pho- the vegetables and delicious and plentiful, such a wonderful variety.

top_reviews.content: I was walking down Columbus Avenue on my way to the Athletic Club to hook up with an old friend just in from Napoli, and this old Chinese lady hits me with her cane!  Then she starts yelling at me in Chinese ...I don't understand anything she's saying, then a crowd forms, and a young guy tells me she's yelling at you because it took you 8 steps to cross her path, and 8 steps to the stop sign, the 88 steps to the Da Flora Restaurant, and she counted all of them!  Then he says the number 8 is the luckiest number in the universe, and I must go into the Fa Flora Restaurant and order the 8th item on the menu for the two of us, and then go to the Lucky 88 Market and get a lottery ticket..1 for her and 1 for me!  Well...I did just that, and the Lasagna was about the best in the city! 5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s and worth the stop!  The lotto tickets..we'll just have to wait and see.

Finally, an Italian restaurant in North Beach that serves excellent food and is not a tourist trap. We had the seared halibut and the spinach and ricotta gnudi. Both were super tasty. My son and I also ordered a butter leaf salad with strawberries and toasted almonds. The salad was nice as well. We were glad we ordered the Gorgonzola dressing on the side since it was relatively strong. The woman who served us was professional, discreet, and knew how to interact with customers. The other waitstaff were attentive throughout the meal. I really liked the atmosphere of the place, which had an old time parlor feel about it. We got to sit by a large window and watch the people walk up and down Columbus Street.

I was wandering North Beach alone, trying to decide what I was in the mood for, when this little restaurant pulled me in purely on ambience. It had that golden, intimate glow that makes you feel like you’ve stepped into someone’s home instead of a dining room.

The second I walked in, I was greeted with smiles and that rare kind of warmth that feels like an old friend you haven’t seen in years. I just knew the food would be good.

I’ll admit, I’ve been heartbroken by gnocchi before. Once it was so dense it felt like chewing clay and I swore I’d never trust again. But then I saw they’re known for their sweet potato gnocchi. Add sage and bacon? Obviously yes. Focaccia? Yes. Tiramisu? Also yes.

Everything was perfectly portioned, indulgent without being too much. I left full, happy, and oddly emotional in the best way. Dinner alone somehow turned into an evening that felt like family.

If I lived nearby, I’d be a regular. For now, I’ll keep finding my way back whenever I’m in North Beach

We happened upon Da Flora when we were heading to Cobbs Comedy club and looking for a place for a pre-show meal. The service was phenomenal and they very kindly made room for us without a reservation on a Saturday evening. We split the Caesar salad and focaccia bread and ordered the ricotta spinach dumplings in a lamb sugo and the house made sweet potato gnocchi. These entrees were some of the best Italian meals we’ve had in years (and my husband had a Nona  from Italy who cooked!) Food was cooked to perfection and the waitstaff were wonderful. They obviously have long time regulars who they knew by name and order and the atmosphere was cozy and elegant with an SF quirky vibe. Definitely coming back!
Great all around experience. Good overall food including fresh focaccia. Service was very friendly and attentive. Setting was cost and intimate. Very much worth a visit.

name: Secrets Of Tiger
address: 6520 Hollis St, Emeryville, CA 94608, United States

google.name: Secrets Of Tiger
google.address: 6520 Hollis St, Emeryville, CA 94608, United States

top_reviews.content:
Fun energy, cool staff. Mushroom dish was easily the best - light on batter, crispy on the outside but soft on the inside, very good veggies and the eggplants and carrots were the perfect size - unique film your typical Thai place. Fried steak is a lot of fun given the options of sides to eat with: sauce, fried garlic, picked veggies, cabbage. Also big portion.

Pineapple fried rice very good. Tons of onions, egg, chicken, and pineapple. Light on shrimp but I'm not offended.

Thai iced tea - I'd personally skip

Crossing the bridge for food is always worth it when you find a spot like this.
I found this place on Xiaohongshu and decided to give it a try — and it ended up being such a pleasant surprise!

We got there right around opening time, but the restaurant already had quite a few tables occupied, which says a lot. The space felt warm and cozy, with lots of plants inside, and you can even see the mural across the street from your seat. I feel like the atmosphere here would be especially nice at night.

We ordered the red curry, which was pretty good, though I do think it could have come with a bit more ingredients. Also, the curry doesn’t come with rice, so you have to order that separately. The rice that day was a little on the firm side.

The real standout on the savory side was definitely the Pad See Ew — super flavorful with amazing wok hei. Absolutely worth ordering. It also came with a good amount of ingredients, not just noodles, which I appreciated.

But the real star was honestly the dessert. It looked extra and tasted amazing too.
The honey toast was baked perfectly, the ice cream wasn’t too sweet, and the mango was super ripe and sweet. Paired with the sticky rice, it was such a good combo.

If you’re ever passing through Emeryville, this place is definitely worth checking out.

Very authentic Thai food. Ate lunch here on a Monday and place wasnt crowded but restaurant is small. Everything tasted great and food came out at okay pace. Mango Sticky Rice was different than other places, rice was blue/purple and had a toasty flavor.

A feast for the senses. The decor is vibrant and fun, the food is beautiful and delicious. Service was attentive and warm. Great experience, highly recommend.

There is a small parking lot but also street parking. It's a small place though so make a reservation if you don't want to wait.

The restaurant gets really busy during rush meal hours so making reservations is highly recommended. Limited large tables so groups larger than 4 would be difficult to fit unless you make reservation in advance so that tables could be put together.

A nice restaurant with lots of live plants - some are expensive tropical plants if you know them - that means the owner takes pride in the plants and does well to take care of them.

Pad see eew was alright. Tasty is flavorful but I like it when there’s some “wok hei” / smokiness when noodles are fried from a well seasoned wok.

Beef fat fried rice was delicious with a good piece of beef. We had it mild medium spicy and even then it was spicy for us. Not sure if they could do it mild. But it was a stellar entree that I would recommend especially with the tender flavorful beef and the sauce that goes with it.

Roast duck lychee curry was delicious! The winner of the night. The lychee imparts natural sweetness and a floral flavor to the curry that was just outstanding. I could eat this and be totally satisfied for a meal instead of all the other dishes.

Hat yai fried chicken was ok. Chicken was tender and crispy, going well with the sauce but the sticky rice was too dry and hard that it didn’t add well to the overall entree.

Would definitely return for the roast duck lychee curry and perhaps try their version of khao soi next time

The food was all really good and the staff were friendly. 10/10 shawarma. The food came out really fast as well. Definitely coming back!

I like the spicy wraps with a slight curry kick that they serve here. The sizes are generous and the staff are always friendly. You can customize your wraps so try one with hummus for a delicious and filling combo. I go here often and the quality is consistently very good.

I saw this on my social media feed and decided to take my family.  We all agreed that 10 out of 10. Food was very good. But the women at the register wasn't very pleasant.  We told her this was are first time so we need her to explain how the ordering process worked. She didn't smile or show any enthusiasm. Debating if we will return. I value customer service.

5/5 Stars – Amazing Food, Huge Portions & Great Prices!

My-O-My is an absolute gem in Berkeley! The food is delicious, the service is fast, and the portions are huge—definitely a great bang for your buck. What I love most is how they cater to everyone, whether you're looking for healthy, diet-friendly options or a hearty, indulgent meal. The menu has such a great variety, making it perfect for groups with different tastes. If you're in the area, don't miss out—this place is a must-try!  Did I mention it’s halal!!

top_reviews.content:
Bua Luang is hands down the BEST Thai restaurant in the entire Bay Area, not just in Albany! I have been enjoying Thai cuisine all around the Bay for over 25 years. My family and I have Thai food at least 2-3 times a week, so we have tried many (and I mean MANY) Thai restaurants over the decades, and without a doubt we all agree that Bua Luang offers the freshest, tastiest, and most delicately prepared Thai cuisine of all. Every dish is packed with the freshest ingredients. The flavors and textures are amazing. Restaurants in Thailand don’t make a Pad Thai as delicious as the Pad Thai at Bua Luang—believe us, we have tried Pad Thai all over Thailand and we still longed for the Pad Thai at Bua Luang. The chef at this restaurant is a culinary master!

Not only are the dishes at this restaurant superb, the atmosphere is serene and delightful. The indoor space is clean, cozy, and modern with soft old-world touches and whimsical lighting. The ambiance music is very pleasant. It’s not too loud, and it’s easy to talk with and hear others in your party. If you choose to dine outside, you are greeted by the most beautiful outdoor seating area on all of Solano Avenue. The space is gorgeous and inviting. And then there is the staff: always friendly and attentive. They provide a truly exceptional dining experience all around.

This restaurant is an absolute gem. If I could give it more stars I would. Don’t walk, run to this spot!

If you look at that picture, do you see a bed of spinach? Me neither.  I bought the Cashew nut chicken because it supposedly comes on a bed of spinach.
I called them and they said all the orders that went out for Cashew nut chicken were on a bed of spinach. When I returned it, they took it back in the kitchen, brought it back out to me where they had pulled most of the food away, and there were a few small pieces of wilted spinach. Not at all what I expected. Bummer, I had high hopes.

Definitely the place to visit when you are very hungry because their portion sizes are big.

Really love the decor at the restaurant because it makes one want to dine-in peacefully.

Their teas are amazing and I was blown away by the blends they offered. It was definitely my first time, having tea that’s blue in color.

The food was well-made, with good seasoning. I had ordered the sautéed mix vegetables with fried tofu and I loved how well-prepared the vegetables were.

Definitely a place that I will visit next time I’m in Berkeley

Our favorite Thai restaurant ever. 💕 They now served Kao Mun Gai (chicken and rice) Thai style. Tasty and good price. We also had Tamarind Prawn. It’s crispy jumbo prawns topped with tamarind sauce and grilled asparagus. Yummm. Best food, service and vibes. Love this place!!! Recommended!!! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We've ordered from Bua Luang several times before but they seem to have gone down hill. Tonight, we paid $94 for a meal and received tiny portions that weren't enough for 2 adults and 2 kids who don't eat much. The portions were about 25-40% what you would expect to get and what we'd gotten in the past. There were a few pieces of beef and chicken in small, half-filled containers. We thought maybe there was a packing error and called them to show them how the food had arrived. They weren't open to rectifying the situation and said this is how their portions are. The food also tasted greasy and not as good as it used to.

top_reviews.content:
Got to try this spot for brunch, and we only had to wait about 5–10 minutes before being seated. Since it was our first time, the staff was super helpful and informative about the menu. I ordered the Sai Oua lava egg plate, pork jowl on the side, and khanom krok.

First of all, holy hell, that egg was SO soft and yummy. I loved how it was prepared—the texture was amazing, and it was seasoned to perfection with such a savory flavor. The sausage was good, but the pork jowl was where the meal really shined. Next time, I’d definitely get the grilled pork jowl lava egg plate instead. I can be pretty picky with pork, but this one melted in my mouth and had so much flavor.

The khanom krok was beautiful and a great dish to order if you have friends to share it with. For me, one bite was more than enough as a sweet little dessert at the end of the meal. Their jasmine Thai tea was also really tasty. :)

I’m so glad I finally got to try this spot and would definitely say it deserves all the hype!

​This was my second time dining here, and it completely solidified this restaurant as one of my absolute favorites. I would easily eat here every single week if I lived closer!
​During this visit, I had the wonderful opportunity to speak with the owner. She is incredibly smart, passionate, and empathetic, and it truly shows in every aspect of the restaurant. I love the way she pours her love for her hometown into the menu and remains unapologetically authentic to her roots.
​That dedication translates perfectly into the food—every dish feels personal, deeply flavorful, and genuinely authentic. It is rare to find a place that hits the perfect balance of amazing hospitality and outstanding, uncompromising regional flavors.
​If you haven't been yet, do yourself a favor and check it out. It is a true gem!

While the inside area was a little loud at times, it was a warm familiar feeling. Being surrounded by the plants and cool air felt amazing and refreshing. The staff were so kind and welcoming, and we could not have asked for a better server.

The food was delicious and felt so worth the price. All of the ingredients were tasted in every dish, and just overall well thought out and balanced. The Lava eggs with the tender wagyu reset my tastebuds - nothing is going to taste as good for weeks. Definitely recommend sharing the Thai Beignets and the Coconut Cakes, as well as the main dishes.

we made a reservation ahead of time and ordered the prix fixe brunch, and they customized the menu to accommodate our dietary restrictions (pescatarian). the food was delicious, the atmosphere was so sweet, and the staff was incredibly thoughtful. 100% would go back! (personal faves: iced ube espresso, lava eggs, smoked sturgeon dip, prawn and fish stew, beignet with ube condensed milk and warm soy milk and bean drink)

Second visit and somehow the prices went up again. Ordered the surf and turf special,  server highly recommended but never mentioned the price! I then got hit with a $51 bill for 2 shrimp, 3 scallops, and a tiny tiny steak. Food was fine but nothing special. Love a good surprise, just not on my credit card statement. I understand surf and turf at a mid-range restaurant usually runs $30–45, and even then you’d expect a more generous cut of meat. At $51 you’re in fine dining territory, where you’d also expect the server to be upfront about pricing. The sparkling water was $8 too and no one mentioned its not free...

top_reviews.content: One of the best bowls of pho in town. I would recommend stopping by for a #13 (small) and an iced coffee. The pho broth is rich and salty, and the strips of brisket are really nice. The service is also very fast and friendly.
No frills authentic Vietnamese restaurant. Efficient, good service, and delicious food. I ordered takeout, there was plenty of seating on a weekday at lunchtime.

I met a friend here for lunch today.
We both ordered the same thing,  combo rice plate with egg roll, 2 giant fried chicken wings and a pork chop! I also wanted to try their jackfruit shake with boba!

The meal came with soup and salad. The soup was flavorful, a tad salty for my taste but that's just me. The jackfruit shake was the bomb with the exception of the bobas, which was a little bit hard on some bites.

I really like this combo. The eggroll was pretty big and tasty. The chicken wings were crispy goodness.  The pork chop was just okay for me.

I would come back here again to try the pho and get me some more jackfruit boba😋, hopefully the boba would be better.

Pho tasted great. Overall, it was a good experience. They give a lot of food and really quickly. Food literally came in less than 3 minutes. Definitely recommend getting the beef balls cause I'm typically not a big fan, but these were fire.

The food was okay but not great.  The place was kind of empty so there was lots of seating to choose from.  We ordered the pho and a plate of grilled pork chop with fried egg.  The flavors were good and it was just enough food for us all.  I would have to complain a bit though at how gross the tableware was. It seemed like they're was a film of sticky/greasy filth on everything. Even wiping them with a napkin didn't help.  The nastiest bit was touching the handle of the knife to cut up my pork chop. It was really nasty to the point I had to use a napkin to hold the handle.  Yuck. Aside from the cleanliness,  I would day the food was good if you are craving vietnamese food and you are also shopping in the mall.  By the way.  There aren't many shops left in the mall.  Guess the rent is too high.

Update 1/1/2023. Came back here with the family to eat some vietnamese food.  The family ordered the usual Pho, but I decided to try something new.  I ordered the BBQ pork & Shrimp vermicelli and it was pretty delicious with the sauce mixed that came with it. The noodles were just right (not too hard and not too soft)  it had a good bite to it. The pork and shrimp were well seasoned, but the shrimp were on the small side. The vegetables were fresh and crunchy and overall the food was really good.
