Would we come back? Possibly... Especially now that we know what to order.

I’ve been here like 4 times in as many weeks. The hand rolls are so fresh, flavorful, and interesting. I love coming for lunch. The staff is very kind and service is great. Highly recommend the black cod with truffle butter and seared albacore with garlic aioli!

I had a reservation for one and was seated at the hightop window corner. The website stated they were booked up, but I was able to call and get a seat. It's an intimate cozy place. My server was attentive and kind, and my favorite item ended up being her recommendation, the negihama (yellowtail & green onion) The rest of the rolls were just okay. The scallop and shiso leaf roll was decent. Salmon belly/yuzu/truffle salt and spicy tuna tempura roll weren't bad, but weren't memorable. I got about 4 rolls and a drink for about $50 and left satisfied, but not overly full.

Restrooms are attached to the ramen restaurant next door.

This was a surprise dinner my friend invited me on. The hand rolls are so fresh and delicious. I had 5 amazing rolls that come out one at a time for freshness m. The server was super sweat and helped me pick out what I wanted. The menu does also have set options, but I decided to do individual rolls. I definitely recommend stopping by if you’re in the Oakland area.

Had the baller set and loved it. They were so generous with the tuna caviar and uni hand rolls (unlike other hand roll bars). The price is so much better than similar hand roll bars in sf. Will be coming back!

top_reviews.content:
Really loved the cucumber lemonade and tacos we got. We wandered in after an event near Union square and we’ll be back again.

My husband tried 3 meat tacos- the Al Pastor was his favorite. I had the tacos as well but I got a shrimp, a nopales, and a coliflor. Loved all 3- the shrimp was my favor- so tasty, and the nopales was surprisingly good. (Nopales sometimes are not well seasoned but here they were great). The tacos were a bit oily. I might ask for light oil next time.

I asked about the agua fresca to confirm that it was just fruit and sugar- no mix, and they confirmed so I picked the cucumber lemonade. It was delicious. They also had hibiscus and strawberry horchata.

We also ordered the chips and salsa. The chips were warm and we enjoyed them while we waited for our tacos. The salsa was delicious.

The staff was friendly, efficient and seamed relaxed creating a nice vibe. The prices were good and I like that you could pop in for a quick snack of a taco if you just need a small bite.

My only complaint was that we had so many little plastic salsa containers to throw away, but this seems to be somewhat normal now days. Would be great to minimize the single use plastic if possible, especially for those dining in.

Wanted some tacos in SanFran, and I got them when I randomly stopped in to this location.
Menu takes a moment to absorb, esp. if you haven't been here before.
Ordering was simple, and staff was friendly and kept location clean. There was a decent amount of people eating here on a Sat
Tacos tasted really good and were filling and had unique flavors, so I felt I got what I wanted and my money's worth.
For sure stop in if you've got a hankerin' for tacos and want a good meal.

This place was one of the best Mexican food places I have eaten. We shared a burrito bowl that had flavored chicken, lettuce, cilantro, black beans, rice, and a red sauce.  Please give them a try. You won’t be disappointed.

When I first had Pastor Papi food truck at the table tops in the Presidio, it was a 10/10 pastor burrito. Piping hot, flavorful including pineapple bits, cheesey, balanced, a next level burrito.  So, my expectations were set but not met at his brick and mortar location.  The pastor burrito was just alright, nothing to tell others about.  Lacked much if not everything from his truck burritos.

Being a pastor connoisseur makes me a little  biased but they put some serious effort and the tacos were really good. I only had pastor, tacos without pineapple (personal preference). They use double tortilla and they give you so much meat on each taco that you can use the extra tortillas to make tacos from the fallout pastor. Worth the drive to such busy part of town. I try to hit them every time I’m in SF.

This restaurant has been on my want to go list, so I was excited to try it out!

We ordered the Pad Kee Mao (drunken noodles) and the Gang Khew-Wan (Green Curry).

The Pad Kee Mao was tasty, the flavor leaned slightly toward to a sweeter, tomato flavor side, but it was still enjoyable.

The Green curry came with generous portion and was really flavorful. I especially really liked the eggplants, the texture was great and the seasoning was on spot!

This place is phenomenal!! Best Thai in Berkeley. I chose this place because the atmosphere was warm and inviting, and beautiful, without being stuffy. I wasn’t disappointed! The food was delicious, and portions are HUGE! You absolutely get an amazing meal for a great price, and our server Theresa was so sweet and patient. I would come back to Berkeley JUST for a hot meal from here. 10/10

Food was delicious! Ordered the vegetable egg rolls, Khaknom Jin Nam Ngaio, and Pad See Yew. It was all so tasty, and there was a spice rack to kick it up. I think I would skip the egg rolls next time, in favor of trying a salad or another entree. Looking. forward to going back and trying to catch the Lunch specials!

I ordered food from this place twice. The first time, I ordered tom yum noodle soup, and it was incredibly sweet. I’ve never had tom yum soup with such a sweet flavor. The second time, I ordered the Thai noodles, which were also sweet but lacked any other distinct flavors.

You have the option for a dollar or so more to have them debone the duck. When we’ve gotten rice plates from other places, there seems to be so much waste (Gristle, fatty parts, funky parts, etc.) But at Quack House they only give you the prime pieces of meat, we observed this w the duck rice plate and chow mein. Prices are a bit higher than your standard Chinese barbecue takeout place, but for the amount of choice cuts and food you it seems totally worth it. top_reviews.content: Great little spot if you're looking for something more casual than Belotti in Rockridge but with the same excellent taste and high quality! Love that they set up little tables on the sidewalk. My personal favorite is the spaghetti with burrata - a classic that never disappoints.

Incredible pastas that taste like you're actually in Italy. Al dente with flavorful sauces. The pastas are so so so good. Best pasta in the East Bay, for sure. Drinks are simple but great also.

Service here is counter, with the pastas coming out almost instantly. Prices are fair for the quality and quantity.

It's nice to have somewhere good within walking distance, plus it's hard to get into the original location and this is a much more chill dining experience.

Highly highly recommend!

We stopped by Belotti Bottega to look at their fresh pastas and authentic italian offerings. To our delight, we discovered they also prepare warm meals on-site, so we decided to stay and enjoy the experience. We ordered a couple of pasta dishes along with drinks and settled into their outdoor seating on a cool yet sunny winter afternoon.

The service was exceptionally friendly and welcoming, making us feel right at home. The food? Absolutely authentic and rich in flavor. We tried the Agnolotti di Lidia and Casoncelli Bergamaschi, and both were outstanding. The pork shoulder and prosciutto in the Casoncelli were especially delicious, while the beef shank-stuffed pasta of the Agnolotti di Lidia left us with clean plates all around.

Belotti Bottega is a gem for anyone craving genuine Italian flavors paired with warm hospitality. Highly recommended for a cozy yet elevated dining experience.

Hands down the best fresh pasta in the East Bay! The quality is incredible, and I love that you can either grab uncooked noodles to make at home or stay for a quick, delicious meal. The staff is also incredibly welcoming and helpful. You have to try the Pappardelle with mushroom and beef reduction, it’s absolutely divine!

Absolute best handmade pasta far and wide, and I’ve had my share of of pastas across Italy. The agnolotti is out of this world good; not something you’re just finding anywhere.

The sidewalk vibes are perfect and easygoing if you dine in, and taking home a package of pasta to cook at home makes for the perfect date night! I’m thrilled to hear another Oakland location is coming!

top_reviews.content:
My favorite restaurant in the whole world, of all time.
My go-to in college. Sadly, I moved away after college. But every time I'm back in town, maybe once a year, I always have to come get my Steve's fix, even though I graduated over 20 years ago. I don't care about Instagrammable presentation, designer art and furnishings, and pork from pigs who were properly socialized and pampered. Just give me simple but delicious food, generous portions, and good value. Can't ever beat that.

Easy ordering, fast prep, tons of food. The place is cost effective and will satisfy even the bigger eaters.

There are several large indoor tables that can accommodate large groups. The same is true outdoors in front of the restaurant.

The pace caters to students and dies a good job. The food is abundant and simple. Solid choice but don't expect a sophisticated food experience.

We came here for lunch, and the prices were OK (each dish was around 20 bucks, and they have large portions). I highly recommend, unless your vegan. Most dishes contain meat, besides a veggie bibimbab.

A little overpriced, but what isn't. The food is always good. Portions are hit or miss. I was full on my last visit, and I like that they have a low carb option. I've had the pork, beef, and chicken and it's all good. Need to try the seafood some time. Self serve water is always a nice touch.

This place is practically a Berkeley staple.
This restaurant has been here longer than I've been alive. Eating here, you'll understand why they've survived all the turnover, while many places haven't.
The staff is friendly.
The food (proteins) is made to order and always fresh. The Kim chi obviously has to be made beforehand.
There's great flavor and the spice for the spicy chicken is enough for you to be satisfied, but not enough for you to breath fire.
I've never been unsatisfied coming here over 20 years.

top_reviews.content: The Monk’s Kettle is my new favorite restaurant in Oakland. This is definitely a hidden gem, and a MUST. We came here to eat the Lamb Shank we once tried and that stuck in our memory forever. And yesterday we realized it was even better than we could remember. The lamb shank was so tender that it could separate from the bone effortless, we did even need to chew it. It was laid on a bed of marinated pickles (pickles with pickled onion or shallots, and black and green olives), and feta cheese with a vinaigrette. On top of the lamb, a tasteful meat Demi-glaze that went along with the vinaigrette and the pickles exquisitely. The demi- glaze is to drink it on its own. It’s simply a genius combination: the acidity of the pickled veggies pairs so good with the fat on the lamb, it helps you clean your palate from the small amount of fat left in the lamb, just genius. But that was not the only good thing in the menu: the mac & cheese was the best we’ve ever tried, and the steak frites was cooked to perfection: pink in the inside, and with a little crust on the outside, simply perfect. The beer selection was also extensive, and the menu included the explanation of every type of beer they have . We will be back soon for sure. In my top list of restaurants in the area.

Unsuspecting from the outside but full of charm inside.

From the old wood bar/tables to the glasses behind the bar, you'll feel welcome.

They have cute kettles sprinkles throughout.

Seating is first come.

Did I mention they have a lot of veggie options and piny the elder on tap?

Server was patient with our group of 5.

Recommend for a spot with brews n food.

What?
Go to Oakland, to a gastro pub, for a lunch with an old friend?
YES - go here, it's fantastic.
1. Parking. Noon on a Thursday afternoon I lucked out and parked on College Ave., just 50 feet from the front door.
2. Service. Greeted as I walked in by a friendly staff person (who was also our waitperson). She was knowledgeable and patient and took our order (2 to stay, and 1 to go) by memory and got it all correct.
3. Food. My buddy and I got the same thing: Pub burger (medium) on brioche bun with gruyere cheese and grilled onions along with a side of kale salad (also could have had chips or fries). Excellent burger although I removed the top bun and ate the burger with a knife and fork. The shocker was the kale salad - no stems, mixed with root vegetables, and dressed with an interesting umami-ish vinaigrette: fantastic. So good, a ordered a full size kale salad to go for dinner later.
4. Dessert. Out of curiosity, I asked for a black coffee, and "do you have any cookies?" thinking maybe some big Costco oatmeal monsters. But, no - they have an in-house cookie plate (a long wooden cutting board with three hand-made cookies: gingerbread chocolate chip, light lemon bar, and a snicker doodle. Hand made by a staff person off premises - wow, really good, fresh, and perfect with robust black coffee.
My buddy and I had a beautiful lunch and sat for awhile talking and enjoying an Arnold Palmer, a black coffee, and cookies - a great mid-day break.
5. Summary: I haven't been to Oakland since the the G.S. Warriors left, but Monk's Kettle is a perfect reason to go back.

Legend has it that the carved wood encasing the shelves behind the bar once framed a (pretty spectacular) fireplace.

This place is my go-to spot whenever my sister stops by my work since it’s so close to the area. The service was pretty good, and the portions were generous, each order could easily be shared by two people. Since my sister and I like trying different dishes, we decided to order three items.

First, we got the Soy Garlic Ollei Chicken Wings. They were flavorful, crispy, and perfectly coated with sauce. Next was the Beef Bibimbap. The beef was well-marinated, and it came with a good amount of veggies and rice, making it a really satisfying and well-balanced dish.

Lastly and definitely the star of our lunch was the Creamy Ttok & Pasta. We originally expected something like a regular creamy carbonara, but we were pleasantly surprised! It was incredibly creamy with a nice kick of spice without being too overwhelming, and it had a delicious drizzle of bacon on top that made it even better!

I would absolutely order the Creamy Ttok & Pasta again, and honestly, I’d recommend trying all three dishes. Everything we had was delicious!

The spices on all the food was very unique and you feel like you can taste Korea with every bite. 9.0/10 Pro Tip: go with a friend and get as much variety as you can. There is too much to try in just one go. Oh and they give you little appetizers at the start of your meal.

Ollei is a fantastic neighborhood find that brings a warm, welcoming vibe and top tier Korean comfort food to the bustling Russian Hill area. The atmosphere is cozy and character filled, making it a perfect spot for everything from a casual dinner to a late night craving. The service is consistently praised for being friendly and attentive, with thoughtful touches like hand drawn happy faces on takeout orders that show they truly care about their guests. The menu is packed with standouts: the Army Stew (Budae Jjigae) and Seafood Pancakes are absolute must orders for their rich flavors and generous portions, while the Soft Tofu Soup and Bulgogi consistently hit the mark for quality and authenticity. Don't miss the Ollei Chicken Wings perfectly crunchy and available with a delicious soy garlic or spicy glaze or the inventive Creamy Ttok & Pasta for a unique fusion twist. Whether you're diving into a hearty bowl of Beef Ramen or sharing a plate of Corn Cheese with friends, Ollei delivers a satisfying, 5-star experience that feels like a warm hug in every bite.

top_reviews.content:
I love to eat at Kura Revolving Sushi Bar in Berkeley! I come frequently, as it is definitely a favorite for me, my friends, and my family.

It’s a fun, modern place to eat. The dining area is clean and sunny (with big windows letting the Berkeley sunshine stream in), and I find the conveyor belt that carries the sushi plates and the robot that brings the water and wasabi to the table so cute!

I like how you order by the plate (most plates are $4.10), which means you can have as much or as little as you can afford or feel hungry for. I’ve come here for just a plate or two before, and I’ve also come with friends and accumulated tall stacks of plates. (If you order enough plates, you might even win cute prizes that are dispensed from above the ordering console at every table!)

The environment and concept are wonderful, but the food here speaks for itself. When it comes to sushi, there’s a variety of choices that range from traditional to modern. The fish and meat are always fresh, the rice is always perfectly sticky and well-seasoned, and the nori is always crisp—especially if you order on the console because then it will come straight to your table from the kitchen on a conveyor belt. I particularly recommend the tekkamkai and the negitoro gunkan; I try these two plates almost every time I come, and I come a lot. The wasabi, soy sauce, and ginger are free and high-quality. I love to use plenty of them with my sushi.

There’s also plenty of great non-sushi items, including ramen, udon, and even fries. The miso soup here is warm and soothing, a perfect appetizer, and the beef udon is also a favorite of mine. (I love the slurpy, chewy noodles and the warm broth with the tender beef).

They take dessert as seriously as the main course. You can’t go wrong here, but for dessert, I recommend the warabi mochi, the sesame balls, and the gooey butter cake. Personally, I often find it hard to choose just one.

The menu is not set in stone, and they frequently circulate exciting specials on and off the menu, so it’s usually worth it to browse the entire menu before ordering. I think my favorite special item that’s ever been on the menu is the negitoro maki roll. (Maybe they'll bring it back, but I don't know.)

They also change out their cute prizes, if you’re into that. I have some cute key chains from when we ordered a bunch of plates a while back.

I downloaded their app, so I can receive discounts/coupons from time to time.

Eating here is always a treat!

I had some bad experiences at other Kura locations, so I was a little hesitant to eat over here, but it all turned out great!

I had a reservation and checked in with the staff when we arrived at the restaurant. We still had to wait about another 15 min for our table to be ready. It's not too bad, but I'm not sure what the purpose of making a reservation is if there's still a wait.

All of the sushi tasted better than I expected. The sushi rice held together well, not too gummy, mushy, or overcooked. And the rice was glossy, hydrated, but not too wet or soggy. The ingredients tasted fresh, and I didn't have any stomach discomfort after getting home. Highly recommended!

The pork slices were not fresh, very chewy, and didn’t taste right. Overall not the best value for portion sizes. If you like gimmicks, this is the place for you!

top_reviews.content: Man oh man is this place awesome!!! I lived in Korea for 5 years, my husband is from Korea, so trust when I say this place does 되지국밥 (pork soup) RIGHT!!!! "Don't judge a book by its cover," but when it comes to restaurants, sometimes this is not the case.... The bright red "Michelin" sign in the front gives it away that there is something special here, on the edges of the Tenderloin.  The food is the star here ... Traditional home cooking, Busan style.... Hearty, very flavorful, the kind of food that fills you up and leaves you with a big smile.  The owners run the place, cooks the food, and serves it... Prices are very fair, considering the quality.... Don't let the neighborhood scare you away; the inside is what counts.

Would not recommend this place to non pork eaters.

To be fair I probably should have looked at their menu beforehand, but I eat at korean restaurants often and never have trouble finding dishes I can eat.

However, they only have 2 dishes that are non pork, and both are soups/noodle dishes.

We ordered the Beef Short Rib Soup and the Kalguksu. I really liked the noodles in the Kalguksu, and really liked the Beef short rib in the soup. However, both soups were very simple and not that flavorful.

Their other dishes looked good, but none could be made without pork. I wanted to order the kimchi pancake, but they said that pork is included in the batter so they could not accommodate us.

I'm sure this place would be more delicious for other people, but as non pork eaters we just couldn't have many dishes. I'm used to most restaurants being very accommodating to this so it's just odd that they are very strict to this considering they are a michelin guide restaurant.

We did not get a reservation, we called ahead and were able to get a table but had to wait 45min.

The location is also not the best as it's deep in the tenderloin, and walking to the restaurant was very unsafe and unpleasant.

Nearest parking is a parking garage that charges $18 an hour..

I saw this on the Michelin website as recommended.

It comes with a side of white rice so you should think it through if you’re getting another dish in addition.
The fried kimchi was not memorable. The edges were a bit burnt. Probably ok as a street food, not so much as an appetizer.
Drinks: the drinks were priced at city prices. Their makgeolli drink was exorbitant at $16 for a 750 ml plastic bottle. Not recommended.
Service:  It was a slow Monday night. The dinner crowd was thin so I got a lot of attention. The server was helpful and pleasant.
Location and facilities: The restaurant was cozy with a modern vibe. The place was clean and you’re not overwhelmed by the odor of food or smoke from the cooking. That’s a plus. The staff were dressed professionally and looked quite competent.
That said, this restaurant is in the heart of the tenderloin. The immediate perimeter did not exude sophistication and cleanliness, let alone a feeling of safety. I don’t recommend lingering in this area late at night or do what I did, walking from Union Square to this restaurant. Not a good idea. Parking can also be a safety issue so probably best to do ride-share.

Overall: Flavorful Korean food, cozy venue, good enough for a night out. I would’ve added another star if there were more options and if you can ignore the surroundings.

top_reviews.content: I’m so happy I stumbled across this place. I ordered a pb&j bowl and my heart was so happy. Acai is a fav of mine so the concept is familiar but these bowls are elevated on the flavor spectrum. You have to experience this for yourself!

I highly, HIGHLY recommend this place. The bowls here are not only incredibly fresh but also absolutely beautiful to look at, which makes the experience even better. They offer a great variety of bowls, including endurance, destination, and wellness bowls, so there’s always something that fits whatever I’m in the mood for. I love coming here after a workout to grab a bowl and add some  protein, but sometimes I’ll stop by just for a dessert-style bowl—it really just depends on how I’m feeling. I love being able to customize and create different variations of bowls. I’ve been coming here off and on since they opened and have always had great experiences.

The staff is very welcoming and helpful with suggestions if you’re unsure what to order. I also really love their rewards program, where you earn points on every purchase and sometimes receive coupons—it honestly feels like getting cash back and definitely makes me want to come back more often. I was even able to find and apply coupons to my order. Shoutout to Johnathan, John, and Kirsten for providing great customer service—they’re always friendly, go above and beyond, and very patient. I love the music choice as well. The only thing I’d hope for in the future is slightly extended hours, but overall this place is a favorite of mine.

top_reviews.content:
Coming from the San Gabriel Valley, which has plenty of Sichuan food, I’m always on the hunt for good Sichuan places in East Bay. Of which, there aren’t that many.

I was pleasantly surprised by the food at Mr. Liu Noodle House.

The noodles in the Beef Noodle Soup were bouncy, and the broth was wonderfully fragrant and savory. It had just the right amount of flavor and salt.

Their chengdu dumplings are delicious as well. Nice homemade wrappers with a chew to them, in a fragrant balanced chili oil. Just the right amount of Sichuan peppercorn.

The blistered green beans had a nice wok hei to them, and packed a salty punch from the pickled vegetable (“sui mi ya cai”)

Service was lovely. The boss lady 老闆娘 refilled our water multiple times.

the wontons were super delicious and filled with a really good amount of meat. the spicy oil they used tasted amazing and added a lot of flavor.

the noodles were really good too. my only complaint is they were extremely greasy, but that might just be how the dish is cooked. overall still very tasty.

My go to combination is the chongqing style special noodles and the chengdu special dumpling. Highly recommended if you can eat spicy. A clean environment and the staff is friendly. My only wish is if they would serve hot tea in non-plastic cups.

It was my first time at Mr. Liu noodle house and I was searching for some truly authentic Chinese noodles in Oakland. I found this place and ordered their beef brisket noodles (原汤牛腩面）, and the flavors instantly transported me back to China! I would highly recommend coming here.
My server was also really kind and helpful, and I liked the cozy interior. If I had any complaints, the prices might be a little high but hey what can you do about the price of food these days.

This noodle spot is truly authentic! The flavors are perfectly balanced—not overly salty like many fast-food places—making it really enjoyable to eat. The shredded chicken in chili oil is especially impressive, with rich, layered flavors that are fragrant without being greasy. Definitely a hidden gem in the area. I’ll be coming back often and recommending it to friends!

I ordered the Bún Bò Huế, but with a twist. I prefer seafood instead of the traditional meat, and they were more than happy to accommodate my request. And let me tell you—it was hands down the best Bún Bò Huế I’ve ever had at a restaurant. The broth was incredibly rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. Every bite was packed with deliciousness.

They also served it with the proper vegetables and herbs that truly complement the dish—and they were generous with them, which I really appreciated. Nothing worse than being stingy with the fresh accompaniments!

I’ll definitely be back. This place is a gem for anyone craving authentic Vietnamese cuisine.

It’s a must-stop in Oakland if you’re craving Vietnamese food beyond just pho or Chinese options. The space is small, so expect a wait during peak hours. Street parking only, so be sure not to leave any valuables in your car.

my Vietnamese friend brought me here, and it was a totally new experience for me. I’m used to just getting different kinds of pho at Vietnamese places. so happy to discover that I love bánh bèo and canh chua (Vietnamese sour soup)!

Super delicious!
Quick service!
Very stuffy and humid as expected.

Paper menus, ask the mall to move the piano, ditch the TVs and it could be a really great place. Still good food and workers. Not sure if I'll go back soon.
I really enjoyed the fresh sushi and the vibe of the restaurant! Nigiri was fresh and delicious. The jack roll with the black rice was insane. Loved the probiotic drink at the end of our meal!

Misleading Rewards Policy - Beware‼️

I’ve been a loyal customer at Kaoru Sushi and have been collecting stamps on their rewards card (10 stamps = 1 free house specialty roll).
The card clearly states it’s redeemable for a free roll with no mention that a purchase is required.

When I finally completed my card and went to redeem it, I was told by a staff member named Johnathan that I couldn’t get the free roll unless I bought something. They told me that the owner Yoyo and co-owner John are not good at english so that could be the case why it wasn’t mentioned on the stamp card. When I received the stamp card this condition was never mentioned by the server who gave it to me and anywhere on the card. It feels misleading and unfair.

I asked about it but instead of honoring the card, they insisted on the extra purchase. It’s disappointing, especially when customers spend time and money to earn rewards in good faith.

If you’re collecting stamps here, be aware that the “free roll” apparently isn’t really free. It’s a bait.

top_reviews.content:
Homeroom always serves up the ultimate comfort food for every occasion!

I frequent Homeroom for takeout, yet I never get bored because they have such a wide variety of flavors to try from. When I’m feeling something simple but aromatic, I go for the Gilroy Garlic. When I’m wanting something a little more refreshing, the Elote Mac or the Garden Pesto Mac hit the spot. And sometimes, when I really just need something to warm my tummy and my soul, the Kogi Mac is what I reach for.

Also, how could I forget? The sides! If you’re not quite in to Mac and cheese, at least come try their Bacon Brussels & Buttery Garlic Green Beans! The Brussels can also be ordered without bacon. I am definitely guilty of just getting an order of Brussels sprouts and taking it home to eat with a hot bowl of rice. Since it’s such a crowd pleaser, you could even bring it to a potluck!

I have yet to dine in at the Berkeley location. But I’ve waited in the lobby for my takeout. It’s spacious, modern, and sleek. There’s also a play area for the little ones! Perfect spot for a family dinner.

I do also want to mention the Vegan Mac! Even though I don’t have a picture of it, I still think about it often. When Trader Joe’s doesn’t have their butternut Mac and cheese in season, the Vegan Mac here is a great dupe! Smooth and creamy without the dairy.

Came here knowing it’s famous for mac and cheese. We ordered the mac and cheese as well as a burger and fries. The mac and cheese was good, portions were generous, and we couldn’t even finish it.

The burger and fries were awesome too, juicy and satisfying. Very kid friendly place, which makes it a great spot for families. Would come back again.

I didn’t know we had something like this nearby! We had the Elote mac, the Patty Melt, Garlic parmesan fries, and Cheddar bacon ranch fries and EVERYTHING WAS SO GOOD!!! The workers are all super nice and we had an amazing time, 110% recommend❤️

3/6/2026*
We were craving mac n cheese and came back to try some of their other flavors.

This time we ordered the Kogi Short Rib Mac and the Garlicky Bacon Mac.

Both were delicious. The kogi short rib mac had a sweet flavor from the kogi bbq sauce, along with Gouda, pecorino, scallions, garlic butter, and sriracha. If you like a little kick of heat, this is your go-to.

The garlicky bacon mac came with lots of bacon, garlic gouda, and pecorino. It tasted cheesier compared to the short rib mac. If you are a bacon lover, this is your go-to.

10/14/2024
We discovered Homeroom through a podcast interview with founder, and was surprised to find they're based in the East Bay, so we decided to check it out. We ordered an elote bowl as a starter and the seasonal special BBQ pulled pork mac and cheese. Unfortunately, the elote bowl arrived after the mac and cheese. The corn was soft and sweet, with delicious cheese and pepper powder that added a great kick to the flavor. The BBQ pulled pork mac and cheese was equally impressive—nice and cheesy, with surprisingly juicy pulled pork.

Our new favorite spot in the bay for a mac&cheese craving, which is way too often lately. Unbeatable prices and the creamiest mac. Vegetarian options galore and so many flavours, it’s impossible to choose.
Luckily they have a mac&cheese trio- great for sharing and date nights. That and a glass of wine? Score and score.

Staff and GM Erick are all so friendly and caring, we just wanted to hang out with them! Can’t wait to come back for one of their event nights- what an amazing spot.

I went in for lunch and I’m not sure what the issue was, but the service was pretty much nonexistent. At the 45-minute mark, we still hadn’t received a glass of water. The people at the table next to us told us it had taken 1 hour and 45 minutes to get their food, and we also noticed a 20-minute lag between serving two patrons their dishes at the same table.

I was super thirsty, and the people around us were warning us about the long wait. We told the server we were going to head out and to cancel our order, and the server said nothing.

I was under the impression they were understaffed and maybe the server didn’t usually work front of house? There’s no way this restaurant would be in business, let alone expanding, based on the experience we had, so maybe it was just a fluke. Oakland’s street food scene did not disappoint on my first visit. I tried the Brussels sprouts with aioli sauce, and they were absolutely awesome. The portion size was generous for the price, making it feel like a great deal.

One tip: eat them right away to fully enjoy that crispness. Overall, a simple yet delicious street food find that I’d definitely recommend.

Staff is extremely friendly, and accommodating for anything you ask for. Parking can be a little challenging because its downtown unless you pay for parking.

Quality food, made with love! I highly recommend trying and promise you will become a regular patron.

Everything was perfect. Friendly and super knowledgeable bartender who made us some of the best cocktails I've ever had. The food was really special too - fine dining in a relaxed atmosphere, with every detail carefully attended to, and yet with no pretentiousness.

This is my first Google review because I have never felt so inclined to write a review. I just want to say how utterly disappointed I am in this place and the experience my friends and I had yesterday. We were all so excited to try the drinks and indulge in the caviar service to celebrate the 4th in the city, but we were practically turned away through no fault of our own.

My friend had our reservation set for the evening of July 4th, and yet, through no fault of our own, Left Door’s reservation system magically had it set for July 5! Genuinely, what? Our email confirmation clearly showed that we did not make the booking error and that it was their system error. Their idea of making up for it was offering to let us hang out at the bar. Mind you, there were 7 of us and there was one seat left at the bar. I’m sorry, do you expect us to split that one remaining seat 7 ways? 🤣

We were so excited to try this place out because we had heard such good things. However, even though this reservation mix-up was their system error, no effort was made to find an alternative, and no offer to make up for the mistake was extended. My friends and I had made our 4th of July plans days in advance around coming to Left Door, and this mix-up left us scrambling to find food when every restaurant in the city had at least an hour-and-a-half wait time (god bless Walgreens). I expected more from an establishment that has earned a reputation for stellar customer service. I understand that mistakes happen, but it was so annoying to have them try to make up for theirs with a simple “Sorry, ladies.”

I would recommend that you double- and triple-check your reservation before going to this place, because their system will just happen to move you around to a different date, and they will “Sorry ladies” you out of the place😭

I recently discovered a one-of-a-kind speakeasy secretly nestled on Union Ave in the prime Cow Hollow area of San Francisco, and it offered one of the best experiences the city has to offer. On a Tuesday evening, the venue was bustling with professionals, creating an elegant and lively atmosphere. Although reservations are highly recommended due to their popularity, we were fortunate enough to wait in the stylish bar area until we were seated. Our evening unfolded beautifully with expertly crafted top-shelf drinks, delectable appetizers, and ultimately, a sumptuous dinner. Each cocktail was visually stunning and perfectly balanced in flavor, while the appetizers were a delightful prelude to the meal, bursting with unique and magical tastes. A special thanks to Marie, whose attentive and accommodating service ensured our experience was not only exquisite but also comforting and inviting. Her dedication truly set this speakeasy apart. We were so impressed that we decided to stay for dinner and are already planning to return with more friends to share this upscale dining haven. Whether you’re seeking a sophisticated night out or a cozy spot to unwind, this hidden gem on Union Ave is the perfect choice. Thank you to the entire team, especially Marie, for making our night truly special. We can’t wait to return!

Holy frickin moly. This is my new favorite Ethiopian place. The food was spectacular. I tried the chicken Tibs and the Asa Kifto (ahi tuna). If you can handle spice, I’d say go full spice. The spicy sauce is incredible and the flavors for the whole plate was amazingly unique. Lastly, the service was so good. All in all, I couldn’t recommend Mela Bistro more to any person wanting to try delicious Ethiopian food.

Mela Bistro is something special. This is the kind of place that reminds you what a gift it is when food, hospitality, and tradition come together so effortlessly.

top_reviews.content:
There's a lot of great pizza in the Bay and State Flour is right up there. The ambiance, service, and starters are too.

I went in with a friend during a busy summer Saturday last month and we were lucky to get a walk-up table without a wait. One downside: they don't take reservations. Elmwood gets busy, especially when something at Cal brings in the parents/alumni.

Our server was great. We asked for the sausage to go on half of the pizza and they happily obliged. We didn't think about the salad. The server intuited that would be desired and simply put the dried prosciutto for the delicious salad when it came out so my dinner mate could enjoy it just as much as I could. When asked something specific about the wine, she said she was newer & didn't know but would ask someone else. Much appreciated.

If you’re in the neighborhood I think this is a solid option, although it’s not something so special that it’s worth a long trip. I tried The Chloe which I was impressed by the depth of flavor, but I would make some changes. The potato on the pizza is basically hiding and is overwhelmed by the other flavors. I think the potato should be put on top instead of bottom so that it crisps instead of the arugula. The classic pep is a decent pizza but nothing really stood out to me about it. The staff was all friendly and came by to check in multiple times and refill waters often.

Take the warmth of a local community-run kitchen, add in some killer flavors and textures, sprinkle on some coziness from the ample mood lighting and you’ve got the magic that is State Flour Pizza.

I don’t think I could’ve asked for a better experience at State Flour Pizza Co, and that includes the 30 minute wait time for a table. This is the kind of place that hires the neighborhood teens in the summers while still taking the time to source all fresh ingredients.

Consensus for favorite was split between the mushroom-sausage and green goddess pizzas, but the margherita and hot honey pepperoni were almost as good. Apple salad gave some much needed freshness to the table.

This pizza place is as perfect for a family dinner as it is for a first date, and is just as likely to have a table of college friends as it is a post-conference debrief. That’s because it’s designed for the community, so it attracts the community.

Yes, the pizza! Grateful for extra mushrooms instead of sausage!
But rarely do I review a salad: the apple endive salad with frozen/sliced/dehydrated prosciutto…MUAAA! The apples were perfectly sliced thin and the tarragon vinaigrette (not overdressed) with the blue cheese crumble and pistachios were proportioned and balanced to taste not visuals. Will try to recreate at home but next time, I’m…not…sharing!! 😂

Pizza is best straight out of the oven there and the service was actually service. ALL the staff were kind and patient.

The state flour salad was beautifully done too!

All in all, we were extremely impressed and would wholeheartedly recommend this place. 🍕

I recently visited Tycoon Kitchen and had a very enjoyable dining experience. The restaurant offers a welcoming atmosphere with a modern and comfortable setting that is perfect for both casual meals and gatherings with friends or family. The food was fresh, flavorful, and prepared with care. The menu features a good variety of dishes, allowing everyone to find something they enjoy. I especially appreciated the quality of the ingredients and the attention to presentation. Portions were satisfying, and everything arrived promptly.

The restaurant was clean, well maintained, and provided a pleasant dining environment from start to finish. Combined with the excellent service and consistently good food, it made for a memorable visit. I would definitely return and recommend Tycoon Kitchen to anyone looking for a reliable and enjoyable dining experience.

I want to share my experience with Tycoon Kitchen. The food is really delicious. I come here 2–3 times a week, and it’s always good. The manager is very attentive and friendly. The soup was spicy but very flavorful. Also, they cooked the rice perfectly lol. The coffee was strong, but delicious.

Tasty and speedy fast casual / takeout-centric Thai spot conveniently located on the first floor of Salesforce Tower, making it the perfect workday lunch spot. Tycoon Kitchen has been quite the prominent feature in my rotation of office lunches, and I’ve been impressed every single time by the consistency and quality of their food, the efficiency of their service (especially with only such a small kitchen), and how friendly the staff and owner are. My go-to is their eggplant and tofu stir-fry, which often seems to take a few extra minutes to prepare, so the owner will often offer me a free Thai tea or spring rolls for waiting for what he considers a long time but what I think is perfectly reasonable given how busy they are. To make things more efficient, they also have two kiosks outside that you can order on, or you can poke your head inside if you’d rather speak to someone live.

The food is absolutely delicious, and I love how flavorful everything is (including the tofu — a rare sight these days)! The portions are also quite generous. I’m often left with a healthy amount of leftovers, perfect for dinner or an afternoon snack.

If you're looking for a pleasant spot for a date or to catch up with a long-time friend, this is a lovely place for that purpose. You'll be able to have an actual conversation because it isn't a loud venue and the architecture is lovely.

We had never been to Julia’s before and now look forward to going there again for another great, special meal.

top_reviews.content: I stumbled upon this spot randomly for dinner on a Sunday night, which is arguably one of the best nights to come. It has a cool vibe and was my first time having Japanese bbq, which apparently comes from Korean bbq. On Friday-Sun they have a set menu, and weekdays à la carte.   This is one of my new favorite restaurants. The owner Andy Chiang cares deeply about the food and provided and exceptional experience for his diners. Every dish was delicious and the sake selection was also great. Easily one of the best meals of all time, and I've dined at multiple 3 Michelin star restaurants and this is my 8th year as a yelp elite member.

Simply the best. The staff were incredibly friendly and made the whole experience feel so special. My friend and I had such a great night here. You can really tell they care about the quality of the meat, and they shared so much knowledge about how everything is grilled and prepared. Amazing food, amazing service, and such a memorable experience.

Dining at Yakiniku Shodai was an outstanding experience from start to finish, seamlessly blending top-tier Wagyu cuts with thoughtfully crafted side courses. The curated tasting menu progressed beautifully, featuring highlights like delicate Australian Wagyu beef tongue topped with scallions, heavily marbled Japanese A5 Wagyu paired with fresh wasabi and kelp, and standout creative dishes like a rich Wagyu chawanmushi and a perfectly seared scallop over crisp nori. Paired with chilled Masumi sake, the exceptional meat quality, artful presentation, and well-paced menu make Yakiniku Shodai a top-tier destination for Japanese BBQ lovers. Definitely a must try.

This place truly exceeded our expectations! The food was outstanding, perfectly seasoned, beautifully plated, and bursting with flavor. You can tell the ingredients are fresh and thoughtfully prepared.

The service was just as impressive. Circle our chef was warm, attentive, and made sure we had everything we needed without ever feeling rushed. The atmosphere was inviting and comfortable, making the whole experience even more enjoyable.

Highly recommend to anyone looking for excellent food and top-notch service. We’ll definitely be returning!

Glad I chose this spot for my birthday night with my girls. We got the reservation a few days ahead. It seems to be quiet popular. The chef and the host gave us such an impressive experience. The food and service are what I would expect from an authentic upscale Yakiniku place. I also enjoyed the conversation with the chefs and the host.

The chefs here cook the meat in front of you and serve to you directly. All the meats are cooked to perfection with just the right amount of seasonings.

I’m glad they don't over season the meat nor over complicate it like other American upscale Japanese restaurants.(I enjoy food creativity if they taste good and if the complexity makes sense but sadly a lot of upscale restaurants failed to make it makes sense to me.)

Reading some other reviews on the bbq smell got me a bit surprised. I wouldn’t mind if the upscale bbq restaurant smells like a bbq place, so I am surprised ppl complained about the smoky smell in this kind of restaurant.

Thank you Chris and Circle for the fun experience!

Three of us had a couple bento boxes and a nigiri  and sashimi combo. Dinner requires three item bento, and the tempura was the star. Nicely battered and fried just right. Chicken teriyaki was chicken teriyaki, if you know what I mean. The California rolls were good… they go the extra mile and mince the imitation crab as opposed to some places that just slice a little chunk. And the spicy tuna roll was not really spicy but tasty enough.

The sashimi and nigiri were very fresh and decently portioned. I prefer smaller and higher quality, which is what they served. They could go a little hotter on the wasabi. Theirs was mild.

And of course miso soup and salad with that sesame dressing I love. Fun meal, great place.

August update.
Visited again cuz we liked it so much the last time. Guess what, still love it! Karage excellent taste and crispness. Hamachi Kama grilled top perfection. Carpaccio melts in your mouth. Bento boxes are good and fill you up. The treasure box sushi was beautiful and simply delicious. Service is good.

I've had sushi in prestigious restaurants, make no mistake, this is quality sushi at a very reasonable price. The seafood/fish was fresh, and the ingredients were done perfectly. Even the tea was exceptional. I haven't enjoyed a sushi this much for a while. Try it out. You won't regret it.

Visited this place just once and were really happy with the quality of their rolls. The fish was fresh and the ingredients were well balanced well. Their menu is pretty big so it took some time to pick different rolls (meaning with different fish) We ordered three sets for two people and all of them were pretty good. The service was fast and overall experience was nice as the neighborhood where this place located is very cute. 4/5 from me just because the place is good but not special

We had a great experience! Sushi and sashimi are very fresh and delicious. The service is fast and friendly. The tuna poke salad is the best! (It comes with soup and salad for only $13!) strongly  recommend this dish. I usually loves oyster. I tried oyster with quail eggs in cold sake. To be honest I didn't like it much. The oyster is not that great, but everything else is phenomenal. We will definitely come back for Bento and Tuna Poke. Sooooo many choices of sushi menu.

This place is awesome. Our new favorite place. Fresh and clean, Our waitress was amazing and friendly, chefs are excellent. Nothing bad to say, totally a five star experience. Thank you for a great time. See you soon.

Best falafel wrap I’ve ever had! Thick, hearty, and absolutely delicious, with incredible flavors bursting in every bite. The owner is also extremely sweet and friendly, and the service is fantastic. Highly recommend!!

The food is some of the best middle eastern cuisine I have had. The tea is also amazing. I felt like I was a host at a friend’s home. I sampled the falafel, had fresh hummus, salad and Yemeni style chicken breast.

Billy is a wonderful host and he takes great pride in his product and service. I HIGHLY recommend visiting Falafelland for fantastic food. Falafelland is like an oasis for any traveler who wants great cuisine and conversation (if you want).

top_reviews.content: This small cafe is on the alley directly across from the hall of justice and has four tables and another dozen seats along a wall. The menu is limited but the food is good and the quantity is large. There’s free water with glass containers you can bring to your seat. We ordered two bulgabi bowls, one a mini and the other the regular.  Both had broccoli, chap chai, brown rice and a lot of beef. It came with sauces as well. The food was good and a mini would’ve been enough for both of us. Service was friendly but the beef was a bit tough to chew. The place is large but spartan but clean.

Both got the cupbap. A decent portion of food but super average taste-wise, no sauce in it so pretty flavorless, atmosphere is so weird. Combination of Mexican Hawaiian Korean. None of the bowls come with kimchi which is crazy for a place called kiss my Seoul. Bulgogi just tastes and looks like beef teriyaki. Don’t think I’d ever come again and shocked at the other ratings.

Excellent food, portion, and service. Was in the area for a meeting and the price to portion ratio was excellent. The restaurant included a side of chicken because they accidentally input it wrong, even though I said it was okay.

Both the chicken and the beef bulgogi are excellent and I'd highly recommend them! Was fast to order and prepare!

Excellent cupbap with generous portion, taco was not great.

I had the regular size bulgogi cupbap ($16) and a single chicken taco ($5) just to try it. I've been meaning to visit this restaurant for years but it just wasn't convenient for me until today.

The cupbap container was filled to the brim and food inside was packed in. I didn't have breakfast today, so I was pretty hungry when I came here for lunch, but I still didn't fully finish it. I recommend ordering the mini size if you're not that hungry and you don't want to have leftovers.

Inside the paper bowl, there was plenty of bulgogi on top of broccoli, zucchini, carrot, cauliflower, glass noodles, and white rice mixed with a little bit of black rice — this dyed the rice purple-ish. It was garnished with green onion and sesame. Everything seemed to be seasoned with black pepper. The bulgogi was tender with some browning and tasted perfect. The glass noodles seemed to have been stir-fried with a sweet soy sauce. The vegetables still retained a bit of a crunch. The rice was a little mushy like it was just slightly overcooked, but I guess that's to fully cook the black rice.

I don't recommend getting a taco. There was a single tortilla. It was slightly toasted but still got pretty soggy from the salsa and chicken juices. The flavors didn't pair well. The chicken tasted like bulgogi and it just didn't work work well with salsa. The salsa verde and salsa roja were also a bit bland. You can get much better tacos in the Mission for less money.

There are plenty of seats here. There's also a small area with packaged Korean snacks like Turtle Chips.

Maybe the other dishes are good, but the smash burger was a huge disappointment. I saw a couple specks of red pepper in the aioli, I assume that’s the “kimchi.” Just a regular burger, not at ALL with any kind of discernible Korean influence.

top_reviews.content: Absolutely phenomenal,  there really isn't enough I can say about Bento and Bowls. Every experience has been excellent from the food to the service and staff. A great selection of meats, sauces, and styles that make you feel warm and comforted.So swing in and get some fantastic Korean food at a super fair price and make sure to try the Milkis soda!

SO good! Hella food, all delicious and super nice peeps work there. The beef bulgogi bento is a classic. I love that the bento comes with a variety of all kinds of food like pickled cucumbers, shrimp skewer and salad. The spicy chicken is amazing too and the kimchi fried rice comes with a perfectly cooked egg on top. The portions are HUGE. Can't wait to go back to try the Katsu!

A nice small place to eat delicious Korean food.  The bulgogi was marinated really flavorful and the soy garlic chicken wings were very tasty too!  Too bad you are only able to order the korean short ribs in a bento box, but not in a bowl.  There is a small parking lot.  They have spam musubi for $2.00, Korean cup noodle for $3.00 or $5.00 and Korean ice -creams and drinks.  It is a convenient go-to for the students from Oakland Tech High School since they are located across the street.  I would definitely go back for the food.

HORRIBLE!!! I went in, and the person who took my order made the food without washing his hands. He was rude and nasty. He made my food in less than 2 minutes. The food looked like scraps. The bibimbap had soggy, wilted green stuff, rice, and very little meat, really no meat. I tried it out, and it had a nasty, weird taste. The food was cold and definitely not fresh. I read previous reviews, and they lied! I should have taken a picture before I threw it out. They should really get zero stars!

Went here with a friend to grab a quick bite. Restaurant is located in a small strip mall with 3-4 other businesses around a shared parking lot. The space is a little dingy / not super inviting and when we went the bathroom was not available. There were some small tables with chairs and a TV playing in the background. I ordered veggie bibimbap and my friend got the kim chi fried rice. I asked for a little extra of one of the sides and was told no which was a little disappointing.... I mean it was a vegetable and we were the only people in there on a quiet night. But I loaded up on hot sauce and made it into smaller 2 meals. Not my favorite Korean spot but a solid choice all around.

The drag show was super fun and interactive, and the service was fast and friendly. Definitely want to come back for more of their events!

I had the pleasure of hosting my 50th birthday celebration at 510 Fluid, and from beginning to end, the experience was exceptional. The hospitality and communication were top tier from the owner all the way to the staff. Everyone was professional, attentive, and made sure everything ran smoothly.

The food was absolutely delicious, and the establishment itself is immaculate and very tastefully designed. The ambiance really elevated the entire event and made it feel special.

I am truly glad I chose 510 Fluid and I look forward to hosting another event there in the future. If you’re planning a dinner, celebration, or special occasion, I highly recommend this venue.

Fluid510 is a great special event venue!  My daughter had her wedding there and it was wonderful.  Fluid510 is a blank slate. You can dress it up or dress it down depending on what you want.  The owners are extremely helpful, flexible, and creative.  Weddings are stressful,  yet the crew at Fluid510 was fantastic the day of the wedding!  They took good care of everyone; they were kind and generous and attentive.  They made sure every detail was right.  The food was customized for our event and our guests loved it and a great time was had by everyone.   Thank you Fluid510!!

top_reviews.content: I’m from the east coast, Philadelphia.. Been eating phó my entire life and let me tell you.. I have NEVER had a bowl of phó as good as the one I got here. Hands down the most flavorful bowl I’ve ever ate anywhere. Service was fast, amazing people, and a relaxing cozy environment. Truly an amazing experience all around. Highly recommend this spot to anyone! I got the grilled fish rolls and the sliced beef and beef balls, *extra beef balls* with the spicy stuff paste for that extra kick

Try the Twisted Thai Tea, a strange and wonderful mix of Thai iced tea and Vietnamese iced coffee.  I was slightly skeptical, but I'm glad that my curiosity triumphed.

My lemongrass beef pho was flavorful and and perfectly executed.  Service was fast and friendly.  The space is comfortable... don't forget to look up at the beautiful murals on the ceiling.

As the kids say  "10/10.  No notes."

Great portions with excellent homemade taste! Staff is friendly and helpful. The chicken broth soup really hit the spot on a chilly day. Had chicken spring roll and grilled pork Banh Mi. Everything tasted great. They have indoor and outdoor seating. Perfect for a quick meal or hangout with friends and family. I would love to come back to try their pho.

The food is top-notch! Served in real fancy ceramic bowls with good quality ingredients. There is also a lovely Buddha statue made out of marble. We spoke to the parent of the owner for about five’s minutes and really liked them. I would return in a heartbeat. 💓

I love this place. Best banh mi hands down. Generous fillings, and attention to detail - even the carrots are amazing! They make their own mayo and paté as well. The bread is specially baked for them, and is the perfect soft-on-the-inside/crispy-on-the-outside loaf that a proper banh mi commands.

My second love there is the "fried egg rolls wrapped in spring rolls." Pure genius of texture and flavor that is the best of both worlds. Oh, that egg roll crunch combined with crisp cucumber and herby goodness, all dipped in a savory sauce! I could eat those every day.

And don't get me started on the pho! I don't get it too often because I end up finishing it all, and it's sleepy time for me about an hour later!

I recommend anything with grilled fish. I'm mainly a pescatarian, so this is what I've tried. My omnivore friends profess their love for the other things on the menu. I've told many friends to go there, and now some of them go sometimes two days in a row!

There is street parking right outside (metered), and you can find free parking around the corner in the residential streets off Gilman. There are both indoor and outdoor seating, the latter an enclosed patio with transparent roofing.

Portions are generous, and there is attention to detail in every ingredient. This is very intentional. I enjoy their posts on social media, too. The only downside to PhoSho is realizing you've taken the last bite!

The guys here that run the place are fantastic! They are really trying to do something special there, and are succeeding at it. When you're there, have a look around at the art - full wall and ceiling murals representing Vietnamese and Asian culture surround you. I feel so at home there!

I hadn’t been in awhile & was wishing there were a good pho place around, so decided to give Tigon a go, after a bit of time has passed.

I am so glad I did!  It surpassed my expectations in all areas. Delicious, artful, fresh, good size portions and value, and very friendly and attentive service. I was hankering for meat, so ordered a build your own beef pho.  And, Vietnamese rolls.  Everything was so fresh!  The menu includes many vegetarian options, too, which is sometimes what I hanker for!

I am so happy they are here and seem to be doing well! The restaurant was fairly busy.  Would be a great place to meet friends before or after a movie!

Surprised by the positive Reddit reviews because my experience was disappointing. The pho was overcooked, oily, and tasted unrefined? That we did not finish. I also ordered the crepe, and unfortunately the lettuce and raw vegetables tasted like soap, which made the dish inedible.

A family place with good food and comfortable setting. As sick, the service was a bit slow but I’m sure the kitchen was doing the best they could. We all quite enjoyed the food and it gave us time to chat anyway.

Open faced crab sandwich and fries.. yum! If you want a cold crab sandwich, you can get that also, but closed with two slices of bread.

Eggs and corned beef hash didn’t disappoint.

They know how to cook hash browns among the best of them! Crispy and yummy! They also know how to make soft eggs when you order them “wet”.

Update Oct 2022 with molcajete photo. Fun and looks quite dramatic.

My favorite here is still the short ribs. Apparently I start eating as soon as they arrive and forget to take a photo 😂

Delicious food, beautifully presented, great service.

They have expanded their Mexican offerings and so we tried the Chile Relleno Plate.  I enjoyed the grilled fish tacos on their original menu and knew it would be good -- and it was!  Was surprised by the tomatoey sauce on top of the chile but it was a great addition.

They offer their amazing breakfast dishes all day. I always love Eggs Benedict so I ordered it with smoked salmon. Yumm and perfectly cooked, as you can see in the photo after I sliced into the egg.

Other great dishes I've had here - the braised short ribs melt in your mouth. Prime rib, not on the menu right now, was huge and fabulous. Fried chicken and waffle was a bit too healthy for me, ha ha, because of the white meat chicken.

I'm always surprised that this place isn't more crowded. I think it may be because this place offers a wide variety of cuisines and people are suspicious when you can get American style burgers, Asian dishes, and Mexican dishes on one menu -- they expect only one cuisine per restaurant for authenticity. But Duo Grill prepares everything very well and always presents every plate beautifully. Especially when there are different tastes and opinions in your group, this is an excellent choice.

Still one of the top breakfast spots under the radar in the area, excellent presentation really delicious breakfast menu, well made espresso drinks, and super friendly and attentive service.
Also nice, and quiet, and a welcome change from the bustling local breakfast scene.

A mellow spot with friendly and attentive service every time. They have a great classic menu with American staples like Cobb salad, burgers, sandwiches, and pasta dishes. They also have a very tasty Mexican menu with dishes like enchiladas, tacos, nachos, burritos, and Chile rellenos. The Chile Verde is flavorful and juicy. To be specific, the tonkatsu was so thin that some pieces were just breading on less than a whisper of pork, yet it still managed to be very tough, the mixed tempura, rather than light and crispy, was a soggy, oily mess almost without flavor, the edamame were undercooked and undersalted, the california roll was a scant 6 piece portion instead of the typical 8, and the greatest offense was the plain rice. It carried a distinct, strong, and revolting aroma of perfume, perhaps from hand soap not sufficiently washed off when washing the rice, or someone walking by the prepared rice while spraying perfume. Regardless, it was inedible. The server seemed disorganized and unable to easily track the contents of a fairly simple order, in spite of the restaurant being quite empty, which is not surprising as the last time I ordered from them, about a year ago, they managed to forget an item entirely, in spite of my having paid for it.

You get 2 Kati rolls per order..warm chewy wraps, the contents SO good: slow-cooked meats and or veggies, and definitely ask for the mild stuff because they can get very spicy! If you do American medium spicy but not indian or Asian medium spicy, get only mild things😉👍

The food here is really amazing. You can taste the authenticity in every bite. The owner makes all the spice blends, sauces, and seasonings from scratch, and it really shows in the flavor. He is passionate about what he does and cares a lot about quality and staying true to the food. It’s rare to find a place with this much heart and attention to detail.

Food prepared with clean ingredients and authentic recipes. Highly recommend!

Wow is an understatement! This concept really intrigued me and I'm so happy we gave Pochys a try! Had the opportunity to connect with the owner when we visited and his passion and mission were undeniable. He told us all of the masalas (spice blends) were roasted and blended in house, something that truly makes a difference. The food was amazing, extremely flavorful and fresh; you can tell it's made upon order because everything comes out piping hot! My favorite was the chicken Kathi/rolls which were bursting with flavor and the texture of the chicken was fall apart. Everything we tried was delicious and we will definitely be back! PS: they are dog friendly and also have an outdoor patio.

I recently visited Pochys for the second time, and it did not disappoint! This time, I tried their Chicken Tenali Kura Roll and Curry, and both were absolutely outstanding. The flavors were rich and vibrant, and the dishes had that comforting, home-cooked quality—like something my mom would make. It’s clear that they use fresh, quality ingredients and take a lot of care in their preparation.

What really sets Pochys apart, though, is the owner. He’s incredibly kind and generous, making sure every guest feels welcomed and well taken care of. It’s rare to find such genuine hospitality these days, and it really adds to the overall experience.

I truly wish Pochys continued success because it deserves to thrive. I’ll definitely be back soon to try more of their amazing dishes! Highly recommend.

First time coming here after the place opened. The staff and owner are very friendly and helpful. I ordered the butter masala, which was excellent and despite a small-ish potion, it was filling. I appreciated the owner telling us about their handmade spices and Michelin star style cooking, making everything from scratch.
A couple pointers to improve the atmosphere and overall experience:
- Replace the AI art with real art (though the giraffe was quite charming)
- Keep the storage shelf in the men’s closed, it gave me an odd feeling
- Either lower the tables or replace the chairs, the tables are a little too tall
- The velvet chairs are comfortable, but I think they’ll get stained easily
Congratulations on your opening!

I tried the Sichuan chilli oil dumpling and the beef and celery dumpling. Both were nice.

I had a very disappointing experience with the food from this restaurant. The meal I received tasted spoiled and not fresh, which made it impossible to finish. Food quality and freshness are extremely important, and this experience raised serious concerns about how the food is being stored and prepared.

I hope the restaurant improves its quality control, because customers should be able to trust that the food they receive is safe and fresh.

Ok it’s been a few months since my visit because I didn’t want to write it right away but I had a disappointing experience.

First, they were out of a few items I wanted. This was Saturday lunchtime. Specifically, all the mini pan-fried buns. He told us after seating and ordering. Bummer but ok. Then we ordered. I won’t go into the details.

He tells us up front they are short staffed in the kitchen and we MUST take our entire order at one time. Okaaay. Well that’s pretty normal I think. So we ordered 5 items. Keep in mind there are three of us so that’s a sizable order I think. And it’s not cheap here.

After 15 minutes one item comes. Ok no sweat, I’m sure it’ll all be out shortly. Nope. 15 minutes later we all what’s up and he says they are short staffed in the kitchen. He’ll check. He brings out second dish. Two dishes in 30 minutes. Still three to go.

Now I’m noticing other tables have been getting their food. And they ordered after us. I’m like, what? I ask the guy again to check. Takes him 8 more minutes to come back. In the meantime I see even more people get their food. Finally he’s back: “I’m sorry, there was an error in the order printing machine”. I’ll make your food now.

It’s 45 minutes since ordering and almost an hour since sitting. I’m like, no thanks we can’t wait longer, we’ll just pay for what we had. He rolls his eyes and said he has to try and back it out, or something like that, like I’m really inconveniencing him. Another 5 minutes for that.

Don’t like the way it happened. Don’t like the customer service or the attitude. My few months cooling off period didn’t help I guess.

I will say the food we did get was good.

top_reviews.content: The sushi and sashimi here were so incredibly tender -- the fish would literally melt in my mouth! We got a tasty soup-based main dish as well, and I'd recommend getting it with the sushi if you're very hungry. The service was fantastic, and our waitress was very kind and generous. If you're craving a good mix of sushi and korean food, this place is definitely worth it!

I really wanted to like Yasijang since it is close to where I live and run by some genuinely nice Korean folks, both in the kitchen and front of house. Unfortunately, most of the dishes fell pretty flat for me.

Here’s a breakdown of everything we tried:

Mini Jeon - This came out as a set of three mini pancakes, and while they were fried expertly with a nice crisp exterior, I did not really get much of the ingredient flavors at all, which was supposed to have an array of vegetables and seafood.

Truffle Bosot Fry - These were fantastic. Each enoki was fried so the stems were splayed out and then dusted in truffle salt. It was clear the chef has a deft hand at the fryer, as both of the first two starters had an amazing crunch to them.

Spicy Tuna Tower - This seemed like a popular item, but it was really disappointing. It felt like a quantity over quality dish, with the spicy tuna indeed piled high, but very clumpy, as if it had just been scooped straight out of the fridge, and not a pleasant texture. There was not much flavor or spice to it and the kappa maki rolls that the tuna sat atop were unfortunately not made well, as most of them fell apart just from picking them up with chopsticks.

K-Fried Chicken - Pretty good value since you get 8 decently sized pieces for $20, or $22 if you want to add a sauce. It was curious that they do not let you do half and half, since the sauces are likely pre-made and that is such a common option at most other KFC spots. The bigger issue was the fry on the chicken as huge pieces of batter were missing from every piece, and it did not have that signature shattering crunch I expect, which suggested the oil was not hot enough and that they did not double fry the chicken. The soy and garlic flavor was actually pretty good, so it was doubly disappointing that the chicken was not fried properly.

Hwe-Muchim. - This dish was an absolute disaster. The cubes of fish and salad were absolutely drowning in cho-jang, and it was really unbalanced, so all you tasted was gochujang. The lettuce was so wilted under the sheer amount of liquid that it made the dish difficult to eat. I actually took this home, drained most of the liquid, rinsed off the fish, added fresh greens and a homemade dressing, and it tasted much better.

The staff were friendly enough, but this place is clearly targeting a drinking or late-night crowd so I would avoid if your main goal is to enjoy the food itself.  Seems like a fun enough place if you were just wanting to stop in and have some snacks with your drinks or as an end of night stop as the 4-cha or 5-cha (IYKYK).

Overall, it’s a Korean pocha (gastropub) with a great vibe. The prices are pretty affordable compared to other places in the area. The service is decent, but the food falls a bit short. I do recommend the Buldak (fire chicken), though.

I came for dinner (made a reservation)  before the symphony (about 1.5 block walk from Herbst theatre).  From the restaurant's website, I imagined the restaurant to be much larger.  Instead, it was small - probably sits 25 (tightly) without the bar and maybe 20 with the bar.  My table was next to the bar - felt cramped sitting in the corner - that's why it is a 4 star rating.  Food was served temperature hot with kindness.  Flavors, smell and presentation were good.  I would recommend the sausage basket, a variety of different sausages, for an appetizer.  It's a good segue into your main entrees which are small shared plates.

They have a bar challenge - filling up a vase with empty bottle caps.  Thought that was fun and an incentive/motivation for returning.  The restaurant definitely would be a good bar place to hang out and simply have fun.

Service was excellent - orders kept coming out as well as for deliveries.  The wait staff always had a smile and kept asking if we are okay or if we need anything else.  I thought the restaurant stools were unusual.   Since there is no space to put your coat, purse, bags, etc., the stools open up for storage.  I thought this was cleaver.
Perfect Korean fare, served by extremely courteous owners. Great spot that feels very authentic.  I did not try the sushi but assume that is great too.

Mango massi tastes like water!!!!!!!

We had such a lovely experience at Naan N Curry.

top_reviews.content:
Belly is a quiet little spot on College Ave right off the Rockridge BART station. We came around noon on a weekday and were pretty much the only patrons there for the duration of our meal outside of a handful of takeout orders.

Service was a little rough since there was only one person working, so we had to flag them down whenever we needed anything. That said, I completely sympathize with how tough it is to run a restaurant in the current environment, and I appreciated the effort.

We started with the kimchi arancini balls, which were excellent. They were fried nicely, the filling was ooey gooey and cheesy, and the kimchi aioli added a great cooling balance to the dish. For my main, I went with the 2 taco platter, which comes with a small salad and chips, and it was more than enough food. I tried one steak, egg, and cheese taco and one surf taco, and both had great flavor. The steak was cooked perfectly, the fried egg added a really nice richness and creaminess, and I loved the fries inside, which reminded me a lot of the Cali style you usually associate with San Diego.

The only real miss for me was the panko batter on the fish taco, since I prefer a lighter, more delicate tempura style batter. The flavor was still solid, just not something I’d order again. My bigger hesitation overall is the price, since the tacos are pretty steep at nearly $8 each and over $20 for the 2 taco platter, which makes it hard to imagine coming back frequently even though I did enjoy the overall flavors.

We just finished eating here for Restaurant week / Date night. Let me start off by saying the food is so packed with Flavor. We had the Kimchi appetizer balls it has Cheese Risotto and Kimchi. We had the Asian salad. It was light and crunchy and perfectly balanced. The Miso Butter Spaghetti was rich and full of flavor I added grilled chicken to it and that was a perfect combo. My wife had the Silk road spaghetti and added Salmon. It was tangy and spicy but not too spicy.  We will definitely be back here soon.       🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥

Been living in Rockridge for awhile and finally got out to try this cute Asian-Mexican fusion joint!

Belly has a darling blue storefront, and the cute aesthetic continues throughout the dining area. Service was really friendly and the vibe is casual but inviting.

I ordered three tacos (Korean Hot Chicken, Cali, and Pork Belly) and enjoyed them all — fresh ingredients and packed full. I do wish they had a bit more flavor, particularly in the Korean Hot Chicken.

The salad was a nice surprise to have included and the vinaigrette was really refreshing! It might have been my favorite part of the platter.

Came to Belly with a belly empty; left Belly with a belly full! Pretty happy about that.

Solid food with really nice staff in a really cute restaurant. My girlfriend and I stopped into Belly for the first time around a week ago and were pretty impressed with our food. My pork belly burrito was big and tasty and her Korean Hot Chicken bowl was pretty great (but probably could have used a bit more of the aioli sauce from the get go, but our server was really friendly and brought more of the kimchi aioli over which was really nice). Also, the habanero salsa I had with my burrito was incredible -- pretty spicy, but also super flavorful. Overall I like the concept of Belly and think their food and service is pretty great.

Belly in San Francisco is a bold, flavor-forward spot that blends comfort food with creative, Asian-inspired twists. The menu is indulgent and unapologetic, focusing on rich textures, layered flavors, and generous portions that feel both satisfying and intentional. From the moment you step inside, the atmosphere feels lively and modern, matching the playful energy of the food itself. Dishes are thoughtfully composed, balancing sweetness, spice, and umami without feeling overwhelming. Service is efficient and friendly, keeping the experience smooth even during busy hours.
