top_reviews.content:
Loved this place! It was packed when I visited, but the food came out much faster than I expected. The staff were warm and welcoming, and the atmosphere felt cozy and inviting.

The portions were generous, and the flavors were authentic and delicious. Every dish we ordered was fantastic. Definitely worth the wait and I’ll be coming back next time I’m in Berkeley.

This dining spot is a must visit. The atmosphere is insanely strikes perfect balance of inviting and intimate. You go in and there’s never a wait, it’s a space where you hold convo without loud acoustics. The service is incredible, you can walk and settle in no wait time.

The food is incredibly authentic and unique, blending Thai dishes with Chinese techniques. Each dish has a balance of bold, complex flavors that reminds me of Thailand. The chive cake pairs perfectly with Thai ice tea, while the crab egg fried rice is rich and creamy that goes perfectly with the pandan desert. The combo of flavors in khao soi  is rich and coconuty, making the dish super filling and satisfying.

I highly recommend planning your next visit to this place in your next Berkeley trip.

If you’re looking for a great Thai restaurant in Berkeley, I highly recommend Praaw Thai.

The restaurant has a very unique old Hong Kong style. The decorations are beautiful, and the atmosphere is cozy and fun.

We loved every dish we ordered, especially the Tum Strawberry, Emily’s Dumplings, Homemade Gui Chai, Tau Huu, Nookie’s Ka-ree Koong, Kao Pad Mun Puu, and Dok Jok. Everything was full of flavor and very tasty.

I forgot to take a picture of Emily’s Dumplings because we ate them right away—they were so good!

The Thai iced coffee was also excellent. It was rich, smooth, and not too sweet, just the way I like it.

Great food, great atmosphere, and friendly service. I will definitely come back and highly recommend this place!

Absolutely loved Praaw Thai in Berkeley! The food was amazing, the atmosphere was cozy, and the owner and staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming.

We’re both from Northern Thailand, so chatting with them honestly felt like being back home ❤️

Highly recommend if you want authentic Thai food and warm hospitality!

the appetizers were amazing, the fried tofu especially. flavors were bold, everyone had solid dishes, especially the khao soi and pad see ew (i’d say the dill fish was just ok, didn’t expect it to be fried). save space till the end with a coconut ice cream dessert with a savory crispy delicate finish.

top_reviews.content: This place has an exceptionally high rating, and after my visit, I agree completely. The food is all prepared to top standard. Our first time at Olchi and our family enjoyed it!  The place is smaller, clean and comfortable.  The service is great - welcoming, friendly and fast!  The food was absolutely delicious!  Everything we ordered we loved - the special Galbi (BBQ ribs), combination Soondubu, Donkatsu, Sweet & Spicy Chicken Bites, Kimbap, and some beers.  Needless to say, we left stuffed and had a nice take away container for another meal!

Visited Olchi in El Sobrante for lunch and had a very solid experience.

The space is noticeably clean and well-kept, which stood out right away. It is a simple, comfortable setting that works well for a casual meal.

The spicy pork is the highlight. It is well-marinated with a balanced heat and strong flavor, and the texture is tender with a slight char. The soups are also excellent, served hot with a rich, savory broth that feels carefully prepared.

Kimbap and appetizers are fresh and well-executed, rounding out the meal without feeling secondary.

Overall, consistent quality across the board. Highly recommend the spicy pork and soups.

Love this place! Great food, service and outdoor seating so we could eat with our furbabies!! We had the seafood pancake and the tofu soup with beef and raw egg - all so delicious and the pickles were great too. The owners were super nice and we will definitely be back!!! Highly recommend!!!
Most delicious and wonderful experience at this place. Dare I say best Korean food in the bay. I’m still so amazed.

top_reviews.content:
Awesome place with a huge portion size of food!

Good:
- Only waited about 5min for a seat on a Sunday night for dinner
- They are generous with the banchan and we had a couple refills
- The galbi jjim for 2 people was way too much and well worth since it powered 2 more meals after - super fresh and so many toppings - the meat is super soft
- The watermelon strawberry drink was huge and great value

Bad:
- Takes a while for the food to come
- The place is pretty small

Overall would come again, super comfort food. Great value and just enjoyed the vibes.

Genuinely excellent and a serious rival to Daeho( without the crazy wait times!). The short ribs are braised to "fall-off-the-bone" perfection and served in massive, bubbling portions. Comes with a standard, generous cheese topping that is torched table-side for that signature smoky, gooey finish.

It’s my first time here today, my mom and I are both very satisfied with our impromptu dinner. We ordered the Galbi Jjim in medium spicy. The portion is very generous, the standard serving already included cheese, rice cake, glass noodles, and plenty of radish-carrots-potatoes! The meat was tender and flavorful, perfectly cooked and served on a cold winter night. We had leftover for another meal. ✌🏼

The food on the very limited menu is tasty, albeit not healthy. I do like that they use Mary’s organic chicken but even that is super fatty. The signature beef dish looked delicious and very decadent but at over $80 and piled high with cheese and toppings, it serves 4 and it’s not my jam. Go if you just want a lot of food generally pretty inexpensive. It’s like $25 a person and tasty, just too unhealthy and casual for me.

We ordered the Spicy Galbi Jjim and had to wait ~20 minutes for it. They offered mild, medium, spicy, very spicy spice levels. It was delicious and had a nice kick of heat. The cheese was included, and they added flat glass noodles to the usual rice cakes, carrots, and potatoes. I would have preferred it to be more saucy, but overall, it was a solid Galbi Jjim minus the wait.

The Soy Glaze wings were nice and crunchy, but I would have liked them better if they were coated with more sauce.

Not to mention, this is the most generous portion of odeng banchan I’ve ever received! Good sour kimchi to balance the Galbi Jjim as well.

address: 1155 Folsom St, San Francisco, CA 94103, United States

top_reviews.content:
Fishbone Charlie lives kitty corner from Akari Japanese Bistro, and picked up an assortment of amazingly delicious foods for the monthly poker game, and what a special treat it was!  The skewers, and sushi stood as tall as John Wayne, as did the fish, which we turned into sandwiches so we could hold them, but there was a rice dish that took the gold medal  ..it was Spectacular!
5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s and they didn't even try!

Excellent Blue Fin Tuna Cutting Experience. Great intimate atmosphere - authentic, Japanese, homey. The cutting itself was quick and precise. I keep thinking about the buffet of excellent sides and entrees that were served alongside the tuna. The buffet included other fish sashimi, nanbanzuke, various cooked salmon and chicken dishes (including yakitori and karaage), tempura, a really delicious beef sukiyaki, and an addictive okra salad. Plenty of seating. Best value in terms of price and food offerings compared to other similar events in the Bay Area.
This was one of the most fun dining experiences we’ve had. We got the omakase kaiseki and sukiyaki meal to share. Each course was phenomenal.

I came here for a private event featuring a live bluefin tuna cutting, and it was my first time experiencing something so incredible. Watching a master sushi chef expertly carve an enormous, fresh tuna was truly mesmerizing—something I had never seen before except videos.

The bluefin was exceptionally fresh and delicious, with different cuts served sashimi-style as well as incorporated into rolls, allowing us to experience the variety of flavors and textures throughout the fish. In addition to the tuna, the restaurant also served other standout dishes, including rich and flavorful sukiyaki beef.

What really elevated the evening was the attentiveness and care of the staff—you could genuinely feel how invested they were in making sure every guest had an unforgettable experience. As a bonus, I even won the raffle and was able to take more tuna home!

An exceptional and truly special experience. I will absolutely be returning to dine here again!

This Japanese restaurant is a true gem in the city. Authenticity is unmatched anywhere else in the US. I’ve had their Makunouchi lunch sets, which are carefully crafted from the best ingredients for a balanced meal. I’ve also tried their sukiyaki with Washu beef, which is already melt in the mouth tender. Flavors are completely on point. You can tell the kitchen staff takes a lot of pride and care in preparation. Sure, it’s not cheap, but this is one of the few Japanese places that I feel is worth the price for authenticity.

Arianna’s meek, bright sweetness makes you feel instantly welcomed, Irene’s kind and soulful energy is unforgettable, and James, the friendly owner, truly creates such a warm vibe. My iced mocha was smooth, flavorful, and perfectly not too sweet—with an awesome variety of milk options too. Wonderful people, amazing atmosphere, and delicious drinks! ☕✨
Enjoyed a delicious melon and prosciutto salad. This is a cute spot to grab lunch with a friend. I can’t wait to go back to try more items on the menu.

I haven't had a salad this good in a very long time. I hope if it's a seasonal salad, they replace it with something just as good, because, Yum. As such, DO NOT expect to be able to park yourself and work on a computer inside here. There are large signs posted everywhere saying "No computers!!" Which I somewhat understand, but I don't see the harm if it's not busy. It seems like people should be able to use responsible freedom on that, but....I digress...

Now that we can bring our dogs again it is convenient to sit on the patio and have a coffee or breakfast. There was one. Where they were not even letting dogs on the patio for no good reason. They reverted  the rule.

The breakfast burritos are surprisingly well stuffed with eggs and cheese and the hot sauce is a good amount of spice. Not too hot not too mild.

They do not have straws. Take your own. If you need it.

Patio is slanted, but it is covered with a tent. There are wooden benches to sit on. They bring you out your food if you are eating there.

What a gem nessled in the hills of Piedmont. Husband and wife pair own the chic coffee and gift store, which also has some nice bistro options - specifically liege waffles. The sound track is a pleasant French style coffee shop.  I am not sure I can say enough good things about this location.  It is a stellar experience.

This taco stand is super conveniently located if you are near North Berkeley! They offer many options including burritos, tacos, and more. The meat selection is wide and delicious. Waiting in line is painful as it is usually cold and the wait is long as people normally order a lot of tacos. The salsas and vegetables are self serve on the side and they also offer agua frescas! The staff was super friendly and I honestly waited less than 3 minutes for my burrito which was huge and super flavorful! Will be back for sure. They had one or two tables on the sidewalk for seating as well.

Delicious! I'd never had mulitas before and they were generously cheesy and tasty. Service was quick and friendly. Being able to speak Spanish is helpful to make customizations (I'm vegetarian). Loved the veggies + beans and pineapple in my mulitas. Don't sleep on the horchata. They're not too sweet and easy to down before you're food arrives! Communal tables with stools available to dine in. Takeout option available too.

Salsa bar is delicious. I love the grilled jalapenos, radishes and pickled veggies too!

Even after leaving a 20% tip, it came out to under $20 per person, which feels like an incredible value for the quality.

The staff was super friendly, and while the space is tiny, we were able to grab a cozy seat at the window which made it even more enjoyable.

The food was fresh and really flavorful. One standout for me was their red salsa—it actually had some heat without that overpowering vinegar taste you sometimes get, which I really appreciated.

Highly recommend checking them out, especially on Taco Tuesday. Definitely a spot I’ll be coming back to again and again.

Got an Al Pastore and a Pollo taco. Both were incredible and definitely made me a fan of this place.

I had a friend visit from Hong Kong and this is where I took him when he asked for authentic tacos

The tacos had too much filling, which is a taco sin, because you couldn't really pick them up to eat. They lacked balance, with the exception of the crispy chicken, which I kind of liked. The limes were cut into tiny pieces in a weird shape so they were basically too small to squeeze.

The pozole was also under seasoned. I wasn't expecting casa de toño, but it was missing flavor. Overall, disappointed.

top_reviews.content:
Awesome spot to spend a beautiful afternoon! Lots of outside seating, great food and drinks, very attentive service. Definitely a great spot for a leisurely brunch!

The OMG sandwich was delicious - the bread was a bit on the dry side but a little dressing (I added) was all it needed. The flavors were incredible.

Heroic Italian in Berkeley is a true find! The lasagna is absolutely delicious—rich, cheesy, and full of flavor. The outdoor seating is super charming, like a little European café tucked away in the city. Friendly service and a cozy atmosphere make it a perfect spot for a relaxed meal. Highly recommend!

$20 is a bit pricey for me for a sandwich, but quality counts for a lot. This place makes some of the best sandwiches in the area. I've had the OMG (a decadent version of an Italian sandwich) and their meatball sandwich. Both were outstanding. The bread is always fresh and everything is perfectly seasoned. It's a splurge for me, but occasionally it's worth it. Friendly and efficient service. Nice outdoor seating area, good drinks selection.

We decided to check out Heroic Italian in downtown Berkeley, next to the library! The outdoor patio was so relaxing on a hot summer day.

If you love Italian food as much as I do, y'all need to check out Heroic Italian! Everything was so fresh and light. It's simply delicioso!

OMG! OMG! The OMG sandwich was light, airy, crispy, and delicious; while the Chicken Tetrazzini Rotini pasta was light, creamy, and tasty, it was perfect with the glass of white wine.

I love me a good salad, and the California Caprese salad did NOT disappoint. Not only was it beautiful, it was so refreshingly delicious! I want one now.

Lastly, the Calabrian Shrimp Roman Pizza was delicious. It was my first time having a shrimp pizza- it had the perfect balance of savory and tartness.

Ps. There’s a parking lot next door, and it cost the same as the street parking meter.

Heroic Italian is located next to the Downtown Berkeley Library on Kittredge Street not far from BART.  There is free 2 hour parking on the street, and there is a parking garage close by.

It is located on the bottom corner of a five story with lots of windows so the restaurant is filled with natural light. There is a large patio outside, so you have the choice of eating inside or out.

David, the owner is friendly and loves to share about his business!!! I had an OMG sandwich to go with an Italian Bio drink. I see why it is called OMG--it was very tasty made with fresh bread, Italian meats, smoked Mozzarella, and Roasted Artichoke Spread. Yum, yum!!!

They have a large variety of Italian wines to choose from to go along with sandwiches, salads, pizzas, and pastas. This is a great place to come for a taste of Italy.

I can only eat here sometimes due to the high cost of tax & extra. The restaurant looks nice.

Ordered a tofu bahn mi and took it to go. When I got home I took a few bites and realized there wasn't any tofu in it just extra carrots. Pretty bad 👎 after spending 12$ plus tax. Don't recommend at all.

Tasty Bowl is a home-style Vietnamese restaurant with a cozy, no-frills vibe. The menu is somewhat limited, but the food and drinks were decent for the price. The restaurant itself feels a bit dated, and while service was generally okay, I did have to flag someone down for a water refill. Overall, it’s an okay spot if you’re looking for a simple Vietnamese meal without high expectations.

We go to Pho King right next door almost weekly, but for whatever reason Pho King was closed today so we decided to give this place a try.

I knew this wasn’t going to be as good because there were always more people at Pho King, but man it was absolutely terrible.

I ordered my usual pho with sliced steak, you know, the most vanilla pho there is next to chicken pho and I’ve never had it this bad. The beef that comes with the pho looks like scrap meat, and there was only a few pieces of it. I really tried to eat the pho, but I just couldn’t, the meat was tough and the soup tasted like it was made from powder.

Never again.

Excellent Eritrean food with a top-injera and a wide variety of delicious vegetarian dishes!

It was my father’s 70th birthday, and it was our first time dining at Lula’s Eritrean Restaurant.

From the moment we walked in, we were captivated by the restaurant’s vibrant colors, elegant décor, and the warm golden glow that filled the space. The air carried the inviting scent of fragrant spices and freshly prepared dishes, creating an immediate sense of comfort and anticipation. Soft conversations and the gentle hum of activity blended seamlessly with the welcoming ambiance, making the atmosphere feel both festive and intimate—the perfect setting to celebrate such a special milestone. The service was exceptional from start to finish—we barely had time to settle into our seats before attentive staff greeted us with genuine smiles and made us feel like honored guests throughout the evening.

As someone who doesn’t regularly eat traditional Eritrean food, other than my mother’s, I wasn’t sure what to expect, but this turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve ever had. The aromas alone were incredible, with notes of warm berbere spices, savory stews, and freshly baked injera filling the table with anticipation as each dish arrived. Every bite revealed layers of flavor—rich, vibrant, and perfectly balanced without feeling overly heavy. Tangy, spongy injera soaked up deeply seasoned sauces, while the blend of spices delivered a satisfying warmth that lingered pleasantly on the palate. The textures and seasonings complemented one another beautifully, from tender, slow-cooked dishes to fresh accompaniments that added brightness and contrast. The presentation was stunning, with colorful platters arranged artfully, transforming the meal into a feast for both the eyes and the palate.

What made the evening even more special was sharing these new flavors with my family while celebrating my father’s milestone birthday. There was a genuine sense of joy and togetherness that made the experience unforgettable. Surrounded by the restaurant’s warm hospitality and the lingering aroma of spices, we found ourselves savoring not only the food but also the moment itself. Everything exceeded our expectations, from the food and service to the welcoming atmosphere. We left feeling grateful, satisfied, and excited to return to explore more of the menu. I highly recommend this restaurant and can’t say enough wonderful things about it and the owner.

top_reviews.content:

CORRECTION: somebody lied to me about the beans, which are in fact vegetarian. i will be tracking this person down to deliver severe social consequences for robbing me of my joy. thank you to chile bravo for clarifying. i will leave up my original review for transparency.

—

at some point, someone told me all their beans are cooked in lard, so i can't order any of the burritos anymore, because i don't eat pork. not to be hyperbolic, but this lowkey ruined my life. for years i had been deliberately electing not to ask because i didn't want to know that. it was a sad day. it's been a couple more years and i'm almost over it now, though; the tacos and quesadillas are still transcendental. this is the real deal; it's exactly what you want out of a taco truck: a slightly-too-long wait, workers who get stuff a little wrong sometimes because they can't quite hear you from up in a small enclosed space full of kitchen noise, likely a level of compliance with health code that is questionable at best, and at the end of the day? street food at the absolute zenith of the medium's potential. both salsas are a powerfully smooth blend of flavors, and both the grilled veggies and the meats themselves have the perfect degree of char & texture. people say if you want a real burrito, go to los angeles, and if you want a real taco, go to tijuana. i'm sure they're right, but this has to be close enough. you can get this one day & an equally out-of-this-world representation of some other cuisine the next without going very far, and that's what is so special about the bay. chile bravo does a commendable job of showing off why oakland is magical, and i think that makes it certifiably iconic. by the way, i'm sure they cook everything on the same grill, and there's probably nothing the lard doesn't touch. i can't emphasize enough how much i DON'T! WANT! to KNOW!

I was intrigued by the traditional name of this South Indian place and decided to check it out during my first visit to Berkeley. Although the curd rice seems to be the star of the place (and much reviewed), I went for the idli vada combo with a filter coffee. Also, out of eye hunger, I ordered Maggi.

The portions were quite small for a full meal, so it’s better suited for a quick snack. The idli batter tasted a bit sour, possibly over-fermented, and the filter coffee didn’t quite live up to expectations. That said, the place itself has a cozy and casual vibe.

We ordered their signature dish, the ThayirSadam, along with curry puffs, masala bites, and filtered coffee.

Everything tasted fresh and was excellent

The coffee was foaming up top and rich.

Great place but really wish they served dosas

I would come here every week if they had dosas

Lovely, fresh, cheerful, simple, spotlessly clean, inexpensive South Indian spot on Telegraph. I tried the Idli Vada Combo with sambar and coconut chutney, and a cup of chai. The sambar was nice and everything was so fresh!  The vada was extra light and crunchy. I'll be back for the thayirsadam when I'm a bit hungrier! Check it out!

The star of the menu is their yogurt (curd) rice—simple, comforting, and incredibly satisfying. What makes it unique is the ability to customize your bowl with a wide variety of toppings, from spicy peanuts and chickpeas to paneer, fruits, nuts, and pickles, so every visit can be a little different.

The concept is refreshingly humble: take a beloved South Indian home-style dish and elevate it with fresh ingredients and thoughtful combinations.

top_reviews.content:
If you’re looking for a true Berkeley classic, La Val’s Pizza absolutely delivers. This place has been serving the community since the 1950s, and you can really feel that history and character the moment you walk in. It’s a family owned pizza shop .The pizza itself is what keeps people coming back. The crust has a unique texture—slightly crisp on the outside with a hearty bite—and the toppings are generous without being overwhelming. Their specialty pizzas, especially the butter chicken and vegetarian piazza .

La Val’s isn’t about being the most modern pizza place—it’s about consistency, tradition, and comfort food done right. If you’re in Berkeley, it’s definitely worth experiencing at least once.

Highly recommended this place ✌️✌️✌️

New ownership, same amazing chicken tikka pizza!! Came by around lunch and was warmly greeted by the husband and wife who had just taken over the restaurant from a family member. They love the area, send their kids to school close by, and look forward to making the pizzas for all their neighbors :) Come by, have a chai, a curry pie, and support family run businesses!!!

Pizza is delicious!! and the customer service is amazing, such sweet people. They’re happy to accommodate any customization which is awesome. we’ve tried the desi vegetarian pizza and the paneer tikka both were amazing!! super vegetarian friendly and rlly good prices. highly recommend

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

One of the best pizzas I’ve had in Albany. We tried the Chicken Tikka pizza and the BBQ Chicken special and both were incredible. Everything tasted very fresh and you can really tell the ingredients are high quality. The crust, sauce, and toppings were all on point.

Roop and his wife provided amazing customer service and made us feel very welcome. If you're looking for great pizza in Albany, LaVal’s is definitely worth checking

We stumbled on this great family owned pizza shop after a comedy show when everything else was closing. They stay open until 10 PM! The owners are super friendly and mentioned they are doing lunch hours now too.
The pizza was incredibly fresh and delicious. They also make Indian inspired pies. We got a traditional pizza this time, but I will definitely be back for the chicken tikka next time. Highly recommend! 5 stars!

google.name: Tacos Sinaloa

top_reviews.content: This taco truck caught my eye on the street and I had to stop by. Im so glad I did because the fish burrito was so fresh and delicious 😋.  They serve the burritos with whole beans and other amenities. Great spot. Will be back
Would not let us order over the phone for pick up - had to order via Doordash, which charged us a service fee and was more expensive than in person. Burrito was also fairly dry.

Great experience came out at a lunchtime, rush, reasonable prices. They accept cash, Venmo, or Zelle. I was pleasantly surprised they hooked it up with a bunch of pickles. And salsas. Will be a regular.

Tacos Sinaloa's latest taco truck is located in Berkeley on the corner of of Sacramento Street near the Spiral Garden Nursery. (Great native plant selection) HEADS UP!  This taco truck is CASH ONLY at the moment.

The carne asada tacos were delicious for me!  My husband didn't like the dryness of the double stack tortillas and the over abundance of onions and cilantro but I was loving it!  We got two large horchatas, which were so creamy and refreshing. This taco truck is unique from nearby trucks because it offers ceviche tostadas.  I love the shrimp ceviche mixed with cucumber, salt, and Tapatio, all on top of a crunchy corn tortilla.  The to-go order comes packaged to travel well- with the ceviche in a plastic container with lid and the crispy corn tortilla in foil separately so it doesn't get soggy.  It comes with salt packet and the hot sauce on the side. It was filling but I still needed to taste the tacos too. To die for!  There is a sappy tree above the truck that will stick your shoes on to the pavement. That part is a bit yucky and I wish it felt a little bit more cozy.  But who doesn't LOVE tacos? I could eat them all day long honestly.  The price was $38 for 10 carne asada tacos, 2 horchatas, and 1 shrimp ceviche tostada. TOTALLY WORTH EVERY CENT!  I love Tacos Sinaloa and would recommend it to my hungry friends located in Berkeley for sure.

Cash only but you can order online? Also, prices went WAY WAY up. Food good, but NOT worth those prices.
A super burrito is and extra large burrito, not a burrito with extra filling.

Very fresh and delicious! Loved the original chicken burger 🍔 and very tasty fries 🍟 at a very good price!
Super nice people, very clean kitchen, nice and freshly renovated interior. They have both indoor and outdoor sitting areas.
Definitely a go to place. Highly recommended.

Slurp!!Yum!!  Love the pizza from here!  The crust tastes like it was lightly dusted with cornmeal.  I ordered the combo special and it was really good.  It wasn't oily and the ingredients were very fresh.  The place is very new and clean.  Extra bonus is that it is opened til 2am.  So if u want pizza late at night, this will be my new "go to" place.

Came here two nights in a row! They have so many items I wanted to try. First I tried the cheese steak. I can definitely say it’s better than the cheese steak shop! I work close by this place and I notice they start having lunch special that changes every day and I can't help trying their new special today called sopes  it comes 3 or 4 Vegi circled looks like home made it tasted  immersing Vegi  bean source cream  more bit spicy but I loved it I can't wait to see what they have tomorrow for  lunch special

top_reviews.content: Checked this place out on my lunch break today. I had no idea this place existed, and I love Banh Mi. Requested a BBQ Pork sandwich, which the team member let me know they do not offer, but they have a grilled pork option. The grilled pork is marinated and was very tasty, and similar to BBQ pork almost. The pickled veggies were extremely fresh and tasty. The bread was toasted and crisp, the sandwich is quite long and wide, but not overly stuffed. The end bites were just bread, but not a big problem. There is a lot of competition in this area for this cuisine, and this one is just ok. They have a great location but need some music or something to make it seem more lively. This is a good alternative to Binge if you are really hungry for Banh Mi! The staff was very friendly.

Got a bánh mì chả lụa (they call it a district 3 ? lol) and it was good! Normal and what you expect from a banh mi shop. What’s interesting about this place is their very lavish colorful names based off of areas of Saigon and other places in Vietnam for what would otherwise be pretty normal banh mis so it was a bit funny as a Vietnamese person but yeah. I also got the coffee which was quite good. Prices though… I mean it is Berkeley what can I say.

Stopped in here before a concert with my partner and was excited to have bahn mi. This was one of the best bahn mi’s I’ve ever had, delicious, fresh, and the bread was perfect. A plus was the lychee iced tea and lemonade made in house, and their new offer of fresh spring rolls. 10/10 will be coming again!

From traditional Banh Mi to a California (bacon & avocado!), this great little shop on Telegraph is full of delicious food, great people watching, and friendly staff. Today I tried the Vietnamese coffee and noticed the subtext on the menu, "Sweet and strong, just like the Vietnamese lady who brews it!" <3
The tofu pagoda and basil seed drink are my go to order. The owner is kind. I do wish there was a bathroom or water station for guests.

reviews_snippets.content: "The drinks were also great-vietnamese coffee and lychee iced tea."

top_reviews.content:
Great first experience.

For the location & price, cant beat that. Close to UCB. Close to Telegraph Ave , amazing for everyone.

We ordered 3 Cheeseburgers burgers, 1 jalapeño burger, and one regular hamburger, two side fries.  Really good deal. Next time, we'll try the shake!

Definitely, a great place for the price. Will be back!

Solid burgers for really affordable prices with a mildly unnerving interior. I got a cheeseburger and fries for $7.70, the most economical option near campus. The cheeseburger had two thin patties and grilled onions, which were a nice touch. The fries tasted great, but I got a lot of bits less than an inch long. Food was out in 3 minutes - amazing.

This place is great, I was really impressed.  No frills cheap burgs that taste great and the lady at counter was really nice.  Parking is bad but that's obvious given the area and the music was like blasting which was slightly annoying.  Small, open air style seating, it's not a large interior so you may or may not have spot to sit depending on time.  For the price it's great and super tasty.  Their house sauce is really good, very different to in n out, I wouldn't say it's better but it's good

You get what you pay for, still good though. The only thing that I don’t like about their food is the house sauce, it tastes a lot like mayo, you can’t really taste the other ingredients they added for it to look orange/pink.
This place deserves more appreciation, absolutely fantastic burgers, the sauce is amazing! I haven’t had the fries but the burgers are great especially for the price

name: The Walnut Tavern Bar & Grill
address: 1508 Walnut St, Berkeley, CA 94709, United States

google.name: The Walnut Tavern Bar & Grill
google.address: 1508 Walnut St, Berkeley, CA 94709, United States

top_reviews.content:
Stopped in to be out of the rainy weather for some cocktails 'n dessert and we were not disappointed!

The Grizzly Peak cocktail was sweet - (green apple 'sweet')- was delicious! Enzo's Elegance cocktail (a minty  cucumber melon craft special) goes down smooth and tastes great!

The chocolate lava cake with vanilla ice cream was wonderfully chocolatey warm yet cold ice cream in the same bite. Strawberry & blueberry was an excellent accompaniment.

Absolutely would return for the dinner/lunch menu without hesitation! When we arrived (after lunch but before dinner time) was a perfect stop in point. Not too busy; just enough of a slow pace to enjoy the atmosphere, drinks, and sweet treat. Seeing the doggies go into and out of the shop next door was a cute sight as well!

Thanks to everyone for making it a delightful stop in.  12/20/25!

Poor food quality, poor service.

Food: My party ordered 5 entrees (grilled vegetable panini, fish and chips, short rib burger,  quinoa salad, and fish tacos) and one appetizer (baby back BBQ pork ribs). The grilled vegetable panini was very salty such that it was difficult to eat. The fish and chips were likely double fried such that the batter was almost inedible because it was hard and burned. The temperature of the pork rib appetizer was luke warm, and the meat was tough, like a leftover heated up in a microwave. The fish tacos were fair but not particularly good. The short rib burger was done well, and the quinoa salad was fresh tasty.

Service: Our server was was very insistent on selling us more items even when it was clear we knew what we wanted. He kept pushing us, which was uncomfortable. One of our water glasses was dirty and we asked for a new one, and the server did not hide his annoyance. Then he brought a new glass with warm tap water, sending a clear message.

Atmosphere: the dining room was pleasant and clean. We wanted to watch the a World Cup game and it was available on a TV in the dining room.

The menu is not too extensive. I appreciated the outdoor seating, reasonably priced cider and the mellow music. To be honest, the service was slow, the burger was dry and there were raisins in the coleslaw. I would return to take advantage of the street parking and outdoor dining.  (I ordered a Nepalese appetizer, fish and chips [nuggets?] and a kids meal.)

Best patio in Berkeley!  The service is always friendly and nice.  The food is prepared fresh and always so good.  Best momos in town!   My husband and I will come for wine, apps and sun.  Their brunch is really good too.   Dog friendly too

Walnut Square is a cool little shopping and eating inlet in Berkeley’s gourmet ghetto. At the west edge of the square you’ll find Walnut Tavern.

Dined here for brunch and enjoyed it quite a bit. They have a nice menu combination of breakfast and lunch items. I chose both! The steak sandwich and a waffle. I know, gluttony.

The steak sando was on ciabatta bread and cooked perfectly. I asked for medium and that’s how it came. Steak fries usually not my thing but these were crispy and seasoned enough.

The waffle loses points because it was soft and had no crispness at all. And the syrup was the fake maple. They improve that and it’s a winner.

The last dish was the Mom’s eggs Benedict which comes with ham. Hash browns were thin and crispy… perfect.

And the atmosphere of this little tavern is great. Natural light. Woody. And a bar. Makes me want to come here to watch a Cal game.

Service was a little spotty. Nice enough but kind of slow and didn’t quite get my order right.

top_reviews.content: Great Chinese food with authentic taste. They have a hotel next door which is connected to the restaurant and they are open till midnight. If you want great Chinese kebab, noodles, rice dishes, seafood, and dumplings. This is the place to be! Food is cooked fast and they accept card and cash. Will be coming back for the authentic and delicious Chinese spot next to Berkeley!

Some unique specialties you can’t get anywhere else. The owners are from Wuhan so the Wuhannese hot dry noodles are legit and the bbq skewers are perfect with generous dusting of cumin and spicy powder.

In a nutshell; great chinese food in the day, even greater at midnight.

Stopped by here to get some good food and something to warm the eve. As the nights were cool and breezy after a days activities. Parking can be a pain as you can only get lucky with street parking and can be tough when there's an event nearby or the aftermath of one. Nonetheless, place served great food even when you're the only customers during the late nights. Overall would stop by again if ever in Berkeley.

The lamb skewers were very on point. I also really liked the chicken gizzards, the tofu and the mushrooms. The lotus root was better in ma la tang. Ma la tang definitely had the ma flavor to it though they seemed skeptical when I asked for extra ma la. The staff was very attentive. Overall very happy with the late night food 🥰

I saw the hands of the owner’s as she brought food to my table, and those are the hands of hardworking people’s. I really appreciate their delicious food, and friendly service, and the value that they hold in the family and their business.
Probably this is also the only restaurant that opens until midnight in the area. It was almost midnight after I finished my meal, and I saw the owner still working hard to prepare fresh ingredients for tomorrow’s business.

INCREDIBLE sushi, wow. The service was so fast and attentive, and sushi was phenomenal, inventive and so buttery. Also the chef was so friendly and knowledgeable! It was actually his 75th birthday the following day, and he let us know this was his 40th year creating sushi. He is a legend!

A must visit if you’re visiting the bay.

For photo reference: we got the Seared Bliss, the Salmon/Avocado, and the Toro and Sake nigiris. SO good.

A delicious,satisfying and lovely dinning experience. If you’re interested in Mongolian Queens and culture you are in for a treat. Food came quickly, was prepared carefully and thoughtfully. They use all real crab meat, and make rolls by hand. Friendly staff greeted us and made sure we had a pleasant experience. The owner is great! Very kind, she treated us to a small dessert on the house(lychee crème brulee, deliciously interesting)! We enjoyed all of our food. Must try the Khatan roll! Also very much savored our Matcha Tres Leches cake!

We’ve been to Khatan probably six times now, and it seems to get better and better each time. We finally had the omakase, and all of the fish was very fresh and delicious.

We also love the shrimp and vegetable tempura. It usually comes with a piece of jalapeño, which makes it feel special.

And we always love the service and atmosphere. Tonight, every other track was Sade, which was lovely. Everything about the whole experience is very thoughtful.

Absolutely amazing experience! Stumbled upon this place on new years and we were kindly squeezed in by the staff. The waitress that tended to us was fantastic, the ambiance was great and most importantly; the sushi to die for!

Both rolls we ordered (rhe Atlas and Bacon of the Sea) were extremely fresh & had unique twists that made them a genuinely new / great experience! They even served our order of green tea in a cute fish pot, so fun! The music was also nice. 100% will return with a reservation next time for sure!

Wow!
I just went for date night with my daughter (back from college) and had the best sushi in the Bay Area!!!

The Omakase was superb!!! The highlight was hamachi with truffle and the unagi was the best I’ve ever tasted.

We also had the lion king (because which was “just right”!

Our server was terrific - she recommended the chef special, Ika Sugata (Grilled whole Squid with Jalapeño & Mango 🤩)

We also got the delicious Garlic Edamame and took an order of Matcha Tres Leche to go.

It wasn’t “cheap” but it was soooo worth it!!!

We will be back!

The khao man gai here is very yummy. Less than $20 with big food portions. I feel like I'm in Thailand again when I have each bite. Very good

The portion size was bigger than I thought ans overall wait time wasn't that long!

Near hotel we were staying at. I’ve eaten a lot of Hainan chicken growing up and I’ve missed it so much had to go in a get it. It did not disappoint! My daughter got the fried chicken and loved it. I ordered through DoorDash and was willing to pay a premium because this burger was significantly more expensive than the competition, and I expected the quality to justify the price. Unfortunately, it did not.

Both the burger and fries arrived cold. The delivery itself took only about five minutes, so the food clearly wasn’t cold because of transit time. In fact, the jalapeños were still warm, which made it obvious that the burger and fries had likely been sitting cold before they were handed off for delivery.

The quality was disappointing as well. I even found small bone fragments in the burger meat, which is not something I would expect from a restaurant charging premium prices.

Overall, the food was overpriced, arrived cold, and failed to meet expectations. Based on this experience, I would not recommend this restaurant.
This place is highly recommended. The food is fresh. It’s Halal. Customer Service is amazing. I must visit if you are in a safe come get a fat burger with some fat tenders and ignite your appetite.

I was  greeted quite nicely by a gentleman who proceeded to take my order( the bacon avocado burger combo)  I waited for about 10 min in a impeccably clean dining area in no time my order arrived  personally !! To my surprise I was sitting in front of a heaping of FRESH French fries real potatoes  I was shocked the burger was juicy and full of flavor  and fries were just out of this world I'm definitely going to recommend to all and for the reasonably fair price of a little under $20 I am pleasantly surprised good job guys for everything DO TRY!!!

name: Dolly's

top_reviews.content:
My husband and I were recently recommended to try Dolly’s restaurant and we’re so glad we did. From the moment we walked in, the whole experience felt relaxed and welcoming. The hosts and owners were incredibly warm and friendly.

The food was delicious. We loved the cheese wheel pasta, the bread and tomato salad, and they also had a really good wine selection. As a small business owner myself, I always appreciate supporting local family-owned spots that truly care about good food and good service. Dolly’s is definitely one of those places. We’ll absolutely be back.

We came here because of the 4.8 star rating and I’m still trying to figure out how that happened. We spent nearly $100 for fast-food quality (or worse) pasta and slow service. I ordered the Alfredo in the Parmesan wheel with smoked salmon. The sauce was incredibly watery and seemed like it was just jarred sauce boiling in a vat. It didn’t even seem like the place had a stove. The pasta was precooked and warmed up before being mixed with the watery sauce and tossed in the cheese wheel. Then they put a whole package of smoked salmon on top, not cut up or mixed in or anything. The only upside was that the servers were very nice! They kept offering us free wine. I’m not sure if they knew it was an off night or if that is the norm there. Based on the kitchen they seem to have I’m not sure how it could be much better.

What do you get when you take a young Sri Lankan chef, (Dolly) who studied under a master of Italian cuisine, (Ruggero Milano, of Milano ristorante in Tiburon), an obsession with fresh pastas, imported desserts and gelatos and add one of the best wine lists in the East Bay and a giant authentic Permesano Regiano cheese wheel?

You get my new favorite Italian place in the Bay Area.
In an out of the way location, one block from the Rialto theaters in El cerrito, this area is mostly known for its Asian cuisine which I have covered extensively, but lo and behold! An authentic Italian ristorante, with a real trained Italian chef, and a casual laid-back setting and unassuming vibe.

Following my patented strategy of emulating success, I asked the guy next to me, (Who turned out to be a baseball scout, and looked super happy with what he was eating) what to order, and he recommended the Smoked salmon Fettuccine Alfredo.
I ordered it and I watched the careful preparation of perfect pasta ending with a generous toss in a Parmesan cheese wheel, and a glass of Daou Cabernet.
Dolly really knows what she's doing, and has set a new standard for my fettuccine enjoyment, and while the dish was so rich I felt guilty eating it alone, she still gave me a spoonful of REAL Italian spumoni, flown in recently.
This place is a kind of restaurant we need more of in the East Bay. Unassuming, friendly, homey, first class Italian food for the people. I cannot recommend this place highly enough if you want to have an actual Italian food experience but need to stick close to the east bay.
And by real Italian I don't mean some shishi spot that's going to charge you $100 to bring out three olives and a single slice of veal, I'm talking about real, hearty, delicious Italian food for the people.
Thanks Dolly.
Strategy: go see a movie at the Rialto, one block away, and arrange to have some Italian food afterwards. You'll be glad you did

top_reviews.content:
When:
Friday evening, 5:45pm, restaurant was pretty empty except some occasional food takeouts. By 6:30, more people coming in to eat in. But it was not full throughout the time we were at the restaurants.

Experience:
Food came out pretty fast and it was hot(!). Overall, service was good and they checked in on us a few times to make sure all is good.

Food:
- Nam Khao was fantastic. Crispy rice, the mixed minced vegetables, and the cooked sausage. Together with the lime that you can squeeze to preference, it was delicious! Haven't had Nam Khao this delicious in a while!
- Pad See Ew with pork was alright. It was cooked well and a little on the sweeter side rather than savory, but missing the smoky flavor "wok hei" that would take this to the next level that I love.
- Fried Sweet Fish was alright too. Fish is fried with a very thin batter but it had black pepper which my kids doesn't want as they're sensitive to anything spicy. The fish had a light fishy taste to it (fresh water fish) which would be better if they even use a little ginger to cut the fishy taste for a better taste.
- Guay Tiew is very similar to Pad See Ew with the exception that it had a fried egg on the top and had seafood (shrimp and squid).
- Vientiane Crispy Roll is different from regular egg rolls. Made with rice paper roll so it was crispy but also chewy, which is different and may not be what everyone is used to.

Will return to try out other dishes.

A Hidden Gem!

I was initially hesitant to come here because, at the time of writing, this place had fewer than 100 reviews. But I’m so glad I gave it a chance!

This place is genuinely good and definitely worth revisiting. My only criticism is that the chicken in the tom yum soup was a little dry, which honestly isn’t shocking. A lot of places dry out their chicken, and getting it right is hard!

But the Thai papaya salad and beef Laab Seen were excellent. Bright, spicy, flavorful, and absolutely worth ordering. This place deserves more attention!

Rose Garden Uptown is a Laotian & Thai restaurant, featuring many dishes common to that region but also Californian ingredients. They offer table service, but the most business was to-go orders while we dined.

From that interior, you can view their mix of modern-day Instagram aesthetics and architecture with more traditional decorated woven trays on the walls and pictures of the menu items that’s nostalgic of many older Asian restaurants: an appealing combination of new and old to me, just like the menu and ingredients. And the pretty sharing plates also brightened my mood.

We started with the Laotian spring rolls, filled with avocado, carrots, rice noodles, and lettuce. The two sauces—one peanut and one mildly sweet and spicy—provided the most flavor for the dish.

Next came the sweet corn salad with carrots, tomatoes, peanuts, green beans, garlic, lime juice, and a mild chili. I love corn, so I expected to love this dish … and I did! Typically, I go for “hot” when asked for a spice level choice, but my friend was right to go with mild here. That added just enough of a kick to complement the corn’s sweetness. The ingredients had a satisfying variety of flavors, textures, and crunch.

We aimed for Rose Garden Uptown’s Laotian specialties for our second dish, settling on the mok pa. That’s catfish steamed in a banana leaf with herbs. It was my first mok pa, and I did not know if I was supposed to treat the lettuce as lettuce wraps, so I went ahead and did so. I scooped catfish into the small leaves, added cilantro and onions, and really enjoyed those flavors and textures all together. The catfish was soft and soothing, and the herbs cooked with it imparted a wonderful freshness. I will definitely order mok pa again.

Would love to try one of their four types of laab another time!

This place is pretty unassuming from the outside, but don’t let that fool you, the food is excellent and full of flavor. The fresh rolls came with both a sweet and sour sauce and a peanut sauce with crushed peanuts, and both were really good.

The Thai fried rice was delicious too, but my favorite was definitely the sweet chicken. It had just the right amount of sweetness without being overpowering, and the flavor was amazing. It’s nothing like the sweet chicken from Panda Express or PF Chang’s, where it’s mostly just sweet.

The service was friendly and attentive, and the whole experience was great. I’d definitely come back and recommend giving this place a try!

We discovered this place two or three weeks ago, and have now ordered from them 4 times. We LOVE the depth and complexity in the flavors, while also being very balanced.

I've had the Kao Poon, Massaman Curry (my current obession), Green Curry, Pad Thai, and Pad Kee Mao, and all have been winners. This has quickly become my favorite Thai place in Oakland, even beating out Pintoh and Attraros.

A Must-Visit East Bay Gem for Spectacular Vietnamese Comfort Food!
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
If you are looking for perfectly executed, deeply flavorful Vietnamese classics, Monsoon in Piedmont is an absolute must-visit. The ambiance is welcoming, but it’s the kitchen’s mastery over crunch, seasoning, and texture that will make you a regular.
On my latest visit, a few standout dishes completely stole the show:
The Standouts
• The Egg Rolls: Hands down some of the best around. They arrive piping hot, shattering into a crisp, flaky crunch with every bite. The filling is perfectly seasoned, savory, and dense without being greasy. Wrap them in fresh lettuce with a dip of nước chấm, and it’s pure perfection.
• The Fried Chicken Wings: Absolute perfection. They hit that elusive sweet spot—shatteringly crisp on the outside while remaining incredibly juicy and tender on the inside. The garlic and savory glaze coats them beautifully without making them soggy. They are addictive.
• The Pork Chop: This is the ultimate test of a great Vietnamese spot, and Monsoon nails it. The pork chop is beautifully marinated with distinct notes of lemongrass and garlic, boasting a gorgeous char from the grill. It’s incredibly tender, packed with smoky flavor, and avoids the dryness you find at lesser spots. Pair it with broken rice, and you have a flawless meal.

Monsoon delivers massive flavor, excellent execution, and fantastic consistency. Whether you're dropping in for a casual weeknight dinner or grabbing takeout, the quality is always top-tier.
Do not skip the wings as an appetizer, and make sure someone at your table orders the pork chop. I’ll definitely be back to work my way through the rest of the menu!

Ying Kee is a true local gem. They’ve been around for over 20 years in the heart of Chinatown, serving good-value, authentic Chinese dishes made with fresh ingredients. While they offer all the classic favorites, they also cook the comforting country-style dishes our parents grew up loving — from salty fish entrées to lamb in Sichuan chili oil, bitter melon spare ribs with gravy over noodles, crispy fried fish, and so much more.

Come here for that warm, family-style feel and enjoy delicious Chinese food paired with friendly service.

**They are known for their shrimp dumplings AKA
(Water dumplings) with the fish skin inside! It’s The Best in Chinatown!

They recently renovated, so the space looks great too.

Fast service and great food. Dried scallops egg white fried rice was awesome, it looked plain but it’s very flavorful. We were so hungry when we arrived without further ado we ordered the fried rice and it’s served in less than 10 mins.

Was excited to try their Curry Beef Brisket, but it was really not enjoyable. The onions and peppers were barely cooked so they still had that raw taste/crunch and the “brisket” was mostly fat/cartilage (as pictured) with about three small chunks of meat in the whole meal. The container also leaked all over since for whatever reason they didn’t think to use one that seals fully.

For a $50+ check, I’m pretty upset that I was served curry with raw vegetables and the scraps you’d trim off a brisket rather than the brisket itself. First and last visit here.

Will definitely come back again when in Oakland. The menu does not look expensive and the food I ordered is pretty tasty. I ordered the Wonton Soup without noodles and also a Chiu Chou Noodles. Friendly staff and credit cards accepted.

My biggest expectation is that food is prepared to expectation and taste. This tuna poke bowl was poorly seasoned and overwhelmed by onion fillers.

I suggest someone with a good pallet go back to the drawing board with the tuna poke bowl and please, for the love of customers, don’t leave out the actual poke marinade.

One of my favorite places in Oakland to grab some dim sum to go.  It's usually a busy place, but the lines move nicely.  There's 2 lines in there so make sure to line up in the right area.  One line is to buy the roasted meats hanging in the front window of the store and the other line is for dim sum.  There's one long table with a few chairs along the wall if you would like to rest a bit and chow down on what you just purchased.

We always try to order the siu mai,chicken feet,tofu skin roll,baked char siu bao,and a few of the fried dumplings when we go.  All of those are so flavorful and tasty.  You don't need any sauces to go with any of those since they themselves are so delicious already,they're not too salty nor too oily or fatty.  The baked char siu baos are a thing of beauty here.  If you don't grab any dim sum then please grab yourselves the baos. The filling is plenty and the ratio of bun to meat is pretty good if you compare it to other places.

I don't really care for the roasted meats myself(the roasted duck,soy sauce chicken,roast pork,etc) because I find them not as good as the other places. I don't necessarily like their seasoning and flavor.  Stick with their dim sum and you should be good but of course this is just my opinion and maybe you would like their roasted offerings.

The workers there are always helpful and friendly.   There's usually 2 or 3 people to serve each line.

this mooncake changes my life, it's just the best I have ever tried, also highly recommended to try the Sesame balls

The shrimp dumpling, bbq pastry puff, taro puff and the shrimp crepe roll are pretty good.  The other stuff has too thick of a dough around them. So they were ok.
Roast Duck is too fatty. Charlie is over grilled. Dim sums okay in a pinch. If u can walk across to FS Center, U'll do better there at either of the two.

My sister-in-law recommended Big Dish to me. It is located in the heartvof Oakland Chinatown, across the street from the East West Bank.

Food is mainly for take out. There are a few tables and chairs for dining indoors.

Purpose of visit: to buy the chicken cage pastries (gai loong). They do sell out fast because it is a very popular item among us elderly Chinese people. The cost for 6 of them is $6.60. I have also purchased 3 sesame balls and 3 savory dumplings.

I’ve also tried their Shrimp Egg Rice Plate, and it’s was really good as well! Their food tasted healthy and fresh, no heavy cream nor sauce that most restaurants have.

If you’re a vegetarian, pescatarian, or just live eat healthy, this is a definitely a great place for you (a log of veggies dishes, including their spring rolls and banh mi) ! And their meat dishes are amazing as well!

Went on a Sunday,  while the flea market was going. Lots of people.  Food was promptly delivered and the lemonade was great. Got home to enjoy my food, and my burger was relaxing comfortable in a oily pit at the bottom of the food container.  Disappointed,  but the burger was decent.

I have yet to try an actual burger from Fast Time Burgers, but just based on their Gnarly Fries alone I can tell you that I will absolutely be back to try everything!

For only $7, you get a pile of French fries covered in what I assume is their Smash Sauce (similar to thousand island but with slightly more acidity), grilled/caramelized onions, and grated aged white cheddar.

First of all, it’s great value plus it smells heavenly! When I took my first bite, I was hit with savory/salty cheese, some sweetness from the onions, and a nice creamy & acidic sauce. Everything brought the classic french fry together. Of course I used a teeny bit of ketchup to dip a few bites and it just made it even better. Next time I’m going to sprinkle some black pepper on it too!

You definitely have to be paying attention to when your order is ready. It didn’t seem like they were calling out names or numbers, but I think in general they send a text when your food is ready.

I got the single Oklahoma burger and the gnarly fries. I'd come back to try the double patty burger. Very nice environment/atmosphere.
Smash burger: 8/10. One of the best smash burgers I had in the US.
- My pros: Bun was cushiony soft with a good bite to it. Sauce mixed well without being too overpowering. Patty seasoned decently.
- My cons: Beef patty didn't taste that beefy. The flavor was a bit mild/lacking for me (maybe the double patty will be better).

Gnarly fries: 7.5/10
Nothing crazy. A fancier In N Out animal fries. Solid flavor and good crunch.
Little overpriced for what it is, but probably a good price point for their intended clientele.

The shake was the best part.. the burger was incredibly greasy and the main flavor was American cheese.. not much meat (on the double burger) lettuce or tomato.. I do appreciate that they use starter bakery buns and Strauss ice cream, but the flavors of the food just weren't there. The fries were lackluster and not very hot or salted enough, the onion rings were good but a little weird with the cornmeal batter. At least there weren't bits of uncooked batter like most places.

The prices are on the high side and the portions are small. $55 for 2 small meals is a lot even with today's beef prices. I wasn't hungry because of the insane amount of grease on the burger, but I'll stick with my local place.

It's in a food court, there's outdoor seating and indoor. Inside was pretty windy in most spots.

Edit July 2026 - finally went in to try their lunch buffet

Selection is limited, and I felt some of the dishes were just fillers

The saag paneer could definitely use some more paneer. The chicken tikka masala was good but was a little watery. Could be thicker.

Garlic naan was one of the best I’ve had in some time. Memorable.

Dishes are still a touch salty.

No desert, and tea is not included in the buffet. No sugar free sweeteners with the tea.

Tandoor chicken was cooked well but tad underpriced

No bowls with the plates. Which is not the best experience when you have multiple curries at the same time.

For $20 a person it’ll do in an otherwise expensive and competitive area.

I think I’ll stick with take out or dine in à la carte.

Just went to Peace for the first time, right as they were closing for the evening. No worry, the owner was super nice and happy to prepare a takeout order. top_reviews.content:
Saam, a Thai restaurant with its own unique character.

The flavors are delicious,
and the presentation of each dish has such a beautiful sense of style.

The interior is just as impressive.
The lighting is beautiful, with warm brown and neutral tones that work perfectly together.

For drinks, the focus is mostly on a carefully selected wine list.
No cocktails though, sadly 🥲

I had the chance to try one of their wines,
and it paired beautifully with the food.
Thank you for the wine 🙂

As for the price…

Ouchhh 😂

The service was okay overall.
One area that could make the experience even better would be more polished and knowledgeable service throughout the meal.

With food presented at this level, I would love to hear the staff explain each dish with more confidence and detail, including the ingredients, flavors, and the chef’s inspiration behind it. I think that extra touch would help guests appreciate the food even more and elevate the overall dining experience.

But overall, I really loved the atmosphere here.
It’s a great choice for a special occasion, especially if you’re looking for somewhere intimate, stylish, and a little elevated.

The whole time I was thinking,
“I really want to photograph this restaurant.” 😂

As a Thai, this is probably the closest thing to fine dining from home that I’ve had in SF.

I’ve been following Chef Ton for years, so when I found out he was opening Saam in San Francisco, I literally counted down the days. I came on opening day and somehow ended up ordering… basically the whole menu. 😂

Every single dish surprised me. Chef Ton, Chef Tee, and Chef Ty took Thai flavors I grew up with and turned them into something completely different while still feeling so Thai. There were so many combinations I would’ve never expected, but they just worked.

The food was incredible, but honestly the whole experience was. The space is beautiful, service was super warm (not stuffy at all), and the drink pairings were on point.

You can tell there’s so much thought behind every dish, from the ingredients to the presentation to the story it tells.

If you’re looking for your typical pad thai or green curry… this isn’t that. This is Thai cuisine on another level, and I’m so happy SF finally has a restaurant like this.

Already planning my next visit. ❤️

The dishes are very special! Beautiful setup.
Just hoping to try cocktails next time when we return. (It’s their first day so not everything is on the menu is ready.)

Dessert is a bit overpriced tbh, but mango & sticky rice is my all time favorite.

My dining experience at SAAM last week
exceeded expectations, blending a gorgeous atmosphere with stellar hospitality and bold, vibrant flavors.

From the moment we walked in, the hospitality stood out. The host at the front greeted us immediately and led us to our table. He even noticed that other servers were tied up with nearby tables and thoughtfully poured our water himself—a small touch of proactive care that set the tone for the night.

The interior ambiance is beautiful, creating a warm and inviting setting. However, the absolute highlight of our evening was our server, Best. Incredibly attentive, hospitable, and full of great energy, Best completely livened up our dinner experience and made us feel genuinely welcome.

Menu Highlights
•    Som Tum Peaches (Appetizer): A fantastic way to start the meal. It carried a bit more heat than expected, but the sweetness of the fresh peaches provided a wonderful balance. I would definitely order this again.
•    Gaeng Kua Beef Curry: When the clam curry we originally wanted sold out, Best proposed substituting it with beef. That pivot turned out to be one of the stars of the night. While also on the spicier side, the curry featured incredible depth of flavor and was exceptionally good.
•    Khao Soi Haeng Seafood: Although we initially expected a traditional soupy noodle dish, this arrived as a dry version. Despite the surprise, it was intensely flavorful, packed with seafood, and easily tied with the curry as our favorite dish of the evening.
•    Mango Sticky Rice Meringue: We finished the night on a high note with this dessert. The mango was exceptionally juicy and sweet, and the meringue topping added a creative and delightful texture.

Because a few items like the pla phao were sold out by the time we ordered, we already have plenty of reasons to return and explore the rest of the menu. Between the stunning interior, Best’s top-tier service, and the phenomenal food, we are eagerly looking forward to our next visit.

I had such a lovely experience at SAAM! Everything was so beautiful and delicious, My favorite dish was the duck curry, the first bite reminded me of the curry my mom used to make at home—it brought back so many wonderful memories. It had that authentic, comforting Thai flavor I grew up with, but presented in such a beautiful and elegant way. It was truly the perfect balance of tradition and refinement. Everyone was so kind and welcoming, and you can really feel the passion behind every dish. I can’t wait to come back and try more of the menu. Thank you for such a wonderful meal!

top_reviews.content: Great food, lovely owners. The veggie platter was a great value for the price and everything was super flavorful and delicious. We walked in and ordered, the food came out in about 10 minutes. This is the only Indian takeout spot I need to go to now :)

Munch India operates with quiet rigor from a compact storefront just off Shattuck. There is no dining room, only a kitchen. The entire floor plan is devoted to the hotline and prep station. There is no freezer, only refrigeration. Ingredients are purchased daily, mostly from Berkeley Bowl a few blocks away. Orders are placed online each morning before noon; cooking begins after.

The daily walk-in menu is limited, changes daily, and is prepared to order. The results are consistently superb. Spicing is precise, textures are balanced, and the dishes—drawn from across India—reflect deep training and care. The chefs, Diana Afroza and Nick Ahmed, have cooked professionally since the early 1990s, with backgrounds in Boston, Europe, and India.

Prices are extremely reasonable given the quality and labor involved. They are searching for a larger, dine-in location. If they find one, their costs—and likely their prices—will rise. For now, this is high-level regional Indian cooking, offered at below-market prices. It smells wonderful inside and the people you’ll meet are awesome. Order while you can.

Well, I went right in and had about the best sandwiches I've ever had.  5 stars and well worth the trip!  ☆☆☆☆☆

Got the roast chicken lunch box—containing enough tasty olives, delicious chicken and unbelievable potatoes to serve 2. I would happily back to try the grab and go food, the sausages, and desserts offerings. The small outdoor dining area and great service are nice, too. Go!

finally went here for a picnic with some friends last weekend and it was such a good time. the grilled cheese was perfect, super crispy and melty, exactly what i wanted. we grabbed a spot on the lawn nearby and just hung out for like two hours cause the food held up well. i honestly dont even remember what my friend ordered but she kept saying how good her sandwich was too. the vibe was just really chill and easy, not pretentious at all. im already planning to go back next time im in the area.

Thoroughly mediocre chicken shop/specialty grocer.

Stopped in for 1/2 rotisserie chicken box. Found they had a decent selection of sodas, non-alc bevs, wines, prepared sausages, specialty goods. May stop back in for these other things.

The half chicken, at almost $20, came packed in the box atop chicken schmaltz roasted potatoes. It was paired with hot olives and roasted garlic. An assortment of sauces (aioli some kind of green sauce and some kind of red sauce) were provided.

The chicken was aggressively seasoned and moist. Unfortunately none of the flavor had penetrated the skin which meant that if the piece was without skin, you’re left with the bland flesh. The sauces were all meh. Potatoes, perfect. Olives, nicely varied. My guess is that the bird could have been cooked a little longer and seasoned a little further in advance. (And also checked for feathers.)

I also had a slice of the key lime pie. The beauty of key lime pie is the sharp acidity of these limes (which are in season right now) and the intense floral profile of the oils in the rind. This pie was all oil and not sharp at all. Which is a shame because otherwise, it was great. Not cloyingly sweet, not too much cream on the palate. Oh well.

Hands down the best rotisserie chicken I ever had! The potatoes are cooked with chicken schmaltz and very addicting. They have so many other amazing selections from handmade sausages to their daily sandwiches. I always highly recommend this place to all of my family and friends and now I’m telling you to go and try it out, you won’t be disappointed!

I don't know about their claim that they have the best paninis in SF, but they certainly today became my favorite panini place in not only SF, but the entire bay area.

I have 3 chilhood perfect food experience that became aldult obsessions. Tiramisu, croque monsieur, and panini. I have been searching for yeaaars for a panini that could live up to the one from my childhood sandwich shop in southeast france, and literally ordered paninis all over the US.

The closest came from Elysee Bakery near UCLA (too far), and 2nd place was Alexander Patisserie's old paninis before they removed them from the menu, then changed the bread when they brought them back.

By the time I just happened to walk by this place, I basically gave up virtually trying every places with paninis in the menu within the vicinity of my outings or even actively searching. I remembered searching years ago for all places with paninis in their menu around Union Square. But having been disappointed so many times within the bay, I didn't have much faith in anything being different in SF and never tried further. And it's been months since I've stopped searching.

So even though I paused in my steps when walked by and I saw that the pics looked somewhat similar to my childhood panini, I just resumed walking past the shop for half a block.

Somehow, something stopped me in my tracks, and I begrudgingly used my precious data to look at the review pictures to check that their display pics were not deceiving. Then, looked at their menu to see if they had an option that at least could potentially recreate the elusive taste of that chilhood panini.

They didn't have what I wanted, but they had a prosciutto option, which was the bare minimum ingredient I wanted. Being obsessed still with recreating that taste, now that I knew about this faint potential, I had to try. At worst, it's still a panini! You can't go wrong with a panini.

OH. EM. Freaking geeee!!! I can't freaking believe it. I went in fully expecting to be disappointed, again. Boy am I shocked. And thankful to whatever made me give this a try. It wasn't the exact taste (my childhood panini was more elaborate with sliced tomatoes and pulled mozzarella), but the taste of the prosciutto was so so close, if not identical. And how the bread was done is exactly the style I'm chasing after. This just made my freaking entire last month of the year.

But what makes me take the unusual effort write a review was not the panini, but the gentleman (owner?) who took in my order. His manners and courtesy were impeccable. Made me feel like he truly valued my patronage.

So even though the panini experience here is unique to me and less relevant to others, I still want to write this review and contribute to the 5 stars because I wanted to reward his conduct which made me feel welcomed.

I'm also writing this review because I can still, despite nostalgia driving my own preference, recommend this place with high confidence:

They claim on their display that their philosophy for a good sandwich is simple but best quality ingredients. I believe them. I tasted quality. So many places prosciutto taste stale, but not this one. And they include quite a generous amount of it! Loved that the bite felt substantial.

So based on that, I feel fairly confident that you can try any options on their menu that suits your own taste (rather than my specific choice) and still come up with a satisfying delish sandwich.
If you ever want to support a place who value their customers, clearly prioritizes on creating quality, uses quality ingredients and are generous with their meat, and try as a bonus what a panini that uses baguette as bread (doughy flavourful inside, satisfyingly crunchy exterior!), give this place a try!

For my part, I'm sad there's no option to add tomatoes or mozzarella (they have halloumi instead), because I'd have been so close to succeeding in recreating my childhood panini then.
But I know I'll definitely come back here every time I'm in SF. I added-on cheddar this time, so I'll try the halloumi next!

top_reviews.content: I was up on the North side boppin around with a group of Jamaican Astro Physicists showing them what a typical Berkeley hipster dofus looks like, and I'll tell you they were not impressed!  This group of intellects even snubbed their noses at the freelanders at the people's park, and our walk up Telegraph Ave didn't even raise an eyebrow..they told me the people in Berkeley don't know how to be layed back, and cool like an island breeze.  We settled in at Bongo Burgers up in Northside because they liked the name, it seams the group also has a band back on the island that is made up mostly bongo drums and steel drums!  Everybody in the group had an amazing lunch and as soon as they were finished, the leader, Bogart passed out Ganja..(weed) to everyone, and the had a group high out on the sidewalk!  I had the chicken sando and rings...it was amazing! 5 ☆☆☆☆☆'s

Bongo Burger in Berkeley is hands down one of my favorite spots! The food is always amazing and consistently delicious every single time. The Persian Burger is by far the BEST burger on the menu — packed with flavor and absolutely unforgettable.

The owner is also incredibly kind and welcoming, which makes the experience even better. Anyone visiting or living in Berkeley needs to stop by and try this place. Highly recommend!

Really enjoyed Bongo Burger! The Persian burger was delicious—great flavor and cooked really well. The fries were crispy and tasty, and the kabob wraps were also really good. Solid spot if you’re craving burgers or Persian-style comfort food. Will definitely be back!

Bongo Burger is still the best burger in the Bay.

What makes it so good is the style. It’s not a massive, overloaded burger… it’s light (but filling), balanced, and somehow they manage to make a thin patty that’s still cooked medium-rare, juicy, and perfectly pink in the center. That’s surprisingly hard to find.

The grilled onions have are so good on the burger, really make it a signature. Add fresh chopped lettuce, ripe tomato, and the classic Bongo Burger bun, and it’s just a perfect combo. Also the use of two different color cheeses really makes it visually appetizing.

The fries are equally impressive. They’re crispy on the outside but somehow stay soft, fluffy, and full of actual potato on the inside instead of drying out.

The cooks are talented clearly.

On top of all that, the prices are incredibly reasonable, the staff is always friendly, and the vibe feels like old Berkeley in the best possible way.

The Euclid location is my favorite. I grew up eating there in the ‘90s, and I’m amazed that the quality is still just as good today. Places like this are rare. I hope Bongo Burger is around forever.

I decided to try this place after seeing a recommendation. While I always enjoy exploring new burger spots, I have to say that my favorite burger is still In-N-Out, especially when factoring in cost.

I arrived early and was the first customer of the day, which gave me the opportunity to observe how the restaurant prepared their food. One thing that stood out to me—but not in a good way—was how they handled the grilled onions and bacon. Rather than cooking fresh ingredients in the morning, they simply reheated leftover onions and bacon from the previous day and used them for my burger. That was disappointing because I expected everything to be freshly prepared, especially for the first order of the day.

That said, there were some positives. The onion rings were excellent—crispy, and cooked perfectly. I really enjoyed them. The burger itself was just okay. One detail I found odd was the cheese. Instead of a traditional slice of cheese, they sprinkled cheese particles on the patty, which didn’t quite give the same melt-in-your-mouth experience.

As for the drink, the Coke (Pepsi) was fine—nothing to complain about, but nothing remarkable either.

Overall, it wasn’t a bad experience, but I wouldn’t go out of my way to return.

Hubby and I are in culinary heaven! Stopped into this Oakland gem inside the Prescott Market. He had the sweet potato pancakes with berry compote , fresh made whipped cream and …wait for it….toasted hazelnuts. I had the andouille shrimp & grits. Ya’ll know that’s my go to meal. Their version was definitely like none I’ve ever had. The grits are imported from Carolina. The texture was amazing. Just the right ratio (cause I’m a math girl) of shrimp, sausage and sauce. And with just the right amount of kick. Will definitely be a regular stop every time we are in town. You’ve gotta go check out this husband & wife team. Tell Marissa that Michelle from Riverside sent you.

Went there for lunch. The owner was friendly, engaged, warm, lively and helpful. The shrimp taco salad was one of the best salads the 3 of us have ever had. The blueberry lemonade was delicious also. We can’t wait to go back!
