top_reviews.content: Fantastic kimbap, very satisfying. Particularly loved the fried shrimp kimbap! The soup that came with was light and refreshing, and the tteokbokki was delicious. Also enjoyed the barley tea and the rice punch. Service was friendly and attentive. Hefty kimbap portions. I didn't personally enjoy having k-pop music videos playing on a whole wall, but I was able to sit facing away and that was just fine. Would love to go back.

Nice interior, good service, decent food, but wish they also had regular size kimbap.

I saw this restaurant a few weeks ago but it was closed. Today, attended an event nearby and decided to try this place out for dinner. After entering the restaurant, I saw that the interior was bright and had wooden panels. A video of a park in Seoul was projected on a wall that also had small achromatic paintings of some dishes. I could tell from the steel beams that the building isn't modern, but this business has done a great job with making the place feel up to date.

I approached the person working and asked to see the menu and was directed to a QR code to scan, which was a little annoying. It would be great if they had a screen near the counter with some of their recommended items or a brief menu. The menu online had a lot of items available, so I needed a few minutes to scroll through. I wanted to try their fried seaweed roll (4pcs for $5) and also ordered bulgogi kimbap ($15), a safe choice for my first visit.

The worker brought over some sweet chili dipping sauce and utensils, and a few minutes later, the food I ordered plus a complimentary bowl of broth. The fried seaweed roll had sweet potato glass noodles, the kind for japchae, in seaweed that had been battered and fried. It was simple but delicious with the dipping sauce. The kimbap came in a long serving container that spanned across my table. Wang kimbap (giant kimbap) is a relatively new thing that looks good for social media but is a bit uncomfortable to eat. Each piece fully filled my mouth and took like 30 seconds to fully chew. But least it was a good amount of food for the price. I wish they sold normal sized kimbap as well though.

While I was eating, I noticed a small fly buzzing around. It eventually landed in my sauce, got stuck, and died in it. Luckily I was already done with the fried seaweed rolls. I asked the worker to take the sauce away and he did it immediately, and he also later apologized for the fly even though it wasn't his fault.

I feel like some of the items' prices were a little high, like $5 for barley tea when some Korean restaurants give that for free, $23 for simple rice plates, or $14 for instant ramyeon, but the kimbap was fair value considering that it's freshly made to order and huge. There is a large selection of noodles, fried chicken, and street food in addition to kimbap.

I noticed that there was a step up from the street to the restaurant level so it might not be wheelchair accessible. The Tenderloin has a lot of people with disabilities who live or access services in the neighborhood. There is one restroom in the back.

We had a great time at Kimbap Heaven! We originally had plans to eat at a brunch spot nearby, but got overwhelmed by the crowd, so we decided to pop in. The restaurant is small, but very clean and well-kept. We had the bulgogi kimbap, the ssam kimbap, and the soy garlic fried chicken, which were all delicious! The kimbap comes with a side of soup for each person, which was very nice. The owner was incredibly kind, and came to check on us every so often (granted, we were the only ones dining in, however we saw several delivery drivers come in to pick up orders).

so happy they got their own brick and mortar store location!!! order ahead for pick up using toast app and it’s so easy. their kimbap is double the size of usual traditional size so the price isn’t so bad at all considering that. i feel lucky to have them nearby. absolutely love their food!

Menu authentic in its delivery of new Korean snack bar (분식).

Fresh kimbap expertly rolled, albeit a little light on the protein-filling.  Kimchi Fish Cake Udon is flavorful, but not crave-worthy.

Clean finish interior.

Take It Easy Thai Cuisine has been around for more than 8 years! I used to come here when my daughter went to the high school around the corner and came by often to get lunch.
I usually get the Pad See Ew, Pad Thai noodles, or the coconut curries. Today, I wanted to try something different, which was the Beef Jungle Curry. This dish is on the dry style curry, not the soupy kind, and I loved the spice and kick it had. The Beef Jungle curry was served over rice, and I must say I was impressed and enjoyed this dish!
Service was fast, and the staff was awesome! Although there's other options in the area, I believe this is one of those mom and pop's restaurants that need some support from the community. The prices are still on the cheaper side for the portion you get. Hole in the wall kinda spot. I would definitely come back and support this neighborhood gem again!

While their Pad See Ew tastes quite different (a bit tangy) compared to other Thai places I've tried, the garlic chicken skewers were pretty good. The place overall looks a bit unmaintained. The good thing they have going is that their menu prices are relatively cheap when compared to the surrounding restaurants.

You order/pay at the counter before sitting down. The food came out within 5 or so minutes. I ordered the Beef Rad Na, my trusty taste test to see if the food is good and it was amazing. I mean you can’t go wrong with Fresh broccoli cooked to perfection, beef seared in a wok just the way you want it and the black sweet soy sauce was oh SOoo delicious Mmmm. I will definitely be back.

This is a great place for a nice date night.

This restaurant is now going to be on our regular rotation when we come over from the City to Berkeley Rep.  The hand rolls are each unique and exquisite; the cocktails are inventive and enhanced w/Japanese touches; and our server couldn’t have been better — friendly and professional and enhanced our experience w/expertise as well as generosity.

top_reviews.content:
This is a local South Indian restaurant chain with locations across the Bay Area, and this Berkeley location is a smaller one. We stopped by on the weekend for a quick filter coffee and a plate of masala/dal vada.

The vada was a little on the dry side, perhaps because it had been sitting for a while, although thankfully it wasn’t greasy. The filter coffee was pretty standard for the chain, and I especially like to have it with a spoonful of jaggery.

Overall, a quick and decent stop for South Indian coffee and snacks.

Very good place! Good deal on the combo in terms of price, only $11 for a dosa, medhu, and idly, and everything was delicious. The chai was very well balanced and they had jaggery to put in which was good and felt special.

In the south Indian desert that is Oakland it is very refreshing to see a stalwart take root in Berkeley. Everything Idly Express touches is savory gold. If you haven't spent time in Madras this will give you a good simulation - the music, the heavy smell of filter coffee in the air, the coffee itself....it all adds towards the small hustling and bustling vegetarian "hotels" one finds in Madras.

The food is unapologetically spicy and that's good. It keeps the flavors and the textures close the source. The soaked idlis were decadent as were the crunchy vadas. The korma had that sharpness to it and the benne dosa's life force ran all over my palm as I devoured it like a mild-mannered Bakasura at the local village.

The place is small and very functional. It's not date night material unless your date is an adventurous eater whose idea of Indian food is all the stereotypical north indian fare. Then, this place is the beginning of an adventure.

Beware, travel with a bottle of lassi, for the road is spicy ahead.

We've eaten at the restaurant 4-5 times since it's opening. Service is always speedy and the food arrives within 5-10 mins consistently. The staff are friendly  & attentive. Nice to have tasty South Indian food in Berkeley. Our favorites are the ghee podi idly, medhu vadai and masala dosa. The thali is great to share with someone if you aren't too hungry. The curd rice in the thali is creamy and delicious. The chai and filter coffee are must haves!

Bonus tip: The dosa batter in the takeout fridges make crispy golden brown dosas. Highly recommend!
It's an amazing experience and the food is unbelievable quality and consistency

​I recently visited Emeryville for a business trip and brought my family along. Our accommodation was close to the Emeryville Public Market, so we ended up trying a bunch of different places there. The food hall has a great variety of options—the burger place was excellent, and so was the sushi spot.
​But Nabi Q Korean BBQ was definitely the highlight for me! As a Korean, it tasted just like home, and even my 5-year-old loved it. We really appreciated that they had both low, round tables for families with kids and high standing tables, so everyone could find a comfortable spot to eat.
​While all the food was good, Nabi Q was my favorite. I've attached a photo of the delicious meal we had there. If you're looking for a casual place with lots of great food options that cater to families, I highly recommend checking out the Public Market food hall!

Hubby and I were attending the opening of the Emeryville Art Exhibition and popped over to the Public Market for a bite to eat. I was hungry but nothing really grabbed me, so after circling twice I ended up at NabiQ and ordered the bibimbap with spicy pork and egg on top while he went to a different food stall. It was a generous portion, enough for two. The food looked appealing but the meat was too sweet for my taste even after mixing the whole thing together. It came with a small cup of kimchi and gochujang sauce. I picked at it the food but left quite a bit uneaten, didn't want to take it home. Price was over $22, including tip.

The person who took my order was friendly and polite. Food came fairly quickly. The kitchen area was clean and tidy, no complaints there.

I'll be back for sure.

top_reviews.content:
Super fresh banh mi with organic tofu! (4/5 Green Stars)
I wish I had tried this place earlier! I had the banh mi with organic tofu for lunch and the total cost, including tax and a 20% tip was $10.50! I was ravenous and had some concerns that it may not be enough – or come fast enough! However, the lady who took my order prepped the sandwich in as much time as it took me to take a few photos. Also, there was really a lot of tofu in the sandwich – two thick layers of it – so in the end it was pretty darn filling.

There were several memorable things about the sandwich, which I ate without any distraction even though I would normally read while eating. The bread was at a perfect state of crispiness – like a proper French roll – very light and also lightly toasted. The crunchy veggies – the daikon in particular, added a freshness to it that counterbalanced the umami of soy and tofu. I’ve only had a couple of banh mi sandwiches in my time but this one was not only the best so far but has also set a pretty high bar to measure others against.

I’m giving the Sidewalk Street Food 4/5 Green Stars for social and environmental impact. It’s a woman-owned and run business that offers affordable food in a fairly unaffordable neighborhood. Every dish option – banh mi, salad bowl, pho, and spring rolls all had a tofu option. Some of the other options – chicken and pork – are among the more sustainable choices for meat eaters. However, beef and shrimp are among the worst options Sidewalk loses a star for that. My sandwich was pretty much zero-waste in that it was wrapped in a sheet of paper and delivered in a reusable basket.
I love coming to this place for my lunch. I either get the pho with only broth and noodles or spring rolls (shrimp).

top_reviews.content: Loved this cozy Thai spot! The food was delicious and beautifully served. The atmosphere was cozy and relaxing, making it a great spot for a date or a nice meal with friends. I’ll definitely be coming back with my boyfriend next time. Highly recommend!

Another favorite of mine is the morning glory salad — a dish that’s practically impossible to find elsewhere. The crispness of the morning glory combined with the refreshing salad dressing makes it unforgettable.

I’ve been back a few times since their opening and will keep coming back for more! (oh yea, don’t forget to book in advance, the spots fill up fast)

Overall, the food tasted authentically Thai, the service was friendly, and the atmosphere was perfect for a date night. I would definitely come back to try more dishes.

top_reviews.content: I believe the restaurant's catch phrase is "one bute, so juicy" and they're right. This place was delicious; they had a such a wide variety of dumplings, skewers, salad, and traditional Chinese dishes. We got a little bit of everything and it was all so tasty. Dumpling Day would be our new go-to Chinese restaurant when we visit Berkeley!

I've passed by this spot many times during my lunch walks and finally got a chance to try it! I usually get Guilin rice noodles from other places in the area, so I was excited to see another option.

I ordered the A1 House Special Pot-Roasted Guilin Rice Noodles with marinated beef, beef tripe, and crispy pork. I really enjoyed it, the flavors were great, the portion size was generous (I could probably split it into two meals), and the price was very affordable.

An acquired taste that diverges from the standard Chinese-American kitchen, Guilin Rice Noodles serves authentic dry noodle, noodle soups and side dishes.

Hot and Sour Guilin Rice Noodles sings of spiciness and a taste of fermentation from pickled vegetables. A healthy, and refreshing option especially when in need of a hangover cure. Liver and intestine toppings for those more adventurous. Smoked peanuts make for a wonderfully savory topping.

The crab sandwiches are divine as they’re crispy, have great fresh flavor, and the bread is perfectly fluffy. Also, the owner Khánh was so informative and engaging as she shared the ethnic roots of her family’s cooking behind the food. Of particular note, if you have been to Japan and have enjoyed the wonders of the aforementioned convini-lifestyle (or other Asian countries for that matter) then you will be pleased to know these egg sandwiches are probably the best American option I’ve had to this date. They’re wonderfully light and have that perfect egg-to-mayo ratio that I’ve missed since returning from Tokyo. Apparently Khánh brought together the influence of having lived in Japan to this setup and it’s such a refreshing take on grab-and-go eateries. The garlic noodles and vermicelli salad (Bún) are must haves. Seriously. You need to try these. I think this is probably my favorite garlic noodles to date as they’re not overpowering or oily but just perfectly balanced for that satisfying savory flavor. They have hot food options in addition to the cold fridge grab-and-go so if you’re there, try everything out. I know I have enjoyed it and will be back to do just that.

Really love this place! The fried banana has me in a chokehold. I crave it weekly and it’s reminiscent of something you’d eat at a night market is SE Asia.

I’m beyond disappointed and won’t be back sadly.

I gotta say the price is a little high for a sandwich/meal, mine came out to 22+(tip).

This now "corporate" chain is a far cry from it's humble beginnings. The portions have been significantly reduced, and I expect more for a $15 sando. I can hit other places for less $ and a better offering.

There are two things/"policies" that don't sit well with me: 1) they have no paper menus to take away. I'm sure the are being environmentally conscientious (they COULD use recycled paper) or they mistakenly assume that EC's older population is tech savvy enough to deal. I see this as a missed opportunity for them, unless they don't feel that is a demographic worth catering to.
2) I paid cash, and did not have any $1 bills to use for the tipping bucket. I asked to change a $5,and was flatly told "we don't give change". Shocked, I begrudgingly dropped a $5 in the bucket.

These may seem like trivial things, but to me seem like a lack of customer focus.

That being said, the staff were polite.

They probably deserve more than a 3, but I'm OK giving this score. I am in no rush to go back.

top_reviews.content:
I can see this becoming a town staple real quick. Food was top notch. The Cali Ceviche was one of the best I’ve had, so good that I practically drank the sauce out of the bottom of the dish. My new obsession. I brought my friend who's visiting from out of town, so this was our first time here. We immediately loved the atmosphere, and the service and people are so nice and attentive. There are some dining experiences where you leave thinking, "I paid all that and could've made it at home," or, "this tastes like so many other places I've been to." For us, most of the dishes we ordered felt special to this restaurant.

Highly recommend!

Oh the years we spent at Lukas’s. Both of our kids went to OSA and Luka’s was on the regular Friday night rotation for sure since it was so close. I would call this an upgraded redo, for sure. The space is casual enough and yet definitely feels like an elevated night out. A very warm welcome at the door and service was friendly and on top of it all night. The crowd was quintessentially Oakland. There were mostly young, fun – looking Oaklanders. But there were a few of us elders, holding things down. The tables on either side of us turned while we were there so we didn’t really talk with the first patrons in those tables, but the second set on each side were super fun. Of course, when one side came in looking like they just did a thru-hike on the PCT with their backpack gear and hiking clothes I had to inquire. Turns out they had gone over to Stern Grove for the Public Enemy concert and just made their way back. Brilliant. So, atmosphere= A+. Food: As a pescatarian, the fact that I could eat 3/4 of the menu items was thrilling. I had the trout, which is from Lassen County and the street corn. Hubby had a steak. The trout was very flavorful and the sauce, which wasn’t a sauce per se, but more of an au jus,, was just right. The street corn was 1000% delicious. We also started with cocktails and moved onto red wine – all were very good. We will definitely return and would probably also enjoy sitting at the bar to eat our meal, as their bar looked fun.

I am so excited about this spot! 10/10  decor, food, drinks, service. The desert heat cocktail was one of the best I’ve had recently and all the sauces were so flavorful and unique. Amazing new oakland mainstay

Those familiar with Caged Heat syrup will love the Desert Heat cocktail and the Pisco Sour was also delicious.  The ceviche with mangos and coconut milk was fabulous.  The muscles were fat and high quality and the lemony broth a perfect accompaniment.  Fideos con queso was a very satisfying side, great caesar salad and finger licking churros with chocolate.  Wait staff were the right amount of attentive and the place had a lively buzz. We will be back as regulars!

top_reviews.content:
What a gem! In the courtyard of the Anthropology Museum, you’ll find this charming oasis. Everything from the furniture, landscape, menu, and soundtrack are all thoughtfully procured. Afternoon tea consisted of 3 refreshing flavors of tea and 3 sweet dishes. The chia seed porridge was a generous portion with a delicious flavor profile as well as texture. The toasted hazelnuts added a tasty crunch. Blackberries and gooseberries were a nice palate cleanser, and the chia seed flour brownie bites were addictive! The black walnuts and coarse East Bay salt were a perfect combination! I’m thankful they don’t sell these individually otherwise I would be eating them daily. In bulk.
Not only was the meal unique and delicious, we also learned some Ohlone history and words as well as heard some lovely songs and spoken word that were pre-recorded. It’s such a nice experience and so much more than just food and drinks!

Truly magical find.

In addition to rare local foods, they treated us to games, stories, and song.

It's difficult to find behind the bookstore, but well worth the unique and private experience.

The decor of acorns, nuts, abalone, and cattails was really lovely.

Also, they provide lovely serapes for the chill.

BE HERE

Tucked behind University Press Books is a transformative place that allows you to turn back time. The lovingly gathered and carefully prepared foods are nothing like any foods typically eaten today. Instead, these foods are the mainstay foods that allowed the Ohlone people to live in peace and in harmony with their environment for thousands of years. The two indigenous men who have created this incredible space and menu come from an unbroken line of people who have lived in the East Bay for thousands of years. The foods they are offering take a tremendous amount of time and labor, but they are not offering them in a simple format. The foods are rich and complex and take freshness to an entirely new level. Be prepared to sit outside, dress warmly. Be prepared to learn. There will be abundant information given about each course. Be prepared to ask questions. They want to start conversations that feed your soul as well as your body. Be prepared for adventure. This is an incredible opportunity to explore foods you may not otherwise taste. This is fine dining at its very best.

This place is a MUST. Deliciously fanciful, natural, clean & exquisitely flavorful dishes from our Bay Areas very own indigenous Ohlone tribe. The experience has been well thought out, and you can truly see the intentions that are full of LOVE here. This is as LOCAL and NATIVE as it gets!! Not enough stars for how happy this place makes me & how fulfilling the tastes!!

The great thing about this place is it is done for awareness of ohlone that are still indigenous to the east bay. They have not moved from here ever. Hopefully this place can raise awareness that they are much alive and well as a culture. I was concerned I might not liie some of the food for the snacks and tea on tuesday night but it was delicious and very natural to the nearby land. The experience is great as it is communal at picnic tables, preceeded by prayer, and the food is explained. Very spiritual and tasty. It was an overall great experience. Highly recommended!

Wish we lived closer and could come all the time - it's well worth a trip from anywhere in the bay, come hungry. 🙌🏻

I was disappointed to find that the only vegan options were simply vegetarian dishes with the cheese removed. A quesadilla without cheese? No thanks. It's frustrating to lose a key component of a meal while still paying full price.

Things became more disappointing when I asked for a side of hot sauce or salsa and was told I'd have to purchase an entire bottle instead. Considering the relatively high prices and modest portion sizes, it seemed unreasonable that a small side of salsa or hot sauce wasn't available. The food itself was fresh and well prepared, but it lacked flavor and felt dry without any sauce or cheese.

The final straw came as we were leaving. After finishing our meal, we were scolded for not bussing our own table. It wasn't obvious that customers were expected to do this, and the interaction felt awkward and unnecessary. It also felt strange that no one checked on us during the meal or refilled our water, yet someone was quick to point out that we hadn't cleared our table.

The table next to us also appeared to have a frustrating experience. The cashier missed part of their order, and when they brought it to the staff's attention, the missing item wasn't prioritized. They ended up waiting long after everyone else at their table had finished eating. When they asked if the order could be expedited, they were essentially told no.

I would have gladly paid the higher prices for better service, more thoughtful vegan options, and a dining experience that didn't feel like I was being nickel-and-dimed at every turn. I really wanted to love this place, but unfortunately I won't be back.

top_reviews.content: I must say I had high hopes for this new restaurant. I've been in this neighborhood for 50 years and loved Uzen. Well, I love Japanese food in general and was excited to try a new place. However, I was quite disappointed in Gamsa's nigiri. THEY DRENCH EACH NIGIRI WITH SOY SAUCE!!!!!!! You don't taste the fish. You just taste SALT!!! Ikura is usually a rich orange color. Because they use soy sauce after making each nigiri, their ikura is BROWN!! I kid you not! ALL their sushi was way too salty, even the barracuda when I asked them to make it without soy sauce. They claim the fish is salty. I consider myself a sushi connoisseur  and I have NEVER tasted salty fish in sushi. To be fair, the chiwanmushi was good (although salty also!) The rainbow roll  was NOT drenched in soy sauce, but the crab inside tasted salty. They only serve full bottles of sake, not glasses. (maybe later?) The service was great, as well as the atmosphere. Very cozy and comfortable. I will give it a second chance and order the sashimi salad, chicken karaagi, and udon and see if they are salty. If so, I'm never going back!

top_reviews.content: Finally Khao soy Lao soup in Albany over in the old matchpoint brewing space. large portions and good prices, $10 rice plates all day is unheard of these days, they're really doing the neighborhood a service by offering fresh affordable food.

I am SO happy souk savanh is back! My sisters and I used to go to their original location back in Oakland on E. 14 many years ago.

We are so happy they have opened up again in Albany. We still live in Oakland but it’s definitely worth the drive to Albany for their delicious Lao and Thai food.

We stopped by yesterday on a Saturday right at opening. I got the kasoy noodle soup and my sister got the boat noodle soup and we also shared a Lao papaya salad.

Everything was great, really good flavors. Their menu also has a variety of rice plates, stir fries, noodle soups, stir fried noodles, combo plates, etc.

Can’t wait to come back soon to try more things. There is plenty of free street parking and a good amount of tables inside the restaurant. I would recommend to anyone looking for some tasty Lao and Thai cuisine.
